The player pays it, or any distribution expectation, with `investor/payReturn { agreementId, amountUsd }` at any time; an inbox reminder fires in week 48. §11 posts the payment as an investor distribution (`eq.draws` sub-ledger per agreement) and it reduces `prefUnpaid`. Unpaid pref stays in `prefUnpaid`, which raises that holder's claim and blocks owner draws above living cost.

| Stance (S) | Equity consequences |
|---|---|
| Content ≥ 60 | Approvals are granted automatically (logged). |
| Concerned 40–59 | Approvals are rolled at p = S/100. Monthly reporting is demanded: an `investorReport` obligation each month end (§6 calendar), filed with `finance/fileReport` or auto-filed by a controller or bookkeeper (§8); a missed report counts in sDistress. |
| Unhappy 20–39 | Draws above living cost are blocked. Minimum cash of $150k becomes a covenant (§11). The threshold halves (floor $25k) and approvals are rolled at p = S/100 − 0.2. The investor may require hedging 30% of next season (§10 `hedgedFineOz` hook). |
| Hostile < 20 for 2 consecutive check-ins | **Redemption demand** (blocking decision): pay BP within 26 weeks (via loans, asset sales, or a partner). Unpaid at the deadline, the run ends: *ousted by investor* (loss). While a reorganization case is open, no demand issues; a hostile holder moves to convert the case instead (below). |

```ts
interface InvestorAgreement {
  id: Id;                                        // prefix 'ivr' (§2.4 registry), e.g. ivr_000001
  name: string; kind: 'equity' | 'royalty';
  source: 'backed' | 'angel' | 'familyOffice' | 'miningFund' | 'rescue';
  contributedCents: Cents; startTurn: number; seniority: number;               // seniority = startTurn (later = senior)
  // equity terms (null for royalty)
  equityPct: number | null; prefRate: number | null; prefUnpaidCents: Cents;
  liquidationPrefMult: number | null;            // backed 1.0; angel 1.0; mining fund 1.5; rescue 1.0 (§11 11.13)
  approvalThresholdCents: Cents | null;          // backed $100k; angel $250k; family office / mining fund $100k; rescue > 50%: $25k
  ownerSalaryCapCents: Cents | null;             // $150k; rescue > 50%: $75k
  drawsBlockedUntilReturnedCents: Cents | null;  // rescue > 50%: 1.5 × contribution
  distributionExpectation: number | null;        // family office 0.25 of free cash flow from year 2
  hedgeShareRequired: number | null;             // mining fund 0.30 (P5)
  returnedCents: Cents;                          // cumulative pref and distributions paid to this holder
  // royalty terms (Backed royalty only)
  productionInterestId: Id | null; minimumAnnualCents: Cents | null; deliveredValueCents: Cents;
  // relationship
  satisfaction: number; stance: 'content' | 'concerned' | 'unhappy' | 'hostile'; hostileStreak: number;
  annualPlan: { year: number; fineOz: number; capexBudgetCents: Cents; capexUsedCents: Cents; approved: boolean } | null;
  approvalTokens: { subject: 'capex' | 'debt'; amountCents: Cents; expiresTurn: number }[];
  approvalCooldownUntil: { capex: number; debt: number };
  approvalRequestCount: { capex: number; debt: number };   // requestIndex of the next approval draw (keys the investor stream)
  redemptionDeadlineTurn: number | null;
  minimumCure: { obligationId: Id; shortfallCents: Cents; deadlineTurn: number } | null;   // royalty only (below)
  // reorganization (P4+; below)
  reorgCaseSeen: Id | null;                      // the §11 case (`reo` id) whose filing penalty this holder has taken
  redemptionStayedTurn: number | null;           // a redemption demand open at filing: stayed, then extinguished at confirmation
}
```

The royalty investor's satisfaction only sets the cure period on a missed minimum. It starts at 60. A year in which deliveries alone meet the minimum is +10; a top-up paid on time is 0; a missed top-up is −20. **Missed minimum (P4+).** §5 creates the week-52 top-up as an `Obligation` with owner `'§1'` (holder kind `'investor'`), and §6 routes a miss to §1's `investor.onMinimumMissed(state, obligationId)` instead of `land.onObligationMissed`. That handler sets `minimumCure`: 26 weeks if S ≥ 40, otherwise 8. Paying the shortfall before `deadlineTurn` clears it. At an uncured deadline (checked in 16b) the investor forecloses on the claim with the highest book value through §5 `land.transferToCreditor(state, tenureId, { kind: 'investor', id: agreementId })`: the tenure ends `'foreclosed'`, its remaining basis goes to `gain.assetSale`, §6 runs the operator change, and the shortfall is extinguished whatever the claim was worth. If no claims are left, the shortfall becomes unsecured debt (§11 `deficiency`). In P1–P3 a missed top-up is simply a failed payment and opens the P1 insolvency counter (1.14).

**Worked example (equity, Q3 check-in).** Plan 450 fine oz; YTD 260; S = 62. planYTD = 337.5, so sProd = 25·(0.770 − 1) = −5.7. Runway is 10 weeks (0). No distress (+2). Drift is 0.1·(60 − 62) = −0.2. ΔS = −3.9, giving S = 58.1: *concerned*. The second plant ($250k) is outside the approved plan budget, so it needs a 58% approval roll; if refused, the player cannot ask again for 4 weeks.

**Worked example (waterfall).** Backed equity, no pref arrears. At start companyNW = $1.5M: claim = min(1.5M, max(1.3M, 0.6M)) = $1.3M; ownerShare $0.2M; owner NW $250k. In week 6 the company has bought $1.2M of iron that marks at $0.9M resale, so companyNW = $1.2M: claim = min(1.2M, 1.3M) = $1.2M and ownerShare = 0 (not −$0.1M). At companyNW $5M: claim = max(1.3M, 2.0M) = $2.0M; ownerShare $3.0M. Now add an angel: $0.5M at V_pre $4.5M buys 10%, and §11's dilution scales the Backed 40% to 36% and the owner to 54%. At companyNW $5M the angel (senior) claims max(0.5M, 0.5M) = $0.5M, the Backed investor min(4.5M, max(1.3M, 1.8M)) = $1.8M, and ownerShare is $2.7M. A $54k owner draw pays the Backed investor $36k and the angel $10k.

**Worked example (two losing seasons → redemption).** Backed equity, standard, no debt. Plan 450 fine oz in both years (at or above the floor, so no −5).

| Check-in | planYTD / YTD oz | sProd | Runway → sCash | sDistress | Drift | S after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| start | | | | | | 65 |
| Y1 Q1 | 0 / 0 | 0 | ≥ 13 wk → +3 | none +2 | −0.50 | 69.5 content |
| Y1 Q2 | 112.5 / 30 | −10 (clamp) | 9 wk → 0 | none +2 | −0.95 | 60.6 content |
| Y1 Q3 | 337.5 / 170 | −10 | 5 wk → −6 | none +2 | −0.06 | 46.5 concerned |
| Y1 Q4 | 450 / 260 | −10 | 4 wk → −6 | none +2 | +1.35 | 33.8 unhappy: draws blocked, $150k minimum-cash covenant, threshold $50k |
| Y2 Q1 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 5 wk → −6 | covenant breach −4 | +2.62 | 26.5 unhappy |
| Y2 Q2 | 112.5 / 50 | −10 | 3 wk → −6 | covenant breach −4 | +3.35 | 9.8 hostile (1st) |
| Y2 Q3 | 337.5 / 210 | −9.4 | 4 wk → −6 | covenant breach −4 | +5.02 | 0 (clamped) hostile (2nd) |

The second hostile check-in (week 39 of year 2) issues the redemption demand, due at year 3 week 13. With companyNW $620k and pref arrears $78k (8% × $1.3M × 39/52), claim_a = min(620k, max(1.378M, 248k)) = $620k, so BP = 1.10 × $620k = $682k. A company with two losing seasons rarely has it: it must refinance, sell iron and ground, or bring in a partner within 26 weeks, or the run ends *ousted* before its third season starts. **Calibration (BALANCE O-06):** among cautious Backed-equity runs with two losing seasons (company-book net income < 0 in years 1 and 2), P(ouster, a forced redemption, or a reorganization filed while a redemption demand is open, by the end of season 3) is 40–70%; across all cautious Backed-equity runs, the 2-season loss rate (a bankruptcy filing of either kind, or ouster; that is, 1 − B2) is 8–25% (D-1.50). Backed-royalty runs report their loss rate without a band: the royalty investor's remedy is a claim, not the run.

**Investors in a reorganization (P4+).** §11 owns the case (eligibility, the automatic stay, the plan, confirmation and conversion). §1 owns what it does to each `InvestorAgreement`; 16b applies it, reading §11's `FinanceSlice.reorg`:
- **Filing penalty.** The first 16b that sees an open case whose id differs from `reorgCaseSeen` lowers S by `game.investor.reorgFilingPenalty` (20, × `penaltyMult`), recomputes the stance at once, and sets `reorgCaseSeen`. It applies once per case and per equity agreement. Royalty agreements take no stance change.
- **Check-ins continue**, with the two sDistress terms above (in reorganization −6; a missed plan payment −8). Approvals still apply to capex and debt above the threshold; new debt also needs the court's approval (§11).
- **The stay holds the investor's remedies.** No redemption demand issues while the case is open. A demand already open at filing is stayed (`redemptionDeadlineTurn` cleared, `redemptionStayedTurn` set) and is extinguished at confirmation: a claim to be bought out of the equity ranks behind every creditor (11 U.S.C. §510(b)), and the plan leaves nothing for it. `hostileStreak` resets to 0 at confirmation. An open `minimumCure` is cleared at filing; §11 carries the shortfall into the plan as a claim secured by the royalty lien, so no claim is foreclosed during the case. In-kind royalty deliveries continue at every cleanup: the interest runs with the claims (§5).
- **Conversion motion.** While a confirmed plan is running and any equity holder is hostile, that holder moves to convert for cause, so a single missed plan payment converts the case to liquidation instead of `finance.reorg.missedPaymentsToConvert` (2). §11 reads `investor.conversionMotionActive(state)`. (A material default under a confirmed plan is cause to convert, 11 U.S.C. §1112(b)(4)(N); the holder's motion is what turns one default into a conversion.)
- **No money to equity until the plan completes.** Pref keeps accruing into `prefUnpaid` (it raises the holder's waterfall claim), but `investor/payReturn` and `investor/buyOut` are refused (`REORG_OPEN`), and the owner's living allowance (1.9) is compensation, not a distribution, so it carries no pro-rata share. Automatic tax distributions continue.

**Worked example (reorganization with a Backed-equity holder).** Take the two-losing-season fixture above at the end of year 1 (S = 33.8, unhappy). In year 2 week 5 the company, about to be liquidated, files for reorganization. The next 16b applies the filing penalty: S = 33.8 − 20 = 13.8, hostile. At the week-13 check-in, sProd = 0 (Q1 profile), sCash = −6 (runway 5 weeks), sDistress = −6 (in reorganization, worse than the covenant breach's −4) and drift = 0.1·(60 − 13.8) = +4.62, so ΔS = −7.38 and S = 6.4: hostile (1st). No redemption demand can issue. The company files its plan in week 12 and the hearing in week 18 confirms it; `hostileStreak` resets to 0, and because the holder is still hostile its conversion motion is live: if the company misses one plan payment the case converts and the run ends in liquidation. Good production then pulls S back up (sProd up to +8 a quarter, drift toward 60); once S ≥ 20 the motion lapses and two missed payments are needed again.

#### 1.8.2 Inheritor: exactly what is inherited

Generated inside `newGame`, in the first `northernFederal` district, from §1's `setup` stream `rng(seed, 'setup', 'inheritor')` and its sub-keys (`'pits'` for §3's family pit logs, `'fleet', i` per machine, `'hand'` for the candidate). Only §1 draws on `setup` (§2.3 rule b), so `newGame` asks §1 for the streams and §1 hands each one to the section that uses it, as §4 hands its `sample` stream to §3's `drawSample` (D-1.65):

```
inheritorStreams(seed) = { ground: rng(seed,'setup','inheritor'), pits: rng(seed,'setup','inheritor','pits'),        // §1 (company/)
                           fleet: i ↦ rng(seed,'setup','inheritor','fleet',i), hand: rng(seed,'setup','inheritor','hand') }
newGame (Inheritor): s = inheritorStreams(seed); §3 genInheritedGroup(state, s.ground, s.pits);
                     §9 materializeInheritedFleet(spec, s.fleet); the former hand's candidate (§8) from s.hand
```

§3 implements the ground as `genInheritedGroup` (3.6.1) on a run of three parcels reserved in every world, so the world is identical across start types.
- **Family ground.** Three contiguous 20-acre unpatented federal valley placer claims (60 blocks) on one creek, with the district's access mix. Fees are paid through the current assessment year, and the owner is waiver-eligible. Tenure origin `'inherited'` (§5). No family override royalty in v1: §5's `'inherited'` interest origin is reserved for scenario content (D-1.41).
  - **Hidden quality.** A tier is drawn from `game.inheritorTierWeights` = {excellent 0.07, good 0.30, marginal 0.38, uneconomic 0.25}. This is clearly better than the open market (about 65% uneconomic) because the family kept the ground. §3 scales the run's grades so its reference economics land on the tier's target CDV (3.6.1: uneconomic −$75k, marginal +$300k, good +$1.2M, excellent +$4.0M). §3 also plays out twelve family seasons (2013–2024, ending three seasons before the 2027 start; ≈ 6,000 bcy each from the best remaining paystreak blocks) and adds `game.inheritorDepletionAdd` = +0.10 of old-timer depletion on the other paystreak blocks, because the family worked the best part. Expected contained-value margin across tiers ≈ +$0.74M (0.07 × 4.0 + 0.30 × 1.2 + 0.38 × 0.3 − 0.25 × 0.075), but a quarter of runs inherit ground that does not pay.
  - **Stripped ahead.** In its last season the family stripped ahead: `game.inheritor.preStrippedBlocks` = 2. §3 sets `strippedBcy = overburdenBcy`, `disturbed = true` and `thawProgress` U(3, 6) ft on the two best undug f ≥ 0.4 blocks of the group, the same rule as its `recentCat` pre-strip (consistent with `geology.oldTimer.preStripMaxAgeYr` 6). The player sees them as `preStripped` and can wash thawed pay early in season 1 instead of waiting on a frozen cut.
  - **Visible.** A family cleanup ledger for 2013–2024, e.g. "55–70 raw oz/yr" (≈ 45 oz true, §3 3.6.1), built from the true family seasons with §3's `optimistic` transform (×1.2–1.6). An honest-looking ledger still overstates what is left, because the family mined the best blocks. Four old test-pit logs dated U{2013..2024}, all on paystreak blocks (`familyRecords` evidence, §4: biased like an optimistic seller and given zero weight in the estimate until verified; verification from P2, while P1 shows them and runs §4's claim-wide plausibility test). A records review can find `filedProduction` for the family seasons. An estate appraisal of $120,000, derived from visible facts only, which becomes the claims' cost basis.
- **Worn fleet.** Already on site, so there is no mobilization. Each machine shows visible age, hours, and a resale estimate: §9's `materializeInheritedFleet` creates the machines (grade D in P1) and the column is §9's `resaleEstimate` output, rounded.

  | Machine (§9 model) | Visible age / hours | Resale estimate (P1, grade D) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 30t excavator (`ex30`) | 24 yr / 21,500 h | ≈ $35k |
  | D6-class dozer with ripper (`dz6`, `hasRipper`) | 30 yr / 26,000 h | ≈ $51k (≈ $48k + the ripper's ≈ $3k) |
  | 950-class loader (`ld950`) | 22 yr / 18,000 h | ≈ $32k |
  | Small trommel (`tr50`, rated 50 bcy/hr) with sluice run | 18 yr | ≈ $10k |
  | 6" diesel pump (`pmp6`) | 12 yr | ≈ $6k |
  | 100 kW generator (`gen100`) | 15 yr / 30,000 h | ≈ $4k |
  | ¾-ton pickup (`pickup`) | 14 yr | ≈ $9k |
  | 8-person camp, basic tier (`campT8`) | 15 yr | ≈ $5k |
  | **Total** | | **≈ $152k** |

  **Hidden condition (P3):** each component's health is `0.25 + 0.35·Beta(2,2)` (range 0.25–0.60, mean 0.425), and one random machine gets one "parked-broken" component at 0.10–0.20. **P1 stub:** the fleet is grade D (`fleet.p1GradeMaintMult[D]` 1.60, `fleet.p1GradeRateMult[D]` 0.85; the older `fleet.p1Inherited*Mult` keys alias grade D).
- **Debt.** The family operation's bank note, assumed at transfer: $320,000 at 8.5% fixed, 84 months, secured by the claims and fleet. It pays on §11's generalized seasonal schedule (`game.inheritor.noteSchedule` = `'seasonal'`): June–November only, $10,281.75 per pay month (≈ $61.7k/yr), interest accruing through the skipped months, nothing due December–May, so the first payment falls in week 26 of year 1 after the first cleanups. An LLC or corp owner must sign a full PG (P4). Fuel vendor AP of $12,000, due week 4.
- **Paper (P2+).** An **active** Plan of Operations on the group, last worked in 2024 (three seasons ago), that transfers to the company at setup (§6 records the operator change). Its disturbance cap is the inherited open acres rounded up plus `game.inheritor.planHeadroomAcres` = 5. It is **under-bonded**: the family's $6,000 cash bond (`cash.restricted.bond`) sits far below §6's current bond estimate, so §6 opens a bond-review obligation in week 1 and blocks mechanized work (`BOND_INSUFFICIENT`) until the top-up is posted (cash or surety). The inherited open acres §3 generated (typically 7–9: the family's 5–7 mined acres plus the two pre-stripped blocks; `disturbanceOrigin = 'inherited'`) are booked as ARO at §6's contractor estimate (≈ $6k/acre). Regulator standing starts at 55 (§6 allows 50–65 for a family record).
- **People.** One former hand appears as a candidate in week 1 asking for $34/hr. P1: attributes shown exactly (§8 shows true attributes until résumés arrive in P3). P3+: a 60–80 operator per résumé, true attributes hidden per §8.

### 1.9 The owner as a person

```ts
interface Owner {
  name: string;
  personalCash: Cents;                  // = §11 owner book `own.cash`; never mixed with company accounts
  personalCreditScore: number;          // 300–850, scored by §11
  personalDebt: Cents;                  // = `own.personalDebt`: card balance when living costs exceed personal cash (P4)
  guaranteeDueCents: Cents;             // = `own.guaranteeDue`: called guarantees not yet paid (§11 11.16)
  taxDueCents: Cents;                   // = `own.taxDue`: owner tax and TFRP assessments not yet paid (§11)
  guarantees: Guarantee[];              // §11 and §6 (surety indemnity) create; entity rules in 1.6
  salaryPerWeek: Cents;                 // corp: W-2 wage via payroll; soleProp/LLC: scheduled draw
  ownerLoanToCompany: Cents;            // = `own.loanToCompany`; company side `debt.ownerLoan` (subordinated)
  assignment: OwnerAssignment;
  pendingAssignment: OwnerAssignment | null;   // applied in the next step 7
  deskDaysUsedThisWeek: number;         // 1.9 owner time; reset in step 7
  injuredUntilTurn: number | null;
}
interface Guarantee { loanId: Id; kind: 'full' | 'limited' | 'indemnity'; capCents: Cents | null; releasedTurn: number | null }
type OwnerAssignment =
  | { kind: 'office' }                                         // default; full desk capacity
  | { kind: 'foreman'; claimId: Id }                           // owner runs this claim (counts as its foreman, §8)
  | { kind: 'operator'; claimId: Id; machineId: Id }           // runs a machine and is the claim's foreman at skill −15 for foreman tasks
  | { kind: 'shop'; mode: 'site'; claimId: Id }               // mechanic background only: that claim's site shop
  | { kind: 'shop'; mode: 'pool'; districtId: Id }             //   or the district pool (P3); §8's shop modes (D-8.50), §9 9.8.6
  | { kind: 'fieldGeologist'; programId: Id };                 // geologist background only
```

- **Owner's labor.** The owner has one assignment per week; a change takes effect at the next step 7. Owner skill in a field role comes from 1.7; owner safety is 60 for §8's injury rolls. As foreman (or as operator, who is also that claim's foreman), the owner covers **one** active claim and up to `staff.foremanMaxLines` (2) of its plant lines; a third line needs a second foreman or a lead hand (§8). Activating a plan on any claim requires a hired foreman or the owner assigned to that claim (§7/§8 `FOREMAN_REQUIRED`), **unless** the claim qualifies for §8's small-crew rule: its crew, excluding the owner, is at most `staff.smallCrewMaxNoForeman` (3), and it runs a single shift and one plant line. Such a claim runs with no foreman at efficiency `ops.noForemanEfficiency` (0.92, §7) and incident odds × `staff.noForemanIncidentMult` (1.15, §8). Reassigning the owner away leaves a claim that needs a foreman without one from the next step 7, and its plan stands down (§8 D-8.18), so alternating the owner between two claims that need a foreman runs neither. A skill-40 owner-foreman (F = 0.85 + 0.15 × 0.40 = 0.91, §7) is slightly less efficient than no foreman on a small crew, but avoids the incident multiplier and the one-shift, one-line limits; an Operator owner (F 0.9775) is clearly better (1.21). A geologist owner assigned foreman or operator on claim C also supervises one §4 program on C without a separate `fieldGeologist` assignment (§4 4.13, §8). Field roles work 60 h/week under §8's fatigue and injury rules; a fatal injury roll on the owner becomes serious (§8 D-8.21). An injured owner reverts to `office` until `injuredUntilTurn`. The owner is excluded from workers' comp in every entity (§11 D-11.27): medical costs of an owner injury are charged to the owner book by severity (§8 owns severity). *Trade-off:* field labor saves a salary but ties the owner to one place.
- **Owner time.** Desk work is measured in owner desk days. Capacity: `office` = `game.owner.deskDaysOffice` (5) per week; any field assignment = `game.owner.deskDaysField` (2.5), which is §6's "0.5 desk-week" for permit preparation. Tasks that cost desk days: §3 site visits and §4 pan surveys (`geology.siteVisit.days` 2 / 3 / 4 / 4 by access; their only owner error is `OWNER_INJURED`), §4 records reviews (3) and seller-data audits, §6 owner-prepared applications (desk-weeks), and §5 closings that need the owner on site (§5 sets days). A task that does not fit this week's remaining capacity carries into next week. If the player forces it now (`ownerTime: 'now'` on the action), each excess day is taken from field time: §8 cuts the owner's `availableFraction` by 1/6 per day for that week, so the claim the owner runs loses foreman presence. `ownerDeskDays(state)` returns `{ capacity, used, queued, forcedThisWeek }` (days taken from field time with `ownerTime: 'now'`) for the UI and for §8's owner `availableFraction`.
- **Living costs (P4).** `game.ownerLivingCostPerWeek` = $900 (× cpiIndex) leaves personal cash each week. When personal cash runs out, it accrues to `personalDebt` at `game.ownerPersonalDebtApr` = 24% and damages personal credit (§11). *Trade-off:* paying yourself drains the company in spring; not paying yourself burns savings and credit.
- **Salary and draws.** In a corp, salary is a deductible wage and draws are dividends. In a sole prop or LLC, both are draws: not deductible, with profit taxed to the owner anyway (§11). Pass-through tax is the owner's: by default §11 makes automatic tax distributions in each estimate week (pro rata with any equity holder), and they are blocked at distress ≥ 3 like any draw. Draws are blocked while the company is at distress stage ≥ 3 "missed payroll" (`DISTRESS_BLOCKED`), at stage 6 for everything, by investor stance and unpaid pref (1.8.1), and by a rescue partner's return condition. Draws within 13 weeks before the bankruptcy petition are clawed back from personal cash at liquidation (D-1.59).
- **In reorganization (P4+).** While a §11 case is open, the owner's salary and draws together are capped at the living allowance, `game.ownerLivingCostPerWeek` × cpiIndex per week, as the court would allow (D-1.59). `owner/setSalary` and `owner/draw` above it fail with `REORG_DRAW_LIMIT`; a salary set above it before the filing is paid only up to it from the next step 14. The allowance is compensation, not a distribution, so no equity holder receives a pro-rata share; for a corp it stays a payroll wage. It replaces the stage-3 block while the case is open: the cap already stops the owner draining the company, and a court allows a debtor's owner a living wage. Automatic tax distributions continue, as a court usually approves for a pass-through owner taxed on the company's profit. Owner injections stay allowed (new money is welcome); owner-loan repayments, entity conversion and sponsorship are refused (`REORG_OPEN`) until the plan completes.
- **Injections.** The owner may put personal cash in as equity (`eq.ownerCapital`) or as an owner loan (`debt.ownerLoan`, subordinated, `game.ownerLoanRate` 6%). Owners with an equity holder can only lend, because new equity would change the cap table. *Trade-off:* an injection saves the company, but personal cash is what survives a liquidation.
- **Personal credit inputs (for §11):** the starting score (1.8), personal debt utilization and lateness, company lateness (sole prop only), guarantees called and unpaid, repossessions on guaranteed loans, TFRP liens, liquidation (sole prop personal; LLC/corp only through unpaid guarantees), a reorganization filing (the company file always; the owner file takes the full bankruptcy mark as debtor or filing guarantor, else §11's affiliate mark), and time.

### 1.10 Modes and goal scenarios

- **Sandbox.** No end date. The run ends at liquidation, at an investor ouster, or when the player retires (`game/retire`), which ends the run with the report and a final net worth. A reorganization (1.14) does not end it.
- **Scenarios** are data in `data/scenarios/`. A scenario fixes the start type (and optionally the background, entity, world templates, a fixed seed, and tuning overrides). The player always picks difficulty, and the score multiplier records it. Worlds are random unless `fixedSeed` is set. Any scenario ends in a loss on liquidation (including a reorganization that converts) or ouster.
- **Reorganization in every mode** (owner ruling 2026-10-05, D-1.57). A reorganization is allowed in the sandbox and in every scenario. A run that has filed for reorganization can still complete a goal scenario, but its medal is capped at **silver** (`game.scenario.reorgMedalCap`): a win in the gold window earns silver, and a win in the silver or bronze window earns that medal. The cap holds once the first filing is seen (`company.scenario.reorgFiledTurn`), even after the plan completes.

```ts
interface ScenarioDef {
  id: ScenarioId; name: string; blurb: string;
  start: StartType; backedTerms?: 'equity' | 'royalty' | 'player';
  allowedBackgrounds?: OwnerBackground[]; allowedEntities?: EntityType[];
  world: { districtTemplates: RegionTemplateId[]; fixedSeed?: string };
  tuningOverrides?: Partial<Record<TuningKey, number>>;
  win: ScenarioCondition[];                 // all must hold at one evaluation point
  deadline: { year: number; week: 52 };
  medals: { gold: { byYear: number }; silver: { byYear: number }; bronze?: { byYear: number } };
}
interface ScenarioCondition {
  metric: 'cumFineOzRecovered' | 'interestBearingDebt' | 'yearFineOzRecovered' | 'ownerNetWorthReal' | 'distressStage';
  op: '>=' | '<=' | '=='; value: number; evaluate: 'weekly' | 'yearEnd';
}
```

| Scenario | Start | Win | Deadline | Medals | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **First Thousand Ounces** | Bootstrapper | `cumFineOzRecovered ≥ 1,000` (weekly) | end of year 3 | gold ≤ yr 2, silver ≤ yr 3 | Gross recovered fine oz from operated claims, before in-kind royalties. A typical northern op makes 300–700 oz/yr. |
| **Debt-Free by Year 5** | Inheritor | At a year-end: `interestBearingDebt == 0` AND `yearFineOzRecovered ≥ 200` AND `distressStage == 0` | end of year 5 | gold ≤ yr 3, silver ≤ yr 4, bronze ≤ yr 5 | Debt counts loans, finance leases, revolver, cards, hard money, and gold loans. It excludes AP within terms, accruals, ARO, operating leases, and royalties. The production test stops "sell everything" wins. |
| **Gold Baron** | Backed (player picks terms) | `ownerNetWorthReal ≥ $5,000,000` at a year-end | end of year 8 | gold ≤ yr 5, silver ≤ yr 7, bronze ≤ yr 8 | Real = nominal ÷ cpiIndex. Starting owner NW is $250k. |

**Metric definitions** (all from player-visible state):
- `cumFineOzRecovered` / `yearFineOzRecovered`: Σ over cleanups of raw oz weighed × fineness, plus §10 lots with `source: 'sample'` (§4 sample programs, which bypass §7) counted when the lot is created at raw oz × the player's estimated fineness. Fineness is the lot's assay once assayed and the player's estimate until then (re-evaluated when the assay lands). The true fineness is never read before the assay. Counts gross production before in-kind interests. §7 records the cleanup part per cleanup; §1 reads sample lots from §10.
- `interestBearingDebt`: Σ `debt.*` (except `debt.ownerLoan`), `lease.*` (finance leases), `cc.cards`, and gold loans, in cents.
- `ownerNetWorthReal`: `ownerNWReal` from 1.13.
- `distressStage`: §11's stage number (0–7). A liquidation ends the run before any evaluation, so 7 is seen only while a reorganization case is filed and not yet confirmed (§11: stage 7, form `reorganization`). From confirmation the ladder is evaluated again, but the plan notes are `debt.*` and count in `interestBearingDebt`, so the debt-free goal cannot be met until the plan is paid off.

**Worked example (medal cap).** A Bootstrapper in *First Thousand Ounces* files for reorganization in year 1 week 44, confirms its plan in year 2 week 5, and reaches 1,000 fine oz in year 2 week 38. The win falls in the gold window (≤ year 2), so it would earn gold; the cap makes it **silver**. The run then ends as `won`, and the end report shows the case beside the medal. The same run reaching 1,000 oz in year 3 week 20 earns silver either way.

Each phase adds scenarios as data. The schema supports others ("Comeback": distressed start; "Desert Rat": arid-only).

### 1.11 Difficulty

The brief scales "ground quality honesty, lender patience, and event severity". §1 reads the first as the honesty of the information about the ground, not ground quality itself: **true geology priors, including the ground on offer, are identical across difficulties** (§3 D-3.18 agrees; owner ruling 2026-10-05 confirmed this reading, OQ-1.3). §1 owns this table, and it lists **every** difficulty-scaled key in any section's tuning: a key that is not here is not difficulty-scaled. Where an implementing section published a key and its values first, the table adopts them so the two never disagree (D-1.32, D-1.44). All values resolve once at `newGame` (§2.10).

| Knob | Key (owner §) | Easy | Standard | Hard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Information honesty** | | | | |
| Seller honesty mix accurate/optimistic/cherry-picked/fraudulent | `geology.seller.honestyMix` (§3) | .55/.30/.12/.03 | .35/.35/.22/.08 | .20/.35/.30/.15 |
| Detecting a seller's tells | `geology.seller.tellDetect` multiplier (§3) | × 1.15 | × 1.00 | × 0.85 |
| Seller asking markup over claimed value | `land.askMarkup` (§5) | 0.25 | 0.30 | 0.35 |
| Hidden title defects (× each channel's defect rate) | `land.titleDefectRateMult` (§5) | 0.6 | 1.0 | 1.4 |
| Records-review find odds (× item weights) | `geology.recordsFindMult` (§4) | 1.0 | 1.0 | 0.9 |

| Private used-iron lemon share | `fleet.privateLemonShare` (§9) | 0.10 | 0.20 | 0.30 |

| **Counterparty patience (lenders, landlords, sellers)** | | | | |
| Late-fee grace: shifts each lender's base grace by (value − 2) weeks (R5: late fee after 10–15 days) | `finance.paymentGraceWeeks` (§11 D-11.14) | 3 | 2 | 1 |

Notes:
- Inspection *detection* has no separate knob: §6 detects through inspections and complaints, both already scaled.
- §14's blast misfire and flyrock odds scale only through `events.severityMult`, and its project loan only through §11's lender-patience knobs above; neither has a knob of its own.
- `ops.freezeDamageProb` (§7) is **not** difficulty-scaled (§7 marks it Diff = no): freeze damage is a risk the player controls by winterizing, and `fleet.failureHazardMult` already scales breakdown odds (D-1.44). `ops.freezeDamageProbMult` stays an event hook only.
- The distress watch window is §11's key, not a UI setting: §13's projected-negative alert and §2.7's run stop read `finance.distress.watchWeeks` (D-1.44).
- The cash multipliers are narrow on purpose. At 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.75 the preflight model found Hard *safer* than Standard for the cautious Bootstrapper (B2 64 / 64 / 88), because less cash bought a smaller, safer fleet (D-1.43). BALANCE O-05 requires monotone ordering with ≥ 8-point S2 steps (checkable in P6).

### 1.12 Reputation (0–100)

Reputation is the company's standing with sellers, workers, vendors, and the community. It is separate from `regulatorStanding` (§6), `safetyRecord` (§8), and credit (§11). The score is fully visible, and its explain tree lists the last 52 weeks of entries.

```
R_{t+1} = clamp(50 + (R_t − 50)·(1 − game.reputation.decayPerWeek) + Σ deltas_t, 0, 100)     // decay 0.005 ⇒ half-life ≈ 139 weeks
other sections report: recordReputation(state, kind, ref) → appended to company.reputation.pending, summed in step 16a
caps: each capped kind tracks capsUsedThisYear[kind]; a delta that would exceed its cap is truncated; caps reset in week 1
```

Deltas recorded during week t take effect in step 16a and are read by other systems from week t+1. A one-week lag is harmless and keeps the order of steps 3–14 free of circular dependencies.

| Input (`game.reputation.delta.*`) | Δ | Cap | Reported by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Missed payroll (any employee unpaid) / partial payroll | −8 / −4 | per week | §11 |
| Vendor bill > 30 days late / vendor stop-supply | −1 each / −3 | −4/month (late bills) | §11 |
| Loan default notice / repossession | −6 / −8 | — | §11 |
| Reorganization filed (`reorgFiled`) / plan completed and debts discharged (`reorgCompleted`) | −10 / +3 | — | §11 |
| Season with ≥ 100 fine oz recovered / record production year | +3 / +2 | per year | §1 (week 52) |
| In-kind royalty paid in full at a cleanup / missed advance royalty / lease terminated for default (incl. lessee-caused forfeiture) | +0.5 / −5 / −8 | +3/yr (royalties) | §5 |
| Deal closed / accepted offer then failed to close (incl. auction non-payment) / walked out after an insulting offer (`lowballWalk`) | +1 / −5 / −0.5 | +3/yr (deals) | §5 |
| Acre reclaimed / claim abandoned unreclaimed / bond forfeited | +0.5 / −10 / −8 | +4/yr (reclamation) | §6 |
| Serious injury / fatality | −3 / −10 | — | §8 |
| Violation (S&S or stop-work) | −1 (−2 / −4) | — | §6 |
| Season bonuses paid in full / ≥ 3 firings in one operating week | +1 / −2 | — | §8 |
| Season bonus cut mid-season (`staff.bonusCutMidSeason`) / layoff without the pro-rata bonus (`staff.layoffWithoutProRata`, per employee) | −1 / −1 each | −3/yr (layoffs) | §8 |
| Community complaint answered / ignored / reaching the media | +1 / −1 / −3 | +2/yr (answered) | §12 (`event.complaintAnswered`, `event.complaintIgnored`, `event.mediaStory`) |
| Concealment caught (e.g. a cultural find) / crew replaced after a walkout | −15 / −3 | — | §12 (`event.concealmentCaught`, `event.crewReplaced`) |
| Other §12 event outcomes | as §12's table, within ±15 per event | — | §12 (`event.<id>.<outcome>`) |
| Community sponsorship (`community/sponsor`, $5k per point) | +1 | +2/yr | §1 |

| Effect | Formula (key, owner §) |
|---|---|
| Negotiation acceptance | +`land.reputationLogitPerPoint` (0.02) × (R − 50) logits (§5). Below R 20 (`land.repRefuseBelow`), estates and JV partners refuse to deal. JV proposals need R ≥ 55 (`land.jvMinReputation`). |
| Lessor credence in royalty offers | q = clamp(0.35 + 0.25·(R − 50)/50, 0.10, 0.70) (§5 5.11) |
| Off-market first look (P5) | R ≥ 70 (`land.firstLookMinRep`): `land.firstLookShare` 0.15 of new private listings reach the player `land.firstLookWeeks` (2) weeks before public (§5 owns listing life and ships it in P5) |
| Labor pool and wage asks | pool × (0.8 + 0.4·R/100); wage ask × (1.04 − 0.08·R/100) (§8) |
| Vendor credit limits | × (0.5 + R/100) (§11) |
| Equity partners | angels need R ≥ 40 (§11 11.13) |
| Local buyer discount | −1 point at R ≥ 70, +1 point below 30 (§10 10.10) |
| Environmental complaints | §6 complaint detection: an always-on multiplier on `permits.complaintRateMult` of (1.4 − 0.8·R/100); §12 `envComplaint` weight × (1.5 − R/100) |
| Crew credibility | §12 walkout "promise to pay" succeeds with p = 0.3 + 0.5·R/100 |
| Competitor JV/merger approaches | only if R ≥ 60 (§12) |

### 1.13 Net worth for scoring

**Rule: scoring uses only player-visible marks.** The same selector feeds the UI, the bots, the scenarios, and the end report. §11 implements `netWorth(state, 'scoring')` exactly as follows (§11 11.20 places every account).

```
companyNW = cash.operating + cash.reserve + cash.restricted.* + deposits.bonds + prepaid
          + ar.refinery + ar.insurance + ar.other                               // at settlement value
          + Σ unsold lots: fineOzEst × netSalePerFineOz(state, lot)
                // §10 best channel usable now, net of fees/discount, at this week's spot;
                // fineness = assay if assayed, else the player's estimate; pledged lots included
          + metalAccountValueForScoring(state)                // §10: Σ account fine oz × spot × (1 − market.metalAccount.bidSpread); pledged oz included
          + inv.parts × game.nw.partsResaleFactor (0.6) + inv.fuel (at cost)
          + Σ owned / financed / finance-leased machines: resaleEstimate(machine)   // §9: model, age, hours, KNOWN condition midpoint
          + mineral.properties − mineral.accumDepletion       // claims at cost basis (purchase price, staking costs, estate appraisal)
          − ( ap.* + accrued.* + cc.cards + Σ debt.* principal (incl. debt.ownerLoan) + Σ lease.* (finance leases)
              + liab.reclamation (ARO at §6's real-cost estimate, not bond face) + liab.suretyIndemnity + liab.agencyJudgment
              + liab.forwardDelivery + liab.deliveryArrears + Σ deferred.revenue.*
              + forwardMtmLossForScoring(state) )             // §10: Σ max(0, spot − forwardPrice) × undelivered oz
ownerShare  = companyNW − Σ_a claim_a                        // equity waterfall, 1.8.1; = companyNW with no equity holder
ownerNW     = ownerShare + own.cash − own.personalDebt − own.guaranteeDue − own.taxDue + own.loanToCompany
ownerNWReal = ownerNW / cpiIndex                              // scenarios and the end report use real
```

Operating-lease commitments are excluded (off balance sheet). Contingent guarantees are not subtracted until a demand exists; they show as a memo line.

**In reorganization (P4+; D-1.60).** While a case is open, pre-filing debts stay in the accounts above at their allowed amounts, and the case's filing, attorney and trustee costs accrue like any bill. Only at the discharge (§11 sets when: at confirmation of a consensual plan, at completion of a non-consensual one) are the discharged claims replaced by what the confirmed plan still has to pay, with the difference booked as a gain. So filing alone never raises the score, and an owner who retires before the discharge is scored with the full debts still on the books. The owner loan is a company debt and an owner asset, so it nets to zero for a company with no equity holder; with one, it is senior to the holders' claims.

**Why hidden truth is never used:**
1. A score must be explainable by clicking it. Marking a claim at its true value would leak its geology through the drill-down.
2. Bots may only use visible state (§2.12), and scoring must match what they optimize.
3. Value the player never proved or realized should not count. Conservative marks reward turning ground into gold, or selling proven ground at a market price.

**Cost:** proving a great claim adds nothing to the score until it is mined or sold. The UI therefore also shows an *informational* "appraised net worth": claims at the player's own P50 value (§4/§5). It is never used for scoring.

**Worked example.** A Bootstrapper ($400k start) at year-1 end holds $292k cash; 18 estimated fine oz in camp × $3,667 local-buyer net (§10: 10% discount on the buyer's ≈ 3% low fineness read, 0.873 × $4,200) = $66k; no metal account; fleet resale $231k (bought for $268k at §9's used prices); one claim at cost $15k; ARO $9k and AP $11k; personal cash $120k (salary draws covered living costs). companyNW = 292 + 66 + 231 + 15 − 9 − 11 = $584k. ownerNW = $704k. Real at cpiIndex 1.03: $683k, up from $520k. A lot large enough for a refinery's minimum would be marked at the refinery net instead (§10).

### 1.14 Losing, liquidation, reorganization, and the end-of-run report

The ladder's mechanics, thresholds, and counter-moves belong to §11, including the whole reorganization case. This is a summary.

| Stage | Trigger (summary) | What the player can do |
|---|---|---|
| 0 Watch | §11's 13-week forecast P50 goes negative within `finance.distress.watchWeeks` (4 on standard; 6 / 4 / 3 by difficulty, 1.11; + §8 controller bonus), or P10 within 2 (alert) | Sell gold, delay capex, draw the line, cut hours, ask for a seasonal schedule, inject |
| 1 Late vendors | Any vendor bill ≥ 1 week past due | Pay down the oldest; payment plan; route to a card; pay COD. Stop-supply (fuel and parts) at 4 weeks. |
| 2 Missed loan / lease payment | Any loan or lease late or delinquent | Late fees; credit marks at 4 weeks. Pay within grace; hard-money refinance; sell the collateral; surrender. |
| 3 Missed payroll | Net payroll short in the last 4 weeks, or a trust deposit ≥ 1 week late | Morale collapse, quits, wage claims, regulator notice, reputation −8. Draws blocked; rescue partner offered. Owner injection, layoffs, idling. |
| 4 Default | A loan in default, an uncured covenant default, or an MCA default | Default interest, cross-default, forbearance offers. Cure, restructure (§5 negotiation, P5), asset sales, rescue partner. |
| 5 Repossession | A repossession scheduled or executed in the last 13 weeks | Collateral is seized and auctioned; the deficiency remains (a guarantee demand if guaranteed). Sell first at a better price. |
| 6 Forced sales / workout | Accelerated debt unpaid 4 weeks after the notice | Lender-driven sales of gold, claims and iron; no new debt; capex and draws blocked |
| 7 Bankruptcy: reorganization (Chapter 11 Subchapter V; P4+) | The player files `finance/fileReorganization` while eligible: distress stage ≥ 2, total non-contingent liquidated debts ≤ `finance.reorg.debtLimitUsd` ($3,424,000 × cpiIndex), and no earlier filing within `finance.reorg.cooldownWeeks` (416, eight years). When an involuntary trigger fires, an eligible company gets a blocking decision (`finance.involuntaryPetition`) to convert the creditors' liquidation petition into a reorganization instead (as of right, 11 U.S.C. §706(a)); §11's `nextTrigger` shows the trigger coming. An LLC or corp owner may join as guarantor (1.6). | **The run continues.** The automatic stay stops repossession, collection and lender default actions. A plan is due within `finance.reorg.planDueWeeks` (13); it runs `finance.reorg.planWeeksMin`–`Max` (156–260 weeks) and pays projected disposable income; secured creditors keep their liens and get at least collateral value; unsecured creditors share disposable income and get at least what a liquidation would pay them; the owner keeps the equity. Costs ≈ `finance.reorg.filingCostUsd` ($40,000 × cpiIndex, of which a $15,000 retainer is paid at filing) plus trustee fees ≈ 3% of plan payments; credit marks on the company and owner files; new debt only with court approval (DIP financing at hard-money terms); vendors on COD; reputation −10 (1.12); a crew morale hit (§11 through §8's morale); owner pay capped at the living allowance (1.9); investors' stance drops (1.8.1). Confirmation needs §11's deterministic feasibility and best-interest tests on the player's own visible forecast; a creditor vote (stream `finance-reorg`) then decides whether it is consensual (discharge at confirmation) or a cram-down (the court fixes a five-year plan; discharge at completion). |
| 7 Bankruptcy: liquidation (Chapter 7) | The player files `owner/fileBankruptcy` (stage ≥ 2, or at any time during a reorganization case, which converts it); involuntary: 3 consecutive short payroll runs, or stage ≥ 4 for 13 weeks while distressed asset value is below zero; or a reorganization converts: no plan filed within 13 weeks, confirmation denied twice, `finance.reorg.missedPaymentsToConvert` (2) missed plan payments within 52 weeks (1 while a hostile equity holder presses its motion, 1.8.1), or a payroll collapse during the case (§11). An ineligible company's only filing is liquidation, and an involuntary trigger liquidates it at once. | **Game over.** Final settlement at distressed marks (§11); entity rules (1.6) settle personal fallout. |

- **P1 simple form (§11).** Any failed payment opens an insolvency counter. It clears when every arrear is paid. After `finance.p1InsolvencyGraceWeeks` consecutive weeks open, the company is liquidated (game over): everything company-side is lost and the owner keeps personal cash. The UI shows "net cash" = cash − arrears as the number below zero. **P1 levers** (§11 11.24 lists them on the counter; §13 shows them on the health tile): sell gold to the local buyer; sell iron to a dealer at 0.80 × resale, instantly (§9); sell a claim by quick sale at `land.quickSaleFrac` 0.6 × the visible buyer valuation, closing next week, or surrender a lease and forfeit its advance (§5); inject personal cash (1.9); cut hours or stand a claim down (§7). Negotiation, forbearance and the rescue partner arrive in P4–P5. The P1 counter has no reorganization path: in P1–P3 the counter's end is a liquidation.
- **Reorganization is a lifeline, not a reset** (owner ruling 2026-10-05; D-11.17 and its §11 subsection own the mechanics). It is offered in every mode from P4. For three to five years the company works for its creditors: every dollar of projected disposable income goes into the plan, the owner draws only the living allowance, credit is closed except by court order, and one bad season can still convert the case to liquidation. In a goal scenario it costs the gold medal (1.10). For the simulator a filing counts as a failure of the survival window it falls in (BALANCE §5.1–5.2, D-1.49), and the run keeps being measured afterwards.
- **Run ends:** liquidation (loss: filed, involuntary, a converted reorganization, or the P1–P3 counter), investor ouster (loss), scenario deadline missed (loss), scenario forfeited (loss), scenario win, retirement (sandbox). A reorganization alone never ends a run: `runStatus` stays `'active'` throughout the case. After the report the save becomes read-only. A "continue in sandbox" option is offered after a scenario *win* only.

**End-of-run report** (`endReport(state)` returns these fields once `runStatus ≠ 'active'`; §13 renders it):
- Outcome (with `endReason` and, for a liquidation, how it came: filed, involuntary, converted from reorganization, or the P1–P3 insolvency counter), dates, seed (with action-log export for replay); score = ownerNWReal × `game.scoreMult`, and the medal, marked "capped at silver" when a reorganization capped it.
- Charts: owner and company NW by week; cash; production by year (raw and fine oz); cash and all-in cost per oz by year. Claims table: how acquired, cost, ounces, per-claim P&L.
- **Reorganization** (when any case was filed; from §11's case record): filing week and debts at filing against the limit; plan length, scheduled payments and the share promised to unsecured creditors; confirmation week and whether it was consensual; payments made and missed; outcome (completed and discharged, converted, or still open when the run ended); its total cost (filing, attorney, trustee); the amount discharged; the investors' stance path through the case.
- **The reveal:** each claim's true block grades next to the player's final estimate and the seller's claims, labeled with the seller's honesty type. Inherited equipment's true condition history (P3+). Allowed because the run is over.
- Biggest decisions timeline: purchases, loans, hires, and sales above $50k, plus distress stages entered, and any reorganization filing, confirmation, missed plan payment and conversion.
- Rule-based "lessons", e.g. "Bought clm_000042 on seller data only (seller was *cherry-picked*)", "Plant idle 31% of season 2: haul-limited", "Filed for reorganization in year 2 with $1.1M of debt; the plan paid unsecured creditors 34%".

### 1.15 First-hour onboarding (first ten turns)

The tutorial is optional and every prompt reacts to real state (§13 owns the UI and implements these beats as its coach steps). P1 includes the arid district, so a January start can complete a full loop in about ten weeks while the north is frozen. The default path is a Bootstrapper at standard difficulty. The "Week" column is the turn on which the player sees and does each thing; results of an advance appear on the next turn.

| Week | The player sees | The player does | Teaches |
|---|---|---|---|
| Setup | Wizard with a one-line trade-off per choice; the summary panel shows cash, credit, assets and debts | Mode; difficulty; names; entity; background; start | Setup is a bet |
| 1 | Welcome letter (start-specific). Season forecast card per district. Runway "≈ N weeks of overhead". | Opens the claims market; filters to arid; pins 3 listings, noting each one's water source (spring, well potential, none); reads a seller history tagged *unverified* | Seller data is not evidence; water decides the plant |
| 2 | Listing detail: visible facts, asking terms, an estimate built from the district prior only | Books site visits with panning on 2 listings (§3/§4; ≈ $1–2k and 4 owner desk days, so the owner stays in `office`) and a records review on the better one (≈ $2–4k, results in 2 weeks) | Paying for information; owner time |
| 3 | Pan results (presence and size hints, not grade); the estimate barely moves | Leases the better claim at a low advance (P1: accept or walk) | Cheap evidence is weak; lease-then-test is the careful play (§4 D-4.29) |
| 4 | Records findings (old workings, past production filings). Equipment market (P1 cash catalog) and capacity preview, which flags water | Orders 4 contractor test pits on the leased claim (≈ $1,900 each at the arid rate, 1-week lead, §4); buys an excavator, a plant matched to the claim's water (a dry-wash plant on a dry claim; a small trommel with pump and full recycle where there is a spring or a proven well), a generator and a pickup; hires an operator and a laborer; assigns the owner as foreman (or operator) on the claim. The coach shows the alternative: a crew this small may run with no foreman (§8 small-crew rule: efficiency 0.92, one shift and one plant line only, incident odds × 1.15) while the owner keeps a full office week; above three crew a plan with no foreman cannot activate (`FOREMAN_REQUIRED`) | Fleet matching; owner labor |
| 5 | Pit results: sample log and the P10/P50/P90 fan, much narrower; mine plan editor | Picks the cut from the block estimates; mobilizes the site (highway, 1 week); sets 6 d × 10 h and cleanup every 2 weeks | Estimates have ranges; the mine plan |
| 6 | Site ready; the plan preview for the first operating week | Advances one week (or sets "stop every cleanup") | Run to next decision |
| 7 | First week report: bcy washed, bottleneck, idle breakdown, costs | Reads why the plant idled (e.g. feed-limited) and fixes it: a used loader, or reassigning the owner | Bottlenecks; the capacity chain |
| 8 | First cleanup: raw oz, estimated fineness, lease royalty taken in kind | Sells to the local buyer, or holds | Raw vs fine; royalties |
| 9 | February month-end P&L; runway update | Reviews cash cost per ounce | Unit economics |
| 10 | Northern prompt: "Winter trail closes in ~3 weeks (wk 13)." Run-to-next-decision explained. | Decides whether to buy northern ground and mobilize now or wait; sets stop rules | Seasons and timing |

**From P2 the path needs operating authority.** A lease of raw ground has none, and a self-prepared plan takes 14–18 months (§6). §3.11 therefore guarantees, in each starting district, at least one listing with a true `planApproved` and its bond posted, offered as a lease or lease-with-option whose advance fits a Bootstrapper's cash (§5 terms; honest or cherry-picked holder), whose plan transfers within 4 weeks (§6.12). The coach filters week 1 to listings presenting a transferable plan (they cost more, §5). Because a listing's permit field is a seller statement (an optimistic seller may upgrade a notice to a plan), the coach routes the player through a records check (`permits/recordsCheck`: $250, 1 week, true permit status and bond, §6) in week 2 before committing in week 3. It also explains the alternative: a Notice bulk sample of under 590 bcy on raw ground while a plan is prepared. If the player leases raw ground anyway, the coach routes weeks 4–8 to the Notice and bulk sample, and the first full cleanup moves to the next season.

**Variants:**
- **Inheritor.** Week 1 brings the estate letter, the note statement (first payment in June), family records, and the fleet. Prompts: inspect the iron (mechanic background or a paid inspector, P3), review records now, plan the first cut on the two pre-stripped blocks so washing starts as soon as they thaw, test-pit the rest of the family ground after thaw, and (P2+) post the bond top-up before breakup.
- **Backed-equity.** Week 1 adds the investor's annual-plan request, a non-blocking decision whose default is the floor plan at week 4 (P4+).

### 1.17 Weekly resolution

| Step (§2.6) | What §1 does |
|---|---|
| `newGame` | Runs step 1 (a)–(f) below for turn 0 (year 1, week 1), because the first `advanceWeek` simulates turn 1 = week 2 (§2.6 turn semantics, D-2.13): the year-1 `DistrictYearSeason`, the week-1 forecasts, week-1 weather (initial state from `weather-init`, then the turn-0 `weather` draw) and the `accessOpen` cache; then the start-type setup (1.8) and, for Backed equity (P4+), year 1's annual-plan request (16b). |
| Action time | `investor/requestApproval` and `investor/submitPlan` resolve at once; their draw is keyed by (agreementId, subject, requestIndex), never by `actionSeq` (1.8.1). `owner/*` actions post through §11 immediately except assignment and salary changes. §11's `finance/fileReorganization` opens the case at action time; §1's effects on investors wait for the next 16b. |
| 1 Calendar & season | Per district in ID order: **(a)** week 1: roll `DistrictYearSeason` (1.4.3) and drop seasons older than last year. **(b)** Apply the §12 shifts recorded last week to unrevealed dates and recompute dependent dates (1.4.4). **(c)** Set `clock.phase[districtId]`; on a phase change mark the date revealed and raise a stop reason (§2.7). **(d)** On issue weeks (week 1 included), issue forecasts for unrevealed dates. **(e)** Draw `WeatherWeek` (temperature with the phase clamp, precipitation, flow, drought, fire) and update `WeatherState`, `lastWeather` and `sffLast4` (1.5). **(f)** Cache `accessOpen` for every mode this week (1.4.5). §8's week-1 experience increments and P1 recall rolls run after (f) (§2.6). |
| 7 Staff availability | Runs first in step 7, before §8 (7a–h) computes `availableFraction` and `foremanFor`: apply `pendingAssignment`; reset `deskDaysUsedThisWeek` and pull queued desk tasks; clear an expired owner injury. |
| 13 Compliance (§6 runs) | A missed Backed royalty minimum (obligation owner `'§1'`) is routed by §6 to `investor.onMinimumMissed`, which opens `minimumCure` (P4+; 1.8.1). |
| 14 Finance (§11 runs) | §11 posts owner salary/draws and automatic tax distributions with their pro-rata investor shares, living costs (P4), annual entity fees (week 13), pref accrual, and the royalty minimum top-up (week 52). While a reorganization case is open, owner salary and draws are paid only up to the living allowance and carry no pro-rata share (1.9). |
| 16 Wrap-up (§2) | **16a** apply reputation deltas and caps (1.12); week 52 adds the production inputs. **16b** first the reorganization effects (P4+; 1.8.1): the once-per-case filing penalty, staying an open redemption demand and clearing `minimumCure` when a case is first seen, extinguishing a stayed demand and resetting `hostileStreak` at confirmation; they run before the deadline checks, so a filing made at action time stays a redemption or cure deadline falling in the very next pipeline. Then investor check-ins (weeks 13/26/39/52; annual plan request in week 1; pref reminder in week 48) → decisions, with no redemption demand while a case is open; expire approval tokens; an uncured `minimumCure` past its deadline forecloses through §5 `land.transferToCreditor`. **16c** scenario evaluation (weekly metrics; year-end metrics in week 52); the first week a case is seen sets `scenario.reorgFiledTurn`, and a win's medal is capped at silver from then on (1.10). **16d** run-end check: §11's `distress.liquidation` from step 15 (cause `filed`, `involuntary`, `converted` from a reorganization, or `p1Counter`; it becomes `liquidationPath`), ouster deadline, scenario win/deadline → `runStatus` and `endReason` and the end report. An open reorganization case leaves `runStatus` `'active'`. Then (§2.6) the other sections' wrap-ups, §13 collation, the history snapshot (weekly owner and company NW) and stop reasons; collation follows 16d so a game over stops a run. |

### 1.18 Interfaces

**Provides:**
- **Types:** `SeasonPhase`, `DistrictYearSeason`, `SeasonForecast`, `WeatherWeek` (+`meanTempF`, `fireLevel`), `WeatherState`, `DistrictClimate`, `ClimateSlice`, `EntityType`, `OwnerBackground`, `StartType`, `Difficulty`, `NewGameSetup`, `Owner`, `OwnerAssignment`, `Guarantee`, `InvestorAgreement`, `ScenarioDef`, `ScenarioCondition`, and:

```ts
interface CompanySlice {
  name: string; entity: EntityType; pendingEntity: { to: EntityType; effectiveTurn: number } | null;
  background: OwnerBackground; start: StartType; difficulty: Difficulty; mode: 'sandbox' | 'scenario';
  owner: Owner;
  investors: Record<Id, InvestorAgreement>; investorIds: Id[];      // sorted; at most 2 equity + 1 Backed royalty
  reputation: { value: number; pending: ReputationEntry[]; log: ReputationEntry[] /* last 52 weeks */; capsUsedThisYear: Record<string, number> };
  regulatorStanding: number;            // 0–100, mechanics §6 (start 60; Inheritor 55)
  safetyRecord: SafetyRecord;           // §8
  scenario: { id: ScenarioId; medal: 'gold' | 'silver' | 'bronze' | null; metTurn: number | null;
              reorgFiledTurn: number | null } | null;   // first turn a §11 reorganization case was seen; caps the medal at silver
  runStatus: 'active' | 'won' | 'lost' | 'retired';     // an open reorganization case stays 'active'
  endReason: 'liquidated' | 'ousted' | 'deadline' | 'forfeited' | 'goal' | 'retired' | null;
  liquidationPath: 'filed' | 'involuntary' | 'converted' | 'p1Counter' | null;   // = §11 distress.liquidation.cause; set with
                                                                                 //   endReason 'liquidated' ('converted' = from reorganization)
}
interface ReputationEntry { turn: number; kind: string; delta: number; ref: Id | null }
```
