### 1.21 Balance levers and risks

- **Biggest levers:** first-season liquidity. A frozen first season with nothing stripped ahead runs 8–10 weeks of wages before the first gold, so starting cash and pre-stripped ground set survival far more than geology (preflight: raising the frozen dig multiplier 0.35 → 0.50 moves S2 < 2 points; pre-stripped ground moves it about 16 points (Inheritor, BALANCE §9.3 lever sweep)). Hence the Bootstrapper's $400k (at $250k the P1 cash curve bottomed at −$156k in week 26 against $120k of personal cash; S2 36–40%) and the Inheritor's $300k, two pre-stripped blocks and seasonal note (at $90k with nothing stripped, S2 0–3%; at $250k 46% in P1 and 30% under full rules; at $300k 60% and 43%, D-1.54). Then: season length (±1 week of mean freeze-up ≈ ±5% of northern annual output); investor terms (a 10% royalty makes marginal ground uneconomic; the pref sets equity drag); from P2, the Inheritor's bond top-up (a surety needs roughly $20–35k of collateral and premium at C/D tier); arid June F_m (steep: 0.48 → 0.8 and 0.53 → 3.2 level-3 weeks a year) and the heat curve's slope.
- **Background dominance.** In P1 the operator and geologist edges are fully live while mechanic, banker and landman run on stubs, so those two may lead early. Counter: the P1 stub sizes above, the simulator parity gate (±5 pp S2; ±7 pp interim in P1–P2), and §4's 1.15× net-worth cap on geologist starts (read on the owner-ahead share for a start whose median sits on the investor-waterfall floor, D-1.55). The mechanic's ×0.70 shop multiplier is worth +1 to +6 points of S2 in preflight; if O-07 fails for the Mechanic in P1, §9 raises `fleet.p1OwnerShopMaintMult` 0.70 → 0.80. **Small-crew rule** (owner ruling 2026-10-05; §8): a crew of three or fewer may run with no foreman at F = 0.92, a hair above the skill-40 owner-foreman's 0.91, so a desk-background owner on a small claim can stay in the office (5 desk days instead of 2.5) and give up almost nothing in efficiency, paying instead in incident odds (× 1.15) and the one-shift, one-line limit. That narrows the Operator's small-crew lead from ≈ 7.4% to ≈ 6.3% and widens the desk edges' room. The parity gate is measured with the bots' defaults (owner as foreman, D-2.32); the `smallCrewNoForeman` test bot measures the option. If it beats `cautious` on S2 and NW for the desk backgrounds, the lever is §7's `ops.noForemanEfficiency` (down toward 0.90, with the owner's approval, since the ruling set 0.92) before any background value.
- **Start dominance.** Backed money is the easiest path to a reference-size fleet; its counters are the payback/pref drag and the investor's teeth. Preflight found Backed starts never failing in two seasons (B2 100%): with that much cash only check-ins, redemption and ouster can end a run, and the model had no check-ins. 1.8.1's calibration (8–25% two-season loss for cautious Backed equity) gives the investor real teeth. Gate: each start type's `cautious`-bot S2 (BALANCE §5.2) within 10 pp of the 60–70% band, and year-5 owner-ahead shares (the share of games whose owner NW ends at or above its start, NW ratio ≥ 1.0, BALANCE §5.3) within 20 pp of each other (BALANCE O-06 b; 1.22). The median NW ratio is reported but does not gate: about half the Backed-equity games end on the investor-waterfall floor, where a median flips on a few seeds (D-1.55).
- **Exploits and counters:**

| Exploit | Counter |
|---|---|
| Drain the company into personal cash before bankruptcy | 13-week clawback from the petition date (a converted reorganization looks back from its own filing); draws blocked at distress ≥ 3; living allowance only during a reorganization case |
| LLC "walk away" | PGs required early; liquidation is game over regardless; personal NW is what scores; TFRP and unpaid wages stay personal; in a reorganization the guarantees stay enforceable unless the owner also files |
| Borrow unsecured, then reorganize to shed it | Debt limit ($3.424M × cpi) and an eight-year cooldown; ≈ $40k plus 3% trustee fees; every dollar of projected disposable income goes to creditors for 3–5 years; unsecured creditors get at least their liquidation value; credit closed except by court order; the score counts the full debts until discharge (1.13); no gold medal |
| File to dodge an equity investor's redemption demand | The filing penalty and the in-case check-in term keep the holder hostile, its conversion motion makes one missed plan payment fatal, pref keeps accruing, and nothing can be paid to equity until the plan completes; the Backed-loss calibration counts such a filing as a forced outcome (1.8.1) |
| Retire right after confirmation to bank a haircut | Discharged claims leave the books only at discharge, which for a non-consensual plan is its completion; until then they score at full value, so only a haircut the creditors voted for counts from confirmation (1.13) |
| Debt-free by liquidating | Production condition (≥ 200 fine oz in the evaluated year) |
| Equity drag dodged through salary | Salary cap; above it is a draw with pro-rata distributions |
| Re-rolling an investor approval every week, or by reloading | One request per subject per 4 weeks after a refusal; budgeted capex approved once a year; the draw is keyed by request index, so a reload returns the same answer (D-1.47) |
| Negative owner share from a preference larger than the company | The waterfall caps claims at company NW (1.8.1) |
| Inflate NW by buying iron | Resale estimate < price, so NW drops on purchase |
| Inflate NW with overpriced claims | Impossible without a counterparty; claims stay at cost |
| Reputation farming | Sponsorship capped at +2/yr; positive inputs capped |
| Seed scouting the weather | Accepted in sandbox; scenarios randomize seeds by default |
| Forecast gaming | Forecasts are calibrated; shifts are short-notice |
| Probing hidden season dates through validators or planning tools | `accessOpen` and `seasonPhase` answer for the current week only; planning uses `accessOutlook` / `phaseOutlook` from forecasts (1.4.5) |

- **Arid as easy mode.** Without heat and fire hour effects, an arid day-shift plan would lose only ≈ 0.9 effective weeks a year (≈ 4.1 with a flat heat factor). With the graded curve and recalibrated fire it loses ≈ 5.0 in P1 and ≈ 5.9 once precipitation hours ship in P5, concentrated in summer. The rest of the balance comes from economics: lower `gMed` (0.0062 vs 0.0095), finer gold, lower fineness (0.78 vs 0.86) and costly water (§3, §7). Hence §7 ships both hour effects in P1 (D-1.25). Watch the simulator's district-choice split for the `cautious` bot: if more than 70% of seeds pick arid, steepen the heat curve before touching grades.
- **Reorganization and the bankruptcy rate.** A reorganization keeps runs alive that would otherwise end, so it can lift late-window net worth for aggressive play without moving the survival gates (a filing fails B_N and S_N for its window, D-1.49). Watch BALANCE O-04: if `aggressive`'s year-5 p90 NW rises mainly through reorganized runs, the levers are §11's `finance.reorg.filingCostUsd`, the trustee rate and the plan length, then §1's `game.investor.reorgFilingPenalty`. The reorganization share is printed beside every survival figure (§2.12).
- **Entity choice.** The sole prop trades the shield for cheaper early credit (the owner's file as company payment history for 104 weeks, ≈ +15 U; D-1.36); gate: its `cautious`-bot S2 within 5 pp of the LLC's (1.22). If it dominates, shorten `finance.credit.solePropOwnerFileWeeks`; if it still trails, add the time-in-business stand-in (timePts uses `max(weeksInBusiness, 104)`, ≈ +30 U more). C-corp vs LLC is the live tax choice, driven by how much profit the player reinvests.

### 1.22 Tests

- **Calendar:** `weekOf(9,1) = 35`; `weekOf(12,30) = 52`; `weekOf(12,31) = 52`; `weekOf(1,1) = 1`; `weekOf(4,1) = 13`; `weekOf(10,31) = 44`; `weekOf(2,10) = 6`. Turn 0 → (1,1); turn 51 → (1,52); turn 52 → (2,1); displayYear(0) = 2027. `monthEndWeeks` matches `weekOf(month, lastDay)` for every month. `reportingMonth(5)` = January and `monthOfWeek(5)` = February; for every week, `reportingMonth(w)` = the month whose `monthEndWeeks` range contains w. `weekToDateRange(2, 9)` = Feb 26–Mar 4, 2028.
- **Season (property, 10k district-years):** northern operating length mean 22.0 ± 0.2, P5 ≥ 19, P95 ≤ 25, always within [17, 27]; `operatingStart > breakupWeek`; `freezeUp > operatingStart`; arid always operating, with monsoon start < end. Easy mean 22.5 ± 0.2, hard 21.6 ± 0.2. The eight season draws happen in the stated order for every template (golden test).
- **Forecasts:** coverage of [P10, P90] within [0.85, 0.98] at each issue; mean width non-increasing across issues; revealed dates stop updating; the worked example fixture (1.4.4) reproduces exactly; with `freezeUpMeanShift` = −0.5 the week-1 freeze-up P50 is 42 − 0.5 rounded = 42 (round half away from zero on 41.5).
- **Shifts:** a +2 breakup shift moves `operatingStartWeek` by +2 and re-applies the operating-week clamps; a shift never lands earlier than the firing week + 1.
- **Weather:** precip marginals per month within ±1.5% of the table over 10k years; phase clamps never violated; mean sff over operating weeks 1.00 ± 0.06 per template; the arid week-25 fixture gives `hot`, `dry`, fireDanger 0.73 (±0.01), level 2, sff 0.38 (±0.01), day-shift heat factor 0.68; northern fireLevel ≡ 0; arid level ≥ 3 weeks per year averaging 1.9 ± 0.3 and level 4 never from weather alone.
- **Access:** maintained seasonal road closed exactly in [breakupWeek − 1, operatingStartWeek + 1]; unmaintained open exactly in [operatingStartWeek + 2, freezeUpWeek + 1]; arid seasonal road closed the week after a storm and only then; `geology.access.closed` closes every mode; `access.airOpen = 0` closes air only.
- **No look-ahead (property):** scrambling the hidden drivers and unrevealed dates of a district (revealed dates kept) leaves every player-visible selector unchanged, including `accessOutlook`, `phaseOutlook`, `seasonForecast` and `validateAction` results for booked future actions.
- **Stream isolation:** perturbing the `weather` stream leaves season dates unchanged; perturbing `investor` leaves weather and §11 equity offers unchanged. **No reload re-roll:** an approval request refused at requestIndex k, then the save reloaded, a dummy action taken and the same request re-sent, gets the same refusal (the draw is keyed by agreementId, subject and requestIndex, not `actionSeq`).
- **Setup:** each start's opening balance sheet balances; owner NW = $520k (Bootstrapper) / $250k / $250k (Backed) and, for the Inheritor in P1, exactly $300k + Σ `resaleEstimate`(inherited fleet, grade D) + $120k − $332k + $40k (≈ $280k with §9's current curve; ≈ $238k in P2+ with the $6k bond and the ARO); Inheritor tier frequencies match {0.07, 0.30, 0.38, 0.25} within ±1% over 10k seeds; exactly two inherited blocks have `strippedBcy = overburdenBcy` and `thawProgress` in [3, 6] ft; family seasons and pit-log years lie in 2013–2024; the inherited fleet is `ex30`, `dz6` with ripper, `ld950`, `tr50`, `pmp6`, `gen100`, `pickup`, `campT8`, all grade D; banker stub payment = $3,113.75 ± $0.01/mo; Inheritor note = $10,281.75 ± $0.01 in each of June–November, $0 in December–May, balance 0 within 1¢ after month 84; easy-difficulty Bootstrapper books $500k company cash and $132k personal; hard-difficulty Backed equity books $1.275M of company cash ($170k owner capital + a $1.105M contribution for 40%) and owner NW = $170k + $45k personal = $215k.
- **Investor:** Q3 example → S = 58.1; the two-losing-season fixture (1.8.1) reproduces S = 69.5 / 60.6 / 46.5 / 33.8 / 26.5 / 9.8 / 0, a redemption demand at year 2 week 39 with BP = $682k, and `ousted` at year 3 week 13 if unpaid. Royalty minimum: a missed top-up opens `minimumCure` (26 weeks at S ≥ 40, else 8); paying it clears the cure; an uncured deadline transfers the highest-book-value claim through `land.transferToCreditor`, extinguishes the shortfall, and leaves unsecured debt only when no claim is left. Waterfall: claim at company NW $1.5M = $1.3M; at $1.2M = $1.2M with ownerShare 0 (never negative); at $5M = $2.0M; the two-holder example (1.8.1) gives $0.5M / $1.8M / $2.7M. Pro-rata distribution: draw $60k → investor $40k with one 40% holder. A refused approval blocks a second request on the same subject for 4 weeks (`APPROVAL_COOLDOWN`), and an approved plan budget pre-approves items within it. Two hostile check-ins → redemption decision with a 26-week deadline → unpaid → `runStatus = 'lost'`, reason `ousted`.
- **Reorganization, §1's side (P4+; §11 drives the case in these fixtures):** the 1.8.1 worked example reproduces S = 13.8 after the filing penalty and S = 6.4 at the week-13 check-in, with no redemption demand issued; the penalty applies once per case and per equity agreement (a second 16b in the same case changes nothing) and scales with `penaltyMult` (hard 1.3 → −26); a redemption demand open at filing has its deadline cleared, survives a deadline week that falls in the next pipeline, and is extinguished at confirmation with `hostileStreak` = 0; an open `minimumCure` is cleared at filing and no claim is foreclosed during the case; while a confirmed plan runs and a holder is hostile, `investor.conversionMotionActive` is true and one missed plan payment converts the case (`runStatus = 'lost'`, `endReason = 'liquidated'`, `liquidationPath = 'converted'`); with no hostile holder, one missed payment does not convert and two do. `owner/draw` and `owner/setSalary` above $900 × cpiIndex a week fail with `REORG_DRAW_LIMIT` during a case, a pre-filing salary above it is paid only up to it, and an allowance draw pays no pro-rata share; `investor/payReturn`, `investor/buyOut`, `owner/repayLoan`, `company/convertEntity` and `community/sponsor` fail with `REORG_OPEN`; `owner/fileBankruptcy` during a case converts it at any stage. `runStatus` stays `'active'` from filing through plan completion; reputation moves −10 at filing and +3 at completion; draws taken 10 weeks before a reorganization filing that later converts are clawed back.
- **Owner time:** a records review (3 days) and two site visits (2 days each) in one office week leave 2 days queued for the next week; forcing them cuts the owner's field `availableFraction` by 2/6 that week. Owner labor: reassigning the owner-foreman from claim A (crew of 5) to claim B stands A's plan down at the next step 7; activating a second plan with no hired foreman fails with `FOREMAN_REQUIRED` when its crew (excluding the owner) exceeds 3 or it runs a second shift or a second plant line, and succeeds at F = 0.92 with incident odds × 1.15 when its crew is 3 or fewer on one shift and one line; an owner-foreman on a three-line claim covers L1 and L2 and L3 runs under a line lead hand (§8 D-8.49); an owner-mechanic in pool mode (P3) adds 50 hours to that district's pool, not to a site shop; a fatal owner roll is recorded as serious.
- **Reputation:** bounded to [0, 100]; from 90 with no inputs reaches 70 in ≈ 139 weeks (±2); sponsorship cap enforced; capped kinds truncate at the cap and reset in week 1.
- **Net worth:** scrambling all hidden truth (geology, component health, honesty, employee truth, true fineness of unassayed lots, season drivers) leaves `netWorth(state,'scoring')` unchanged (property); the worked example (1.13) reproduces ($584k company, $704k owner, $683k real); metal-account ounces are valued by `metalAccountValueForScoring`, never by `netSalePerFineOz`; real NW divides by cpiIndex; contingent guarantees change nothing until demanded; a reorganization filing leaves `netWorth(state,'scoring')` unchanged except for the case costs, and the discharged claims leave it only at discharge (confirmation of a consensual plan, completion of a non-consensual one). `seasonView` never returns an unrevealed date (scrambled-truth property).
- **Difficulty:** every key in 1.11 exists in the tuning schema with exactly these values; conversely, every key marked difficulty-scaled in any section's tuning file appears in 1.11 with identical values (schema scan; `ops.freezeDamageProb` must be marked Diff = no); resolution applies each multiplier exactly once; geology priors are identical across difficulties.
- **Scenarios:** fixtures for 1,000 oz reached in year 2 week 30 → gold; the 1.10 medal-cap example (filed year 1 week 44, 1,000 oz in year 2 week 38) → silver, and the same run reaching it in year 3 → silver; a reorganized Debt-Free run cannot win before confirmation (`distressStage` 7) or while plan notes remain (`interestBearingDebt` > 0); a scenario run whose case converts ends `lost` / `liquidated`; debt-free evaluated only in week 52; Gold Baron uses real owner NW; `cumFineOzRecovered` uses estimated fineness until the assay and re-evaluates on assay, counts every plant line's cleanups, and counts a `source: 'sample'` lot once, at creation.
- **Simulator gates (BALANCE; bots from the §2.12.1 catalog, standard, 500 seeds per cell).** "Survival" is gated both ways (D-1.49): BALANCE O-01 needs the `cautious` bot's pooled going-concern S2 in 60–70% **and** its pooled no-bankruptcy B2 ≥ 75% (interim bands in BALANCE §7). B2 = not lost and no bankruptcy filing of either kind (liquidation or reorganization) in seasons 1–2 (BALANCE §5.1); S2 = B2 plus production in at least one season, no distress fleet sale, and at season 2's end a claim plus a fleet washing ≥ 20 bcy/hr, or company cash ≥ $150k × cpiIndex (BALANCE §5.2). A reorganized run keeps playing and is measured normally afterwards, but it has failed every window that contains its filing. Every survival figure prints S2, B2, the reorganization share and the retreated share B2 − S2 beside it; B2 per start type is reported, and the pooled B2 gates. Other gates: `cautious` S2 by background within ±5 pp of the mean (±7 pp interim in P1–P2), with §4's Geologist net-worth cap (median NW ratio ≤ 1.15 × the other four backgrounds', BALANCE O-07) read on the owner-ahead share for a start whose median sits on the waterfall floor; `cautious` S2 by start type within 10 pp of the 60–70% band; year-5 owner-ahead share within 20 pp between any two starts (BALANCE O-06 b; median NW ratios reported beside it). Owner-ahead share = share of games whose owner NW ends at or above its start (NW ratio ≥ 1.0, BALANCE §5.3). Wherever a Backed median sits on the investor-waterfall floor (a ratio of $50k ÷ $250k = 0.20), an outcome gate uses the owner-ahead share instead of the median (D-1.55); Inheritor season-1 production attempt rate ≥ 80%; arid chosen by `cautious` in ≤ 70% of seeds; sole-prop `cautious` S2 within 5 pp of the same bot as an LLC (P4+); Backed equity: among `cautious` runs with two losing seasons, P(ouster, forced redemption, or a reorganization filed while a redemption demand is open, by the end of season 3) in 40–70%, and the 2-season loss rate (a bankruptcy filing of either kind, or ouster: 1 − B2) of all `cautious` runs in 8–25% (P4+).

### 1.23 Decisions

- **D-1.1:** fixed 365-day calendar, no leap days; week 52 absorbs Dec 31. Rationale: one deterministic week ↔ date map, and the deadlines land as §2.4 expects.
- **D-1.2:** a deadline is due in the week containing its date, with no weekday or weekend shifting. Rationale: simple, visible, and testable.
- **D-1.3:** "operating window" means the *site season*. Start-up, cold-water recovery losses, wet-weather hours and §7's cool-week plant-hours cut (adopted, P1) leave effective full-rate sluicing ≈ 20 weeks. Listed in §0's deviations table (OQ-1.1); owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (§0.2). Rationale: reconciles the brief's 20–26 weeks with research showing 18–22 sluicing and 22–26 site weeks (R2).
- **D-1.4:** refined the freeze-up anchor. Mean is week 42 (σ 1.4), so the 90% range is weeks 40–44, against the guide's 39–43. Rationale: keeps the typical 22-week window with an early-May breakup. "Freeze-up" here means sustained cold that ends work, not first frost (Fairbanks first freeze ~Sept 15, but mild falls sluice into late October; R2).
- **D-1.5:** forecasts are re-issued noisy observations of the hidden anomaly, not exact shrinkage. Rationale: a calibrated, tightening forecast that cannot be decoded into the true date.
- **D-1.6:** §12 freeze-up and breakup events are short-notice shifts layered on the annual roll, and forecasts ignore them. Rationale: avoids double-counting normal variability while keeping a real surprise.
- **D-1.7:** weather is continuous temperature banded into five classes, with persistent precipitation that keeps the monthly marginals exact. Rationale: realistic streaks, simple tables, easy tests.
- **D-1.8:** `streamFlowFactor` carries the seasonal hydrograph, and §3 supplies one baseline gpm per source. Rationale: one owner for seasonal shape; no double-counting.
- **D-1.9:** fire restrictions use one 0–4 level scale for both the IFPL-like and Stage-like regimes. Northern districts have none (wildfire events only). Rationale: one effect table; matches real practice closely enough.
- **D-1.10:** each background is "the owner counts as one skilled professional", sized to ~$90–150k/yr of value. Rationale: guarantees one edge per background, roughly equal value, and distinct strategies, all built on §8's role curves.
- **D-1.11:** field edges (operator, mechanic) use the owner's single assignment at skill 85; desk edges run on desk days at skill 80 (landman) or 75 (geologist, §4's calibrated value, D-1.33). Rationale: compensates for the desk owners' free mediocre-foreman option.
- **D-1.12:** the banker edge is +1 credit tier (§11's `finance.bankerCreditTierBonus` 1 × `finance.tierWidthPoints` 35 = 35 U points) plus §11's one-year bank history gate (`finance.bank.bankerMinProfitableYears` 1 instead of 2), not a controller equivalent. Both are one edge, access to capital, and both are listed in 1.7 so the edge's value estimate matches what §11 implements. Rationale: "access to capital" is the banker's real advantage and is distinct from the other four; §11's U-point mechanism is canonical, so §1 cites §11's keys (D-11.58) instead of defining its own.
- **D-1.13:** P1 stubs: banker starter loan, landman price and royalty discount, mechanic maintenance discount. The geologist needs none because §4 ships its edge in P1. Rationale: keeps every background meaningful before its home system ships.
- **D-1.14:** no S-corp election in v1. Rationale: three entity types already cover the shield and tax trade-off. S-election adds tax code without adding a new kind of decision.
- **D-1.15:** Backed-equity requires an LLC or corp. Entity conversions are one-way. Rationale: real constraints that prevent entity hopping.
- **D-1.16:** investor money is booked so the owner's starting NW is $250k under both terms, with a 1× non-participating preference waterfall. Royalty terms follow R5's payback structure (10% of attributable ounces until 2.0×, then 3%) with less cash ($0.9M) than equity ($1.3M). Both are above R5's market upfront multiple (≈ 5.0× vs 2–4×) on purpose, while the investor still earns ≈ 17% IRR at the engine's reference output (430 fine oz, D-1.51). Rationale: no paper windfall from someone else's cash; the two terms trade control against cash and drag.
- **D-1.17:** an equity investor can end the run (ouster) after two hostile check-ins and an unpaid redemption. While a reorganization case is open the stay holds the demand, and the hostile holder's remedy is the conversion motion instead (D-1.58). Rationale: "expects returns" must have teeth. The 26-week window leaves room to fight.
- **D-1.18:** the Inheritor's claim tier mix is better than the market's (25% uneconomic vs ≈ 65%; D-1.42), with extra old-timer depletion and an optimistic family ledger. Rationale: survivor bias plus family memory makes the inherited ground "unknown quality", not "bad".
- **D-1.19:** difficulty never changes true geology, only information honesty and the other knobs. §3 agrees (D-3.18) and has no per-difficulty grade multiplier, and Hard does not thin the listing pool either. Listed in §0's deviations table; owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed, honesty only (§0.4, OQ-1.3). Rationale: matches the brief's "ground quality honesty", gives one seed the same world at every difficulty, and keeps balance targets comparable.
- **D-1.20:** scoring uses owner net worth at visible marks, in real dollars. Claims stay at cost basis. Owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (§0.11, OQ-1.2). Rationale: explainable, bot-consistent, and rewards realized value.
- **D-1.21:** owner living costs ($900/wk, from P4) make the owner's salary a real decision. Rationale: cash-flow pillar; no zero-cost owner.
- **D-1.22:** draw clawback of 13 weeks and blocking of draws at distress stage ≥ 3. The look-back runs from the bankruptcy petition, so a reorganization that converts looks back from its own filing (D-1.59). Rationale: closes the "drain then bankrupt" exploit.
- **D-1.23:** the end-of-run report reveals hidden truth. Rationale: teaches the game without affecting score or play.
- **D-1.24:** scenario worlds are random by default, with an optional fixed seed. Rationale: replayable; authors can still pin a world.
- **D-1.25:** heat and fire-level hour effects are required in P1 for the arid district; §7 adopted this and ships them in P1 (D-7.29), with precipitation hours in P5. Rationale: without them an arid summer is barely different from its winter, which weakens the "no dominant strategy" pillar; with them a P1 arid day-shift plan loses ≈ 5.0 weeks a year, ≈ 5.9 from P5.
- **D-1.26:** every equity holder (Backed investor, angel, family office, mining fund, rescue partner) is an `InvestorAgreement` with its own terms, and claims are paid by a seniority waterfall capped at company NW. Rationale: §11 admits up to two equity holders and a rescue partner; a single uncapped `investorClaim` made the owner's share negative whenever iron marked below cost.
- **D-1.27:** `accessOpen` and `seasonPhase` answer only for the current week; planning and validation of future actions use forecast-based `accessOutlook` / `phaseOutlook`. Rationale: a function that takes any week would let the UI, bots or validators decode hidden breakup and freeze-up dates.
- **D-1.28:** the owner's desk work is a weekly budget of desk days (5 in the office, 2.5 in the field), and forcing more takes field presence. Rationale: §3 site visits, §4 records reviews and §6 permit preparation all spend owner time; one budget makes "the owner's week" a real constraint instead of three unrelated rules.
- **D-1.29:** the Inheritor's paper is an active, under-bonded Plan of Operations sized to the inherited open acres + 5, with a bond review in week 1 and standing 55 (§6's recommendation). Rationale: a lapsed 5-acre plan was smaller than the acres §3's family mining generates (≈ 6), and an under-bond is the realistic inherited problem: a cash decision before breakup rather than a paperwork wait.
- **D-1.30:** arid fire factors raised to May 0.46 / June 0.50 / July 0.47, so level ≥ 3 occurs ≈ 1.9 weeks/year (mostly dry Junes); level 4 never comes from weather in the `stage` regime, and a full shutdown comes only from §12 wildfire closures. Rationale: at the earlier values level 3 occurred 0.8 weeks/year and level 4 was unreachable, so restrictions barely mattered. Permitted mines under Stage 2 usually work with a waiver and fire watch, so "no weather-driven shutdown" is realistic.
- **D-1.31:** the suggested heat effect is graded by weekly mean temperature (`1 − 0.03·(T − 80)`, floor 0.55, day shift), not a flat band multiplier. Rationale: July in the low desert (weekly mean ≈ 92 °F, highs ≈ 105 °F) must be much worse than May (≈ 77 °F); a flat 0.85–0.90 made them nearly equal. A night shift is the counter-play.
- **D-1.32:** the difficulty table adopts the keys and values that implementing sections already published and calibrated: §3 `geology.seller.*`; §6 `permits.insp.diffMult` / `fineDiffMult` / `reviewTimeMult` 1.2 / `infoDiffMult` / surety premium / auto-pay; and §11's lender-patience mechanism, `finance.paymentGraceWeeks` 3 / 2 / 1 as the late-fee grace (each lender's base grace shifted by value − 2) plus `finance.defaultTimelineMult` 1.25 / 1.00 / 0.75 on each lender's notice weeks (§11 D-11.14). There is no additive notice buffer and no separate detection knob. Rationale: one table, no contradictions; §11's version lands standard notices at ≈ 70 days (bank) and ≈ 50 (equipment lenders), inside R5; §1 still owns which knobs exist.
- **D-1.33:** the geologist owner is §4's skill-75 geologist (`geology.ownerGeologistSkill`) with §4's effects (program supervision, records 0.9, audits, recommendations), shipped in P1. Rationale: §4 owns the estimator and calibrated the edge against its own dominance risk; §1's earlier "passive staff-geologist estimates" did not match how §4's estimator works.
- **D-1.34:** after a refused approval, a holder will not consider another request on the same subject for 4 weeks; an approved annual capex budget pre-approves items within it. Rationale: with p = S/100 per request, weekly re-asking was a degenerate click loop.
- **D-1.35:** climate state is a §1-owned top-level `climate` slice. Rationale: it is §1 data; §3's `WorldSlice` does not carry it, and §1 cannot add fields to another section's slice.
- **D-1.36:** the sole proprietorship gets a concrete edge instead of being weakly dominated: no formation or annual cost and no entity filings, and for its first 104 weeks the owner's personal file stands in for the company's payment history (U's paydex term, §11 11.5, D-11.52), so early credit prices about half a tier better (U ≈ 168, C near B, vs ≈ 153 C for a Bootstrapper at week 3). It keeps full personal recourse and the royalty-only rescue. Gate: sole-prop `cautious` S2 within 5 pp of the LLC's. Rationale: the brief's three entities must each be a real choice; a sole proprietor's business credit really is the owner's credit, so the edge is realistic, and it costs exactly what the LLC buys (the shield).
- **D-1.37:** the freeze-up phase follows §7's continuous model: the plant may keep running at a falling multiplier with freeze-damage risk (P3), instead of a one-week "push". Breakup allows reduced-rate strip and dig. Rationale: §7 owns operations and already specifies it; a cliff at freeze-up week 1 added a rule without adding a decision.
- **D-1.38:** two month mappings: `reportingMonth` (first day; §11 and §13) and `monthOfWeek` (middle day; climatology only). Rationale: reports must partition exactly on `monthEndWeeks`, while weather tables should switch at the week that is mostly in the new month.
- **D-1.39:** scenario fine-ounce metrics use assayed fineness, or the player's estimate until the assay. Rationale: true fineness is hidden until assayed; scoring must not read it.
- **D-1.40:** difficulty's company-cash multiplier scales the Backed investor's contribution (and the royalty minimum) with the owner's capital; investor percentages and rates stay fixed. Rationale: keeps the owner's starting share of the company identical across difficulties.
- **D-1.41:** no inherited family override royalty in v1. Rationale: the Inheritor already carries debt, worn iron and an under-bond; another burden would make it the clearly weakest start. §5's `'inherited'` origin stays available for scenarios.
- **D-1.42:** starting liquidity was raised after the preflight model (500 games per cell): Bootstrapper company cash $250k → $400k; Inheritor $90k → $250k, plus two pre-stripped blocks, the estate note moved onto a June–November seasonal schedule (same $320k, 8.5%, 84 months), a ripper on the D6, and tier weights {0.05, 0.22, 0.40, 0.33} → {0.07, 0.30, 0.38, 0.25}. Rationale: both starts died of first-season liquidity, not geology (cautious S2: Bootstrapper 36–40%, Inheritor 0–3%; good Inheritor ground failed too). With the changes S2 is ≈ 57–64% and ≈ 39–52%; cash alone (Inheritor $300k with nothing stripped) only reached 29%, which is why the pre-strip and the seasonal note matter. The Inheritor's extra cash is the estate account, not unsold family gold, so no lot or fineness estimate is needed at setup. The Inheritor's cash was raised again, to $300k, by D-1.54.
- **D-1.43:** the difficulty cash multipliers are narrowed to 1.25 / 1.0 / 0.85 (company) and 1.1 / 1.0 / 0.9 (personal). Rationale: at 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.75 less cash made Hard play a smaller, safer fleet, so B2 was non-monotone (64 / 64 / 88); the brief's difficulty axes are honesty, lender patience and event severity, which the rest of 1.11 carries.
- **D-1.44:** 1.11 lists every difficulty-scaled key in any section (it gained §4's pit-stop, records and contractor-lead multipliers, §5's land keys, §8's résumé bias, §11's default timeline and distress watch, and §12's budget, catastrophe and mercy keys), and a schema test enforces it both ways. `ops.freezeDamageProb` is not scaled. The 13-week-forecast watch window is §11's `finance.distress.watchWeeks`, not a UI key. §4's knobs are multipliers (`geology.pitStopMult`, `recordsFindMult`, `contractorLeadMult`) rather than per-key notes. Rationale: one table that is complete is the only way §1 can own the knobs; distress thresholds belong to the distress owner; multipliers keep §4's base tables single-valued.
- **D-1.45:** the Inheritor fleet's values are §9's `resaleEstimate` outputs at grade D (≈ $152k), not hand-set figures (a hand-set $197k overstated §9's own formula by ≈ 30%), and the camp is §9's `campT8`. Rationale: §9 owns resale; net worth must use one valuation. The lost ≈ $45k of paper value is far smaller than D-1.42's cash change.
- **D-1.46:** the sole prop's credit edge is limited to U's paydex term, as §11 implements it (`finance.credit.solePropOwnerFileWeeks` 104, D-11.52); the time-in-business stand-in is held in reserve as a tuning lever (1.21). Rationale: the owner's file really is the business's payment history; adding timePts as well would push a Bootstrapper to ≈ 197 and make a sole-prop banker an A-tier startup. §11 owns the score formula.
- **D-1.47:** investor approval draws are keyed by (agreementId, subject, requestIndex); the annual plan's roll by subject `'plan'` and the year. Rationale: keying by `actionSeq` let a reload plus a dummy action re-roll a refusal, against §13's undo rules and §6 D-6.33; the cooldown alone did not stop it.
- **D-1.48:** `InvestorAgreement` IDs use the prefix `ivr`, not `inv`. Rationale: `inv.*` already names the ledger's inventory accounts (`inv.gold`, `inv.parts`), and explain links route by prefix, so `inv_000001` would read as an inventory record.
- **D-1.49:** survival is gated both ways (owner ruling 2026-10-05, §0.3 "gate both"; it replaces the earlier S2-only reading). BALANCE O-01 requires, for the `cautious` bot on standard, pooled going-concern survival S2 (BALANCE §5.2) in 60–70% **and** pooled no-bankruptcy B2 (BALANCE §5.1) ≥ 75%, with phase interim bands for both in BALANCE §7. A bankruptcy filing of either kind (liquidation or reorganization) inside seasons 1..N fails both B_N and S_N for that window; a reorganized run keeps playing and its later metrics are measured normally, and the reorganization share is reported separately. B2 per start type is reported; the pooled B2 gates. Every survival figure prints S2, B2, the reorganization share and the retreated share B2 − S2. Rationale: the two readings differ by 20–35 points. S2 alone would pass an economy in which every careful player who stops being a going concern also goes bankrupt (S2 = B2 = 60%, a 40% bankruptcy rate); B2 alone counts a careful bot that retreats with no iron and no cash as surviving. Counting a reorganization as a failure keeps the new lifeline from inflating survival. The preflight B2 with the adopted sections (pooled 93% under P1 rules and 90% under full rules, BALANCE §9.3; the model had no reorganization, so every failure there was a liquidation) already clears 75%, so the change adds a floor without forcing a retune.
- **D-1.50:** Backed-equity runs carry a loss calibration: P(ouster, a forced redemption, or a reorganization filed while a redemption demand is open, by the end of season 3 | two losing seasons) 40–70%, and an 8–25% two-season loss rate (a bankruptcy filing of either kind, or ouster; 1 − B2) across cautious runs. Backed-royalty runs have no band. Rationale: preflight Backed starts never failed (B2 100%); the investor's teeth need a target, and only the equity investor can end a run.
- **D-1.51:** the reference-operation anchor is restated from the guide's ≈ 460 fine oz / $1.9M to the engine's ≈ 430 fine oz in an established season (≈ 350 in a first frozen season), ≈ $1.8M at spot; D-1.16's investor figures are recomputed at 430 oz (10% ≈ $181k/yr, payback ≈ 10 seasons, IRR ≈ 17%). Rationale: §7's engine is canonical for production; the anchor must match what the simulator produces.
- **D-1.52:** a missed Backed royalty minimum is §1's obligation: §5 creates it with owner `'§1'`, §6 routes the miss to `investor.onMinimumMissed`, and an uncured miss forecloses one claim through §5's generic `land.transferToCreditor`, extinguishing the shortfall. Rationale: §1 owns the cure rule; §5 owns tenure transfer; the carry-note `land.onForeclose` (revert to seller) has the wrong semantics.
- **D-1.53:** family seasons are 2013–2024, so the plan "last worked three seasons ago" (2024) and the pre-stripped blocks (within `geology.oldTimer.preStripMaxAgeYr` 6) agree with the 2027 start. Rationale: the earlier 1998–2009 left 18 years between the last family season and the plan's last use.
- **D-1.54:** the Inheritor's company cash rises from $250k to $300k (`game.start.inheritor.companyCashUsd`; BALANCE R-3, the lever 1.21 named next). Owner NW at start rises by $50k, to ≈ $280k in P1 and ≈ $238k in P2+. Rationale: with D-1.42's package the second preflight still put the Inheritor's `cautious` S2 at 46% (P1) and 30% (full rules), against 50–80% for O-06 (a), the weakest start by far. At $300k it is 60% and 43%, the P1 pooled O-01 value moves from 63% to 68% (inside both the interim and the final band), and full-rules pooled S2 with D-3.48 is 55%. The value is data and cheap to reverse. Owner ruling 2026-10-05: R-3 approved; the 60–70% band stays, and the remaining full-rules gap is closed by P2–P4 tuning in BALANCE §9.5 item 5's order (`permits.reviewTimeMult`, `geology.supply.starterLeasePerDistrict`, then the Inheritor terms), not by widening the band.
- **D-1.55:** where a Backed median sits on the investor-waterfall floor (owner NW ratio within 0.01 of $50k ÷ $250k = 0.20, BALANCE §5.3), an outcome gate reads the **owner-ahead share** (the share of games whose owner NW ends at or above its start) instead of the median. Start parity is the owner-ahead share at year 5 within 20 pp between any two starts (BALANCE O-06 b), replacing "no start's year-5 median NW ratio above 1.5× another's"; the Geologist's 1.15× net-worth cap in the background-parity gate (BALANCE O-07) and §4's value-of-information gain (BALANCE O-08) switch the same way. Medians stay in every report. Rationale: about half the Backed-equity games end on the floor, so the median of one cell read 0.20 on one seed set and 0.85 on another, and a small calendar correction moved a five-year median from 0.37 to 0.83 (BALANCE §9.3); a share is stable where a median flips on a few seeds. Owner ruling 2026-10-05: the owner-ahead share is approved.
- **D-1.56:** only a liquidation ends a run in bankruptcy; a Chapter 11 Subchapter V reorganization keeps `runStatus` at `'active'` (owner ruling 2026-10-05, §0.9 "allow reorganization"). `endReason` `'bankrupt'` becomes `'liquidated'`, with `liquidationPath` ∈ `filed`, `involuntary`, `converted`, `p1Counter` (= §11 `distress.liquidation.cause`); `'forfeited'` is added for `scenario/forfeit`, which ended a run with no reason of its own. Reorganization ships in P4 with §11's full ladder; the P1–P3 insolvency counter still ends in liquidation. §11 owns every rule of the case; §1 owns its effects on investors, the owner's pay, reputation, scoring, scenarios and the report. Rationale: the real small-business path (Subchapter V, 2019) lets an owner keep the company by paying disposable income for 3–5 years, which is exactly the fight-back the brief's distress pillar wants, and calling both outcomes "bankrupt" would hide the difference from the player and the simulator.
- **D-1.57:** reorganization is allowed in every mode, and a run that filed can still win a goal scenario, but its medal is capped at silver (`game.scenario.reorgMedalCap`), from the first filing on, even after the plan completes. The `distressStage` metric is §11's stage, 7 until confirmation, and plan notes count as interest-bearing debt. Rationale: the owner's ruling; a capped medal keeps a comeback worth finishing while the gold medal still means a clean run, and counting plan notes as debt stops a run from meeting "debt-free" while it is still working off a plan.
- **D-1.58:** investors in a reorganization: a once-per-case filing penalty of 20 S points (× `penaltyMult`); check-in terms −6 while a case is open and −8 for a missed plan payment; no redemption demand during a case, an open one stayed at filing and extinguished at confirmation (a buy-out claim ranks behind every creditor, 11 U.S.C. §510(b)), with `hostileStreak` reset; an open royalty `minimumCure` carried into the plan as a secured claim; while any equity holder is hostile, one missed plan payment converts the case (the holder's conversion motion); pref accrues but nothing is paid to equity until the plan completes. Rationale: the owner's ruling says the equity investor's stance drops and it may push for conversion; the stay really does hold a redemption, so the realistic lever left to a hostile holder is a motion to convert on default under the plan (§1112(b)(4)(N)). Without the motion a filing would be a cheap shield against redemption.
- **D-1.59:** during a reorganization case the owner's salary and draws together are capped at the living allowance (`game.ownerLivingCostPerWeek` × cpiIndex), paid as compensation with no pro-rata share to equity; owner-loan repayments, buy-outs, return payments, entity conversion and sponsorship are refused (`REORG_OPEN`); injections stay open. The 13-week draw clawback is measured from the bankruptcy petition, so a reorganization that converts looks back from its own filing date. Rationale: a debtor in possession lives on a court-approved allowance and may not pay insiders; measuring look-backs from the petition is the real rule, and it stops a player from draining the company during the case and then letting it convert.
- **D-1.60:** in scoring, pre-filing debts stay at their allowed amounts until the discharge (§11: at confirmation of a consensual plan, at completion of a non-consensual one); then they are replaced by the plan's remaining payments. Rationale: a filing alone must never raise the score, and the discharge is the legal moment the haircut becomes real; it closes the "reorganize, then retire" loop.
- **D-1.61:** reputation −10 at a reorganization filing and +3 when the plan completes (`game.reputation.delta.reorgFiled` / `reorgCompleted`, reported by §11). Rationale: a bankruptcy filing is public, and vendors, sellers and crews read it; −10 matches the heaviest single inputs already in 1.12 (an unreclaimed abandonment, a fatality). Finishing the plan earns a little back, not all.
- **D-1.62:** §1's owner rules follow the multi-claim rulings (owner ruling 2026-10-05, §0.7 "all of these"): the owner-foreman covers one claim and up to `staff.foremanMaxLines` (2) plant lines; a claim with a crew of three or fewer (excluding the owner), one shift and one line may run with no foreman at F = 0.92 and incident odds × 1.15 (§8), so `FOREMAN_REQUIRED` applies only above that; the owner-mechanic's `shop` assignment names a site or a district pool, like a hired mechanic's. The tutorial shows the small-crew choice next to the owner-foreman, and the Operator edge is restated against it. Rationale: §7, §8 and §9 own the mechanics; §1 owns the owner and the tutorial beats, which must not say that every claim needs a foreman when a small one no longer does.
- **D-1.63:** setup validation adds `BACKED_TERMS_UNEXPECTED` (terms given without a Backed start), `START_NOT_IN_PHASE` (a start the build cannot run; a P0 build runs only the Bootstrapper), `START_YEAR_INVALID` (not an integer in 1900–2500) and `OPENING_SPOT_INVALID` (neither null nor a positive finite number); a sandbox setup with a scenario id is `SCENARIO_UNKNOWN`; names are checked after trimming against the exported `NAME_MAX_LENGTH` (40). `validateSetup` returns every issue with its field, and `newGame` throws `SetupError` with them. Rationale: every field of `NewGameSetup` gets a typed reason the wizard and the simulator's flag parser can show, and no build starts a game it cannot run.
- **D-1.64:** `newGame` posts the start's cash through the ledger: company cash as owner capital in the company book (`cash.operating` / `eq.ownerCapital`) and personal cash in the owner book (`own.cash` / `own.equity`), each × its difficulty multiplier. New keys: `game.start.bootstrapper.personalCashUsd` (120,000), `game.startCompanyCashMult` and `game.startPersonalCashMult` (base 1.0; 1.11 sets the difficulty values). Rationale: a Bootstrapper's scoring net worth must start at 1.8's $520,000, and cash changes only through ledger postings (§11), so even the opening balance has an explanation.
- **D-1.65:** only §1 draws on its `setup` stream. §1's `inheritorStreams(seed)` builds the Inheritor's streams and hands `ground` and `pits` to §3's `genInheritedGroup`, `fleet(i)` to §9's `materializeInheritedFleet` and `hand` to §8's candidate, as §4 hands `sample` to `drawSample`. Rationale: §2.3 stream rule (b), which the registry test checks by engine folder (§2.14); the stream names and keys are unchanged, so the generated content is the same.
- **D-1.66:** the calendar helper is `weekToDateRange(week)` → `{ start, end }` with no year; `turnDate(turn, startCalendarYear)` adds the year, week and display year for labels. Rationale: with no leap days (D-1.1) a week has the same dates every year, so the year belongs to the turn, not to the week.

### 1.24 Open questions

None open. The owner answered all three on 2026-10-05; they stay listed so other documents can cite them.

- **OQ-1.1: season-length calibration.** *Resolved — owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (§0.2).* The brief says northern seasons are "roughly 20–26 weeks"; research shows real sluicing seasons of 13–21 weeks in interior Alaska and 18–22 in the Klondike. The design keeps a 19–25-week site season (typically 22) with ≈ 20 effective full-rate sluicing weeks (D-1.3, D-1.4).
- **OQ-1.2: scoring basis.** *Resolved — owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (§0.11).* Scenario and leaderboard net worth stay at conservative visible marks with claims at cost; appraised NW is shown as information only (D-1.20). A reorganization changes the scored debts only at discharge (D-1.60).
- **OQ-1.3: does Hard thin the ground itself?** *Resolved — owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (§0.4).* Honesty only: true geology, including the ground on offer, is identical at every difficulty, and Hard makes sellers, records and résumés less truthful, lenders less patient and events more severe (D-1.19, §3 D-3.18).
