### 2.17 Decisions

- **D-2.1** — Randomness is stateless keyed streams: FNV-1a 64 + SplitMix64 seeding into xoshiro128\*\*, with no RNG state in `GameState`. — Stream isolation makes tuning one system leave the others byte-identical, and nothing about RNG needs saving.
- **D-2.2** — Money is integer cents, rounded half away from zero at posting. — Float drift in a ledger breaks balancing tests and golden hashes.
- **D-2.3** — Transcendental math comes from our own `dmath`, not `Math.*`. — Engines differ in the last bit, which can fork a replay across browsers.
- **D-2.4** — Immer for immutable updates; auto-freeze off in the simulator. — Structural sharing keeps UI selectors cheap; freezing costs too much over 130,000 weeks.
- **D-2.5** — Saves go into IndexedDB through a thin `idb-keyval`-style wrapper; exports are gzipped JSON. — Simple, async and large-quota storage, and human-readable files when unzipped.
- **D-2.6** — Simulator worker pool: game *i* uses seed `seedBase + i`, and results aggregate in index order. — Output is identical for any worker count, so runs on 4 and 8 cores compare directly.
- **D-2.7** — Data files are `as const satisfies Schema`, plus a zod test with cross-reference checks. — Compile-time types and runtime validation of designer edits.
- **D-2.8** — ID collisions are resolved this way: §9 uses `fo`, `aev`, `rct`, `mi`; §6, §5 and §4 keep `ord`, `insp`, `auc`, `ctr`. `lst` is one counter with two branded types; `ivr` for investor agreements; `emp_owner` is the only reserved non-counter id. Longer names (`ford`, `eauc`, `ectr`, `minsp`, `elst`, `inv`) were considered and not adopted. — §9 (D-9.43) and §1 (D-1.48) already adopted these; a shared counter keeps listing ids unique, and `EntityRef` routes them.
- **D-2.9** — The stream registry uses the owners' adopted names: `finance-lender`, `finance-royaltyco`, `finance-equity`, `finance-insurance` (§11 D-11.57) and `market-buyers` (§10 D-10.37), not `royalty-co`, `equity-offer` or `gold-buyers`. §4's `seller-data` stream does not exist and is not registered. — One name per stream, matching the text engineers will implement.
- **D-2.10** — In step 12, §11's deferred-revenue drawdowns run before §4 `recordProduction`, as §7, §10, §11 and §12 wrote, not the reverse order. — The two read disjoint data and commute (property test), and four owners already agree.
- **D-2.11** — Step 3's order is §5 (calling §3 `supplyTick` first) → §4 → §8 → §9. — The three later markets read no step-3 output of each other; fixing one order removes ambiguity, and a permutation test guards the independence.
- **D-2.12** — Obligation timing is keyed on `settlementClass` (statutory vs billable) as in 2.6. — It keeps the Sept 1 forfeiture real and stops a lease payment made in step 14 from being called missed in step 13 of the same week.
- **D-2.13** — Turn semantics: step 0 increments the turn, so a pipeline runs as the new week; `newGame` runs the year-1 week-1 initializations. — This matches the original step-0 contract the sections were written against, and makes "last chance to act = turn d − 1" explicit.
- **D-2.14** — Save budget: per-slice budgets summing to 3.5 MB of state and 4.0 MB per file at year 10, gzip on export, instead of a single 2 MB or 2.8 MB total. — The owners' own commitments (world 1.0, finance 0.6, inbox 0.3, permits 0.25, gold 0.2, knowledge 0.3 MB) already exceed 2.8 MB, and §11's compaction (52-week detail, one payroll transaction per run) is in place. 4 MB is cheap in IndexedDB and in one structured clone per run.
- **D-2.15** — Performance target: 3.5 ms mean per simulated week, with per-system budgets and an 8 ms ceiling for a mid-game operating week. — A 5 ms median budget gave 162 s per cell on 4 cores, over the stated 2 minutes; the per-system budgets keep §4's estimator and §7's flow from spending the week.
- **D-2.16** — Survival is gated both ways (owner ruling 2026-10-05, §0.3 "gate both"; it replaces the S_N-only reading). The simulator computes going-concern S_N and no-bankruptcy B_N exactly as BALANCE §5.1–5.2 define them, and BALANCE O-01 gates the `cautious` bot's pooled S2 in 60–70% and pooled B2 ≥ 75% on standard. A bankruptcy filing of either kind (liquidation or reorganization) inside seasons 1..N fails both B_N and S_N for that window; a reorganized run keeps playing and its later metrics are measured normally. Every survival figure prints S_N, B_N, the reorganization share and the retreated share B_N − S_N, and the bankruptcy rate is split into liquidations and reorganization filings. — The two readings differ by 20–35 points: under B_N alone a bot that retreats with no iron and no cash "survives", and under S_N alone an economy where every failed careful run ends bankrupt would pass. Counting a reorganization as a failure for its window stops the new lifeline from inflating survival, while measuring the run afterwards keeps late-window net worth honest.
- **D-2.17** — The bot catalog lives in §2.12.1 with camelCase ids matching BALANCE §4. Its testing budgets make BALANCE's "light test" concrete (balanced: until `inferred` on one listing; aggressive: ≤ 3 pits on each of 3). Aggressive buys new iron when dealer or captive finance is offered. BALANCE §4 1.0's refined rules are adopted by D-2.29. — One definition for every section's gates; the concrete budgets make the bots implementable without guessing.
- **D-2.18** — Phase rules are a runtime switch, `meta.rulesPhase`, set at `newGame`. Later builds keep the earlier phases' stub paths behind `rulesAtLeast(state, n)`. — BALANCE §7 checks interim bands and P1-vs-full comparisons after later phases ship; a git-tag comparison would mix engine versions.
- **D-2.19** — Pure memo caches are allowed under the 2.3 item-6 conditions. — §3's truth decode, §4's estimator and §12's `effective()` would blow the time budget without them; the conditions keep saves and hashes cache-free.
- **D-2.20** — Records are iterated through sorted-key helpers, with numeric-aware `compareIds` and code-unit string order; raw `Object.keys` is banned in `engine/`. — Insertion order depends on the path a game took. One helper is cheaper than an `ids` array on every Record, and owners that keep arrays stay compatible.
- **D-2.21** — Action-time draws are keyed by subject and a per-subject counter in state; the `action` stream is limited to draws with no gameplay consequence. — With `actionSeq` keys, a reload plus a dummy action could re-roll an inspection, an offer or an approval.
- **D-2.22** — The engine, not the UI, decides `undoable`: RNG use is detected, and reveals and commitments are declared per action. — Undo must never become a re-roll or a free peek (§13 D-13.11).
- **D-2.23** — Warning-level stops can be muted per alert kind; critical and blocking never. — §13's muting, without letting a player silence a missed payroll.
- **D-2.24** — Grade conversion is 1 g/m³ = 0.024581 oz/yd³ (from §13 D-13.14). — The earlier 0.0243 was off by 1.2%.
- **D-2.25** — Annual rates compound weekly via dmath, except loans and cards, which use APR/12 per month (§11 D-11.4). — Real loan quotes reproduce exactly; everything else keeps one convention (§12 now uses it for competitor debt).
- **D-2.26** — History is one 157-turn weekly ring that starts with §10's pre-history at negative turns, plus annual rollups. — The price chart (with its pre-history), the net-worth and production charts and the end report read one structure, and the slice stays bounded.
- **D-2.27** — `--background none` is a simulator-only owner with no background edge. — BALANCE's core matrix compares bots and starts without an edge; §1's five backgrounds are measured separately in the background block.
- **D-2.28** — `effective()` and the extended `EffectModifier` are engine core, hosted by §2, with semantics from §12 12.3. — Every section reads modifiable values through it from P1, so it cannot live in a P5 system.
- **D-2.29** — The 2.12.1 catalog adopts BALANCE §4 version 1.0's six *(refined)* rules in substance, and the catalog ships as `BOT_VERSION` 1.0: (1) a reserve of N weeks is the largest cumulative net cash outflow over the next N weeks of `cashPlan`, covered by company plus personal cash; (2) the owner is the foreman, and a foreman is hired only for a second claim or a third plant line (one foreman covers both shifts, D-8.33); (3) the cautious starter tier buys a grade-D excavator, dozer and plant; (4) a mechanic is hired in P1–P2 when 30% of projected season maintenance exceeds the mechanic's projected wages, and from P3 when projected maintenance exceeds $120k a season; (5) an arid bot runs a single water truck only when the well alone cannot hold 20 bcy/hr; (6) `aggressive` counts a listing as affordable only when its price plus the planned fleet fits liquidity. `sizeFleet`'s sizing rule is unchanged (BALANCE R-6 is a P1 trial, approved by the owner on 2026-10-05 as a trial only). Owner ruling 2026-10-05: R-2 approved. — Without these the bots did not behave as the brief describes (BALANCE R-2): a gross 13-week reserve (≈ $400k) stopped every Bootstrapper from operating, a $125k foreman fit no starter budget, B–C starter iron broke the 60% cap, the aggressive bot bought ground it could not equip and sold its fleet before mining, and an arid starter lost ≈ $127k a year to a water truck it did not need. The version bump keeps baselines honest (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
- **D-2.30** — Reorganization in the frame (owner ruling 2026-10-05, §0.9 "allow reorganization"; §11 owns the case). An open case leaves `runStatus` at `'active'`, so `canAdvance`, the step-0 guard, `runToNextDecision` and the simulator harness treat it as a running game; only a liquidation (filed, involuntary, converted from reorganization, or the P1–P3 insolvency counter), an ouster, a scenario result or retirement ends a run, and §1's `endReason` `'bankrupt'` becomes `'liquidated'` (D-1.56). Step 15 judges the case under the automatic stay and raises the liquidation flag that 16d reads; 16b applies §1's investor effects before any deadline check. The creditor vote draws on a new stream, `finance-reorg`, registered to §11; it is a pipeline draw at the hearing, keyed by turn and case id, so neither a reload nor a dummy action can re-roll it. The case is a counter id with the new prefix `reo`, so explain links, inbox subjects, §13's plan screen and the end report can name it, and a later case in a long game gets its own id. — Every other reading of "game over" in the frame assumed bankruptcy ends the run; the stream and prefix rules require one registered owner for each, and keying the vote by the case keeps undo and reload honest (D-2.21).
- **D-2.31** — Plant lines and shop modes in the frame (owner ruling 2026-10-05, §0.7 "all of these"; §7, §8 and §9 own the rules). `MinePlan.lines` holds one to three lines, always exactly L1 … Ln, so the array is already in `lineId` order; lines run in ascending `lineId` wherever the pipeline processes them (step 9 within each hour, step 10's re-resolve, step 12's cleanups after claims ascending). A line is named by `${claimId}/${lineId}` in an `EntityRef`, never a counter id. The `WeekReport` entry becomes `{ result, cleanups[] }`; §7's `ops-freeze`, `ops-audit` and `ops-skim` take `lineId` as their last key part. §7's time budget becomes per line (`sim.perf.opsPerLineMs`, renamed from `opsPerClaimMs`), and the mid-game perf fixture gains a two-line claim and a district pool. Mechanics and welders carry a shop mode (`site` at one claim, or `pool` for a district from P3; §8 D-8.50), and step 8 plans a shop per site and per pool. — Determinism needs one fixed line order and stable line references; a per-claim time budget would hide a three-line claim's triple flow cost; a claim may now clean up two or three times in one week, which a single optional cleanup could not report.
- **D-2.32** — Every catalog bot keeps one plant line per claim, a foreman (owner or hire) on every claim, and mechanics in site mode, unless its row says otherwise; three named bots, `smallCrewNoForeman` (P1), `multiLine` (P3) and `poolMechanics` (P3), each take one of the new options. BALANCE §4.0's last-resort fleet sale is mirrored into the catalog's common rules. — The owner asked that bots keep these defaults, so the 1.0 baselines and the preflight figures stay comparable; one named bot per option measures whether it dominates (BALANCE O-04, O-07), which is the only way the simulator can catch a dominant multi-claim strategy. The last-resort rule was in BALANCE §4.0 but missing here.
- **D-2.33** — Bots never file on their own initiative; from P4 they answer §11's involuntary-petition decision with *reorganize* when eligible (no guarantor filing), file the first plan that passes `reorgPlanPreview` in a fixed order of terms and schedules, and pay it before discretionary spend. — With no rule the simulator could never measure the reorganization share the owner asked for, and every bot would give up where a careful owner fights on. Answering only the petition, the moment a liquidation would otherwise happen, means the rule turns no recoverable run into a failure: the run fails that window either way, so B_N and S_N read as they would without it, while later-window net worth is measured as a careful owner would play. A fixed search order keeps bot decisions deterministic and identical under scrambled hidden state (§11's preview reads only visible state).
- **D-2.34** — Saves from phase N load in phase N+1: every schema change from P1 on ships a migration and a fixture; P0 saves are not supported (owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed, §0 smaller call 1, OQ-2.1). — Retrofitting migrations later is expensive, and dropping playtesters' saves at each phase would cost goodwill for little saving.
- **D-2.35** — The game's resolved tuning lives in the state as `meta.tuning` (part of the state and its hash), and `meta.tuningHash` is its hash, re-checked at load. The load codec compares a save's tuning with what this build resolves for the save's own setup, so a save on another difficulty raises no `TUNING_DIFFERS` notice and genuinely different tuning does; the notice carries both hashes. — "A game keeps its tuning until the player migrates" (2.9, 2.10) needs the resolved values inside the save; a hash alone could only say that they differ. Comparing with the build's default game would flag every easy or hard save.
- **D-2.36** — Tuning resolution has a `setup` layer between the scenario and the simulator overrides: the setup's `world.startCalendarYear` replaces `game.startCalendarYear`, and a non-null `world.openingSpotUsdPerFineOz` replaces `market.openingSpotUsdPerFineOz` (also §10's `referenceSpot`). — Dates and the opening price each read one tuning key, whoever set them, and a simulator override still wins over the wizard's choice.
- **D-2.37** — `newGame(setup, seed, tuning?, options?)` takes a non-empty string seed and an optional `{ rulesPhase }`, which defaults to the build's phase (`BUILD_RULES_PHASE`) and may not exceed it; `meta.rulesPhase` is 0–6, and a P0 build records 0. — `--rules pN` (2.12) had no way into `newGame`; a game must record the rules it actually ran, and no build can run rules it does not have.
- **D-2.38** — `state.ids` is `Partial<Record<IdPrefix, number>>` (an absent prefix counts as 0), and `newGame` raises each counter past the highest canonical id in the generated world (`reserveIdsFrom`). — A new prefix then needs no save migration. §3's generator mints world ids on its own counters and returns only the `WorldSlice`, so without the reservation a later `nextId` could collide with a generated id.
- **D-2.39** — Decisions are created only through §2's `createDecision`, which checks the spec and mints the `dec` id. A closed decision moves to `inbox.closedDecisions` (sorted ids) as `{ closedTurn, outcome: 'answered' | 'defaulted', optionId, errorCode? }` and is pruned `game.alerts.inboxRetentionWeeks` after it closed. A default whose action no longer validates still closes as `'defaulted'`, recording the validator's code; in P0, step 16 applies every due default. — The `dec` prefix is §2's, so other owners need a §2 helper (2.14). Without the closed record, validation could not tell `DECISION_CLOSED` from `DECISION_NOT_FOUND`. A deadline must always close its decision, even when the world has moved on and the default is no longer valid.
- **D-2.40** — `HandlerContext.rng` has core `rng`'s exact signature and wraps it to record draws; the context adds `applyNested`, `markReveals` and `markCommits`; `decision/answer` carries `decisionId`, `optionId` and flat primitive `params` merged into the option's action, never replacing its `type`; `clock.actionSeq` counts player actions only. — The literal-stream lint rule and the registry test must still see each stream name; an option run inside an answer must carry its draws and flags into the answer's `undoable`; params that could change the type would let an answer run an action the decision never offered; defaults the pipeline applies are not player actions, so they must not shift the flavor stream's keys.
- **D-2.41** — The `effective()` memo is scoped to the identity of the immutable `events.modifiers` Record and keyed `(tuningHash, turn, modifiersVersion, key, q)`; a key that no modifier targets skips the cache; `effective()` also reads numeric tuning keys that are not registered hooks. The same text is in §12 12.3. — A version counter alone cannot tell two games in one process apart, nor an undone branch from a redone one with different modifiers (undo restores the counter). Immer changes the Record's identity exactly when a modifier changes, and skipping the cache keeps an event-free game from growing it.
- **D-2.42** — Step 0 derives `clock.year` and `clock.week` from the new turn; step 1 derives the week's `WeekCalendar` (display year, reporting month, quarter, month-, quarter- and year-end flags, year start) into the step context, and later steps read it there. — One derivation per week, so no two steps can disagree about the calendar; P0's step 1 has nothing else to do.
- **D-2.43** — Loading validates the invariants the engine relies on, not only the shape: the tuning hash, the clock against the turn, registered id prefixes, ledgers that balance and match a recomputation, `…Ids` arrays against their Records, an ascending history and a known run status. Any failure is `SAVE_CORRUPT`. — A damaged or hand-edited save that broke one of them would otherwise fail far from the cause, or fork a replay without a word.
- **D-2.44** — `canAdvance` checks `GAME_OVER` before `BLOCKING_DECISION_OPEN`. `runToNextDecision` throws `EngineGuardError` when the start state cannot advance and `RangeError` when `maxWeeks` is not a positive integer, defaults its anchor to `defaultRunAnchor` (`runId` `run_t<turn>`), and always stops with a reason at a state that cannot advance. — A finished run must report game over even with a decision left open; a run that cannot take a single week is a caller bug, not an empty result; every stopped run must say why.
- **D-2.45** — `WeekOpsResult`, `CleanupResult` and `OpsHint` are placeholders in `turn/types.ts` until §7 defines them (`CleanupResult` holds the `lineId` the every-cleanup stop names); `AlertKind` is §13 13.10's taxonomy list (`ALERT_KINDS`). — The frame and the stop rules need the names before §7 and §13 ship their bodies, and one list keeps the alert kinds a closed, typed set.
- **D-2.46** — The layering test reads the real import graph, re-exports, dynamic `import()` and `require()` included. The engine's one package is Immer, which `sim/` may also import; no engine or data file imports `data/tuning/ui.ts`; only `sim/` (and `data/balance/` itself) imports `data/balance/`. The raw-hook-read lint rule allows a hook-key literal only as a direct argument of `effective()` or `effectiveValue()`, or in a type position, and is off for `data/events/**`, `data/tuning/**`, `data/difficulty.ts` and `data/scenarios/**`. — These are CLAUDE.md rules that 2.1 and 2.10 did not spell out; the exempt files name hook keys by design (the registry, event and preparation effects, tuning, difficulty and scenario overrides).
- **D-2.47** — The registry test maps every engine folder to one section and fails on an unmapped folder; each stream is drawn and each prefix minted only from its owner's folders; `nextClaimListingId` may be called only from §5's folders and `nextEquipListingId` only from §9's, a raw `nextId(_, 'lst')` from either; `dec` and `action` are §2's, so other owners create decisions through `createDecision`. — Stream rule (b) and the prefix registry can only be checked against a fixed folder-to-owner map (CLAUDE.md: no system folder without an owning section); the typed wrappers keep each listing kind with its section while the shared counter keeps every `lst_` id unique (D-2.8).
- **D-2.48** — `dmath` also provides `expm1`, `log1p`, `tan`, `atan2`, `erfc` and `lgamma`; `sin`, `cos` and `tan` accept |x| ≤ 2²⁰·π/2 and throw `RangeError` beyond; `exp(1)` returns `Math.E`; `lgamma` accepts x > 0 only. — The game never takes the sine of a huge argument, so the Payne–Hanek path would be untested code; fdlibm's `exp(1)` is one ulp high; the engine takes log-gamma of positive arguments only, so the reflection branch is left out.
- **D-2.49** — A very large Record iterated every week keeps a sorted `…Ids` array (`insertSortedId`, `removeSortedId`) instead of calling `sortedKeys` weekly, and full-state hashing is for tests and saves, never per simulated week. — Measured in P0: `Object.keys` on 20,000 keys costs ≈ 3 ms in V8, close to the 3.5 ms week budget, and hashing a 3.5 MB state ≈ 0.17 s.

### 2.18 Open questions

None open.

- **OQ-2.1: save compatibility across phases.** *Resolved — owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (D-2.34).* Saves made under phase N load in phase N+1, so every schema change from P1 on carries a migration and a fixture; P0 saves are not supported.

## 3. World and Geology

> **At a glance.** At `newGame` this system builds the whole physical world. It generates 2–6 mining districts from region templates. Each district gets a creek network on a simple 2D map, a service town, an access class and its land overlays (withdrawn and special-status stretches). Claim parcels are laid along the creeks and benches. Every parcel gets visible environmental attributes (wetland and channel blocks, fish-bearing water, sensitivity) and hidden, immutable true geology at **1-acre block** resolution. Grade follows a district → creek → claim → block lognormal hierarchy, with a down-valley paystreak, rare rich pockets and old-timer workings that took the richest bedrock pay. §3 also owns the physics of sampling (`drawSample`): a compound-Poisson particle model in which pans and drill holes are dominated by the nugget effect and bulk samples converge. It generates what a listing shows, the seller's (possibly dishonest) claims built from truth, the stream of listing candidates handed to §5, and open ground for staking. Calibration target: of the ground on the market, about 70% is uneconomic for a typical operator at $4,200, about 22% marginal, about 7% good and about 1% excellent. Finding the good ground is the game. §3 itself gives the player only two choices: where to look (district, creek, listing) and whether to make a site visit. Every other way of buying down uncertainty belongs to §4, and every way of acquiring ground belongs to §5.

### 3.1 World structure, generation order, storage

**Hierarchy.** World → `District` (2–6) → `Creek` (a tree of 5–12 per district) → `Claim` parcel (60–80 per district, hard cap 320 per world, 3.4) → `Block` (1 acre = 209 × 209 ft; 1 ft of thickness = 1,613 bcy). A claim is an `nAlong × nAcross` grid, with the along axis following the valley downstream→upstream.

| Claim acres | Grid (along × across) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 20 (federal placer) | 5 × 4 (bench: 10 × 2) | 1,045 × 836 ft; stands in for the real 1,320 × 660 ft aliquot |
| 40 (association, 2 locators) | 10 × 4 | |
| 80 | 10 × 8 if valley half-width ≥ 700 ft, else 20 × 4 | |
| 160 (association, 8 locators) | 20 × 8 or 40 × 4 | |
| 23 (Yukon creek claim, P6) | 3 × 8 | 500 ft along × 2,000 ft across |
| 40 / 160 (Alaska MTRSC, P6) | 8 × 5 / 20 × 8 | |

Claim size mix (P1 templates): 20 ac 55%, 40 ac 20%, 80 ac 15%, 160 ac 10%. That averages ≈ 47 blocks per claim, so a 300-claim world has ≈ 14,000 blocks.

**Units (§2.4).** Every "raw oz" in §3 (grades, contained gold, seller history, `SampleResult` ounces) is a **metal ounce**: gold plus its natural silver alloy, before gold-room dirt. Every `fineness` in §3 (block truth, template and district means, `claimedFineness`) is **alloy fineness**, fine oz per metal oz. Weighed raw (metal ÷ (1 − dirtFrac)) and fineness per weighed ounce belong to §7 and §10.

**Everything is generated at `newGame`.** Claims never spawn later. Supply over time works by changing status (open ↔ held ↔ listed ↔ owned; 3.11), and staking uses the pre-generated open parcels. True geology is **immutable** after generation. Play changes only `Block.state` (3.5).

**Storage.** Each claim's block truth is quantized at generation and stored as a packed base64 string (`claim.hidden.truthPack`), with a 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the string in `claim.hidden.truthHash`. The engine decodes it lazily into a non-serialized, memoized cache keyed by `(claimId, truthHash)`. The key deliberately excludes the seed: the simulator replays one seed under many tuning overrides in one process, and the Inheritor step (3.6.1) re-packs a claim inside `newGame`, so a `(seed, claimId)` key could return stale truth. The packing itself is part of generation: history, seller evidence, classification and sampling all use the *decoded* (quantized) values, so stored and used truth can never disagree. Quantization:

```
claim header                                  coarseMeanMg uint16 = round(mg × 10)   // claim-level coarse particle mass (3.5.3), read by drawSample
lengthsFt (overburden, pay, bedrock cleanup)  uint16 = round(ft × 100)          // 0.01 ft resolution
grades (current, virgin, pocket, tailings)    uint16 = round(8000 × log10(max(g, 1e-7) / 1e-7))  // 0.03% relative, 1e-7..15 oz/bcy; 0 decodes as 1e-7
fractions (sizeMix×4, permafrost, clay, boulders, cementation, minedOut, paystreakFraction, bedrockGoldShare)
                                              uint16 = round(x × 65535)          // sizeMix renormalized on decode
fineness                                      uint16 = round((x − 0.5) / 0.5 × 65535)
verticalDecayFt                               uint16 = round(ft × 1000)
bedrockType                                   uint8 enum; pockets and old tailings: sparse list appended per claim
```

Size: ≈ 36 bytes per block, about 0.5 MB raw and 0.7 MB base64 at 300 claims (≈ 0.3 MB for a P1 world). Decoding one claim takes < 0.2 ms. The decode cache holds ≈ 3 MB for a full world; it is a pure memo cache under §2.3's rule (keyed by content hash, never serialized or hashed). Seller evidence is *not* stored in full (3.10.2): holders keep a ≈ 100-byte summary per claim, and the public-record extras (creek histories, ≈ 30 old drill logs) add < 15 kB, so the whole world slice stays ≈ 0.9 MB at 320 claims, inside §2.13's 1.0 MB `world` budget.

**Data shapes** (the `world` slice; hidden fields are marked and are read only by engine physics, never by UI or bot selectors):

```ts
interface WorldSlice {
  genParams: GeoGenParams;                          // snapshot of generation tuning (D-3.2)
  districts: Record<DistrictId, District>; districtIds: DistrictId[];
  creeks: Record<CreekId, Creek>;                   // prefix 'crk'
  claims: Record<ClaimId, Claim>; claimIds: ClaimId[];
  blockStates: Record<BlockId, BlockState>;         // sparse: only touched blocks
  holders: Record<HolderId, SellerProfile>;         // prefix 'hld'
  siteVisits: Record<ClaimId, SiteVisitReport[]>;   // player-visible
  watch: { districtIds: DistrictId[]; claimIds: ClaimId[] };   // player-visible inbox preferences (world/setWatch); claimIds ≤ geology.maxTrackedClaims
  supplyQueue: { claimId: ClaimId; situation: SellerSituation; queuedTurn: number }[];   // relistClaim requests for the next step-3 supplyTick
}
interface District {
  id: DistrictId; name: string; templateId: RegionTemplateId; regime: Regime;
  climateTemplateId: ClimateTemplateId; fireRestrictionRegime: 'none' | 'stage' | 'ifpl';   // §1 1.4.1
  stateOverlayId: 'northernOverlay' | 'aridOverlay';                                         // §6 overlay rules
  jurisdictionId: JurisdictionId; wageRegion: WageRegion;                                    // copied from the template (3.2): §8 payroll, §9 sales tax, §11 tax
  recordsQuality: number;                                                 // 0..1, copied from the template; §4 records review (3.6)
  mapMi: { w: number; h: number }; outletMi: PointMi; roadClass: Access; roadWinterMaintained: boolean;
  town: { name: string; tier: TownTier; positionMi: PointMi /* may lie off the map */; roadMiFromOutlet: number; services: TownServices };
  hub: { name: string; roadMiFromTown: number };
  aquifer?: { wellGpm: [number, number]; depthFt: [number, number] };     // arid: visible regional range
  overlays: LandOverlay[];                                                // visible
  npcHeldBaseline: number;                                                // NPC-held parcels at newGame (3.11 scarcity multiplier)
  hidden: { gradeFactor: number; obFactor: number; finenessMean: number };
  creekIds: CreekId[]; claimIds: ClaimId[];
}
interface LandOverlay { kind: 'withdrawn' | 'specialStatus'; label: string;   // e.g. "Wild & Scenic River corridor", "Conservation Area"
  creekId: CreekId; rowFrom: number; rowTo: number }
interface Creek {
  id: CreekId; districtId: DistrictId; name: string; order: 1 | 2 | 3; parentId: CreekId | null; junctionRow: number | null;
  polylineMi: PointMi[]; rows: number; valleyHalfWidthFt: number; upstreamMiAtRow: number[];   // for water and map
  noTrail: boolean; fishBearing: boolean; anadromous: boolean;                                  // visible (3.4.1)
  hidden: { goldBearing: boolean; gradeFactor: number; obFactor: number; payFactor: number;
            history: CreekHistory | null };                                                    // public record, found by §4 (3.6)
}
interface CreekHistory { histOz: number; histBcy: number; era: [number, number] }   // historic production of the creek, raw oz and yards
interface Claim {
  id: ClaimId; districtId: DistrictId; creekId: CreekId; name: string;      // e.g. "Mosquito Creek No. 4 Above Discovery"
  acres: number; nAlong: number; nAcross: number; blockIdBase: number;     // blockId = blk_(blockIdBase + i*nAcross + j)
  geometry: { rowStart: number; axisOffsetFt: number; centerMi: PointMi; headingDeg: number; lengthFt: number; widthFt: number };
  setting: ListingInfo['setting']; titleKind: 'unpatented' | 'patented' | 'state'; regime: Regime;   // the parcel's legal type; patented → 'private'
                                                                            // (the player's holding is §5 Tenure.kind)
  status: 'open' | 'heldNpc' | 'listed' | 'player' | 'competitor' | 'withdrawn';
  holderId: HolderId | CompetitorId | 'player' | null;
  access: Access; trailMi: number; distanceToTownMi: number;
  visibleFeatures: ListingInfo['visibleFeatures']; improvementsUsd: number;   // cabin, pad, access road left by a recent operator
  env: ClaimEnv;                                                            // visible (3.4.1); read by §6
  water: { sourceKind: WaterSourceKind; baseGpm: number; benchLiftFt: number; nearestFillMi: number;   // 3.3.4
           rightStub?: { priority: 'senior'; gpm: number; source: 'surface' | 'groundwater' };       // recorded right (§6 6.4); shown from P2
           hidden: { wellYieldGpm: number; depthToWaterFt: number } };
  hidden: { depositType: DepositType; oldTimerKind: OldTimerKind; oldTimerEra: [number, number] | null;
            truthPack: string; truthHash: string; trueHistory: TrueSeason[]; publicRecord: PublicRecord;
            permitStub: { status: 'none' | 'noticeOnFile' | 'planApproved'; bondPostedCents: Cents | null };   // truth; §6 instantiates
            econClass: 'uneconomic' | 'marginal' | 'good' | 'excellent' };   // refEconomics at opening spot (3.7); supply only
  listingSeq: number; cooldownUntilTurn: number | null;
}
interface ClaimEnv {
  surfaceCodes: string;            // one char per block in blockIdx order: 'u' upland | 'w' wetland | 'c' channel (§6 404, §7 inStream)
  fishBearing: boolean; specialStatus: boolean; sensitivity: number /*0..1*/; previouslyDisturbed: boolean;
  adjacentClaimIds: ClaimId[];     // shares a block edge (§6 claim groups, §5 association, §12 disputes)
  thawAspectMult: number;          // §7 thaw: bench slope facing north 0.65 … south 1.35; valley bottom 1.0
}
interface TrueSeason { year: number; bcy: number; rawOz: number; blockIdxs: number[] }
interface PublicRecord {                // stored per claim; publicRecord(state, claimId) adds creekHistory from the claim's creek
  oldTimer: { kind: OldTimerKind; era: [number, number]; workedBlockIdxs: number[] } | null;   // null when not on record
  filedSeasons: TrueSeason[]; priorPermits: string[]; inheritedAcres: number; lapses: number[] /* years */;
  priorDrill: OldDrillHole[] | null;    // old churn-drill line, on geology.records.priorDrillP of claims (3.6)
  creekHistory?: CreekHistory | null }  // filled by publicRecord(), not stored on the claim
interface OldDrillHole { blockIdx: number; year: number; reportedGradeOzPerBcy: number; depthToBedrockFt: number | null;
  payThicknessFt: number | null; colorsBySize: Record<SizeClass, number>; volumeMeasuredBcy: number }   // compact SampleResult
```

**What the player sees vs what is true.** The player sees the map geometry (creeks, parcels and their block grids), overlays, status, access, distance, town, water estimates, environmental attributes (`env`), aerial-visible features and the seller's claims. No `hidden` field and no `BlockTruth` value is ever shown. Grade, thickness and ground conditions reach the player only through §4 evidence (samples, records, reviews), the seller's claims (3.10) and, eventually, production.

**Generation order** (each step uses its own named stream, so adding draws in one step never changes another):

```
generateWorld(seed, opts: WorldGenOptions, tuning) -> WorldSlice      // opts.templateIds = setup.world.districtTemplates (§1)
  gp = snapshotGenParams(tuning)                     // stored in world.genParams (D-3.2)
  for d in 0..opts.districtCount-1:
    D  = genDistrict(templates[d], rng(seed,'world','district',d))                    // 3.3: factors, town, road, D.nTarget =
                                                    //   min(U{tpl.parcelsPerDistrict}, floor(geology.world.maxClaims / districtCount))
    N  = genCreekNetwork(D, rng(seed,'world','creeks',D.id))                          // 3.3.1: creeks, overlays, fish
    for C in N.creeks (ID order): C.profile = genCreekProfile(C, D, rng(seed,'world','creek',C.id))   // 3.5.2, transient
    P  = layParcels(D, N, D.nTarget, rng(seed,'world','layout',D.id))                 // 3.4 (+ reserved family run, 3.6.1)
    for K in P (ID order):
      T = genClaimTruth(K, D, rng(seed,'world',D.id,K.id))                            // 3.5
      applyOldTimers(K, T, rng(seed,'world','oldtimers',K.id))                        // 3.6
      K.water = genWater(K, D, rng(seed,'world','water',K.id))                        // 3.3.4 (rightStub drawn last on this stream)
      K.hidden.truthPack = pack(T); K.hidden.truthHash = fnv64(K.hidden.truthPack)    // decode(pack(T)) is canonical
      K.status = assignStatus(K, decode(K.hidden.truthPack), rng(seed,'world','status',K.id))  // 3.4 (open/withdrawn: rightStub cleared)
      K.env = genEnv(K, D, rng(seed,'world','env',K.id))                              // 3.4.1 (needs overlays and old-timer state)
      K.hidden.publicRecord.priorDrill = genPriorDrill(K, decode(K.hidden.truthPack), rng(seed,'world','drill',K.id))   // 3.6
    for C in N.creeks (ID order): C.hidden.history = genCreekHistory(C, D, rng(seed,'world','creekHist',C.id))  // 3.6, after
                                                    //   every claim of D (reads the creek's historic workings)
    assignHolders(D, rng(seed,'world','holders',D.id))                                // 3.10
    D.npcHeldBaseline = count of D's parcels with status 'heldNpc'                    // 3.11
  createInitialListings(world, rng(seed,'supply','init'))                             // 3.11 (P2+: one starter permitted lease per district)
  // creek profiles are discarded: nothing after generation needs them
newGame (after generateWorld): if setup.start = 'inheritor': s = §1 inheritorStreams(seed); genInheritedGroup(state, s.ground, s.pits)   // 3.6.1
                               (then that district's npcHeldBaseline is recomputed without the family run)
```

**RNG streams owned by §3** (§2.3 registry): `'world'` (all generation, sub-keyed as above; §3 is its only user, §10's buyers draw on `'market-buyers'`), `'seller'` (`rng(seed,'seller',claimId,holderId)`: seller evidence and claims), `'seller-tells'` (`rng(seed,'seller-tells',listingId,channel)`), `'supply'` (`rng(seed,'supply',turn)`, plus `rng(seed,'supply',turn,claimId)` for per-claim rolls and `rng(seed,'supply',turn,districtId)` for week-40 NPC staking), and `'site'` (`rng(seed,'site',turn,claimId)` for site visits, keyed by the turn the visit resolves). §3 never calls `rng(…, 'setup', …)` itself: it receives §1's Inheritor streams, `rng(seed,'setup','inheritor')` and its `'pits'` sub-key for the family pit logs, from §1's `inheritorStreams` (§1 1.8.2, D-1.65). `drawSample` takes its stream from the caller. The player's and competitors' samples draw on §4's `'sample'` stream, keyed `(claimId, blockId, methodId, k)` (competitors prefix `cmpId`); §4 owns it.

### 3.2 Region templates

A region template is data (`data/regions/*.ts`) that sets a district's climate, access, town, regime and geology priors. Grade medians are the **median paystreak-centre grade** (`gMed`, raw oz/bcy) *before* paystreak dilution, background mixing and old-timer removal. 3.7 gives the resulting distributions.

**Jurisdictions** (owner ruling 2026-10-05; §6 6.1 maps the real agencies). Districts, creeks, towns and people are fictional, but each template sits in a real jurisdiction: `northernFederal` and `alaskaState` in Alaska, `aridFederal` in Nevada, `yukon` in Yukon; `temperateFederal`'s state is chosen with its P6 overlay (§6 D-6.56).

| Field | `northernFederal` (P1) — interior Alaska BLM, Fortymile/Circle feel | `aridFederal` (P1) — Nevada BLM placer ground |
|---|---|---|
| Climate band / §1 climate template / fire regime | `subarctic` / `northernInterior` / `none` (season dates are §1's: breakup wk 18–20, freeze-up wk 40–44 at 90%, 1.4; ≈ 22-week site season, 19–25) | `arid` / `aridDesert` / `stage` (water-limited; heat and fire Jul–Sep; monsoon floods) |
| Regime / §6 state overlay | `usFederal`; patented share 0.03 of held parcels *with old workings* (≈ 2% of held) → `private` / `northernOverlay` | `usFederal` (same patented rule) / `aridOverlay` |
