|---|---|---|---|
| Climate / §1 template | `temperateMontane` / `temperateMountain`; snow-free May/Jun–Oct; Aug–Sep low flow; fire (`ifpl`) | `subarctic` / `northernInterior`; §1's season: site season ≈ 22 wk, sluicing ≈ 20 (D-1.3) | `subarctic` / `northernYukon`; sluicing 16–24 wk (mean 20) |
| Regime / claim units | usFederal, 20/40/80/160 ac | alaskaState, MTRSC 40/160 ac | yukon, ~23-ac creek claims |
| Jurisdiction / wage region / records quality | `temperateStyle` / `temperate` / 0.8 | `akStyle` / `alaskaState` / 0.75 | `yukon` / `yukon` / 0.85 (YGS placer yearbooks) |
| Access road class | highway 0.5, seasonalRoad 0.5 | highway 0.45, seasonalRoad 0.35, winterTrail 0.10, flyIn 0.10 | highway 0.35, seasonalRoad 0.60, flyIn 0.05 |
| `gMed` / overburden / pay | 0.0080 / 8 ft / 5 ft | 0.0100 / 25 ft (deep muck common) / 6 ft | 0.0105 / 20 ft (Dominion 2–16 m muck) / 6 ft |
| Fineness N(μ, sd), clamp | N(0.78, 0.04), [0.70, 0.85] | N(0.84, 0.02), [0.80, 0.90] | N(0.80, 0.03), [0.70, 0.88] |
| Deposit mix | creek 0.5, bench 0.2, dredgedGround 0.2, hydraulicked bench 0.1 | creek 0.5, deepMuck 0.3, bench 0.1, dredged 0.1 | creek 0.55, bench/White Channel 0.25 (cemented 0.4), dredged 0.20 |
| Old-timers | dredge/hydraulic heavy; drift rare | drift (deep shafts 50–250 ft), dredge | drift 0.5, dredge 0.25 (very high intensity) |
| Bedrock | slate 0.3, granite 0.3, karstLimestone 0.1, basalt 0.3 | schist 0.8, granite 0.2 | schist 0.9, granite 0.1 |

```ts
type RegionTemplateId = 'northernFederal' | 'aridFederal' | 'temperateFederal' | 'alaskaState' | 'yukon';
type ClimateBand = 'subarctic' | 'arid' | 'temperateMontane';
type DepositType = 'creek' | 'bench' | 'deepMuck' | 'dredgedGround' | 'desertFan' | 'gulch';
type BedrockType = 'schist' | 'slatePhyllite' | 'granite' | 'basaltVolcanic' | 'clayFalse' | 'karstLimestone';
type OldTimerKind = 'none' | 'handCut' | 'drift' | 'dredge' | 'dryWash' | 'hydraulic' | 'recentCat';
type TownTier = 'outpost' | 'serviceTown' | 'hubCity';
type ClimateTemplateId = 'northernInterior' | 'aridDesert' | 'northernYukon' | 'temperateMountain';   // §1 owns the climate data
type WaterSourceKind = 'creek' | 'spring' | 'well' | 'ephemeralWash' | 'none';                       // §1 1.5.4 source scaling
type JurisdictionId = 'akStyle' | 'nvStyle' | 'temperateStyle' | 'yukon';      // = §11 TaxJurisdictionId; §8 and §9 key on it too
type WageRegion = 'northern' | 'arid' | 'temperate' | 'alaskaState' | 'yukon';   // §8 wage tables

interface RegionTemplate {
  id: RegionTemplateId; phase: number; climateBand: ClimateBand; climateTemplateId: ClimateTemplateId;
  fireRestrictionRegime: 'none' | 'stage' | 'ifpl'; regime: Regime; stateOverlayId: string;
  jurisdictionId: JurisdictionId; wageRegion: WageRegion; recordsQuality: number;   // copied onto District
  districtRoadMix: Partial<Record<Access, number>>; roadWinterMaintainedP: number; townTierMix: Partial<Record<TownTier, number>>;
  townRoadMi: [number, number]; hubRoadMi: [number, number];
  parcelsPerDistrict: [number, number]; stakedFraction: number /* logistic intercept */; patentedShare: number;
  overlayP: { withdrawn: number; specialStatus: number };
  env: { fishByOrder: [number, number, number]; anadromousP: number; wetlandP: Partial<Record<DepositType, number>> };
  claimSizeMix: Record<number, number>; depositMix: Partial<Record<DepositType, number>>;
  gMed: number; sigma: { district: number; creek: number; rich: number; claim: number; block: number };
  richRangeFt: number; halfWidthMedFt: number; sigHalfWidth: number; wanderSdFt: number; bgRatio: number;
  overburden: { medFt: number; sig: [number, number, number, number, number] };
  pay: { medFt: number; sig: [number, number, number] };
  depositMult: Record<DepositType, { grade: number; ob: number; pay: number; halfWidth: number }>;
  bedrockMix: Partial<Record<BedrockType, number>>; permafrostP: Partial<Record<DepositType, number>>;
  clayMed: number; boulderMed: number; cementMed: number;
  fineness: { mean: number; districtSd: number; claimSd: number; lo: number; hi: number };
  sizeMixPriors: Record<string, [number, number, number, number]>; coarseMg: Record<string, number>;
  verticalDecayFt: Partial<Record<DepositType, number>>; pocketP: number;
  oldTimerMix: Partial<Record<DepositType, Partial<Record<OldTimerKind, number>>>>;
  water: { kind: 'creek'; gpmPerUpstreamMi: number; sig: number }
       | { kind: 'arid'; springP: number; springMedGpm: number; springSig: number; wellMedGpm: number; wellSig: number; depthMedFt: number };
}
```

### 3.3 Districts: map, creek network, town, access, water

#### 3.3.1 District map and creek network

A district is a 12 × 10 mi map area (coordinates in miles; the outlet sits on one edge, where the access road enters). The creek network is a small tree:

```
genDistrict(tpl, r):   gradeFactor = LN(1, σdistrict); obFactor = LN(1, σobDistrict); finenessMean = clamp(N(μ, districtSd), lo, hi)
                       roadClass = pick(districtRoadMix); roadWinterMaintained = roadClass = highway or r.u() < roadWinterMaintainedP
                       town tier, roadMiFromOutlet = U(townRoadMi), hub.roadMiFromTown = U(hubRoadMi); nTarget (3.1, transient)
                       jurisdictionId, wageRegion, recordsQuality = the template's (no draw)
genCreekNetwork(D, r):
  main: order 1, starts at D.outlet, heading into the map ± 30°, length U(6, 9) mi
        polyline in 0.25-mi steps, heading += N(0, 12°) per step, reflected 1 mi inside the map edge
  nTrib = U{3..6} order-2 tributaries at U(0.10, 0.90) of main length (min spacing 0.6 mi), sides alternate,
        angle U(35°, 70°) off the local main heading, length U(1.5, 4) mi
  each tributary: w.p. 0.4 one order-3 branch at U(0.3, 0.8) of its length, length U(0.75, 2) mi
        (≈ 565 valley rows per district → ≈ 56 valley parcels + ≈ 15 bench parcels ≈ nTarget; D-3.33)
  valleyHalfWidthFt: order 1 U(500, 900); order 2 U(250, 500); order 3 U(150, 300)
  goldBearing = r.u() >= geology.world.barrenCreekP (0.20); creek.gradeFactor = goldBearing ? LN(1, σcreek) : barrenCreekFactor (0.15)
  noTrail = order >= 2 and r.u() < geology.world.noTrailCreekP (0.15)
  fishBearing = r.u() < tpl.env.fishByOrder[order−1]; anadromous = order = 1 and fishBearing and r.u() < tpl.env.anadromousP
  rows: creek.rows = ceil(lengthFt / 209); row 0 at the mouth, increasing upstream
  upstreamMi(row) = channel miles above that row, including tributaries above it
  overlays: w.p. overlayP.withdrawn one 'withdrawn' stretch covering 10–25% of the main stem (Wild & Scenic corridor);
            w.p. overlayP.specialStatus one 'specialStatus' stretch covering 15–30% of a random tributary and its branch (NCA, ACEC)
```

In the arid template the "creeks" are dry washes draining to a fan at the outlet. The lower 30% of main-stem rows is `desertFan`; tributaries are `gulch`. The arid special-status overlay covers 20–40% of the fan rows (tortoise-habitat ACEC).

**Overlays follow valid existing rights.** A withdrawal closes *open* ground to new location; claims already held inside it stay valid but are `specialStatus` (§6: no Notice tier, plan plus validity examination). A special-status stretch stays open to staking, but every parcel in it is `specialStatus`. §12's "land opened to entry" event (`landOpened`) calls `openWithdrawnOverlay(state, districtId)`, the single entry point for this effect (R1: the 2025 Alaska d-1 revocations):

```
openWithdrawnOverlay(state, districtId): ClaimId[]
  O = the district's 'withdrawn' overlay (none, or already opened → return [])
  for K in D.claimIds (ID order) with status 'withdrawn' inside O: status = 'open'
  O.kind = 'specialStatus'      // the stretch stays sensitive: claims in it keep env.specialStatus (§6 plan tier)
  return the opened IDs          // §5's staking race reads them as ordinary open parcels; §12 publishes the news
```

#### 3.3.2 Town and services

```ts
interface TownServices { fuel: boolean; partsCounter: boolean; weldingShop: boolean; goldBuyer: boolean;
  airstrip: boolean; clinic: boolean; motel: boolean; laborPoolMult: number }
```

| Tier | Services | `laborPoolMult` (§8) |
|---|---|---|
| outpost | fuel, airstrip, seasonal gold buyer | 0.3 |
| serviceTown | fuel, parts counter (filters, hoses, GET), welding shop, gold buyer, clinic, motel, airstrip | 0.7 |
| hubCity (or adjacent) | all, plus equipment dealers (§9 uses `hub.roadMiFromTown`) | 1.0 |

#### 3.3.3 Claim access and the access factors

Trail distance is the in-district distance from the outlet to the claim along the network: `trailMi = channelMi × geology.world.trailTortuosity (1.2)`. The claim's distance to town is `distanceToTownMi = D.town.roadMiFromOutlet + trailMi`. Access degrades with trail distance:

```
a = D.roadClass
if trailMi > geology.access.trailDegrade1Mi (6):  a = degrade(a)
if trailMi > geology.access.trailDegrade2Mi (18): a = degrade(a)
if creek.noTrail: a = 'flyIn'
degrade: highway → seasonalRoad → winterTrail → flyIn   (arid: capped at seasonalRoad; no winter trail or fly-in)
```

The district access anchors are owned here and apply at a reference distance. They scale with distance by a square root:

```
accessFactors(state, claimId):
  dRef = geology.access[a].refMi
  s = clamp((distanceToTownMi / dRef)^geology.access.distExponent (0.5), 0.6, 1.8)
  distScale          = s                                            // returned for callers that scale a per-class rate by distance
  fuelAdderUsdPerGal = geology.access[a].fuelAdder × s × cpiIndex   // added to §10 dieselRackUsdPerGal; year-1 anchor × CPI
  partsLeadWeeks     = geology.access[a].partsLead × s              // popular brand, nothing in stock; §9 adds brand and hub terms
  mobMult            = geology.access[a].mobMult × s                // ALREADY includes distance
  mobMultClass       = geology.access[a].mobMult                    // class anchor, no distance term
```

Who uses which: §7 site mobilization, §4 contractor mobilization and §6's RCE mobilization line and contractor assessment work use `mobMult` and add no distance term of their own. §9 prices transport miles itself (per-leg costs, 9.5), so it uses `mobMultClass` for per-load fixed handling and `distScale` for air freight; using `mobMult` there would count distance twice.

**Windows belong to §1.** Whether a mode is open in a given week is §1's `accessOpen(state, districtId, mode, week)` (1.4.5). §3 only maps a claim's access class to the modes it uses, and supplies the district data the windows need (`roadWinterMaintained`, the closure hook):

```
claimAccess(state, claimId, turn): { heavyOpen, freightOpen, freightMode: 'road' | 'trail' | 'air' | null }
  highway:      heavy = freight = accessOpen('highway'); freightMode 'road'
  seasonalRoad: heavy = freight = accessOpen('seasonalRoad'); freightMode 'road'   // plus winter closure if !roadWinterMaintained (§1)
  winterTrail:  heavy = accessOpen('winterTrail')
                freight = accessOpen('winterTrail') ∨ accessOpen('flyIn air')      // air always flies when the trail is shut
                freightMode = accessOpen('winterTrail') ? 'trail' : 'air'          // §7 and §9 price 'air' at the flyIn adder
  flyIn:        heavy = accessOpen('winterTrail') (overland cat-train, mob × 1.0) or accessOpen('flyIn barge') where the district
                has a barge river (P6 Yukon; mob × 1.5); freight = accessOpen('flyIn air'); freightMode 'air'
  freightMode = null when freight is closed
  every mode is closed in a week carrying EffectModifier 'geology.access.closed' for the claim's district or claim (§1 applies it)
```

§10's courier and shipment rules use `!claimAccess(state, claimId, turn).freightOpen` as "closed this week" (`accessFactors` carries no weekly state).

| Access | Fuel adder ($/gal) | Parts lead (wk) | Mob mult | refMi | Windows (§1 1.4.5) and notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| highway | 0.35 | 0.5 | 1.0 | 40 | always, except event closures |
| seasonalRoad | 0.90 | 1.0 | 1.4 | 80 | north: closed around breakup (3–6 wk); unmaintained roads also closed from freeze-up + 2 to breakup (Taylor Highway pattern, R2); arid: proposed closure the week after a `storm` week (washout, needs §1) |
| winterTrail | 1.75 | 2.0 (air freight in summer) | 2.2 | 120 | heavy iron and bulk fuel in §1's trail window (typically weeks 2–13 and 50–52); the fuel adder assumes winter-hauled fuel, and summer fuel is air freight at the flyIn adder (§7 tracks tank stock) |
| flyIn | 5.50 | 2.5 | 4.0 | 150 | everything by air; heavy iron overland in the winter-trail window |

Worked example: a northern claim 14 mi up a tributary from a district on a seasonal road, with the town 45 mi from the outlet. It degrades once, to winterTrail, and `distanceToTownMi = 45 + 14 = 59`. Then s = (59/120)^0.5 = 0.70: fuel adder = 1.75 × 0.70 = $1.23/gal (year 1), parts lead 1.4 wk, mob mult 1.54 (class anchor 2.2), and heavy iron arrives only in the trail window (≈ Jan–Mar). In week 30 the trail is shut, so freight goes by air (`freightOpen` true, `freightMode` 'air').

#### 3.3.4 Water

Water truth is fixed per claim: one source kind and one baseline gpm for an **average operating week**. The seasonal shape (breakup flood, early-season high, late-season decline, winter ice) and weekly weather come only from §1's `streamFlowFactor` (D-1.8), so §3 applies no seasonal profile of its own (D-3.20).

```
north:  sourceKind = 'creek'; baseGpm = usableFrac (0.8) × 150 × upstreamMi(claim mid-row) × LN(1, 0.35)   // benches pump from the creek
        benchLiftFt = bench ? U(30, 300) : 0                                             // §7 pump head
arid:   r.u() < 0.20 ? (sourceKind = 'spring', baseGpm = usableFrac × LN(40, 0.5)) : (sourceKind = 'none', baseGpm = 0)
        hidden: wellYieldGpm = clamp(LN(120, 0.8), 5, 1500); depthToWaterFt = clamp(LN(180, 0.5), 30, 800)
        nearestFillMi = distanceToTownMi × U(0.3, 1.0)                                   // §7 water trucking
rightStub (recorded senior water right; the last draws on this stream, recentCat claims only):
        if r.u() < geology.water.rightStubP (north 0.10, arid 0.30):
          creek or spring source: { priority 'senior', gpm: min(lowFlowGpm, U(50, 300)), source 'surface' }
          arid, sourceKind 'none': { priority 'senior', gpm: U(50, 300), source 'groundwater' }   // a pumping right: a well must
                                                                     // still be drilled (§7), and physical draw ≤ wellYieldGpm
        cleared by assignStatus on open or withdrawn parcels and by forfeitToOpen (the right lapses with the claim)

waterAvailableGpm(state, claimId, turn) = baseGpm × sourceScale(sourceKind, sff) × droughtMult
  sourceScale: creek, ephemeralWash → sff;  spring, well → 0.9 + 0.1 × min(sff, 1.5);  none → 0      (§1 1.5.4; sff = WeatherWeek.streamFlowFactor)
  droughtMult = sourceKind ∈ {spring, well} ? Π EffectModifiers('ops.waterAvailableMult', scope) : 1
              // §12 aims the drought hook at springs and wells; creek and wash drought already arrives through §1's sff
  // this is the final physical figure: callers must not multiply by sff or the event modifier again. §7 adds a drilled well
  // (wellYieldGpm × the spring/well scale × effective('ops.waterAvailableMult', claim), §7 7.6.6) and trucked water;
  // §6 caps the draw (maxWaterGpm) and exempts a senior rightStub from curtailment.
lowFlowGpm(claimId)   = baseGpm × geology.water.lowFlowShape[sourceKind] (creek 0.45, spring 0.90)   // §6 water-grant cap; climatological
listedFlowGpm(claimId) = baseGpm × geology.water.listingShape (early 1.40 / mid 0.90 / late 0.75) × LN(1, 0.20) per listing
                         // typical §1 hydrograph values at the three periods; display and §5 waterScore only
```

Example: a claim with 4 upstream channel miles has a raw flow of 600 gpm and a usable baseline of 480 gpm. In June (sff ≈ 1.4) that is ≈ 670 gpm; in a dry late August (sff ≈ 0.6) ≈ 290 gpm; the climatological low flow is 216 gpm. A 50 bcy/hr plant at 15 gpm per bcy/hr needs 750 gpm once-through, so it must recycle all season (§7), and a §6 water grant is capped at 0.8 × 216 = 173 gpm of fresh draw. If the claim had a recent operator and rolled a senior right, its gpm is min(216, U(50, 300)): a right of 216 gpm or less that a drought cannot curtail (§6). §3 gives physical availability and the recorded right only.

### 3.4 Parcel layout and status

```
layParcels(D, N, nTarget, r):
  reserve: in the first northernFederal district only, pick a main-stem rowStart outside every overlay and emit three
           consecutive 20-ac valley parcels there first (the Inheritor's family run, 3.6.1; ordinary parcels in other games);
           the main-stem loop below steps over the reserved rows
  for creek in N (order: main stem, then tributaries by junction row, then branches), stopping once nTarget parcels exist:
    row = U{0..5}
    while row < creek.rows − 4:
      acres = pick(tpl.claimSizeMix); (nAlong, nAcross) = dims(acres, creek.valleyHalfWidthFt)
      emit {creek, rowStart: row, nAlong, nAcross, axisOffsetFt: 0, depositType: valleyType(creek, row)}
      row += nAlong + (r.u() < 0.2 ? U{1..5} : 0)
    if creek.order == 1 or creek.valleyHalfWidthFt >= 400:              // benches
      for side in [−1, +1]: if r.u() < geology.world.benchSideP (0.6):
        on a random stretch covering 30–70% of the creek: 20/40-ac bench parcels, nAcross = 2,
        axisOffsetFt = side × (valleyHalfWidthFt + U(100, 600)), depositType 'bench'
  the 3.3.1 network lays ≈ 71 parcels on average; once nTarget is reached, the remaining creeks in the order above (branches
  first) stay "unlocated" valley (drawn on the map, not stakeable). If all creeks are done and fewer than tpl.parcelsPerDistrict.lo
  exist, bench stretches are added on creek sides that rolled none (main stem first) until the floor is met or sides run out.
valleyType: dredgedGround = contiguous stretches (each 1–3 mi) in the lower 60% of the main stem and the largest tributary, added until
            the dredged share of valley parcels reaches tpl.depositMix.dredgedGround ± 0.05; deepMuck w.p. tpl.depositMix.deepMuck
            (renormalized over valley parcels) per parcel; else creek (arid: desertFan in the lower 30% of main-stem rows, else gulch)
// depositMix shares are targets: benchSideP and bench stretch length are tuned so benches reach their share ± 0.05
```

**Status by selection.** Good ground was staked long ago, so open ground is worse because of *which* parcels stayed open, not because of a flat penalty. Ground whose quality is hard to see (benches, deep muck) is claimed almost at random, which leaves overlooked good ground open.

```
assignStatus(K, T, r):
  PS = blocks with f >= 0.4
  zq = PS empty ? geology.world.zqNoPaystreak (−3) : ln(mean virgin gStreak over PS / tpl.gMed) / 0.5   // "reputation" vs the region
  b  = K.depositType ∈ {bench, deepMuck} ? geology.world.selSlopeOverlooked (0.3) : geology.world.selSlope (1.2)
  pHeld = logistic(logit(tpl.stakedFraction) + b × zq)     // virgin grade already encodes the old-timers' footprint
  status = r.u() < pHeld ? 'heldNpc' : 'open'
  if status = 'open' and K overlaps a 'withdrawn' overlay: status = 'withdrawn'   // held parcels keep valid existing rights
  titleKind = held and oldTimerKind ≠ none and r.u() < tpl.patentedShare ? 'patented' : 'unpatented';  regime = patented ? 'private' : D.regime
  if status ≠ 'heldNpc': K.water.rightStub = undefined                            // no recorded right on unclaimed ground
```

`stakedFraction` is the logistic intercept, not the realized share: barren creeks (zq ≈ −3.8) stay open almost entirely, so the realized held share is ≈ 0.70 north and ≈ 0.57 arid. Held parcels are later split between NPC holders (3.10) and AI competitors (§12 picks 15–25% at newGame, P5).

#### 3.4.1 Environmental attributes (visible; read by §6 and §7)

```
genEnv(K, D, r):
  channel column: valley parcels (not bench) get channelOffsetFt = U(−80, 80) from the valley axis; the one column whose span
                  contains it is 'c' (the active creek or wash bed: §6 404 and fish windows, §7 inStream)
  wetland:        other valley blocks are 'w' w.p. tpl.env.wetlandP[depositType] (north muskeg); arid: the spring's block only
  everything else 'u' (benches, dredge tailings, uplands)          → surfaceCodes
  fishBearing     = creek.fishBearing (the parcel touches the channel)
  specialStatus   = K overlaps any overlay (withdrawn parcels held under valid existing rights, or a special-status stretch)
  previouslyDisturbed = any pre-game Block.state disturbance (3.6) or oldTimerKind ∈ {dredge, handCut, hydraulic, dryWash}
  sensitivity     = clamp(0.10 + 0.30·fishBearing + 0.25·anadromous + 0.25·wetlandShare + 0.20·specialStatus + N(0, 0.05), 0, 1)
  adjacentClaimIds = parcels sharing a block edge (same creek and touching rows, or a bench beside a valley parcel on shared rows)
  northness       = cos(direction the bench slope faces, toward the creek: headingDeg + side·90° + 180°)   // +1 faces north
  thawAspectMult  = bench ? 1 − 0.35 × northness : 1.0                                                   // 0.65 … 1.35
```

Example: a 20-ac valley parcel on a fish-bearing (not anadromous) main stem with 4 of its 15 non-channel blocks wetland: sensitivity ≈ 0.10 + 0.30 + 0.25 × 4/20 = 0.45. Working the channel column needs a 404 individual permit (fish-bearing), and the wetland blocks need 404 fill coverage too, so a player who mines only the upland blocks avoids it at the cost of the paystreak if it hugs the creek. That is a real §6 trade-off generated here.

### 3.5 The block model: true geology per block

#### 3.5.1 Truth and state shapes

```ts
interface BlockTruth {                     // hidden; decoded from claim.hidden.truthPack
  overburdenFt: number;                    // waste above pay (muck + barren gravel), ft, 0..120
  payThicknessFt: number;                  // pay gravel above bedrock, ft, 1..15
  bedrockCleanupFt: number;                // bedrock that must be ripped and washed to get its gold, ft
  gradeOzPerBcy: number;                   // CURRENT raw (metal) oz per bcy of the pay column (pay + bedrock cleanup), net of old-timer removal
  virginGradeOzPerBcy: number;             // before old-timers (drives records and old reports, never mining)
  sizeMix: Record<SizeClass, number>;      // current gold mass shares, sum 1
  coarseMeanMg: number;                    // mean coarse-particle mass (claim header, same for every block of the claim)
  fineness: number;                        // alloy fineness (fine oz per metal oz), 0.70..0.92
  permafrost: number; clay: number; boulders: number; cementation: number;   // 0..1
  bedrockType: BedrockType; bedrockGoldShare: number;   // share of the column's gold inside the bedrock cleanup zone
  verticalDecayFt: number;                 // λg: gravel gold density ∝ exp(−h/λg), h = height above bedrock
  paystreakFraction: number;               // f: share of the block width inside the paystreak, 0..1
  minedOutFraction: number;                // share of virgin gold actually removed by old-timers (descriptive; = 1 − grade/virgin)
  pocket?: { bcy: number; gradeOzPerBcy: number };      // sub-block rich body (included in gradeOzPerBcy)
  oldTailings?: { bcy: number; gradeOzPerBcy: number; sizeMix: Record<SizeClass, number> };  // pile on the surface
}
interface BlockState {                     // stored sparsely: world.blockStates[blockId] only once touched
  strippedBcy: number; minedBcy: number; sampledBcy: number; oldTailingsTakenBcy: number;
  disturbed: boolean; disturbedTurn?: number; disturbanceOrigin: 'player' | 'inherited' | 'historic';
  reclaimed: boolean; thawProgress: number;   // ft thawed below the current surface (§7 advances it)
}
```

Derived per block: `payBcy = (payThicknessFt + bedrockCleanupFt) × 1613`, `overburdenBcy = overburdenFt × 1613 + (oldTailings?.bcy − oldTailingsTakenBcy if not processed)`. Contained gold now is `gradeOzPerBcy × (payBcy − minedBcy − sampledBcy)`. **Consumers must not multiply by `(1 − minedOutFraction)` again** (D-3.4). Block coordinates for the grid, the map and §7 haul distance: `blockCoords(blockId) = { claimId, i, j }`, i along the valley (0 = downstream end, increasing upstream), j across (0 = left bank looking upstream); 4-adjacency is |Δi| + |Δj| = 1.

#### 3.5.2 Creek profiles (along-valley structure shared across claims)

Each creek carries 1D processes on its rows. `AR1(n, range, σ)` is a stationary Gaussian AR(1) series with z₀ ~ N(0,1), zᵢ = ρ zᵢ₋₁ + √(1−ρ²) εᵢ, ρ = exp(−209 / range), and output σ·z.

```
richLog[row]  = AR1(rows, tpl.richRangeFt (3,000 north), σrich (0.28))        // rich and poor stretches spanning claims
centerFt[row] = AR1(rows, 2,000 ft, tpl.wanderSdFt (140)), clamped to ±max(0, valleyHalfWidthFt − halfWidthFt[row])   // wanders off the creek
hwLog[row]    = AR1(rows, 1,500 ft, tpl.sigHalfWidth (0.40));  halfWidthFt = tpl.halfWidthMedFt × depositMult.halfWidth × exp(hwLog)
obLog[row]    = AR1(rows, 2,500 ft, σobAR (0.25))
payLog[row]   = AR1(rows, 1,500 ft, σpayAR (0.15))
junction boost: for each gold-bearing tributary joining at parent row k: richLog[k−7 .. k] += geology.world.junctionBoostLog (0.25)
                (the 7 rows ≈ 1,500 ft just downstream of the junction)
proximal flag: rows in the top 30% of a creek, and all order-3 creeks → proximal size-mix prior; otherwise mid-reach
```

#### 3.5.3 Block grade: hierarchy, paystreak, correlation, pockets

```
Per claim K (rng(seed,'world',D.id,K.id)), draws in this order:
  claimGrade = LN(1, σclaim) × depositMult.grade         // bench 0.8, deepMuck 1.3 (old-timers couldn't reach it), others 1.0
  claimOb    = LN(1, σobClaim) × depositMult.ob           // bench 2.5, deepMuck 2.8, others 1.0
  // depositMult.pay = 1.0 for every P1 type; depositMult.halfWidth: bench 2.0, others 1.0 (values as calibrated in 3.7)
  bedrockType = pick(tpl.bedrockMix); B0, s0 = BEDROCK[bedrockType]
  sizeMixK = normalize(prior_k × LN(1, 0.25)) per class; coarseMeanMg = tpl.coarseMg[setting] × LN(1, 0.3)
  finenessK = clamp(D.finenessMean + N(0, tpl.fineness.claimSd), lo, hi); λg = tpl.verticalDecayFt[dep] × U(0.75, 1.25)
  frozenDegree = r.u() < clamp(tpl.permafrostP[dep] × (bench ? 1 + 0.6 × northness : 1), 0, 0.95) ? U(0.6, 1.0) : 0   // 3.4.1
  clayK = min(1, LN(tpl.clayMed, 0.6)); bouldersK = min(1, LN(tpl.boulderMed × settingMult, 0.6)); cementK = min(1, LN(cementMed, 0.5))
      settingMult: proximal 1.5, gulch 1.4, desertFan 0.6, bench 0.8, else 1.0
  field z[i][j] (separable AR, unit variance):
      ρa = exp(−209 / geology.grade.blockRangeAlongFt (700)) = 0.742;  ρc = exp(−209 / geology.grade.blockRangeAcrossFt (120)) = 0.175
      for each row i: u[j] = AR(1) across j with ρc;  z[i][j] = (i == 0) ? u[j] : ρa·z[i−1][j] + √(1−ρa²)·u[j]
      → Corr(z[i][j], z[i'][j']) = ρa^|i−i'| · ρc^|j−j'|

  for i in 0..nAlong−1, j in 0..nAcross−1 (row-major):
    row = K.rowStart + i
    x   = K.axisOffsetFt + (j − (nAcross − 1)/2) × 209                 // block centre, ft from the valley axis
    d   = x − (bench ? K.axisOffsetFt : 0) − centerFt[row]             // offset from the paystreak centreline
    f   = max(0, min(d + 104.5, halfWidthFt[row]) − max(d − 104.5, −halfWidthFt[row])) / 209
    gStreak = tpl.gMed × D.gradeFactor × C.gradeFactor × exp(richLog[row]) × claimGrade × exp(σblock × z[i][j])   // no difficulty term (D-3.18)
    g = f × gStreak + (1 − f) × gStreak × tpl.bgRatio                  // block mean mixes paystreak and valley fill
    OB = clamp(tpl.ob.medFt × D.obFactor × C.obFactor × exp(obLog[row]) × claimOb
               × (1 + 0.3 × exp(−((x − K.axisOffsetFt)/400)²)) × LN(1, σobBlock), 0, 120)   // muck thickest on the valley axis
    T  = clamp(tpl.pay.medFt × C.payFactor × exp(payLog[row]) × depositMult.pay × (0.7 + 0.3 f) × LN(1, σpayBlock), 1, 15)
    Bc = B0 × U(0.8, 1.2);  bedrockGoldShare = s0 × U(0.8, 1.2)
    payBcy = (T + Bc) × 1613
    if f >= 0.4 and r.u() < pocketP:                                   // rare rich pocket
      pocket = { bcy: min(U(300, 3000), 0.5 × payBcy), grade: clamp(gStreak × LN(15, 0.5), 0.15, 2.0) }
      g = (g × (payBcy − pocket.bcy) + pocket.grade × pocket.bcy) / payBcy
    sizeMix = normalize(sizeMixK with coarse × (0.5 + 0.5 f), each class × LN(1, 0.10))   // coarse gold stays in the channel
    fineness = clamp(finenessK + N(0, 0.006), lo, hi)
    permafrost = frozenDegree > 0 ? clamp(frozenDegree + N(0, 0.08), 0, 1) : (climate subarctic ? 0.15 × r.u() : 0)
    clay = clamp(clayK + N(0, 0.05), 0, 1) (clayFalse bedrock: ≥ 0.4); boulders = clamp(bouldersK + N(0, 0.05), 0, 1)
    cementation = clamp(cementK + N(0, 0.05), 0, 1)
    virginGrade = g; minedOutFraction = 0
```

| `BEDROCK` | Cleanup depth B0 (ft) | Gold share in cleanup zone s0 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| schist | 1.5 | 0.20 | foliated and fractured; gold 1–3 ft into cracks |
| slatePhyllite | 2.5 | 0.30 | steep cleavage acts as natural riffles |
| granite | 1.0 | 0.10 | weathers to grus; gold stays near the top |
| basaltVolcanic | 0.7 | 0.08 | smooth, poor trap |
| clayFalse | 0.3 | 0.12 | gold sits *on* the clay, partway up the column |
| karstLimestone (P6) | 3.0 | 0.35 | deep natural riffles |

#### 3.5.4 Vertical gold profile (used by sampling, cleanup depth and old-timers)

Height h is measured in ft above the bedrock surface (h = 0); the gravel spans 0..T and the bedrock zone −B..0. The cumulative share of the column's gold below height h is:

```
G(h) = s_b + (1 − s_b) × (1 − e^(−min(h,T)/λg)) / (1 − e^(−T/λg))                  for 0 ≤ h ≤ T
G(h) = s_b − s_b × (1 − e^(−min(B,−h)/λb)) / (1 − e^(−B/λb))                       for −B ≤ h < 0
       s_b = bedrockGoldShare, λg = verticalDecayFt, λb = geology.vertical.bedrockDecayFt (0.6 ft)
interface VerticalProfile { Tg: number; B: number; sb: number; lambdaG: number; lambdaB: number }   // T = Tg in G(h) above
profileOf(bt) = { Tg: payThicknessFt, B: bedrockCleanupFt, sb: bedrockGoldShare, lambdaG: verticalDecayFt,
                  lambdaB: geology.vertical.bedrockDecayFt }
verticalGoldShareProfile(p, h1, h2) = G_p(h2) − G_p(h1);        verticalGoldShare(bt, h1, h2) = verticalGoldShareProfile(profileOf(bt), h1, h2)
positionMultProfile(p, h1, h2) = verticalGoldShareProfile(p, h1, h2) / ((h2 − h1) / (Tg + B))   // grade of an interval ÷ block mean
positionMult(bt, h1, h2) = positionMultProfile(profileOf(bt), h1, h2)
// §4 evaluates positionMultProfile on its expected profiles; drawSample and §7 use the BlockTruth forms. One implementation.
trace gold in overburden: obGrade = geology.vertical.obGradeRatio (0.03) × gradeOzPerBcy   // sampling only: lets an overburden
                          // pan show the odd colour; not counted in contained gold or in §7's accounting (overburden is barren there)
```

Worked example (T = 6, B = 1.5, s_b = 0.20, λg = 2.0): if §7 cleans only 0.5 ft of the 1.5-ft bedrock zone, it leaves `0.20 × (1 − (1 − e^(−0.83))/(1 − e^(−2.5)))` = 0.20 × 0.38 = **7.7% of the block's gold** in the ground. Skipping bedrock cleanup entirely leaves 20%. That is the bedrock-cleanup trade-off: ripping wears equipment but recovers the gold that sits in bedrock.

### 3.6 Old-timer workings and pre-game history

Each parcel gets an `OldTimerKind` from the template mix (3.2). Old-timers took the **richest** paystreak blocks: let PS be the blocks with f ≥ 0.4, sorted by virgin grade, descending.

| Kind | Era (records) | Blocks affected | Extraction x (share of virgin gold removed) | Side effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| drift | 1898–1930 | top U(40%, 80%) of PS, each w.p. 0.8 | `bottomShare × U(0.6, 0.9)`, where bottomShare = G(5 ft) − G(−1 ft) ≈ 0.70–0.85 | winter-dump tailings pile; λg × 2 and s_b × 0.6 (bottom pay gone) |
| handCut | 1898–1940 | top 30% of PS with OB < 10 ft | U(0.5, 0.8) | tailings pile |
| dredge | 1920–1962 | every block with f > 0.05 on the dredged stretch | U(0.80, 0.92) | OB → 0, permafrost → 0, boulders × 0.3, λg → 6.0; remaining gold mostly fine or in bedrock below dredge depth (s_b → max(s_b, 0.5)) |
| dryWash (arid) | 1930–1942 | top 50% of PS | U(0.10, 0.30) (upper 2–3 ft only) | small dry-wash reject piles, fine gold |
| hydraulic (P6) | 1870–1900 | benches | U(0.5, 0.8) | OB reduced, huge tailings fans downstream |
| recentCat | 1985–2018 | top U(15%, 50%) of the PS blocks not already depleted | the whole column is **mined** (`Block.state`) | production history, own tailings, possible inherited liability |

```
deplete(b, x, w):          // w = size weights: drift/handCut/dryWash [1.3, 1.1, 0.7, 0.3]; dredge [1.1, 1.05, 0.9, 0.6]; x ≤ 0.92
  removed_k = min(0.95 × mix_k, c × w_k × mix_k), with c found by water-filling so that Σ_k removed_k = x exactly
            // sort classes by w_k; classes that hit the 0.95 cap pass their excess to the rest; always feasible since x ≤ 0.95
  b.sizeMix = normalize(mix_k − removed_k); b.minedOutFraction = x; b.gradeOzPerBcy = b.virginGradeOzPerBcy × (1 − x)
  // a second depletion of the same block (3.6.1) removes Δ of the *virgin* gold: x' = min(0.92, x + Δ), applied as
  // deplete(b, (x' − x)/(1 − x), w) on the current mix, then minedOutFraction = x'
tailingsPile(b, x, histRec ~ U(0.60, 0.85)):
  removedOz = x × virginGrade × payBcy;  lostOz = removedOz × (1 − histRec)
  pileBcy = drift: 5 × 1613 × U(0.4, 0.7) | handCut: payBcy × U(0.3, 0.6) | dryWash: 2 × 1613 × U(0.2, 0.5)
  b.oldTailings = { bcy: pileBcy, gradeOzPerBcy: lostOz / pileBcy, sizeMix: [0.05, 0.20, 0.45, 0.30] }
```

Worked example (drift). Virgin grade 0.030 oz/bcy, T + B = 7.5 ft, so payBcy = 12,098 and the block held 363 oz. With bottomShare 0.75 and extraction 0.75, x = 0.56 and 203 oz were removed. With hand recovery of 75%, 51 oz were lost to a dump of 5 × 1,613 × 0.55 = 4,436 bcy, which grades **0.0115 oz/bcy** (fine gold). The in-place grade left is 0.030 × 0.44 = **0.0132**. At $4,200 both the drifted ground and its dump can be worth mining. Old cutoffs were 5–50× today's, and old recovery lost the fines.

**Recent operators (`recentCat`).** Their mined blocks get the pre-game state `minedBcy = payBcy, strippedBcy = overburdenBcy, disturbed = true`. `disturbanceOrigin` is `'inherited'` if the season year is ≥ `geology.oldTimer.liabilityEraYear` (1981, when 43 CFR 3809 began) and otherwise `'historic'`. `reclaimed` is set w.p. 0.45. One recovery model drives both the history and the losses: per size class, `rec_k = geology.oldTimer.recentCapture [0.93, 0.85, 0.55, 0.20]_k × opSkill`, with `opSkill ~ U(0.85, 1.0)` per operator; recovered = Σ contained_k × rec_k (≈ 0.63–0.74 of contained for a mid-reach mix), and `lost_k = contained_k − recovered_k` becomes a tailings pile on the same block with `bcy = payBcy × U(0.6, 0.9)` (the rest went back as backfill). If the operator's last season is ≥ startYear − 6, w.p. 0.25 they also pre-stripped 1–3 further paystreak blocks (`strippedBcy = overburdenBcy`, `disturbed = true`, `thawProgress = U(3, 6)` ft, drained ground thawed over the intervening summers). These blocks are a real asset on a listing. **True history:** blocks are grouped 1–3 per season, starting in a year U{1985..2018} with occasional gaps. Each season records `{year, bcy: Σ payBcy, rawOz: Σ recovered}`. Because recent operators mined the best blocks, an *honest* history overstates what is left. That trap needs no dishonesty. **Improvements:** a recent operator leaves `improvementsUsd = LN(25,000, 0.6)` (cabin, pad, access trail), × 0.4 if the last season is before startYear − 15; others 0.

**Historic disturbance** needs no `Block.state`: `historicAcres` = blocks with minedOutFraction > 0 under `dredge`, `handCut`, `hydraulic` or `dryWash` (surface workings; drift leaves only shafts and dumps). It is nobody's liability; the player's first strip of such a block makes it `'player'` disturbance (§6/§7).

**Public record** (what §4's records review can find; `publicRecord(state, claimId)`; §4 decides what a reviewer finds):
- **Old-timer footprint** w.p. 0.7: kind, era and `workedBlockIdxs` (the blocks with minedOutFraction > 0 from a historic kind; for `recentCat`, the mined blocks).
- **Filed production:** agency filings for each true post-1990 season w.p. 0.8 each (including the Inheritor family's seasons, 3.6.1).
- **Prior permits, post-1981 disturbance acres, claim lapses.**
- **Creek history** (shared by every claim on the creek; null for barren creeks and for creeks with no historic workings). Drawn after all of the district's claims on `rng(seed,'world','creekHist',C.id)` from the creek's real old-timer footprint:

  ```
  W = worked blocks of every parcel on C whose oldTimerKind ∈ {handCut, drift, dredge, dryWash, hydraulic}
  histBcy = Σ_W (drift ? 6 × 1613 : payBcy)                  // drifters hoisted only the bottom 5 ft of gravel + 1 ft of bedrock
  creekMedianGrade = tpl.gMed × D.gradeFactor × C.gradeFactor  // median virgin paystreak-centre grade of the creek
  histOz = histBcy × geology.records.historicGradeRatio (2.5) × creekMedianGrade × LN(1, geology.records.creekProdLogSd (0.5))
  era = [min era start, max era end] over the kinds present
  ```

  The ratio 2.5 is the selection effect: old-timers mined only the richest ground, at cutoffs 5–50× today's. §4 enters it as a creek-mean observation with log-sd 0.5 (both keys are §3's; §4 reads them).
- **Old drill logs** on `geology.records.priorDrillP` (0.10) of claims: one churn-drill line across the valley at a random row i0, `U{3..8}` holes, one per block across (j = 0, 1, …), wrapping to row i0 + 1 when the holes outnumber the columns, year `U{1935..1985}`, drawn with `drawSample` in `fullColumn` mode using §4's `churnHistoric` method parameters (snapshotted in `genParams`, D-3.2) on `rng(seed,'world','drill',K.id)`, and stored as compact `OldDrillHole` summaries. These are pre-game: they change no `Block.state` and book no gold.
- **Records quality.** `recordsQuality(state, claimId) = District.recordsQuality × (claim.access = 'flyIn' ? geology.records.flyInQualityMult (0.5) : 1)`: north 0.8 (0.4 on fly-in ground), arid 0.7. §4 multiplies its find probability by it.

Drift shafts and their winter dumps are overgrown and are **not** visible from the air (a site visit finds them); hand-cut, dry-wash and hydraulic piles, dredge tailings and recent disturbance are (3.9). That is what makes drift the hidden old-timer kind in §4's prior.

#### 3.6.1 Inherited family ground (§1 Inheritor start)

§1 1.8.2 fixes what is inherited: three contiguous 20-ac unpatented valley claims (60 blocks) in the P1 northern district, a hidden quality tier drawn from `game.inheritorTierWeights` {excellent 0.07, good 0.30, marginal 0.38, uneconomic 0.25}, extra depletion `game.inheritorDepletionAdd` (+0.10), `game.inheritor.preStrippedBlocks` (2) paystreak blocks the family stripped in its last season, an optimistic family ledger for 2013–2024 (twelve seasons ending three before the 2027 start) and four old pit logs. All of it runs inside `newGame`, before the first turn, so truth stays immutable afterwards.

```
genInheritedGroup(state, r, rPits):   // received from §1 inheritorStreams: r = ground (rng(seed,'setup','inheritor')), rPits = pits
  G = the reserved run of three 20-ac parcels (3.4); status 'player', holderId 'player', tenure created by §5 (origin 'inherited')
  family mining (volume first, independent of grade): seasons 2013..2024; each season digs bcy_s = LN(6,000, 0.5) from the
      best remaining paystreak block of G (partial blocks allowed): minedBcy, strippedBcy pro rata, disturbed, origin 'inherited',
      reclaimed false; losses to a tailings pile as for recentCat
  depletionAdd: each f ≥ 0.4 block of G that the family did not dig gets the second-depletion rule of deplete() with Δ = 0.10,
      handCut weights (bedrock sniping and high-grading around the cuts)
  pre-strip: the game.inheritor.preStrippedBlocks (2) undug f ≥ 0.4 blocks of G with the highest current grade get the recentCat
      pre-strip state: strippedBcy = overburdenBcy, disturbed = true, origin 'inherited', thawProgress = U(3, 6) ft (2024 strip,
      drained over the 2025–26 summers; consistent with geology.oldTimer.preStripMaxAgeYr 6)
  tier conditioning: tier = pick(tierWeights); if refEconomics(G as one property).class ≠ tier, scale every grade of G
      (current, virgin, pocket, tailings) by k ∈ [0.25, 4], found by bisection (≤ 16 steps; CDV rises monotonically in k) to hit
      the tier's target CDV: uneconomic −$75k | marginal +$300k | good +$1.2M | excellent +$4.0M; for good and excellent, k is the
      smallest value meeting both the CDV target and the 3.7 margin floor (margin also rises with k). refEconomics counts only
      remaining overburden, so the pre-stripped blocks are part of the value being conditioned
  family history: recovered_s from the scaled grades; trueHistory = the twelve seasons; each season enters publicRecord.filedSeasons
      w.p. 0.8 (post-1990 rule, so §4's records review can find filedProduction); ledger shown = §3 'optimistic' transform:
      rawOz_s × U(1.2, 1.6), basis 'unspecified'
  family pit logs: 4 × drawSample(sellerPit3, 3.10.2) on 4 distinct f ≥ 0.4 blocks of G (on rPits), year U{2013..2024},
      lab 'local' → §4 'familyRecords' evidence (zero weight until verified, §4)
  permitStub: planApproved on all three claims of G (one plan, last worked in 2024), with one $6,000 cash bond for the run
      (bondPostedCents on the lowest claim ID, null on the others); §6 6.12 builds the Inheritor package from it in P2+
  re-pack G's truth (new truthHash), recompute econClass
```

Example: the run's raw class is good (CDV $0.9M) but the tier roll says marginal. Bisection finds k ≈ 0.78, which leaves CDV ≈ $300k. Twelve family seasons of ≈ 6,000 bcy at ≈ 0.011 oz/bcy recovered ≈ 45 raw oz a year, shown in the ledger as 55–70 oz. Grades stay inside the creek's own range, and an honest-looking ledger still overstates what is left, as the brief's Inheritor intends. The tier targets are positions inside each class (just below zero, mid-marginal, 1.6× the good floor, 1.33× the excellent floor), so they did not move when the yardstick gained its frozen-ground wash term (3.7, D-3.36). On the frozen family run the same targets now need a median 6–11% larger k (preflight generator, 300 runs per tier), so a "good" family run is good for the engine too.

### 3.7 Distribution targets and calibration

**Yardstick.** The classes are defined against a *reference operator* (truth-based, used only by the simulator, tests and the dev reveal). It runs a sluice-only plant at $4,200 and mines exactly the blocks that pay:

```
refEconomics(K, T):  (only blocks not already mined; partly mined blocks count their remaining pay and overburden)
  R_b    = Σ_k sizeMix_k × capture_k(§7 sluice-only anchors 0.95/0.88/0.62/0.25) × (1 − 0.15 × clay)
  rev_b  = payBcy × g × R_b × fineness × spot (4,200) × payable (0.95)
  cost_b = overburdenBcy × stripUsd × (1 + 0.6 × permafrost + 0.5 × cementation)
         + payBcy × washUsd × (1 + 0.3 × boulders + 0.3 × clay + geology.refEcon.frozenWashAdd (0.40) × permafrost)
         north: stripUsd 2.50, washUsd 12.00 | arid: stripUsd 2.20, washUsd 14.00 (water)
         // frozenWashAdd charges frozen pay for the throughput the engine loses digging and thawing it (§7): it sets the yardstick's
         // frozen (0.8) / thawed break-even ratio at strip 3:1 to 1.36, against the engine's 1.38 ± 0.05 (§7 fixture; D-3.36)
  mined set M = { b : rev_b > cost_b }
  CDV    = Σ_M (rev_b − cost_b) − devBase (north $150k, arid $120k) − devPerAcre ($8k / $7k) × |M|
  margin = Σ_M (rev_b − cost_b) / Σ_M rev_b
  class  = CDV ≤ 0 → uneconomic | CDV ≥ $3.0M and margin ≥ 0.60 → excellent | CDV ≥ $0.75M and margin ≥ 0.40 → good | else marginal
```

Check against the reference northern operation: 60,000 bcy washed at a 3.3:1 strip costs $1.29M on thawed ground, at the top of the anchor's $0.9–1.3M, and $1.76M on frozen ground (permafrost 0.8), before royalties and debt. The frozen figure is not a cash cost: it folds the yards the engine fails to wash on frozen ground into a cost per yard, so that class boundaries on frozen ground match what the engine pays. The yardstick is deliberately conservative, and the dev costs come on top.

Worked block (north): OB 15 ft, T 5 ft, B 1.5 ft → payBcy 10,485, obBcy 24,195 (strip 2.3:1). g = 0.012, mix 25/40/27/8 → R = 0.777 × 0.978 = 0.760; fineness 0.86; permafrost 0.8, clay 0.15, boulders 0.2. Revenue = 10,485 × 0.012 × 0.760 × 0.86 × 4,200 × 0.95 = **$328k**. Cost = 24,195 × 2.50 × 1.48 + 10,485 × 12.00 × (1 + 0.06 + 0.045 + 0.32) = $89.5k + $179.3k = **$268.8k**. Margin $59k (18%); the block breaks even at 0.0098 oz/bcy (0.0084 before the frozen wash term). The same block thawed breaks even at 0.0073.

**Calibrated results.** These are 40 generated districts per template (≈ 4,000 parcels each), with the selection of 3.4 and the steady-state listing pool of 3.11 (pool weight ∝ held count × inflowMult × mean listing life; `listingPoolWeights` exposes it for §4's listing-pool calibration). The calibration harness implements the pseudo-code above, including barren creeks (0.20 at ×0.15) and junction boosts; it simplifies the network to independent creeks (3.21). The north rows include the frozen wash term: they are the harness values shifted by the change the term makes in the preflight generator (an independent implementation of the same pseudo-code, same 40 districts per template). The term does not touch arid ground (no permafrost).

| Population | Uneconomic | Marginal | Good | Excellent | Target (listing pool) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| North, all parcels | 73.2% | 18.3% | 7.0% | 1.5% | |
| North, held (staked) | 66.4% | 22.3% | 9.3% | 2.0% | |
| North, open ground | 88.9% | 9.3% | 1.6% | 0.2% | |
| **North, listing pool** | **73.1%** | **20.5%** | **5.6%** | **0.8%** | 60–72 / 18–30 / 5–10 / 0.7–2.5 |
| North, listing pool, preflight generator (cross-check) | 64.0% | 25.4% | 9.1% | 1.5% | same |
| Arid, all parcels | 68.7% | 21.9% | 8.3% | 1.1% | |
| Arid, held (staked) | 57.5% | 27.5% | 13.0% | 1.9% | |
| Arid, open ground | 83.5% | 14.4% | 2.1% | 0.1% | |

The two implementations sit either side of the 72% uneconomic ceiling. The frozen wash term moved the north pool by +3.1 / −1.6 / −1.1 / −0.3 points, which puts this harness one point over the ceiling while the preflight generator sits at 64%. Neither grade median changes now (D-3.36): `gMed` feeds §4's worked prior examples, and the P0 full-generator run (BALANCE T-02, 3.18) decides. If the north pool's uneconomic share exceeds 72% there, north `gMed` rises in 5% steps (≈ −1.1 points each). If arid good exceeds 10% with §7's arid water change (D-7.37) in place, arid `gMed` 0.0062 → 0.0056 (preflight at × 0.9: 66.6% uneconomic; BALANCE §9.2).
