|---|---|---|---|
| Median paystreak-block (f ≥ 0.4) grade per claim, p10 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p90 | 0.0013 / 0.0030 / 0.0057 / 0.0094 / 0.0145 | 0.0012 / 0.0027 / 0.0049 / 0.0080 / 0.0125 | "most claims 0.004–0.012" holds for ≈ p35–p85 |
| Grade of economically mined blocks, bcy-weighted, p10 / p50 / p90 / p99 | 0.010 / 0.016 / 0.034 / 0.086 | 0.010 / 0.016 / 0.035 / 0.090 | brief 0.005–0.03, rare rich pockets |
| Strip ratio, whole claim p10 / p50 / p90 | 1.9 / 4.1 / 10.3 | 0.7 / 1.5 / 3.6 | R3 north 2–10:1; desert 0.5–3:1 |
| Strip ratio, mined blocks p10 / p50 / p90 | 1.7 / 3.2 / 7.6 | 0.6 / 1.3 / 2.9 | R3 typical 3–6:1 north |
| Median contained raw oz in mined blocks: marginal / good / excellent | 620 / 1,790 / 3,550 | 460 / 1,340 / 3,730 | R2: 300–700 oz/yr typical operation |
| Open overlooked ground (bench + deep muck) that is economic | 16% (vs 9% of open creek ground) | 29% (vs 15%) | |
| Share uneconomic by claim size (held claims): 20 / 40 / 80 / 160 ac | 71 / 67 / 62 / 49% | 66 / 55 / 49 / 31% | larger groups dilute the fixed development cost |

**Listed-claim prior.** Adverse selection makes the listing pool poorer than the held stock, so `visiblePrior(..., 'listed')` uses its own multiplier: `geology.prior.statusMult.listed` = (geometric-mean paystreak grade of the steady-state listing pool) ÷ (that of held claims). The preflight generator measures 0.93 north and 0.92 arid; the default is **0.92** for both, and the P0 harness resets it (3.18). The pool's spread of log grade is slightly narrower than the held stock's (−0.03 to −0.05 in log variance), so `geology.prior.listedSigmaAdj` stays 0 (the prior stays a little wide, which is the safe side for §4's coverage gate).

Truth is identical across difficulty levels (D-3.18), so these numbers hold for every difficulty. The simulator test (3.18) checks the listing-pool shares and these grade and strip bands on 200 seeded worlds.

### 3.8 The sample-draw model: `drawSample`

**Contract.** `drawSample(bt: BlockTruth, bs: BlockState, req: SampleRequest, m: SampleMethodParams, rng): SampleResult` is pure. It never mutates state. The caller (§4 programs) applies `extractedBcy` to `Block.state.sampledBcy` (or to `oldTailingsTakenBcy` for a tailings sample) and books the gold lines below; §3's own draws of pre-game sampling (seller evidence, old drill logs, family pit logs) apply nothing. §3 owns the physics; §4's method table supplies `SampleMethodParams`. The guide's sketch `drawSample(block, volumeBcy, method, rng)` is refined so that the block state (stripping, thaw) and the request details (interval, open cut, target) are explicit inputs rather than hidden lookups (D-3.34).

```ts
interface SampleMethodParams {               // values owned by §4's method table
  id: string;
  positionMode: 'exposure' | 'pit' | 'fullColumn' | 'interval';
  exposureDepthFrac?: number;                // 'exposure': sampled share of the gravel top (default 0.4)
  maxDepthFt: number | null;                 // excavator reach, hand-pit depth; null = unlimited (drills)
  frozenOk: boolean;                         // drills, or pits with ripping; else stops at thaw depth
  bedrockPenFt: number;                      // bedrock taken into the sample
  captureBySize: Record<SizeClass, number>;  // processing capture of the sample (pans lose ultrafine)
  volumeCv: number; weighCv: number;         // measurement noise (multiplicative, mean 1)
  geomCv: number;                            // depth logging error
  thickCv?: number;                          // pay-thickness logging error; default 0.10 (§4 fills it per method)
  biasMult: number;                          // systematic bias (RC fine-gold smearing < 1), default 1
}
interface SampleRequest { blockId: BlockId; volumeBcy: number; interval?: { h1: number; h2: number }; fromOpenCut?: boolean;
  target?: 'inSitu' | 'oldTailings';          // default inSitu; old dumps and tailings piles are a classic cheap target
  samplerCaptureMult?: number /* §4/§8 skill, default 1 */ }
interface SampleResult {
  blockId: BlockId; methodId: string; volumeBcy: number; volumeMeasuredBcy: number;
  intervalDepthFt: [number, number] | null;  // below surface, for display
  reachedPay: boolean; reachedBedrock: boolean; stopReason: 'none' | 'reach' | 'frozen' | 'water';
  reportedGradeOzPerBcy: number; recoveredMg: number;
  colorsBySize: Record<SizeClass, number>;   // particles seen (count × capture, rounded)
  massBySizeMg: Record<SizeClass, number> | null;   // pits and bulk only (sieved); pans: null
  observed: { overburdenFt?: number; payThicknessFt?: number; depthToBedrockFt?: number; bedrockType?: BedrockType;
              permafrost: boolean; clay: 'low' | 'med' | 'high'; boulders: 'low' | 'med' | 'high' };
  extractedBcy: number;
  hidden: { drawnRawOz: number; recoveredRawOz: number; accountingRawOz: number };   // engine-only; stripped by selectors
}
```

**Algorithm** (draw order is fixed; `LNmean(1, cv)` = exp(σZ − σ²/2) with σ² = ln(1 + cv²)):

```
0. Old tailings (req.target = 'oldTailings', block has a pile): g = pile grade, mix = pile sizeMix, posMult = 1, no pocket, no
   frozen or reach limits (piles are on the surface and thawed); Vb = remaining pile bcy; go to step 4. No pile → error NO_TAILINGS.
1. Geometry. T, B, OB_now = max(0, OB − bs.strippedBcy/1613); depthToBedrock = OB_now + T.
2. Interval [h1, h2] in height above bedrock:
   exposure:   if req.fromOpenCut or OB_now ≤ geology.sample.exposureMaxObFt (0.5):     // stripped, dredged or bare pay: a face sample
                  [h1, h2] = req.interval ?? [−min(B, m.bedrockPenFt), T]
               else if the block's surface code is 'c' (cutbank or bar on the active channel): h2 = T; h1 = T × (1 − exposureDepthFrac)
               else: nothing exposed; the pan comes from a surface scrape → reachedPay = false, overburden-only (below)
   pit:        frozenLimit = (bt.permafrost >= geology.sample.frozenThreshold (0.5) && !m.frozenOk)
                             ? max(geology.sample.activeLayerFt (2.0), bs.thawProgress) : ∞      // ft below the current surface
               (in winter the active layer is frozen too: §4 blocks non-frozenOk methods then; drawSample assumes summer thaw)
               bottom = min(m.maxDepthFt ?? ∞, frozenLimit, depthToBedrock + m.bedrockPenFt)
               if bt.permafrost < 0.5 and depthToBedrock > geology.sample.waterTableFt (north 6, arid 15)
                  and rng.u() < geology.sample.waterInflowP (north 0.25, arid 0.05): bottom = min(bottom, depthToBedrock − U(1, 4))
               h1 = depthToBedrock − bottom; h2 = T; stopReason from whichever limit bound
               if h1 >= T: reachedPay = false, overburden-only (below)
   fullColumn: h1 = −min(B, m.bedrockPenFt); h2 = T          (subject to maxDepthFt like a pit)
   interval:   req.interval
   h1 = max(h1, −B); reachedBedrock = (h1 <= 0)
   overburden-only: gLoc = obGrade (3.5.4), mixLoc = bt.sizeMix, skip to step 5; the extracted volume is overburden
                    (no sampledBcy change, accountingRawOz = 0)
3. Position: posMult = positionMult(bt, h1, h2)                              (3.5.4)
4. Local grade (sub-block variability, de Wijs) and pocket:
   Vb = (T + B) × 1613;  V = req.volumeBcy
   gMatrix = pocket ? (g × Vb − pocket.bcy × pocket.grade) / (Vb − pocket.bcy) : g
   σL² = V < Vb ? geology.sample.deWijsAlpha (0.028) × ln(Vb / V) : 0
   gLoc = gMatrix × posMult × exp(σL·Z − σL²/2);  mixLoc = bt.sizeMix
   if pocket and rng.u() < min(1, (pocket.bcy + V) / Vb):
       φ = min(1, pocket.bcy / V); gLoc = (1 − φ)·gLoc + φ·pocket.grade·posMult
       mixLoc = (1 − φ)·mix + φ·geology.sample.pocketMix [0.60, 0.30, 0.08, 0.02]
5. Compound Poisson, per size class k in [coarse, medium, fine, ultrafine]:
   m_k = [bt.coarseMeanMg, 3, 0.1, 0.004] mg;  c_k = geology.particle.massCv [2.0, 1.0, 0.7, 0.5]
   λ_k = gLoc × V × mixLoc_k × 31,103.5 / m_k
   N_k = λ_k < 30 ? poissonKnuth(λ_k) : max(0, round(λ_k + √λ_k · Z))
   M_k = N_k <= 40 ? Σ_{i=1..N_k} m_k · LNmean(1, c_k) : max(0, N_k·m_k + √N_k · m_k · c_k · Z)
6. Capture and measurement:
   W_k = M_k × min(1, m.captureBySize[k] × (req.samplerCaptureMult ?? 1))
   Vmeas = V × LNmean(1, m.volumeCv);  Wmeas = Σ W_k × LNmean(1, m.weighCv)
   reportedGradeOzPerBcy = Wmeas / 31,103.5 / Vmeas × m.biasMult
7. Observations (only what the sampler could see):
   if reachedPay: observed.overburdenFt = OB_now × LNmean(1, m.geomCv)
   if reachedBedrock: depthToBedrockFt = depthToBedrock × LNmean(1, m.geomCv); payThicknessFt = T × LNmean(1, m.thickCv ?? 0.10);
                      bedrockType = true type w.p. 0.9, else a random other type
   permafrost = bt.permafrost >= 0.5 && h1 < T; clay/boulders = tercile(x + N(0, 0.10)) at cuts 0.33 / 0.66
   colorsBySize_k = round(N_k × capture_k); massBySizeMg = pits/bulk ? W_k : null
   extractedBcy = V (exposure-mode pans and drill holes: V, negligible); hidden.drawnRawOz = Σ M_k / 31,103.5
   hidden.recoveredRawOz = Σ W_k / 31,103.5; hidden.accountingRawOz = g × V (the block-mean gold the volume carries in the ledger)
```

**Closed forms for §4's estimator.** These are formulas only; §4 feeds them *its* estimates, never truth.

```
particleCv(g, V, mix, coarseMg) = √( m_eff / (g × V × 31,103.5) ),   m_eff = Σ_k mix_k × m_k × (1 + c_k²)   [mg]
N_eff = g × V × 31,103.5 / m_eff                    // equivalent particle count; ±50% at 95% needs N_eff ≈ 16–20 (Clifton 1969)
logVarMeas(g, V, mix, coarseMg, m) ≈ ln(1 + particleCv²) + deWijsAlpha × ln(Vb / V) + ln(1 + volumeCv²) + ln(1 + weighCv²)
medianRatio ≈ Σ_k mix_k × capture_k × [λ_k ≥ 0.7]   // classes with P(N_k = 0) > 0.5 drop out of the typical sample
```

Mid-reach mix 25/40/27/8 with 150 mg coarse gives m_eff = 187.5 + 2.4 + 0.04 + 0.0004 ≈ **190 mg**. Coarse gold contributes 99% of the particle variance.

**Worked example 1: CV vs sample volume** (closed form, true grade 0.01 oz/bcy, coarse 150 mg, block pay volume 8,000 bcy; the particle CV scales as 1/√g):

| Sample | V (bcy) | Particle CV: proximal 45/35/15/5 / mid 25/40/27/8 / fan 10/30/40/20 | σL (local) | Total CV: prox / mid / fan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| One pan | 0.0067 | 12.8 / 9.6 / 6.1 | 0.63 | 15.6 / 11.7 / 7.4 |
| 6-in sonic core, 5 ft of pay | 0.036 | 5.5 / 4.1 / 2.6 | 0.59 | 6.6 / 4.9 / 3.2 |
| Hand pit | 0.5 | 1.48 / 1.11 / 0.70 | 0.52 | 1.78 / 1.38 / 0.98 |
| Small excavator pit | 3 | 0.60 / 0.45 / 0.29 | 0.47 | 0.84 / 0.71 / 0.59 |
| 10-yard test pit | 10 | 0.33 / 0.25 / 0.16 | 0.43 | 0.58 / 0.53 / 0.49 |
| Trench composite | 30 | 0.19 / 0.14 / 0.09 | 0.40 | 0.46 / 0.44 / 0.42 |
| Bulk sample | 300 | 0.06 / 0.05 / 0.03 | 0.30 | 0.32 / 0.31 / 0.31 |
| Large bulk sample | 1,000 | 0.03 / 0.02 / 0.02 | 0.24 | 0.25 |

Below about 1 bcy the particle term (nugget effect) dominates and is extremely skewed. Above about 10 bcy the symmetric local-variability term dominates, and averaging several pits beats one big sample of the same volume.

**Worked example 2: why a pan is useless in coarse-gold ground and a 10-yard pit is informative.** Proximal block, g = 0.01, mix 45/35/15/5, full-column position (no position bias). Placeholder captures: pan 0.98/0.95/0.85/0.50, pit 0.97/0.93/0.80/0.45. Expected particles per pan λ = 0.006 coarse, 0.24 medium, 3.1 fine, 26 ultrafine; per 10-bcy pit λ = 9.3 / 363 / 4,666 / 38,880. Monte Carlo of 20,000 draws, reported ÷ true:

| Sample | P(no coarse particle) | p10 | Median | Mean | p90 | p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 pan | 99.4% | 0.02 | 0.14 | 1.00 | 1.45 | 6.4 |
| Mean of 40 pans | — | 0.31 | 0.51 | 0.91 | 1.52 | — |
| 6-in sonic, 5 ft of pay | 96.7% | 0.06 | 0.31 | 0.96 | 1.26 | 12.1 |
| 3-bcy pit | 11.3% | 0.29 | 0.71 | 0.90 | 1.74 | 3.6 |
| 10-bcy pit | 0.3% | 0.39 | 0.79 | 0.91 | 1.56 | 2.7 |
| Mean of 10 × 10-bcy pits | — | 0.71 | 0.89 | 0.90 | 1.11 | — |
| 300-bcy bulk sample | 0% | 0.58 | 0.86 | 0.91 | 1.29 | 1.8 |

A typical pan reports 14% of the truth (it holds only fine and ultrafine colours). A 1-in-170 pan catches a coarse flake and reports about 70×. Pans also sample exposures, which exist only on the channel column or in an open cut: the upper 40% of the gravel has posMult ≈ 0.30 for T = 6, B = 1.5, which cuts the median a further ~3×, and off the channel an unstripped block yields only overburden colours. Pans therefore tell you *gold is present in the creek and what size it is*, but not the grade of the claim. 80% of single 10-yard pits report between 0.4× and 1.6× the truth, and the mean of ten pits falls between 0.7× and 1.1×. The means below 1.0 are capture losses, which are real and identical for every method.

**Worked example 3: position effects** (T = 6, B = 1.5, s_b = 0.20, λg = 2.0, λb = 0.6):

| Sample interval | posMult | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| Pit stops 2 ft above bedrock (30-t reach 22 ft vs 24 ft to bedrock) | 0.50 | misses the bottom gravel and all the bedrock: reports half the grade |
| Pit stopped by water inflow 3 ft above bedrock | 0.37 | |
| Exposure pan (upper 40% of gravel) | 0.30 | |
| Full gravel column, no bedrock | 1.00 | (coincidence: s_b equals the bedrock volume share here) |
| Full column + 1 ft bedrock | 1.05 | correct practice |
| "Bedrock scrape" (bottom 1 ft gravel + top 1 ft bedrock) | 1.90 | the classic seller overstatement |

**Gold accounting.** Sampling does not change `gradeOzPerBcy`. `extractedBcy` leaves the block at block-mean grade for volume accounting, so the block's contained gold falls by `accountingRawOz = g × V` (pile grade for a tailings sample). **Every** sample that reaches pay or a pile books its lines, whatever its size; there is no small-sample exemption. `sampleGoldLines(result, credited)` is pure and splits `accountingRawOz` exactly:

```
accountingRawOz = creditedRawOz + sampleCaptureLoss + sampleProcessingLoss + samplingVariance
  sampleCaptureLoss    = drawnRawOz − recoveredRawOz           // gold the sample's processing missed
  creditedRawOz        = credited ? recoveredRawOz : 0           // pits, trenches, bulk (§4 D-4.23)
  sampleProcessingLoss = credited ? 0 : recoveredRawOz           // pans and drill holes: the colours are not kept
  samplingVariance     = accountingRawOz − drawnRawOz            // mean zero; the luck of the draw. Signed so that every line
                                                                 // adds in §2.14's identity (a rich draw books a negative line)
overburden-only results: all lines 0 (trace gold in overburden is not contained gold, 3.5.4)
```

The caller applies `extractedBcy` to `Block.state` and posts the lines to the gold balance in the same step. Credited concentrate goes through §5 `settleProductionInterests`, then §10 `addLot(source: 'sample', trueAlloyFineness: the concentrate's tracked true fine ÷ metal ratio (the claim's mean alloy on single-fineness ground), trueDirtFrac: ops.goldRoomDirtFrac.noTable)` (§4 4.12, D-4.38). These are the sample terms of §2.14's identity (sample recovered + sample capture and processing loss + sampling variance), so the property holds to the micro-ounce from the first pan. Seller evidence (3.10.2), old drill logs and the Inheritor's pit logs describe sampling before the game. They are never applied to `Block.state` and book no lines.

### 3.9 Visible listing information

The player sees `ListingInfo`, a snapshot §3 builds when a listing candidate is created; §5 stores it on its `Listing` record (`info`). Every field is derived from truth or from the seller model, as follows. Grade appears only as the seller's claim.

| Field | Shown | Derived from | Noise or bias |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acreage, grid, title kind, regime | exact | `claim.acres`, `titleKind`, `regime` | none |
| Location, creek, setting | map position; "valley bottom" / "bench" / "dredged ground" / "fan" / "gulch" | parcel geometry; deposit type (deepMuck shows as valley bottom) | none |
| Access, seasonal note | access class plus window text | 3.3.3, §1 windows | none |
| Distance to town | miles, plus town tier and services | `D.town.roadMiFromOutlet + trailMi` | none |
| Environment | wetland / channel acres, fish-bearing, special status, sensitivity band (low < 0.35 ≤ med < 0.6 ≤ high) | `claim.env` (3.4.1) | none (public maps) |
| Water (north) | typical flow early / mid / late season | `listedFlowGpm` (3.3.4) | × LN(1, 0.20), fixed per listing (gauge estimate) |
| Water (arid) | "no surface water"; spring if any; regional wells 50–300 gpm at 100–300 ft; nearest fill mi | district aquifer prior; `sourceKind = 'spring'`; `nearestFillMi` | spring flow × LN(1, 0.3); claim well yield hidden |
| Recorded water right (P2+) | "senior right, N gpm (surface / groundwater)" or none | `claim.water.rightStub` (3.3.4) | none (recorded; §6 confirms) |
| Visible features (aerial imagery) | dredge tailings, tailings piles, recent disturbance, ponds, pre-stripped ground, improvements | dredge tailings ← `dredge`; tailings piles ← `oldTailings` of `handCut`, `dryWash`, `hydraulic` and `recentCat`; recent disturbance and ponds ← `recentCat` mined blocks; pre-stripped ← stripped, unmined blocks; improvements ← `improvementsUsd > 0` | drift shafts and their dumps are *not* visible from the air (3.6) |
| Existing permits and bond (stub until §6) | the seller's statement: none / notice on file / plan approved / unknown; bond posted | truth `permitStub`: recentCat claims whose last season ≥ `geology.permitStub.minLastSeasonYear` (2000) are plan 0.60 / notice 0.20 / none 0.20 (one draw; D-3.48), every other claim none; plus the starter lease stratum (3.11); a stub's `bondPostedCents` = U(0.5, 1.0) × §6 `reclamationCostEstimate` of its open acres (old bonds sit below today's RCE, as §6 expects); statement by honesty type (3.10.3) | from P2 §5 calls §6 `instantiatePermitStub` when it creates the listing, and §6 `records check` reveals the truth; a statement that differs from truth is §5's `misstatedPermit` defect; §6 defines meaning and transferability; P1 hides the field |
| Inherited reclamation liability | unreclaimed acres (post-1981); historic acres shown separately; $ estimate | `Block.state` with `disturbanceOrigin = 'inherited'` and not reclaimed; `historicAcres` (3.6) | acres exact (visible on the ground); $ = §6 `reclamationCostEstimate`; P1 stub $6,000/acre, labelled "estimate (no enforcement until permits)"; §5 defects may add undisclosed acres |
| Claimed grade, samples, history, thickness, old report | seller's data | 3.10 | by honesty type |
| Seller name, situation, data package | e.g. "Retiring operator; full data package" | holder situation; package level (3.10) | the package level is a soft tell |
| Asking terms, channel, weeks on market | price or lease terms | §5 (`priceListing`, listing lifecycle) | §5 |

```ts
interface ListingInfo {                // built by §3 at candidate creation; stored by §5 as Listing.info
  claimId: ClaimId; districtId: DistrictId; creekName: string; acres: number;
  titleKind: 'unpatented' | 'patented' | 'state'; regime: Regime;          // §13's listing filter reads titleKind
  setting: 'valleyBottom' | 'bench' | 'dredgedGround' | 'fan' | 'gulch';
  access: Access; accessNote: string; distanceToTownMi: number; town: { name: string; tier: TownTier; services: TownServices };
  env: ClaimEnv;
  water: ({ kind: 'creek'; flowGpm: { early: number; mid: number; late: number } }
       | { kind: 'arid'; springGpm: number | null; regionalWellGpm: [number, number]; regionalDepthFt: [number, number]; nearestFillMi: number })
       & { seniorRight: { gpm: number; source: 'surface' | 'groundwater' } | null };   // P2+; null in P1
  waterScore: number;                  // §5: clamp(expectedGpm / 750, 0, 1); expectedGpm = shown mid flow, or spring + 0.5 × regional median well
  visibleFeatures: ('dredgeTailings' | 'tailingsPiles' | 'recentDisturbance' | 'ponds' | 'preStripped' | 'improvements')[];
  improvementsUsd: number;             // §5 improvement credit
  permits: { status: 'none' | 'noticeOnFile' | 'planApproved' | 'unknown'; bondPostedCents: Cents | null };   // seller's statement
       // §5 derives presented authority from it: none | unknown → none, noticeOnFile → notice, planApproved → plan
  disturbance: { inheritedUnreclaimedAcres: number; historicAcres: number; liabilityEstimateCents: Cents };
       // §5 reads liabilityEstimateCents directly as the disclosed ARO
  claimed: ClaimedEvidence;
  summary: SellerClaimSummary;         // §5 pricing inputs (3.10.3); belief fields hidden
  seller: { holderId: HolderId | CompetitorId; displayName: string; situation: SellerSituation;   // = §5 SellerKey
            dataPackage: 'complete' | 'partial' | 'none' };
}
interface OpenParcel {                 // §5 staking view of a claim with status 'open'
  id: ClaimId; districtId: DistrictId; blockIds: BlockId[]; acres: number; setting: ListingInfo['setting'];
  visibleOldWorkings: ListingInfo['visibleFeatures']; env: ClaimEnv; priorContainedOz: number }
interface ListingCandidate {           // supplyTick output, claim-ID order (3.11)
  claimId: ClaimId; holderId: HolderId | CompetitorId; situation: SellerSituation; info: ListingInfo;
  firstLookUntilTurn: number | null;   // P5+, rolled once here; §5 does not redraw it
  starterLease: boolean }              // P2+ initial-market stratum: §5 offers lease / lease-with-option terms (3.11)
```

**Visible priors** (what any player may assume before sampling; §4's estimator starts here and §5 prices unproven ground from it). They are template constants plus visible facts, never hidden district or creek factors:

```
visiblePrior(districtId, setting, status) = {
  gradeMedOzBcy = tpl.gMed × depositMult.grade[setting] × geology.prior.statusMult[status]   (held 1.0, listed 0.92 (3.7), open 0.6)
  gradeSigLn    = √(σdistrict² + σcreek² + σrich² + σclaim² + σblock² + (listed ? listedSigmaAdj (0) : 0))
                  (north 0.76, arid 0.92); pBarrenCreek = 0.20
  paystreakShare = geology.prior.paystreakShare[setting] (valley 0.30, bench 0.40, fan / gulch 0.30)
  obMedFt, payMedFt and their σ, bedrock mix, B̄ = Σ bedrockMix × B0 (north 1.54 ft, arid 0.68 ft), size-mix prior, fineness range, P(frozen) }
priorContainedOz(claimId) = nBlocks × paystreakShare × (payMedFt + B̄) × 1613 × gradeMedOzBcy × oldWorkingsMult
  oldWorkingsMult: dredge tailings visible 0.15 | tailings piles visible 0.6 | else 1.0
```

Example: a held 20-ac northern valley claim with no visible workings: 20 × 0.30 × (5 + 1.54) × 1,613 × 0.0095 ≈ 600 raw oz, close to the median contained oz of a marginal claim (3.7). The same parcel listed: ≈ 550 oz; open: ≈ 360 oz.

**Claim priors for §4** (`claimPriors(state, claimId): ClaimPriors`; the interface is printed in §4 4.5.1, and §3 fills every field from template constants and visible geometry only, never from `hidden` fields; memoized per claim and status):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `logGradeMedian` | ln `visiblePrior(districtId, setting, status).gradeMedOzBcy` (status `listed` while a listing is open) |
| `sigma` | `tpl.sigma` {district, creek, rich, claim, block}; when listed, `claim` = √(σclaim² + `listedSigmaAdj`) (a log-variance, default 0) |
| `rangeAlongFt` / `rangeAcrossFt` | the template's block range along (north 700, arid 500) / `geology.grade.blockRangeAcrossFt` (120) |
| `streak` | `wanderSdFt`, `halfWidthMedFt × depositMult.halfWidth`, `sigHalfWidth`, `bgRatio` from the template |
| `pBarrenCreek` / `barrenMult` | `geology.world.barrenCreekP` (0.20) / `barrenCreekFactor` (0.15) |
| `pocket` | `pPerStreakBlock` = `tpl.pocketP` × 1.5 on proximal rows or gulches; `bcyMean` 1,650 and `bcy2Mean` 3.33e6 (moments of U(300, 3,000)); `gradeMin` 0.15; `gradeMult` 15 (median of the LN(15, 0.5) law, clamp [0.15, 2.0]) |
| `oldTimer.pKind` | `oldTimerOdds(depositType, visibleFeatures)`: the 3.2 mix for the deposit type, renormalized over the kinds consistent with what is visible (3.6, 3.9): no features → {none, drift}; tailings piles without recent disturbance → {handCut, dryWash, hydraulic}; recent disturbance → recentCat; dredge tailings → dredge. North creek, no features: drift 0.30 / (0.25 + 0.30) = 0.55. `knownKind` and `workedBlockIds` are left for §4 to fill from records it has found |
| `sizeMixPrior` / `sizeMixJitterLogSd` | `tpl.sizeMixPriors` for the setting (proximal: top 30% of the creek's rows or an order-3 creek; else mid-reach; bench; fan; gulch) / 0.25 |
| `coarseMeanMg` / `coarseMassLogSd` | `tpl.coarseMg` for the setting / 0.30 |
| `fineness` | the template's alloy fineness `{ mean, districtSd, claimSd }` (visible; §10 uses the same) |
| `verticalDecayFt` / `bedrockMix` | `tpl.verticalDecayFt[depositType]` (centre of its U(0.75, 1.25) jitter) / `tpl.bedrockMix` (B̄ and s̄_b follow from the BEDROCK table) |
| `geometry` | `obMedFt` = `tpl.overburden.medFt × depositMult.ob`; `obSigClaim` = √(district² + creek² + AR² + claim²) of the overburden σ; `obSigBlock` = its block σ; `payMedFt` = `tpl.pay.medFt`; `paySigClaim` = √(creek² + AR²); `paySigBlock` = the pay block σ |
| `blocks` | per block: `blockId`, `i`, `j`, `xFt` = block centre from the paystreak reference axis (`axisOffsetFt + (j − (nAcross − 1)/2) × 209`, minus `axisOffsetFt` on a bench), `acres` 1, `surface` (`env.surfaceCodes`), `visibleWorkings` (the block carries a visible feature) |

### 3.10 Sellers and the honesty model

#### 3.10.1 Holders (sellers)

Every NPC-held parcel belongs to a holder. A holder owns 1–6 parcels: contiguous held runs on a creek are grouped w.p. 0.5. **Honesty is a property of the holder**, so it persists across relistings and across all of that holder's claims.

```ts
type SellerHonesty = 'accurate' | 'optimistic' | 'cherryPicked' | 'fraudulent';
type SellerSituation = 'retiringOperator' | 'estate' | 'prospector' | 'distressedOperator' | 'absentee' | 'competitorBust';
interface SellerProfile {                 // world.holders[id]; prefix 'hld' (§5 SellerKey = HolderId | CompetitorId, hld_ / cmp_)
  id: HolderId; displayName: string; situation: SellerSituation;   // situation can change (distress) per listing
  honesty: SellerHonesty;                 // hidden
  knowledge: 'operator' | 'prospector' | 'heirs' | 'absentee';
  claimIds: ClaimId[];
  evidence: Record<ClaimId, SellerEvidenceSummary>;   // hidden; written at first listing; ClaimedEvidence is regenerated on relist
}
interface SellerEvidenceSummary {         // ≈ 100 bytes; full samples are NOT stored (save budget, D-3.31)
  nPitsDug: number; nPansDug: number; nScrapes: number; honestGradeOzPerBcy: number | null; honestPayFt: number | null;
  nPaystreakBlocksBelieved: number; omittedSeasonYears: number[]; kMult: number;   // kOpt or kFraud as drawn
  permitStatementTrue: boolean; beliefRawOz: number }
interface ClaimedEvidence {
  gradeOzPerBcy: number | null; gradeBasis: 'bank' | 'screenedFeed' | 'unspecified';
  thickness?: { overburdenFt: number; payFt: number };
  samples: { blockIdx: number | null; method: 'pan' | 'testPit' | 'bedrockScrape'; volumeBcy: number; gradeOzPerBcy: number;
             year: number; lab: 'none' | 'local' | 'certified' | 'unknown'; finenessNote?: string }[];
  history: { year: number; bcy: number; rawOz: number; basis: 'bank' | 'loose' | 'unspecified' }[];
  oldReport?: OldReport;            // { year, usdPerYd, goldPriceThenUsd, author } e.g. 1938, $0.85/yd at $35 → 0.0243 oz/yd
  narrative: string[];              // templated statements
}
```

Situation mix for new holders: prospector 0.35, absentee 0.25, retiringOperator 0.15, estate 0.10, distressedOperator 0.15. Situation determines knowledge: operators → `operator`; prospector → `prospector`; estate → `heirs`; absentee → `absentee`. **Channel and motivation are §5's, keyed on the situation the candidate carries** (§5 5.3); §3 draws no channel:
- the listing channel is `estate` if and only if the holder's situation is `estate`;
- §5's distressed roll (`land.distressedShareBase` with its gold ripple) applies only to `distressedOperator` and `retiringOperator` holders; when it fires, the listing shows situation `distressedOperator`;
- §5 draws the motivation prior `m0` by situation;
- `competitorBust` exists only on candidates from `relistClaim` (3.11).

The honesty tilt uses the situation drawn when the holder is created and never changes.

**Honesty mix** (difficulty-scaled; the values are §1's canonical difficulty table, 1.11). Situation tilts are odds multipliers, applied before renormalizing:

| Difficulty | accurate | optimistic | cherryPicked | fraudulent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| easy | 0.55 | 0.30 | 0.12 | 0.03 |
| standard | 0.35 | 0.35 | 0.22 | 0.08 |
| hard | 0.20 | 0.35 | 0.30 | 0.15 |
| Tilts | estate ×1.6, retiring ×1.3 | prospector ×1.3, absentee ×1.2 | distressed ×1.5 | prospector ×1.5, distressed ×1.2, estate ×0.3 |

#### 3.10.2 Seller evidence (real draws from truth)

The seller's evidence uses the same `drawSample` physics on the true blocks. An *accurate* seller can therefore still be wrong, through particle noise, pits that missed bedrock, or history from mined-out blocks.

```
genSellerEvidence(H, K, T, r = rng(seed,'seller',K.id,H.id)):
  plan by knowledge:  operator   → pits U{6..15} (3 bcy, reach 22 ft) + trueHistory
                      prospector → pans U{10..30} (exposure) + pits U{0..4} (3 bcy, reach 18 ft)
                      heirs      → no samples; oldReport w.p. 0.6; trueHistory w.p. 0.5 ("records in the attic")
                      absentee   → oldReport w.p. 0.5; pits U{0..6}
  cherryPicked: pit count × geology.seller.cherryPitMult (2.5)
  where: pits by block weights w_b = (0.15 + f_b) × (OB_b + T_b ≤ reach ? 1.0 : 0.4), excluding mined blocks;
         pans on channel ('c') blocks only, uniformly (the only natural exposures, 3.8)
  gSamples = pits ≥ 1 ? mean(pit grades) : mean(pan grades)
  gHist    = Σ history rawOz / Σ history bcy           // recovered oz per yard: sellers don't correct for recovery
  wH       = histBcy / (histBcy + geology.seller.historyWeightBcy (20,000))
  honestGrade = wH × gHist + (1 − wH) × gSamples        (none of these → oldReport grade, else null)
  oldReport: grade0 = mean virgin paystreak grade × LN(1, 0.4); era price ∈ {20.67 (pre-1934), 35.00 (1934–1971)};
             usdPerYd = grade0 × priceThen (year U{1905..1965})
  honestPayFt = mean observed payThicknessFt of pits that reached bedrock, else null
  nPaystreakBlocksBelieved = operator / heirs with history: count of unmined blocks with f ≥ 0.4; others: that count × U(0.7, 1.3), rounded
```

Seller methods are §3 data, so seller evidence never depends on §4's tuning. Operators had years on the ground and sampled thawed or stripped cuts, so their pits are `frozenOk`:

| `geology.seller.methods` | positionMode | maxDepthFt | frozenOk | bedrockPenFt | captureBySize | volumeCv / weighCv / geomCv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sellerPan` (0.0067 bcy) | exposure (0.4) | — | false | 0 | 0.98 / 0.95 / 0.85 / 0.50 | 0.15 / 0.10 / 0.15 |
| `sellerPit3` (3 bcy) | pit | reach (22 operator, 18 prospector) | true | 0.5 | 0.97 / 0.93 / 0.80 / 0.45 | 0.15 / 0.05 / 0.10 |
| `bedrockScrape` (0.5 bcy) | interval [−1, +1] ft | — | true | 1.0 | 0.97 / 0.93 / 0.80 / 0.45 | 0.15 / 0.05 / 0.10 |

**Storage.** Only `SellerEvidenceSummary` is kept on the holder. `ClaimedEvidence` is a pure function of (truth, holder, claim, stream), so it is regenerated identically when the same holder relists, and the copy the player saw lives on §5's `Listing.info` and in §4's evidence log. Full per-sample results would cost ≈ 15 kB per holder-claim pair and break the 2 MB save budget within a few game years.

#### 3.10.3 What each type claims

| Type | Claimed grade | Samples shown | History shown | Thickness and other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| accurate | `honestGrade` (3 s.f.), basis `bank` | all, true locations | all seasons, bank yards | honest (pit observations) |
| optimistic | `honestGrade × kOpt`, kOpt = clamp(LN(1.45, 0.15), 1.15, 2.2); basis `screenedFeed` w.p. 0.5 (the story behind the inflation; real screened-feed factor 1/(1 − oversize 0.2–0.4) = 1.25–1.7), else `unspecified` | all | w.p. 0.5 each season's bcy ÷ 1.2 (loose yards reported as bank: +20% grade) | pay × 1.2, overburden × 0.85 |
| cherryPicked | mean of the samples shown | top max(3, ⌈0.35 n⌉) by grade; w.p. 0.5 add 1–3 bedrock scrapes (interval [−1, +1] ft) on the best blocks | only seasons at or above the median recovered grade | honest |
| fraudulent | max(honestGrade, 0.6 × tpl.gMed) × kFraud, kFraud = clamp(LN(4.0, 0.35), 2.5, 10) | U{5..12} fabricated: grade × LN(1, 0.25) (suspiciously tight), lab `unknown`, w.p. 0.6 "0.95–0.99 fine" or "flour gold" in a coarse creek | true history × U(2, 3); or, with none, 2–4 invented seasons (bcy U(15k, 40k), rawOz = bcy × claimed × 0.75) | (P5+, when §5 runs defects and diligence) title defect w.p. `geology.seller.fraudTitleDefectP` 0.3 → §5 |

**Permit statements** (the listing's `permits` field, P2+): accurate and cherry-picked state the truth; optimistic upgrades `noticeOnFile` to `planApproved` w.p. 0.25 and `none` on a recent-operator claim to `noticeOnFile` w.p. 0.20; fraudulent states `planApproved` with a bond equal to §6's RCE w.p. 0.5; `heirs` and `absentee` state `unknown` w.p. 0.5 whatever their honesty. `SellerEvidenceSummary.permitStatementTrue` records whether the statement matches the truth (`unknown` counts as true: it claims nothing). A false statement is **§5's `misstatedPermit` defect**: §6's records check ($250) or §5's basic diligence detects it with p = 1, and a buyer who closes without detecting it can sue as for a concealed defect (§5 5.6). The `permitStatusMismatch` tell (3.10.4) is the same fact surfacing in a records or geologist review.

Data package (visible soft tell): accurate complete 0.7 / partial 0.3; optimistic 0.5 / 0.5; cherryPicked complete 0.3 / partial 0.6 / none 0.1; fraudulent complete 0.3 / partial 0.4 / none 0.3 (fraudsters fabricate tidy binders). Estates are `none` w.p. 0.5 whatever their honesty. At the standard mix, P(fraudulent | complete) ≈ 0.05 and P(fraudulent | none) ≈ 0.25 against a prior of 0.08: informative, never a guarantee (the earlier "fraud never complete" split made a complete package a fraud-proof filter).

**Seller claim summary for §5** (`ListingInfo.summary`):

```ts
interface SellerClaimSummary {
  evidenceClass: 'none' | 'anecdotal' | 'history' | 'report' | 'production';
  claimedGradeOzBcy: number | null; claimedRawOz: number; claimedFineness: number | null;
  recordsQuality: 'none' | 'fair' | 'good';             // = dataPackage none / partial / complete
  hidden: { beliefRawOz: number } }                      // reservation input; never rendered
```

```
evidenceClass: 'production' if ≥ 3 history seasons shown and the latest ≥ startYear − 8 (operators only)
               | 'report' if an oldReport exists, or ≥ 6 pits shown with lab local/certified and package complete
               | 'history' if ≥ 1 season shown | 'anecdotal' if any sample or claimed grade | else 'none';   estates capped at 'history'
claimedRawOz  = claimedGrade × nPS_claimed × (claimedPayFt + B̄) × 1613         (0 when no grade is claimed)
   nPS_claimed = nPaystreakBlocksBelieved × {accurate 1.0, optimistic 1.2, cherryPicked 1.0, fraudulent 1.5}
   claimedPayFt = claimed.thickness?.payFt ?? tpl.pay.medFt;  B̄ from visiblePrior (3.9)
beliefRawOz   = beliefGrade × nPaystreakBlocksBelieved × ((honestPayFt ?? tpl.pay.medFt) + B̄) × 1613
   beliefGrade = honestGrade × (optimistic ? √kOpt : 1)     // optimists half-believe their story; others know their own data
               ?? visiblePrior median (no evidence at all: heirs and absentees value from the region)
claimedFineness = operators with history: true claim fineness rounded to 0.01 (optimistic +0.02); fraudulent: 0.95–0.99 w.p. 0.6; else null
```

Fraudulent `beliefRawOz / claimedRawOz` ≈ 1 / (kFraud × 1.5) ≈ 0.1–0.25, so a fraudster folds fast on a deep discount (§5 D-5.1).

**Analytic size of cherry-picking.** If pit grades across paystreak blocks are lognormal with σ ≈ 0.85 (block 0.50 ⊕ local 0.47 ⊕ particle 0.45), the mean of the top 35% is `(1 − Φ(z₀.₆₅ − σ)) / 0.35` = (1 − Φ(0.385 − 0.85)) / 0.35 = **1.94×** the mean of all pits.

Worked example. The truth is a paystreak averaging 0.009 oz/bcy in place. The seller dug 18 three-yard pits (expected mean ≈ 0.009 × 0.91 capture = 0.0082) and shows the best 7 (≈ 0.0159) plus 2 bedrock scrapes (≈ 0.0159 × 1.90 ≈ 0.030). The claim is (7 × 0.0159 + 2 × 0.030) / 9 = **0.019 oz/bcy, 2.1× the truth**, with every sample genuine. Player pits on random paystreak blocks average ≈ 0.008. Pits *at the seller's spots* come back ≈ 0.011–0.014: the spots really are better, but they regress to the mean. Partial reproduction at the seller's spots is the signature of cherry-picking. Fraud's spots do not reproduce at all.

#### 3.10.4 Tells

Tells are rolled once per (listing, channel) on `rng(seed,'seller-tells',listingId,channel)`, with `p = min(0.98, base × skillMult)`. §4 supplies `skillMult` from the geologist, consultant tier or owner background. Found tells become evidence notes (§4 `EvidenceRef`) and inbox lines. Accurate sellers generate **no** tells: a review returns "consistent with records".

| Tell | Applies to | Records review | Geologist review | Site visit | Text (template) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gradeBasisScreened` | optimistic with basis screenedFeed | 0.10 | 0.85 | — | Grade quoted per yard of screened plant feed, not bank yards; overstates by 25–70% |
| `historyLooseYards` | optimistic, loose-yard seasons | 0.50 | 0.60 | — | Filed production volumes are larger than the seller's figures |
| `thicknessOverstated` | optimistic | 0.20 | 0.50 | 0.30 | Cutbank exposures show thinner gravel than claimed |
| `sampleClustering` | cherryPicked | — | 0.75 | — | Reported samples cluster on 2–3 blocks; most of the claim is untested |
| `unreportedPits` | cherryPicked | 0.55 | 0.30 | 0.60 | The Notice file / old pit scars show about N pits; only k are reported |
| `bedrockScrapeSamples` | any listing with scrape samples | — | 0.80 | — | Some samples are bedrock scrapes, not full-column samples |
| `historyGaps` | cherryPicked | 0.65 | 0.20 | — | Filings exist for seasons the seller omitted, at lower grades |
| `noProductionRecord` | fraudulent, invented history | 0.85 | 0.30 | 0.50 | No filed production; no disturbance where mining is claimed |
| `inflatedHistory` | fraudulent, true history × 2–3 | 0.75 | 0.30 | 0.30 | Filed ounces are a fraction of the claimed ounces |
| `saltedSignature` | fraudulent | — | 0.65 | — | Sample spread far too tight for placer; fineness or particle shape foreign to the creek |
| `unknownLab` | fraudulent | 0.30 | 0.70 | — | Assay certificates from an unregistered lab |
| `permitStatusMismatch` | any misstated permit (P2+) | 0.90 | 0.10 | — | Agency records show a different permit status than the seller states |

```ts
interface SellerTell { id: string; listingId: ListingId; channel: 'recordsReview' | 'geologistReview' | 'siteVisit';
  text: string; foundTurn: number }                  // only tells that were found are stored; misses leave no trace
interface OldReport { year: number; usdPerYd: number; goldPriceThenUsd: number; author: string }
```

Records review also returns non-dishonest facts for every listing (§4 renders them): the old-timer footprint, era and worked blocks, which blocks the history came from ("production came from blocks now mined out"), filed production, the creek's historic production, old drill logs, prior permits, and lapses (3.6).

### 3.11 Claim supply over time

**Who owns what.** §3 decides *which* claims come to market and when: the off-market churn of NPC holders, the listing candidate (claim, holder, situation, `ListingInfo`, first-look window), cooldowns, holder changes after a sale, forfeiture, NPC staking and open ground. §5 turns each candidate into a `Listing` and runs its life: channel (from the holder's situation, 3.10.1), asking terms, expiry (`expiresTurn = listedTurn + round(16 × LN(1, 0.4))`), background sales to unmodeled buyers and the hold-open rule. §3 supplies the truth-based quality multiplier §5 applies to background sales (`saleQualityMult`, D-3.9) and is told when a listing closes.

**Initial market (newGame).** Of the held parcels, 17% are listed (`geology.supply.initialListedShare`, the steady-state share), with at least 6 per district. The initial set is stratified so each district offers at least one listing with history or a report (operator or estate), at least two cheap unproven ones (prospector), and at least one absentee or estate holder (lease-friendly; §5 sets the terms). The rest are off-market.

**Starter permitted lease (P2+).** So that a new player's first northern season need not be all paperwork, each district's initial market also holds at least one listing with true `planApproved` authority and a full bond, held by an `accurate` or `cherryPicked` holder (who states permits truthfully), flagged `starterLease: true` on the candidate. §5 offers it as a lease or lease-with-option whose advance fits Bootstrapper cash (5.4, 5.7). Selection, in claim-ID order over the district's NPC-held parcels with such a holder:
1. a parcel whose truth stub is already `planApproved`;
2. else the `recentCat` parcel with the latest last season, whose stub is set to `planApproved`;
3. else the first held valley parcel, whose stub is set to `planApproved` (a permitted plan never worked).

Its `bondPostedCents` = §6 `reclamationCostEstimate` of the plan cap (open acres + 5), so no top-up is due on transfer. The listing's ground quality is not conditioned: the starter lease removes the permit wait, not the need to evaluate the ground. With the widened stub (3.9: last season ≥ 2000, plan 0.60; D-3.48) ≈ 10% of northern listings carry true transferable plan authority (preflight: north 10.0%, arid 6.6%, against 4.8% and 4.3% at the earlier 2010 / 0.50; gate ≥ 8%, BALANCE T-15 b; checked in the P2 simulator).

**Weekly listing hazard** for each off-market NPC-held parcel past its cooldown:

```
h_list = min(geology.supply.maxListHazard (0.10),
             geology.supply.baseListHazard (0.025 / wk) × seasonMult(week) × goldMult × scarcityMult × inflowMult[class]
             × Π events('geology.supply.listingHazardMult'))
seasonMult: weeks 40–52 and 1–12 (off-season) 1.4 | weeks 13–20 (pre-season) 1.2 | weeks 21–39 0.6     (mean 1.08)
goldMult = rippleTwoSided(state, 1, eUp 0.5, eDown −1.5, lag 8, 1.0, 2.5).value       // §10; on goldIdxReal, no escalation
           = clamp(max(x^0.5, x^−1.5), 1.0, 2.5), x = goldIdxReal lagged 8 weeks       // rising gold, owners cash in; falling, distress
scarcityMult (P2+; 1 in P1) = clamp(D.npcHeldBaseline / max(1, npcHeld_D), 1.0, geology.supply.scarcityMax (2.5))
           // npcHeld_D = the district's parcels now held by NPC holders (off-market or listed)
inflowMult = { uneconomic 1.1, marginal 1.0, good 0.8, excellent 0.6 }      // owners of good ground mine it themselves
saleQualityMult(claimId) = { uneconomic 0.7, marginal 1.0, good 1.8, excellent 2.5 }[class]   // §5 multiplies its background-sale p by this
```

`goldIdxReal` is §10's real market index (`goldIdx / cpiIndex`, D-10.32), so inflation alone never moves the listing hazard. It is 1.0 in P1–P4, so goldMult = 1 until P5. `max(x^0.5, x^−1.5) ≥ 1` for every x, so the lower clamp is 1.0 (the canonical §10 10.8 row has clamp [1.0, 2.5]). The class is truth-based (adverse selection; D-3.9): `claim.hidden.econClass` is computed once at generation at the opening spot. It is not recomputed as gold moves; the gold multiplier carries the price effect. The share of new listings sold as distressed belongs to §5's channel roll (`land.distressedShareBase` with its own gold ripple), not to §3.

**Scarcity.** As the player and competitors take parcels out of NPC hands, each remaining NPC parcel lists proportionally more often, so the flow of new listings and the number on the market stay at their baseline until the NPC stock falls below 40% of `npcHeldBaseline` (the 2.5 clamp). Thin markets churn faster: buyers are many and owners are tempted (D-3.42).

**Candidates and closings.** `supplyTick(state, turn): ListingCandidate[]` returns candidates in claim-ID order: first the `relistClaim` requests queued since the last tick (`world.supplyQueue`), then the hazard rolls. **First look (P5+, §5 5.3).** When the player's reputation is ≥ `land.firstLookMinRep` (70), a candidate whose holder is not an estate carries `firstLookUntilTurn = turn + land.firstLookWeeks (2)` w.p. `land.firstLookShare` (0.15, §1 1.12), drawn once here as the last draw on `rng(seed,'supply',turn,claimId)`. Only the player sees it until then: neither §5's background sales nor §12's competitors may act on it. §5 does not redraw it, and drops it if it assigns a channel other than private. `onListingClosed(state, claimId, outcome)` applies: `expired` or `withdrawn` → off-market with `geology.supply.relistCooldownWk` (20); `soldOffscreen` → new holder (fresh situation and honesty draws), 52-week cooldown; `soldToPlayer` / `soldToCompetitor` → status `player` / `competitor`. On relist the same holder regenerates the same `ClaimedEvidence`; §5 applies its stale-listing discount.

**Expected flow (P1, standard).** About 70 parcels per district with a realized held share of 0.70 (north) and 0.57 (arid) give ≈ 49 + 40 = 89 held parcels. One cycle of a held parcel is: off-market wait 1 / (0.025 × 1.08) ≈ 37 weeks, then a listing life of ≈ 13 weeks (§5's expiry, mean ≈ 17 weeks, competing with background sales at ≈ 0.02 × 0.87), then a cooldown averaging 0.77 × 20 + 0.23 × 52 ≈ 27 weeks. So 13 / 77 ≈ 17% of held parcels are listed at any time: **≈ 15 active listings** across two districts and **≈ 60 new listings a year**. Steady-state pool quality is shown in 3.7. Good listings disappear fast, so weeks-on-market is an honest (statistical) signal that a listing is weaker.

**Open ground and staking.** Open parcels are visible on the map (status `open`) with their aerial-visible features and environmental attributes; `openParcel(state, claimId)` gives §5 its `OpenParcel` view. Staking is §5's flow (P2): a staked parcel keeps its pre-generated geometry (OQ-3.2). The parcel's truth already exists, and staking reveals nothing about grade.

**NPC forfeiture (P2+).** At week 36 (just after the Sept 1 fee deadline, week 35), each off-market NPC-held unpatented parcel forfeits w.p. `geology.supply.npcForfeitRate` (0.03), × `lowGoldMult` 1.5 when `goldIdxRealAt(state, turn)` < 0.85. Forfeited parcels become `open` *with their real (held-quality) truth* (or `withdrawn` if they lie in a withdrawn overlay: rights lapse and the land is closed); a recorded water right lapses with them. Their prior disturbance becomes `historic` for a new locator. A news item lists them, which creates a small yearly staking race. Withdrawn stretches can open by event (§12 `landOpened`, `openWithdrawnOverlay`).

**NPC staking (P2+).** Local prospectors re-locate lapsed ground, so forfeiture churns the NPC stock instead of draining it. At week 40 each district's NPCs stake as many open parcels as NPC parcels forfeited there at week 36 (`geology.supply.npcRestakeRatio` 1.0 × that count). They pick without replacement on `rng(seed,'supply',turn,districtId)`, with weights ∝ `priorContainedOz` (prospectors stake what looks good from the road, which includes the just-forfeited parcels). Each staked parcel gets a fresh `prospector` holder (fresh honesty draw), status `heldNpc` and a 52-week cooldown. The four weeks between the forfeiture list and the NPC staking are the player's (and from P5 the competitors') head start in the staking race.

**Supply floor (P5+).** Scarcity (above) holds the listing flow until the NPC stock falls to 40% of its baseline. As a backstop, at week 36 §3 computes each district's `takenShare` = (parcels held by the player or competitors) ÷ (parcels not `withdrawn`). If `takenShare` > `geology.supply.landOpenedTakenShare` (0.35) and the district still has a withdrawn overlay, §3 posts a `landOpened` request for that district, which §12 schedules with its usual two-week news lead. The event then opens the overlay through `openWithdrawnOverlay` (once per overlay). Districts are never added mid-game (D-3.1, D-3.42).

**Competitors (P5).** §12 AI companies bid on listings (step 5) and stake open ground. Claims they win get `holderId = competitorId` and are off-market. When a competitor goes bust, §12 calls `relistClaim(state, claimId, 'competitorBust')`. That queues the claim on `world.supplyQueue`, and the **next** step-3 `supplyTick` emits it as a candidate with situation `competitorBust`; §5 then makes it a distressed listing or a claim auction (§12 12.15 sets the split). A bust in step 5 therefore lists the following week, never in the same pipeline pass.

### 3.12 Player actions

| Action `type` | Params | Validation (error codes) | Effect | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `world/siteVisit` | `claimId`, `ownerTime?: 'queue' \| 'now'` (default `'queue'`) | `CLAIM_UNKNOWN`, `ACCESS_CLOSED` (`claimAccess.freightOpen` false; fly-in claims go by charter whenever air is open), `OWNER_INJURED` (§1: `owner.injuredUntilTurn` > turn), `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | Pays `geology.siteVisit.costUsd[access]` × cpiIndex (highway $400, seasonalRoad $800, winterTrail $1,800, flyIn $3,500) through `finance.pay` to `exp.prospecting` (memo "site visit", ref claimId) at action time; a failed payment rejects the action. Books `geology.siteVisit.days[access]` (2 / 3 / 4 / 4) as a §1 owner desk-day task (1.9, D-1.28): if the days fit this week's remaining capacity, or with `ownerTime: 'now'` (each excess day cuts the owner's field `availableFraction` by 1/6 this week, applied by §8), the visit resolves now; otherwise it joins §1's desk queue and resolves at the step 7 in which §1 books its days (if the claim's freight is closed that week it stays queued, no days spent). On resolution it reveals ground-level features (drift subsidence and shafts w.p. 0.9, ×0.4 under snow; surface boulder tercile; vegetation permafrost indicator: frozen likely / unlikely, correct w.p. 0.8; this week's flow from `waterAvailableGpm` ± 10% in season; pit scars for `unreportedPits`) on `rng(seed,'site',turn,claimId)` (turn = the resolution turn) and rolls the site-visit tells if the claim is listed. §4's `prospect/panSurvey` books its visit through this action with the same `ownerTime` option. **No grade information.** | P1 |
| `world/setWatch` | `districtId` or `claimId`, `on: boolean` | `UNKNOWN_TARGET`, `WATCH_LIMIT` (adding a claim when `world.watch.claimIds` already holds §4's `geology.maxTrackedClaims`, 40) | Adds or removes the target from `world.watch`; drives the step-16 inbox lines for new listings, forfeitures and price changes, and §4's weekly estimate tracking. §13's star on a listing dispatches this action | P1 |
| `debug/revealTruth` | `claimId` | dev builds only (compiled out) | Overlays truth on the block grid | P0 |

```ts
interface SiteVisitReport { turn: number; claimId: ClaimId; features: string[]; boulders: 'low' | 'med' | 'high';
  permafrostIndicator: 'likely' | 'unlikely'; flowGpm: number | null; tellIds: string[]; snowCovered: boolean }
```

**Land-choice trade-offs that §3's world creates** (decided through §5 and §4 actions, but shaped here):
- **North vs arid district:** higher grade and fineness (0.86 vs 0.78) and coarser, easier-to-recover gold, against frozen ground, 3–4:1 strip, an ≈ 22-week site season (19–25) with ≈ 20 sluicing weeks (§1 D-1.3) and remote access. Arid ground has 1–1.5:1 strip, cheap access and a long season, but lower grade, finer gold and water that must be drilled or hauled.
- **Headwater vs lower creek:** coarse, nuggety gold (high recovery, impossible to value with small samples) and little water, against finer gold (needs a fines circuit), more water and wider paystreaks.
- **Valley bottom vs bench:** benches are better drained and less frozen (south-facing ones especially), and often overlooked and cheap, but carry 2.5× the overburden and are sometimes cemented. Valley bottoms carry the channel and wetland blocks that §6's stream and wetland permits gate.
- **Old-timer ground vs virgin ground:** drifted or dredged ground is cheaper, has visible history and carries low-strip tailings feed, but the in-place grade is 25–60% of virgin on drifted ground and 8–20% on dredged ground, and the gold left is finer. Virgin ground is unknown and usually staked or priced high.
- **Ground with recent history vs unproven:** history is evidence, but it describes the blocks already mined. Unproven ground is cheap and entirely uncertain.
- **Act fast vs diligence:** good listings sell to others at 1.8–2.5× the base hazard, while every week of sampling costs money and time.

Trade-off: a site visit is cheap and quick, but it says nothing about grade, and a winter visit sees little. It mostly rules claims *out* (bouldery, frozen, already drifted) before money is spent on §4 sampling. Every other action that uses §3 belongs to another section: buy, lease and stake (§5); sampling, records and geologist review (§4); mining (§7).

### 3.13 Weekly resolution

| Step (§2.6) | What §3 does |
|---|---|
| `newGame` | `generateWorld` (3.1); holders; initial listing candidates (with the P2+ starter lease) handed to §5 (which prices them, and in P2+ calls §6 `instantiatePermitStub`). For §1's Inheritor start, `genInheritedGroup` (3.6.1) conditions and transfers the family run. |
| 3 Markets refresh (owner §5) | §5 calls `supplyTick` first, as its sub-step (a), before the rest of §5 and then §4, §8 and §9 (§2.6, D-2.11). In claim-ID order on `rng(seed,'supply',turn,claimId)`: (i) P2+, week 36: NPC forfeitures, then (P5+) the supply-floor check; (ii) P2+, week 40: NPC staking on `rng(seed,'supply',turn,districtId)`; (iii) queued `relistClaim` candidates; (iv) listing-hazard rolls for off-market NPC-held parcels past cooldown, building `ListingInfo` (first-listing `ClaimedEvidence` on `'seller'`), then the P5+ first-look roll. §5 then creates the listings (calling §6 `instantiatePermitStub` in P2+) and runs expiry and background sales, calling `onListingClosed` for each listing that ends. |
| 5 Competitors (P5) | §12 bids land on listings; competitor wins arrive through `onListingClosed`; bust ground through `relistClaim`, which queues it for next week's step 3. |
| 7 Staff availability (owner §1) | §1 pulls queued desk tasks; a queued site visit whose days are booked now resolves (report, tells). |
| 9 Operations | `drawSample` is called by §4 programs (pure); §4 posts `sampleGoldLines`. `accessFactors`, `claimAccess`, `waterAvailableGpm` and the ground fields are read by §7 and §9. |
| 16 Wrap-up | Inbox alerts (§13 taxonomy, all severity `info`): `listing.new` and `listing.priceChanged` for listings on watched districts or claims and next to ground the player holds; `claims.forfeitureList` (week 36–37, with the open parcels and the week-40 NPC staking date); `siteVisit.report` for each visit resolved this week. |

Block-state changes come from §7 (stripping, mining, thaw, disturbance, reclamation) and §4 (`sampledBcy`). §3 does not run anything else weekly.

| Phase | §3 content |
|---|---|
| P0 | Generator, packing and decode, `drawSample` and the closed forms, calibration harness in `sim/` (on the full network generator); dev reveal. |
| **P1** | Two districts (`northernFederal` + `aridFederal`; §1 fixes two for P1–P5). Full block model, old-timers and recent history, overlays and environmental attributes (generated and shown; they gate nothing until §6 P2). Jurisdiction and wage-region fields. Inheritor family run (3.6.1, with its pre-stripped blocks). All four honesty types, with tells reachable through whichever §4 channels exist in P1 (own sampling always works). `claimPriors`, `visiblePrior` with the listed multiplier, and the public record (footprint with worked blocks, filed production, creek history, records quality) for §4's P1 estimator; old drill logs are generated from P1 and used by §4 from P2. `sampleGoldLines` for every sample. Supply: initial listings plus weekly hazard; §5 runs expiry and background sales; no staking, forfeiture or competitors. `goldIdxReal` = 1, so the gold multiplier is 1. Permit field hidden. Liability shown in acres plus a $6,000/acre stub estimate labelled "estimate (no enforcement until permits)". Site visit (owner desk days), watch list (cap 40), and the base district map (claims, creeks, town, routes, ownership fills; §13's permit, risk and activity layers come in P2+). |
| P2 | Staking open parcels (§5); week-36 NPC forfeitures and week-40 NPC staking; the scarcity multiplier; permit and bond statements become real (§6 `instantiatePermitStub` at listing, records check, `misstatedPermit` on a false statement); the starter permitted lease in each district's initial market; recorded senior water rights on listings; environmental attributes gate §6 permits; inherited liability enforced. |
| P3 | No new content. Ground fields drive §9 wear. |
| P5 | Gold ripple on listing hazard (on `goldIdxReal`); competitors hold, bid on and relist claims (busts list the week after); first-look candidates once §1's reputation reaches 70 (they also bar competitors); title defects for fraudulent sellers (§5 diligence); the supply-floor `landOpened` request; "gold rush" and "land opened to entry" events. |
| P6 | `temperateFederal`, `alaskaState` and `yukon` templates (claim units 40/160 and 23 ac); 4–6 districts (default 5); regime-specific holders (state rental and labor filings feed forfeiture odds). Last and optional: the hard-rock track (§14). §14 owns the lode deposit model and its generation rules (`genLodeSystems`, `layLodeParcels`, 14.2–14.3); §3 only hosts the results in the world slice (`world.lodes`, `world.lodePanelStates`) and calls §14's generator, adding no lode rules of its own. |

**Phase exit gates** (§1 1.19) that §3's content must pass: **P1** — listing-pool class shares in band for both templates and the grade and strip bands (3.18 simulator), the sample-gold conservation property, and the Inheritor tier test; **P2** — ≥ 8% of northern listings with true transferable plan authority and a starter lease in every district; **P5** — the long-run supply test (3.18).
