| Diligence, records check or title review on a deal that does not close; lapsed inspection fee; suit legal costs; forfeiture damages | `exp.ga` | cash / `prepaid` / liability |
| Lien paid; dispute settlement; royalty buy-down; option fee | `mineral.properties` | cash |
| Recorded-royalty arrears | `exp.royaltyCash` | cash |
| Suit recovery | cash | `inc.other` |
| Claim sold (listing, quick or forced sale) | cash; `mineral.accumDepletion` | `mineral.properties`; `gain.assetSale` (or Dr if a loss) |
| Tenure ends without sale (void, voidedByExam, forfeited, foreclosed incl. transfer to a creditor, relinquished, lost blocks pro rata) | `gain.assetSale` (loss); `mineral.accumDepletion` | `mineral.properties` |

| `type` | Params | Validation (errors) | Effect | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `land/acceptAsk` | listingId, structure `'sale'\|'lease'\|'jv'`, useCarry? | LISTING_NOT_OPEN, STRUCTURE_NOT_OFFERED, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, CARRY_NOT_OFFERED, REPUTATION_TOO_LOW, WALK_COOLDOWN, REORG_COURT_APPROVAL (before plan confirmation) | P1: tenure transfers immediately; P2+: Closing created (the records check rides in it; P5+ the title review too) | P1 |
| `land/makeOffer` | listingId, structure, terms (may include `inspection` and `sellerBondCarryWeeks`) | LISTING_NOT_OPEN, OFFER_ALREADY_PENDING, TERMS_OUT_OF_BOUNDS, WALK_COOLDOWN, REPUTATION_TOO_LOW, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS (cash part must be on hand), REORG_COURT_APPROVAL (before plan confirmation) | creates or advances a Negotiation (also the best-and-final offer); one response next week | P5 |
| `land/requestInspection` | listingId, weeks 2–8, allowedTier `'casual'\|'notice'` | LISTING_NOT_OPEN, INSPECTION_REFUSED, NO_SELLER_NOTICE, INSPECTION_ACTIVE, TERMS_OUT_OF_BOUNDS, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, REORG_COURT_APPROVAL (before plan confirmation) | fixed fee paid (credited if the player closes); exclusive access per 5.5 | P2 |
| `land/respondCounter` | negotiationId, `'accept'\|'decline'` | NEGOTIATION_NOT_AWAITING_PLAYER, COUNTER_EXPIRED, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS | accept → Closing at the counter terms | P5 |
| `land/withdrawOffer` | negotiationId | NEGOTIATION_CLOSED | status `withdrawn` | P5 |
| `land/orderDiligence` | listingId, `'basic'\|'full'` | LISTING_NOT_OPEN, LEVEL_NOT_AVAILABLE, ALREADY_ORDERED, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS | job; report in 1 or 3 weeks | P5 |
| `land/respondTitleFinding` | closingId, `'proceed'\|'cancel'` | DECISION_CLOSED | proceed at the re-priced terms or concession, or cancel with escrow refunded less the check or review cost | P2 (records findings; title findings P5) |
| `land/placeBid` | auctionId, maxBidCents or sealedBidCents | AUCTION_CLOSED, BELOW_MIN_BID, BID_DECREASE, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS (deposit), REORG_COURT_APPROVAL (before plan confirmation) | deposit → `cash.restricted.escrow` | P5 |
| `land/stake` | parcelId, units 1–8 | PARCEL_NOT_OPEN, UNITS_EXCEED_PARCEL, ACCESS_CLOSED, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, REGIME_NOT_SUPPORTED | StakingJob | P2 (state P6) |
| `land/fileRecording` / `land/setAutoFile` | stakingId / stakingId, on | ALREADY_FILED, WINDOW_CLOSED, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS | records with county and files with BLM now / toggles automatic filing | P2 |
| `land/respondStakeConflict` | decisionId, `'yield'\|'contest'` | DECISION_CLOSED, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS | unit dropped, or contest pending 26 weeks | P2 |
| `land/buyDownRoyalty` | interestId, points (0.5 steps) | NO_BUYDOWN_CLAUSE, BUYDOWN_FLOOR, IN_DEFAULT, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS | rate lowered; cost capitalized | P1 |
| `land/exerciseOption` | tenureId | NO_OPTION, OPTION_EXPIRED, IN_DEFAULT, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, REORG_COURT_APPROVAL (before plan confirmation) | Closing (P1 instant); lease converts to owned | P1 |
| `land/setLeaseRenewal` | tenureId, renew | NO_RENEWAL_RIGHT, IN_DEFAULT | renewal election | P1 |
| `land/surrenderLease` | tenureId, confirmUnreclaimed? | UNRECLAIMED_CONFIRM_REQUIRED (P2+) | lease ends after 4 weeks' notice; §5 obligations due after the notice are cancelled; paid AMR and credits forfeited | P1 |
| `land/requestLeaseAmendment` | tenureId, terms (AMR deferral, royalty cut) | NOT_LEASED, NEGOTIATION_OPEN | Negotiation with the lessor (their alternative = taking the claim back) | P5 |
| `land/listClaim` / `land/delistClaim` | tenureId, ask, structures, disclosure | TENURE_NOT_OWNED, TENURE_NOT_FILED, ALREADY_LISTED, LIEN_UNRESOLVED, FEE_UNPAID, JV_CONSENT_REQUIRED, FORCED_SALE (delisting a creditor's sale) | player listing; during a reorganization stay a court sale (no lien checks; delisting after a stalking horse costs its breakup fee) | P4 |
| `land/respondBuyerOffer` | negotiationId, accept / counter terms / decline | NEGOTIATION_NOT_AWAITING_PLAYER, LIEN_SHORTFALL | sale Closing, or counter (P5) | P4 |
| `land/quickSell` | tenureId | TENURE_NOT_OWNED, TENURE_NOT_FILED, LIEN_UNRESOLVED, LIEN_SHORTFALL, FEE_UNPAID | closes next week at the quick-sale price (5.14); during a reorganization stay a court sale with the quick-sale offer as stalking horse, closing at the hearing 3 weeks later | P1 |
| `land/relinquish` | tenureId, confirmUnreclaimed? | TENURE_CANNOT_RELINQUISH, UNRECLAIMED_CONFIRM_REQUIRED, REORG_UNRECLAIMED (open acres during a case) | tenure ends; §6 abandonment check | P1 |
| `land/payLien` / `land/fileSuit` | tenureId, defectId | INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, NO_CLAIM_FOR_SUIT (defect not concealed, or auction quitclaim), SUIT_PENDING | lien cleared / suit pending | P5 |
| `land/respondDispute` | decisionId, `'survey'\|'settle'\|'litigate'\|'yield'` | DECISION_CLOSED, OPTION_NOT_AVAILABLE, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS | see 5.6 boundary disputes | P5 |
| `land/proposeJv` / `land/buyoutJv` / `land/withdrawJv` | listingId or tenureId, JvTerms or offer | JV_NOT_OFFERED, REPUTATION_TOO_LOW, TERMS_OUT_OF_BOUNDS, REORG_COURT_APPROVAL (proposals before plan confirmation) | Negotiation / exit at season end | P6 |

### 5.16 Weekly resolution

Sub-order within each step follows §2.6: in step 3 §5 runs first (calling §3 `supplyTick` as its sub-step a), before §4, §8 and §9; in step 6 §5 (a)–(h) run before §9, §10, §11, §4 and §7; in step 12 §5's settlement sits between §7's gold room and §10 `addLot`; in step 15 §5 acts only when §11 calls it.

- **Step 3, markets refresh.**
  - (a) Take §3's new listing candidates (`supplyTick`, including relists §12 queued through `relistClaim` last week), then assign channel, structures, terms, disposition and defects (5.3–5.6); copy `firstLookUntilTurn` and `starterLease` from the candidate. P2+: call §6 `instantiatePermitStub(state, claimId, { transferDefect? })` for each new listing, after defects are drawn.
  - (b) For each open listing in ID order: advance weeks on market and `m_t`, refresh `ci`, re-price with hysteresis (not while an inspection runs), expire (increment `lapsedListings`; §3 `onListingClosed`), end inspection periods at `untilTurn`, or convert to auction at the deadline. Refresh `U_res` of any open negotiation on it (5.11).
  - (c) Roll background sales (skipped during first look, an inspection period and the starter hold). A sale on a listing with an open negotiation becomes a rival bid instead (5.11).
  - (d) Roll buyer arrivals for player listings (including forced sales and court sales) and create buyer Negotiations; on a court sale whose stalking horse is set, an arrival registers as an overbidder instead (5.14).
  - (e) Open scheduled auctions.
- **Step 5:** §12 places competitor bids on listings and auctions (never on a listing under first look or inspection), and starts competitor staking jobs.
- **Step 6, deals.**
  - (a) Resolve `bestAndFinal` negotiations (deterministic compare), then every Negotiation in `awaitingCounterparty` with `resolveOffer`, after comparing rival bids. Forced-sale and plan-sale listings accept the best offer ≥ the reserve (a plan sale's accepted offer becomes its stalking horse). Court-sale hearings due this week resolve with the competitor caps §12 registered in step 5 and close at once; plan sales past their deadline take their fallback (5.14).
  - (b) Close auctions due this week; handle non-payment of last week's winners (runner-up or relist).
  - (c) Advance closings. Week 1 of a P2+ closing: records-check findings; of a P5+ closing: title-review findings; either opens `land/respondTitleFinding`. At completion: settle lender liens through §11 `lienPayoff` (player sales), transfer the claim owner in §3, create the Tenure, post the ledger, call §6 `registerTenureObligations` and `permitTransferOutcome` (with `sellerBondCarryWeeks`; §6 creates the buyer's `transferOfInterest` obligation there), create ProductionInterests, create any carry loan through §11, set natural-discovery turns for remaining hidden defects, and emit `dealClosed`. A `voidClaim` that slipped past review fails here: the money is spent and the parcel opens with the 1-week head start. Quick sales requested last week close here.
  - (d) Deliver diligence reports.
  - (e) Staking: field completion (tenure `staked`; `registerTenureObligations` creates the recording obligation(s)), auto-recording and filing (pays them; tenure becomes `ownedUnpatented`; `registerTenureObligations` again for the annual obligations), conflict rolls, contest resolutions. Missed recording windows are voided by §6 in step 13, not here.
  - (f) Lease and JV anniversaries: AMR obligations, shortfall and work tests, credit expiry, renewal decisions, option expiry, minimum-annual shortfalls on other interests (owner per 5.12). JV: add last week's recoverable costs and interest; season-end review in the first week after `operatingEndWeek`.
  - (g) Defect clocks: lien demand letters and royalty notices reaching their `naturalDiscoveryTurn`; overstaking discovery (any affected block now `disturbed`, or a new §12 `boundarySurvey` → boundary dispute, 5.6); lien foreclosures; dispute, litigation and suit resolutions (clearing `ops.blockLocked`). §10 calls `onAssay` in its own step-6 slot (5.12).
  - (h) Expire stale counters and lapsed decisions (apply their defaults).
- **Step 12, cleanup:** §7 calls `settleProductionInterests` for each cleanup (5.12), and §4 for sample gold. Cash accruals go to `accrued.royalties` and to `pendingTrueUps`.
- **Step 13, compliance** (D-5.49): §6 applies *statutory* consequences (`forfeitClaim`, `voidLocation`, …) at the end of step 13 of `dueTurn`, ending tenures through `onTenureEnded` (5.14). Every §5-created money obligation (`leaseAdvanceRoyalty`, `leaseShortfallRoyalty`, `workInLieu`, `leaseCure`, `royaltyArrears`, `forfeitureDamages`, `minimumRoyaltyShortfall`) is *billable*, consequence `default`: §11 bills it in its due week and pays it in step 14, and §6 evaluates "missed" in step 13 of `dueTurn + graceWeeks + 1` (§2.6, §6 6.9; §5 creates these with `graceWeeks` 0, so `dueTurn + 1`). For an owner-§5 obligation still unpaid then, §6 calls `land.onObligationMissed(obl)`, which issues a default notice with a cure Obligation (`land.leaseCureWeeks`), or terminates after the cure lapses; owner-§1 obligations go to §1 `investor.onMinimumMissed`. §6 calls `land.revealDefect(tenureId, 'undisclosedReclamation')` when an inspection or baseline finds the extra acres.
- **Step 14, finance:** §11 pays the due week's bills (category `royalty.cash` for §5 obligations), carry-note installments (week 44 north, week 18 arid; `land.carryPaymentWeekByClimate`), the month-end `accrued.royalties` bill, stream receipts, auction balances and patented property tax. Accruals from `settleSaleInterests` (which §10 calls when raw ounces leave inventory, D-10.38, P6) join the month-end `accrued.royalties` bill.
- **Step 15, distress:** §11 calls `land.onForeclose(tenureId)` for a carry note past its cure, `land.forcedSale` for workout listings and `land.transferToCreditor` for lien enforcement; §11 or the player may request a quick sale, which closes in next week's step 6. During a reorganization stay these three calls fail with `REORG_STAY` unless §11 records relief for that creditor. §11 calls `land.onReorganizationFiled(state)` when a filing takes effect and `land.applyPlanTreatments(state)` in the week it confirms a plan (5.14).
- **Step 16, wrap-up:** inbox signals with §13's kinds: `offer.received` / `offer.countered` / `offer.expired`, `offer.bestAndFinal`, `auction.closingSoon`, `auction.result`, `land.diligenceReport`, `land.titleFinding` (records or title finding), `lease.anniversarySoon` (within 4 weeks), `staking.windowSoon` (recording window within 3 weeks), `land.disputeOpened`; and `land.inspectionEnding` (info: an inspection term ends within 1 week, P2) and `land.forcedSale` (warning: a forced-sale listing opened or expired, P4); `land.courtSaleHearing` (warning: a court-sale hearing on a player claim next week, with the stalking-horse bid and the qualified overbid count, P4; 13.10). Stop reasons: offer received, countered or expired; best-and-final; auction closing next week; records or title finding.

Listing supply is §3's (`geology.supply.listingHazardMult`), and opening a withdrawn overlay is §3's `openWithdrawnOverlay`; §5 publishes neither.
- Gold sensitivities (applied through `gm`, 5.2, on §10's real index `goldIdxReal`; money values also carry `cpiIndex` once):

| Item | Elasticity | Lag (wk) | Clamp |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acreage value | 0.8 | 8 | 0.5–2.0 |
| Resource value | 1.3 | 8 | 0.35–2.5 |
| Royalty demand | +0.06 points per unit of `goldIdxReal` (additive) | 13 | ±0.04 |
| Distressed share (of distressedOperator and retiringOperator listings) | −2.5 | 26 | 0.5–3.0 |
| Background sales, buyer arrivals, auction bidders, stake conflicts | 1.5 | 4 | 0.3–3.0 |

### 5.18 Phase plan

- **P1.** Tenure kinds `ownedUnpatented` and `leased` (plus §1's inherited claim). Private channel only (every situation lists privately, with its situation prior, 5.3). Asks are priced by 5.4 with `auth=none`, P = 0, L = 0 and a flat gold index (`gm` ≡ 1, `cpiIndex` ≡ 1). **Fixed asking terms: `acceptAsk` or walk away.** No negotiation, no defects, no diligence; cash only; transfer at action time with flat closing costs ($400 + 1% + the $12 county recording); options exercise instantly. Stubs: `ci = 0` (no §12), so background sales run at the 2%/wk base × §3's `saleQualityMult` and are the only competition; the landman stub prices of 5.4 apply. Leases include royalty in kind, advance AMR (recoupable, life of lease, maxRecoupShare 1.0), a work commitment with automatic in-lieu, term and auto-renewal, and fixed option and buy-down clauses on some listings. The full ProductionInterest waterfall runs (leases, and the investor royalty with its step-down if Backed), for cleanup gold and §4 sample gold. `samplingAccess` answers for owned and leased ground and for listings (casual, seller permission always granted). Player valuation uses §4's minable set and planning costs with `delay`, `permitCostToGo`, `reclamationEstimate` and `bondCarry` all 0 (no §6 yet). **Distress levers (D-5.50):** `land/quickSell` (0.6 × the summary buyer value, closes next week, unmodeled buyer) and lease surrender (advance forfeited, later obligations cancelled). §5 lease obligations are bills paid in step 14 and judged missed at `dueTurn + 1`. Relinquish and surrender have no reclamation consequence until §6 exists. No staking, no claim fees.
- **P1 does not include:** carry notes, listing claims for sale (beyond the quick sale), auctions, estate/distressed listings, patented ground, state tenure, JVs, staking, inherited override royalties (scenario content only, §1 D-1.41).
- **P2.** Staking (federal) with §6's fees and recording obligations; claim-fee and waiver obligations via §6 (counting by claims); fee-paid transfers; the lessee pays maintenance; patented listings (property tax stubbed at 0 until P4); permitted listings with `permitResourceMult` and P, stubs instantiated by §6 at listing; the guaranteed starter permitted lease in each starting district (5.3); `misstatedPermit` from §3's false statements; closing periods with the folded records check (5.5); the fixed-price inspection period and notice-tier `samplingAccess` (5.5); `sellerBondCarryWeeks` as a fixed listing term; disclosed reclamation liability (true = disclosed until P5); relinquish triggers §6 abandonment; background stake conflicts.
- **P3.** No changes.
- **P4.** Seller carry notes (§11; week 44 north, week 18 arid); selling claims to background buyers (fixed offers); lender-lien payoff at sale (`LIEN_SHORTFALL`); `land.forcedSale` (listing format) and `land.transferToCreditor` for §11's workout and lien enforcement and §1's investor foreclosure; property tax live; lease-forfeiture damages as §11 liabilities; reorganization (5.14): the stay on creditor paths, lease and JV treatment, court sales against background buyers, plan treatments and `planInventory`.
- **P5.** The negotiation model (land, plus §9 and §11 reuse, including `vendorPlan`); estate, distressed and auction channels by holder situation, with competitor bids, competitor sales and busts via §3 relists; title defects, diligence and the closing title review; suits and disputes (incl. §12 boundary events, `boundarySurvey`, `ops.blockLocked`, `land.excludeBlocks`); gold sensitivity on asks and royalties (real index); best-and-final; disclosure-based selling with counters; negotiable inspection and bond-carry terms; forced sales by auction; competitors buying quick sales and bidding at court-sale hearings; the no-reserve auction fallback for unsold plan sales; the assay true-up (`onAssay`); lease amendments; P5 lease clause variety (shortfall mode, 50% recoup share, no in-lieu); reputation gates and first look (from §3's candidate); site-sampling permission drawn (0.85); the landman P1 stub is replaced by `landSkill`.
- **P6.** JVs (and AI-proposed JVs); AK-style and Yukon-style tenure and staking (fees and windows from §6); sale-triggered interests (`settleSaleInterests`, the Yukon-style export royalty); owner-contributed machines; delegation (a land specialist auto-files recordings and renewals).
- **Exit gates that touch §5** (§1 1.19 owns the checklist; bots from the §2.12.1 catalog): P1, `leaseOnly` and `buyOnly` show no strict dominance and the landman background stays within ±5 pp of mean survival (stubs on); P2, ≥ 8% of northern listings carry true transferable plan authority (with §3, BALANCE T-15 b; ≈ 10% with §3's D-3.48 stub) and every starting district has the starter permitted lease; P5, competitor contested-listing win share 35–60%, median auction hammer / V_claimed 0.45–0.70, and median accepted private price 75–85% of ask.

### 5.20 Balance levers & risks

- **Biggest profitability levers:**
  - `land.inGroundFrac` (what good evidence costs).
  - `land.royaltyBase` and `amrFrac` (lease burden). Royalties decide seasons on proven ground, so these most directly set the bankruptcy rate of lease-heavy strategies.
  - `defectLambda` (bargain risk).
  - `resMotivationDisc` and `negConcession` (negotiated discount; target: a median accepted price of 75–85% of ask on private listings).
- **Exploit: buy proven listings outright.** Proven ground is priced at 3–4.5% of in-situ gross, which is below the player's P50 NPV. Counters: seller claims are biased upward (§3); evidence classes `report` and `production` are rare (≤ 10% of listings); permitted ground carries P and the multiplier; competitors bid on the same listings. **Sim check:** buying `report`/`production` listings at ask must have positive expected NPV only when the bot also samples: `cautious` must beat `noTest` (§2.12.1 bot catalog) on those listings. Otherwise raise `inGroundFrac`.
- **Exploit: lease, high-grade, surrender.** First-year AMR is paid at signing, royalties are owed on every ounce anyway, and reclamation of the player's disturbance stays with the player. No counter needed beyond those.
- **Exploit: stake-spam.** Each claim costs $286 ($274 BLM + $12 county, §6) plus $200/yr and enters at `speculative`. Above 10 claims the waiver is lost on all claims (§6 warning).
- **Exploit: lowball spam.** Walk probability, the 12-week cooldown and `lowballWalk` reputation hits. Reputation feeds the lessor credence `q` and the accept logit.
- **Exploit: flipping** (buy, prove, sell). This is legitimate as a prospect-generator strategy. It is bounded because buyers value only disclosed evidence at the same `inGroundFrac`, the bid-ask gap is ≈ 25%, and closing costs and weeks are real. Flipping pays only when sampling actually raised the evidence class.
- **Risk: buy-downs too cheap in bull markets.** This is by design (a fixed nominal price). Cap with `buyDownFloorFrac`.
- **Risk: option with 100% royalty credit is near-free.** It appears with p 0.2 and carries the 20% option premium plus a 3% fee. The exercise price floors at $0, so on a rich claim the royalties buy the ground (rent-to-own); the lessor's `U_opt` prices that in.
- **Auctions:** the proxy second-price format removes sniping. The deposit and the non-payment penalty stop griefing. The public opening bid (15% of V_claimed) stops absolute auctions from selling permitted ground for $500; watch the sim's median hammer/V_claimed (target 0.45–0.70).
- **Diligence as a click-tax (fixed).** A cheap `basic` check would be near-universal, so it now rides in every P5+ closing as a title contingency (D-5.31); likewise §6's $250 records check rides in every P2+ closing, with a walk-away right on a material finding (D-5.45). The real choices are `full` (3 weeks and $7.5k, with rivals circling), diligence *before* offering (prices defects in before commitment), and the auction cap. Watch the sim's share of hidden-defect losses: target 10–20% of purchased claims carry an undetected defect for players who skip `full`.
- **Lease vs buy dominance.** At P50 a lease costs several times the purchase price (5.7), so cash-rich bots will buy. Run `leaseOnly` and `buyOnly` (§2.12.1) on the Bootstrapper (cash-constrained) and Backed (cash-rich) starts: the dominance matrix must show the Bootstrapper surviving more often by leasing, and `cautious` (samples) beating `noTest` among buyers. If `buyOnly` dominates at every cash level, raise `land.askMarkup` or lower `royaltyBase`.
- **Permitted supply and the first northern season (§0.6, BALANCE T-15 b).** Under full rules a careful run mines in season 1 only on ground with authority in hand. Levers: §3's true permit-stub shares (the supply), the guaranteed starter permitted lease per starting district (5.3), and `land.permitResourceMult` / `permitReplacementUsd` (what permitted ground costs). Gate: ≥ 8% of northern listings carry true transferable plan authority (BALANCE T-15 b; preflight ≈ 10% with §3's D-3.48 stub), in service of BALANCE O-02 (first-season profit 15–35% for `cautious`).
- **Exploit: inspection to park listings.** An inspection freezes a listing for up to 8 weeks. Counter: the fee (≈ 0.7% of the ask per week, × 1.5 at notice tier) is lost on walking; sellers with `ci` > 0.5 refuse; one inspection per listing.
- **Quick sale as an exit lever.** At 0.6 × the summary buyer value it returns under a third of a typical purchase price (5.14 example): a real lever against insolvency from P1, but never a profitable flip. Watch the P1 share of bankruptcies preceded by a quick sale; if quick sales rescue runs that should fail, lower `land.quickSaleFrac`.
- **"Offer just above the floor and wait."** Offers with z ≥ 0 never trigger a walk, and the final counter lands at `U_res`. The counters are that patience costs weeks of rival risk (background sales ≈ 2–20%/wk, competitor bids), that the reservation is unknown (the landman band is ±20% and noisy), and that `U_res` drifts with gold momentum while the player waits.
- **Reputation snowball.** First look (≥ 70) and the ±1.0 logit compound. They are capped by §1's annual caps on positive reputation inputs (+3/yr from deals).
- **Reorganization as a land tool (P4; 5.14).** Three uses to watch: (1) filing to escape a `LIEN_SHORTFALL` or a creditor's forced sale: countered by §11's filing cost (≈ $40,000 plus the trustee's share), the credit and reputation hits and the plan's payments, so a filing should never beat an ordinary sale for a solvent company; (2) rejecting expensive leases: the lessor's claim (arrears plus 1–3 years of AMR) joins the unsecured class, so rejection turns future AMR into the plan's dividend on 1–3 years of it, an intended lever of reorganization whose price is losing the ground; (3) court sales as a price lever: competition lifts the expected quick-sale price only ≈ 5% (example) at the cost of 3 weeks. Sim check (BALANCE, P4): the `cautious` bot never files while solvent, and among runs that file, the share that reach confirmation and keep at least one claim is reported beside S2 and B2.

### 5.21 Tests

- **Asking terms:** example A gives A = 18,000, V_claimed = 174,151.8, askSale = 205,000 (noise 1), R = 132,484 ± 1, royalty 0.13, AMR 12,000, buy-down 27,000/pt, in-lieu $2.78 (before rounding).
- **Gold sensitivity:** real gold index 1.3 multiplies Rv by 1.3^1.3 = 1.406 and A by 1.234; the royalty ask rises 1.8 points. `pD` (distressedOperator and retiringOperator listings) at real index 0.7 = 0.27 × 0.7^−2.5 = 0.659, and at 1.5 = 0.135 (clamped). With `cpiIndex` 1.1 and real index 1.0 (nominal 1.1), A, Rv and P each rise exactly 10% (escalated once, not 1.1^1.3), and `pD` and the background-sale probability do not move (`gm` reads the real index and carries no CPI).
- **Channels by situation:** an estate holder always lists `estate` (P5+) and never draws the distressed roll; prospector and absentee holders never list `distressed`; a `competitorBust` candidate lists `auction` w.p. 0.30, else `distressed`; over 20,000 seeded candidates with §3's situation mix, the distressed share of NPC listings at real index 1.0 is 0.081 ± 0.01. First look is copied from the candidate and never drawn on `'land-list'` (adding or removing §3's first-look roll leaves every other `'land-list'` draw unchanged). A third lapsed listing by the same holder raises m0 by 0.24, and a fourth by no more.
- **Negotiation:** example B probabilities to 3 dp (0.176 / 0.189 / 0.635; 0.415 / 0.081 / 0.504; insult 0 / 0.434 / 0.382 / 0.184); counters $180,000 then $170,000; the lease alternative U = 155,310 ± 5; the lease ask U = 204,076 ± 5; landSkill 80 round-1 pAccept 0.256; fraudulent-seller counter to $90k = $165,000.
- **Negotiation properties (fast-check):** probabilities in [0, 1] summing to 1; pAccept = 0 when z < 0; pWalk = 0 when z ≥ 0 and patience ≥ 1; after the final offer pReject = pCounter = 0; a counter is never below U_res (cpBuys: above) and never moves away from the player; the final counter equals U_res; `U_res` never exceeds `U_last` after a refresh; the bisection solution reproduces U_new within $1; best-and-final is decided without a draw; the same seed always gives the same outcome. The same suite runs with `direction: 'cpBuys'` (buyer of a player claim).
- **Settlement:** example C gives deliveries 2.400 / 12.159 / 5.160, player 100.281, cash attributable royalty accrual $11,052.72, stream receipt $3,508.80, credit $0. JV example: 31.989 / 118.011. Step-down example: delivery 5.057, `stepped` true, minimum annual ended. A cash interest with an AMR credit accrues `val − min(maxRecoupShare × val, credits)`.
- **Conservation (fast-check):** Σ deliveries_m + player lot_m = G_m exactly in integer milli-ounces, for random interest sets, rates (each level < 1; otherwise rejected with PI_BURDEN_TOO_HIGH), credits, caps and step-downs. Credits never go negative. FIFO expiry is exact at the expiry turn. JV `unrecovered` never goes negative, and interest accrues at the weekly-converted rate.
- **AMR modes:** advance-recoupable with maxRecoupShare 0.5 never offsets more than half of any royalty. Shortfall mode bills exactly `max(0, min − paid)`. Credits are forfeited on termination.
- **Option and buy-down:** option exercise price 190,950 for the 5.7 inputs; credited royalties above the price give $0, never negative. Buy-down below `minRate` returns BUYDOWN_FLOOR.
- **Staking:** 4 claims on a seasonal road cost $2,144 (field $1,000 + county $48 + BLM $1,096), posting $1,344 to `mineral.properties` and $800 to `exp.claimFees`; the amounts come from `permits.fed.*` (changing §6's county fee to $30 changes the total to $2,216 with no §5 edit). At location `registerTenureObligations` creates exactly one `claimRecording` obligation due at `locatedTurn + 13` (plus a `countyRecording` obligation when the overlay window is 4 weeks); filing satisfies both and a second call creates the annual obligations. An unfiled claim is voided only by §6 (step 13 at the due turn) through `onTenureEnded(claimId, 'void')`, and the parcel reopens 1 week later. A competitor job completing first aborts the player's job.
- **Closing costs:** a $10,500 unproven claim closes for $517 in P1 and $767 from P2 (records check), never including the $15 BLM transfer fee, which appears once, as §6's `transferOfInterest` obligation.
- **Records check at closing (P2+):** a listing presenting `planApproved` whose true stub is `noticeOnFile` produces a `misstatedPermit` finding in closing week 1 with certainty; proceeding re-prices the fixed ask to `auth = 'notice'`; cancelling refunds escrow less $250; a stand-alone check within 4 weeks waives the folded one. A recorded `nonTransferablePermit` cause is found iff `detectU < 0.90`; `undisclosedReclamation` is never found by the check.
- **Sampling access:** owned, leased, staked (filed or not) and JV-operated claims return `operator` with `untilTurn` null in every phase (so §4's P1 programs pass check 1); a P1 listing returns `casual` until expiry; a P5 listing with `ci` 0.6 returns `none` unless an inspection is active; an active notice-tier inspection returns `operator` with the seller's real notice id until `untilTurn`.
- **Inspection:** example A's listing, 4 weeks: fee $5,700 casual and $8,600 notice; refused at `ci` 0.55 and on auctions; notice tier on a seller with no recorded notice or plan → NO_SELLER_NOTICE; no background sale, competitor bid or re-pricing while it runs; closing by `untilTurn + 1` credits the fee against the price (basis unchanged in total), otherwise it posts to `exp.ga`.
- **Obligation timing (D-5.49):** a P1 lease AMR due in week t and paid by §11 in step 14 of week t is never marked missed and never fires `land.onObligationMissed` or the −5 reputation event; an AMR unpaid at step 13 of week t + 1 fires both exactly once and creates a cure obligation due `leaseCureWeeks` later. A Backed royalty-minimum shortfall obligation has owner `'§1'` and never reaches `land.onObligationMissed`.
- **Sale-triggered interests (P6):** a Yukon-style regime interest accrues $0.27 × fine oz on a refinery (export) sale and $0 on a local-buyer sale.
- **Assay true-up (P5):** a 3% cash interest accrued at f_est 0.85 on a cleanup whose lot then assays at 0.83 posts Δ = val × (0.83/0.85 − 1) to `accrued.royalties`; in-kind deliveries are unchanged; two shipments covering one cleanup's lot true it up exactly once in total.
- **Auctions:** the English proxy example gives a hammer of 358,750 and total 394,625. An absolute auction with no other eligible bidder hammers at the opening bid ($90,000 for V_claimed $600k). Sealed auctions are first-price. No bid at or above max(opening, reserve) leads to relist or withdrawal. Non-payment passes the claim to the runner-up at its last eligible bid.
- **Defects:** over 20,000 seeded listings, defect counts match λ within 2%, and detection rates per level match the table within 2%. Every defect found by `basic` is also found by `full`; re-ordering `basic` never finds a new defect. Patented listings never generate `voidClaim` or `overstaking`, and patented purchases never carry lien losses (title insurance). A void claim found by the closing title review cancels the deal at a cost of only the review fee.
- **Disputes:** over 10,000 seeded disputes, survey dismissal of spurious claims ≈ 0.8 and litigation wins ≈ 0.15 (real) / 0.6 (spurious), each within 2%. A spurious dispute with `assertedFrac` 0.10 on a 20-block claim asserts 2 blocks; the asserted blocks carry `ops.blockLocked` from opening until resolution and never after; a claim with a §12 `boundarySurvey` dismisses every spurious dispute automatically and detects a hidden overstake iff `detectU < 0.90`. `land.excludeBlocks` removes blocks from valuation and plans without a ledger posting.
- **Reputation gates:** an estate listing rejects `acceptAsk` at reputation 19 (REPUTATION_TOO_LOW); first-look listings get no background sale or competitor bid before `firstLookUntilTurn`.
- **Stream isolation:** adding a diligence draw leaves listing asks, auction results and the gold price unchanged.
- **Hidden-info guard:** UI selectors for listings, tenures, auctions and negotiations never return `hidden`, `hiddenDefects`, `detectU`, `reserveCents`, `reservationU`, `rivalBidU`, `motivation` or `competingInterest` (the scrambled-hidden-state bot test from §2.12). Scrambling a player-held claim's true geology leaves `buyerClaimView` at every disclosure level, `V_buyer` and every background-buyer offer unchanged (property); `gradeView × payBcyView = ozView` exactly.
- **Valuation:** the 5.13 example gives NPV P10/P50/P90 of −700,321 / 288,530 / 1,816,753 (±1), $408,609 with a plan in hand, a breakeven grade of 0.01022 oz/bcy (§4's cutoff on the same block 0.00865), a breakeven spot of $3,555 (±1), `breakevenOz` 1,403.5 at the $205,000 ask (NPV at that ounce count equals the price within $1), and gold ±20% → $809,924 / −$232,864. In P1 (no §6) the P50 value is $460,609 (delay, permit, reclamation and bond terms all 0). With zero burden and capital charge, `breakevenGradeOzPerBcy` equals §4 `cutoffOzPerBcy` for every block.
- **Quick sale, forced sale, transfer:** the 5.14 P1 quick sale pays $48,537 and closes the next week; from P5 a competitor whose cap exceeds the price buys at the price. A forced sale with reserve $X never accepts an offer below $X, cannot be delisted (FORCED_SALE), and pays §11's `lienPayoff` before any cash reaches the player; unsold after 8 weeks it closes `expired`. `transferToCreditor` ends the tenure `foreclosed`, sets §3's owner to the creditor and writes off the basis net of accumulated depletion. A sale whose proceeds are below the lender payoff with insufficient cash fails with LIEN_SHORTFALL.
- **Reorganization (P4; 5.14):** the court-sale example resolves to $48,537 (no overbidder), $50,964 less a $971 breakup fee (one) and $76,849 less $971 (two), and over 10,000 seeds its mean net is $51,000 ± 1%; a stalking horse with the highest maximum keeps the claim at max(S, min(M_h, M_2nd + 0.05 × S)); a claim with a $60,000 lender lien sells in a court sale without `LIEN_SHORTFALL`, the lender receives min(60,000, proceeds − fee) and the rest of its claim is reported to §11 as a deficiency; `forcedSale`, `transferToCreditor` and `onForeclose` fail with `REORG_STAY` from the filing to confirmation and succeed for a creditor §11 has granted relief; a forced listing open at filing is withdrawn that week; a title lien's foreclosure turn does not arrive during the case; the filing never moves a lease to `inDefault`, an AMR falling due after the filing and left unpaid reaches `land.onObligationMissed` at `dueTurn + 1` as usual, `assume` pays `cureCents` at confirmation and `reject` ends the tenure `terminated` with a rejection claim of arrears + AMR × min(3, max(1, 0.15 × years left)) (a $10,000 AMR with 10 years left → $15,000 + arrears); a plan without an election for every lease fails `REORG_LEASE_ELECTION`; an unsold `sell` claim takes its fallback at confirmation + 26 weeks (surrender if encumbered; else quick sale in P4, no-reserve auction in P5); `acceptAsk`, `makeOffer`, `placeBid`, `requestInspection`, `exerciseOption` and JV proposals fail `REORG_COURT_APPROVAL` during the stay while `land/stake` succeeds; `land/relinquish` with open acres fails `REORG_UNRECLAIMED`; scrambling the true geology of every held claim leaves every `planInventory` value unchanged.
- **Tenure end:** every path that ends a tenure produces one `TenureEndReason` from the shared enum and runs §5's and §6's handlers exactly once each, whichever section initiated it; `voidedByExam` writes the basis off like `void`.
- **Sale accounting:** selling a claim with $X of accumulated depletion debits `mineral.accumDepletion` by $X; the ledger balances.
- **Carry note:** the annual installment falls in week 44 on a northern claim and week 18 on an arid claim, each a §1 `monthEndWeeks` entry (October and April month ends); a company holding carry notes in both climates pays each in its own claim's week.

### 5.22 Decisions

- D-5.1 — The ask is built from the seller's *claimed* figures and the reservation from their *private belief*. — This makes fraudulent sellers fold fast on deep discounts, an honest and readable tell, and ties §3's honesty model to negotiation without extra rules. The tell is read from counters to *low* offers (an accepted offer is binding), so probing low is the skill it rewards.
- D-5.2 — Sellers price resource as a fraction of in-situ gross value by evidence class (0–4.5%), not by DCF. — It matches how illiquid claim markets talk ("$/oz in the ground"), is cheap to compute, and reproduces every land anchor (5.4 calibration).
- D-5.3 — Royalty demand ripples additively in points (+6 points per 1.0 of gold index, lag 13, cap ±4). Signed contracts never re-price. — The guide's "royalty in points" convention. Fixed contracts are what make timing a lease a decision.
- D-5.4 — Resource value elasticity 1.3 and acreage elasticity 0.8 (refining the ≈ 1.0 anchor), both on §10's *real* gold index. Every money value (acreage, resource, permit, improvements, closing) is escalated exactly once by `cpiIndex`, including the gold-denominated resource value (D-10.32). — Claim value is leveraged to real margin. With the real index, inflation alone moves asks by exactly CPI, never by CPI^1.3, and never moves shares or probabilities.
- D-5.5 — The AMR floor is $2,000, not the anchor's $5,000. — A $5k AMR on a $10k unproven claim would make leasing irrational. Claims with history still land at $5–50k.
- D-5.6 — A player company is one locator, so player-staked federal claims are 20-acre individual claims. Association placers (40–160 ac) arrive only by acquisition and count as one claim for the waiver. — R1: a corporation counts as one locator. This gives association placers real waiver value.
- D-5.7 — A leased claim never uses the player's waiver count. The lessee pays the full maintenance fee. — The lessor's waiver status isn't modeled. Keeps the waiver test about the player's own holdings.
- D-5.8 — One negotiation round per counterparty per week, resolved in step 6. — Real-time deals create rival-buyer risk and make diligence time matter. Replays stay simple. (OQ-5.1; owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed.)
- D-5.9 — The reservation is a hard floor. The player never sees response probabilities. A land skill ≥ 70 (landman owner or a good specialist) gets a noisy ±20% band. — Keeps hidden information hidden while giving the edge a tangible, purchasable form.
- D-5.10 — The counter keeps the player's deal structure and solves the primary term by bisection on the counterparty's utility. — It is generic across land, equipment and loans, and avoids hand-written counter logic per subject.
- D-5.11 — Property-level interests each apply to gross. The JV split applies to post-burden metal. Streams and investor royalties apply to attributable production. — Matches common practice (burdens run with the land; financings attach to the company's share). It is non-compounding and easy to explain.
- D-5.12 — In-kind deductions are by raw weight. Cash interests are valued at spot × best-known fineness, trued up at assay. In-kind ounces are presented net (never in inventory). — No hidden truth leaks into the ledger, and conservation is exact. §11 confirms the presentation.
- D-5.13 — AMR credits offset in-kind royalties at the spot-valued ounce, FIFO. The default is unlimited carryforward with maxRecoupShare 1.0 (P1); P5 adds 2-year expiry and 50% recoup variants. — Simple first, real clause variety later.
- D-5.14 — Buy-down prices are fixed in nominal dollars at signing. — Turns a gold rally into a real buy-down opportunity, a timing decision.
- D-5.15 — Six title-defect types, with two diligence levels. A discovered void claim gives a 1-week staking head start. — Each defect maps to an existing system (fees, blocks, liens, ARO, permits, interests). The head start rewards diligence.
- D-5.16 — Auctions use an English proxy (second-price) or a sealed first-price format, with a 10% buyer's premium. They are as-is with basic diligence only. — Removes sniping, and keeps auctions the cheapest and riskiest channel.
- D-5.17 — P1 purchases transfer instantly. Closing periods start in P2, when the folded records check (D-5.45) gives the closing something to do; the title review joins in P5. — No reason to make P1 players wait when there is nothing to do during closing.
- D-5.18 — Seller carry notes pay annually in week 44 (the October month end; §11 `payMonths: [10]`). Arid ground pays in week 18 instead (D-5.56). — After freeze-up, so the season's gold is in, and a §1 `monthEndWeeks` entry, so §11 schedules it like every other loan (week 40 was not a month end). Lenders' seasonal products are §11's.
- D-5.19 — Patented purchases include title insurance that absorbs lien defects and boundary disputes (patented ground is surveyed, so overstaking is never generated there). — The reason patented closings take 4 weeks and cost more; a real difference between tenures (R5: title insurance is generally unavailable for unpatented claims).
- D-5.20 — Lessee-caused forfeiture costs damages equal to the lessor's V_belief, plus a reputation hit. — Makes the lessee's Sept 1 obligation as dangerous as it is in the real world.
- D-5.21 — A purchase assumes all pre-existing disturbance. A lease or JV assumes only its own disturbance plus re-disturbed blocks. — Mirrors operator-responsibility practice and gives leases one more risk advantage.
- D-5.22 — Option and buy-down clauses ship in P1 as fixed terms. — Cheap to implement, and they give P1 lease decisions real depth.
- D-5.23 — The valuation cost is §4's planning cost (north $12/bcy mine-wash + $2.50 per bcy stripped; arid $14 + $2.20; ground multipliers; §11's trailing actual after 4 operating weeks) plus §5's $4/bcy capital charge. — One cost model for cutoff and value (D-5.47); still calibrated to R3's breakeven grades (≈ 0.008 oz/bcy at low strip, ≈ 0.01 at 6:1).
- D-5.24 — Landman edge follows §1 1.7: the owner is a skill-80 land specialist that does not stack with a hire (`landSkill` = the higher). From P5 that gives +0.48 accept logit, +0.096 detection and the hint band; in P1–P4 §1's stub applies (asks ×0.925, royalty −1 point). — §1 owns backgrounds; one skill variable keeps the landman and a hired specialist exactly comparable (§1's parity rule).
- D-5.25 — Buyers of player claims value disclosed evidence only, never truth. This includes §12 competitors, which read `buyerClaimView` (D-12.46). — Required by §2's hidden-information rule. It makes disclosure a real choice.
- D-5.26 — Leasing *out* player claims to AI operators is out of scope through P6. — It would need reduced-form AI production on player ground. Revisit after P6.
- D-5.27 — ProductionInterest is extended with additive fields (`origin`, `level`, `seniority`, `rateUnit`, `trigger`, `recoupCredits`, `cap`, `stepDown`, `runsWithClaims`, `excludedClaimIds`, `costRecovery`, `streamPricePerFineOzCents`, `paidToDate`). `minimumAnnual` becomes a structured record, and the pre-agreed `advanceRecoupable` flag is kept in step with it. An underlying recorded royalty is `kind:'leaseRoyalty'` with `origin:'recordedOverride'`. — Keeps the pre-agreed union intact while covering every real case, including §1's payback-then-tail investor royalty.
- D-5.28 — Unrecouped AMR credits are forfeited on termination. They count toward an option price only through `royaltiesCreditedShare`. — Standard lease drafting, and it closes a credit-banking exploit.
- D-5.29 — Distressed share elasticity is −2.5 with a 26-week lag (clamped 0.5–3×). — Busts follow price falls with a lag. It reproduces "falling gold creates distressed sellers" at a visible but not overwhelming rate.
- D-5.30 — The default for a lease renewal decision is to renew. — Losing ground through inaction is harsher than the 1-point step-up.
- D-5.31 — A `basic` title review rides in every P5+ non-auction closing as a contingency (cost added to closing costs; findings → proceed at a concession or cancel). — A $750 check that every sensible buyer runs was a click-tax; real purchase agreements carry a title contingency. `full` diligence, pre-offer diligence and the auction cap remain real choices.
- D-5.32 — Detection uses one stored uniform per defect (`detectU`) compared against the level's probability. — `full` ⊇ `basic` by construction, repeat orders cannot re-roll, and detection is stream-isolated from everything else.
- D-5.33 — Settlement arithmetic runs in integer milli-ounces. — Float subtraction cannot guarantee the exact conservation the §2.14 property test demands.
- D-5.34 — `fineOz`+`inKind` settles exactly like `rawOz` (raw gold carries its own fineness); the fine-ounce form that differs economically is cash at spot × fine content (`grossValue`). Lease generation uses only rawOz/inKind and grossValue/cash. — Satisfies "basis raw or fine" without a degenerate second in-kind mode, and accepts §1's `fineOz` investor royalty unchanged.
- D-5.35 — §5's gold multiplier `gm` is §10's `rippleRate` on `goldIdxRealAt(turn − lag)`, and §5 applies `cpiIndex` explicitly, once, to money values only. — One rule with §10 (D-10.32): the real index keeps distressed and background-sale rates from drifting with inflation, and explicit escalation keeps shares and probabilities CPI-free. P1–P4 are unchanged (both indices are 1).
- D-5.36 — Auctions have a public opening bid of 15% of V_claimed (min $1,000); non-payment passes the lot to the runner-up. — Without a floor, an absolute auction with no rival bidder sold permitted ground for one increment.
- D-5.37 — `U_ask` is frozen when a negotiation opens; `U_res` refreshes weekly as `min(R_t, U_last)`; best-and-final is a deterministic utility compare; after the final offer, anything short of acceptance is a walk. — Market drift keeps acting during a deal without letting sellers retract their own counters, and the end state of every negotiation is defined.
- D-5.38 — Player valuation discounts operating value by the seasons until production authority and charges bond carry. — "Permitted ground is worth far more" is mostly *time*; in the example a plan in hand is worth ≈ $120k to the player, which the seller's P and permit multiplier approximate.
- D-5.39 — Patented ground skips the BLM 3809 tiers (state permit path, §6) and is bankable (§11). Its property tax uses an assessed value equal to acreage value A × cpiIndex. — Gives patented ground real reasons to cost 10× raw unpatented acreage, and keeps tax independent of truth and of the player's estimate.
- D-5.40 — JV asks are generated as multiples of the royalty ask (gross 1.2×, after-costs 3.2×), clamped to 10–35% and 25–50%. JV cost-recovery interest accrues weekly on last week's closed costs. — It prices JVs near the owner's indifference with the lease, and the one-week lag removes the same-week dependency on §11.
- D-5.41 — Staked claims carry the locator's rights (sampling, notice work) but cannot be sold, leased or optioned until filed. A missed county window voids the claim like a missed BLM window. — Matches the 1872 Law's location-then-record sequence; closes a flip-before-filing exploit.
- D-5.42 — Closing costs are $400 fixed for unpatented (deed and filing) and $1,500 for patented, plus 1%, plus §6's county recording fee. — The earlier $1,200 fixed fee was 12% of an unproven claim's price; a quitclaim deed and recording cost a few hundred dollars.
- D-5.43 — The listing channel follows the holder's §3 situation: estate holders list as estates; competitor busts list as distressed (70%) or at auction (30%); the gold-rippled distressed roll applies only to `distressedOperator` and `retiringOperator` holders, with its base renormalized from 0.08 to 0.27 so the overall share stays ≈ 8%; private-channel motivation, patience and structures come from the situation. First look and relists come from §3's candidate. — One decision per fact: §3 owns who sells and why, §5 owns how the sale is run. A prospector never turns into a trustee sale, and the visible situation becomes an honest coarse tell.
- D-5.44 — §5 owns sampling access: `samplingAccess(claimId)` answers for held ground and listings from P1, and a fixed-price, exclusive inspection period (2–8 weeks, 0.7% of the ask per week, × 1.5 at notice tier, credited if the player buys) opens notice-tier testing of listed ground from P2; it becomes a negotiable offer term in P5. — This is §4's OQ-4.1 default made concrete. Test-before-buy has a real price (the fee is lost on walking) and a real risk (sellers with hot interest refuse), and P1 programs pass their access check on owned ground.
- D-5.45 — §6's $250 records check rides in every P2+ purchase, lease and option closing, with a walk-away (or re-priced proceed) on a material finding; the stand-alone check stays for pre-offer use. — At $250 against six-figure deals the check was a universal click with no decision. Folding it in also protects the onboarding coach from steering a novice onto a misstated plan.
- D-5.46 — A false permit statement is a deterministic `misstatedPermit` defect (from P2; always concealed, found with certainty by any records check or `basic` diligence, suable). A drawn `nonTransferablePermit` writes its cause (suspension, bond cancel notice or forfeiture) into §6's real record, so a records check finds it at 0.90. Surviving authority on a non-transferable package is `casual`. — §5's price, §6's record and §3's statement can then never disagree, and a $250 check cannot beat $7,500 of diligence on something the record does not show (undisclosed acres stay at 0).
- D-5.47 — §4 owns the minable set, recovery, payable and planning costs; §5 owns NPV, adding only a capital charge. Valuation runs on `minableOzP*` (metal oz, alloy fineness), and `breakevenOz` is the minable ounce count at which NPV equals the price. — One cost model: the player sees one cutoff (§4) and one "after royalties and capital" breakeven (§5) that differ for a visible reason. Mostly through payable 0.95, the example's P50 falls from $409k to $289k.
- D-5.48 — Creditors act on claims through two §5 functions: `forcedSale` (creditor-controlled listing from P4, auction from P5, reserve set by §11, proceeds to `lienPayoff` first) and `transferToCreditor` (tenure ends `foreclosed`, basis written off, §6 operator change). Lender liens are paid from proceeds (`LIEN_SHORTFALL`); title and vendor liens must be cleared first (`LIEN_UNRESOLVED`). — §11's workout, prepay and rescue liens and §1's investor foreclosure need one tested path; the carry-note `onForeclose` (revert to seller, no deficiency) stays separate because its economics differ.
- D-5.49 — Every §5-created money obligation is billable (consequence `default`): §11 bills and pays it in step 14 of its due week, and §6 judges it missed in step 13 of `dueTurn + 1`, then calls the owner (§5 `land.onObligationMissed`, or §1 for the investor minimum). — A paid AMR could otherwise be marked missed in step 13 of the week it is paid in step 14, firing default notices and −5 reputation every year.
- D-5.50 — The quick sale (0.6 × the summary buyer value, closes next week) ships in P1, together with lease surrender; full selling stays in P4/P5. — P1 must be playable to bankruptcy *or* a fight against it; without a claim-side lever the only P1 exits were dealer iron sales and owner cash.
- D-5.51 — The guaranteed starter permitted listing (P2+) is a lease with option: AMR ≤ $15,000 × cpi, option fee 0, 13 weeks of seller bond carry, a 13-week hold from background sales and a 26-week minimum life. Its royalty and option price follow the normal formulas. — A Bootstrapper can then start a northern season on permitted ground without a 14–18-month plan; the price of the shortcut is a permitted-ground royalty, not a cash wall (§0.6).
- D-5.52 — One tenure-end enum (`TenureEndReason`, including `voidedByExam`) and one shared `onTenureEnded` event that runs §5's then §6's handler, whichever section initiates; leases end `terminated`. — The two sections had different reason names and no void-by-exam handling; one event removes double write-offs and missed permit consequences.
- D-5.53 — Every claim fee and window is §6's (`permits.fed.*`, overlay county window, `permits.ak.*`, `permits.yukon.*`); §5 runs the field flow and pays §6's obligations, and only §6 voids. The BLM transfer-of-interest fee is charged once, as §6's obligation, and the deed's county recording reads §6's $12 per claim. — Two copies of the fee table had already diverged (county $30 vs $12; staking $2,216 vs $2,144; waiver filing $15 vs $27).
- D-5.54 — §5 provides `settleSaleInterests` (sale-triggered interests; regime royalties skip local-buyer sales, P6) and `onAssay` (cash accruals at f_est re-valued at assay, FIFO by raw oz, P5); f_est is fineness per *weighed* raw oz (alloy × (1 − dirt)). — §5 owns every ProductionInterest settlement; §10 only reports sales and assays. The Yukon-style royalty applies to exports, and a local-buyer sale is not one.
- D-5.55 — Sales close fee-paid (the seller of record pays or waives the current year; waiver credit never transfers; `FEE_UNPAID` for a player seller), and `sellerBondCarryWeeks` (0–13) is a sale and lease term, fixed by the listing in P2–P4 and negotiable from P5. — Matches §6 D-6.27 and 6.12 without a hidden cross-owner waiver state; bond carry is how real buyers keep a permitted operation running through the transfer.
- D-5.56 — A seller carry note's annual payment falls at the month end at or after its claim district's typical season end + 2 weeks, by climate template (`land.carryPaymentWeekByClimate`: northern week 44, `payMonths: [10]`; arid week 18, `payMonths: [4]`). It replaces the single `land.carryPaymentWeek` 44. — Week 44 was "after freeze-up" only in the north; arid ground works October–April (§1 1.2), so a week-44 payment fell at the start of its season with no gold in hand. Keying the week to the claim's own district keeps D-5.18's rationale (the season's gold is in) in every climate. §11 does the same for its annual tests with `finance.seasonYearEndWeek` (D-11.62), but on the company's primary climate, because a carry note belongs to one claim and a covenant to the whole company.
- D-5.57 — In a reorganization (§11, P4) the automatic stay blocks every creditor path on the player's ground from filing to confirmation: `forcedSale`, `transferToCreditor`, carry-note reversion (`onForeclose`) and title-lien foreclosure, unless §11 records relief for that creditor; open forced listings are withdrawn at filing. Claim-holding obligations (§6) are not stayed. — This is what Chapter 11 and Subchapter V give a debtor (11 U.S.C. §362(a)), and it is the reason to file: the ground stays in the company while the plan is built. Sept 1 still forfeits because §6's rules sit under the regulatory exception.
- D-5.58 — A filing never terminates or defaults a lease or JV; pre-filing cure clocks freeze, post-filing obligations must be paid on time, and the plan assumes (cure at confirmation) or rejects (tenure `terminated`, lessor's claim = arrears + AMR × min(3, max(1, 0.15 × years left))) each one. — Bankruptcy-termination clauses are unenforceable (§365(e)(1)), §365(d)(3) keeps post-filing rent current, and §502(b)(6) caps a landlord's damages; mapping AMR onto rent makes rejection a priced way to shed bad leases.
- D-5.59 — During the stay a claim sale outside the ordinary course (listing or quick sale) is a court sale: a stalking-horse bid, a 3-week notice, overbids of at least 5% from background buyers and (P5) competitors, a 2% breakup fee to a losing stalking horse, and a sale free and clear of liens, which attach to the proceeds; there is no credit bidding. — Section 363 sales work this way; the notice period trades speed for competition, and free-and-clear removes the `LIEN_SHORTFALL` dead end that blocks underwater sales outside a case. Leaving out credit bids keeps lenders as holders of money, not operators of ground (they get ground only through a plan surrender).
- D-5.60 — The plan treats each claim as keep, sell (plan sale with a reserve and a 26-week deadline, then surrender or a no-reserve sale) or surrender (`transferToCreditor` at confirmation); §5's `planInventory` values claims at the summary buyer view (collateral) and the quick-sale price (liquidation), never truth. Buying, leasing, optioning, JV proposals and auction bids are refused until confirmation; staking stays open; relinquishing a claim with open acres is refused during the case. — §11's feasibility, cram-down and best-interest tests need claim values that the player can see and that agree with what the claim would really fetch in §5's markets; new acquisitions outside the ordinary course need court approval the game does not model before a plan exists, while staking is a miner's ordinary business.

### 5.23 Open questions

- **OQ-5.1 — Negotiation pacing.** Owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed. One round per week (D-5.8), so a deal takes 2–4 weeks and rivals can intervene; instant multi-round haggling inside one turn was the rejected alternative (faster, but no rival risk). No §5 question is open.

### 5.24 Sources

- **R1 (U.S. federal, 2026):**
  - BLM fees: $25 processing + $49 location + $200 per 20 ac initial maintenance = $274 per placer claim (fees effective 2024-09-01, unchanged for the 2027 assessment year); $200 per 20 ac annual fee due Sept 1 with automatic forfeiture; $15 transfer-of-interest and affidavit fees; Small Miner Waiver ≤ 10 claims, $100 work per claim, Dec 30 affidavit.
  - Canonical fee values live in §6 (`permits.fed.*`, D-5.53); §5 cites them for its examples.
  - Claim rules: 90-day BLM recording window; county fees $12–30; 20 ac per locator, 160-ac association with 8 locators, a corporation counts as one locator (model knowledge); association counts as one claim for the waiver (verify); the summer-staking double-fee trap.
  - Patent moratorium since 1994-10-01; no federal royalty on unpatented claims; contracted staking $100–500 per claim (model knowledge); plan permitting costs $10k–250k.
- **R2 (Alaska and Yukon, 2025–26):**
  - AK state claims of 40/160 ac; rent $40 / $85 / $205 per 40 ac by age; $100 labor per 40 ac with cash in lieu ≤ 5 years; 45-day recording and first rent; 3% net-income royalty with rent credited.
  - Yukon creek claims ≈ 23 ac; $10 application; $200 representation work; travel-time window; royalty C$0.375/oz on export (≈ $0.27).
  - Typical operation output 300–700 crude oz/yr (used for `lessorAnnualOzCap`).
- **R3 (geology and sampling):** reconciliation of production to estimate 0.6–1.5, with seller and pan-based claims tending to underperform; breakeven ≈ 0.008 oz/bcy at low strip and ≈ 0.01 at 6:1 (valuation heuristic); records review $500–5k; geologist reports $15–50k.
- **R1 (bonds and plans):** full-cost BLM placer bonds $1.5–15k/ac and plan review median ≈ 9 months (lognormal 4–30), which are the inputs to §6's `bondEstimate` and `permitDelayEstimate` behind D-5.38.
- **R5 (finance, all model knowledge):** unpatented claims have little or no collateral value and title insurance is generally unavailable for them, while patented land lends at 50–65% of appraised value (D-5.39, 5.5); streams take 2–10% of payable gold at 10–30% of spot, often stepping down after a threshold; private royalty deals run "10% of gross until 1.5–2.0× returned, then 2–3% for life" (`stepDown`); unpaid vendors file liens that block a claim sale; gross income from the property excludes royalties paid out (consistent with net presentation, D-5.12).
- **Guide calibration anchors** (domain knowledge, not independently sourced): unproven claim $5–20k; claim with history and a report $50–250k; permitted producing groups $0.5–3M+; patented $3–15k/ac; lease royalties 3–8% / 10–15% / 15–25%; AMR $5–50k/yr.
  - No research sheet covers the private placer lease and claim-sale market directly. Royalty bases, `inGroundFrac`, AMR, option, buy-down, carry, closing, diligence and auction parameters are designer estimates calibrated to these anchors and should be checked with the simulator and, where possible, against broker listings.

---

## 6. Licensing, Permitting, and Compliance

> **At a glance.** Owning a claim gives the right to the gold, not the right to dig. This system decides three things: what the player may do on each claim (`operatingAuthority`), what it costs to keep ground, and what happens when rules are bent.
>
> Every approval is a **pipeline**: preparation cost, a stochastic review, possible information requests, then a decision with conditions or a refusal. Every deadline is an **`Obligation`** on one compliance calendar. Every disturbed acre is a **reclamation liability** backed by a **bond**.
>
> The player's trade-offs: permit raw ground yourself (cheap, slow, risky) or buy permitted ground; who prepares applications (owner, specialist, or a consultant tier); how many acres to bond and with what (cash locks capital, a surety costs premium and collateral); reclaim now or later; run past a limit when the season is short; contest a citation or pay it.
>
> **Regulator standing** (0–100) turns past behaviour into future review speed, inspection frequency and condition severity. Missing paperwork is a **gate**; condition **limits** can be exceeded by choice, at a risk of detection; **inspections** roll dice on housekeeping. The U.S. federal regime ships in P2; the Alaska-style and Yukon-style regimes reuse the same shapes in P6.
>
> **Real agencies, fictional places.** The districts are fictional but sit in Alaska, Nevada and Yukon, and the real agencies run them (BLM, MSHA, the Corps of Engineers, the state and territorial bodies; 6.1). The game says plainly that its rules are simplified mechanics, not legal or regulatory advice.

### 6.1 Regimes, agencies and the permit catalog

**Agencies and where the districts sit (D-6.1; owner ruling 2026-10-05).** The game names the real agencies. Districts, claims, creeks, towns, companies and people stay fictional, but every district sits in a real jurisdiction, and that jurisdiction's real bodies administer it:

| District (§3 template) | Permits from | Jurisdiction | Regime / overlay |
|---|---|---|---|
| Northern federal district (`northernFederal`) | P2 | Alaska: federal (BLM) land in the interior | `usFederal` / `northernOverlay` |
| Arid federal district (`aridFederal`) | P2 | Nevada: federal (BLM) land | `usFederal` / `aridOverlay` |
| Alaska-style district (`alaskaState`) | P6 | Alaska: state land (federal claims inside it use `alaskaOverlay`, 6.13) | `alaskaState` |
| Yukon-style district (`yukon`) | P6 | Yukon | `yukon` |
| Temperate district (`temperateFederal`) | P6 | a Western state chosen when its P6 overlay is written (D-6.56) | `usFederal` / P6 overlay |

**Agency map.** One row per `AgencyKey`. The key names the job; each cell names the real body that does that job in that jurisdiction (data: `data/permits/agencies.ts`).

| Key | Job in the game | Northern district: Alaska (P2) | Arid district: Nevada (P2) | Alaska-style state land (P6) | Yukon-style (P6) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `land` | claim recording and fees; notices, plans and bonds; land inspections and orders | Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Alaska State Office | Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Nevada State Office | Alaska Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Division of Mining, Land and Water | Yukon Department of Energy, Mines and Resources (EMR): mining recorder, placer land-use approvals, inspections |
| `water` | discharge coverage, monitoring, reports | Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC): the APDES placer general permit | Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), Bureau of Water Pollution Control | DEC, through the consolidated application | Yukon Water Board (YWB): the water licence |
| `waterRights` | water-use authorization | DNR, Water Resources Section: temporary water use authorization (TWUA) or water right | Nevada Division of Water Resources (NDWR; the State Engineer) | DNR, through the consolidated application | YWB, inside the water licence |
| `wetlands` | dredge and fill in waters and wetlands (Clean Water Act §404) | U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Alaska District | USACE, Sacramento District | USACE, Alaska District | inside the YWB licence |
| `safety` | mine IDs, training, inspections, citations, accident investigations | Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA), U.S. Department of Labor | MSHA | MSHA | Yukon Workers' Safety and Compensation Board (WSCB) |
| `stateReclamation` | state reclamation plan above the overlay trigger | DNR, Division of Mining, Land and Water: reclamation plan | NDEP, Bureau of Mining Regulation and Reclamation (BMRR) | DNR, through the consolidated application | EMR, inside the class approval |
| `revenue` | business license; production-tax registration | Alaska Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development (business license); Alaska Department of Revenue (mining license tax) | Nevada Secretary of State (state business license); Nevada Department of Taxation (net proceeds of minerals) | as the northern district | Yukon Department of Finance; EMR collects the gold royalty |
| `labor` | workers' compensation coverage; wage claims | Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development (DOLWD) | Nevada Division of Industrial Relations (DIR; workers' compensation); Nevada Labor Commissioner (wages) | DOLWD | WSCB (workers' compensation); Yukon Employment Standards Office (wages) |
| `fishHabitat` | fish-habitat authorization | none in P2: fish timing windows ride on plan and 404 conditions | none | Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G), Habitat Section, through the consolidated application | Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO): the Yukon placer authorization |
| `assessmentBoard` | environmental and socio-economic assessment | — | — | — | Yukon Environmental and Socio-economic Assessment Board (YESAB) |
| `firstNation` | views on assessments; the relation score (6.14) | — | — | — | the affected First Nation (fictional names from §3's pool, D-6.55) |
| `air`, `explosives` | hard-rock track only (§14 14.10) | DEC Air Permits Program; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) | NDEP, Bureau of Air Pollution Control; ATF | as the northern district | Yukon Department of Environment (air); Natural Resources Canada, Explosives Regulatory Division |

- **EPA.** The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has no key. It delegated the discharge program to DEC and NDEP and keeps oversight and its own enforcement power; the game's water and wetlands fine cap is EPA's Clean Water Act administrative cap (6.10), and Help names EPA in that role.
- **County recorders** take the county share of claim recording (6.2). They are offices, not agencies with keys.
- **The northern district and Alaska's single application.** In Alaska one Annual Placer Mining Application (APMA) carries the DNR, DEC, ADF&G and BLM filings together. P2 files the same pieces separately with the same agencies, which is simpler to teach and to tune; P6's consolidated application (6.13) is the APMA form and serves Alaska-style districts. The northern federal district keeps the separate filings in every phase, so P2 balance does not move in P6 (D-6.57).

**Codes and text.**
- `AgencyKey` codes are job names, not abbreviations, so one code works in every jurisdiction: `safety` is MSHA in Alaska and Nevada and the WSCB in Yukon.
- Identifiers built on a retired fictional abbreviation or on one agency's name take job names (D-6.53): violation kinds `msa.*` → `safety.*` and `corps.unauthorizedFill` → `wetlands.unauthorizedFill`; obligation kind `msaRegistration` → `mineIdRegistration`; tuning keys `permits.msa.*` → `permits.safety.*`.
- Player-facing text gets agency names only through `agencyFor(state, claimId, key)`: the full name with the abbreviation at the first mention in a message, the abbreviation after that. Agency messages are plain game text, with no seals, logos, letterhead or names of real officials, and no forms presented as real filings.
- The Help glossary lists each agency with its job in the game and the rule the game simplifies (for example, "BLM: surface management under 43 CFR 3809, simplified").
- **Disclaimer** (text key `permits.disclaimer`): "Rules in this game are simplified game mechanics, not legal or regulatory advice." §13 shows it at the foot of every Permits tab, at the top of the Help glossary and on the setup wizard's World step, where districts are chosen (13.8, 13.14).

```ts
type AgencyKey = 'land'|'water'|'waterRights'|'wetlands'|'safety'|'stateReclamation'|'revenue'|'fishHabitat'|'assessmentBoard'|'firstNation'
  | 'air' | 'explosives'                        // P6, §14 hard-rock rows
  | 'labor';                                    // workers' comp and wage claims (D-6.54); last, so AgencyKey-ordered draws keep their positions
type AgencyJurisdiction = 'US' | 'US-AK' | 'US-NV' | 'CA' | 'CA-YT';   // ISO 3166 codes; the temperate state joins in P6
interface AgencySpec {
  name: string;                                 // 'Bureau of Land Management, Alaska State Office'
  short: string;                                // 'BLM'
  jurisdiction: AgencyJurisdiction;
  roleKey: string;                              // Help text: the job in the game and the rule it simplifies
  via?: 'consolidatedApplication' | 'waterLicence' | 'classApproval';   // filed through another body's process
}
function agencyFor(state: GameState, claimId: ClaimId, key: AgencyKey): AgencySpec | null;   // the overlay's entry, else the regime's; null if the key has no body there
interface RegimeSpec {
  id: Regime;                                   // 'usFederal' | 'alaskaState' | 'yukon' | 'private'
  agencies: Partial<Record<AgencyKey, AgencySpec>>;   // bodies that do not change with the state (MSHA, USACE), and every body of a regime without overlays
  claimRules: ClaimRuleSpec;                    // 6.2 (federal), 6.13, 6.14
  authorityModel: 'federalTiers' | 'privateState' | 'consolidated' | 'yukonClasses';
  permitTypeIds: PermitTypeId[];
  bondRules: BondRuleSpec;                      // 6.7
  inspection: Partial<Record<AgencyKey, InspectionRateSpec>>;  // 6.10
  violationTableId: string;
  currency: 'USD' | 'CAD';                      // CAD converted at §10 market.cadToUsd (0.72); §6 keeps no FX key
}
interface StateOverlaySpec {                    // one per U.S. district (federal or private regime)
  id: string; jurisdiction: 'US-AK' | 'US-NV';  // the temperate state's code joins in P6
  agencies: Partial<Record<AgencyKey, AgencySpec>>;   // state bodies and the BLM state office; replace the regime's entry for that key
  reclamationTriggerAcres: number; reclamationTriggerBcyPerYr: number;
  bondShared: boolean;                          // one instrument satisfies the land and state-reclamation agencies (BLM + DNR; BLM + NDEP)
  waterAppropriated: boolean;                   // fully appropriated basin -> 1-yr waivers only
  dischargeGpCycleYears: number; dischargeGpFirstExpiryYear: number;
  countyFilingUsdPerClaim: number; countyIntentToHoldWeek: number | null;
  countyRecordingWindowWeeks: number;           // county recording deadline after location; < 13 → separate countyRecording obligation (6.2)
  turbidityLimitNtu: 5 | 25; fishWindows: { startWeek: number; endWeek: number }[];
  bondPoolId: string | null; consolidatedApplication: boolean;   // null/false in P2
  ip404MitigationUsdPerAcre: number;
  newWaterPriority: 'temporary' | 'junior';     // priority of new water grants (6.4); 'senior' exists only on §3 stubs
}
interface ClaimRuleSpec { kind: 'federalFees' | 'stateRental' | 'representationWork' | 'none';   // 'none' = patented
  feeKeys: string[]; dueWeeks: number[]; workPerClaimUsd: number; cashInLieu: boolean }
interface BondRuleSpec { triggerAcres: number; perAcreFloorUsd: number | null; poolId: string | null;
  instruments: BondInstrument[]; securityFracOfRce: number }     // 1.0 federal; Yukon 0.10 / 0.25 (6.14)
interface InspectionRateSpec { perYear: Partial<Record<SiteState | AuthorityTier, number>> }
type TriggerSpec = { activity: ActivityKind; gpmAbove?: number } | { unreclaimedAcresAtLeast: number | string }
  | { plannedBcyPerYrAtLeast: number | string } | { surface: ('wetland' | 'channel')[] } | { always: true };
```

P2 ships two overlays (P6 adds `alaskaOverlay` for federal claims inside Alaska-style districts, 6.13):

| Overlay | Jurisdiction | Reclamation permit trigger | Turbidity limit | Fish window | GP first expiry | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `northernOverlay` | Alaska (`US-AK`) | 5 ac or 50,000 bcy/yr moved (strip + pay; Alaska's reclamation-plan threshold) | +5 NTU | wk 20–24 on fish-bearing creeks | year 1 | new water grants `temporary` (a DNR TWUA, no priority) |
| `aridOverlay` | Nevada (`US-NV`) | 5 ac or 21,600 bcy/yr moved (NDEP's 36,500 short tons at 1.69 t/bcy) | — | — | year 3 | water appropriated (new grants `junior`; 1-yr waivers from the State Engineer); county intent-to-hold $12/claim by wk 44 |

Both overlays use a shared bond (BLM and the state agency accept one instrument), a $12/claim county fee and a 13-week (90-day) county recording window, the same as BLM's, so P2 creates no separate county obligation; a later template with a 30- or 60-day county window sets `countyRecordingWindowWeeks` 4 or 9 (6.2).

**State slice.** Everything §6 owns lives in `state.permits`; `company.regulatorStanding` is stored on §1's company slice but written only through `applyStandingDelta` (6.11).

```ts
interface PermitSlice {
  permits: Record<PermitId, Permit>; permitIds: PermitId[];               // 6.6 (prefix prm)
  applications: Record<AppId, Application>; appIds: AppId[];             // 6.5 (prefix app)
  bonds: Record<BondId, Bond>; bondIds: BondId[];
  suretyQuotes: Record<SuretyQuoteId, SuretyQuote>; suretyQuoteIds: SuretyQuoteId[];   // 6.7 (bnd, sq)
  obligations: Record<ObligationId, Obligation>; obligationIds: ObligationId[];   // 6.9, exists from P1 (obl)
  autoPay: Partial<Record<ObligationCategory, boolean>>; autoFile: { owner: boolean };
  holdings: Record<ClaimId, ClaimHolding>;                                // 6.2 fee units, waiver, assessment credit
  reclamation: Record<ClaimId, ReclamationLedger>;                        // 6.8
  complianceMode: Record<ClaimId, { exceed: ConditionKind[]; acknowledgedTurn: number }>;   // 6.6
  conditionUsage: Record<ClaimId, ConditionUsage[]>;                      // last resolved week (§13 meters)
  inspections: Record<InspectionId, Inspection>; inspectionIds: InspectionId[];
  violations: Record<ViolationId, Violation>; violationIds: ViolationId[];
  orders: Record<OrderId, StopWorkOrder>; orderIds: OrderId[];            // 6.10 (insp, vio, ord)
  standingLedger: { turn: number; delta: number; reason: string; ref?: Id }[];   // 6.11
  standingCapsUsed: Record<string, number>;                               // reset week 1
  sanctions: Partial<Record<Regime, { nonCompliance: Id[]; debarredUntil: number | null }>>;   // 6.8
  mines: Record<string /* claim-group key */, { firstMechTurn: number; registeredTurn: number | null }>;   // 6.4 MSHA mine IDs
  fnRelation?: Record<DistrictId, number>;                                // P6 Yukon (6.14)
}
interface ClaimHolding { claimId: ClaimId; feeUnits: number; countsAsClaims: 1; groupKey: string;   // 6.2
  waiverIntent: boolean; creditCents: Record<number /* assessment year */, Cents>; payer: 'player' | 'counterparty' }
```

**Iteration order** (§2.3). Every entity Record above has a sorted `…Ids` array, and systems iterate that array. Records keyed by `ClaimId`, `DistrictId` or group key (`holdings`, `reclamation`, `complianceMode`, `conditionUsage`, `mines`, `sanctions`, `fnRelation`) are always iterated in ascending key order through §2's sorted-key helper, never by raw `Object.keys`.

Retention (saves, §2.9): closed applications keep only their outcome and last 10 log lines after 156 weeks; inspections, violations and the standing ledger older than 156 weeks are compacted into annual counts (the history windows used by `M_history`, repeat multipliers and the 3-strike rule are all ≤ 156 weeks); satisfied, waived, cancelled and cured obligations older than 52 weeks are dropped (their ledger transactions stay in §11). With these rules the `permits` slice of a 12-claim company stays under 250 kB in year 10 (the per-slice budget §6 asks of §2.13; test in 6.21).

**Permit catalog (U.S. federal, P2).** Pipeline parameters are in 6.5.

| `PermitTypeId` | Agency | Required when | Gates / grants | Term | Agency fees | On sale (6.12) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fed.notice` | land | mechanized exploration; ≤5 ac unreclaimed; bulk sample <590 bcy | authority `notice` | 104 wk, +104 by filing | $0 | transfers with bond replacement |
| `fed.plan` | land | any mining or processing; exploration >5 ac; bulk ≥590 bcy; anything above casual in special-status areas | authority `plan` | 520 wk (D-6.9) | $0 for an EA; EIS cost recovery $60,000 | transfers with bond replacement |
| `fed.planAmendment` | land | raising the cap or gpm; adding blocks or claims; renewal | modifies its parent | parent's | $0 | — |
| `st.waterUse` | waterRights | fresh-water draw > `waterAuthThresholdGpm` (3.5 gpm ≈ 5,000 gal/day) for `wash` or `bulkSample` | `wash` | 260 wk (52 in appropriated basins) | $150 | reissue (abbreviated); a §3 `senior` right transfers with the claim |
| `st.dischargeGP` | water | `dischargeMode = 'discharge'`; optional for closed loop | `discharge` | to the end of the district GP cycle | $315/yr | reissue (notice of intent) |
| `fed.nwp404` | wetlands | work in wetland/channel blocks ≤0.5 ac with no fish-bearing channel | `inStreamWork` on those blocks | 260 wk | $0 | transfers (letter) |
| `fed.ip404` | wetlands | >0.5 ac, or any fish-bearing channel | same | 260 wk | $100 | transfers (letter) |
| `st.reclamation` | stateReclamation | unreclaimed acres ≥ trigger, or planned bcy/yr ≥ trigger | disturbance above the trigger | with the plan | $1,000 + $300/yr | transfers with bond replacement |
| `fed.mineId` | safety | first week of mechanized work on a mine (one claim group, 6.2) | mechanized work after a 4-week grace | none | $0 | operator-change filing |
| `fed.trainingPlan` | safety | training with your own safety officer | in-house MSHA training | none | $0 | company-specific |
| `st.businessLicense` | revenue | the company exists | plan-tier operations | 52 wk | $50/yr | company-specific |
| hard-rock rows (P6) | land, explosives, air, water, safety | the §14 hard-rock track only | lode notice and plan, blasting, milling | per §14 14.10 | per §14 14.10 (ATF user permit $100, renewal $50, 156 wk) | per §14 |
