```ts
  createdTurn: number; windowOpenTurn: number; dueTurn: number;
  amount?: Cents;                      // cents; estimate, the owner re-prices at payment (pre-agreed name)
  filing?: { formKey: string; prepWeeks: number; requires?: string };   // e.g. 'assessmentCredit>=required'
  prepLeadWeeks: number;               // alerts fire this much earlier than the §13 ladder (8/4/1 weeks)
  payableNow: boolean; autoPayEligible: boolean; autoPay: boolean;
  consequence: { kind: 'forfeitClaim' | 'voidLocation' | 'lapsePermit' | 'suspendPermit' | 'violation' | 'withdrawApplication'
                       | 'lateFee' | 'escalate' | 'bondForfeiture' | 'gateCloses' | 'default'; text: string; severity: 'info' | 'warning' | 'critical' };
  graceWeeks: number;                  // weeks after dueTurn before the consequence (0 for statutory deadlines)
  status: 'upcoming' | 'due' | 'satisfied' | 'missed' | 'waived' | 'cancelled' | 'cured'
        | 'inPlan';                    // pre-filing money held in a reorganization plan (6.8); §11 pays it through the plan
  satisfiedTurn?: number; satisfiedVia?: 'payment' | 'filing' | 'work' | 'autoPay' | 'autoFile'; ledgerTxnIds?: string[];
  recurrence?: { kind: 'annualWeek'; week: number } | { kind: 'everyWeeks'; weeks: number } | { kind: 'anniversary'; baseTurn: number };
}
function createObligation(state, spec: ObligationSpec): { state; id: ObligationId };
function satisfyObligation(state, id, via, refs?): GameState;      // idempotent
function obligationsInRange(state, fromTurn, toTurn, filter?): Obligation[];
function settlementClass(obl: Obligation): 'statutory' | 'billable';
```

**Settlement rule by `consequence.kind`** (D-6.41; §11 11.4 applies the same rule, D-11.44).

```
settlementClass(obl) = 'billable'   if obl.owner ∈ {'§1', '§5', '§11'}                       // every §1, §5 and §11 money obligation
                                    or consequence.kind ∈ {'lateFee', 'escalate', 'default'}
                     = 'statutory'  otherwise: forfeitClaim, voidLocation, lapsePermit, suspendPermit, withdrawApplication,
                                    gateCloses, violation, bondForfeiture (all owned by §6, or §8 for training)
```

| | Statutory | Billable |
|---|---|---|
| Settled by | a player action only (`permits/payObligation` or `fileObligation`, `postBond` / `adjustBond`, the work itself, §8 training) or §6 auto-pay and auto-file in step 13. §11 never bills it. | a §11 bill. In step 14c of the due week §11 bills each open billable obligation that has no bill and was not already paid; step 14e settles it under §11's priority order, and paying the bill calls `satisfyObligation(state, id, 'payment')`. The player may pay earlier with `permits/payObligation`. |
| Consequence | at the end of step 13 (sub-step f, after the last auto-pay try) on `dueTurn + graceWeeks` | "missed" is evaluated at `dueTurn + graceWeeks + 1`, after the due week's settlement and any player payment before the week advances: by §6 in step 13 for owners §6, §5 (`land.onObligationMissed(obl)`) and §1 (`investor.onMinimumMissed(state, obligationId)`); by §11 in its step 14f for its own |
| Paid after `dueTurn`, before the consequence | "late within grace": standing −2 (6.11) | §6-owned: standing −2; §1, §5 and §11 apply their own remedies, which run off the bill |
| Typical kinds | claim fee (Sept 1), recording, waiver and affidavit, permit renewals and fees, bond top-ups, MSHA mine ID registration, reports | lease AMR, loan payments, minimum royalties, fines, bond premiums, late-fee filings, judgments |

So a Sept 1 fee is never in §11's queue: nothing can pay it after the end of step 13 in week 35, and the forfeiture is real. A lease AMR or loan payment that §11 pays in step 14 of its due week is never called missed in step 13 of that same week.

| Kind (federal, P2) | Class | Due | Amount | If missed | Grace |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claimRecording` | statutory | location + 13 wk | $86/claim + $200/unit (+ $200/unit more if recorded after the wk 35 following location) | location void (a lawful lapse: no standing hit) | 0 |
| `countyRecording` (only where the overlay's county window < 13 wk) | statutory | location + `countyRecordingWindowWeeks` | county fee per claim (then not in `claimRecording`) | location void (no standing hit) | 0 |
| `claimMaintenanceFee` | statutory | wk 35 | $200/unit | claim forfeited | 0 |
| `smallMinerWaiver` (filing) | statutory | wk 35 | $0 | fee falls due; unpaid → forfeited | 0 |
| `assessmentAffidavit` | statutory | wk 52, the following year | $27/claim ($15 BLM + $12 county) | forfeited | 0 |
| `waiverCure` | statutory | notice + 9 wk | full fee | forfeited | 0 |
| `countyIntentToHold` (arid) | billable (`lateFee`) | wk 44 | $12/claim | late fee $50/claim added to the bill, standing −1; the bill stays in §11's queue | 0 |
| `transferOfInterest` | billable (`lateFee`) | sale + 9 wk | $15/claim | as above | 0 |
| `mineIdRegistration` | statutory | first mechanized week + 4 | $0 | gate closes | 0 |
| `permitRenewal` / `noticeExtension` | statutory | expiry − lead / expiry | per type / $0 | permit lapses | 0 |
| `infoResponse` | statutory | issue + 26 wk | response cost | application withdrawn, standing −3 | 0 |
| `bondPremium` | billable (`escalate`) | anniversary | premium | the surety's 9-week cancellation notice and a `bondReplacement` (6.7) | 4 |
| `bondTopUp` / `bondIncrease` / `bondReplacement` | statutory | +8 / +4 / +9 wk | delta | covered permits suspended | 0 |
| `bondCollateralCall` (reorganization, 6.8) | statutory | filing + 9 wk | (0.50 − collateral share) × face | bond cancelled; covered permits suspended until replaced | 0 |
| `dischargeAnnualFee` / `stateReclamationFee` | statutory | wk 13 | $315 / $300 | coverage lapses / permit hold at trigger | 4 |
| `dischargeAnnualReport` / `monitoringReport` (filing) | statutory | wk 6 | $0 | `water.missingReport` | 0 |
| `businessLicense` | statutory | wk 52 | $50 | gate closes | 0 |
| `finePayment` | billable (`escalate`) | issue + 4 wk | fine | +1%/month; after 13 weeks referral ×1.5, standing −3 | 0 |
| `abatement` | statutory | per order | per cure | escalation to failure-to-abate (6.10) | 0 |
| `reclamationOrder` | statutory | 26 wk / end of next season | — | bond forfeiture | 0 |
| `agencyJudgment` / `suretyIndemnity` | billable (`default`) | forfeiture + 26 wk | judgment / 1.10 × face | `DEBARRED` 104 wk; §11 distress ladder | 0 |
| `trainingRefresher` (created and resolved by §8) | statutory | last + 52 wk | $200 contract | employee cannot work (`isTrainedForFieldWork`) | 0 |

Other sections create `leaseAdvanceRoyalty`, `leaseShortfallRoyalty`, `workInLieu`, `leaseCure`, `royaltyArrears`, `forfeitureDamages` and `minimumRoyaltyShortfall` (§5; owner `'§1'` for an investor-held minimum, `'§11'` for a lender-held one), and `loanPayment`, `insuranceRenewal`, `taxFiling` and `taxPayment` (§11). All are billable. P6 adds the kinds listed in 6.13 and 6.14. During a reorganization case, pre-filing `finePayment`, `agencyJudgment` and `suretyIndemnity` items, and the pre-filing billable items behind bills §11 stays (AMR arrears, minimum top-ups, `loanPayment`), sit `inPlan` and are paid through §11's plan; everything else, and everything incurred after the filing, keeps its class and timing (6.8).

**Reminders, auto-pay and auto-file.**
- §13's alert ladder (info at 8 weeks, warning at 4, critical at 1) counts back from `dueTurn − prepLeadWeeks`.
- **Auto-pay** (per category or per obligation) covers **statutory payments only**:
  - `autoPayEligible` = statutory with an amount and no instrument choice: claim fees, recording, affidavit and waiver-cure fees, permit fees, the business license, and a `bondTopUp` on a cash bond. Billable items need no auto-pay, because §11's settlement already pays them in their due week by priority (their `autoPayEligible` is false).
  - It runs in step 13 at `dueTurn − autoPayLeadWeeks` (1) through `finance.pay(origin: 'pipeline')`, which respects §11's priority reserve (payroll and higher categories this week come first).
  - If payment fails or is partial, it raises a critical alert and retries each week through `dueTurn + graceWeeks`; then the consequence applies.
  - `permits.autoPayDefault` is **on for `land` (claim fees and recording) at every difficulty**; `permit` and `bond` are on in easy and off in standard and hard (D-6.16). The setup wizard (§13.14) shows the toggle with its trade-off: cash leaves a week early, against a missed Sept 1 forfeiting the claim.
- **Auto-file** (zero-cost routine forms: waiver, notice extensions, reports, `mineIdRegistration` and the MSHA operator-change filing, every other no-fee registration, and the affidavit once credit is met; its $27/claim goes through auto-pay), filed in the first week of their window:
  - by an employed permitting specialist: no owner time, professional defect rates;
  - or, if the player sets `permits/setAutoFile { owner: true }`, by the owner: each form costs `ownerFilingDeskDays` (0.25) of §1 desk days and carries the owner defect rate where one exists (waiver 0.03).
- **Batch actions** (D-6.42). `permits/payObligations { ids[] }` and `permits/fileObligations { ids[] }` (6.15) act on many obligations at once, in priority order: statutory before billable, then consequence severity (critical first), then `dueTurn`, then ID. Each payment is its own `finance.pay(origin: 'player', allowPartial: false)` call. The batch stops at the first payment that would fail and reports the paid and unpaid IDs (a `BATCH_PARTIAL` notice, not an error); filings that need preparer weeks are queued. §13 groups obligation alerts by (category, due week) and offers "Pay all due this week".
- **Trade-off:** the specialist's salary buys defect-free filing without owner time, plus better applications; the owner can automate too, but pays in desk days and in the occasional defective waiver. Nothing needs a click unless the player wants control (D-6.23).

### 6.10 Inspections, violations, fines, orders and contesting

**When inspections happen.** For each claim and agency, every week:

```
λ_week = baseRate[agency][siteState] / expectedActiveWeeks(district, year) × M_standingInsp × M_history × M_diffInsp × M_event('permits.inspectionRateMult')
  type SiteState = 'active' | 'dormant'
  siteState: 'active' if any above-casual activity on the claim this week; 'dormant' if openAcres > 0 and idle (land only, operating weeks)
  expectedActiveWeeks = §1 expectedActiveWeeks(state, districtId, year) (north ≈ 22, arid 46)
  M_standingInsp = 0.5 + (1 − S/100)  (S=60 → 0.9);   M_history = 1 + 0.25 × min(4, this agency's violations in last 104 wk);   M_diffInsp = 0.7 / 1.0 / 1.3
p_week = 1 − exp(−λ_week); at most one inspection per agency per claim per 3 weeks
draw: rng(seed,'permits-inspect',turn,claimId), agencies in AgencyKey order
forced: §12 forceInspection(state, claimId, agency, withinWeeks, reason) schedules one in a week drawn uniformly in [t+1, t+withinWeeks]
        (ignores the cooldown). For reason = 'complaint' §6 first rolls whether the agency acts at all: p = insp.complaintForcedProb (0.6),
        drawn on rng(seed,'permits-inspect','forced',turn,claimId,agency); every other reason always schedules. §12 calls it
        unconditionally (envComplaint uses withinWeeks 2) and applies no probability of its own.
```

```ts
interface Inspection { id: InspectionId; agency: AgencyKey; claimId: ClaimId; turn: number;
  trigger: 'routine' | 'forced' | 'reinspection' | 'release' | 'investigation';
  findings: { kind: string; violationId?: ViolationId }[]; clean: boolean }   // clean → standing input (6.11)
```

| Agency | Base rate per year | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| safety (MSHA) | 2.0 while mechanized work runs (R1: at least 2/yr for surface mines) | citations (below), Mine ID, training records |
| land | plan 1.5; notice 0.75; dormant with open acres 0.25 | condition states (6.6), bonded vs open acres, reclamation, housekeeping |
| water | 1.0 with coverage while washing; 0.3 for a closed loop without coverage | discharge state this week, pond ratio, reports |
| waterRights | 0.5 with an authorization while washing | gpm meter |
| stateReclamation | 0.5 with `st.reclamation` | acres vs permit, fees |
| wetlands | 0.15 with a 404; 0.05 if the claim has channel blocks | fill acres vs authorization |

**Safety citations (MSHA).**

```
n ~ Poisson(μ),  μ = 3.0 × M_safetyStaff × M_culture × M_fleet × M_size × M_hist × M_diffInsp
  M_safetyStaff = 1 − 0.45 × §8 safetyOfficerCoverage(state, claimId) (0..1);   M_culture = 1.5 − company.safetyRecord/100 (§8, 0..100)
  M_fleet = 1 + 0.6 × max(0, 0.6 − §9 avgKnownHealth(claimId)) / 0.6 (1.0 until P3);   M_size = min(2.0, 0.6 + 0.08 × fieldCrew)
  fieldCrew = §8 fieldCrewCount(state, claimId)
  M_hist  = min(1.5, 1 + 0.1 × S&S citations in last 104 wk)
each citation: S&S with p = 0.18 × M_culture; flavor category (guarding, berms, highwall, first aid, fire, mobile equipment, electrical, training records)
penalty: non-S&S LN(180, 0.45) clamp [168, 3,000]; S&S LN(900, 0.7) clamp [300, 20,000]; × sizeMult (0.8 + 0.04 × fieldCrew, ≤ 1.6) × fineDiffMult × cpiIndex
abatement: auto-abate on by default → LN(600, 0.8) + 4 support hours (§7) next week; off and unabated within 2 weeks → failure-to-abate:
  withdrawal order on the affected machine (guarding → the plant) until abated + $5,000 per week (MSHA allows up to $9,820/day)
```

- **Typical cost.** A crew of 5 with safety record 50 and no safety officer has μ = 3.0. That is about $1,100 in penalties plus $2,500 in abatement per inspection, or about $6,200 per season.
- **A safety officer** cuts this by about 45% at full coverage. The officer's real case is injuries (§8), which is realistic.
- **Citation feed.** Each citation is pushed to §8 (`{ claimId, ss: boolean, turn }`) for the safety record (−0.5 non-S&S, −2 S&S).
- **Accident investigations** (§8 calls `openInvestigation(state, claimId, 'serious' | 'fatal')`; §12's `seriousIncident` uses the same hook):
  - serious: LN(25,000, 0.6) clamped to [5,000, 90,649]; the area stops for 1 week; standing −8;
  - fatal: LN(120,000, 0.6) clamped to [30,000, 332,376]; the claim stops for 2–4 weeks; standing −15;
  - late notification (§8: a serious or fatal injury under a lead hand, p 0.3): `safety.lateNotification` on top.

**Violation catalog.** Fine median and σ are year-1 USD, clamped to [min, max], then scaled by the repeat multiplier up to the agency cap and multiplied by `fineDiffMult` (0.7 / 1.0 / 1.3). Every violation that brings a stop-work order or is S&S also reports `permits.violation` to §1 reputation (−1; −2 with a stop-work order; −4 for a claim-wide suspension).

| Violation | Agency | From | Fine min / median / max (σ) | Standing | Order / cure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `safety.citation` (non-S&S / S&S) | safety | Poisson above | above | −0.25 / −1 | abate in 1–2 wk |
| `safety.failureToAbate` | safety | abatement missed | $5,000/wk | −4 | withdrawal (machine or area) |
| `safety.accident` | safety | §8 serious / fatal | above | −8 / −15 | investigation stop |
| `safety.lateNotification` | safety | §8 late report of a serious or fatal injury | 7,555 / 12,000 / 90,649 (0.6) | −3 | — |
| `land.overDisturbance` | land | `maxDisturbedAcres` | none (no federal fine authority) | −6 | reclaim the excess or amend within 8 wk, plus bond increase in 4 wk; else suspension |
| `land.seasonWindow` | land | `seasonWindow`, `highFlowInStream`, `noNightShift` (timing conditions) | none | −5 | order; a second → 4-wk suspension |
| `land.reclamationLag` | land | `concurrentReclamation` | none | −3 | reclaim within 6 wk; else suspension |
| `land.excludedBlock` | land + state historic | excluded or buffer block disturbed | 5,000 / 15,000 / 50,000 (0.6) + mitigation LN(30,000, 0.5) | −10 | 4-wk suspension |
| `land.deficiency` | land | housekeeping, p = 0.25 × (1.5 − 0.01S) per inspection | none | −1 if unabated | abate in 4 wk, LN(1,500, 0.6) |
| `water.dischargeSelfReported` | water | discharge model | 1st: warning; repeat 1,000 / 3,000 / 10,000 (0.5) | −2 | — |
| `water.dischargeDetected` | water | discharge model | 3,600 / 8,000 / 27,378 (0.6), ×2.5 per repeat, cap 342,218 | −6 | cease discharge until the pond is fixed and re-sampled (1–3 wk) |
| `water.unpermittedDischarge` | water | closed-loop overflow without coverage | 5,000 / 15,000 / 68,445 (0.6) | −8 | cease washing until the pond is fixed and re-inspected (≈ 2 wk); coverage must be filed before the next overflow or a repeat is ×2.5 |
| `water.pondDeficiency` | water | `pondCapacity` | warning, then 1,000 / 3,000 / 10,000 | −2 | add capacity within 4 wk |
| `water.missingReport` | water | report missed | 500 / 1,500 / 5,000 (0.4) | −2 | file |
| `water.overUse` | waterRights | `maxWaterGpm` | 1,000 / 5,000 / 25,000 (0.6) + $2,500 per excess acre-foot | −5 | return to the grant and install a meter ($3,000); grant cut 10% for the rest of its term (6.4); a second → 4-wk washing suspension |
| `wetlands.unauthorizedFill` | wetlands | `noInStreamWork` | 10,000 / 25,000 / 68,445 (0.6) + restoration $8,000/ac | −10 | channel blocks stopped until an after-the-fact individual permit |
| `state.overPermit` | stateReclamation | acres over the state permit | 1,000 / 5,000 / 20,000 (0.6) | −4 | as for land |
| `state.insuranceLapse` | labor (WC lapse) or land (GL, a plan condition) | §11 cancels WC or GL | none | −2 | gate closes until reinstated |
| `state.noWorkersComp` | labor | §8 injury charged while WC lapsed | 2,500 / 10,000 / 50,000 (0.5) | −4 | — |
| `land.concealment` | land | §12 `culturalFind` concealment caught | per §12 ($50–250k) | −30 | plan suspended 13–26 wk (§12 draws) |

**General fine formula.**

```
base = clamp(median_v × exp(σ_v × normInv(u)), min_v, max_v)
fine = min(base × repeatMult_v^n, fineCap[agency]) × fineDiffMult × cpiIndex
n = same-kind violations within 156 weeks; repeatMult 2.0 (discharge 2.5); draw #1 of rng(seed,'permits-violation',violationId)
fineCap: water and wetlands 342,218 (EPA Class II administrative cap); stateReclamation, revenue and labor 100,000; safety 90,649 (30 CFR 100;
         MSHA citations and accident fines use their own clamps above, up to the $332,376 flagrant maximum)
```

A third same-kind violation within 156 weeks revokes the underlying permit, and the player must re-apply. Fines become `finePayment` obligations posted to `exp.fines`. Escalation runs: warning → fine → order → suspension → revocation → forfeiture or referral.

```ts
interface Violation { id: ViolationId; kind: string; agency: AgencyKey; claimId: ClaimId; issuedTurn: number; fineCents: Cents;
  selfReported: boolean; merit: number /* hidden U(0,1) */; contest?: { filedTurn: number; resolveTurn: number; outcome?: 'vacated' | 'reduced' | 'upheld' };
  orderId?: OrderId; obligationIds: ObligationId[]; standingDelta: number }
interface StopWorkOrder { id: OrderId; agency: AgencyKey; claimId: ClaimId;
  scope: { kind: 'claim' } | { kind: 'activities'; activities: ActivityKind[] } | { kind: 'machine'; machineId: MachineId } | { kind: 'blocks'; blockIds: BlockId[] };
  violationId: ViolationId; issuedTurn: number; minWeeks: number; cure: CureSpec; cureDoneTurn?: number; reinspectTurn?: number; liftedTurn?: number }
type CureSpec = { kind: 'abate'; cents: Cents } | { kind: 'reclaimAcres'; acres: number } | { kind: 'postBond'; cents: Cents }
  | { kind: 'pondCapacity'; bcy: number } | { kind: 'obtainPermit'; typeId: PermitTypeId } | { kind: 'investigation'; weeks: number };
```

**Stop-work orders.** An order lifts after its cure plus a re-inspection LN(1.5, 0.4) weeks later (minimum 1). The order card shows weeks lost so far. Typical losses:

| Order | Scope | Weeks lost |
|---|---|---|
| MSHA withdrawal | one machine | 1–2 |
| water cease-discharge | discharge | 1–3 |
| land suspension | whole claim, reclaim-only | 2–8 |
| fatal accident | claim | 2–4 |
| unauthorized fill | channel blocks | about 36 |

**Contesting** (`permits/contestViolation`).
- Must be filed within 4 weeks (`CONTEST_WINDOW_CLOSED`).
- Costs `max(2,000, 0.25 × fine)`, capped at $25,000, and lasts LN(16, 0.5) weeks, clamped to [6, 52].
- The outcome is set by the hidden merit m (draw #2 of the violation's stream, taken at issue), with qMult = 1 + 0.5 × (Q_handler − 0.6), where Q_handler is the handler's preparer quality from 6.5 (owner, specialist or consultant tier):
  - **vacated** if m < 0.15 × qMult;
  - **reduced by 50%** if m < 0.50 × qMult;
  - **upheld** otherwise.
- The fine is held while the contest runs. Orders are not stayed, except that a land suspension gets a stay with p 0.2.
- A vacated citation leaves the history and its standing delta is reversed. An upheld one costs −1 more.
- **Player sees vs true:** the player sees the base odds (15% / 35% / 50%), never m.
- **Trade-off:** legal fees and weeks of uncertainty, against a lower fine and a record that escalates more slowly.

### 6.11 Regulator standing

`company.regulatorStanding` S ∈ [0, 100] is one visible, company-wide score with a ledger of every delta (D-6.17).

```
S_t = clamp( 60 + (S_{t−1} − 60) × k + Σ deltas_t , 0, 100 ),   k = 2^(−1/104) = 0.99336 (half-life 104 weeks)
S_start = §1 start value: 60 (Inheritor 55; §6 accepts 50–65 for a family record)
deltas_t = all applyStandingDelta(state, delta, reason, ref) calls this week, after per-input annual caps (capsUsed reset in week 1)
```
Deltas recorded in week t are summed in step 13i and read by every system from week t+1, so no step within a week depends on another step's standing change.

| Input | Delta (annual cap) |
|---|---|
| §6 obligation satisfied on time | +0.25 (+3) |
| info response faster than median | +0.5 (+1) |
| clean inspection: land or water / safety | +1 / +0.5 (+4) |
| abated before deadline | +0.5 (+2) |
| concurrent reclamation (condition met or none) | +0.5/ac (+4) |
| bond stage-2 release | +1 (+2) |
| claim fully reclaimed and released | +3 |
| late within grace | −2 |
| obligation missed (forfeiture, lapse) | −8 |
| info deadline missed | −3 |
| violations | per catalog (−0.25 to −15); self-reported discharge −2 vs −6 when detected |
| contest upheld | −1 |
| insurance lapse (6.4) | −2 |
| §11 labor-department wage-claim notice (unpaid wages 4+ weeks) | −3 |
| §12 event outcomes (via `applyStandingDelta`) | per §12 table, within ±15 per event |
| bond forfeiture or abandonment | −30 |

A diligent operator settles around 80–85; a sloppy one around 40–50.

| S | Review time | Info factor | Deny factor | Inspection rate | Extra-condition odds (Mx base) | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | ×0.80 | ×0.70 | ×0.40 | ×0.50 | ×0.50 | best surety `c_stand` |
| 80 | ×0.85 | ×0.82 | ×0.64 | ×0.70 | ×0.70 | |
| 60 | ×0.99 | ×0.94 | ×0.88 | ×0.90 | ×0.90 | start |
| 40 | ×1.23 | ×1.06 | ×1.12 | ×1.10 | ×1.10 | below 30: bond pool ineligible (P6) |
| 20 | ×1.57 | ×1.18 | ×1.36 | ×1.30 | ×1.30 | below 25: high-risk operator |
| 0 | ×2.00 | ×1.30 | ×1.60 | ×1.50 | ×1.50 | |

A **high-risk operator**:
- can get surety tier D at best;
- has `monitoring` and `concurrentReclamation` added to every new permit;
- gets at least 1 land inspection per year.

### 6.12 Permits as assets: transfer on sale and valuation

§5's sale, purchase, lease and option closings call `permitTransferOutcome(state, claimId, buyer, { kind: 'sale' | 'lease' | 'optionExercise'; nonTransferable?: boolean; sellerBondCarryWeeks?: number })` at completion (per claim; `transferPackage(state, claimIds, from, to, opts)` is the multi-claim wrapper). It applies the rules below, creates the buyer's obligations, and returns the authority that survives. §5's hidden `nonTransferablePermit` defect passes `nonTransferable: true`: every land-agency permit is treated as `reissue` from scratch and the surviving authority is `casual` (no notice or plan; §5 uses the same word) until the buyer re-applies. A lease follows the same path with the lessee as operator; the lessor stays claimant of record, and claim fees fall on the lease's `payer` (6.2). When the lease ends (`terminated`) the permits go back to the lessor (6.8).

| Item | On sale | Buyer must | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unpatented claims | transfer | `transferOfInterest`, $15/claim (the only BLM transfer charge; not a §5 closing cost) | 9-wk window |
| Notice, plan, state reclamation | transfer with bond replacement | post a replacement bond within `transferBondWeeks` (4), counted from the end of any seller bond carry; authority is `casual` while none covers the open acres | agency acknowledgment LN(3, 0.4) wk; it does not gate work (the permit shows `pendingTransfer`) |
| Water authorization | reissue (abbreviated: stages ×0.5, prep $500); the seller's grant continues for the buyer until the reissue is decided if the buyer files within `transfer.reissueFileWeeks` (4) of closing (D-6.44) | file | ~4 wk |
| Discharge coverage | reissue (new notice of intent), continuing as above | file | ~3 wk |
| 404 NWP / IP | transfer (letter) | sign | 1 wk |
| MSHA mine ID | operator-change filing | file within 4 wk | instant |
| Training plan, business license, insurance, SMW | company-specific | get their own | — |
| Bonds | never transfer | replace | seller's bond released after the buyer's is accepted, + LN(3, 0.4) wk |
| Open violations and orders | site conditions transfer; fines stay with the seller | cure site conditions | — |
| Alaska CMA / Yukon water licence (P6) | transfer with approval | file | 4 / 8 wk |

During a transfer the permits show `pendingTransfer`. Operations continue under the seller's bond only for the deal's `sellerBondCarryWeeks` (§5 `SaleTerms` / `LeaseTerms`, 0–13, default 0; `sellerBondCarryMaxWeeks` 13). Otherwise the buyer has `casual` authority, and above-casual work fails with `BOND_INSUFFICIENT` until the buyer posts its own bond, which must cover the RCE of the open acres at today's cpi (6.3); a carry that ends before the buyer's bond is accepted drops authority to `casual` the same way. The buyer inherits the reclamation ledger, including §3 `inherited` acres and any §5 `undisclosedReclamation` acres (revealed by §6's first inspection or baseline, which calls `land.revealDefect`).

**Starter permitted lease** (P2+; §3 3.11, §5 5.4). The guaranteed permitted, fully bonded lease in each starting district reaches `plan` authority within 4 weeks of offer acceptance, and in practice in 2:
- week 1: §5's folded records check (below) and the 1-week lease closing; at completion `permitTransferOutcome(…, { kind: 'lease', sellerBondCarryWeeks: 13 })` keeps the plan in force under the lessor's bond, whose face §3 sets to the RCE of the plan cap, so there is no shortfall;
- the agency acknowledgment of the operator change runs alongside and does not gate work; water and discharge continue while their abbreviated reissue runs (filed by auto-file in the closing week); the MSHA operator-change filing is instant;
- the lessee must post its own bond within the 13 carry weeks (a surety quote takes LN(3, 0.3) weeks; cash is accepted the next week).

**Packages that exist before the player.** At `newGame` (P2+) and whenever §5 lists a claim, `instantiatePermitStub(state, claimId, { transferDefect? })` turns §3's `permitStub` truth into real records held by `'npc'` (or the competitor): `planApproved` → an active `fed.plan` (cap = open acres rounded up + 5, 10-year term with a random 1–9 years left), an `st.waterUse` with 0–4 years left, discharge coverage on the district GP cycle, and a bond whose face is `bondPostedCents` (often below today's RCE); `noticeOnFile` → an active `fed.notice` and its bond. When §5 has drawn a `nonTransferablePermit` defect it passes the cause, and the record carries it (D-6.45):
- `suspended`: the plan or notice is `suspended` by a land-agency order (`land.overDisturbance`, cure `reclaimAcres`) dated before the listing;
- `bondCancelNotice`: the bond is in `cancelNotice`, with `cancelEffectiveTurn` U{2..9} weeks after the listing (`permits-bond`, purpose `stubCancel`);
- `bondForfeited`: the bond is `forfeited` and the permits are `suspended` for want of a bond.

The **Inheritor** (§1 1.8.2) receives such a package at setup: the family's active plan, last worked in 2024 (§1 D-1.53; issued U{2018..2024}, so 1–7 years of its 10-year term remain), cap = inherited open acres rounded up + `game.inheritor.planHeadroomAcres` (5), a $6,000 cash bond, standing 55. §6 records the operator change, opens a `bondTopUp` obligation in week 1 for the shortfall (due in 8 weeks; at an operator change there is no authority grace), and blocks mechanized work with `BOND_INSUFFICIENT` until it is posted. The inherited open acres are typically 7–9: 5–7 mined acres plus the two pre-stripped blocks (`game.inheritor.preStrippedBlocks`, typed `stripped`). At standard rates on a seasonal road at its reference distance the RCE of 7–9 open acres is ≈ $42–51k (8 acres: (6 × 2,600 + 2 × 1,200) × 1.15 + 11,200 = 31,900; × 1.45 = $46,255), so the shortfall is ≈ $36–45k. Water and discharge reissue by abbreviated filing under continuance, and the MSHA mine ID by operator change.

**Valuation hook.** §5 owns the dollars; §6 supplies the inputs.

```ts
interface PermitPackageValue {
  claimIds: ClaimId[]; tier: AuthorityTier; permits: { typeId: PermitTypeId; status: Permit['status']; expiresTurn: number | null; conditions: string[] }[];
  avoidedPrepCostCents: Cents;       // expected prep + info cost to rebuild this package now (standard consultant, current cpi)
  expectedWeeksSaved: number;        // P50 critical path: desk + baseline wait + review + E[info]
  seasonsSaved: number;              // northern: 1 if self-permitting would miss next season's operating start
  approvalRiskAvoided: number;       // p_deny + p(capFactor < 1) at the buyer's standing
  replacementBondCents: Cents; bondShortfallCents: Cents;   // RCE(open acres) − existing face
  transferCostCents: Cents; openViolations: number | null;  // null until a records check
}
function permitPackageValue(state, claimIds, perspective: 'player' | CompetitorId): PermitPackageValue;
// Scalar estimators §5 calls (5.13), all from visible state and the buyer's standing:
function permitCostEstimate(state, claimId): Cents;     // = avoidedPrepCostCents for the authority still missing (0 with a plan in hand)
function permitDelayEstimate(state, claimId): number;   // P50 seasons until production authority (state path for patented ground)
function bondEstimate(state, claimId): Cents;           // requiredBond at the default planned mix and cap
function reclamationEstimate(state, claimId): Cents;    // liability of existing + planned disturbance (6.8 formula)
function reclamationCostEstimate(state, acres, districtId): Cents;   // RCE (bond basis) of `acres` at the default planned mix, plan-tier
                                                                     // mobilization, the district's road class at s = 1; §3 listing display
                                                                     // and the starter lease's bond face (3.11)
```

**Example** (the 6.5 package, valued at standing 60):
- avoided cost ≈ $59,800 + 0.37 × $10,300 + $5,000 of ancillaries ≈ **$69k**;
- weeks saved ≈ 16 + 6 + 34 + 5 ≈ 61, so `seasonsSaved` = 1;
- risk avoided ≈ 0.25.

On a $2M NPV, starting a season earlier at a 15% discount rate is worth about $260k. That is why permitted ground lists at a premium (anchor: permitted and bonded producing groups $0.5–3M+).

**Records check.** $250 × cpi and 1 week. It reads the agency record, which is exactly §6's state (D-6.39), and returns:

```ts
function recordsCheck(state, claimId): RecordsCheckResult;   // pure; no RNG of its own
interface RecordsCheckResult { authorityOnRecord: AuthorityTier; permits: { typeId: PermitTypeId; status: Permit['status']; expiresTurn: number | null }[];
  bondFaceCents: Cents; rceCents: Cents; openOrders: number; openViolations: number; recordedDisturbedAcres: number;
  transferCause?: 'suspended' | 'bondCancelNotice' | 'bondForfeited' }
```
- **What it catches** (D-6.45): a misstated authority always (`misstatedPermit`, p 1: the record shows the real tier); a recorded `nonTransferablePermit` cause with p `recordsCheck.transferCauseDetectP` (0.90), decided by the defect's stored `detectU` from §5 5.6 (`transferCause` is set iff `detectU < 0.90`), so the check and §5 diligence never disagree (an undetected cause reports the permit and bond as they stood before it, i.e. active); `undisclosedReclamation` never (p 0: the acres are unrecorded by definition).
- **Folded into closings (P2+).** §5 runs it automatically in week 1 of every non-auction purchase, lease or option closing and shows the $250 in closing costs (skipped if the player ran one on this claim within `land.recordsCheckReuseWeeks`, 4); §5 decides what counts as a material finding and the walk-away.
- **Stand-alone** `permits/recordsCheck` (on a listing or an owned claim) remains as an optional pre-offer check for players who want the answer before negotiating. Before any check, a listing shows only the seller's statements (§3 honesty model).

### 6.13 Alaska-style regime (P6)

This regime covers Alaska state land (`Regime = 'alaskaState'`; DNR, DEC, ADF&G, MSHA and USACE, 6.1). It reuses every shape above. Federal claims inside the same P6 districts stay `usFederal` with `alaskaOverlay`: the consolidated application below replaces `st.waterUse`, `st.dischargeGP` and `st.reclamation`, the federal notice or plan is still required, and the pool covers $750/ac of the federal RCE (the rest needs another instrument).

| State claims (`ClaimRuleSpec.kind = 'stateRental'`) | Rule |
|---|---|
| Units | 40-ac quarter-quarter (QQ) or 160-ac quarter-section (QS = 4 × QQ) grid claims; tenure `ownedState` (§5) |
| Location | record within `ak.recordingWindowWeeks` (7; 45 days) at `ak.recordingFeeUsdPerClaim` ($35) and pay first rental (QQ $40, QS $165), which covers to the next wk 35; one statutory `akRecording` obligation created by `registerTenureObligations` at location (missed → location void) |
| Annual rental | 0–5 yrs $40/QQ, 6–10 yrs $85, 11+ yrs $205 (QS ×4); pay window wk 35–48; unpaid at end of wk 48 → claim abandoned (no cure, D-6.20) |
| Annual labor | $100/QQ, $400/QS per labor year ending wk 35; same qualifying spend as federal assessment work (6.2); no cap on claim count |
| Labor statement | `akLaborStatement` filed by wk 48; missing → abandoned |
| Cash in lieu | pay the labor amount by wk 35, at most 5 years in a row; excess labor banks up to 4 years |
| Rental credit | rental paid is credited against the production royalty (§11) |

**Consolidated application (`ak.cma`: Alaska's Annual Placer Mining Application, APMA).** One application, filed with DNR, covers land use, the reclamation plan and water use (DNR), discharge (DEC) and fish habitat (ADF&G).
- **Flow:** `intake` (fixed 2 weeks) → sub-reviews in parallel (`parallelGroup = 'cma'`, each drawing its own completeness, info and deny outcomes with the 6.5 formulas) → `decision` (1 week) once all sub-reviews finish.
- **A denied sub-review gives partial approval:**
  - fish habitat denied → `noInStreamWork` and no discharge in fish windows;
  - water denied → no `wash`, so exploration only.

  The denied piece can be refiled as an amendment.
- **Prep:** fee $8,000, direct $2,000, baseline $3,000 (fish-bearing creeks only), 4 desk weeks; application fee $100.
- **Summer queue:** review entered in the operating phase runs ×1.4 (`permits.ak.summerQueueMult`; first come, first served), replacing the federal ×1.10.
- **Term:** requested 1–10 years; granted as asked with p 0.8, otherwise min(requested, 5).
- **Authority:** a CMA with mining scope → `plan`; exploration scope → `notice`. Federal plans (on federal ground) and 404 permits (on wetlands) still apply.

| Sub-review | When included | Median (σ) | baseDeny |
|---|---|---|---|
| landUse (DNR) | always on state land | 6 (0.4) | 0.03 |
| reclamationPlan (DNR) | open acres ≥ 5 or ≥ 50,000 bcy/yr; otherwise a Letter of Intent filing | 6 (0.4) | 0.03 |
| discharge (DEC) | `dischargeMode = 'discharge'` | 4 (0.3) | 0.01 |
| waterUse (DNR) | gpm > 3.5 | 6 (0.4) | 0.03 |
| fishHabitat (ADF&G) | fish-bearing creek or in-stream work | 8 (0.5), +6 if the creek is anadromous (§3 `Creek.anadromous`) | 0.08 |

**Annual obligations.**
- `akBondRenewal` (bond and pool fees) by wk 13.
- `akReclamationStatement` plus next season's plan or Letter of Intent by wk 52. Missing it puts next season on hold (authority capped at `notice`) until filed, with standing −4. A second miss within 5 years ends pool eligibility.

**Bonding.**
- A bond is required at 5 open acres, at `ak.bondPerAcreUsd` ($750/ac) unless a third-party RCE is lower. On federal land the federal RCE applies.
- **Pool** (`ak.pool`): a $112.50/ac deposit (15%), refunded at stage-2 release, plus a $37.50/ac/yr fee (5%) that is never refunded (D-6.19).
  - Eligibility: S ≥ 30, no past pool forfeiture, gravity processing only.
  - On federal land the pool covers $750/ac; the rest of the RCE needs another instrument.
- **Example:** 20 pooled acres cost $3,000 in year 1 ($2,250 of it refundable), then $750/yr, against a $15,000 direct bond.

**Taxes and royalty.** §11 owns and computes the mining license tax: its brackets, and the 182-week new-operation holiday (`finance.tax.akLicenseHolidayWeeks`), which starts at the company's first cleanup in an `akStyle` district (§11 11.18). §6 only registers:
- `akMiningLicense` registration (no fee);
- the `akInitialProduction` affidavit (a no-fee filing on the auto-file list), due within `ak.initialProductionFilingWeeks` (4) of that first cleanup. It records the start date §11 already uses; it does not start the holiday, and missing it costs standing −2 (a missed filing, consequence `violation`), never the holiday.
- **Production royalty:** 3% of net income on state land, created through §5 `addProductionInterest` as `{ kind: 'governmentRoyalty', origin: 'regime', level: 'property', holder: { kind: 'government', id: 'akDnr' }, basis: 'netIncome', rate: 0.03, rateUnit: 'fraction', settle: 'cash', trigger: 'annual' }`, with rental credited against it (§11 settles at week 52).
- Returns are due wk 18.

**Calendar:** wk 13 bond and pool; wk 18 returns; wk 35 rental year starts, labor year ends, cash-in-lieu due; wk 48 rental and labor statement; wk 52 reclamation statement.

### 6.14 Yukon-style regime (P6)

**Claims** (`ClaimRuleSpec.kind = 'representationWork'`; amounts in C$, converted at §10 `market.cadToUsd` 0.72):
- A creek claim is about 23 ac. Record it within `ceil((yukon.recordingBaseDays (10) + distanceToTownMi / yukon.recordingMiPerDay (10)) / 7)` weeks for `yukon.recordingFeeCad` (C$10 ≈ $7; the mining recorder sits in the district town; §3 `claim.distanceToTownMi`). `registerTenureObligations` creates the statutory `ykRecording` obligation at location (missed → location void).
- Each claim runs for 1 year from its recording anniversary. Renewal needs C$200 of representation work per claim plus a C$10 fee; there is no cash in lieu.
- Excess work banks in C$200 steps, up to C$800 per claim per year.
- Grouping lets work anywhere in the group renew all of it (C$5 per claim for the first 10, C$1 after).
- A missed renewal lapses the claim.

**Class determination.** Recomputed whenever the plan changes, from the §7 plan, §9 `fuelStorageGal(claimId)` and §8 `personDays(state, claimId)`:

```
m3PerDay = gpm × 0.0037854 × 60 × plantHoursPerDay                 // 300 m3/day ≈ 120 gpm over 11 h: an 8 bcy/hr once-through plant, ≈ 22 bcy/hr at 80% recycle
gpm = §7 opsWaterUse(state, claimId).avgGpm (fresh withdrawal); plantHoursPerDay from the §7 plan
      // with several plant lines (§7 MinePlan.lines) the claim's daily volume is Σ_lines gpm_line × 0.0037854 × 60 × hours_line:
      // water and the permit footprint are claim-level, so one class covers every line on the claim
class = 4 if beyond any Class 2 limit AND (m3PerDay > 300 OR inStreamWork OR dischargeMode = 'discharge' (waste to a watercourse))
        // any production plant is beyond Class 2 limits, so in practice the water test decides
      = 3 if beyond any Class 2 limit;   = 2 if beyond any Class 1 limit;   = 1 for any other mechanized work
authority: none → 'casual'; class 1–2 → 'notice' (class limits become conditions); class 3–4 → 'plan' (class 3 adds maxWaterM3PerDay 300)
```

| Limit | Class 1 | Class 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Fuel on site | ≤ 1,320 gal (5,000 L) | ≤ 10,570 gal (40,000 L), ≤ 2,640 gal per container |
| Person-days per year per camp | ≤ 250 | > 250 |
| Trenching | ≤ 523 bcy/claim (400 m³), ≤ 1,570 per 3-claim group | `yk.class2TrenchBcyPerClaim` 2,000 (designer estimate) |
| Stripping | ≤ 0.15 ac/claim/yr (600 m²) | `yk.class2StripAcresPerClaim` 1.0 (designer estimate) |
| Water | Schedule 3 notice only (< 300 m³/day) | same |

| Type | Stages, median wk (σ) | Prep (C$): fee / direct / baseline; desk / field wk | Term and fee |
|---|---|---|---|
| `yk.class1` | notification, fixed 4 (25-day First Nation and stakeholder review) | owner 500 / 0 / 0; 1 / 0 | 260 wk |
| `yk.class2` | adequacy 3 (0.4) → seekingViews 4 (0.3) → recommendation 4 (0.3) → decisionDocument 6 (0.4) → notification fixed 2 | 6,000 / 1,000 / 0; 4 / 0 | 260 wk |
| `yk.class3` | as Class 2, then operating-plan approval 4 (0.4) | 10,000 / 2,000 / 3,000; 6 / 3 | 260 wk |
| `yk.class4` | YESAB: adequacy 12 (0.5) [4–40] → seekingViews 4 (0.3) → recommendation 5 (0.3) → decisionDocument 9 (0.4) [4–26]; then the Yukon Water Board: boardReview 14 (0.45) [6–52] → licenceDecision 6 (0.4) | 25,000 / 5,000 / 10,000; 12 / 6 | 260 wk (C$250) or 520 wk (C$500) |

**Class 4 outcomes and timing.**
- `baseInfo` is 0.45, checked at the end of seekingViews; `baseDeny` is 0.06, expressed as a recommend-against.
- Filing to licence takes a median of about 54 weeks (12–13 months), with P90 about 20 months.
- A recommend-against is followed by rejection with p 0.85; otherwise approval with 2 extra condition draws.
- Class 4 above 80 ac is referred to YESAB's executive committee with p 0.03, adding 52 weeks.

**Backlog.** Each district has renewal-wave years every 10 years (data offset), when Yukon Water Board and YESAB workload runs ×1.5. A renewal filed at least 26 weeks before expiry gets an automatic 52-week extension while it is pending.

**First Nation relation.** F runs 0–100 per district (`fnRelation`, distinct from §1 reputation R), starts at 50 and decays toward 50 with a 156-week half-life.
- **Inputs:**
  - engagement meeting: +5 ($3,000 × cpi, at most 2 per year);
  - benefit agreement: +20 while in force (max(US$25,000, 1% of the company's gold revenue from the district) per year, `exp.permitsFees`);
  - local-hire share of crew: +10 × share (§8);
  - habitat or water violation: −5;
  - forfeiture: −25;
  - reclamation: +0.5 per acre (cap +4 per year).
- **Effect at seekingViews:** `p_oppose = clamp(0.25 − 0.004 × (F − 50) + 0.3 × sensitivity, 0.02, 0.7)`, `p_concerns = 0.35`, otherwise support (one draw on `permits-app`, stageKey `fnViews`).
  - Opposition: recommend-against with p 0.35, otherwise +2 condition draws.
  - Concerns: +1 condition draw (wetland progressive reclamation, a timing window, or a cultural exclusion).
  - Support: information-request odds ×0.7.

**Other rules.**
- **Habitat class** (§3 `streamHabitatClass`, from the Fish Habitat Management System that DFO and Yukon run together) sets the settleable-solids compliance level and scales the 6.6 discharge base by `sqrt(0.2 / level)`:

  | Habitat class | Compliance level | Discharge base multiplier |
  |---|---|---|
  | High | closed loop mandatory | — |
  | Moderate-High | 0.8 mL/L | 0.50 |
  | Moderate-Moderate | 1.0 mL/L | 0.45 |
  | Moderate-Low | 1.3 mL/L | 0.39 |
  | Low | 2.0 mL/L | 0.32 |

- **Security:** 0.25 × RCE for Class 4 and 0.10 × RCE for Class 3. A §12 "security reform" event can raise it to 1.0 × RCE.
- **Royalty:** C$0.375 per crude oz exported, created through §5 `addProductionInterest` as `{ kind: 'governmentRoyalty', origin: 'regime', level: 'property', holder: { kind: 'government', id: 'ykEmr' }, basis: 'rawOz', rate: yukon.royaltyCadPerOz × market.cadToUsd (= 0.27), rateUnit: 'usdPerOz', settle: 'cash', trigger: 'sale' }`. At every sale §10 calls §5 `settleSaleInterests(state, { lotIds, channel, fineOz, priceUsd })`, which charges it on refinery sales (exports) and skips it when `channel = 'local'` (a local-buyer sale is not an export). This interest *is* the Yukon royalty: §11's Yukon `productionTax` is `'none'`. The real cost of this regime is time, not tax.
- **Inspections:** EMR (land) 1.5/yr, YWB (water licence) 1.0/yr, WSCB (safety) 1.0/yr; fines come from a C$ table (data).

All payments go through `finance.pay`. Gate codes other sections receive from `activityAllowed`: `PERMIT_REQUIRED`, `BOND_INSUFFICIENT`, `WATER_AUTH_REQUIRED`, `DISCHARGE_COVERAGE_REQUIRED`, `WETLAND_PERMIT_REQUIRED`, `MINE_ID_REQUIRED`, `TRAINING_REQUIRED`, `LICENSE_REQUIRED`, `INSURANCE_REQUIRED`, `PERMIT_LIMIT`. `permits/recordsCheck` and every action that draws dice are not undoable (§13).

### 6.16 Weekly resolution

§6 runs only in step 13; everything else is a pure function other steps call. `workloadIdx` is computed on demand from its keyed stream, so no state is rolled at year start.
- **Step 4 (§12).** One-shot calls (`forceInspection`, `recordExceedance`, `openInvestigation`, `addCondition`) only queue records; §6 resolves them in step 13 of the same week (including the complaint go/no-go roll of a `forceInspection` with reason `'complaint'`).
- **Step 7 (§8).** Assignments are gated with `isTrainedForFieldWork`.
- **Step 9 (§7, §4).** §7 reads `operatingAuthority`, `activityAllowed` and `conditionLimits` (which already reflect `complianceMode` and this week's flow), and reports `WeekOpsResult` plus `disturbance()`, `opsWaterUse()` and pond state; §4 programs read the same gates and report `programDisturbance`.
- **Step 13 (§6)** runs these sub-steps in order, entities in ascending ID (P1 runs only sub-step f, for other sections' obligations):

  | Sub-step | What happens |
  |---|---|
  | a. Applications | advance prep (desk, baseline, response weeks; owner desk days from §1); submit when ready; at `stageDueTurn`, resolve stage-end draws and enter the next stage, drawing its duration (`permits-app`) |
  | b. Permits | expiries, continuances, status changes, GP-cycle lapses; week 1: create the calendar-year obligations (license, annual fees, reports) and flag GP-renewal and Yukon wave years (year 1's are created by `newGame`, since the first pipeline runs as week 2; §2.6 turn semantics, D-2.13) |
  | c. Ledgers | rebuild reclamation ledgers (6.8 mapping), assessment credit, condition usage; discharge draw (`permits-exceed`) |
  | d. Inspections | roll and resolve routine and forced inspections (`permits-inspect`); complaint detection for exceeded conditions (`permits-exceed`) |
  | e. Violations | violations, fines (`permits-violation`), orders and abatement obligations; check deadlines and escalate; lift cured orders after re-inspection; report §8 citation feed and §1 reputation kinds |
  | f. Obligations | open windows; run auto-pay (statutory items, `finance.pay`, origin `pipeline`) and auto-file; then, after the last auto-pay try (no later sub-step or step pays a statutory item, so this is "the end of step 13" of 6.9): **statutory** items unsatisfied at `dueTurn + graceWeeks` take their consequence (forfeiture → `onTenureEnded(claimId, 'forfeited')` and §3 `forfeitToOpen`; `voidLocation` → `onTenureEnded(claimId, 'void')`); **billable** items unsatisfied at `dueTurn + graceWeeks + 1` (after last week's §11 settlement) go `missed` and route by owner: §6's own consequence, §5 → `land.onObligationMissed(obl)`, §1 → `investor.onMinimumMissed(state, obligationId)` (§11's own are checked by §11 in step 14f); create recurrences |
  | g. Bonds | premiums, reviews, top-ups, pending increases, surety cancellation (from last week's §11 distress and credit; during a reorganization case, collateral calls instead, 6.8), release inspections, stage-2 checks at the operating-end week (`permits-bond`), pool fees, forfeiture |
  | h. Liability | recompute liability and RCE; hand deltas to §11, which posts `liab.reclamation` and accretion in step 14 |
  | i. Standing | decay, then this week's capped deltas; P6 First Nation relations |
  | j. Alerts | `obligation.dueSoon/missed`, `permit.decision`, `permit.infoRequest`, `inspection.result`, `permit.conditionExceedance` (§13) |

- **Step 14 (§11).** Bills every open billable obligation due this week (14c), settles bills by priority (14e) and evaluates its own obligations at `dueTurn + graceWeeks + 1` (14f); §6 sees the result in next week's sub-step f.
- **Reorganization (P4, 6.8).** `permits.onReorganizationFiled` runs when §11's filing takes effect (pre-filing fines, judgments and indemnity → `inPlan`; one `bondCollateralCall` per active surety bond); the calls are statutory obligations settled in sub-step f like any other. §11 never bills `inPlan` items in 14c.

`PendingDecision`s: an info response is non-blocking with a deadline. A stop-work order that idles a claim's whole plan is blocking: the player must choose to reclaim, idle, or reassign the crew.

### 6.17 Interfaces

**Provides.**
- **Authority:** `operatingAuthority`, `authorityDetail`, `activityAllowed` (incl. `'bulkSample'` with `{ bcy, gpm }` for §7 bulk-sample plans), `conditionLimits(state, claimId)` (already reflecting `complianceMode`, flow and drought), `conditionUsage(state, claimId): ConditionUsage[]`.
- **Obligations (from P1):** the `Obligation` model with `createObligation`, `satisfyObligation`, `obligationsInRange`, `settlementClass(obl)` (the statutory/billable rule of 6.9, which §11 applies too); flags `category`, `payableNow`, `autoPayEligible`, `autoPay`, `prepLeadWeeks`, optional `payCategory`; owner routing of misses to `land.onObligationMissed` (§5) and `investor.onMinimumMissed` (§1).
- **Pipeline:** the `PipelineStage` enum and `stageForecast(state, appId)` with P10/P50/P90 per stage (for §13).
- **Reclamation and bonds:** `reclamationLiability(state, claimId)`, `rceEstimate(state, claimId, acresByType, tier)`, `reclamationCostEstimate(state, acres, districtId)` (RCE basis; §3 listings and the starter lease's bond face), `bondSummary(state)`.
- **Land (§5):** `registerTenureObligations(state, tenure)` (idempotent; called at location, at filing and at every closing; with `payer`); §6's handler on the shared `onTenureEnded(state, claimId, reason: TenureEndReason)` event, using §5's enum `'sold' | 'relinquished' | 'forfeited' | 'terminated' | 'foreclosed' | 'void' | 'voidedByExam' | 'converted'` (§6 sends `'forfeited'`, `'void'` and `'voidedByExam'`; 6.8 lists the handler per reason); `permitTransferOutcome(state, claimId, buyer, { kind, nonTransferable?, sellerBondCarryWeeks? })`, `transferPackage`, `permitPackageValue`, `permitCostEstimate`, `permitDelayEstimate`, `bondEstimate`, `reclamationEstimate`, `instantiatePermitStub(state, claimId, { transferDefect? })`, `recordsCheck(state, claimId)` (folded into §5 closings); calls `land.revealDefect` and `land.onObligationMissed`.
- **Training (§8):** `isTrainedForFieldWork(state, employeeId)`, `trainingRequirement(employee)`, `openInvestigation(state, claimId, tier)`, the safety (MSHA) citation feed.
- **Standing:** `applyStandingDelta(state, delta, reason, ref)`, for other sections' regulatory events.
- **Agencies (6.1):** `agencyFor(state, claimId, key)` → `AgencySpec` (real name, abbreviation, jurisdiction, job) for every text that names an agency (§12 events and news, §13 inbox, Permits screen and Help); the text key `permits.disclaimer`.

- **P6:** government `ProductionInterest` records through §5 `addProductionInterest` (AK net-income royalty, settled annually by §11; Yukon export royalty, settled by §5 `settleSaleInterests`); the machinery for §14's hard-rock permit rows.

### 6.18 Phase plan

| Phase | §6 scope |
|---|---|
| **P1** | **No permits.** `operatingAuthority` returns `plan` for every held claim and `activityAllowed` always succeeds. The **Obligation store, calendar queries, the statutory/billable rule, batch pay and step-13 sub-step f exist** for other sections' deadlines (§5 lease advance royalties, §11 loan payments, §1 investor items), all billable: §11 bills and pays them in step 14 of the due week, and §6 checks them at `dueTurn + 1` and routes misses to §5 or §1; §6 itself creates no obligations, bonds, inspections or standing changes. §7 records disturbed acres, but no liability is booked (§3 shows a $6,000/acre stub). The claim screen notes that permitting arrives later. |
| **P2** | **The full U.S. federal regime,** with northern and arid overlays. (1) Claim fees, recording, waiver and affidavit, forfeiture. (2) Casual, notice and plan tiers, validity examination. (3) All ancillary approvals, with insurance through §11's stub. (4) The pipeline: info requests, conditions, contests, appeals, renewals, amendments. (5) Exceedance and the discharge model. (6) RCE (with §7's work estimate and §3 `accessFactors`); cash and surety bonds (surety on §11's P2 stubs: `companyScore850` = the thin-file blend, `workingCapital`, `tangibleNetWorth`, `ownerPersonalNW`, `distressStatus`); staged release; forfeiture and debarment. (7) Liability; §6-created obligations, auto-pay (land on at every difficulty) and auto-file (incl. `mineIdRegistration`); batch filing. (8) Inspections, violations, orders, contests. (9) Standing, transfers (incl. leases and the starter permitted lease's ≤ 4-week path), stub instantiation with transfer-defect causes, the records check folded into §5 closings, the Inheritor's package and valuation. (10) The private (patented) variant. (11) The agency map for the Alaska and Nevada overlays (6.1), `agencyFor` and the disclaimer. Stubs: `M_fleet` = 1; no competitor workload; `loc` unavailable (`LOC_UNAVAILABLE`); insurance through §11's automatically bound GL stub. **Exit gates** (§1 1.19): the §2.12.1 `exceeder` and `abandoner` gates (6.20) and a plan-approval share of 35–45% (standing-60 plans filed in January approved before the next breakup). |
| **P3** | The safety (MSHA) citation rate uses fleet condition (`M_fleet`); machine withdrawal orders interact with the shop. |
| **P4** | Letter-of-credit instrument; surety underwriting on full credit profiles; owner indemnity hits personal guarantees; real insurance gates; reorganization handling (6.8: no stay for regulators, `inPlan` pre-filing money, surety collateral calls, no relinquishing open acres during a case). |
| **P5** | Complaint and inspection events (`forceInspection` with §6's complaint roll, `recordExceedance` incl. `'pondBreach'`, `openInvestigation`, `addCondition` incl. `noNightShift`); rule-change events (`permits.feeAdd.<feeKey>`, `permits.bondRateMult`, `permits.reviewTimeMult`, `permits.noticeMaxAcresSet`); competitors share agency workload (+0.02 to `M_workload` per §12 `competitorPermittingCount(districtId)`); permit package value drives negotiation. |
| **P6** | Alaska-style and Yukon-style regimes and districts, with their 6.1 agency rows (recording keys `permits.ak.*` / `permits.yukon.*`, CAD at §10 `market.cadToUsd`); bond pools; consolidated and staged pipelines; First Nation relations; government royalty interests (AK tax brackets and holiday stay §11's). The hard-rock track's permit content is §14's (14.10: lode notice and plan, ATF explosives user permit, blaster certification, air and water-pollution-control permits, RCE types, agencies `air` and `explosives`); §6 runs it with the P2 machinery. |

### 6.20 Balance levers and risks

**Strongest levers:**
- **Plan review medians, `info.baseInfo` and `info.fieldDataProb`** decide whether self-permitted raw ground loses a northern season. Target (a P2 exit gate, §1 1.19): about 35–45% of standing-60 plans filed in January are approved before the next breakup. These review times are realistic and stay; first-season mining under full rules is raised through supply instead (§3's widened `permitStub`, which gives ≈ 10% of northern listings a true transferable plan against an 8% gate, D-3.48, and the starter permitted lease, 6.12).
- **Surety tier thresholds and collateral** set the spring cash a bootstrapper loses to bonding, about $10–45k for a first plan.
- **`rceDirectPerAcre`, `rceEquipUsdHr` and `rceIndirectRate`** set bond and liability per acre; `rceEquipUsdHr` sets the bond penalty for dumping instead of backfilling (§7's lever).
- **Exceedance detection, fines and `water.overUseGrantCut`** decide whether bending limits dominates.

**Exploits and counters:**
1. **Always exceed.**
   - Counter: about 74% detection per season at e ≈ 0.33; the meter and escalation make a second offense near-certain to be caught and to cost a suspension; a water overuse cuts the grant 10% for the rest of its term, so it pays only on a short horizon (6.6); standing compounds into slower approvals.
   - Sim gate (P2 exit): the `exceeder` bot of §2.12.1's catalog (cautious with every exceedable kind in `exceed`) must not beat `cautious` on 5-year median net worth by more than 10%, and its bankruptcy rate (BALANCE BK_5: filings of either kind, §5.1; G-04) must not be lower. Tune `exceed.*.complaintSlope` first, then `water.overUseGrantCut`.
2. **Serial notices instead of a plan.** Notices never authorize production. Bulk samples are capped at 590 bcy (≤ ~7 oz) and blocked for 104 weeks per claim group.
3. **Abandon instead of reclaim.**
   - Counter: the forfeited bond is 1.26× the booked liability and 2–3× the true own-crew cost, plus the excess judgment, −30 standing, the hold, debarment, and reputation (−10 and −8).
   - Sim gate (P2 exit): the `abandoner` ablation (cautious, but relinquishing mined-out claims unreclaimed with `confirmUnreclaimed`) ends 3 years with lower net worth than `cautious` on the same seed in at least 95% of seeds.
4. **Waiver gaming with 10 association placers (1,600 ac).** A real loophole that we accept. It is bounded by the cost of buying association placers and by the December affidavit risk.
5. **Thin-collateral surety, then walk away.** The indemnity becomes company debt, and the owner's under §11 guarantees.
6. **Permitted ground always wins.** §5 prices `permitPackageValue` into asks, so the premium tracks the season saved. Self-permitting stays the cheap, slow path.
7. **Just-in-time bonding.** Raising B one acre at a time would minimize premium and locked cash; the 2-week acceptance lag, the $150 surety rider and the strict-mode stop at B make the player bond a few weeks of stripping ahead instead.
8. **Dump everything, bond later.** Unbackfilled dumps price at ≈ $27k/ac direct through `excessHours`, so skipping concurrent backfill shows up in the next bond review and in ARO at once.
9. **File to shed fines and bonds.** A reorganization (6.8) pays pre-filing fines in full through the plan, leaves every statutory obligation and reclamation order running, and makes sureties call collateral, so filing never makes compliance cheaper; it only spreads pre-filing judgments and indemnity over the plan.
10. **Contest everything.** The minimum $2,000 legal fee makes contesting a $200 MSHA citation a loss; contests pay only on large fines or where the record matters (repeat multipliers, the 3-strike rule).
11. **Owner as the only clerk.** Owner auto-file removes the click tax but costs desk days at the busiest time (§1) and carries the owner's waiver defect odds; the specialist is the clean, expensive answer.

**Harshness and pacing.** Instant forfeiture on Sept 1 is the real rule, with no grace period. It is mitigated by the alert ladder, land auto-pay on by default at every difficulty, specialist or owner auto-file, and batch pay (D-6.16, D-6.42); because a claim fee is statutory, nothing pays it late by accident (D-6.41). Long reviews could make year 1 dull; the counters are Notice bulk sampling, permitted listings, and the starter permitted lease in each starting district that reaches `plan` authority within 4 weeks (6.12). See OQ-6.2.
