```
            salaried: annual salary + 52 × (share + 0.5 × bonusAccrual8w) / n8
n8        = weeks in the last8 window (1–8);  bonusAccrual8w, goldShare8w, straightEqHours8w = sums over that window
share     = goldShare8w once the employee has shared in ≥ 2 cleanups this season; before that
            0.5 × n8 × pct × §7 projectOpsVisible(claim) recovered raw oz/week × est. fineness × spot   (pool: × the member's hours share)
straightEqHours8w = Σ last8 (REG + otMult × OT);  if 0, payRate = base rate
marketRef = marketWageBase[role, district] × remotePremium[access]      // no seasonWage (8.4); salaried: annual vs annual
payScar  += 12 for each payroll run with this employee short (unpaidWages.newMissThisRun); × 0.95 per week
qF        = claim, camp or site-shop staff: foremanFor(claim, line).skill, where line = the line of the machine the
            employee ran most this week (§7 crewHours lineId), else L1; a small crew's lead person counts (8.12);
            program crew: the skill of §4 programCrewUse's
            supervisingGeologist (employee: effective true skill; 'owner': ownerSkill('geologist'); a consultant
            EngagementId: §4's tier skill 50 / 70 / 85; null: 50); office, pool-shop and district roles: 50 (neutral)
safetyRecord = company.safetyRecord.value at the end of last week's step 10 (8.10; start 50)
```

**Shocks** (points, applied before adjustment): first missed paycheck (`unpaidWages.misses` goes 0 → 1) −15; firing a coworker on the same site −3 (−6 if the fired employee had tenure > 13 weeks and morale > 55, i.e. seen as unfair; 0 if fired for a documented cause); a coworker quits −1; layoffs of others −2 to survivors; a pay cut −0.5 per % cut; a one-off bonus +4 per week of pay (cap +10); a raise flows through the pay term; promotion +5; recall +3; injuries (8.10); a season bonus paid in full +6; `moraleShock` from §12 events and from §11 (the crew's morale hit when the company files for bankruptcy reorganization, Chapter 11 Subchapter V: §11 calls `moraleShock('company', points)` with its own value). Shocks raised by actions or by later steps (injuries in step 10, payroll in step 14) are queued in `moraleMem.pendingShock` and applied in the next step 7.

There is no separate owner-background bonus. An operator-background owner running the claim is a skill-85 foreman, worth +4.2 through the leadership term (D-8.9).

**Safety record.** Two terms carry safety into morale. `injuryMemory` is local and fades in weeks. The company `safetyRecord` term follows the crew to every claim, including one opened after the injury. A careful company drifts toward a record of 75 (+1.5; +2.4 at 90 with a full-coverage officer). A fatality takes 40 points off the record, −2.4 on every claim, and the drift closes half the gap in about 35 field weeks (D-8.40).

**Worked example.** An operator (reliability 60) on a seasonal-road claim is paid $36 against marketRef $37.80 ($36 base market × 1.05 remote; the operating-season wage bump applies only to new hires). He works 66 h (26 OT) with fatigue 36, in a standard (skid) camp with a skill-60 cook, under an operator-background owner-foreman (85), in his 14th week on site, at reputation 50 and a company safety record of 50 (the starting value, so the record term is 0). M* = 51.2 − 3.9 − 9.6 + 5.0 + 0.8 + 4.2 − 2.0 = **45.7**. From M = 52: M' = 52 + 0.25 × (45.7 − 52) = **50.4**.
*Then payroll misses one week.* Shock −15 gives 35.4. The target falls by 15 (unpaid) + 12 (scar) to 18.7, so M' = 35.4 + 0.25 × (18.7 − 35.4) = **31.2**. The weekly quit probability goes from 0.27% to 7.8% (8.8). A second missed week takes him to 21.5 and 50%.

### 8.8 Quits, poaching and walk-offs

Rolled in step 7 after the morale update, for every active, injured or rotation-off employee (stream `rng(seed,'staff-quit',turn,empId)`: first draw the quit, second the walk-off):

```
logit p = −5.8 + 1.0 × (50 − M)/10 + 0.7 × [tenure < 4 wk] + 1.5 × min(unpaidWages.weeks, 3)
        + 0.8 × (CLD_d − 0.5) + 0.4 × (truth.skill − 50)/50                  // good people have options
        − 0.25 × min(unvestedBonus / weeklyPay, 3) − 0.3 × [gold share] − 0.15 × min(seasonsWithCompany, 3)
p_quit  = min(0.95, σ(logit) × effective('staff.quitHazardMult', scope))      // difficulty-resolved (§1 1.11) × event modifiers
weeklyPay = mean gross over last8 (rate × 40 h, or salary/52, if last8 is empty);  CLD_d = 0.5 in P1–P4 (term vanishes)
```
Calibration: morale 50 → 0.30%/week; 30 → 2.2%; 15 → 9%; 70 → 0.04%. A quitter walks off at once with p `staff.quit.walkOffShare` 0.5 (availability 0 this week); otherwise they work this week and leave. Final pay is due in full. With unpaid wages ≥ 2 weeks, hourly staff refuse to work (availability 0; salaried at ≥ 3 weeks) until paid. §12 owns the collective `walkout`. Every departure writes a `Separation` (8.16) with its kind: `quit`, `poached`, `fired`, `firedCause`, `layoff`, `injuryExit`, `fatality`.

**Why mid-season quits are the worst.** In week 28 on the reference seasonal-road claim, the loader operator feeding the plant walks off. The outpost operator pool in the operating season expects 10 × 0.3 × 0.45 = 1.35 people (about 1.0 once competitors hire, P5) and has none this week. A recruiter takes 2 weeks, then 2 weeks' travel and 8 h of training. The foreman shifts the dig excavator to part-time feeding, and §7 shows the plant at about 55% for 4 weeks. That is 4 × 0.45 × 27 raw oz ≈ 49 raw oz ≈ **$173k of gold pushed out of this season** (0.85 fineness, $4,200), with debt service still due. His 8% completion bonus would have cost about $5k.

**Poaching** (§12 creates `keyPoach`; §8 decides acceptance):

```
poachAcceptProb(emp, offerWage) = σ(−1.6 + 8 × ln(offerWage / payRate) + 0.6 × (50 − M)/10
                                   − 0.25 × min(unvestedBonus/weeklyPay, 3) − 0.6 × [gold share] − 0.4 × [seasonsWithCompany ≥ 2])
```
A content employee (M 60) offered 1.2× accepts with p 0.32. With 3 weeks' pay unvested, 0.18. An unhappy one (M 35), 0.68. §12's responses (match, retention bonus) multiply this, and §12 draws the acceptance on its own event stream; §8 only returns the probability. An accepted poach leaves one week later as a `poached` separation (no UI charge, no coworker shock beyond the −1 for a quit).

### 8.9 Fatigue and hours

Fatigue F ∈ [0, 100] per person (the owner too, with §7's `ownerHours`, 60 h by §1's default), updated in step 10 from actual hours, after the injury rolls. The value used all week (effSkill in steps 7–9, injury hazard in step 10) is the start-of-week F_t:

```
consecutiveNoDayOffWeeks = (days off this week = 0) ? previous + 1 : 0          // updated first
load   = 0.40 × max(0, H − 40) + 0.015 × max(0, H − 60)² + 1.0 × min(consecutiveNoDayOffWeeks, 8)
       + (night shift ? 3 : 0) + heatAdd + (overCapacity > 0 ? 3 : 0) + (commuting ? 2 : 0)
heatAdd = day-shift field work: staff.heatFatiguePerDegF (0.4) × max(0, meanTempF − 80)    // §1 WeatherWeek; 88 °F → 3.2
          night shift: × 0.3
rec    = staff.fatigue.recByDaysOff[days off]: 0 → 0.25, 1 → 0.30, 2 → 0.40, 3–4 → 0.55, 5–6 → 0.62, 7 → 0.70
         (7 = a week not worked: layoff, rotation off, injury)
       + (on site: cook skill ≥ 60 ? 0.03 : 0) + campRec[tier] (good +0.02, premium +0.03)
F_{t+1} = clamp(F_t × (1 − rec) + load, 0, 100)
effSkill = classSkill (or role skill) − 0.35 × max(0, F_t − 30)        // the single channel to productivity and wear
```
Steady states: 10 × 6 (60 h) → 27; 11 × 6 (66 h) → 36; 12 × 6 (72 h) → 50; 11 × 7 (77 h) → 100 eventually. The 7-day trajectory from F 20 is 35, 48, 58, 66, 74, 81, 87, 92 by week 8, consistent with R4's "risk climbs after ~60 h/week and after week 8–10 of no days off". At F 87 a skill-60 operator works at effSkill 40: productivity −10% and wear +23% against the same operator fresh, and injury hazard ×4.0 per week against a 66-hour week (8.10). Fatigue also enters morale (8.7) and absence (below). *Trade-off:* a 7th day adds 17% of hours. By week 8, output per hour is down about 10%, so the net gain in output is about +5%. Meanwhile the wage bill is up 21% (all overtime), injuries are ×4 and morale is about 20 points lower. On marginal ground it stops paying.

**Absence** (step 7, stream `rng(seed,'staff-absence',turn,empId)`): days absent ~ Binomial(scheduled days, a) with `a = 0.02 × exp(−0.035 × (reliability − 50)) × (1 + max(0, 40 − M)/40) × (1 + max(0, F − 60)/80)`. That is 2% at reliability 50 and 5.7% at 20.

**Rotation** (P5, `staff/setRotation`): `3on1off` puts each worker off one week in four (offset by `rotationOffset`). The off week is unpaid for hourly staff, recovers fatigue at 0.70, resets season drag and is worth +2 morale. On winter-trail and fly-in claims, each off week costs a round trip. *Trade-off:* continuous coverage needs a third more crew and more travel.

### 8.10 Injuries, safety culture and the safety record

Rolled in step 10 for each person with hours this week, in ascending ID (stream `rng(seed,'staff-injury',turn,empId)`). §8's sub-step runs after §9's wear and failure sub-step and §7's re-resolve, so H is the hours actually worked:

```
λ = h0 × H × M_hours × M_fatigue × M_person × M_skill × M_culture × M_equip × M_new × M_night × M_heat × M_role
      × M_sup × effective('staff.injuryHazardMult')
h0        = staff.injury.basePerHour 1.6e-5            // all tiers incl. first aid
M_hours   = 1 + 0.025·max(0, H − 50) + 0.0025·max(0, H − 60)²        // 60 h 1.25 · 66 h 1.49 · 72 h 1.91 · 77 h 2.40
M_fatigue = 1 + 2·max(0, F_t/100 − 0.5)                                // start-of-week F; matches §12's incident driver
M_person  = exp(−0.02 × (safety − 50))                                 // safety 20 → 1.82; 80 → 0.55
M_skill   = exp(−0.012 × (effSkill − 50))                              // machine roles (operator, driller, plant, mechanic, welder); else 1
M_culture = 1.6 − crewSafetyIndex(location)                             // claim, or the claim of a program/site shop; a pool mechanic:
                                                                        //   the claim with most of his hours this week (ties: lower ID),
                                                                        //   company mean with none; office roles: 1
M_equip   = 1 + 1.5·max(0, 0.7 − §9 meanTrueHealth(claimId))           // SMR-weighted true health on that claim; P1–P2: 1
M_sup     = staff.noForemanIncidentMult (1.15) on a claim running as a small crew with no foreman (8.12); else 1
M_new     = 1.5 for tenure < 4 weeks;  M_night = 1.15 on second shift
M_heat    = day-shift field work: 1 + staff.injury.heatPerDegF (0.02) × max(0, meanTempF − 80)   // heat illness, §1; 92 °F → 1.24
M_role    : laborer 1.2, operator 1.0, mechanic 1.3, welder 1.3, plantOperator 1.1, driller 1.4, foreman 0.6,
            geologist (field) 0.6, safetyOfficer 0.4, cook 0.5, office roles 0.05
p_injury  = 1 − exp(−λ)
crewSafetyIndex = clamp(0.15 + 0.30·officerCoverage + 0.15·trainingCompliance + 0.25·safetyRecord/100
                        + 0.15·foremanSafety/100, 0, 1)        // trainingCompliance = share of field crew current; owner safety 60
```
The typical small operation (no officer, trained crew, record 50, foreman safety 50) scores 0.50, giving M_culture 1.10. With a full-coverage officer, record 80 and foreman safety 70 it scores 0.905, giving 0.70.

**Severity** (stream `rng(seed,'staff-injury-sev',turn,empId)`; draw order: tier, time lost, never-returns, WC amount, medical-only, late notification; a fatality's coworker quits draw on `rng(seed,'staff-injury-sev',turn,coworkerId)`):

| Tier | Share | Time lost | WC incurred → §11 `handleLoss` | MSHA (§6) | Morale (claim / company) | Safety record | Reputation (§1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| firstAid | 0.707 | U(1, 4) h this week | p 0.35 a medical-only claim LN(1,500, 0.6) [300, 8,000] | not reportable | −0.5 / 0 | −0.5 | — |
| lostTime | 0.260 | days LN(12, 0.8) [3, 120] × incidentMult | LN(35,000, 0.8) [4,000, 250,000] | reportable; records only | −4 / −1 | −8 | — |
| serious | 0.030 | weeks LN(12, 0.5) [4, 52] × incidentMult; p 0.25 never returns | LN(180,000, 0.6) [40,000, 1,500,000] | `openInvestigation(claim, 'serious')` | −10 / −3 | −20 | −3 |
| fatal | 0.003 | employee removed | LN(500,000, 0.4) [200,000, 1,500,000] | `openInvestigation(claim, 'fatal')` | −22 / −6; each coworker on the claim quits with p 0.15 | −40 | −10 |

- `incidentMult = 1.2 − 0.004 × qF` (foreman 50 → 1.0; none → 1.2; a small crew uses its lead person's qF, 8.12).
- **Morale.** On the injured worker's claim, everyone takes an immediate shock of half the claim value, and the full claim value is added to `claimSafety.injuryMemory` (a target term, decaying ×0.92/week, so a fatality still weighs about −11 eight weeks later). Every other employee takes the company value as a one-off shock.
- From P5, the serious and fatal shares ×`staff.seriousShareAfterEvents` 0.75 (remainder to lostTime), because §12's `seriousIncident` adds site-level incidents (D-12.12).
- Lost-time and serious injuries set `status: 'injured'` until `returnTurn = turn + ceil(lostDays / 7)` (calendar days away, as WC counts them; serious weeks are used directly). WC pays indemnity, so the company pays no wages meanwhile. A serious injury that never returns ends employment at `returnTurn` (`injuryExit`, no UI charge); a fatality ends it at once (`fatality`).
- **Director.** For every serious or fatal injury whose `cause` is `'work'`, §8 calls §12 `events.noteExternalShock('injury', injuryId)` in step 10, so pacing sees it (§12 D-12.31). Injuries §12 itself caused carry the event id and are not reported again.
- If WC has lapsed, the incurred amount falls on cash as bills over 26 weeks, and §6 records the violation.
- If the claim ran under a lead hand or as a small crew (no foreman or owner present), a serious or fatal injury is notified late with p 0.3 (§6 violation kind `safety.lateNotification`; MSHA in the U.S. districts).
- **The owner** rolls with safety 60 and his ops skill. He has no WC (§1, D-11.27): medical costs come from personal cash (lostTime LN(8,000, 0.6); serious LN(45,000, 0.6)) and `owner.injuredUntilTurn` is set. A fatal roll on the owner becomes serious (D-8.21).

**Calibration.** At reference conditions (66 h, F 36, culture 1.10, average skill and safety) λ per operator-week = 66 × 1.6e-5 × 1.49 × 1.10 = 0.173%. At neutral multipliers, lost-time-or-worse is 0.94 per 200,000 h, inside R4's surface metal/non-metal 0.8–1.2, and recordables (lost-time or worse plus medical-only first aid) are 1.73, inside R4's TRC 1.5–2.2. At the reference small op's long weeks and average culture it rises to 1.54, above the all-mines average, as befits small seasonal camps. The fatality rate at multipliers of 1.0 is 9.6 per 100k FTE (R4: 10–15; §12's `seriousIncident` adds about 17%). A 6-person crew at reference conditions expects 0.06 lost-time injuries per season. A reckless one (77 h weeks, F 90, culture 1.30, effSkill 40, h̄ 0.5, half new hires) runs at ×7.3: **0.43 lost-time and 0.05 serious per season**. *Trade-off:* safety spending rarely pays in one season; recklessness compounds into EMR (§11), citations (§6), morale and reputation.

**Safety record** (`company.safetyRecord`, 0–100, visible, start 50; feeds `crewSafetyIndex`, §6's inspection `M_culture` and the morale target, 8.7):

```
weekly: SR += 0.02 × (target − SR),  target = 70 + 15 × companyOfficerCoverage + 5 × trainingCompliance   (0.01/wk with no field work)
        companyOfficerCoverage = field-crew-weighted mean of safetyOfficerCoverage over claims (8.5)
events: firstAid −0.5, lostTime −8, serious −20, fatal −40; MSHA citation (§6 feed) non-S&S −0.5, S&S −2
interface SafetyRecord { value: number; lastLostTimeTurn: number | null; log: { turn: number; delta: number; ref: Id }[] /*52 wk*/ }
interface InjuryRecord { id: Id /* inj_ */; turn: number; empId: EmployeeId | 'owner'; claimId: ClaimId | null;
  tier: 'firstAid'|'lostTime'|'serious'|'fatal'; lostDays: number; returnTurn: number | null; neverReturns: boolean;
  wcIncurredCents: Cents; medicalOnly: boolean; lateNotified: boolean; cause: 'work' | string /* §12 event id */ }
```
The calc tree of each roll lives in the `WeekReport`, not in state (§2.8), so the sim (explanations off) and the UI produce identical state.

### 8.11 Skill multiplier functions (consumed elsewhere)

All take an effective skill s ∈ [0, 100] (8.9: class skill minus the fatigue penalty) unless noted. Pure, monotone, and listed in `data/tuning/staff.ts`.

```
skillProductivityMult(s) = 0.70 + 0.0065·s − 0.00001·s²                      // §9 machineEffectiveRate; §4 rigs
skillWearMult(s)         = s < 50 ? 1 + 0.8 × ((50 − s)/30)^1.3 : 1 − 0.003 × (s − 50)     // §9 wearPerHour
skillRecoveryMult(s)     = s ≤ 55 ? 1.5 − s/110 : 1.0 − (s − 55)/180         // §7 loss exponent (D-7.20)
inspectionAccuracy(s)    = { healthSd: 0.20 − 0.0015·s, defectDetectP: 0.30 + 0.0065·s, optimism: 0.06 × (1 − s/100) }   // §9
repairQuality(s)         = 0.80 + 0.002·s            // share of the targeted health gain achieved (§9)
repairHoursMult(s)       = 1 + 0.006 × (50 − s)      // labor hours per work order (§9)
reworkHazardMult(s)      = 1 + 1.5 × (1 − s/100)²    // failure hazard on the repaired component for its first 200 h (§9)
permitApplicationQuality(s) = 0.45 + 0.005·s         // §6 (as §6 specified)
drillerNoiseMult(s)      = 1.25 − 0.005·s            // §4 sample noise on company-drilled holes
controllerQuality(s)     = clamp(s / 70, 0.5, 1.3)   // scales §11's controller effects
```

| s | 0 | 20 | 35 | 50 | 65 | 80 | 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| skillProductivityMult | 0.700 | 0.826 | 0.915 | 1.000 | 1.080 | 1.156 | 1.250 |
| skillWearMult | 2.554 | **1.800** | 1.325 | 1.000 | 0.955 | 0.910 | 0.850 |
| skillRecoveryMult | 1.500 | 1.318 | 1.182 | 1.045 | 0.944 | 0.861 | 0.750 |
| inspection healthSd / detectP | 0.20 / 0.30 | 0.17 / 0.43 | 0.148 / 0.53 | 0.125 / 0.63 | 0.103 / 0.72 | 0.08 / 0.82 | 0.05 / 0.95 |
| repairQuality / hoursMult | 0.80 / 1.30 | 0.84 / 1.18 | 0.87 / 1.09 | 0.90 / 1.00 | 0.93 / 0.91 | 0.96 / 0.82 | 1.00 / 0.70 |

Anchors: productivity 1.00 is the guide's "average operator, rough ground" rate, and skill 100 reaches R4's typical sheet rate (+25%). R4's Cat operator factors (poor 0.60 / average 0.75 / excellent 1.0) map to 0.80 / 1.00 / 1.33 relative to average. The game compresses the top end because skill also cuts wear. Wear: a skill-20 operator wears an undercarriage at 1.8×, so a 4,000 h D8 track group lasts about 2,200 h, R4's "severe" life. **Recommended per-component sensitivity for §9:** `1 + sens × (skillWearMult − 1)` with undercarriage and tires 1.0, structure 0.8, drivetrain 0.7, hydraulics 0.5, engine 0.3, electrical 0.1.

### 8.12 Delegation, the owner, and the office roles

**The foreman rule.** Every active claim (washing, or a plan with mechanized work) needs a foreman: either a hired foreman (or a promoted employee in the foreman role) assigned to it, or the owner (§1 assignment `foreman`, or `operator` at foreman skill −15), unless it runs as a small crew (below). The owner covers one claim. Activating *any* claim's plan (`ops/setMinePlan` with `active`, `ops/setPlanActive`, `ops/setLineActive`) fails with `FOREMAN_REQUIRED` whenever `foremanFor(state, claimId).kind` would be `'none'` at activation, counting assignments that take effect at the next step 7: no hired foreman and no owner assigned to *that* claim, and the plan does not qualify as a small crew. The first claim is not exempt, and a second claim with more than three hands, a second shift or a second plant line needs a hired foreman (§7 7.2 enforces it). The foreman is set only through people's assignments: §8 `staff/assign` with `{ kind: 'claim', claimId }` for a hired foreman, or §1 `owner/setAssignment`; §7's `MinePlan` has no foreman field and §13's plan editor links to Staff instead. One foreman covers both shifts of a two-shift claim (the night shift's looser supervision is already in §7/§8's night factors, D-8.33) and up to `staff.foremanMaxLines` (2) plant lines (below, D-8.49).

**Lead hand.** When a supervisor *assigned* to the claim is still assigned but unavailable this week (injured, absent, rotation off, forced desk days) or quit within the last 3 weeks, the best effective-skill operator on the lines he covers (on site, for a one-line claim) serves as **lead hand** at `staff.leadHandSkillFrac` 0.6 × skill. The counter `leadHandWeeks` (`StaffSlice.supervision`, per line) counts lead-hand weeks and resets to 0 only after `staff.leadHandResetWeeks` (4) consecutive weeks with the foreman present. When it passes `staff.leadHandMaxWeeks` (3), `foremanFor` returns `none` and the plan (or, beyond L1, that line) stands down: crew on guaranteed hours, alert `crew.noForeman`. **Reassigning** the foreman (or the owner) away is not an absence: the claim has no foreman from the next step 7 and stands down at once. Alternating the owner between two claims therefore does not run both (D-8.18).

```
qF = a × effSkill(foreman) + (1 − a) × leadHandSkill        a = foreman's availableFraction this week (0..1)
     hired: effSkill of the foreman role; owner: ownerSkill('foreman') − (owner assignment 'operator' ? 15 : 0), less fatigue
     leadHandSkill = 0.6 × best effSkill among the covered lines' operators this week (0 if none; then 'none' when a = 0)
```

**Small crews** (owner ruling 2026-10-05, D-8.48). A claim with no hired foreman and no owner assigned runs as a **small crew** when, this week (and at activation, with assignments effective at the next step 7):
- `fieldCrewCount(state, claimId)` ≤ `staff.smallCrewMaxNoForeman` (3), the owner excluded, and ≥ 1;
- its plan has one active plant line and `shiftsPerDay` = 1.

`fieldCrewCount(state, claimId)` counts the employees whose assignment this week puts them on the claim: `claim`, `camp`, `security` or `caretaker` on it, a site-mode shop at it, and §4 program crew whose program is on it (§6's `M_size` reads the same count). A small crew has no supervisor: the best hand sets the pace informally. `foremanFor` returns `kind: 'smallCrew'`, `empId` = the employee with the best effective skill among the claim's operators and plant operators this week (ties: lower ID), `skill` = `staff.leadHandSkillFrac` (0.6) × that skill, and that person's `safety`. Then:
- §7 runs every machine at the flat `ops.noForemanEfficiency` (0.92), not the qF formula; redeployment and pay contact use the lead person's qF;
- leadership morale and `incidentMult` use the same qF; injury hazard takes `M_sup` = `staff.noForemanIncidentMult` (1.15) (8.10), and a serious or fatal injury is notified late with p 0.3, as under a lead hand;
- the test runs at every step 7: a fourth hand on the claim, a second shift or a second line ends it, and from the next step 7 the claim needs a foreman or stands down (`crew.noForeman`). `staff/hire`, `staff/assign` and `staff/recall` return the non-blocking validator warning `SMALL_CREW_ENDS` when the action would take a claim now running as `smallCrew` past `staff.smallCrewMaxNoForeman` with no foreman or owner assigned, so §13's modals can say so before the player commits (13.7).

`smallCrew` only replaces `none`. Where a foreman or the owner is assigned, the rules above apply, including the lead-hand limit; but when the lead-hand counter would turn a claim to `none`, a claim that passes the test runs as `smallCrew` instead.

**Plant lines and foreman span** (P3; owner ruling 2026-10-05, D-8.49). With several plant lines (§7 7.2.1), supervision is per line:

```
supervisors(C)  = [owner, if assigned foreman or operator on C] ++ [hired foremen assigned to C, ascending EmployeeId]
coverage        : supervisor k (k = 0, 1, …) covers the active lines at positions k·S … k·S + S − 1 in lineId order,
                  S = staff.foremanMaxLines (2); availability and the lead-hand rule apply per supervisor
leftover lines  : a line lead hand: kind 'leadHand', qF = 0.6 × best effSkill among that line's operators and plant
                  operators this week, with no week limit while L1's supervisor is 'hired' or 'owner';
                  otherwise the line follows L1 (lead hand or none with it)
```

Two lines need one foreman; three need two, or the third runs under a line lead hand at 0.6 × skill (§7 warning `LINE_LEAD_HAND`). Lines covered by the same supervisor share their counters. `staff/assign` of a foreman to a claim fails with `FOREMAN_SLOT_TAKEN` when the claim already has `max(1, ceil(active lines / S))` supervisors.

```ts
foremanFor(state, claimId, lineId: LineId = 'L1'): {
  kind: 'hired'|'owner'|'leadHand'|'smallCrew'|'none'; empId?: EmployeeId | 'owner';
  skill: number /* qF above: effective (fatigue- and availability-adjusted), true-based */;
  shownSkill: Range; safety: number; leadHandWeeks: number;
  lineIds: LineId[] /* the active lines this supervisor covers */ }
// without a line: L1's supervisor, the claim's senior one
```
§7 reads `skill` as qF for `F` (except a small crew's flat 0.92), redeploy and `S_dig`, per line; machines in shared roles use L1's. §8 uses it for leadership morale (each employee under the supervisor of the line he worked most), `crewSafetyIndex` (`safety` = the foreman's, or the lead hand's or small crew's lead person's) and `incidentMult`. `supervisionIncidentMult(state, claimId)` returns 1.15 for a small crew and 1 otherwise, for §12's site incidents. *Trade-off:* a $125k foreman unlocks a second claim with more than three hands, a second shift or a second plant line, and frees the owner, but a weak one quietly costs 5–10% of every machine hour on that claim.

**Worked example: a small crew.** Claim B is a 20-acre highway claim worked by three hands: a skill-60 excavator operator feeding a `tr50` directly, a skill-50 plant operator and a laborer. The owner runs claim A. With no foreman, B is a small crew: F = 0.92; the lead person's qF = 0.6 × 60 = 36, so the redeploy share is 0.6 × 0.36 = 0.22, S_dig = 0.8 × 60 + 0.2 × 36 = 55.2, leadership morale is 0.12 × (36 − 50) = −1.7, and each operator's injury hazard rises ×1.15 (0.173% → 0.199% per week at reference conditions). A skill-60 hired foreman ($125k: $2,404 a week, $2,933 with the 1.22 burden) would give F = 0.94 (+2.2% of every machine hour), S_dig 60, leadership +1.2 and no ×1.15. On a claim grossing about $50k of gold a week the +2.2% is worth about $1.1k a week, so on three hands the foreman does not pay. Hiring a truck driver makes four hands: from the next step 7 B stands down until a foreman is assigned.

**Worked example: three lines.** An 80-acre claim runs three lines under one skill-70 hired foreman. He covers L1 and L2 (F = 0.955). L3 runs under its best hand, a skill-55 operator (qF 33, F = 0.900). A second foreman of skill 60 lifts L3 to F = 0.94, +4.5% of L3's machine hours, for about $2.9k a week loaded.

**P6 delegation depth.** `staff/setForemanAuthority { claimId, canHire, maxWageMult, discretion }`. With `canHire`, a hired foreman replaces a quitter within the wage cap from the district pool, at the next step 3. He ranks candidates by `résuméMid + (qF/100) × (trueSkill − résuméMid) + N(0, 12 × (1 − qF/100))` (stream `rng(seed,'staff-delegate',turn,claimId)`), so a good foreman sees through résumés and a weak one hires on paper. With `discretion: 'adjust'`, §7's P6 auto-plan runs on that claim, with decision noise `foremanDecisionNoise(qF) = 0.25 × (1 − qF/100)` on its objective.

**Owner as pseudo-employee** (`emp_owner`, §1 1.7/1.9). `ownerSkill(role)` (values are §1's; §8 holds the `staff.*` keys):
- foreman and operator: `staff.ownerOpsSkillByBackground` 85 for an operator background, 40 otherwise (any machine class, no class penalty);
- mechanic: `staff.ownerMechanicSkill` 85 (mechanic background only), with +`staff.ownerShopHoursPerWeek` 50 shop hours/week in `shop` (site or pool mode, under the same rules as a hired mechanic; §1's owner assignment carries the mode) and `staff.ownerInspectionsPerWeek` 2 free inspections/week;
- geologist: §4's `geology.ownerGeologistSkill` 75 (geologist background; §4 owns the value and the effects, D-1.33): program supervision as `fieldGeologist`, records reviews and audits on desk days. A geologist owner assigned `foreman` or `operator` on claim C also supervises one §4 program located on C without a separate assignment (§4 4.13); a program elsewhere needs `fieldGeologist`;
- landSpecialist: `staff.ownerLandSpecialistSkill` 80 (landman background, desk). The 80 drives §5's `landSkill` only. Applications the owner prepares use §6's owner-prep keys (`permits.ownerPrepQuality.landman` 0.65, `permits.ownerPrepSpeed.landman` 1.1), not this section's `permitApplicationQuality` curve (which would give 0.85 / 0.85 at 80), because the owner prepares on desk days (§1 1.7).

Owner and hire do not stack: role effects use the higher skill, but shop hours add. The owner works §7's `ownerHours` (60 h/week by §1's default) in a field role, with fatigue and injury rolls but no wage, morale or quits. Owner presence on a claim sets §7's `ownerPresentSecurity`.

**Controller and bookkeeper** (P4).

```
alertBonusWeeks = controller ? round(2 + 2·s/100) : bookkeeper ? 1 : 0      // added by §11 to finance.distress.watchWeeks
                                                                              //   (stage 0 and §13 cash.projectedNegative); skill ≥ 75 → +4
leakage/week    = 0.015 × vendor-billed spend (fuel, parts, consumables, camp, contractors) + 0.005 × hourly gross
caught          = leakage × max(controller ? 0.50 + 0.004·s : 0, bookkeeper ? 0.40 + 0.002·s : 0)
unrecovered     = leakage − caught → billed as `vendor.other`, posted to exp.ga ("billing errors and shrink")
§11 effects     = finance.controllerAppetiteBonus × controllerQuality(s); finance.controllerSpreadDiscount × controllerQuality(s);
                  forbearance odds ×(1 + 0.2 × controllerQuality(s)) (§11's ×1.2 at skill 70);
                  BBC and reporting covenants auto-filed (bookkeeper: BBC and quarterly statements only); no outsourced-bookkeeping fee
vendor-billed spend = this week's §7 OpsCostLines (fuel, supplies, camp, trucking, transport) + §9 parts and contract repairs
```
The leakage line is deterministic and visible, with an explain tree showing the industry rate and what was caught. It is chronic shrink and billing errors, separate from §12's discrete theft events.

**Controller flags** (step 16; §13 alert kind `controller.flag`, severity warning, with `flag` naming the item):
1. `productionVariance`: two consecutive cleanups of the same plant line weighing more than 15% below the foreman's estimate (§7). This points to losses, theft or an optimistic estimate.
2. `covenantHeadroom`: projected covenant headroom below 10% within 13 weeks (§11 computes).

Two controller outputs are deliberately not `controller.flag` alerts (D-8.44). The early cash warning is §11's: `alertBonusWeeks` widens `finance.distress.watchWeeks`, so §13's `cash.projectedNegative` fires that many weeks sooner and its explain tree credits the controller. The weekly "recovered $X in billing errors" is the caught line of the leakage explain tree and the Staff screen's controller panel; a warning kind that fired every week would stop every run.

*Value check:* on the reference operation (~$650k vendor spend, $375k payroll), a skill-70 controller saves about $9k of leakage, $10.8k of outsourced bookkeeping and about $2.5k/yr of spread on $1M of debt, against a cost of about $127k. At a mature operation with $5M of spend and $5M of debt the savings approach $90k plus access to credit. That makes the controller a scale hire (D-8.24).

**Permitting & land specialist.** §6 owns quality (`permitApplicationQuality`), speed (`1.25 − 0.005·s`), 2 concurrent applications and auto-filing. §5 owns `landSkill = max(owner landman 80, best specialist true skill)`.

### 8.13 Firing, layoffs, recall and retention

**Firing** (`staff/fire { cause: 'none' | 'noShow' | 'safety' | 'theft' }`): final pay of everything earned, return travel, optional severance weeks, coworker morale shocks (8.7), and the bonus forfeited (cause) or pro-rated (no cause). The separation is logged. `cause: 'none'` is always allowed. A claimed cause must be documented, or the action fails with `CAUSE_NOT_DOCUMENTED`:
- `noShow`: ≥ 2 absence events in 8 weeks;
- `safety`: an injury or citation attributed to the employee;
- `theft`: high-grading discovered (§12).

A firing for cause triggers no UI charge and no coworker shock, except a `noShow` firing within 4 weeks of bonus vest (8.6). Three or more firings in one operating week cost reputation −2 (§1).

**UI charges** (P4, for §11's SUTA experience rating): each separation not for cause carries `uiCharge = min(staff.uiReplacementRate (0.5) × weeklyWage, staff.uiMaxWeeklyBenefitUsd ($370) × cpiIndex) × expectedWeeks`, with expectedWeeks 16 for a seasonal layoff and 10 for a firing (0 for quits, poaching, injury exits, fatalities and firings for cause). weeklyWage is the mean gross over last8. Almost every placer hand hits the benefit cap: a laid-off operator ($2,844/week) charges 370 × 16 = **$5,920**, and so does a laborer on a bare 40 h week (0.5 × $1,000 = $500 > $370).

**Layoffs** (`staff/layoff { employeeIds, recall, retainerWeeklyCents }`): status `laidOff`, off payroll except any retainer, return travel paid. The bonus vests if the layoff falls on or after `vestTurn`, otherwise it is pro-rated. At freeze-up §8 raises a non-blocking decision ("Lay off the seasonal crew?", alert `staff.layoffDecision`). The default lays off hourly field crew on the recall list and keeps salaried staff and anyone in `shop`. In P1–P3 (no recall hazard) each laid-off employee on the recall list rolls once, in week 1 of the next year, whether they will come back (`staff.p1RecallProb` 0.75, stream `staff-rehire`).

**Recall hazard.** Each off-season week, a laid-off employee on the recall list takes another job with probability (stream `rng(seed,'staff-rehire',turn,empId)`):

```
logit h = −4.0 + 0.5 × (50 − M_layoff)/10 + 0.3 × (truth.skill − 50)/25 + 1.0 × (CLD_d − 0.5)
          − 0.75 × (retainerWeekly / weeklyWage)/0.25 − 0.4 × [last bonus paid in full] − 0.2 × min(seasonsWithCompany, 3)
```
weeklyWage here is straight time (rate × 40 h, or salary/52). Over a 26-week winter: M 60, skill 55, bonus paid, one season gives **85%** back in spring. M 50 with no bonus gives 66%. Add a 25% retainer and it is 82%. Gone employees leave the roster (status `gone`; the `layoff` separation and its UI charge were logged at layoff). They may re-enter the pool later as former employees (8.4) or join a competitor's crew. `staff/recall` brings the rest back with lead time and travel. Morale on recall = 50 + 0.5 × (M_layoff − 50) + 3. A recalled employee expects max(old rate, current market × askMult); paying less shows up in the pay term.

**Year-round retention.** Keeping key people through winter costs their wages but removes recall risk and lands rebuild hours in the shop (§9). *Trade-off:* a mechanic kept on in winter ≈ $45 × 40 h × 26 wk ≈ $47k plus burden, against losing him with p ≈ 0.3 and rebuilding the fleet with a field service contractor.

| `staff/changeRole` | employeeId, newRole, pay | `ROLE_NOT_ELIGIBLE` | promotion; +5 morale | P3 |

Trade-offs, one line each: hire now vs later (pool depth vs back-outs and idle wages); references (cost and delay vs a bad hire); probation (cheap exit vs −3 morale); recruiter (certainty vs a 15% fee and lead time); raises (morale and retention vs cost); bonus or share (retention and cash timing vs cost when the ground is good); firing (a better crew vs shocks and UI charges); retainers (spring certainty vs winter cash). Poach responses go through §12 `event/respond`; owner assignment is §1 `owner/setAssignment`.

### 8.15 Weekly resolution

| Step | §8 work |
|---|---|
| 1 (week 1) | After §1 (a)–(f): experience-year increments (+1 for ≥ 12 weeks worked last year); P1–P3 recall rolls; `seasonsWithCompany` updates |
| 3 Markets | Position among §4, §5 and §9 per §2.6; §8 reads only step-2 values and last week's §12 `competitorLaborDemand`, so its place changes no result. Per district: rush window from the forecast breakup; `marketWage` and `marketWageBase` (ripple, season, scarcity from last week's `competitorLaborDemand`, reputation, difficulty, events); pool targets; churn exits and arrivals; referrals; former-employee re-entries; recruiter deliveries; references ready (recentre `shown`); P6 foreman replacement hires |
| 5 Competitors | §12 calls `removeCandidate`, `returnToPool`, `addCandidate`; poach attempts become `keyPoach` events |
| 7 Availability | After §1 applies the owner's `pendingAssignment`, resets desk days, pulls queued desk tasks and clears an expired owner injury (§2.6): (a) back-out rolls, then arrivals (travel bill, training plan, first-payroll signing bonus); (b) returns from injury or rotation; (c) **morale update** from last week's inputs (`unpaidWages`, hours, fatigue, camp, injuries, foreman); (d) **quit rolls**, recall-hazard rolls for laid-off staff; (e) absence draws; (f) training gating and this week's training hours; (g) unpaid-wage refusal and `staff.crewAvailableFrac`; (h) `availableFraction`, then supervision per claim and line: `foremanFor` for every active line, lead-hand counters (`StaffSlice.supervision`) and the small-crew test (8.12), coverage, cook and camp occupancy |
| 9 Operations | (read by §7/§4) |
| 10 Injuries | §2.6 order: §9 failure rolls → §7 re-resolve → §9 wear → §7 freeze damage → **§8** → §12 external shocks. §8, on the hours actually worked: gather hours (§7 `crewHours.byDay`, §4 `programCrewUse`, §9 `shopHours` incl. pool travel by claim, training, office, camp); injury rolls and severity (start-of-week F); §11 `handleLoss` (P4); §6 `openInvestigation`; §12 `noteExternalShock` for serious and fatal work injuries; morale shocks, injury memory and safety record; then fatigue update; skill growth; observation (P3); owner fatigue and injury; training completions create the next `trainingRefresher` obligation (§6) |
| 14 Finance | 14b: §11 calls `payrollForWeek` (wages, OT, salary, retainers, bonus accrual and vest payments, signing and one-off bonuses, gold share on this week's cleanups). 14c: staffing bills (travel, recruiting, references, training fees) to `exp.staffing`, recruiter deposits to `prepaid` (8.6); leakage bill (P4). 14e: after settlement §11 calls `recordPayrollOutcome` for each employee in ascending ID |
| 16 Wrap-up | After §1 16a–16d, before §13 collation (§2.6): safety-record drift, then `AlertSignal`s with §13's kinds: `employee.quit`, `employee.injury`, `crew.moraleLow` (avg < 40 or key < 30), `crew.noForeman` (warning; one per claim naming the lines stood down, shared with §7), `crew.leadHand` (info, with weeks of cover left, or "standing" for a line beyond the foremen's span), `staff.trainingDue` (warning: a field hire's training or a refresher due within `staff.trainingDueWarnWeeks` (2) with no session scheduled), `staff.bonusVestSoon` (info: a vest next week), `staff.recallDecision` (warning with a non-blocking decision, at forecast breakup − 6), `staff.layoffDecision` (warning with a non-blocking decision, at freeze-up), `controller.flag` (warning, 8.12) |

RNG streams (§2 registry; §8 owns each): `staff-cand`, `staff-market`, `staff-refs`, `staff-hire`, `staff-quit`, `staff-absence`, `staff-injury`, `staff-injury-sev`, `staff-rehire`, `staff-delegate` (P6). The one player-triggered draw (P5 sub-ask offers) is keyed by subject on `staff-hire` with `('offer', candId, offerIndex)`, never by `actionSeq` (§2 rule). ID prefixes (§2.4 registry): `emp`, `cand`, `inj` (injury records), `rcr` (recruiter orders); `emp_owner` is §2's reserved non-counter id for the owner pseudo-employee.

### 8.16 Interfaces

**Provides.**
- Types: `Role`, `OpClass`, `Employee`, `Candidate`, `CandidateSnapshot`, `PayStructure`, `Assignment`, `LaborMarketState`, `StaffSlice`, `UnpaidWages`, `SafetyRecord`, `InjuryRecord`, `Separation { empId, turn, role, districtId, kind: 'quit'|'poached'|'fired'|'firedCause'|'layoff'|'injuryExit'|'fatality', uiChargeCents }`.
- Skill curves (8.11): `skillProductivityMult`, `skillWearMult`, `skillRecoveryMult`, `inspectionAccuracy`, `repairQuality`, `repairHoursMult`, `reworkHazardMult`, `permitApplicationQuality`, `drillerNoiseMult`, `controllerQuality`, `foremanDecisionNoise`.
- People queries:
  - `operatorProfile(state, empId | 'owner', classId) → { effSkill, shownSkill: Range } | null` (§9 `classId` through the 8.2 class map; `null` for classes with no operator; §9 `machineEffectiveRate` and `wearPerHour` take this as `operator`);
  - `canFill(state, empId | 'owner', opsRole, machineClass?) → { ok, effSkill, reason? }` (§7 pairing);
  - `availableFraction(state, empId | 'owner', turn)` (8.5), `ownerSkill(state, role)`, `foremanFor(state, claimId, lineId = 'L1')` (8.12, effective qF; kinds incl. `'smallCrew'`; `lineIds` covered), `supervisionIncidentMult(state, claimId)` (1.15 for a small crew, else 1; §12 site incidents);
  - `shopCapacity(state, shop: { mode: 'site'; claimId } | { mode: 'pool'; districtId }) → { mechHours, weldHours, mechSkill, weldSkill }` (the mechanics and welders assigned in that mode; hours-weighted effective skill, incl. the owner-mechanic);
  - `minCrewReliability(state, claimId)` (lowest true reliability among employees with hours on the claim this week; 100 when only the owner or nobody works it, so an owner-only site never skims) and `crewGoldShareFrac(state, claimId)` (hours share of the claim's field crew on any gold share): the §8 inputs to §7 7.10's skim roll (pSkim × (1 − 0.5 × crewGoldShareFrac), P5);
  - `crewSafetyIndex(state, claimId)` ∈ [0, 1], `crewFatigue(state, claimId)` (mean F/100, §12's F̄), `newCrewShare(state, claimId)`, `safetyOfficerCoverage(state, claimId)`, `fieldCrewCount(state, claimId)` (8.12's definition; §6 M_size and the small-crew test), `personDays(state, claimId)` (§6 Yukon classes), `localHireShare(state, districtId)` (share of the district's field crew with origin `local`; §6 First Nation relation, P6);

- Payroll: `payrollForWeek(state): PayrollLine[]`, `recordPayrollOutcome(state, empId, paidCents, shortCents)` (8.1).
- Event one-shots (§12): `applyInjury(empId, tier, cause)`, `moraleShock(scope, points)`, `forceQuit(empId, reason)`, `setAbsent(empId, weeks, paid)`, `addCandidate(spec)`, `removeCandidate(candId, reason)`, `returnToPool(snapshots, reason)`.

### 8.17 Phase plan

- **P1 (core loop).**
  - *Roles:* foreman, operator, mechanic, plant operator, geologist, cook, laborer.
  - *Attributes:* visible exact attributes and class skills; asks = market × askMult; a static district pool with season factors (no ripple, competitors or scarcity); recruiter.
  - *Hiring and pay:* arrival lead times, travel and remote premium; hourly pay with weekly overtime and the 40 h guarantee; salary for exempt roles; minimum wage and the exempt floor keyed on §3's `District.jurisdictionId` (`akStyle` for the northern template, `nvStyle` for the arid one) and wages on `wageRegion`; staffing bills to `exp.staffing` and the recruiter deposit in `prepaid`.
  - *Morale and quits:* morale terms for pay, hours, fatigue, camp and cook, foreman, unpaid wages and season drag; quits (logistic with tenure and unpaid terms); fatigue with effSkill, including §1's temperature-graded heat load (shipped in P1 with §1's heat hours).
  - *Shared functions:* the owner pseudo-employee; the foreman rule with lead hand and the small-crew exception (F 0.92 in §7; its ×1.15 injury multiplier waits for P2's injuries); site-mode shop assignments; the 8.11 curves for §7/§9 (wear multiplier on flat maintenance); `payrollForWeek` with §11's flat 1.22× burden; `availableFraction`.
  - *Firing and layoffs:* firing with final pay and shocks (cause `none` only); layoff and recall at a fixed `staff.p1RecallProb` 0.75, with the `staff.layoffDecision` and `staff.recallDecision` alerts.
  - *Not in P1:* injuries, training, résumés, bonuses (except one-off `giveBonus`), gold share, retainers, controller, competitors, the safety record (its morale term is 0).
  - *Stubs:* scarcity 1.0, CLD 0.5 in the quit and recall logits, `meanTrueHealth` 1, training always current.
- **P2 (licensing).** MSHA training scheduling and gating (MSHA card on résumés); injuries (all tiers) with §6 investigations and §11's flat WC stub, including the small crew's `M_sup`; `crewSafetyIndex`, safety record and its morale term (8.7), safety officer and permitting specialist roles; `safety.lateNotification`; heat injury multiplier; alerts `staff.trainingDue` and `employee.injury` (§13's Safety tab ships with them).
- **P3 (equipment depth).** Hidden attributes, résumés, references, probation, observation, promotions; welder and driller; mechanic curves live in §9 inspections and repairs; pool-mode shop assignments with pool cost centers (8.5, 8.6; §9 9.8.6); per-line supervision and the foreman span with §7's plant lines (8.12); `skillWearMult` drives component wear; `M_equip` in injuries; documented firing causes.
- **P4 (finance depth).** Full payroll taxes and `akStyle` daily overtime and flex plan (with §11); WC claims through `handleLoss` and EMR; UI charges; season bonus and gold share with accruals; retainers and the recall hazard; bookkeeper and controller (leakage, the alert bonus on `finance.distress.watchWeeks`, §11 effects, `controller.flag`); `staff.bonusVestSoon`; owner medical costs from personal cash; `noteExternalShock` reports to §12's director (§12 P4).
- **P5 (living market).** Wage and pool ripples by role; seasonal rush wages (forecast-keyed window); scarcity from competitors; competitor hiring and poaching (`poachAcceptProb`); event hooks; offers below ask (subject-keyed draw, 8.5); signing bonuses; rotations; the serious/fatal share ×0.75.
- **P6 (expansion).** Delegation depth (foreman authority, discretion, decision noise); `alaskaState` and `yukon` wage regions; `temperateStyle` and `yukon` payroll jurisdictions (minimum wage, exempt floor, Yukon daily overtime after 8 h; §11 owns their payroll taxes, Yukon in C$); `localHireShare` for §6 First Nation scoring; controller multi-claim reporting. Hard-rock roles, wages and Part 48 Subpart A training for the optional track are specified in §14 14.10–14.11 on §8's machinery; see §14.
- **Phase exit (§1 1.19).** Each phase closes with the 8.20 tests for what it ships, inside §1's simulator gates:
  - P1: curves, P1 payroll (weekly OT, guarantee, salary, `akStyle`/`nvStyle` minimum wage, `recordPayrollOutcome`, cost centers, staffing bills and the deposit), market and pool examples, no look-ahead, morale and quit examples, fatigue, foreman and small crew, class map, properties; the owner pseudo-employee feeds §1's O-07 background parity (±7 pp interim).
  - P2: injury calibration, safety record and its morale term, training gating.
  - P3: résumé, references and observation; driller and welder; `M_equip`; foreman span and pool-mechanic payroll; O-07 background parity at ±5 pp.
  - P4: daily OT and flex plan, bonus and gold-share accruals, UI charges, recall hazard, controller and leakage, the season scenario.
  - P5: ripples, back-outs, poaching, subject-keyed offers, the ×0.75 serious share.
  - P6: `temperateStyle` and `yukon` jurisdiction fixtures, delegation.

### 8.19 Balance levers and risks

**Biggest levers.** These move survival the most:
- `roleBase` × `ripple.wageAsk`: labor is 35–45% of operating cost (R4);
- `quit.q0` and the unpaid terms: the speed of a payroll-miss death spiral;
- `seasonPool` operating 0.45: how bad a mid-season quit is;
- `fatigue.*` and `injury.basePerHour`: whether long weeks pay;
- `skillWearMult` below 50: the cost of cheap operators;
- `goldShareMaxTotal`.

**Dominant-strategy risks and counters.**

| Risk | Counter |
|---|---|
| 12 × 7 all season | Fatigue reaches ~90 by week 8: −10% output per hour, +23% wear, ×4 injuries, morale −20 or worse; `akStyle` daily OT. Sim target: 6 × 11 beats 7 × 11 over a full season for the median crew. |
| Cheapest crew | Productivity 0.83 and wear 1.8× at skill 20; absence and high-grading track reliability. The wage spread is only ±25%, so skill is cheap per point, but scarce (5% above 80) and contested by competitors. |
| Everyone on gold share | Caps (5% individual, 15% claim); minimum-wage base; on poor ground the trailing pay term drags morale once real cleanups replace the projection; on rich ground it is the most expensive structure. |
| Hire-and-fire screening | Each bad hire costs travel (fly-in $2.4k round trip), $450 training, 1–3 weeks of lead time, a $5,920 UI charge after probation and coworker shocks. Probation is the intended, priced version. |
| Lay off everyone, no retainers | ~66% return, so a third of the crew is rehired from a thinner, pricier spring pool, with refresher hours and new-hire injury and quit premiums. |
| Owner-operator plus skeleton crew | §1's background-parity gate. The owner covers only one claim and fatigues like anyone. |
| Owner shuttles between two claims, a lead hand covering the other | Reassignment is not an absence: the claim left behind stands down the next week, and the lead-hand counter only resets after 4 weeks of presence (8.12). |
| Many three-hand claims with no foremen (D-8.48) | Each runs at 0.92 efficiency, one line and one shift, with injuries ×1.15 and late incident notification; each needs its own camp, site costs and mobilization; a fourth hand or a second shift ends the exception. On three hands a foreman does not pay (8.12 example), which is intended; the sim reports claims per foreman by strategy and checks that a company of small foreman-less claims does not beat fewer, larger operations at equal capital. |
| A third plant line under a lead hand instead of a second foreman (D-8.49) | The line runs at 0.6 × its best hand's skill (F ≈ 0.90 against 0.94 with a skill-60 foreman), with the lead hand's safety in `crewSafetyIndex` and a higher `incidentMult`. A second foreman costs about $2.9k a week; on a line washing $50k+ of gold a week he pays. |
| One pool mechanic for a whole district | Travel overhead per job (1.5 / 3 / 6 h by access) eats capacity, every blocking repair waits `fleet.poolResponseDelayHours` (8 h) more, and fly-in claims are out of reach (§9 9.8.6). |
| Firing for cause just before vest to keep the bonus | A `noShow` firing within 4 weeks of vest counts as without cause for shocks and the reputation counter (8.6); forfeits still save the accrual, which is realistic and costly in crew goodwill. |
| Hiring only MSHA-card holders | Card holders are the experienced hands, who ask more and are scarcer; a green hire costs $450 and 24 paid hours instead. A visible, priced choice, not a dominant one. |
| Safety spending "never pays" | Intended for small crews (D-8.17). It pays at scale through EMR (§11), citations (§6) and tail events. The sim reports injury cost by strategy. |

### 8.20 Tests

- **Curves:**
  - `skillProductivityMult` 0 → 0.700, 50 → 1.000, 100 → 1.250; strictly increasing on [0, 100].
  - `skillWearMult` 20 → 1.800, 50 → 1.000, 100 → 0.850; continuous at 50; strictly decreasing.
  - `skillRecoveryMult` 0 → 1.5, 55 → 1.0, 100 → 0.75; monotone.
  - `inspectionAccuracy(50)` = {0.125, 0.625, 0.03}.
  - `controllerAlertBonusWeeks` at s 24/25/75 → 2/3/4.
- **Payroll:**
  - `akStyle` 6 × 11 at $36 → $2,844.00; 4 × 10 (P4) → $1,584.00 without a flex plan, $1,440.00 with one, and $1,440.00 for a company with 3 employees; `nvStyle` 4 × 10 → $1,440.00; `yukon` 4 × 10 → OT_day 8 with no employee minimum.
  - Jurisdiction keys: every §3 `JurisdictionId` has `minWage`, `exemptMinWeekly` and `dailyOtAfter` rows and every `WageRegion` a `regionWageMult` (schema test); each `PayrollLine.jurisdictionId` equals the work district's `District.jurisdictionId` (office staff: the home district's); an `nvStyle` rate of $11.99 → `BELOW_MIN_WAGE`.
  - Salary $125k → $2,403.85/week. Guarantee: 30 scheduled hours on site → 40 paid; with 1 of 6 days absent → 33.33 h.
  - Bookkeeper at $26.44 on 40 office hours → $1,057.60, no overtime.
  - `akStyle` minimum wage in a year with cpiIndex 1.03 → $15.45; a $15.00 rate is raised automatically at the next payroll.
  - `recordPayrollOutcome`: short, short, paid in full → `weeks` 1, 2, 0 and `misses` 1, 2, 2; the −15 shock fires once.
  - Cost centers: 50 h on the claim of which 6 h in role `reclaim` → two lines (`site` 44 h, `reclaim` 6 h) with overtime premium pro rata.
  - 8% bonus on $2,844 → $227.52 accrual. Forfeit on quit reverses the accrual exactly.
  - Gold share 6% on a 33.998 raw oz lot at 0.83 estimated fineness and $4,200 → $7,111.02; a pool split by straight-time-equivalent hours sums to the total to the cent (largest remainder).
  - UI charge: laid-off operator ($2,844/week) → $5,920; laborer on 40 h → $5,920; a 20 h/week hand at $25 → $4,000; quit → $0.
  - Recruiter fee for a $38/hr operator → $5,700 less the $1,000 deposit credit.
  - Staffing bills: the $1,000 deposit posts to `prepaid`, not to expense; the first hire posts $5,700 to `exp.staffing` ($1,000 from `prepaid`, a $4,700 bill); with no hire 4 weeks after delivery the $1,000 moves to `exp.staffing` with memo "forfeited"; travel for a field hire posts with cost center `site` and the assignment's claim, for a bookkeeper with `ga`.
- **Market:**
  - Candidate example (8.4) reproduces ask $38.33 and $40.25 with the stated draws.
  - P1 market wage equals base (index 1, cpi 1).
  - Ripple at idx 1.30 and cpi 1.06 gives operator $41.28 and mechanic $53.68.
  - Pool example (8.4): outpost operator targets 3.0 / 2.25 / 1.35 / 3.9 for winter / rush / operating / post-freeze.
  - Back-outs over 18 weeks: 10.3% / 15.9% / 19.5% at CLD 0 / 0.3 / 0.5.
  - No look-ahead: scrambling the hidden true breakup week leaves every `marketWage`, pool target and arrival unchanged until breakup is revealed (§1 1.22 property).
- **Morale and quits:**
  - 8.7 example: target 45.7, then 50.4; missed pay → 31.2, then 21.5.
  - Quit probability at M 50 (other terms 0) → 0.30%; M 31.2 with one unpaid week, skill 62, one season → 7.8%.
  - Poach: M 60 at 1.2× → 0.32.
  - Rehire over 26 weeks → 85% / 66% / 82% for the three 8.13 cases.
  - Season start: an employee's morale target is identical in the last rush week and the first operating week when nothing else changes (marketRef ignores `seasonWage`).
  - Camp terms: basic / standard / good / premium → −5 / 0 / +3 / +5; one cook for 18 on site (cookShort 0.5) → −3 morale and availability ×0.98.
  - Gold-share morale before the second cleanup uses 0.5 × the projected share; after it, the trailing share.
  - Safety-record term: record 10 → −2.4, 50 → 0, 100 → +3.0; P1 (no record) → 0; after a fatality takes the record from 60 to 20, an employee on a claim opened the next week gets −1.8 with no `injuryMemory` there.
  - Program crew: qF from a consultant engagement of tier skill 70 → leadership +2.4; no supervising geologist → 0.
- **Fatigue:** 66 h, 6 days → steady 36.5; the 7-day trajectory matches 8.9 to ±0.5; an 88 °F day-shift week adds 3.2 load; a 5 × 8 office week recovers at 0.40.
- **Foreman:**
  - Foreman injured for 4 weeks on a claim with six employees → lead hand weeks 1–3, `none` in week 4, plan stands down; `leadHandWeeks` resets only after 4 weeks of presence. The same on a three-employee, one-line, one-shift claim → week 4 is `smallCrew`, not `none`.
  - Owner reassigned from claim A to claim B → A has no foreman from the next step 7; alternating weekly never keeps both running.
  - qF with the foreman available 0.5 (skill 70) and best operator 60 → 0.5 × 70 + 0.5 × 36 = 53.
  - Activating a plan with the owner in `office`, no hired foreman and four employees on the claim → `FOREMAN_REQUIRED`, on the first claim as on any other; with a hired foreman assigned this week (effective next step 7) → allowed.
  - Small crew (D-8.48): three employees on the claim (an operator, a plant operator and a laborer), one line, one shift, no foreman or owner → `kind: 'smallCrew'`, `empId` the best of the operator and plant operator, skill 0.6 × that effective skill (60 → 36); with a cook added (four on the claim), or `shiftsPerDay` 2, or a second active line → `FOREMAN_REQUIRED` at activation and `none` (stand-down) at the next step 7 for a running plan; the owner counted out (owner as operator plus three hands → `owner`, not `smallCrew`).
  - `fieldCrewCount`: claim crew 2 + camp cook 1 + a site-mode mechanic at the claim 1 = 4; a pool mechanic who worked there that week is not counted.
  - `M_sup`: a small-crew operator at reference conditions → λ = 0.00173 × 1.15 = 0.00199/week; `supervisionIncidentMult` → 1.15, and 1 under any supervisor.
  - Foreman span (D-8.49): owner foreman plus hired foremen emp_000012 and emp_000007 on a three-line claim → the owner covers L1 and L2, emp_000007 covers L3, emp_000012 covers none; one hired foreman and three lines → L3 `leadHand` at 0.6 × its best hand's effective skill with no week limit, `crew.leadHand` "standing"; that foreman injured → L1 and L2 under the claim lead hand with the 3-week counter and L3 follows L1; assigning a third foreman to a three-line claim with two → `FOREMAN_SLOT_TAKEN`.
  - Morale qF per line: an operator who ran an L3 machine most of the week takes L3's supervisor qF; a strip-dozer operator takes L1's.
  - Owner foreman (skill 85, fresh) with 2 desk days forced by `ownerTime: 'now'` and a best operator at 60 → `availableFraction` 0.667 and qF = 0.667 × 85 + 0.333 × 36 = 68.7; the same days queued → 1.0 and 85.
- **Shop modes and payroll:** a pool mechanic with 60 paid hours of which 18 on claim A's jobs (4.5 of them travel), 24 on claim B's and 18 at the yard → three payroll lines: `site` A 18 h, `site` B 24 h, `ga` 18 h, overtime premium pro rata; his jurisdiction is the pool's district; his camp term is commuting (−2) and fatigue load +2; a site-mode mechanic's 60 h → one `site` line on his claim. `staff/assign` with `mode: 'pool'` under P1–P2 rules → `ASSIGNMENT_INVALID`.
- **Class map and skim inputs:** `operatorProfile` for `artTruck` and `roadTruck` uses `classSkill['truck']`; for `drill`, the driller's role skill; for `washPlant`, `pump` and `site`, `null`. `minCrewReliability` with only the owner on the claim → 100; with crew reliabilities 30 and 70 → 30.
- **Offers (P5):** an offer at 0.95 × ask draws on `('offer', candId, offerIndex)`; reloading the save and dispatching a dummy action before the same offer gives the same outcome; a second offer to the same candidate uses `offerIndex` 1.
- **Injury:**
  - Reference λ = 0.00173 ± 1e-5/week; reckless ratio 7.3 ± 0.1.
  - Tier shares sum to 1; from P5, serious and fatal ×0.75 with the remainder in lostTime.
  - Neutral-multiplier rates: lost-time-or-worse 0.94 per 200k h, recordables 1.73, fatalities 9.6 per 100k FTE (±1% over 10^6 simulated hours).
  - `M_heat` at 92 °F day shift → 1.24; night shift → 1.
  - `noteExternalShock` is called exactly once per serious or fatal injury with cause `'work'` and never for a §12-caused injury.
  - `returnTurn = turn + ceil(lostDays/7)`; a never-returns serious injury writes an `injuryExit` separation at `returnTurn`.
- **Properties (fast-check):**
  - Determinism under replay.
  - Stream isolation: adding a candidate changes no injury or quit draw of existing employees.
  - Every person is in exactly one of pool, player and competitor crews.
  - No employee holds two assignments.
  - `availableFraction` ∈ [0, 1].
  - Morale and fatigue stay in [0, 100].
  - Accrued bonus = paid + forfeited + outstanding.
  - Résumé ranges never widen with observation.
  - Higher true skill never lowers productivity or raises wear.
  - Derived class skill never exceeds skill and moves one-for-one with skill growth.
  - Every departure from the roster writes exactly one `Separation`.
  - `unpaidWages` changes only inside `recordPayrollOutcome`.
  - State is identical with explanations on and off (calc trees live in the `WeekReport`).
  - Bots see only `shown` (hidden-field scrambling test, §2.12).
  - Every alert kind §8 emits has a row in §13's taxonomy (§13 T21); the leakage "recovered" line raises no alert.
- **Scenario:** one season of the reference operation on 6 × 11 with an 8% bonus → quits ≤ 1 in 80% of seeds. The same crew with one missed payroll in week 26 → median ≥ 2 quits.

### 8.21 Decisions

- **D-8.1** — Thirteen roles; bookkeeper and controller are separate roles. — §11 already distinguishes them (BBC vs lender effects), and the price gap ($55k vs $110k) is a real choice.
- **D-8.2** — Operator skill is per machine class (dozer, excavator, loader, truck), with off-class penalties. — "A good dozer hand" is the scarce thing in placer. The penalties make crew assignment a decision.
- **D-8.3** — Morale and fatigue are visible exactly; skill, reliability and safety are hidden. — The crew tells you how they feel. Hiding ability is where the uncertainty belongs.
- **D-8.4** — Fatigue reaches productivity and wear only through effective skill (−0.35 per point above 30). — One channel, consistent with §9's operator input, with no new hooks.
- **D-8.5** — Résumés inflate (+6/+10/+6), and narrow deterministically with observation. — Real oversell. Deterministic narrowing keeps explain trees honest and replay simple.
- **D-8.6** — Asks partly reveal true skill (60% true skill, 40% experience proxy, ±6% noise). — People know their worth; an attentive player gets a fuzzy, legitimate signal.
- **D-8.7** — Wage elasticity to gold is 0.3 by default, ×1.5 for mechanics; the pool shrinks with gold (−0.5). — §10's table plus R4's "mechanics run hottest". The operator multiplier stays 1.0 so §10's worked example holds.
- **D-8.8** — Remote premium is per assigned claim's access (5/10/15%), not per candidate. — The job, not the person, is remote (R4 +5–15%).
- **D-8.9** — The owner gets no separate leadership bonus; the operator-background edge flows through the foreman skill (85). — Keeps §1's "exactly one edge" rule.
- **D-8.10** — Hourly staff on site get a 40 h weekly guarantee. — Camp crews are paid when they sit, so idling a staffed claim has a real cost.
- **D-8.11** — Overtime = max(weekly, daily) with Alaska-style daily OT after 8 h (10 h with a flex plan). — Correct law (R4 §13); it matters only for short-week, long-day schedules.
- **D-8.12** — The season bonus vests at the site's operating end (arid: week 17, the end of the prime season), is pro-rated on a layoff by default, and is forfeited on a quit or a firing for cause. — Standard practice (R4). Pro-rating protects reputation when the player ends the season early.
- **D-8.13** — Gold share is paid at each cleanup on net-of-royalty raw oz × estimated fineness × spot; neither it nor the season bonus is added to the overtime regular rate. — Cash-flow-true and simple. The FLSA regular-rate rule for non-discretionary pay is deliberately omitted.
- **D-8.14** — Gold share is capped at 5% per person and 15% per claim. — R4's ranges. Without caps it becomes a free loyalty machine.
- **D-8.15** — Morale updates in step 7 from last week's outcomes. — Payday lag is natural, and it lets §11's step-14 payment results drive next week's quits without reordering the pipeline.
- **D-8.16** — Quit hazard is logistic in morale (0.30%/week at 50, 9% at 15), with unpaid weeks at +1.5 logit each. — "Missed payroll is catastrophic": one miss takes a 6-person crew to a ~39% chance of a quit that week, before §12's walkout.
- **D-8.17** — The injury base is calibrated to research rates (lost-time ≈ 1.5 per 200k h at reference), not inflated for drama. — Behavior multipliers (×7 when reckless) make injuries a consequence of choices; §12 adds site incidents.
- **D-8.18** — Every active claim needs a foreman, and activation requires a hired foreman or the owner on that claim. A lead hand covers up to 3 weeks of an assigned foreman's *absence* at 0.6 × operator skill (reset after 4 weeks of presence); reassignment is not an absence, so the claim stands down at once. *Amended by owner ruling 2026-10-05:* the rule no longer applies to a small crew (≤ `staff.smallCrewMaxNoForeman` (3) employees on the claim, one plant line, one shift), which may run with no foreman (D-8.48); above that threshold it stands unchanged. — It implements "each additional claim requires a hired foreman" for any claim beyond a three-hand operation, and stops the owner shuttling between two claims under lead-hand cover; the owner chose to let tiny crews run unsupervised at a price.
- **D-8.19** — Safety-officer coverage is fractional (district cover = 25 / field crew). — Lets one officer serve a district honestly. §6's multiplier becomes 1 − 0.45 × coverage.
- **D-8.20** — Office roles carry a 0.05 injury multiplier and `wcClass 'clerical'`. — Keeps WC premiums realistic per R5 (clerical $0.10–0.40 per $100).
- **D-8.21** — The owner cannot die; a fatal roll on the owner becomes serious. — The run continuing is the point; fatalities stay for employees, with full consequences.
- **D-8.22** — Leakage (1.5% of vendor spend + 0.5% of hourly payroll) is a deterministic visible line that office staff partly catch. — It gives the controller and bookkeeper a measurable job without random fraud events (§12 owns discrete theft).
- **D-8.23** — `controllerQuality = s/70` (clamped 0.5–1.3) scales §11's flat controller constants. — §11's constants stand for a typical (skill-70) controller; skill still matters.
- **D-8.24** — The controller is a scale hire: it does not pay on the reference small operation. — Matches small-placer practice (outsourced books). It keeps "hire every manager" from dominating.
- **D-8.25** — The recall hazard is a weekly logistic over the off-season, cut by retainers, a paid bonus and tenure. — It makes winter retention a priced choice (66% → 82% with a 25% retainer).
- **D-8.26** — Recruiters exist from P1. — Outpost pools can be empty (0.3 × base); the player must never be hard-blocked from staffing.
- **D-8.27** — UI charges are computed here and priced by §11's SUTA rating. — Firing and layoff costs are real, without §8 owning tax rates.
- **D-8.28** — Labor wage anchors are kept as given, with refinements: AK ×1.12, Yukon ×0.80, temperate ×0.95, Alaska-style minimum wage $15.00 (2027, then CPI-indexed). — R4 §12/§17: the anchors suit an AK/YT blend. The minimum-wage schedule is from R4 (Ballot Measure 1, 2024: $15 from July 2027, indexed after; the game applies $15 from January 2027 for simplicity).
- **D-8.29** — The spring-rush window is keyed to §1's forecast breakup, not the true date. — The true date is hidden until revealed; wages and pools moving 8 weeks ahead of it would leak it, which §1 forbids (1.4.5).
- **D-8.30** — Morale's pay reference (`marketWageBase`) excludes the seasonal wage factor; only asks carry it. — Otherwise every crew's morale target would drop about 7.6 points the week the operating season begins, a mid-season quit spike nobody chose. The 8.7 worked example uses this reference.
- **D-8.31** — UI charges are `min(0.5 × weekly wage, $370) × expected weeks`. — The weekly benefit is half the wage up to the state cap; placer wages put nearly every hand at the cap, so a seasonal layoff charges about $5.9k.
- **D-8.32** — Before an employee has shared in two cleanups, the gold-share pay term uses half the projected share from §7's visible projection. — A lower base with a promised share would otherwise read as a 20% pay cut every spring and make the cash-friendly structure self-defeating.
- **D-8.33** — One foreman covers both shifts of a claim (and, since the owner ruling of 2026-10-05, up to `staff.foremanMaxLines` plant lines, D-8.49). — §7 has one F per line; night-shift supervision losses are already in the night fatigue (+3), injury (×1.15) and §7 lighting terms. A per-shift foreman would double the hire for little extra decision.
- **D-8.34** — MSHA training status is drawn at candidate generation and shown on the résumé. — It is a certificate the hire carries; showing it makes "pay more for a trained hand" a priced choice instead of an arrival-day surprise.
- **D-8.35** — Camp morale uses §9's tiers (basic −5, standard 0, good +3, premium +5); no camp means commuting on highway claims near town, otherwise everyone is over capacity. — One tier vocabulary across §7, §8 and §9, and a claim without camp units still needs a rule.
- **D-8.36** — Fly-in travel is $1,200 one way per person (winter trail $700). — R4 prices charters at $1,500–5,000 per load; a seat share on a crew or supply flight, not a private charter, is the normal way a hand reaches camp.
- **D-8.37** — Fatigue recovery scales with days off (0.25 at none to 0.70 for a week off), heat adds 0.4 load and 2% injury hazard per °F above 80 on day shift. — Every schedule (5-day office weeks, partial weeks) needs a recovery rate, and §1 asks for temperature-graded heat effects rather than a flat hot-week bump.
- **D-8.38** — Injury rolls use start-of-week fatigue, after §9's failures and §7's re-resolve in step 10. — One fatigue value per week for skill and hazard; hours are the hours actually worked.
- **D-8.39** — An injury hits its own claim with a shock of half its claim value plus injury memory, and the rest of the company with the company value. — One rule: the severity table's two morale columns, applied where the injury happened and everywhere else.
- **D-8.40** — The company `safetyRecord` enters the morale target as `0.06 × (record − 50)` (±3), beside the per-claim `injuryMemory`. — The brief names the safety record as a morale driver; injury memory alone forgot a bad record on any newly opened claim. Centred on the starting value so P1 (no record) and a new company read 0, and a clean record earns a little (+1.5 at 75), which gives safety spending a small morale return.
- **D-8.41** — Payroll law (minimum wage, exempt floor, daily overtime) is keyed on §3's `District.jurisdictionId` (`akStyle`, `nvStyle`, `temperateStyle`, `yukon`), wages on `District.wageRegion`; the hours' work district decides, office staff use their home district. `temperateStyle` (min $11.00 indexed, no daily OT) and `yukon` (C$17.94 indexed, daily OT after 8 h for all employers) are model-knowledge values for P6. — One field serves §8, §9 and §11, so a district can never pay wages under one law and taxes under another; every jurisdiction needs a value before its template ships.
- **D-8.42** — The P5 sub-ask acceptance draw is keyed by subject, `rng(seed,'staff-hire','offer',candId,offerIndex)`, with `offerIndex` stored on the candidate. — Keyed by `actionSeq`, a reload plus a dummy action re-rolled it (§2 rule, §13 13.26); keyed by subject, only a better offer changes the answer.
- **D-8.43** — §9's `artTruck` and `roadTruck` map to the `truck` class, `drill` to the driller role, and plant, pump, generator, conveyor and site items take no operator. — §9 has more classes than §8 has crafts; driving any truck is one skill, drilling is its own role, and plant skill already acts on recovery in §7.
- **D-8.44** — `controller.flag` covers production variance and covenant headroom only. The controller's early cash warning is §11's widened watch window (`cash.projectedNegative`), and the weekly "recovered in billing errors" note is a line in the leakage explain tree, not an alert. — Two alerts for one cash projection would double-count, and a warning kind that fires every week would stop every run.
- **D-8.45** — Staffing costs (travel, recruiter fees, references, training fees) post to §11's `exp.staffing` with cost center `site` for field roles and `ga` for office roles; the recruiter deposit sits in `prepaid` until credited or forfeited. — Hiring cost shows beside wages in site labor, and a refundable deposit is not an expense until it is used or lost.
- **D-8.46** — Program crews take leadership from §4's supervising geologist: an employee's effective skill, the owner's 75, a consultant's tier skill (50/70/85), or a neutral 50 with none. — §4 allows consultants and unsupervised programs, and each needs a defined value.
- **D-8.47** — The owner has no absence state in §8. Desk tasks (site visits, pan surveys, records reviews, applications, closings) are §1 desk days; only days forced with `ownerTime: 'now'` cut the owner's `availableFraction` (1/6 each), and §8 has no `OWNER_UNAVAILABLE` code. — One owner-time model (§1 1.9) instead of two that could disagree.
- **D-8.48** — Small crews may skip the foreman (owner ruling 2026-10-05). A claim with no foreman or owner assigned, at most `staff.smallCrewMaxNoForeman` (3) employees on it (`fieldCrewCount`, owner excluded), one active plant line and one shift runs as `kind: 'smallCrew'`: §7 efficiency `ops.noForemanEfficiency` 0.92, qF for redeploy, pay contact, morale and lost days = 0.6 × the best operator's or plant operator's effective skill, injury hazard and §12 site incidents × `staff.noForemanIncidentMult` 1.15, and lead-hand late notification. `smallCrew` replaces `none` only, so an assigned foreman's absence still runs under a lead hand first. — It saves a foreman's wage on tiny operations and costs efficiency, safety and growth, as the ruling sets out; reusing the lead-hand fraction for the informal leader keeps one rule for unsupervised hands, and testing every step 7 makes the fourth hire, a second shift or a second line the visible point where a foreman becomes mandatory.
- **D-8.49** — One foreman covers up to `staff.foremanMaxLines` (2) plant lines (owner ruling 2026-10-05). A claim's supervisors (the owner first, then hired foremen in ascending employee ID) each cover the next two active lines in lineId order; a line beyond their span runs under a standing line lead hand (0.6 × the line's best hand) while L1 has a foreman or the owner. `foremanFor(state, claimId, lineId = 'L1')` returns the line's supervisor; without a line it is L1's, so every claim-level reader keeps one answer. — A third line needs a second foreman or a lead hand, as ruled; automatic, visible ordering avoids a new assignment field, and the lead hand prices the shortcut (F ≈ 0.90 against 0.94).
- **D-8.50** — A mechanic's or welder's shop assignment is `{ kind: 'shop', mode: 'site', claimId }` or `{ kind: 'shop', mode: 'pool', districtId }` (owner ruling 2026-10-05; pool from P3). A pool mechanic is based at the district yard, which replaces the yard shop location; he commutes from town (camp term −2, fatigue +2, remote premium 1.00), works under the pool district's payroll law, books his claim-job hours (travel included) to each claim's `site` cost center and the rest to `ga`, and takes injury `M_culture` and `M_equip` from the claim where he worked most. — The ruling's shape, flattened into §8's `Assignment` union so the `kind` discriminant still works; per-claim cost centers keep per-claim P&L honest when one mechanic serves several claims.
- **D-8.51** — `fieldCrewCount(state, claimId)` counts the employees whose assignment puts them on the claim (claim, camp, security, caretaker, a site-mode shop there, and program crew on the claim's programs), the owner excluded; §6's inspection `M_size` and the small-crew test read the same number. — One head count for "people on this site", so a cook or a site mechanic cannot be left out to stay under the small-crew limit.
- **D-8.52** — §8 names the real U.S. mine safety agency, MSHA, wherever it cites §6's safety citations, investigations and late-notification violation (owner ruling 2026-10-05 on real agency names; §6 owns the agency table and the violation keys). — §8 already used MSHA for training cards and Part 48; one real name throughout.

### 8.22 Open questions

- **OQ-8.1 — Injury frequency.** *Resolved — owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (§0).* Research rates stay (D-8.17). Injury rates at research magnitudes make injuries rare for careful small crews (≈ 0.06 lost-time per season). If playtests want injuries as a regular stressor, the change is `injury.basePerHour` ×2–3 and a re-tune of §11 WC and §12 incidents together. That is cheap in code but would move the BALANCE targets for survival and cost per ounce. **Default until answered:** research magnitudes, `staff.injury.basePerHour` = 1.6e-5 per hour (D-8.17). Decision needed before P2 balancing.
- **OQ-8.2 — answered (owner ruling 2026-10-05).** Small crews may run without a foreman: a claim with at most 3 employees, one plant line and one shift runs at a flat 0.92 efficiency with injuries ×1.15 (D-8.48); above that the foreman rule stands (D-8.18), and one foreman covers up to two plant lines (D-8.49).

Nevada 15–25% below Alaska, Yukon in USD ×0.75–0.85. Camps pay +5–15%. Minimum wages AK $14.00 (2026-07-01), $15 (2027); NV $12.00. HD technicians are the scarcest hire. Crews of 2–6 / 8–15 / 20–40.
