## 9. Equipment

> **At a glance.** Iron is the company's biggest capital bet after ground, and the place where cash and output leak away quietly. This section owns the **catalog** (classes, sizes, models, fictional brands with distinct reliability, parts cost, parts lead time, resale and fuel profiles), the **markets** (factory-new with warranty, dealer-certified used, private used, timed as-is auctions; procedural listings whose prices ripple with gold and crash when busts flood the auctions), **acquisition** (cash, loans and captive promos via §11, operating and finance leases, short-term rental, rent-to-own), **transport and mobilization** to remote claims, **hidden condition** and inspections, the per-machine **productivity, fuel, wear and failure** functions that §7 consumes, the **shop** (mechanics and welders at a claim's site or in a district pool, PM schedules, repairs, rebuilds, backlog, field service), **parts**, and **ownership economics** (book depreciation, resale, insurance hook, cost per hour, selling).
> The player sees hours, age, a seller's description and, if they pay for one, an inspection report with ranges. The engine knows each component's true health. Core trade-offs: new (cash, reliability, warranty) vs used (cheap, hidden condition) vs rent (no capital, ~1.8× ownership cost at placer hours); inspect (money, a week) vs gamble; PM and a staffed shop (wages now) vs wear and mid-season breakdowns; a mechanic at every site vs a shared district pool (fewer wages, travel and slower response); parts on the shelf (cash tied up) vs downtime; rebuild in winter (cash and shop time) vs run to failure in July; premium brand (price, parts cost) vs value brand (hazard, lead time, resale).

### 9.1 Scope, state and data model

§9 owns every machine the company owns, finances, leases or rents, every equipment listing, and the shop. It does not own ground or task productivity multipliers (§7, D-7.2), people and their skill curves (§8), loan and lease pricing and accounting (§11), or price indices (§10).

```ts
interface FleetSlice {
  machines: Record<MachineId, Machine>; machineIds: MachineId[];            // sorted iteration order (§2.3)
  listings: Record<EquipListingId, EquipmentListing>; listingIds: EquipListingId[];
  auctions: Record<AuctionId, AuctionEvent>; auctionBanUntilTurn: number;   // 0 = not banned (9.3.4)
  orders: Record<OrderId, FactoryOrder>;                                    // new units on order (9.4)
  workOrders: Record<WorkOrderId, WorkOrder>; workOrderIds: WorkOrderId[];
  parts: Record<PartsSku, PartsStock>; partsOrders: Record<PartsOrderId, PartsOrder>;
  contracts: Record<ContractId, RentalContract | LeaseTerms | RentToOwnContract>;  // physical terms; §11 holds the money side
  transports: Record<TransportId, TransportJob>; inspections: Record<InspectionId, InspectionJob>;
  callouts: Record<CalloutId, FieldCallout>; sales: Record<SaleId, PrivateSale>;    // player's private sale listings (9.10)
  shopPolicy: ShopPolicy; shopBays: Record<DistrictId, number>;             // rented heated bays in the district's town
  dealers: Record<DistrictId, DealerState>;                                 // the dealers at each district's hub (§3 District.hub)
  market: { usedMult: Record<'placer'|'general'|'light', number>; newMult: number; floodIdx: number; repoBustLots13w: number[] };  // cached in step 3
}
interface Machine {                                    // extends the pre-agreed shape
  id: MachineId; modelId: ModelId; classId: ClassId; sizeClass: SizeKey; brandId: BrandId;   // SizeKey = catalog size slot, e.g. 'ex30'
  modelYear: number; hours: number;                    // SMR meter, true and visible
  components: Partial<Record<ComponentKey, ComponentState>>;   // the family's list (9.2.5); empty in P1–P2 and for `site` items
  grade?: 'A' | 'B' | 'C' | 'D';                       // P1–P2 visible condition grade
  status: 'working'|'idle'|'down'|'inShop'|'inTransit'|'rentedOut'|'assembling'|'destroyed';
  downReason?: 'failure'|'waitingParts'|'damage'|'lenderLockout'|'grounded'|'stolen'|'fire';   // 'down' (§11 lockout, §12 recall);
                                                       // 'stolen' / 'fire' with status 'destroyed'
  location: LocationRef;
  acquisition: 'owned'|'financed'|'operatingLease'|'financeLease'|'rental'|'rentToOwn';
  financeRef?: Id; contractRef?: ContractId;
  pm: { lastAt: Record<PmLevel, number>;               // TRUE meter hours at last service of each level (history drawn at listing, 9.3.3)
        knownLastAt?: Partial<Record<PmLevel, number>> };   // what records or own service show; undefined level = unknown
  options: MachineOption[];
  warranty?: { untilTurn: number; untilHours: number; scope: 'full'|'powertrain'|'structure' };
  purchase: { turn: number; costCents: Cents; channel: Channel; capitalizedCents: Cents };
  bookValueCents: Cents;
  down?: { workOrderIds: WorkOrderId[]; readyTurnFrac?: number };   // estimated return, fractional turn (step-8 plan)
  weekly: MachineWeekLog[];                            // ring of 52 for 9.10
}
type ComponentKey = 'engine'|'hydraulics'|'undercarriage'|'tires'|'drivetrain'|'electrical'|'structure'
                  | 'screen'|'pumpEnd'|'sluiceRiffles';
interface ComponentState {
  health: number;                 // TRUE 0..1 (hidden). 1 = new; 0 = worn out
  knownHealth?: Range;            // player's latest range; undefined = never assessed
  knownAt?: { hours: number; turn: number; source: 'inspection'|'dealer'|'pmLook'|'repair'|'symptom'|'damage'|'delivery'; inspector?: string };
  hoursSinceRebuild: number;      // TRUE (hidden); seller records may claim a value
  rework?: { mult: number; untilHours: number };   // §8 reworkHazardMult of the last mechanic to repair or rebuild it (9.7.5)
  defect?: { facade: number; revealAtHours: number };  // lemon mask (9.6)
}
type PmLevel = 250 | 500 | 1000 | 2000;
type Range = { lo: number; hi: number };            // inclusive, clipped to [0, 1]
type LocationRef = { kind: 'claim'; id: ClaimId } | { kind: 'yard' | 'dealer' | 'auctionSite'; id: DistrictId }
                 | { kind: 'transit'; id: TransportId };          // yard = a rented lot in the district's town (9.5)
type Channel = 'dealerNew' | 'dealerCertified' | 'private' | 'auction' | 'inherited' | 'rental' | 'rentToOwn' | 'lease';
type MachineOption = 'ripper' | 'fireSuppression' | 'extWarranty' | 'scrubber';
interface MachineWeekLog { turn: number; work: number; smr: number; outputBcy: number; fuelGal: number;
  costCents: Record<'fuel'|'pm'|'repairs'|'operator'|'rental'|'holding', Cents>; downHours: number; failures: number }
interface DealerState { brands: BrandId[]; promos: Record<BrandId, Promo>; certified: EquipListingId[];
  rental: Record<SizeKey, { available: boolean; offerId?: Id }> }
interface Promo { kind: 'none' | 'rebateOnly' | 'promoOrRebate'; rebatePct: number; apr?: number; months?: number; untilTurn: number }
interface FactoryOrder { id: OrderId; listingId: EquipListingId; modelId: ModelId; brandId: BrandId; depositCents: Cents;
  balanceCents: Cents; etaTurn: number; deliverTo: LocationRef; payment: 'cash' | { applicationId: Id } | { leaseQuoteId: Id };
  options: MachineOption[]; promoChoice?: 'rebate' | 'promo' }
interface PartsStock { sku: PartsSku; qty: number; unitCostCents: Cents; location: LocationRef; minQty?: number; maxQty?: number }
interface PartsOrder { id: PartsOrderId; sku: PartsSku; qty: number; costCents: Cents; etaTurnFrac: number;
  mode: 'normal' | 'expedite' | 'charter'; deliverTo: LocationRef; forWorkOrder?: WorkOrderId }
interface ShopPolicy { autoPm: boolean; autoFieldService: boolean; partsPolicy: 'normal' | 'expediteMajor' | 'expediteAll';
  autoReorder: boolean; baselineServiceOnPurchase: boolean }        // defaults true, true, 'expediteMajor', false, true
interface InspectionJob { id: InspectionId; target: { listingId: EquipListingId } | { machineId: MachineId };
  by: 'ownMechanic' | 'owner' | 'thirdParty' | 'auctionPreview'; employeeId?: EmployeeId; oilSample: boolean;
  orderedTurn: number; dueTurn: number; costCents: Cents; report?: InspectionReport }
interface InspectionReport { turn: number; hoursAtInspection: number; by: InspectionJob['by']; inspectorLabel: string;  // never the skill
  components: Partial<Record<ComponentKey, Range | 'notAssessed'>>; defectFound?: ComponentKey;
  refused?: boolean; pmRecords?: 'full' | 'partial' | 'none'; notes: string[] }
interface FieldCallout { id: CalloutId; claimId: ClaimId; workOrderIds: WorkOrderId[]; arriveTurnFrac: number;
  techSkill: number /* hidden */; stdHoursPerWeek: number; ratePerHrCents: Cents; travelCents: Cents }
interface PrivateSale { id: SaleId; machineId: MachineId; askCents: Cents; listedTurn: number; expiresTurn: number;
  counter?: { priceCents: Cents; expiresTurn: number } }
interface CostPerHourBreakdown { window: 'ttm' | 'season'; smrHours: number; workHours: number; outputBcy: number;
  lines: Record<'econDep'|'interest'|'insurance'|'leaseRental'|'fuel'|'pm'|'repairs'|'operator'|'partsHolding', Cents>;
  perSmrHourCents: Cents; perWorkHourCents: Cents; perBcyCents?: Cents; availability: number }
```

**IDs.** §9's prefixes in §2.4's registry: `fo` factory order (`OrderId`), `aev` auction event (`AuctionId`), `wo` work order, `po` parts order, `rct` rental / lease / rent-to-own contract (`ContractId`; §11's money record keeps its own `lease_` id), `trn` transport job, `mi` machine inspection (`InspectionId`), `fsc` field-service callout, `sale` private sale. The names `ord`, `auc`, `ctr` and `insp` would collide with §6's stop-work orders and inspections, §5's claim auctions and §4's contractors, so §9 uses its own (D-9.43). Equipment listings share §2's `lst` prefix with §5's claim listings, but the type is branded `EquipListingId` (§5's is `ClaimListingId`), so a function that takes a claim listing does not type-check with an equipment listing.

**Iteration order.** Every `Record` in `FleetSlice` is iterated in ascending key order through §2.3's sorted-key helper, never in `Object.keys` insertion order. This includes the collections without an `ids` array (`auctions`, `orders`, `parts`, `partsOrders`, `contracts`, `transports`, `inspections`, `callouts`, `sales`, `shopBays`, `dealers`, `market.usedMult`). IDs are zero-padded counters, so key order is creation order and does not depend on the path taken.

**Hidden vs shown.** True `health`, `hoursSinceRebuild`, `rework`, `defect` and `pm.lastAt` are never shown (§2.5). The UI reads `knownHealth` ranges, `pm.knownLastAt`, seller descriptions, records and reports. A machine delivered new gets `knownHealth = [1, 1]` (`source: 'delivery'`) and `knownLastAt` = 0 for every level. From then on the visible range follows the drift selector (9.6) like any other machine's. The player never sees the true wear rate.

### 9.2 Catalog

#### 9.2.1 Classes and families

| classId | Family (depreciation, components) | Spec unit | §7 roles | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `excavator` | excavator | bcy/hr loading trucks | strip, dig, feed, support, reclaim | ref: 90° swing, average gravel |
| `dozer` | dozer | bcy/hr at 150 ft push | strip, dig (rip assist), support, reclaim | D7+ carry a ripper; D6 ripper is an option (+$35k) |
| `artTruck` | wheeled | bcy per load (weight-limited gravel) | haul | |
| `loader` | wheeled | bcy/hr load-and-carry feed | feed, haul, support, reclaim | |
| `washPlant` | plant | rated bcy/hr; `prep` ∈ trommel, shakerDeck, grizzly, dryWasher | plant | includes base sluice runs (component `sluiceRiffles`) |
| `recovery` | recovery | `fineTreatCapBcyHr` (plant-feed equivalent) | plant | jig, centrifuge; shaker table and gold-room kit are gold-room items |
| `pump` | light | gpm at 100 ft TDH | water | diesel, `powerKw` 0 |
| `generator` | light | kW (75% continuous) | power | |
| `drill` | light | ft/hr; `frozenOk`, `bouldersOk` | (§4 programs) | |
| `conveyor` | plant | `stackerCapBcyHr` | support | cuts §7 tailings-handling hours |
| `roadTruck` | light | service / fuel-lube / lowboy tractor | support | self-propelled on roads |
| `site` | none (no components) | pickup, fuel tank, shop building, camp, gold room, camp safe, §4 tools | — | flat upkeep only |

Family drives the depreciation curve (9.3.2), the component list and the hazard profile (9.2.5). The hard-rock track adds the `underground` and `mill` families and their models (§14 14.11); §9's classes, brands, markets, wear, shop, parts and financing apply to them unchanged.

```ts
interface EquipmentModel {
  id: ModelId; classId: ClassId; sizeKey: SizeKey; brandId: BrandId; name: string;
  newBaseUsd: number;                         // Tier-1 reference (9.2.2–9.2.4); list = newBaseUsd × brand.newPriceMult × cpiIndex × newMult
  scale: 'small' | 'medium' | 'large';        // labor and PM scaling (9.2.5, 9.8.1)
  spec: { rateBcyHr?: number; payloadBcy?: number; ratedBcyHr?: number; prep?: 'trommel'|'shakerDeck'|'grizzly'|'dryWasher';
          fineTreatCapBcyHr?: number; pumpGpm?: number; generatorKw?: number; powerKw?: number; drillFtHr?: number;
          frozenOk?: boolean; bouldersOk?: boolean; hasRipper?: boolean; stackerCapBcyHr?: number; tankGal?: number;
          capacity?: number; campTier?: 'basic'|'standard'|'good'|'premium'; security?: number; extraRatedBcyHr?: number;
          reachFt?: number /* excavators: §4 test-pit depth */; hasSafe?: boolean /* campSafe, goldRoom */ };
          // the test plant's rate is §4's geology.testPlantBcyPerHr (5), not a §9 spec
  hp?: number; gph: number; weightLb: number;
  transport: { loads: number; oversize: boolean; superload: boolean; airliftable: boolean; assemblyCrewHours?: number };
  taxClass: 'mining7' | 'lightTruck5';        // §11 MACRS class: road trucks and pickups lightTruck5, everything else mining7 (R4 §8)
  firstYear: number; lastYear?: number; tier4FromYear?: number; phase: 1 | 3 | 5 | 6;
}
interface EquipmentPackage {                  // dealer turnkey spread (9.2.3), listed as one dealerNew listing
  id: string; name: string; items: { modelId: ModelId; brandId: BrandId }[]; discountPct: number; assemblyCrewHours: number;
}
interface Brand {
  id: BrandId; name: string; newPriceMult: number; hazardMult: number; partsCostMult: number; partsLeadMult: number;
  retention: number; fuelMult: number; captive: boolean; dealerP: number; share: Partial<Record<ClassId, number>>;
  warranty: { weeks: number; hours?: number; scope: 'full' | 'powertrain' | 'structure' }[]; pmPartsFree?: { weeks: number; hours: number };
  defunctYear?: number;
}
```

Reference rates are average operator (skill 50), health 1.0, thawed average gravel (§7 `REFERENCE_GROUND`). They sit at the anchors. Excavator and loader rates are about 80% of R4's Cat-handbook "typical", which a skill-100 operator reaches (§8 `skillProductivityMult(100)` = 1.25, 9.7.2). Dozer rates equal R4's average-operator practical rate at a 150 ft push, so a skill-100 operator runs about 25% above it, at the top of R4's range. Excavator `reachFt` (§4 test pits): 13t 13, 20t 16, 30t 22, 45t 27, 70t 32. Rent is `fleet.rentalMonthlyFactor[family]` × list: excavators 0.035, dozers 0.033, trucks and loaders 0.029 (9.4).

**The price range.** The catalog spans the brief's "$15k to $1.5M+". At the bottom, a tired `ex13` (P3; Caldera, Hokuto, Ironside and Marlow make it; `fleet.listingSizeWeights.excavator` gives it 0.10, almost all private and auction lots) hammers near $15k, and used pumps, generators ≤ 100 kW, grizzly boxes, dry washers and `tr30` trommels sell for $3–25k. At the top, a new D9 lists at $1.5M and a D10 at $2.3M; the largest single plant (`tr300`) is $950k, and the `pkg300` turnkey spread built around it lists at $1.58M (9.2.3, D-9.44).

An extra run's +20 bcy/hr follows R2's ≤ 8 loose yd³/h per foot of sluice width (3 ft ≈ 24 lcy/h ≈ 20 bcy/hr); its mats are part of the plant's `sluiceRiffles`. `fineTreatCapBcyHr` converts concentrator feed tonnage to plant feed: `tph / (1.6 t/bcy × 0.30 screened-fines share)`. Diesel trommels to 150 carry their own engine (powerKw 0); larger plants are electric and need a generator. Water demand (~15 gpm per bcy/hr) is §7's. Pumps are rated at 100 ft total dynamic head; higher lifts (bench claims, long lines) are §7's staging rule (`ops.pumpStageHeadFt`, pumps in series), so §9 publishes one rated point per pump and `H_prod` (worn `pumpEnd`) scales it.

**Dealer packages (P3).** A package (`EquipmentPackage`, data) is a turnkey spread a hub dealer lists as one `dealerNew` listing. `fleet/buy` on it creates one factory order per item with a shared ETA (the slowest item's lead), one 10% deposit and one balance; on delivery each item becomes its own `Machine` (own components, wear, book schedule, resale and liens). Price = Σ item list × (1 − `discountPct`, default `fleet.packageDiscountPct` 0.03); assembly uses the package's crew hours instead of the items'. *Trade-off:* 3% off and one delivery schedule, against sourcing used items piecemeal for far less cash.

```
pkg300 (Klondike turnkey 300-bcy/hr spread; northern hubs with a Klondike dealer; year-1 USD):
  Klondike tr300 950,000 + Klondike scrub 140,000 + Klondike cnv24 (feed conveyor) 60,000
  + Vortex cenL 240,000 × 1.10 = 264,000 + Caldera gen500 200,000 × 1.05 = 210,000          = 1,624,000 list
  price = 1,624,000 × (1 − 0.03) = $1,575,280;  power 220 + 55 + 45 + 15 = 335 kW ≤ gen500's 375 kW continuous
  assemblyCrewHours 300 (tr300 240 + scrubber 40 + conveyor 20) × $115 = $34,500
```
This is the brief's "$1.5M+ new wash plant": the plant alone is $950k (R4 large plant $0.6–1.5M); with its scrubber, fines circuit, feed conveyor and power it clears $1.5M (D-9.44).

Camp tiers map to §7 `ops.campTierMult` (basic 0.8, standard 1.0, good 1.25, premium 1.5) and to §8 morale. Camp power is inside §7 camp cost. **`campSummary`** is the single camp read for §7 (camp cost, theft exposure), §8 (morale, fatigue), §10 (gold storage) and §12 (security, theft drivers):

```
campSummary(state, claimId) → { capacity, tier, security, overCapacity, hasSafe }
  units        = camp items located at the claim (campT8, campS12, campSlp6, campM25, campP25), status not 'destroyed'
  capacity     = floor( Σ_units spec.capacity × effective('ops.campCapacityMult', claim) )      // §7 hook, e.g. §12 campFire
  tier         = capacity-weighted mean of the units' tiers (basic 1, standard 2, good 3, premium 4), rounded down;
                 no units → capacity 0, tier 'basic' (§8 D-8.35 decides commuting vs over capacity)
  security     = min(§7 ops.siteSecurityCap 0.9, max_units spec.security + 0.15 × [goldRoom at the claim]
                     + §12 campSecurity add (0.15 / 0.30 / 0.50 by tier, 0 if none))
                 // §7 adds ownerPresentSecurity on top and re-caps (D-7.43); no units → 0 before the adds
  overCapacity = max(0, people housed at the claim this week (§8 assignments, incl. the owner) − capacity)   // 0 = within capacity
  hasSafe      = a campSafe or a goldRoom located at the claim, status not 'destroyed'
```
`ops.campCapacityMult` acts before `overCapacity`, so a camp fire that halves capacity puts half the crew over capacity at once. A `campSafe` adds no site security: its effect is §10's `campSafe` tier (theft hazard ×0.2, loss U(0.4, 1.0)), which requires `hasSafe`; §10 has no safe purchase of its own (D-9.45). Example: a `campT8` plus a `goldRoom` with §12 campSecurity tier 1 gives security min(0.9, 0.20 + 0.15 + 0.15) = 0.50, `hasSafe` true; with 10 people housed, `overCapacity` = 2; a camp fire modifier 0.5 makes capacity floor(8 × 0.5) = 4 and `overCapacity` 6.

`rocker`, `drywasherHand` and `testPlant` are §4's prospecting tools: `site` family (no components), rentable at `fleet.toolRentUsdPerDay` (rocker 25, drywasherHand 40, testPlant 150) from any service town or hub, which are §4's day rates. A pump-fed highbanker is not offered (§4 D-4.14). **Yard:** a machine parked at `{ kind: 'yard', id: districtId }` sits in a fenced lot in the district's town at `fleet.yardUsdPerMachineMonth` (150). §12 reads it as off-season theft protection. **Options:** fire suppression is priced by size, `fleet.fireSuppressionUsd` small 8,000 / medium 15,000 / large 25,000 (R4 $8–25k installed). A D6 ripper is $35k.

#### 9.2.5 Components

Each family has a fixed component list. **Base life** `L_c` is hours to health 0 at wear multiplier 1.0 (skill-50 operator, clean thawed gravel, PM on schedule, mild weather); typical placer service runs 1.2–1.5× faster. **Parts %** is the rebuild/exchange parts cost as a share of the class's base new price (labor separate). **w** is the productivity weight (9.7.1). **λ-share** splits the family's base hazard among components (9.7.5).

| **Ironside** | Value American iron; cheap parts, slower to find | 0.86 | 1.10 | 0.90 | 1.3 | 0.85 | 1.05 | 52 wk full | no | p 0.7 | ex, dz, loader, pump, generator, roadTruck |
| **Tianlong** | Low price, long warranty, weak resale, parts from the lower 48 | 0.66 | 1.35 | 0.75 | 2.5 | 0.65 | 1.08 | 156 wk / 5,000 h full | yes | p 0.25 | ex (20/30/45), loader (950/966), dz6, tr50/75, generator |

- "Dealer in hub" is rolled per district at world generation (`rng(seed,'fleet-world',districtId)`) for the district's hub (§3 `District.hub`); a brand without a dealer there adds `fleet.noLocalDealerWeeks` (1.0) to every parts lead and has no new, certified or rental listings there.
- Brand trade-offs, in one line each: Caldera buys uptime and resale; Hokuto buys running cost (fuel, PM parts) at slightly more failures; Nordvik buys truck fuel economy at parts cost and lead; Ironside buys a cheap entry at hazard and resale; Tianlong buys price and warranty at hazard, lead and resale; Marlow buys a cheap orphan that a mechanic can keep alive. The sim's brand-mix check (9.17) must show no brand dominates across access types.
- **Tier 4 aftertreatment.** Models from 2014 on carry DEF/DPF: engine and electrical hazard ×`fleet.tier4ColdHazardMult` (1.3) in `cold`/`deepCold` weeks. Pre-2014 units sell at ×`fleet.preTier4RemotePremium` (1.05) in winterTrail and flyIn districts (R4).
- Market share by class (listing weights) is in data (`brand.share[classId]`); default Caldera 0.30, Hokuto 0.22, Ironside 0.16, Nordvik 0.10 (0.35 of trucks), Tianlong 0.10, Marlow 0.12 (used only).

#### 9.2.7 Phase-1 catalog

P1 ships 18 machine models, cash only, with brand names for flavor but all brand multipliers 1.0: `ex20`, `ex30`, `dz6`, `dz8`, `ld950`, `ld966`, `adt30`, `grz40`, `tr50`, `tr75`, `tr150`, `dw20`, `jigS`, `cenM`, `pmp6`, `gen100`, `pickup`, `campT8`. It also ships §4's three prospecting tools, `rocker`, `drywasherHand` and `testPlant`. This covers a bootstrapper fleet (used 20t, used D6 or 950, grizzly sluice or trommel 50, 6" pump, tents) through the reference operation (30t, D8, 966, 30t truck, trommel 75, generator) to a first growth step (trommel 150 + centrifuge), plus the arid dry washer. It is four more than the guide's ≈ 14. Both dozer sizes matter (the D6 is the bootstrapper's stripper, the D8 the reference op's). The 950 loader and trommel 50 are in §1's Inheritor fleet (1.8.2), so P1 must be able to price, run and sell them. `jigS` is the cheap fines circuit for arid fine gold, so §7's full P1 recovery model (jig and centrifuge circuits) can be built in P1. §1's inherited camp is a `campT8` (8 persons, basic tier).

### 9.3 Markets, listings and prices

#### 9.3.1 Channels

| Channel | Where | What the player sees | Condition truth | Warranty | Price | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dealerNew` | hub dealer of the brand | model, list price, promo, delivery lead | new: health 1.0 | brand terms (9.2.6) | list × newMult − rebate | P1 |
| `dealerCertified` | hub dealer, 6–12 units | hours, age, dealer report: every component as a range ±0.08 (sd `fleet.certReportSd` 0.0625), biased +0.03 | reconditioned: all components ≥ `fleet.certMinHealth` (0.45) | 26 wk / 1,000 h engine, drivetrain, hydraulics | FMV(report) × `fleet.certPremium` (1.12) | P3 |
| `private` | district town or the seller's claim | hours, age, seller's description bands, records yes/partial/no | per seller type (9.6) | none | ask = FMV(claimed) × LN(1, 0.07), clamp 0.85–1.2 | P1 (grade only) / P3 |
| `auction` | regional sale at the hub, or on-site at a bust | hours, age, "runs and operates / non-runner", lot source (repo, estate, consignment, bust) | as-is; adverse selection (9.3.3) | none | timed bidding (9.3.4) | P3 (P5 competitor bids) |

```ts
interface EquipmentListing {
  id: EquipListingId; channel: 'dealerNew' | 'dealerCertified' | 'private' | 'auction'; modelId: ModelId; location: LocationRef;
  modelYear: number; hours: number; askCents?: Cents; expiresTurn: number; auctionId?: AuctionId; brandId: BrandId;
  shown: { bands?: Partial<Record<ComponentKey, 'excellent'|'good'|'fair'|'worn'|'needsWork'>>; records?: 'full'|'partial'|'none';
           report?: Partial<Record<ComponentKey, Range>>; grade?: 'A'|'B'|'C'|'D'; runs?: 'runs'|'nonRunner';
           source?: 'repo'|'estate'|'consignment'|'bust'; deliveryWeeks?: number; promo?: Promo };
  truth: { components: Partial<Record<ComponentKey, ComponentState>>; care: number;          // hidden
           pmLastAt: Record<PmLevel, number>; inspectAllowed: boolean;
           sellerType?: 'honest'|'optimistic'|'concealing'|'lemon' };
  bids?: { by: 'player' | CompetitorId; maxCents: Cents; actionSeq: number }[];             // sealed
}
interface AuctionEvent { id: AuctionId; site: LocationRef; siteAccess: Access; previewTurn: number; closeTurn: number; lotIds: EquipListingId[] }
```

Trade-off: new buys reliability, warranty and promo financing at full price; certified buys a reconditioned unit and a short warranty for a 12% premium; private is cheaper and riskier; auctions are cheapest, as-is, with transport and surprises on the buyer.

#### 9.3.2 Price model

```
FMV(model, ageYr, hours, condSignal, t) =
      newBase_model × brand.newPriceMult × cpiIndex
    × dep_family(ageEq) ^ (1 / brand.retention)
    × condMult(condSignal, hours)
    × usedMult_tier(t) × (1 − fleet.floodPriceCut × floodIdx) × E('fleet.usedPriceMult')
    × (preTier4 && remote ? fleet.preTier4RemotePremium : 1)

ageEq       = (1 − w_h) × ageYr + w_h × hours / fleet.refHoursPerYear          // years; w_h = fleet.hoursWeight (0.5; plant and light 0.3)
dep_f(a)    = A_f × exp(−λ_f × a) + F_f                                       // share of new at the AVERAGE condition for that age
condSignal  = Σ_c v_c × h_c / Σ_c v_c                                          // v_c = rebuild parts share (9.2.5); h_c = claimed, reported or known midpoint
condRef(H)  = piecewise-linear fleet.condRefByHours: 0 h 1.00 · 1,500 0.85 · 3,000 0.71 · 5,000 0.61 · 7,500 0.50 · 10,000 0.53 · ≥ 15,000 0.58
              // the mean condSignal the 9.3.3 generator produces at H hours (care Beta(2,2)); the dip at 7,500 h is the first overhaul wave
condMult    = clamp(1 + fleet.condPriceSlope × (condSignal − condRef(hours)), 0.55, 1.35)   // slope 0.8
usedMult_tier(t) = §10 ripple(state, 1, ε_tier, fleet.usedLagWeeks, 0.6, 1.6, { escalate: false })   // ε: placer 0.5, general 0.35, light 0.15
newMult(t)  = §10 ripple(state, 1, fleet.newGoldElasticity 0.15, fleet.newLagWeeks 13, 0.85, 1.25, { escalate: false })
floodIdx    = clamp(fleet.floodMomentumCoef × max(0, −§10 goldMomentumAt(state, t − fleet.floodLagWeeks) − 0.05)
                    + fleet.floodLotCoef × repoBustLots13w, 0, 1)
```

**Real index only.** Every dimensionless gold multiplier in §9 reads the real index, §10 `goldIdxRealAt(state, turn − lag)`, either inside `ripple` or directly (auction bidders, rental availability, new-unit delivery lead, listing sell hazard), and `floodIdx` reads `goldMomentumAt`. §9 never reads nominal `goldIdx`, which §10 keeps for display (D-10.32); inflation enters once, through the explicit `cpiIndex` factor. In P1–P4 the real and nominal indices are equal.

The depreciation curve already prices an average machine for its age, so condition is measured against the average condition at that meter reading, not against a fixed level: a delivery-new unit (condSignal 1.0 at 0 h) has condMult 1.0 and is worth `dep(0)` of list, and a 1,500-h unit claimed "everything excellent" (0.9) gets only 1.04. `cpiIndex` is applied once, explicitly, so every ripple here is called with `escalate: false` (§10 D-10.32). §9's ripple domains (used, new, parts, rental and field-service prices) read the scalar keys of 9.15 (`fleet.usedGoldElasticity`, `fleet.usedLagWeeks`, `fleet.newGoldElasticity`, `fleet.newLagWeeks`, `fleet.partsGoldElasticity`, `fleet.rentalGoldElasticity`, `fleet.fieldServiceGoldElasticity`; forms and values in 9.13), which §10's 10.8 table cites. §10's separate auction-hammer and auction-supply rows are not used: hammer prices come out of the bidder model (9.3.4), and supply out of `floodIdx`.

| Family | A | λ (per yr) | F | Resale at age 1 / 3 / 5 / 8 / 12 / 20 (R4 check) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| excavator | 0.809 | 0.1165 | 0.03 | 75 / 60 / 48 / 35 / 23 / 11% (R4 70–80 / 55–65 / 45–55 / 30–40 / 18–28 / 5–10) |
| dozer | 0.820 | 0.1024 | 0.06 | 80 / 66 / 55 / 42 / 30 / 17% (75–85 / 60–70 / 50–60 / 38–48 / 25–35 / 8–15) |
| wheeled | 0.809 | 0.1300 | 0.03 | 74 / 58 / 45 / 32 / 20 / 9% (70–78 / 52–62 / 40–50 / 28–38 / 15–25 / 5–10) |
| plant, recovery, conveyor | 0.72 | 0.150 | 0.04 | 66 / 50 / 38 / 26 / 16 / 8% (60–75 / 40–55 / 30–45 / 20–35 / 15–25 / scrap–10) |
| light (pumps, gensets, drills, road trucks, camps) | 0.75 | 0.140 | 0.05 | 70 / 54 / 42 / 29 / 19 / 10% (R4 used ~40–50%) |

- Placer-specific (ε 0.5): wash plants, recovery, conveyors, dozers ≥ D8, excavators ≥ 45t. General earthmoving (0.35): the rest of the heavy iron. Light (0.15): pumps, generators, road trucks, site items. Lag `fleet.usedLagWeeks` = 4 on top of §10's EMA13.
- Retention below 1 deepens depreciation: a Tianlong (0.65) at ageEq 5 keeps 0.48^(1/0.65) = 32% (R4 Tier-3 25–35%); a Caldera (1.10) keeps 51%.
- New units lose `1 − dep(0)` ≈ 16% (dozers 12%, plants 24%) the day they are delivered: FMV is resale, not list. Because condMult is 1.0 at delivery (condRef(0) = 1), no used unit can price above an identical new one.
- **Busts.** `floodIdx` multiplies auction lot counts by `1 + fleet.floodAuctionLotBoost` (1.5) × floodIdx, private listings by 1 + 0.5 × floodIdx, and cuts auction bidder counts by 0.4 × floodIdx (9.3.4). At goldMomentum −25% with 10 repo/bust lots in 13 weeks: floodIdx = 2.0 × 0.20 + 0.02 × 10 = 0.6; with goldIdxReal 0.75 (lagged), a placer-specific used price is 0.75^0.5 × (1 − 0.15 × 0.6) = 0.79 of neutral, and auction hammers fall further through thinner bidding (≈ 0.63 of neutral). R4: mining-class iron fell 30–50% in 2013–16.

**Worked example: a private listing.** 2019 Caldera 30t, 9,800 h, listed in 2027 (age 8) by an *optimistic* seller, goldIdxReal (lagged) 1.10.
- ageEq = 0.5 × 8 + 0.5 × 9,800/1,500 = 7.267; dep = 0.809 × e^(−0.847) + 0.03 = 0.377; Caldera: 0.377^(1/1.10) = 0.412. Base: $430k × 1.05 × 0.412 = $186.0k.
- condRef(9,800 h) = 0.50 + 0.03 × 2,300/2,500 = 0.528. Claimed bands (engine good, hydraulics good, UC fair, drivetrain good, electrical and structure excellent) give midpoints 0.7/0.7/0.5/0.7/0.9/0.9 → condSignal 0.694 → condMult 1 + 0.8 × 0.167 = 1.133. Ripple 1.10^0.35 = 1.034 (general earthmoving). FMV(claimed) = **$218.0k**; ask with noise ×1.02 = **$222.3k**.
- Truth 0.52/0.61/0.38/0.66/0.85/0.88 → condSignal 0.595 → condMult 1.054 → FMV(true) = **$202.7k**. Buying blind overpays ~$19.7k (10%); a $1,200 third-party inspection would very likely show it (9.6).

#### 9.3.3 Listing generation and rotation

Step 3 runs per district in ID order on `rng(seed,'fleet-market',turn,districtId)`. Each listing's hidden attributes are drawn once from `rng(seed,'fleet-listing',listingId)`, so they never change on re-derivation.

```
private arrivals ~ Poisson(fleet.privateListingsPerWeek (0.8) × townTierMult[outpost 0.5 | serviceTown 1.0 | hubCity 1.6] × (1 + 0.5 × floodIdx))
lifetime         ~ U{fleet.listingLifeWeeks 3..10} weeks;  weekly hazard of selling to an unseen buyer = fleet.listingSellHazard (0.10) × goldIdxReal
certified stock  : per district hub, target fleet.certStockTarget (8); each unit sells w.p. fleet.certSellP (0.08)/wk; refill Poisson to target
auctions         : a regional sale every fleet.auctionEveryWeeks (8; weeks 1–13 every 6, lots ×1.5: "winter auctions")
                   lots ~ Poisson(fleet.auctionLotsMean 16 × (1 + 1.5 × floodIdx) × E('fleet.auctionSupplyMult')) + every §11 repo and §12 bust lot
                   catalog posted fleet.auctionPreviewWeeks (3) before the close turn
class ~ fleet.listingClassWeights (ex .22, dz .18, artTruck .12, loader .14, washPlant .10, pump .08, generator .06, other .10)
size  ~ fleet.listingSizeWeights[class]; brand ~ brand.share[class] restricted to feasible ages
ageYr ~ clamp(LN(median fleet.listingAgeMedian[channel], 0.5), 1, 40)      // private 12, certified 5 (2–8), auction 14
        Marlow ≥ 16; Tianlong ≤ 12
hours = ageYr × LN(fleet.hoursPerYearMedian 1,150, 0.35)                     // plants and light × 0.6
κ (care) ~ Beta(2, 2); auction Beta(1.6, 2.4); repo lots Beta(1.2, 2.8); certified Beta(2.6, 1.6)
```

**True component health from history.** Previous owners rebuilt components when they wore out; careful owners rebuilt earlier.

```
careWear   = fleet.careWearMax − (fleet.careWearMax − fleet.careWearMin) × κ      // 1.45 (abused) → 0.70 (meticulous)
Leff_c     = L_c / careWear × U(0.85, 1.15)
rebuildAt  = fleet.priorRebuildAtHealth (0.30) × κ                                 // abused owners run to failure
cycle_c    = Leff_c × (1 − rebuildAt)
hoursSinceRebuild_c = hours mod cycle_c
h_c        = clamp(1 − hoursSinceRebuild_c / Leff_c + N(0, 0.06), 0.02, 1)
parked     : electrical, hydraulics, tires −fleet.parkedDecayPerYear (0.02) × max(0, ageYr − hours / 1,500)
repo lots  : engine and hydraulics −fleet.repoDeferredPmHit (0.10) (deferred PM before default)
certified  : every component below fleet.certMinHealth (0.45) is reconditioned to U(0.45, 0.65); hoursSinceRebuild set to match
PM history : pm.lastAt[k] = hours − I_k × U(0, 1 + 2 × (1 − κ))          // careless owners run up to 3 intervals overdue
             (certified and new: every level just done)
records    : honest sellers show pm.knownLastAt for every level when records = 'full', the 1000/2000 levels missing when 'partial'
```

**Inherited fleet.** `materializeInheritedFleet(spec, fleetRng)` turns §1's Inheritor list (1.8.2; the D6 carries a ripper, `hasRipper`) into machines on the family claim. Machine i draws on `fleetRng(i)`, the stream `rng(seed,'setup','inheritor','fleet',i)` that §1's `inheritorStreams` builds and hands over; §9 never names the `setup` stream itself (§2.3 rule b, D-1.65). In P1 they are grade D. In P3 each component's health is §1's `0.25 + 0.35·Beta(2,2)`, with one parked-broken component at U(0.10, 0.20) on one machine; κ = 0.3 for PM history; records are `partial` (family notes); `knownHealth` stays unset until inspected.

Competitor fleets reach the market through `materializeFromStub(stub, cause)` (§12 12.13): the stub's model, age and hours are kept and κ = clamp(stub.condition + N(0, 0.1), 0, 1) on `rng(seed,'ai',turn,cmpId,'mat',stubId)`; lots sold by a lender take the repo-lot hits. `createListingFromStub(stub, channel, askMult)` then lists it (private at the stated multiple of FMV(claimed), or as an auction lot).

The listing's **seller type** (private only) and description are drawn next (9.6). P1 used listings skip all of this: grade ~ {A .15, B .40, C .30, D .15}, age by grade (A 1–4, B 3–9, C 7–15, D 12–30 yr), hours as above, model from the P1 catalog by the class weights, condition visible and exact, `fleet.p1UsedListingsPerDistrict` (6) live per district, one new per week, 6-week life, ask = FMV(at condRef) × `fleet.p1GradePriceMult[grade]` (A 1.20, B 1.05, C 0.90, D 0.70).

#### 9.3.4 Auctions

Timed, unreserved, as-is. The player places a sealed **maximum bid** (`fleet/bid`) any time before the close; §12 competitors place theirs in step 5; step 6 resolves.

```
// drawn at close on rng(seed,'fleet-auction',lotId): independent of when or whether the player bids
bidders n ~ Poisson(fleet.auctionBidderMean (3.5) × siteRemoteMult[highway 1.0 | seasonalRoad 0.8 | winterTrail 0.55 | flyIn 0.4]
                    × goldIdxReal^fleet.auctionBidderGoldExp (0.8) × (1 − fleet.auctionFloodBidderCut (0.4) × floodIdx))
each background valuation v_i = FMV_visible × LN(median fleet.auctionValMedian 0.74, σ fleet.auctionValSigma 0.18)
FMV_visible = FMV(model, age, hours, condSignal = condRef(hours), t)     // condMult 1: nobody at the sale knows the truth
opening = max(fleet.auctionOpeningMinUsd 2,500, 0.15 × FMV_visible)
winner  = highest of {player max, competitor maxes, v_i} among those ≥ opening;  hammer = max(opening, min(winnerMax, second + increment))
second  = the second-highest such max, or the opening if there is none;  increment = max(500, 0.025 × second)
ties    → earliest bid (player and competitor bids carry actionSeq / step order; background bidders bid last)
no max ≥ opening → the lot rolls to the next regional sale (a repo lot's proceeds wait with it)
buyer pays hammer × (1 + fleet.buyerPremium 0.06, premium capped at fleet.buyerPremiumCapUsd 7,500) + fleet.auctionDocFeeUsd 300
```
- Payment is due at close (`finance.pay`, no partial). Failure → the lot goes to the runner-up, a default fee of `fleet.auctionDefaultFeeShare` (0.10) of hammer is billed, and `auctionBanUntilTurn` = turn + `fleet.auctionBanWeeks` (26).
- Removal within `fleet.auctionRemovalWeeks` (3), else storage `fleet.auctionStorageUsdPerDay` (50) per machine.
- Bots and background bidders value lots on visible information only; nobody at an auction knows the truth.

Trade-off: the auction discount (median hammer ≈ 74% of visible FMV, lower at remote sites and in busts) against no inspection beyond a preview look, no warranty, and the transport bill.

#### 9.3.5 Haggling (P5)

Private and dealer-used listings accept offers through §5's generic negotiation (`resolveOffer`) with the registered `equipmentSale` utility model: primary term price, secondary warranty months.

```
U_cp(price, warrantyMo) = price − warrantyMo × fleet.negWarrantyCostPerMonth (0.004) × price
U_res (dealer certified) = acquisitionCost × 1.05;  dealer new = list × (1 − fleet.dealerMargin 0.12)
U_res (private)          = FMV(TRUE condSignal) × (0.85 + 0.10 × motivationInverse)      // sellers know their machine
patience: dealers 5, private 3; motivation rises with listing age (+0.1 per 2 weeks listed)
```
A lemon seller's reservation sits on the true (low) value, so it accepts lowballs quickly. That is an honest tell. Auctions and new list prices with an active promo are not negotiable.

### 9.4 Acquisition modes

| Mode | Mechanics (§9 side) | Money side | Trade-off (one line) | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cash** | Full price + sales tax (`fleet.salesTaxRate[§3 District.jurisdictionId]`: `akStyle` 0, `nvStyle` 0.071, `temperateStyle` 0, `yukon` 0 (GST recoverable)) + buyer premium if auction; capitalized with delivery | `finance.pay`, no partial | Cheapest total cost; drains spring working capital | P1 |
| **Equipment loan** (bank, finance company) | Machine is collateral: new = invoice, used = §11 OLV of `resaleEstimate`; listing held `fleet.holdWeeks` (2) on a `fleet.holdDepositPct` (5%) refundable deposit while §11 decides; on approval §11 `createFinancedAcquisition(offerId, machineId)` | §11 rates, terms, PG, liens | Keeps cash; interest, guarantees, covenants, repossession risk | P4 |
| **Captive promo** | Each quarter every captive brand's promo is drawn (`rng(seed,'fleet-promo',year,quarter,brandId)`): `none` 0.4; `rebateOnly` 0.3 (cash rebate U(3, 8)%); `promoOrRebate` 0.3 (0% × 48 or 2.9% × 60 through `captive.<brandId>`, **or** the same cash rebate: the buyer picks one at purchase, `promoChoice`). New units only; promos (not rebates) suspended while goldMomentum < −0.15 | §11 `captive.<brandId>` (tier A/B, ≥ 104 weeks in business); §11 shows the forgone rebate | 0% looks free but forgoes the rebate; a cash buyer takes the rebate | P4 |
| **Operating (FMV) lease** | §11 sets the payment (rate factor by tier), the hour cap (1,500 h/yr) and the overage (`finance.lease.overagePerHrPctOfCost` 0.0001 × cost per hour, 30t ≈ $43/h). §9 meters hours, bills overage at each lease anniversary, and computes `returnConditionCharge(machine) = Σ_c max(0, fleet.leaseReturnMinHealth (0.40) − h_c) × rebuildParts_c` at return; lessee maintains and insures; buy at FMV or renew at end (§11) | off balance sheet (D-11.9); `exp.opLease` | Low payment, no residual risk; hour caps and return bills punish placer hours | P3 (one lessor, fixed B-tier terms) / P4 |
| **Finance lease** ($1 out) | As a loan; ownership at the last payment; 10% down | §11 `lease.<id>` on the balance sheet | Like a loan, sometimes easier approval | P3 (fixed lessor) / P4 |
| **Rental** | Monthly = `fleet.rentalMonthlyFactor[family]` × list (excavator 0.035, dozer 0.033, truck/loader 0.029, pumps/gensets 0.07, camp units 0.02; list already carries cpiIndex) × §10 ripple(state, 1, 0.30, 4, 0.75, 1.40, { escalate: false }) for 176 h per 4-week period; weekly = monthly / 3 for 44 h; hours over the basis billed pro rata. Rental company does all PM and repairs: a minor failure waits for its field tech (`fleet.fieldServiceDelayWeeks[access]`), a major or catastrophic one is swapped after `fleet.rentalSwapWeeks[access]` (0.3 / 0.6 / 1.2 / 1.5). Damage waiver (12% of base rent) covers §12 damage (fire, overturn, flood) and abuse; without it the renter pays the repair cost (cap = unit FMV) for those and for catastrophic failures in an abuse week (operator skill < 25 or plant φ̄ > 1.3). Renter pays transport both ways; the clock runs in transit and during access closures. Rental units: age U(2, 6) yr at 1,500 h/yr, health U(0.55, 0.85) | `exp.rental`; unpaid 2 weeks ⇒ recall (§11 priority 5, `debt.secured`; during a §11 reorganization the stay holds recalls for arrears from before the filing, 9.10) | No capital, little breakdown risk; ~1.8× ownership cost at placer hours | P3 |
| **Rent-to-own** | RPO at a rental company: 70% of **base** rent paid in the first 26 weeks (50% to week 52; overage, waiver and transport never count) credits against a fixed price (FMV at start × 1.05). Small-dealer RTO: no credit check, monthly 0.058 × price for 24 months (APR ≈ 34%), 2 missed payments ⇒ recall, payments forfeited | `exp.rental` until exercise; at exercise the cash paid is capitalized | Ownership without credit; the most expensive path | P3 |

**Rental availability.** Hubs and service towns stock excavators 20–45t, D6–D8, ADT 30–40, loaders 950–966, pumps to 8", generators to 300 kW and skid camp units (no wash plants except a Klondike `tr50` w.p. 0.3). Each class-size is available w.p. `fleet.rentalAvailP` (0.8) × (1 − `fleet.rentalAvailGoldSlope` (0.5) × max(0, goldIdxReal − 1)) × (operating phase ? `fleet.rentalAvailOperatingMult` (0.8) : 1) × E('fleet.rentalAvailMult'), drawn weekly on `rng(seed,'fleet-rental',turn,districtId)`.

```ts
interface RentalContract { id: ContractId; machineId: MachineId; vendorDistrict: DistrictId; term: 'weekly' | 'monthly';
  rateCents: Cents; basisHours: number; damageWaiver: boolean; startTurn: number; endTurn?: number;
  periodHours: number; rpo?: { priceCents: Cents; creditedCents: Cents } }
interface LeaseTerms { id: ContractId; machineId: MachineId; kind: 'operating' | 'finance'; termMonths: number;
  hourCapPerYear: number; hoursThisLeaseYear: number; returnMinHealth: number; financeRef: Id }   // payment and overage rate: §11
interface RentToOwnContract { id: ContractId; machineId: MachineId; monthlyCents: Cents; months: number; paid: number; missed: number }
interface TransportJob { id: TransportId; machineIds: MachineId[]; from: LocationRef; to: LocationRef; mode: 'road' | 'barge' | 'air';
  legs: { kind: 'paved' | 'seasonalRoad' | 'winterTrail'; miles: number; doneMiles: number }[]; costCents: Cents;
  startTurn: number; arriveTurnFrac: number; ownLowboyId?: MachineId; assembleUntilTurnFrac?: number; stalled?: 'accessClosed' }
```

**Worked example: rent vs buy a 30t for one season.** Caldera 30t list $451.5k; monthly rent 0.035 × 451.5k = $15.8k per 176 h. Twenty working weeks at 66 h are five 4-week periods at 15.8 × 264/176 = $23.7k ($118.5k), plus two weeks of transit and start-up at base rent ($7.9k): $126.4k; waiver $15.2k; transport both ways (240 mi, 1 load) 2 × $3.2k. **≈ $148k, no repair bills, no capital.** Owning the 8-year unit of 9.3.2 (~$200k) for a year costs about $20k economic depreciation, $16k interest or imputed capital (8%), $3k insurance and ~$45k R&M and PM (1,320 h × ~$34/h mid-life, R4 §7): **≈ $84k**, plus $200k of capital at risk and the breakdown risk. Renting costs ~1.8× owning: the right call on unproven ground, ruinous as a permanent fleet (R4).

**Delivery lead (new).** In stock w.p. `fleet.newInStockP` (earthmoving 0.55, plants 0.15, recovery 0.5, pumps/gensets 0.7, site 0.6): 1 week dealer prep. Otherwise factory order, drawn at listing on `rng(seed,'fleet-delivery',listingId)` and shown: excavators, loaders, trucks 6–12 weeks; D6/D7 6–12; D8+ 10–20; plants 10–20 (Klondike in the north 8–14); recovery 4–10; pumps/gensets 2–6; drills 8–16; camps 6–14; all × clamp(goldIdxReal, 0.7, 2.0) (booms create backlogs) + §12 `fleet.newLeadAddWeeks`. Orders take a `fleet.newDepositPct` (10%) deposit, posted to `prepaid` (non-refundable after 2 weeks); the balance is due at delivery (`finance.pay`; a failed payment holds the unit at the dealer, and after 4 weeks the order lapses and the deposit is forfeited).

### 9.5 Delivery, transport and mobilization

Every machine move is a `TransportJob` priced per load over legs. §9 builds the legs from §3's district and claim fields (no new §3 function is needed): hub → town is paved (`District.hub.roadMiFromTown`); town → outlet has the district road class (`District.town.roadMiFromOutlet`, kind `District.roadClass`); outlet → claim has the claim's access class (`Claim.trailMi`, kind `Claim.access`). A `flyIn` claim's heavy route is the winter trail (cat-train, §3 `claimAccess`), or a barge where §3 flags a barge river (P6 content). A yard or another claim in the district drops the hub leg; another district adds `fleet.interHubMiDefault` (300) paved miles until §3 publishes hub coordinates (P6).

```
transportLegs(from, to) → { kind: 'paved'|'seasonalRoad'|'winterTrail', miles }[]     // highway road class → 'paved'
loads      = Σ heavy machine loads + ceil(Σ fractional light loads)      // 9.2.2–9.2.4
perLoad    = fleet.lowboyLoadFixedUsd (1,200) × mobMultClass(§3 accessFactors, destination claim; 1.0 for a yard or the hub)
           + Σ_legs miles_leg × rate_leg              // class anchor, no distance term: the legs already price the miles
rate_leg   = paved: fleet.lowboyUsdPerLoadedMile (5.5) × fleet.lowboyDeadheadMult (1.5)
             seasonalRoad: fleet.legUsdPerLoadMile.seasonalRoad (14)
             winterTrail:  fleet.legUsdPerLoadMile.winterTrail (300)      // cat-train / trail move
permits    = OS loads × fleet.permitOsUsd (150) + SL loads × (fleet.permitSlUsd 2,500 + 2 cars × fleet.pilotUsdPerMi 2 × miles)
air        = weightLb × fleet.airUsdPerLb (1.40) × §3 accessFactors.distScale    // airliftable items only
barge      = weightLb × fleet.bargeUsdPerLb (0.30) + fleet.bargeHandlingUsd (3,000) per machine   // barge-river districts, operating phase (P6)
cost       = (loads × perLoad + permits) × cpiIndex × E('fleet.transportCostMult') × springMult
springMult = fleet.springRestrictionMult (1.35) for OS/OW loads on paved or seasonal legs in a northern district whose phase is
             'breakup', or 'winter' with week ≥ fleet.springRestrictStartWeek (10); else 1      // phase-based: no hidden dates
weeks      = fleet.transportSchedulingWeeks (1) + pavedMi / 1,500 + seasonalMi / 600 + trailMi / fleet.trailMilesPerWeek (60)
             (air 1; barge fleet.bargeWeeks 3); plants then spend assemblyCrewHours / fleet.riggingCrewHoursPerWeek (120) weeks 'assembling'
assembly   = plant assemblyCrewHours (tr75 60, tr150 90, tr300 240, sh200 160, sh350 240) × fleet.riggingUsdPerHr (115)
```
- **Windows** (§1 1.4.5, D-1.27). A move is **validated** against `accessOutlook(state, districtId, mode, week)` for every week a leg is scheduled to occupy: `ACCESS_CLOSED` if any is `'closed'`, a warning if any is `'uncertain'`. It **executes** against this week's `accessOpen`: paved needs `highway`, seasonal legs `seasonalRoad`, trail legs `winterTrail` (heavy haul). A leg whose mode is closed this week stalls (`stalled: 'accessClosed'`). The loads wait at the leg's start (the town or the outlet), the job slips week by week as §1 prescribes, and the rental clock runs. A trail leg stranded by an early breakup waits for the next window or is cancelled back to town. Missing the window means waiting a year, or air for what can fly.
- **Own lowboy.** With a `lowboy` and an assigned operator, paved and seasonal legs cost fuel (`miles × 2 / fleet.ownLowboyMpg (4.5) × delivered diesel`) plus lowboy wear hours, but move one load per round trip (`2 × miles / 40 mph + 4 h` each). Trail legs are always contracted. Trade-off: ~70% cheaper per load, but a 10-load move takes one driver 2–3 weeks.
- Self-propelled road vehicles drive at `fleet.driveUsdPerMile` (2.5) and their own hours. Inbound transport and plant assembly on a purchase are capitalized; every later move posts to `exp.mobilization` (9.10).
- **Distance counts once.** §3's `mobMult` already includes distance (`mobMultClass × distScale`), so §9 uses the class anchor `mobMultClass` for the fixed per-load handling and prices miles in the legs; air freight scales by `distScale` (D-9.13).
- **Freight to winter-trail claims** (§3 `claimAccess`). Parts, kits and other freight move whenever `freightOpen` holds: by trail in the trail window, by air otherwise (air always flies when the trail is shut). With `freightMode` 'air' they are priced as fly-in freight: airliftable machines by the `air` formula, parts at the access's lead (already air in summer, 9.9) with 9.9's charter option. Heavy iron still needs `heavyOpen` (the trail window).

**Worked example: reference fleet to a winter-trail claim.** §3's example claim: hub 200 mi paved to town, 45 mi seasonal road to the outlet, 14 mi winter trail (`mobMultClass` 2.2; `mobMult` 1.54 is not used here, because the legs carry the distance). Loads: 30t (1 OS), D8 (2, 1 OS), 966 (1), 30t truck (1), trommel 75 (2, 1 OS), plus pump 0.3 + generator 0.4 + tent camp 0.5 + 10k tank 1 + centrifuge 0.5 → 7 + ceil(2.7) = 10 loads.
- Per load: 1,200 × 2.2 + 200 × 8.25 + 45 × 14 + 14 × 300 = 2,640 + 1,650 + 630 + 4,200 = **$9,120**; × 10 = $91.2k; permits 3 OS × $150 = $450; trommel assembly 60 h × $115 = $6.9k. **Total ≈ $98.6k**, 1.44 → 2 turns plus half a week assembling, and only inside §1's trail window (typically weeks 2–13).
- The same fleet 350 mi by highway (`mobMultClass` 1.0): 10 × (1,200 + 350 × 8.25) = $40.9k + permits $450 + assembly $6.9k = **$48.2k** (R4 highway $25–80k; winter trail $100–400k for longer trails).

### 9.6 Hidden condition and inspections

**Seller types (private listings).** Drawn per listing: lemon w.p. `fleet.privateLemonShare` (§1: easy 0.10 / standard 0.20 / hard 0.30); the rest honest 0.45, optimistic 0.35, concealing 0.20.

| Type | Description bands (excellent ≥ .8, good .6–.8, fair .4–.6, worn .2–.4, needs work < .2) | Records | Allows an inspection |
|---|---|---|---|
| honest | true band of each component | true (full or partial) | p 0.95 |
| optimistic | each band +1 w.p. 0.6 | omits bad entries | p 0.85 |
| concealing | true, except the worst component claimed "good" | omits it | p 0.70 |
| lemon | everything "good" or better; one of engine, hydraulics, drivetrain, structure has true h ~ U(0.02, 0.15) behind a `defect.facade` ~ U(0.60, 0.75) that hides symptoms until `revealAtHours` = hours + U(20, 80) | fabricated w.p. 0.5 | p 0.50 |

The player sees the description, records status, hours and age; never the type. Whether the seller allows an inspection (own mechanic or third party; auction previews are always allowed) is drawn once per listing on `fleet-listing`, so asking twice does not re-roll it. A refusal costs nothing and returns a report with `refused: true`. Tells: a refused inspection, missing records, a lowball accepted fast (P5).

**Inspection kinds.** Accuracy comes from §8 `inspectionAccuracy(s) = { healthSd, defectDetectP, optimism }` (8.11: at skill 50 sd 0.125, detect 0.63, optimism +0.03; at 100 sd 0.05, detect 0.95, optimism 0).

| Kind | Who | Cost and time | Accuracy | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Own mechanic | employee with mechanic role (§8) or the owner (mechanic background: free, 1 day, ≤ 2/week, §1) | 6 std shop hours + travel (`fleet.inspectTravelUsdPerMi` 1.5 round trip if away); result next week | `inspectionAccuracy(skill)` | all components, PM records |
| + oil sample | add-on | `fleet.oilSampleUsd` 45 × 3 compartments; +1 week | healthSd × `fleet.oilSampleSdMult` (0.5) on engine, hydraulics, drivetrain; detect +0.20 there | |
| Third party | dealer or independent | `fleet.thirdPartyInspectUsd` 1,200 + 1.5/mi beyond 50 mi (cap 3,500) × cpi; 1 week | `inspectionAccuracy(fleet.thirdPartySkill 70)` | all; seller may refuse |
| Auction preview | own mechanic or owner at the sale site | 4 std h + travel | healthSd × `fleet.previewSdMult` (1.5) on structure, undercarriage, tires; engine and hydraulics from a run-up at max(healthSd × 1.5, `fleet.runUpSdMin` 0.20); drivetrain, electrical `notAssessed`; detect × 0.5 | partial |
| Dealer report | certified listings | free | sd `fleet.certReportSd` (0.0625, so ±0.08 at 80%), optimism +0.03, no defect check (certified units carry none) | all |
| PM look | every PM by a mechanic (9.8.1) | free | healthSd × `fleet.pmLookSdMult` (2.0; 1.5 on 500+ levels, which include an oil sample) | engine, hydraulics, drivetrain |

```
// rng(seed,'fleet-inspect',turn,inspectionId); one draw per component in ComponentKey order, then the defect roll
h_seen   = defect present and not detected ? facade : h
z        ~ N(0, 1)
center   = h_seen + optimism + healthSd_k × z                 // healthSd_k = healthSd × the kind's multiplier
w        = fleet.inspectRangeZ (1.28) × healthSd_k            // half-width: an unbiased report contains the truth ~80% of the time
range    = [center − w, center + w] ∩ [0, 1]
P(detect defect) = min(0.98, defectDetectP × kindMult + oilBonus)   // detected ⇒ h_seen = h and defectFound is set
```

**Knowledge drift on owned machines** (selector, no state; never reads truth). The displayed range shifts down by the *visible* expected wear since `knownAt` and widens by `fleet.knownRangeWidenPerKHr` (0.05) per side per 1,000 h. Visible expected wear = 9.7.4 with the operator's résumé midpoint in place of true skill, `fleet.visibleGroundMult` (1.25, a typical placer) in place of `M_gr`, the known PM state and the week's visible weather. A component below `fleet.symptomThreshold` (0.15) true health produces an operator symptom report w.p. `fleet.symptomP` (0.3) per working week (`rng(seed,'fleet-symptom',turn,machineId)`), which sets its range to [0, 0.25] and raises a `machine.symptom` alert. A failure's repair report sets the range at the repairing mechanic's accuracy; a §12 or §7 damage hit shifts the range down by the hit (source `damage`). A lemon facade drops at `revealAtHours` with a `machine.symptom` alert ("engine knocking under load") and sets that range to [0, 0.25].

**Worked example.** The player's skill-60 mechanic inspects a used 30t (true engine 0.55, UC 0.12): healthSd = 0.20 − 0.0015 × 60 = 0.11, optimism +0.024, w = 1.28 × 0.11 = 0.14. Draws: UC z = +0.45 → center 0.12 + 0.024 + 0.05 = 0.19 → **[0.05, 0.33]**; engine z = −0.70 → 0.55 + 0.024 − 0.077 = 0.50 → **[0.36, 0.64]**. The report says "undercarriage near the end of its life; engine mid-life". An auction preview of the same machine reads the UC at healthSd 0.165 (w 0.21: about [0, 0.40]) and the engine from a run-up at w 0.26. The owner-mechanic (skill 85) would read w 0.09.

### 9.7 Per-machine functions

All four pre-agreed functions are pure, return `{ value, calc }` (§2.8), and read only state and their arguments. Randomness lives in the weekly failure roll (9.7.5) on a named stream.

#### 9.7.1 Health → productivity

```
H_prod(m) = Π_c ( 1 − w_{f,c} × (1 − h_c) ^ fleet.healthProdExp )        // exp 2.5; w from 9.2.5; h_c true health
```
Convex on purpose: wear barely shows until late. An excavator with every component at 0.5 runs at 0.92; at 0.25 it runs at 0.80; a near-dead engine alone (0.1) costs 11%. Undercarriage and tires carry small weights: worn tracks raise risk and cost far more than they cut output.

#### 9.7.2 `machineEffectiveRate`

```
machineEffectiveRate(m, operator, ground, ctx: { task, tempBand, phase }) → { value, unit, calc }
  value = spec(m) × Q(m) × S(m, operator) × G(m, ground, ctx.task) × C(m, ctx.tempBand) × E(m)

spec(m) = excavator, loader: rateBcyHr | dozer: rateBcyHr at 150 ft push | artTruck: payloadBcy (bcy per load)
          | washPlant: ratedBcyHr | recovery: fineTreatCapBcyHr | pump: pumpGpm | generator: generatorKw | drill: drillFtHr
Q(m)    = P3+: H_prod(m)                     P1–P2: fleet.p1GradeRateMult[grade] (A 1.00, B 0.96, C 0.91, D 0.85)
S       = operated classes (excavator, dozer, artTruck, loader, drill): §8 skillProductivityMult(operator.effSkill), with
          operator = §8 operatorProfile(state, empId | 'owner', classId) (effSkill already nets fatigue and cross-role cover);
          no operator ⇒ the machine has no rate. Every other class: 1. Plant-operator skill acts on recovery in §7, not here.
          §8 (8.2) maps §9 classes to its OpClass: excavator, dozer, loader → the same; artTruck and roadTruck (lowboy
          driver) → truck; drill → the driller role; other classes take no operator.
G       = 1 when ground = REFERENCE_GROUND (how §7 calls it, D-7.2); otherwise §7 groundTaskMult(classId, task, ground)
C       = fleet.coldRateMult[tempBand]: deepCold 0.92, cold 0.97, else 1.0 (machine warm-up, sluggish hydraulics;
          classes with engines or hydraulics only)
E       = Π §12 EffectModifiers on 'fleet.rateMult' scoped to the machine or its claim
unit    = 'bcyHr' | 'bcyPerLoad' | 'gpm' | 'kW' | 'ftHr'
```
- §7 uses the truck value as its payload `P_k`, so a worn or badly driven truck delivers less per cycle; §7 uses `machineEffectiveRate(plant) / ratedBcyHr` as plant `cond`.
- A machine that is `down`, `inShop`, `inTransit` or `assembling` has no rate this week (9.12 step 8 publishes availability).

#### 9.7.3 `fuelBurnGalHr`

```
fuelBurnGalHr(m, loadFactor, ctx) = gph(m) × brand.fuelMult × loadFactor × W_eng × fleet.coldFuelMult[ctx.tempBand] × E_fuel
gph(m)      = catalog gal/hr at medium load (9.2.2–9.2.4); 0 for electric or unpowered items
loadFactor  = §7 task factor (strip/dig/haul/plant 1.0, ripping 1.15, feed 0.85, idle ops.idleLoadFactor 0.30);
              generators: clamp(demandKw / (0.75 × kW), 0.35, 1.33)
W_eng       = 1 + fleet.wornEngineFuelMax (0.15) × (1 − h_engine) ^ fleet.wornEngineFuelExp (1.5)      (P1–P2: 1)
coldFuelMult: deepCold 1.15, cold 1.05, else 1.0 (§1 suggested values; warm-up idling and heaters, R4 +10–20%)
E_fuel      = Π §12 modifiers on 'fleet.fuelBurnMult' scoped to the machine or claim (e.g. §12 badFuel)
```
A mid-life engine (0.5) burns 5% more; a tired one (0.2) 11% more (R4 wear multiplier 1.0–1.15).

#### 9.7.4 `wearPerHour`

```
wearPerHour(m, operator, ground, maint, temp) → Record<ComponentKey, number>        // health lost per working hour
  wear_c = (1 / L_c) × M_op,c × M_gr,c × M_ov,c × M_pm,c × M_cold,c × M_rt × E_wear

M_op,c  = 1 + σ_c × (§8 skillWearMult(S_op) − 1)                 // S_op: §7 MachineWeekHours.operatorSkill, the hours-weighted
                                                                   // TRUE effSkill (plant: plant operator); σ from 9.2.5
M_gr,c  = 1 + a_b,c·boulders + a_f,c·frozenShare + a_r,c·[ripping] + a_k,c·bedrockShare + a_cl,c·clay   // §7 GroundCtx
M_ov,c  = plant screen, drivetrain, structure, sluiceRiffles: max(1, φ̄) ^ fleet.overloadWearExp (2.0)  // φ̄ = §7 phiAvg; else 1
M_pm,c  = 1 + s_c × fleet.pmSkipWearSlope (0.6) × min(r, fleet.pmOverdueCap (2.5))
            r = max_k max(0, hours − pm.lastAt[k] − I_k × (1 + fleet.pmToleranceFrac 0.10)) / I_k    // k over the machine's PM levels
M_cold,c = fleet.coldWearMult[temp]: deepCold 1.3, cold 1.1, else 1.0 (all components except sluiceRiffles; §1)
M_rt    = 1 + fleet.routineShortWearAdd (0.30) × (1 − ρ_site)                                       // routine servicing, 9.8.3
E_wear  = §12 modifiers on 'fleet.wearMult'

weekly:  Δh_c = −( work × wear_c + idleSmr × fleet.idleWearShare (0.3) × wearIdle_c ),  h_c ← max(0, h_c + Δh_c)
         wearIdle_c = (1 / L_c) × M_pm,c × M_cold,c for engine, electrical, hydraulics; 0 otherwise;  idleSmr = smr − work (§7)
```
- Effective lives land in R4's ranges: a dozer undercarriage at 4,500 h base, under boulders 0.2, 20% frozen and 25% bedrock, lasts 4,500 / (1 + 0.16 + 0.12 + 0.125) = 3,200 h (R4 2,000–4,000 in abrasive placer); a skill-20 operator (§8 `skillWearMult(20)` = 1.80) cuts that to 1,780 h, R4's "severe" life.
- **Hours that wear.** Step 10 sums §7's `MachineWeekHours` and §4's `programMachineUse(state, turn) → { programId, claimId, machineId, hours: MachineWeekHours }[]` for the week. Program hours add to the meter, wear, hazard exposure and (P1–P2) flat maintenance; §7's `smr` excludes them, so nothing counts twice. They carry §4's `GroundCtx` (`task` 'dig' with `frozenShare` = frozen ft ÷ depth dug, `ripping` when any frozen ft, `boulders`, `clay`, `bedrockShare`; drill rigs `task` 'drill') and the program operator's true effSkill. Program fuel is §7's (7.11 fuel line, D-7.44); §9 posts no fuel. A machine `rentedOut` under §12 `contractWork` wears at `fleet.rentedOutHoursPerWeek` (40) with reference ground and a skill-50 operator. A machine that does not run does not wear, except calendar decay: an owned machine with no SMR all week loses `fleet.parkedDecayPerYear` / 52 on electrical, hydraulics and tires (×0.5 in a heated shop or yard building).

#### 9.7.5 `failureHazard` and the weekly failure roll

```
failureHazard(h, ctx: { machine m, component c, temp, r, rho }) =        // failures per exposure hour
    λ0_f × share_{f,c} × brand.hazardMult × effective('fleet.failureHazardMult', m)   // tuning by difficulty (§1: 0.80 / 1.00 /
                                                                                       // 1.15) × §12 modifiers scoped to the model or machine
  × (1 + fleet.hazardWearA (9) × (1 − h) ^ fleet.hazardWearExp (4))      // ×1 at h 1.0; 1.56 at .5; 3.16 at .3; 6.9 at .1; 10 at 0
  × (1 + 0.5 × s_c × fleet.pmSkipWearSlope × min(r, fleet.pmOverdueCap)) // skipped PM: up to ×1.75
  × fleet.coldHazardMult[temp] (deepCold 1.5, cold 1.2) × (tier4 && cold-or-deepCold && c ∈ {engine, electrical} ? 1.3 : 1)
  × (1 + fleet.infantHazardMult (1.0) × max(0, 1 − hoursSinceRebuild_c / fleet.infantHours (300)))   // after rebuilds; new machines ×0.5 of this
  × (rework_c && hours < rework_c.untilHours ? rework_c.mult : 1)      // §8 reworkHazardMult(skill of the last repairer), first 200 h
  × (1 + fleet.routineShortHazardAdd (0.25) × (1 − rho))

exposure t_c = work + fleet.idleHazardShare (0.3) × idleSmr   for engine, electrical, hydraulics;  work otherwise
Λ           = Σ_c failureHazard_c × t_c
roll (step 10, machines in ID order, rng(seed,'fleet-fail',turn,machineId)):
  u1: fail iff u1 < 1 − exp(−Λ);  atWorkFrac = −ln(1 − u1) / Λ            // share of the week's exposure before the failure
  u2: component c with probability ∝ failureHazard_c × t_c
  u3: catastrophic if u3 < c0_c (1 − h_c)^3; else major if u3 < c0_c (1 − h_c)^3 + m0_c + m1_c (1 − h_c)^2; else minor
  u4: fire on a catastrophic engine or electrical failure (9.7.6);  u5: warranty denial roll (9.8.5)
  at most one failure per machine per week; a machine with E('fleet.machineGrounded') = 1 (§12 recall) is 'down', reason 'grounded'
```
Calibration (30t excavator, 66 h/week): new ≈ 0.08 failures/week, mid-life (all h 0.5) ≈ 0.12, tired (0.25) ≈ 0.30 with 35% majors. With the downtime rules below and §7's 0.97 routine availability this gives mechanical availability ≈ 95% new, ≈ 90% mid-life, ≈ 75% tired, and ≈ 70–85% on remote claims with no parts stocked, reaching the low end with Tier-3 brands and old fleets (R4: 90–95 / 85–90 / 70–85 / 60–80%).

#### 9.7.6 Severity and downtime

| Severity | Health effect | Parts | Labor (std h × size scale) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| minor | h_c −0.02, then fixed back (9.8.2) | clamp(`fleet.minorPartsShare` 0.012 × rebuildParts_c, $150, $3,000), or one wear kit | minor column, 9.2.5 | hoses, sensors, belts, a blown tire |
| major | h_c −0.10; must be repaired before the machine runs | `fleet.majorPartsShare` 0.30 × rebuildParts_c, or one `major:<c>` kit | major column | a pump, a final drive, a track chain |
| catastrophic | h_c = 0; needs a rebuild or exchange | rebuildParts_c × `fleet.catCollateralMult` 1.2 | rebuild column | engine or electrical: fire w.p. `fleet.fireOnCatastrophicP` 0.06 (×0.25 with fire suppression) ⇒ total loss, §11 insurance |

```
rebuildParts_c = partsShare_c × newBase_class × brand.partsCostMult × cpiIndex
                 × §10 ripple(state, 1, fleet.partsGoldElasticity 0.10, 26, 0.90, 1.15, { escalate: false }) × E('fleet.partsPriceMult')
work order     = diagnosis std h, then repair (or rebuild) std h; created blocking for major and catastrophic
diagnosis      = fleet.diagStdHours (minor 2, major 8, catastrophic 16) × (service truck at the site ? 0.5 : 1)
timeline       = [field-service arrival, if no in-house mechanic (9.8.4); fleet.poolResponseDelayHours (8 h), if the district pool
                 takes the order (9.8.6)] → diagnosis labor → parts: 0 if the kit is on hand,
                 else ordered when diagnosis completes and waited for partsLeadWeeks (9.9) → repair labor
labor time     = std hours / the capacity the step-8 plan gives the order, at most fleet.maxMechanicsPerOrder (2) people on one machine
```
The fire draw (u4) makes the machine `destroyed`, calls `fleet.totalLoss`, and emits a §11 `LossEvent { source: '§9', cause: 'fire', totalLoss: true }`. Every major or catastrophic failure on an owned or financed machine also emits `LossEvent { cause: 'breakdown', lossCents: parts + contract labor, breakdown: { component, healthAtFailure, pmOverduePct } }` so §11's breakdown endorsement can decide cover (it pays only if health ≥ 0.25 and PM ≤ 50% overdue). Each catastrophic failure on a player machine is reported to §12 through `events.noteExternalShock('failure', machineId)` for event pacing.
- **Mask to §7.** Each failure becomes a `FailureMask { machineId, atWorkFrac, downHours? }` for §7's step-10 re-resolve. `downHours` is set only when the machine returns the same week: a minor failure with the kit (or a counter run) available and either a site mechanic whose step-8 leftover capacity covers it, or else the district pool's leftover covering it plus the job's travel (9.8.6). Then `downHours = [pool: fleet.poolResponseDelayHours] + (diagnosis + labor std h) × §8 repairHoursMult(mechSkill) / jobEff` (9.8.3), and step 11 books those hours first. Otherwise the machine is down for the rest of the week, and step 8 publishes later weeks' down shares from the shop plan.
- Wear for the week is charged on the planned hours up to the failure (`work × atWorkFrac`), not on re-resolved hours (D-9.17).
- Warranty-covered failures cost nothing but wait for the dealer's tech (9.8.5).
- **Damage** (not wear). `componentDamage(state, machineId, damage: Partial<Record<ComponentKey, number>>, cause)` is the single entry point for §7's frost damage (§7 calls it `fleet.applyDamage`) and §12's one-shot `fleet.componentDamage`. It subtracts each hit from true health (floor 0) and shifts the visible range down by the same amount, because damage is seen. A hit ≥ `fleet.damageBlockingHit` (0.10), or one that leaves h < 0.15, opens a blocking `repair` work order priced as a major. Smaller hits open a non-blocking one. Damage from a §12 cause on the floater's list (fire, flood, overturn) also emits a `LossEvent` with that cause; frost damage is uninsured wear.

#### 9.7.7 Worked example: an auction 30t with a hidden worn undercarriage and a skill-30 operator

**The lot.** A 2015 Ironside 30t, 12 years, 14,800 h, a repossession, "runs and operates", at the regional sale in the hub (highway site). P3, gold flat (ripples 1.0).
- Visible FMV: ageEq = 6 + 14,800/3,000 = 10.93; dep = 0.809 e^(−1.273) + 0.03 = 0.2563; Ironside retention 0.85 → 0.2563^(1/0.85) = 0.2016; × $430k × 0.86 = **$74.6k** (condition unknown, so condSignal = condRef(14,800 h) = 0.578 and condMult 1).
- Three background bidders value it at 0.66 / 0.78 / 0.70 of FMV: $49.2k, $58.2k, $52.2k. The player's max is $65k. Hammer = min(65,000, 58,200 + 1,455) = **$59,655**; premium 6% $3,579; doc fee $300.
- Transport to a seasonalRoad claim 59 mi past town (`mobMultClass` 1.4): 1,200 × 1.4 + 200 × 8.25 + 59 × 14 + OS $150 = 1,680 + 1,650 + 826 + 150 = $4,306. **Landed: $67,840.**

**The truth** (hidden): engine 0.55 (overhauled at 8,050 h), hydraulics 0.48, **undercarriage 0.12** (replaced at 9,100 h, 5,700 h ago), drivetrain 0.60, electrical 0.70, structure 0.80. True condSignal 0.499 → condMult 1 + 0.8 × (0.499 − 0.578) = 0.937 → true FMV **$69.8k**. The landed $67.8k is roughly fair for this machine, but a $25.2k undercarriage (6.5% × $430k × 0.90 Ironside parts) is about to come due. A preview look would have read the UC at about [0, 0.40]; a skill-60 inspection at [0.05, 0.33] (9.6).

**Rate.** H_prod = 0.980 (engine) × 0.961 (hydraulics) × 0.971 (UC) × 0.996 × 0.999 × 1 = 0.909. With the skill-30 operator (§8 `skillProductivityMult(30)` = 0.886): 150 × 0.909 × 0.886 = **120.9 bcy/hr** at reference ground (a skill-70 operator, 1.106: 150.9). §7 then applies dig, boulder and frozen multipliers.

**Fuel.** 6.0 × 1.05 (Ironside) × (1 + 0.15 × 0.45^1.5 = 1.045) = **6.59 gal/hr** vs 6.0 for a fresh Tier-1 unit.

**Undercarriage wear.** Ground: boulders 0.25, frozen 0.10, bedrock 0.27, clay 0.10 → M_gr = 1 + 0.20 + 0.06 + 0.135 + 0.02 = 1.415. Operator: §8 `skillWearMult(30)` = 1 + 0.8 × (20/30)^1.3 = 1.472 (σ 1). PM current. wear = 1.472 × 1.415 / 6,500 = **0.000320 per hour**: 0.019 per 60-hour week; the UC reaches 0 after **374 h** (6.2 weeks). With a skill-70 operator (0.94): 586 h.

**Hazard.** UC: 0.0012 × 0.15 × 1.10 × (1 + 9 × 0.88^4 = 6.40) = 0.00127/h. Whole machine: 0.00276/h, so **P(failure in a 60-h week) = 15.3%**, 46% of it the UC. At UC 0 the UC alone is 11%/week. A UC failure at h = 0.12 is major w.p. 0.54 and catastrophic w.p. 0.07. A major costs 0.30 × $25.2k = $7.6k parts + 32 std h, after a parts wait of 1.0 × 0.86 (distance scale) × 1.3 (Ironside) = 1.1 weeks.

**The season** (machine-level Monte Carlo of 9.7.4–9.8.2, 20,000 seeds, 20 weeks × 60 h, skill-30 operator, one skill-50 mechanic with capacity free, parts lead 1.1 weeks, no kits stocked):

| Plan | P(UC failure) | Majors / catastrophics (all comps) | Downtime (scheduled h) | Repair parts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Run it as bought | 0.87 | 1.42 / 0.19 | 170 (2.8 weeks) | ≈ $17k |
| Rebuild the UC in the off-season first | 0.26 | 0.82 / 0.02 | 87 | ≈ $8k + the $25.2k rebuild and 40 std h |

If this is the only digger, the 83 extra hours of downtime stop the plant for 1.4 weeks. Against §7's 7.11.1 week, that runs ≈ $32k of wages, camp and site cost with no output ($23.4k a week). It also pushes ≈ 4,500 bcy (≈ 36 raw oz, ≈ $130k of gold) into next season, plus ~$9k more parts. The off-season rebuild wins clearly, *if the player knows*. It adds only $9.5k of resale (true FMV $69.8k → $79.3k): rebuilds pay through uptime, not resale. A skill-70 operator barely changes this one season (the UC is already spent). Hazard does not read the operator; the operator works through wear.

**The operator.** The skill-30 operator costs 20% of output against a skill-70 one on the same machine (0.886 / 1.106). He wears the undercarriage 57% faster (1.472 / 0.940) and the engine 16% faster (σ 0.3: 1.142 / 0.982): the rebuilt UC lasts 3,120 h instead of 4,890 h on this ground. That is "a bad operator destroys an undercarriage", in numbers.

### 9.8 Maintenance, mechanics and the shop

#### 9.8.1 Preventive maintenance

| Level | Interval (h) | Labor std h (small / med / large) | Parts base $ | Content |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 250 | 250 | 2.5 / 3 / 4 | 600 | engine oil and filter, fuel pre-filter, oil sample |
| 500 | 500 | 4 / 5 / 7 | 1,050 | + fuel and hydraulic filters, air filter |
| 1000 | 1,000 | 6 / 8 / 12 | 2,100 | + transmission, swing and final-drive oils |
| 2000 | 2,000 | 10 / 13 / 20 | 4,250 | + hydraulic oil, coolant, valve lash |

- Parts × `fleet.pmPartsScale` (light 0.3, small 0.8, medium 1.0, large 2.0) × brand.partsCostMult × cpiIndex (0 inside a brand's `pmPartsFree` window, e.g. Hokuto's 156 weeks / 2,000 h on new units). A level-k service also resets every lower level. Plants have a 250-h "grease, belts, bearings" service (parts $400 × scale); pumps and generators run 250/500/1000 at light scale.
- Spend lands on R4: a 30t over a 2,000-h cycle costs 4 × 600 + 2 × 1,050 + 2,100 + 4,250 = $10,850, i.e. **$5.4/h** (R4 $3–6); a D8 $10.9/h (R4 $8–15). Labor is ≈ 0.02 std h per operating hour.
- With `shopPolicy.autoPm` (default on) a PM work order is created when a level falls due (by `pm.knownLastAt`) within the next week's expected hours. On a one-shift schedule PM happens off-shift and costs no machine hours; with two shifts it takes machine time equal to labor hours ÷ mechanics on the job.
- **Baseline service.** A used machine arrives with true PM history (9.3.3) but the player knows only what the records show. With `shopPolicy.baselineServiceOnPurchase` (default on) every acquired used machine gets a level-2000 order on arrival, which resets all levels and gives a PM look. Skipping it saves ~$4–9k and a day of shop time but runs any hidden overdue PM on (r up to 3 intervals for an abused machine).
- Skipping PM raises wear (`M_pm`, up to ×2.5 on the engine) and hazard (up to ×1.75). One missed 250-h service (r ≈ 0.9 by the next interval) makes the engine wear ×1.54.

Trade-off: PM costs mechanic hours and parts every 250 h; skipping it is free this week and expensive in July.

#### 9.8.2 Work orders, repairs and rebuilds

```ts
interface WorkOrder {
  id: Id; machineId: MachineId; kind: 'pm'|'repair'|'rebuild'|'exchange'|'rebuildAll'|'inspect'|'routine';
  component?: ComponentKey; pmLevel?: PmLevel; severity?: 'minor'|'major'|'catastrophic';
  stdHours: number; doneHours: number; weldShare: number;
  parts: { sku?: PartsSku; costCents: Cents; status: 'none'|'onHand'|'ordered'|'arrived'; etaTurnFrac?: number };
  assignee: 'auto' | EmployeeId | 'fieldService' | 'dealer';
  priority: number; playerPriority?: number; createdTurn: number;
  source: 'failure'|'schedule'|'player'|'warranty';
  status: 'requested'|'waitingParts'|'inProgress'|'done'|'cancelled';     // §13 kanban columns
  blocking: boolean;                                                      // machine cannot run until done (major, catastrophic)
  fabricate?: boolean;                                                    // welder-made parts (below)
}
```

**Fixing a minor failure** restores the 0.02 hit (the hose is replaced, not the pump), at the minor parts and labor of 9.7.6. **Repair** (after a major failure, or player-ordered on a worn component) patches but cannot make old parts new:
```
s_m      = skill of the lead mechanic (§8 shopCapacity hours-weighted mechSkill), field tech or dealer tech (75)
q        = §8 repairQuality(s_m) = 0.80 + 0.002 × s_m           // share of the targeted health gain achieved
ceiling  = clamp(fleet.repairCeilingNew (0.90) − fleet.repairCeilingDecay (0.40) × hoursSinceRebuild_c / L_c, fleet.repairCeilingMin (0.45), 0.90)
Δh       = min(fleet.repairMaxGain (0.30), q × max(0, ceiling − h_c))
parts    = max(severity floor (9.7.6), rebuildParts_c × fleet.repairPartsPerHealth (0.55) × Δh)
stdHours = max(severity labor, rebuildLabor_c × fleet.repairLaborPerHealth (0.60) × Δh, 2)       // skill-50 hours;
                                                   // rebuildLabor_c = rebuild column (9.2.5) × fleet.sizeLaborScale
labor h  = stdHours × §8 repairHoursMult(s_m) = stdHours × (1 + 0.006 × (50 − s_m))
after    : rework_c = { mult: §8 reworkHazardMult(s_m), untilHours: hours + fleet.reworkHours (200) }
```
**Rebuild** resets: `h_c = 1 − fleet.rebuildQualityGap (0.30) × (1 − q)` (skill 50: 0.97; skill 0: 0.94; skill 100: 1.0), `hoursSinceRebuild_c = 0`, infant hazard and rework apply; parts = rebuildParts_c, labor = rebuild column × size scale.
**Fabrication.** With a welder assigned to the site, the player may set `fabricate` on a major repair or rebuild of `structure`, `screen` or `sluiceRiffles` on a Klondike Steelworks or generic item (both in the north): partsWait 0, parts × `fleet.fabricatePartsMult` (0.6, steel and wear plate), stdHours × 1.5, all of it weld work. It is a real reason to keep a welder, and to buy northern plant.
**Exchange** (dealer reman unit): h = 1.0 regardless of mechanic, parts × `fleet.exchangePartsMult` (1.25), labor × 0.5. **Rebuild all** (certified rebuild): every component, parts × 0.9; a D8 ≈ 0.305 × $1.05M × 0.9 = $288k parts + ~400 std h, ≈ 30–45% of new (R4 40–50% with labor).

Trade-off: repairs are cheap and fast but leave an aging component at mediocre health and rising hazard; a rebuild costs 3–5× a major repair and a week or more of shop time, so it belongs in winter.

#### 9.8.3 Shop capacity, routine servicing, backlog and priority

```
§8 shopCapacity(state, shop) → { mechHours, weldHours, mechSkill, weldSkill }     // shop = { mode: 'site', claimId } | { mode: 'pool',
                                                                                //   districtId } (9.8.6); labor hours this week incl. the owner-mechanic's
                                                                                // 50 h at skill 85 (§1, §8); skills hours-weighted, true
capMech (std h/week) = mechHours × fleet.wrenchTimeShare (0.80) / §8 repairHoursMult(mechSkill)   // skill 50: ×1.00; 100: ×1.43
capWeld (std h/week) = weldHours × fleet.wrenchTimeShare / §8 repairHoursMult(weldSkill)
job efficiency  jobEff = (service truck at the site or machine indoors ? 1.0 : fleet.fieldNoTruckEff 0.85)
                       × (outdoors: fleet.outdoorColdEff cold 0.80 | deepCold 0.60; 1.0 in a heated shop building or rented bay)
                       × (weld portion: fleet.fieldRepairMultByFireLevel[fireLevel] (§1: 0.6 at level ≥ 2, else 1))
                       // an order's std hours progress = allocated std-hour capacity × jobEff
weld portion    = weldShare_c × stdHours; welders work it at full speed, mechanics at fleet.mechWeldEff (0.6);
                  welders do no non-weld work
reach           : site mode (§8 `{ kind: 'shop', mode: 'site', claimId }`): the mechanic serves his claim's site; a job at another
                  claim in the district, when the player names him on the work order, costs fleet.travelStdHoursPerJob (3) per job,
```
