## 10. Gold Market and Sales

> **At a glance.** This section prices gold and sells it. Each week a regime-switching price model (bull / range / bear) produces the spot price in USD per fine troy ounce. The model has GARCH volatility clustering, fat-tailed shocks, rare jumps and a slow pull toward an inflation-tracking fair value. A visible macro layer drives it, and the player watches it through a news feed: policy rate, inflation (the `cpiIndex` that escalates every cost in the game), the dollar, central-bank buying, geopolitical risk, equity risk mood, and diesel. Every other section reads the **market index** (`goldIdx`, `goldIdxReal`, `goldMomentum`) through one family of **ripple functions**, so claims, iron, wages, lenders and competitors move with gold in a consistent, explainable way. The player's decisions are *how* and *when* to turn weighed raw gold into cash:
> - sell to a local buyer: cash today, at a discount, on the buyer's guess of fineness;
> - ship to a refinery: about 99% of value after assay, but a minimum lot and 2–4 weeks of price and cash exposure;
> - hold: in a camp safe (theft risk), a bank box in the district town, or a refined metal account (insured, and the gold §11 lends most against);
> - hedge with forward sales: locks a price, but variation margin drains cash in rallies, and a production shortfall is bought back at market.
>
> The player is paid on **fine** gold. Raw weight × fineness is always explicit, and true fineness is known only after an assay. Phase 1 ships a flat price, the local buyer, and camp storage with no theft. Phase 4 adds prepay deliveries from held lots for §11. Phase 5 ships the living market, refineries, storage, theft and hedging. Phase 6 adds the Yukon currency and the export royalty hook.

### 10.1 Price model: structure and state

Weekly log return (all rates annual, `dt = 1/52`; μ terms are **log** drifts, with no Itô correction):

```
ret_t   = (μ_regime[s_t] + μ_macro,t)·dt                 // trend: hidden regime + visible macro drift (10.2, 10.4)
        + κ·(ln F_t − ln S_{t−1})·dt                      // pull toward fair value (10.2)
        + Σ_k ψ_k·Δx_k,t                                  // same-week reaction to macro moves (10.4)
        + σ_t·z_t                                         // diffusion: GARCH σ_t, Student-t z_t (10.3)
        + J_t                                             // jump, drawn one week ahead (10.3)
S_t     = bound(S_{t−1}·exp(ret_t))                       // valuation band + hard rails (10.3)
```

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `S_t` | spot, USD per fine troy oz (`spotUsdPerFineOz`) | USD/fine oz |
| `s_t` | regime ∈ {bull, range, bear} (**hidden**) | — |
| `F_t` | fair value, an inflation-tracking anchor (**hidden**) | USD/fine oz |
| `v_t` | valuation `ln(S_{t−1}/F_t)` (**hidden**) | log |
| `σ_t` | weekly diffusion standard deviation (hidden; shown as "implied vol", 10.13) | per week |
| `Δx_k,t` | this week's change in macro driver k | driver units |
| `ψ_k` | same-week pass-through of driver k (`market.pass.*`) | log return per driver unit |

```ts
type Regime = 'bull' | 'range' | 'bear';
type MacroDriver = 'realRate' | 'usd' | 'cb' | 'geo' | 'equity';
type JumpCause = 'warScare' | 'bankingScare' | 'currencyCrisis' | 'surpriseEasing'        // up
               | 'liquidation' | 'hawkishSurprise' | 'flashSellOff' | 'riskOnRotation';  // down
interface PriceState {
  spot: number; lnSpot: number;
  regime: Regime; regimeAgeWeeks: number;                               // hidden
  h: number; lastResid: number;                                         // GARCH variance (stored clamped), last diffusion residual (hidden)
  fairValueBase: number;                                                // F_0 (hidden); F_t = F_0·cpi_t·exp(g·turn/52)
  pendingJump: { size: number; cause: JumpCause; precursorShown: boolean } | null; // drawn last week, lands this week (hidden)
  ema13: number;
  spotRing: number[];      // 53 weekly spots, t−52..t; pre-history fills t < 0 (momentum, 26-wk high, analysts)
  idxRing: number[];       // 53 goldIdx values; 1.0 for t < 0 (D-10.3)
  idxRealRing: number[];   // 53 goldIdxReal values; 1.0 for t < 0
  recordHigh: number;      // max spot over pre-history and play
  weekRecord: GoldWeekRecord;                                           // decomposition for explain/news
}
interface GoldWeekRecord {
  turn: number; spot: number; ret: number; sigmaWeekly: number;
  visible: { macroDrift: Record<MacroDriver, number>; sameWeek: Record<MacroDriver, number>; jump: number; jumpCause?: JumpCause };
  other: number;          // regime drift + pull + diffusion + band reflection, shown as one "Other / unexplained" node
}
```

**What the player sees vs what is true.** The player sees spot, every macro series, news, analyst views, and an "implied vol" figure. Regime, fair value, GARCH state and the pending jump are never shown. In the explain tree, the week's move breaks into *macro drift*, *same-week macro moves* and *shock (jump, with cause)*. All three are computed from visible data and public tuning. The remainder is shown as one node, **Other / unexplained (trend, valuation, noise)**. The diffusion term (about 2%/week) dwarfs the regime drift (about 0.3%/week), so one week's residual says almost nothing about the regime; averaged over a year it reveals no more than the price trend itself already does. Implied vol is a function of `h`, which realized volatility also reveals (D-10.15).

The player is a price-taker. No player action touches the `macro`, `gold-*`, `news` or `analyst` streams, so a seed fixes the price path for every playthrough (D-10.20). Market-news draws are keyed by source (`'wrap'`, `'bigMove'`, `'rumor'`, `'analyst:harrow'`, …), never by a running counter, so items other sections publish cannot shift them.

| Stream (§2.3) | Key parts | Draws, in fixed order, always all taken |
|---|---|---|
| `macro` | turn | 17 draws (10.4) |
| `gold-regime` | turn | `u_exit`, `u_dest` |
| `gold-price` | turn | 6 normals for `z_t` |
| `gold-jump` | turn | occurs, sign, size, cause |
| `gold-prehistory` | k, subsystem (`macro` / `regime` / `price` / `jump`) | as the four rows above, per burn-in week k; initial regime at k = 0 |
| `news` | turn, sourceKey | template variant, noise cause, rumor publish / false rumor, preview noise, hint delay |
| `analyst` | turn, houseId | Harrow noise |
| `market-buyers` | districtId | buyer count, basis, bias, name (at `newGame`; §10's own stream, not §3's `world`, D-10.37) |
| `buyer` | buyerId, claimId | per-claim fineness error (drawn once) |
| `assay` | shipmentId | assay error |
| `events` | turn, `'goldTheft'`, locationKey | occurs, loss fraction (rolled by §12's framework; §12 owns the stream) |

### 10.2 Regimes, drift and mean reversion

**Regime chain.** A three-state Markov chain advances weekly. Exit hazards are tilted by valuation and macro, so a regime change has a readable cause ("the bull ran out of steam as real rates climbed and gold looked stretched").

```
μ_regime          = { bull: +0.14, range: +0.01, bear: −0.16 } /yr           market.regime.drift.*
volMult_regime    = { bull: 1.10, range: 0.80, bear: 1.10 }                  market.regime.volMult.*
p_exit,base       = { bull: 0.0045, range: 0.0085, bear: 0.0045 } /wk       market.regime.exitProb.*
m_t               = μ_macro,t / market.macroDriftScale (0.05)                 // macro tailwind in "units"
hazMult_bull      = clamp(exp( ηV·max(0, v_t) − ηM·m_t), 0.4, 3.0)          // stretched or macro headwind ⇒ bull ends sooner
hazMult_bear      = clamp(exp( ηV·max(0,−v_t) + ηM·m_t), 0.4, 3.0)          // cheap or macro tailwind ⇒ bear ends sooner
hazMult_range     = 1
p_exit            = p_exit,base·hazMult                                      ηV = 1.0, ηM = 0.5
On exit, destination tilt τ = 1.5·(−v_t) + 0.5·m_t:
  bull → bear  w.p. logistic(logit 0.30 − τ), else range
  bear → bull  w.p. logistic(logit 0.40 + τ), else range
  range → bull w.p. logistic(logit 0.45 + τ), else bear
Draws: rng(seed,'gold-regime',turn): u_exit, u_dest (both always drawn).
```

**Fair value and mean reversion.** `F_t = F_0 · cpiIndex_t · exp(market.fairValueRealGrowth · turn/52)`, with real growth 0.005/yr. The pull is `κ·(−v_t)·dt` with `κ = market.meanReversionKappa = 0.25/yr` (half-life 2.8 years). F itself grows at π + g, so persistent drift holds price away from F at an equilibrium gap of `v* ≈ (μ_regime + μ_macro − π − g)/κ`: about +0.42 in a bull, −0.10 in range and −0.78 in a bear, with neutral macro. So gold can stay "expensive" for years, but each stretch makes the bull more likely to end.

**Macro moves the anchor in effect.** The price settles around `F_t·exp(v*)`, not F. A persistent macro drift shifts that level by `exp(μ_macro/κ)`: four points a year of tailwind (high CB buying, low real rates) is worth about +17%. That is how real rates, the dollar, central banks, geopolitics and risk mood set the "macro fair value", while F carries only the decades-long inflation link (D-10.29).

`F_0` comes from the pre-history (10.5): the opening valuation is whatever the burn-in left. Its median is 0.00, with p10/p90 of −0.50/+0.41. Some seeds therefore start rich and bear-prone, others cheap.

### 10.3 Volatility clustering, fat tails, jumps, bounds

**GARCH(1,1) with regime target and inverse leverage.** The regime sets the long-run variance that GARCH reverts to. Positive shocks raise volatility more than negative ones, because gold's volatility rises in rallies (Baur 2012, via R5).

```
σ̄      = market.garch.sigmaBarWeekly (0.0180) × market.volMult (difficulty 0.85/1.0/1.15)
ω_s    = σ̄²·volMult_regime[s]²·(1 − α − γ/2 − β)
h_t    = clamp(ω_s + (α + γ·[e_{t−1} > 0])·e_{t−1}² + β·h_{t−1}, σmin², σmax²)   α 0.07, γ 0.03, β 0.88 (persistence 0.965)
σ_t    = √h_t                                            σmin 0.008, σmax 0.065 per week
z_t    = t5 rescaled to unit variance = N0 / √((N1²+…+N5²)/5) · √(3/5)    // 6 normals (dmath normInv) from rng(seed,'gold-price',turn)
e_t    = σ_t·z_t                                         // the jump is not part of e_t
```

Long-run diffusion σ is 0.0198/wk (14.3%/yr) in bull and bear and 0.0144/wk (10.4%/yr) in range. With macro pass-through and jumps added, total vol is about 17% in bull and bear and about 12% in range, matching R5's regime table (16–18 / 11–13 / 17–20%).

**Jumps.** Week t+1's jump is drawn during week t (`rng(seed,'gold-jump',turn)`, four draws always taken). That lets news precede it (10.7).

```
occurs      ~ Bernoulli(market.jump.probWeekly = 0.025)                       // ≈1.3/yr
pUp         = { bull 0.60, range 0.50, bear 0.40 } + (v_t > 0.25 AND S_t ≥ max(spotRing last 26) ? −0.25 : 0)   // blow-offs end in crashes
size        = min(0.15, (0.02 + Exp(mean 0.015))·market.volMult)             // mean ≈3.5%; tail to 15%; Exp = −mean·ln(1 − u)
cause       = uniform within the sign's set: up {warScare, bankingScare, currencyCrisis, surpriseEasing},
              down {liquidation, hawkishSurprise, flashSellOff, riskOnRotation}
```

**Bounds.** After `ret` is applied, `v' = ln(S_t/F_t)`. If `v'` leaves `[ln 0.40, ln 2.80]`, it is reflected back by half the excess (`market.valuationFloor`/`Cap`, `reflectFactor 0.5`) and the adjustment joins the "other" node. A hard clamp of `[$800, $40,000] × cpiIndex` protects against bugs. In calibration runs the band almost never binds.

**Worked example (one P5 week).** Start: bull, `S_{t−1}` = $4,400, `F_t` = $3,900 (v = +0.1206), `σ_t` = 0.0205, no jump. Macro: base 4.25%, expected inflation 3.0%, so the real rate is 1.25% (+0.25 pp vs neutral 1.0%), unchanged this week. Published CB buying is 900 t/yr, geo risk 60 (last week 57), equity mood 0.10 (last week 0.12). The USD index went from 101.0 to 101.8.

```
regime drift     0.14/52                                        = +0.002692   (hidden)
macro drift      (−0.03·0.25 + 0.02·2.5 + 0.0008·(60−45) − 0.04·(0.10−0.20))/52 = 0.0585/52 = +0.001125
pull             0.25·(−0.1206)/52                              = −0.000580   (hidden)
same-week        −0.6·ln(101.8/101.0) + 0.0012·3 + 0.05·(−0.02) + (−4.0·0) = −0.004734 + 0.0036 − 0.001 = −0.002134
diffusion        0.0205 · z(0.85)                               = +0.017425   (hidden)
ret                                                             = +0.018528 → S_t = 4,400·e^0.018528 = $4,482.28
Player's explain: macro drift +0.11%, same-week −0.21% (dollar −0.47%, geopolitics +0.36%, risk mood −0.10%), other +1.95%.
Next h: ω_bull = 0.018²·1.21·0.035 = 1.372e-5; h = 1.372e-5 + 0.10·0.017425² + 0.88·0.0205² = 4.139e-4 → σ = 0.02035.
```

### 10.4 Macro layer

Every driver is a small AR(1) or regime process with shocks, stepped in this fixed order in step 2. The draws come from `rng(seed,'macro',turn)` in a fixed order, and every draw is taken even when unused. Order: oil ε, spike u, spike size, glut u, glut size, inflation ε, equity ε, crash u, crash size, policy ε, USD ε, CB exit u, CB destination u, CB ε, geo ε, geo-spike u, geo-spike size.

```
// 1. Diesel rack (USD/gal at the regional hub, before §3 access adders). Anchor escalates with CPI.
D̄_t     = market.openingDieselRackUsdPerGal (3.60) · cpi_{t−1}
dev_t   = 0.98·dev_{t−1} + 0.030·ε + spike − glut,  dev = ln(D/D̄), clamp [ln 0.5, ln 2.5]
          spike ~ Bernoulli(0.005)·U(0.12, 0.30)   glut ~ Bernoulli(0.005)·U(0.10, 0.30)     // two-sided: 2008/2014/2022-style moves
dieselRackUsdPerGal = D̄_t·exp(dev_t)
// 2. Inflation (annualized rate) and CPI. Oil feeds inflation.
π_t     = clamp(0.030 + 0.985·(π_{t−1} − 0.030) + 0.02·(ln D_t − ln D_{t−1}) + 0.0020·ε, −0.02, 0.12)
cpi_t   = cpi_{t−1}·(1+π_t)^(1/52);  πExp_t = πExp_{t−1} + (2/27)·(π_t − πExp_{t−1});  cpiYoY = cpi_t/cpi_{t−52} − 1
// 3. Equity risk mood eq ∈ [−1 panic, +1 euphoria]
eq_t    = clamp(0.20 + 0.96·(eq_{t−1} − 0.20) + 0.06·ε − crash, −1, 1),  crash ~ Bernoulli(0.005)·U(0.6, 1.0)
// 4. Policy rate (baseRate): Taylor-style target, 25 bp steps at 8 meeting weeks {5,11,18,24,31,37,44,50}
target  = 0.010 + πExp + 0.5·(πExp − 0.030) + 0.015·(eq − 0.20) + pol_t,  pol_t = 0.98·pol_{t−1} + 0.0005·ε
meeting week: |target − base| ≥ 0.625 pp → ±50 bp; ≥ 0.125 pp → ±25 bp; else hold
crash week with gap ≤ −0.5 pp and base ≥ 0.5%: emergency −50 bp.  base ∈ [0, 0.10], kept on the 25 bp grid
realRate = baseRate − πExp
// 5. USD index (100 = opening)
ln U_t  = ln U_{t−1} + 0.005·(ln 100 − ln U_{t−1}) + 2.0·ΔrealRate − 0.02·Δeq + 0.009·ε,  U ∈ [70, 140]
// 6. Central-bank buying (t/yr, annualized). Hidden state {low 350, normal 650, high 1000}; exit 0.006/wk.
  low → normal 0.8 / high 0.2;  normal → high w.p. clamp(0.5 + 0.01·(geo − 30), 0.2, 0.9) else low;  high → normal 0.85 / low 0.15
cb_t    = cb_{t−1} + 0.03·(level − cb_{t−1}) + 12·ε          // hidden weekly flow
cbPublished = cb_t at report weeks {6, 19, 32, 45}, else unchanged   // the visible series; the gold drift reads this
// 7. Geopolitical risk index (0–100); quiet baseline 30, long-run mean ≈ 45 because of spikes
geo_t   = clamp(30 + 0.97·(geo_{t−1} − 30) + 1.5·ε + spike, 5, 100),  spike ~ Bernoulli(0.02)·U(12, 35)
```

```ts
interface MacroState {
  dieselDev: number; dieselRack: number;                 // log deviation from anchor; USD/gal
  infl: number; inflExp: number; cpi: number; cpiRing: number[];   // annualized π, EMA26, index, 53 weekly values (cpiYoY)
  eq: number;
  base: number; polShock: number; realRate: number; previewSign: -1 | 0 | 1 | null;   // preview published before a meeting
  lnUsd: number;
  cbState: 'low' | 'normal' | 'high'; cb: number;        // hidden
  cbPublished: number;                                    // visible, quarterly
  geo: number;
  queuedShocks: { driver: ShockDriver; size: number; sourceEventId: Id }[];   // from §12; applied at the next step 2
  flags: { dieselSpike: boolean; dieselGlut: boolean; crash: boolean; geoSpike: boolean; emergencyCut: boolean; policyMoveBp: number };
}
type ShockDriver = 'oil' | 'geo' | 'equity' | 'policy' | 'usd';
```

**How macro moves gold.** Each driver has a drift effect (a slow flow of demand) and a same-week effect (an immediate repricing). The same-week effect works on *changes*, so a geopolitical premium fades as the risk index decays. That matches R5: "+2–8% over days to weeks, then fading within 1–3 months". Drift gaps are measured from each driver's long-run mean, so the explain tree does not show a permanent "geopolitics" tailwind (D-10.30).

| Driver | Drift β (annual, on the gap from neutral) | Same-week ψ_k | Causal story shown in news | Source anchor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Real rate | −0.03 per +1 pp above 1.0% | −4.0 × Δ (−1.0% per +25 bp) | opportunity cost of holding gold | R5: −15–25% per +100 bp (2006–21), link broke 2022–25, so the effect is moderate |
| USD index | — | −0.6 × Δln U | gold priced in dollars | R5: beta −0.5 to −1.0 |
| CB buying | +0.02 per 100 t/yr of `cbPublished` above 650 | — | reserve diversification | R5: 1,000 t+ (2022–24) credited for the bull |
| Geo risk | +0.0008 per point above 45 | +0.0012 × Δ (25-pt spike → +3%) | safe-haven demand | R5: +2–8%, fading |
| Equity mood | −0.04 × (eq − 0.20) (fear raises the drift) | +0.05 × Δeq (crash → gold sold first) | liquidation, then flight to safety | R5: Mar 2020 −12%, 2008 −30%, then recovery |
| Inflation | via `F_t ∝ cpi` (long run only) | — | gold keeps pace over decades | R5: near-zero short-run correlation |
| Diesel | via inflation only | — | cost driver for the player | R4 §6 |

`μ_macro,t = Σ β_i·gap_i,t`. In calibration runs its weekly values run p5–p95 −7% to +10%/yr with a mean of +1.8%/yr; the mean is positive because CB buying spends more time in its high state than its low one.

**Market shocks from events.** §12 queues shocks with `applyMarketShock(state, {driver, size, sourceEventId})`. They land in **next** week's step 2, before the macro draws, because events (step 4) run after prices (D-10.11). Events move drivers, never the gold price directly, so every event-driven move has a visible cause.

| `driver` | `size` unit | Applied to | Example (§12 data owns sizes) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `oil` | log | `dieselDev += size` (then the clamp); flags a diesel spike for news | `fuelPriceSpike`: `U(0.10, 0.15)` minor to `U(0.30, 0.40)` catastrophic |
| `geo` | points | `geo += size` | war scare +20 |
| `equity` | units | `eq += size` | market crash −0.7 |
| `policy` | rate | `polShock += size` (the target moves; the next meeting acts) | hawkish surprise +0.005 |
| `usd` | log | `lnUsd += size` | currency crisis −0.05 |

**CPI and costs.** `cpiIndex` starts at 1.000 and averages +3%/yr (p5–p95 of annual inflation 1.0–5.0%). Every year-1-dollar anchor in other sections is multiplied by it. Example: π = 3.1% gives a weekly factor of (1.031)^(1/52) = 1.000587.

**Diesel example.** cpi 1.04 gives D̄ = $3.744. Last week dev = 0.10 and ε = −0.5, so dev = 0.098 − 0.015 = 0.083 and the rack is $3.744·e^0.083 = **$4.068/gal**. Delivered to a seasonal-road claim at §3's reference distance: + $0.90 × 1.04 = $5.00 (§3 scales the adder with distance). Simulated rack at year 5: p5 $3.11, p50 $4.21, p95 $5.74 (nominal).

**Policy example.** πExp 3.4%, eq 0.20, pol 0: target = 1.0 + 3.4 + 0.5 × 0.4 = 4.6%. Base is 4.0%, so the gap is 0.6 pp and a meeting week brings +25 bp to 4.25%. The real rate becomes 0.85%. §11 sets prime at base + 3.0%.

### 10.5 Pre-history and opening state

P5 `newGame` runs the full model for `market.preHistory.burnInWeeks` = 260 weeks from neutral macro (F = S = opening spot, π = πExp = 3%, eq 0.20, base 4%, U 100, CB normal 650, geo 30, h = σ̄²). The starting regime is drawn from {bull 0.35, range 0.40, bear 0.25}, using streams `rng(seed,'gold-prehistory',k,subsystem)`. Then:

1. The last 156 weeks are kept as visible history in §2's `HistorySlice`, at negative turns (−156…−1).
2. The price path and `F` are rescaled together so the last price equals `market.openingSpotUsdPerFineOz` (4,200). Valuation is preserved.
3. Diesel: the visible path is rescaled by 3.60 / D_end and `dev` is reset to 0, so the rack opens on its anchor. Base rate: the path is shifted to end at 4.0% (floored at 0) and `pol` is shifted by the same amount, so the Taylor gap carried into turn 0 is unchanged and the first meetings do not lurch. USD: the path is rescaled so U_0 = 100. CPI is renormalized to 1.000 at turn 0 (π and πExp carry over). Regime, GARCH `h`, CB state, `cbPublished`, eq and geo carry over.
4. `ema13` is seeded at the opening spot, and `idxRing` / `idxRealRing` hold 1.0 for every t < 0. So `goldIdx` = `goldIdxReal` = 1.000 at turn 0, every lagged ripple reads 1.0 until real weeks replace the seed values, and every calibration anchor holds at start. `goldMomentum`, the analysts and the price chart use the real pre-history (D-10.3).

Opening regime mix (3,000 seeds): bull 44%, range 27%, bear 29%. Year-1 `S_52/S_0`: p10 0.83, p50 1.05, p90 1.32. 12% of seeds lose more than 15% in year 1; 29% gain more than 15%. P1 skips all of this: the history is a flat line.

### 10.6 Calibration targets (what the simulator verifies)

These parameters were calibrated with a scratch Monte Carlo of this model: 2,000 seeds × 10 years, standard difficulty, after burn-in. A second run used the D-10.30 neutral levels, the published-CB drift and jump sizes scaled by `volMult`; the table shows that run. `npm run sim -- --market-only` reproduces it in CI (10.21). Pass bands are wide enough to survive dmath, named-stream RNG and the one-week-ahead jump draw (the scratch sim drew jumps in-week, which is statistically equivalent).

| Statistic (10-year paths unless noted) | Simulated | Pass band | Historical reference (R5) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annualized vol of weekly log returns, pooled | 15.9% (path median 15.4%, p10–p90 13.5–18.4%) | 14.5–18.0% | ~15–17% since 1990; 19–20% incl. the 1970s |
| SD of annual log returns | 17.9% | 15–21% | ~18% (2002–2025) |
| Excess kurtosis, weekly | 5.6 | 2–8 | daily 5–10 |
| Weeks with abs. move ≥ 5%, per year | 1.75 | 1.0–3.0 | 1–3 in calm regimes |
| P(any week with abs. move ≥ 10%) | 53% | 30–70% | ±8–12% extremes since 1990 |
| Median max drawdown (p10 / p90) | 40% (24% / 60%) | median 33–44% | −45% (2011–15), −33% (2008), −22% (2020–22) |
| P(price doubles from start at some point) | 47% | 35–55% | about half of 1971–2015 start years |
| P(price halves from start at some point) | 7.8% | 3–12% | only start years near 1980 |
| P(doubles within 5 years) | 20% | 12–25% | R5 target 15–25% |
| P(drawdown ≥ 30% within 3 years) | 25% | 18–35% | R5 target 20–35% |
| Ending price / start: nominal p50 (p10–p90) | 1.48 (0.75–2.82) | p50 1.25–1.70 | — |
| Ending price / start: real p50 (p10–p90) | 1.10 (0.56–2.12) | p50 0.95–1.20 | long-run real ≈ flat to slightly positive |
| Bear episodes ≥ 52 wk: median max drawdown (p75) | 34% (45%) | 28–40% | −30 to −45% bears |
| Bull episodes ≥ 52 wk: median gain (p75) | +54% (+103%) | +40–70% | doubled in ~3 yrs in 2008–11 and 2022–25 |
| Mean completed regime length bull / range / bear | 2.3 / 1.7 / 2.0 yr | 1.8–3.0 / 1.2–2.3 / 1.5–2.6 | R5 3–5 / 1–3 / 2–4; bulls end sooner here because stretch shortens them |
| Regime occupancy bull / range / bear | 46 / 27 / 28% | each ±8 pts | — |
| Jumps per year | 1.31 | 1.1–1.5 | λ 1–2/yr weekly-equivalent |
| Base rate p5 / p50 / p95 (quarterly samples) | 1.3 / 4.0 / 6.5% | p50 3.5–4.5% | prime 6.75–7.5% in 2025 |
| Inflation p5 / p50 / p95 | 1.0 / 3.0 / 5.0% | p50 2.6–3.4% | — |

Difficulty (`market.volMult`, which scales σ̄ and jump size): easy 0.85 gives pooled vol 14.1%, median max drawdown 37%, P(halve) 5.8%. Hard 1.15 gives 17.7%, 43%, 9.7%. Vol and drawdown pass bands are therefore per difficulty (10.21).

### 10.7 News feed and analysts

§10 owns the feed infrastructure and the market news. Other sections publish through `publishNews`.

```ts
interface NewsItem {
  id: NewsId; turn: number;
  kind: NewsKind;                     // 'macro.cpi' | 'macro.policy' | 'macro.cb' | 'macro.geo' | 'macro.equity' | 'macro.oil'
                                      // | 'gold.wrap' | 'gold.bigMove' | 'gold.record' | 'gold.rumor' | 'gold.regimeHint' | 'analyst'
                                      // | 'district.*' | 'competitor.*' | 'regulation.*' | 'event.*'
  tags: ('macro'|'gold'|'district'|'competitor'|'regulation'|'diesel')[];
  templateId: string; vars: Record<string, number | string | Id>;   // the UI renders text (§13); the engine stores no prose
  refs: EntityRef[]; importance: 1 | 2 | 3;
  analystView?: { analystId: AnalystId; view: 'bullish' | 'bearish' | 'mixed'; horizonWeeks: 13; targetUsd: number };
  truthful: boolean;                  // HIDDEN: false for false rumors, false regime hints and noise attributions
}
interface NewsTemplate {               // data/text/news.ts
  id: string; kind: NewsKind; importance: 1 | 2 | 3;
  vars: { name: string; type: 'usd' | 'pct' | 'bp' | 'tpa' | 'index' | 'entity' | 'pool' }[];
  variants: string[];                  // 2–4 phrasings; the engine picks an index into vars.v from the 'news' stream
}
```

**Template catalog (excerpt).** Pools (`pool`) are data lists of named causes or places; the engine stores the picked key.

| `templateId` | Vars | Rendered example |
|---|---|---|
| `macro.cpi.release` | cpiYoY, prevYoY | "Inflation runs at 3.4% year on year, up from 3.1%." |
| `macro.policy.preview` | expected (−1/0/+1) | "Markets lean toward a 25 bp hike at next week's meeting." |
| `macro.policy.move` | bp, base | "Central bank raises rates 25 bp to 4.25%." |
| `macro.cb.report` | cbTpa, prevTpa | "Central banks bought gold at a 980 t annual pace last quarter, up from 720 t." |
| `macro.geo.spike` | region (pool), geo | "Border clashes flare in the {region}; the risk index jumps to 62." |
| `macro.equity.crash` | eqPct | "Stocks plunge; funds sell gold to meet margin calls." |
| `macro.oil.move` | rack, pct4w | "A refinery outage lifts hub diesel 14% in a month to $4.10." |
| `gold.wrap` | spot, pct, driver | "Gold ends the week at $4,482 (+1.9%); the dollar was the biggest mover." |
| `gold.bigMove.attrib` | pct, driver | "Gold climbs 3.4% as the dollar slides." |
| `gold.bigMove.noise` | pct, cause (pool) | "Gold drops 3.1% in thin trade; dealers cite options expiry." |
| `gold.record` | spot | "Gold sets a record at $5,012." |
| `gold.rumor` | cause (JumpCause) | "Talk of a liquidity squeeze circulates on trading desks." |
| `gold.regimeHint` | — | "Strategists debate whether gold's trend has turned." |
| `analyst.call` | analystId, view, targetUsd | "Harrow Macro turns bearish, with a 13-week target of $3,950." |
| `competitor.bust` (§12) | companyId, claims, machines | "Ridgeback Placer files for bankruptcy; 4 claims and 11 machines head to auction." |

**Generation, step 2 (P5).** Template choice and noise come from `rng(seed,'news',turn,sourceKey)`, separate from price streams. So editing templates never changes prices (stream isolation).

| Source | Rule |
|---|---|
| Scheduled releases | CPI at weeks {2,6,10,15,19,23,28,32,36,41,45,49}; policy decision at meeting weeks; a preview the week before, with the expected move = sign of (target + N(0, 0.10 pp) − base) rounded to the 25 bp grid; CB buying at report weeks. |
| Macro shocks | geo spike or Δgeo ≥ 8; equity crash or abs(Δeq) ≥ 0.25; diesel spike/glut or abs(4-week change) ≥ 10%; any applied `applyMarketShock` (the event's own item comes from §12). |
| Big moves | abs(ret) ≥ `market.news.bigMovePct` (0.03). Attribution goes to the largest *visible* component if it carries ≥ 40% of the move with the same sign (e.g. "Gold climbs 3.4% as dollar slides"). Otherwise a noise headline is drawn from {position squaring, technical breakout, options expiry, Asian buying, fund rebalancing}, with `truthful = false`. |
| Records | `S_t > recordHigh` ("Gold hits record {spot}"). |
| Jump precursors | When next week's jump is drawn, a rumor matching its cause (and so its sign) is published with p = 0.40. False rumors, with a uniformly drawn cause, are published with p = 0.012/week. Rumors are therefore about 45% reliable. |
| Regime hints | On a hidden regime change, with p = 0.5, a direction-free item appears after U{2..6} weeks. False hints appear with p = 0.002/week, so a hint is about 60% reliable. |
| Weekly wrap | One line every week (importance 1): spot, change, the biggest visible driver. |
| Other sections | `publishNews(state, {kind, templateId, vars, refs, importance})`, e.g. §12 competitor bankruptcy or wildfire closure, §3 district staking rush or new road, §6 rule change, §11 lender policy change. These take no §10 randomness. |

**Analysts.** Three houses each publish a 13-week call every 4 weeks, staggered (offsets 0/1/2). Analysts disagree by design. After 13 weeks each call is scored: a hit if the direction matches, and "mixed" is a hit if the move was under 3%. Each house's trailing-104-week hit rate is shown, so the player can learn whom to trust. `goldMomentum26 = S_t / S_{t−26} − 1`.

| House | Signal (view = bullish if > +0.5, bearish if < −0.5, else mixed) | Hidden skill |
|---|---|---|
| Harrow Macro | `0.5·μ_regime/0.15 + m_t + N(0, 0.7)`, drawn from `rng(seed,'analyst',turn,'harrow')` | leaks the hidden regime, noisily (≈60–65% hit rate) |
| Kestrel Quant | `goldMomentum26 / 0.05` (pure momentum) | none beyond regime persistence |
| Bullion Bulletin | bullish unless `goldMomentum < −0.20` (then mixed) | perma-bull |

Target price = `S·exp(0.05·signal)`. Volume is about 150–180 items/yr, roughly 3 a week. State keeps the last `market.news.retainItems` = 300 items; prices live on in `HistorySlice`.

### 10.8 Market index and the ripple function

```
goldIdx_t      = ema13_t / referenceSpot           ema13_t = ema13_{t−1} + (2/14)·(S_t − ema13_{t−1});  referenceSpot = market.openingSpotUsdPerFineOz
goldIdxReal_t  = goldIdx_t / cpiIndex_t            // used inside every ripple form
goldMomentum_t = S_t / S_{t−52} − 1                // pre-history supplies S_{t−52} for t < 52
```

The ripple API is owned by §10 and pure. Lags of 0–52 weeks are read from the 53-entry rings; a lag outside that range is a data-validation error.

```ts
// accessors
function goldIdxAt(state, turn: number): number;       // nominal, for display and audit
function goldIdxRealAt(state, turn: number): number;   // what every ripple uses
function goldMomentumAt(state, turn: number, weeks: 26 | 52 = 52): number;
// X = base × (escalate ? cpiIndex : 1) × clamp(goldIdxReal_{t−lag} ^ elasticity, lo, hi)
function ripple(state, base: number, elasticity: number, lagWeeks: number, clampLo: number, clampHi: number,
                opts?: { escalate?: boolean /* default true */ }): { value: number; calc?: CalcNode };
const rippleRate = (state, base, e, lag, lo, hi) => ripple(state, base, e, lag, lo, hi, { escalate: false }); // §3's name
// V-shaped: rises on both sides of 1 (e.g. listings: owners cash in when gold is high, distress when low). eUp > 0, eDown < 0
// X = base × (escalate ? cpiIndex : 1) × clamp(max(x^eUp, x^eDown), lo, hi),  x = goldIdxReal_{t−lag}
function rippleTwoSided(state, base: number, eUp: number, eDown: number, lagWeeks: number, lo: number, hi: number,
                        opts?: { escalate?: boolean /* default false */ }): { value: number; calc?: CalcNode };
// additive, for rates in points: X = basePts + clamp(slope × g(x), loPts, hiPts),  g = x − 1 ('linear', default) or ln x ('log')
function rippleAdd(state, basePts: number, slope: number, lagWeeks: number, loPts: number, hiPts: number,
                   opts?: { shape?: 'linear' | 'log' }): { value: number; calc?: CalcNode };
// trend tilt: X = clamp(1 + slope × goldMomentum_{t−lag}, lo, hi)
function momentumTilt(state, slope: number, lagWeeks: number, lo: number, hi: number): { value: number; calc?: CalcNode };
// convenience: reads { form, e | slope, eDown?, lag, lo, hi, escalate?, shape? } from the owner's tuning key
function rippleDomain(state, base: number, key: RippleKey): { value: number; calc?: CalcNode };
```

**Real, not nominal (D-10.2, D-10.32).** Every ripple form raises `goldIdxReal`, never `goldIdx`. Money values apply inflation exactly once through `cpiIndex`: either inside the call (`escalate: true`) or as an explicit `× cpiIndex` factor next to an `escalate: false` call (the style §5 and §9 use); never both. Shares, rates, counts and probabilities never carry `cpiIndex`. A gold-denominated base (§5's resource value, priced at the opening spot) is money and also escalates. Using the nominal index would escalate gold-linked prices twice for inflation alone (by `cpi^e` instead of `cpi`), and would push listing and distress rates as inflation accumulates even when real gold is flat. Every consumer reads the real index: §3 (3.11 listing hazard and forfeiture), §4 (4.12), §5 (5.2 `gm`, money × `cpiIndex`), §8, §9, §11 and §12 (borrowing capacity, auction bids, respawn and junior raises are dimensionless multipliers on `goldIdxReal`). Nominal `goldIdxAt` is for display and audit only. In P1–P4 the two are identical.

**Ripple table (cross-reference).** Every row is canonical in the owning section; this table restates the owners' values so that BALANCE and reviewers have one list (D-10.45). The owner's tuning file always wins, and a disagreement between this table and the owner is a bug in this table. §10 keeps no "recommended" rows.

| Domain | Owner, key | Status | Form | Elasticity / slope | Lag (wk) | Clamp | `cpiIndex` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claim asks: acreage value | §5 `land.rippleElasAcre` | canonical | `rippleRate` (5.2 `gm`) × explicit cpi | 0.8 | 8 | 0.5–2.0 | once, explicit |
| Claim asks: resource value | §5 `land.rippleElasResource` | canonical | `rippleRate` (`gm`) × explicit cpi | 1.3 | 8 | 0.35–2.5 | once, explicit (D-10.32) |
| Royalty demand | §5 `land.royaltyRipplePts` | canonical | rippleAdd, linear | +0.06 per 1.0 of index | 13 | ±0.04 | — |
| Seller reservation | §5 `land.resMomentumSens` | canonical | 1 + 0.5 × clamp(goldMomentum, ±0.3) | 0.5 | 0 | ±0.15 | — |
| Background sales, buyer arrivals, auction bidders, stake conflicts | §5 (`land.backgroundSaleBase`, `buyerArrivalBase`, `auctionBgBidderMean`, `stakeConflictBase`) | canonical | `rippleRate` | 1.5 | 4 | 0.3–3.0 | no |
| Distressed share (of `distressedOperator` and `retiringOperator` listings) | §5 `land.distressedShareBase` (0.27) | canonical; the only distressed-share rule (§3 cedes it, 3.11) | 0.27 × `rippleRate` | −2.5 | 26 | 0.5–3.0 | no |
| Listing hazard | §3 `geology.supply.goldElasticityUp/Down` | canonical | rippleTwoSided | +0.5 / −1.5 | 8 | 1.0–2.5 | no |
| NPC forfeiture | §3 `geology.supply.lowGoldMult` | canonical | × 1.5 when `goldIdxRealAt(turn)` < 0.85 | step | 0 | — | no |
