**Cross-default and dragnet.** A loan with `crossDefault` enters default (with its own cure clock) when any other debt with balance ≥ `finance.crossDefaultThresholdUsd` ($50k) is in default or worse; it cures when the trigger cures. Cards and the owner loan carry no cross-default.

**Forbearance and restructuring.** At a default notice, a lender offers forbearance with probability `forbearanceAppetite` (bank 0.6, captive 0.6, equipFinance 0.4, hard money 0.1; × (1 + `finance.controllerForbearanceBonus` (0.2) × q) with a controller, q = §8 `controllerQuality` (11.6), i.e. × 1.2 at skill 70; cap 0.9; drawn on `rng(seed,'finance-lender',turn,loanId,'forbear')`): 13 weeks interest-only (or 50% payments), fee 1% of balance, default interest +2 instead of +3 points, a blanket lien added, and the PG reaffirmed (a limited PG becomes full). From P5 the player can counter through §5's negotiation model: `Negotiation { counterparty: { kind: 'lender', id: lenderId }, subject: 'loan', subjectRef: loanId, utilityModel: 'loanRestructure', askTerms: lender offer }` (subject names the deal, the utility model the scorer), with hidden motivation = f(FLV coverage of the balance, tier, gold stress, lender patience) passed to `resolveOffer`. Terms on the table: extension ≤ 24 months, re-amortization on a seasonal schedule, IO months, rate, deficiency settlement at a discount. Vendor payment plans use the same model with `subject: 'vendorPlan'`, `utilityModel: 'vendorPlan'` (4–12 weeks at 1%/month; P4 fixed rule for `finance/requestPaymentPlan`: accepted if reputation ≥ 30 and arrears ≤ 8 weeks old; while the plan's installments are paid, the account stays out of stop-supply and collections, and lateness stops accruing in Paydex).

### 11.15 Seasonality: the canonical northern cash curve

Costs are front-loaded in spring, gold arrives June–November, and debt service runs all year. **Worked example** (monthly sums of weekly cash, $k): the BALANCE fixture `refSmallNorthDebt` in year 2, an established season (one block stripped ahead, §7.20): $900k of fleet debt at 10% over 60 months, 427 gross recovered fine oz, a 10% in-kind lease royalty, and 384 fine oz sold through the refinery at ≈ $4,135 net with a 2-week lag (receipts $1,588k), with $400k of cash on Jan 1. Ops outflows ($1,344k/yr, the fixture's total) are payroll with burden, fuel, R&M, camp, insurance, G&A ($5k/month), fees and mobilization. About $110k of the year's R&M is winter rebuild and shop work paid in January–April: the fixture accrues R&M per operating hour, but the cash for rebuilds goes out before the season, which is what deepens the spring trough.

| Month | Ops outflows | Gold in | Debt service (level) | End cash (level) | Debt service (seasonal Jun–Nov) | End cash (seasonal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan (winter rebuilds) | 33 | 0 | 19.1 | 348 | 0 | 367 |
| Feb | 38 | 0 | 19.1 | 291 | 0 | 329 |
| Mar | 38 | 0 | 19.1 | 234 | 0 | 291 |
| Apr (rebuilds finish, early hires) | 69 | 0 | 19.1 | 146 | 0 | 222 |
| May (crew, fuel fill, mobilization) | 185 | 0 | 19.1 | **−59** | 0 | 37 |
| Jun (first cleanups settle) | 183 | 150 | 19.1 | **−111** | 38.9 | **−35** |
| Jul | 224 | 360 | 19.1 | 6 | 38.9 | 62 |
| Aug | 183 | 300 | 19.1 | 104 | 38.9 | 140 |
| Sep | 182 | 300 | 19.1 | 203 | 38.9 | 219 |
| Oct (final cleanup, bonuses) | 169 | 330 | 19.1 | 345 | 38.9 | 342 |
| Nov (winterization; last settlement) | 28 | 148 | 19.1 | 446 | 38.9 | 423 |
| Dec | 12 | 0 | 19.1 | 415 | 0 | 411 |

The operation is profitable (EBITDA ≈ $244k; cash +$15k after $229k of debt service, of which $161k is principal), yet a level schedule needs about $111k of credit by June. The seasonal schedule ($38,896.80 × 6 instead of $19,122.34 × 12) cuts the trough to −$35k for $3.9k of extra interest (cash +$11k for the year). Then the pass-through owner's April 15 and June 15 tax payments on last fall's gold (11.18) land in the same trough. This is the core cash-flow problem: profitable on paper, out of cash in June. The fixes, in rising cost: seasonal schedules (good credit, 2 seasons), a revolver with seasonal over-advance (bank, 2 profitable years), cards and vendor float (thin, 4 weeks), hard money (always, 18% effective), MCA (fatal in winter), selling ounces forward through a prepay or royalty (permanent).

### 11.16 Distress and insolvency ladder

```ts
interface DistressState {
  stage: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7; enteredTurn: number; history: { turn: number; stage: number }[];
  form: 'reorganization' | 'liquidation' | null;   // stage 7 only: an unconfirmed reorganization case, or the terminal liquidation (11.16.1)
  nextTrigger: { stage: number; text: string; week: number; amountCents: Cents } | null;   // §13 ladder widget
  missedPayrollRuns: number;            // consecutive weekly runs with net pay short by ≥ payrollShortPct (involuntary trigger)
  weeksAtStage4Plus: number;
  guaranteeDemands: { loanId: Id; amountCents: Cents; dueTurn: number; paidCents: Cents }[];
  tfrp: { assessedCents: Cents; unpaidCents: Cents; assessedTurn: number | null; pausedSinceTurn: number | null };  // paused in a case
  p1: { openSinceTurn: number | null };
  petitionDecisionId: Id | null;        // open involuntary-petition decision (11.16.1)
  liquidation: { turn: number; cause: 'filed' | 'involuntary' | 'converted' | 'p1Counter'; caseId: Id | null } | null;  // §1 16d ends the run
}
```

`distressStatus(state)` returns `{ stage, stageKey, form, nextTrigger, counterMoves, reorg, liquidation }`. `stageKey` names the stage for equality tests in other sections (`none` | `watch` | `lateVendors` | `missedLoan` | `missedPayroll` | `default` | `repossession` | `workout` | `reorganization` | `liquidation`), and `reorg` summarizes an open case (11.16.7). Numeric comparisons such as "stage ≥ 3" keep working.

The stage is the highest condition currently true (re-evaluated in step 15). A stage clears only when its condition clears; stage 3 clears 4 weeks after the last short payroll with no trust arrears. While a reorganization case is filed and not yet confirmed, the stage is 7 (`reorganization`) whatever else holds. From confirmation it is evaluated again from the conditions below, and plan installments count as loan payments (11.16.5; D-11.63). *Visible:* the stage, the next trigger, and counter-move buttons (§13).

```
nextTrigger: scan forecast13Week P50 weeks t = 1…13 (11.19.6); funds_t = endCash_{t−1} + revolver availability_t (held flat)
  first t where funds_t < payrollNet_t + taxDeposit_t        ⇒ { stage: 3, amount: payrollNet_t + taxDeposit_t, week: t }
  else first t where funds_t < that week's loan/lease dues    ⇒ { stage: 2, ... }
  else first t where funds_t < that week's vendor dues        ⇒ { stage: 1, ... }
  for stage ≥ 4: the next lifecycle milestone of the worst loan (acceleration, repossession, workout) with its week, and the week an
               involuntary trigger would fire ("Creditors' petition in 3 weeks")
  in a reorganization case: the next case deadline (adequate-protection payment, plan due, hearing); during a plan: the next
               installment and the missed payments that would convert the case (11.16.5)
text: "Missed payroll if cash < $38,400 at Wk 24 payroll" (amount = the obligations due that week ahead of payroll in priority + payroll)
```

| Stage | Enter when (any) | Automatic consequences | Counter-moves (trade-off) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 Watch | `forecast13Week` P50 ending cash < 0 within `finance.distress.watchWeeks` (6/4/3 by difficulty, §1.11; + §8 `alertBonusWeeks` for a controller or bookkeeper), or P10 < 0 within 2 | Alert (§13 `cash.projectedNegative` reads the same key); stop reason | Sell gold now (discount vs waiting for the refinery); draw the line; delay capex; cut hours; ask for a seasonal schedule; owner injection |
| 1 Late vendors | Any vendor bill ≥ 1 week past due | Finance charges; Paydex falls; stop-supply at 4 weeks | Pay down the oldest; payment plan (11.14); route to card; pay COD from cash |
| 2 Missed loan / lease payment | Any loan or lease `late` or `delinquent` | Late fees; credit marks at 4 weeks | Pay within grace; refinance with hard money (fast, 18%); sell the collateral (payoff first); voluntary surrender |
| 3 Missed payroll | Net payroll short in the last 4 weeks, or a trust deposit ≥ 1 week late | §8 morale, quits, work refusal; §12 walkout risk; reputation −8/−4; wage claims at 4 weeks; draws blocked; rescue partner offered | Owner injection (personal cash is what survives a liquidation); layoffs (§8); idle operations; sell gold, iron, claims (§5 quick sale at 0.6 × buyer value, closes next week); rescue partner |
| 4 Default | Any loan in `default` or worse; an uncured covenant event of default; MCA default | Default interest; cross-default; forbearance offers; bank setoff at acceleration | Cure; forbearance; restructure (§5 negotiation, P5); asset sales; hard-money refinance; rescue partner; file for reorganization (11.16.1) |
| 5 Repossession | A repossession scheduled or executed in the last 13 weeks | Collateral locked out, then seized and auctioned; deficiencies; guarantee demands | Sell before seizure (better price); surrender (half the repo cost); negotiate the deficiency; file for reorganization (the stay stops the seizure) |
| 6 Forced sales / workout | Accelerated debt unpaid `finance.workoutWeeks` (4) after the acceleration notice | Blanket-lien lenders liquidate gold and list claims (§5 `land.forcedSale`, reserve 50% of cost; unsold claims pass by `land.transferToCreditor`, 11.14); no new debt; capex and draws blocked | Voluntary sales at better prices; rescue partner; payoff; file for reorganization |
| 7 Bankruptcy: reorganization (P4) | The player files `finance/fileReorganization` while eligible (stage ≥ 2, debts within the Subchapter V limit, no filing in 8 years; 11.16.1), or converts an involuntary petition | Automatic stay; case costs; vendors on COD; cards and the revolver closed; credit marks; owner pay capped at the living allowance (§1 1.9); plan due in 13 weeks (11.16.2) | File the plan: term, schedule, reserve, surrenders, lease rejections, owner contribution (11.16.3); DIP loan; court-approved asset sales; owner injection; convert to liquidation |
| 7 Bankruptcy: liquidation (**game over**) | The player files `owner/fileBankruptcy` (allowed at stage ≥ 2, and at any time in a reorganization case, which converts it); **involuntary**: (a) net payroll short by ≥ `finance.bankruptcy.payrollShortPct` (25%) of that run's net for `finance.bankruptcy.missedPayrollRuns` (3) consecutive runs, or (b) stage ≥ 4 for `finance.bankruptcy.defaultWeeks` (13) consecutive weeks while V_dist (11.13, without the max) < 0, when the company is not eligible to reorganize or chooses liquidation (11.16.1); a reorganization case converts (11.16.5) | Final settlement (below); §1 end report | — |

**Final settlement at liquidation** (Chapter 7). Company assets are liquidated at distressed marks (machines at FLV, gold at local-buyer net, claims at 50% of cost). Proceeds go, in order: secured creditors (up to their collateral), administration (`finance.bankruptcy.adminCostUsd` $40,000), employee wages up to $17,150 each (R5, 11 USC 507(a)(4)), priority taxes, unsecured creditors pro rata, then equity. In a converted reorganization case, unpaid case fees and the DIP loan rank as administration (the DIP first, from its own collateral), and plan notes are claims of their class at their unpaid balances. Personal fallout follows the table below and §1.6. The same waterfall, evaluated without ending the run, is the best-interest benchmark of a reorganization plan (11.16.3).

**Personal exposure by entity** (the owner book settles these from `own.cash`):

| Exposure | Sole proprietor | LLC / corp, guaranteed debt | LLC / corp, unguaranteed debt |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deficiency after repossession or workout | Owner owes it: demand on personal cash | Guarantee demand for min(deficiency, PG cap) | Dies with the company |
| Vendor or unsecured judgments (13 weeks in collections) | Levied on personal cash | Company only, unless the vendor holds a PG | Company only |
| Trust-fund taxes unpaid 13 weeks (TFRP) | Personal | Personal | **Personal** (all entities; never discharged; a reorganization plan pays them in full and the assessment waits while it is current) |
| Unpaid wages after the bankruptcy wage priority | Personal | Personal (owner with operational control is an FLSA "employer") | Personal |
| Credit file | Every company lateness | Only charge-offs, unpaid demands, repossessions | None |
| At liquidation (game over) | Personal cash above `game.personalBankruptcyExemptionUsd` ($25k) seized; bankruptcy mark | Unpaid demands charged to personal cash; draws in the 13 weeks before the (first) filing clawed back | Clawback only |
| In reorganization (11.16) | The owner is the debtor: personal debts join the plan; personal cash above the exemption counts in the best-interest test; `bankruptcy` mark | Guarantee demand at confirmation for what the plan will not pay, unless the owner files as guarantor (the guarantee then joins the plan and the owner takes the `bankruptcy` mark); otherwise the `affiliateBankruptcy` mark | Discharged under the plan; `affiliateBankruptcy` mark |

Guarantee demands are due in `finance.guaranteeDemandWeeks` (4); they are paid automatically from personal cash as far as it goes. Any remainder becomes `own.guaranteeDue` at `finance.judgmentRate` (9%) with a `chargeOff` mark. TFRP assessments post to `own.taxDue`; any payment by either book reduces both the company's and the owner's trust liability (no double collection). Unpaid TFRP 13 weeks after assessment adds a `taxLien` mark.

**Phase 1 form** (§1.14). Any failed payment opens `p1.openSinceTurn`. It clears when every arrear is paid. After `finance.p1InsolvencyGraceWeeks` (8/6/4) consecutive open weeks, the company is liquidated (game over; P1 settlement: everything company-side is lost; the owner keeps personal cash). The UI shows "net cash" = cash − arrears as the "below zero" number. While the counter is open, `distressStatus(state).counterMoves` lists the P1 levers with their cash effect and timing (§13 shows them on the P1 health tile):

| P1 lever | Owner | Cash and timing |
|---|---|---|
| Sell gold | §10 local buyer | net at the local buyer, this week |
| Sell iron | §9 dealer sale | 0.80 × resale estimate, this week |
| Sell a claim | §5 quick sale | `land.quickSaleFrac` (0.6) × the visible buyer valuation, closes next week; liens paid at closing (`lienPayoff`) |
| Surrender a lease | §5 | stops future minimums and AMR; the paid advance is forfeited |
| Owner injection | §1 `owner/inject` | personal cash, this week |
| Cut hours or lay off | §7 plan, §8 | lower payroll from the next run |

Negotiated restructuring, forbearance and the rescue partner arrive with the full ladder (P4/P5). The P1 counter has no reorganization path: under `--rules p1`–`p3` its end is a liquidation (D-11.73).

**11.16.1 Reorganization: eligibility and filing** (P4; owner ruling 2026-10-05; D-11.17, D-11.63). The model is Chapter 11 Subchapter V (11 U.S.C. §§1181–1195), the small-business reorganization: the owner stays in control as debtor in possession, a Subchapter V trustee monitors, only the debtor may propose a plan (within 90 days), and the owner keeps the equity if the plan pays creditors the company's projected disposable income for three to five years (Subchapter V has no absolute-priority rule). An individual in business qualifies too, so a **sole proprietor** files the same case as an individual: the owner is the debtor, and the case covers the owner's personal debts. In every other entity the company files; the owner may join as a guarantor (below).

```
debtsNCL = Σ debt.* (balance + accrued interest + fees; excluding debt.ownerLoan, an insider debt) + Σ lease.* (finance leases)
         + ap.* + accrued.* + cc.cards + liab.suretyIndemnity + liab.agencyJudgment + liab.forwardDelivery
         + liab.deliveryArrears + liab.refineryAdvance + deferred.revenue.<prepay agreements>
         + sole proprietor: own.personalDebt + own.guaranteeDue + own.taxDue
         (excluded as contingent or unliquidated: liab.reclamation, guarantees with no demand, royalty-sale and stream deferred
          revenue (interests sold in the claims, not debts), operating-lease rent not yet due)
eligible ⇔ rulesAtLeast(state, 4) ∧ distress stage ≥ 2 ∧ no case open
          ∧ debtsNCL ≤ finance.reorg.debtLimitUsd (3,424,000) × cpiIndex             // the Subchapter V limit (April 2025 figure)
          ∧ no earlier filing with filedTurn > turn − finance.reorg.cooldownWeeks (416)
```
An ineligible company's only filing is liquidation (`owner/fileBankruptcy`). `reorgEligibility(state)` shows each condition, debtsNCL against the limit, the cooldown end, and the retainer.

**Filing** (`finance/fileReorganization { guarantorFiles? }`; resolved at action time; `undoable: false`, it commits to the court):
1. The retainer `finance.reorg.retainerUsd` ($15,000 × cpiIndex) is paid through `pay` (origin `player`; `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` otherwise, and the owner can inject first). The rest of `finance.reorg.filingCostUsd` ($40,000 × cpiIndex: filing fee, attorney, the trustee's case work) accrues as an administrative claim, `Dr exp.reorganization / Cr accrued.other` (memo "reorganization professional fees"), paid on the effective date.
2. The case opens: `FinanceSlice.reorg.active` (11.16.7; id prefix `reo`), status `filed`, `planDueTurn = turn + finance.reorg.planDueWeeks` (13, the 90-day deadline). Stage 7, form `reorganization`. Pre-filing claims are fixed at this turn and the automatic stay starts (11.16.2). The case stays **open** (status `filed`, then `confirmed`) until completion or conversion, so every rule that applies "while a case is open" (§1's living allowance, §6's `inPlan` handling, court approval of new credit) covers the plan period too.
3. Side effects: every vendor account goes to `cod`; card accounts close (balances become claims); the revolver commitment ends, since a lender cannot be made to extend new credit to a debtor (§365(c)(2)), and its balance is a stayed secured claim; §6 `permits.onReorganizationFiled(state)` (fines, judgments and surety indemnity become `inPlan`; surety collateral calls, §6 6.8); §1 `recordReputation(state, 'reorgFiled', caseRef)`; a `PaymentEvent { kind: 'reorgFiled' }` (§1) and the crew's morale hit through §8 `moraleShock('company', finance.reorg.crewMoraleShock)` (−10, applied in the next step 7; §11 owns the value); credit marks (11.16.6); the TFRP clock pauses; §9 holds pre-filing rental and rent-to-own recalls, and §11 calls `releaseLockout(machineId)` for every machine locked out but not yet removed (§9 9.10, D-9.56).

**Guarantor filing** (LLC or corp; `guarantorFiles: true`; D-11.72). The owner joins as a co-debtor in a jointly administered personal case. Guarantee demands are stayed and the guaranteed exposure, `own.personalDebt`, `own.guaranteeDue` and `own.taxDue` become claims in the plan; personal cash above `game.personalBankruptcyExemptionUsd` ($25,000) counts in the best-interest test (11.16.3); the owner's file takes the full `bankruptcy` mark. Without it, guarantees stay enforceable against personal cash (11.16.4). A sole proprietor is always in this position. *Trade-off:* protecting personal cash from demands costs the heavier personal mark and puts that cash in front of the creditors.

**Involuntary petition** (D-11.64). When involuntary trigger (a) or (b) of the ladder fires and no case is open, the creditors' petition is a liquidation petition, which the debtor may convert to reorganization as of right (§706(a)). An eligible company gets a **blocking** decision `finance.involuntaryPetition` (§2 `PendingDecision`, owner §11) with options *reorganize* (action `finance/fileReorganization`; an LLC or corp also gets *reorganize with the owner as guarantor*) and *liquidate* (action `owner/fileBankruptcy`, recorded with cause `involuntary`). An ineligible company is liquidated at once (`distress.liquidation`, cause `involuntary`). The ladder's `nextTrigger` counts down to either trigger, so a player can file before it.

**11.16.2 The case: the automatic stay and operating under it** (D-11.65). From the filing turn until confirmation:

| Pre-filing item | Treatment during the case |
|---|---|
| Loans, finance leases, the revolver balance, MCA, hard money, estate and carry notes, gold loans; prepay delivery schedules (11.12) | Status `stayed`: no payments, late fees, default interest, notices, acceleration, cross-default, bank setoff, repossession or forced sale; interest stops accruing (adequate protection replaces it); covenant tests stop; `resetCovenant` and `scheduleNonRenewal` are no-ops (§12 `lenderPolicy`) |
| Open bills in `debt.*`, `vendor.*`, `royalty.cash`, `tax`, `payroll.taxDeposit`, and `autoDebit` items (MCA debits, card autopay, setoff) | Status `stayed`: out of settlement; each becomes a claim. A billable obligation behind a stayed bill takes §6's status `inPlan`, so no owner evaluates it as missed (§5 lease defaults, §1 minimums); §11 settles it through the plan |
| `payroll.net` arrears and wage-claim damages | Paid on: a first-day wage order lets settlement pay pre-filing net wages up to `finance.bankruptcy.wagePriorityUsd` ($17,150) per employee (§507(a)(4)); any excess is an unsecured claim |
| `regulatory.critical` and `insurance` bills; every §6 statutory obligation | Not stayed: regulators act under their police power (§362(b)(4); §6 6.8) and coverage must be kept. The exception is §6's pre-filing fines, agency judgments and surety indemnity, which become `inPlan` and are paid through the plan |
| Pre-filing accruals not yet billed (`accrued.*` at the filing turn: income, production, property and payroll taxes, royalties, bonuses, interest) | Held as claims of their class (11.16.3) and never billed in the case; accruals after the filing are billed as usual |
| §10 forwards and their margin calls | Not stayed (the Bankruptcy Code's safe harbor for forward contracts, §556); gold-loan margin calls are stayed with the loan |
| In-kind production interests (lease royalties, royalty sales, streams, §1's Backed royalty) | Unaffected: they run with the claims and §5 settles them at every cleanup |
| §9 rentals and operating leases; §5 mineral leases | Executory contracts: rent, rental and AMR falling due after the filing are paid currently; pre-filing arrears wait for the plan to assume (cure) or reject each one |

- **Post-filing bills** are administrative expenses: payroll, payroll taxes, COD deliveries, insurance, rent, royalties and §6 amounts are paid currently in the normal priority order. They are never stayed.
- **Adequate protection** (§361, §362(d)(1)). At each month end every stayed secured loan is billed `min(claim, collateral value) × (contract rate without default or step-up points) / 12` (category `debt.secured`; `Dr exp.interest`), where collateral value is the 11.16.3 secured value. One left unpaid at the next month end lifts the stay for that lender: the loan re-enters 11.14 at `accelerated`, its collateral is repossessed on the usual clock, and its deficiency stays a claim in the case. §6's surety collateral call is also recorded as court-approved adequate protection.
- **New credit is a DIP loan only** (D-11.71). `finance/apply` accepts only `product: 'dip'` from the hard-money lender (`IN_REORGANIZATION` otherwise): amount ≤ the hard-money LTV on offered unencumbered collateral (0.60 × OLV on machines; certified claims as 11.6), at the hard-money terms (14%, 3 points, 1% exit, interest-only). The decision comes `finance.reorg.courtApprovalWeeks` (2) later and is approved whenever the collateral covers it: the court order and the collateral decide, so there is no appetite roll. At confirmation the DIP rolls into a plan-term secured note at its own rate. Until confirmation the rescue partner is not offered and `finance/seekRescue` fails (`REORG_OPEN`).
- **Sales.** Selling gold is ordinary course. Selling a claim or a machine needs court approval: §5 and §9 close it no earlier than `finance.reorg.saleNoticeWeeks` (3) after acceptance, competitors may bid in the meantime (§12), liens are paid at closing through `lienPayoff` (the secured claim falls by the payoff), and net proceeds stay in the company.
- **Owner.** From filing to completion, salary and draws are capped at the living allowance (§1 `ownerPayCapCents(state)`) with no pro-rata investor share, tax distributions continue, and injections are welcome (§1 1.9). `owner/repayLoan` fails with `REORG_OPEN` until the plan completes.
- **Distress.** Stage 7 (`reorganization`). Involuntary trigger (b) is suspended (the stay); trigger (a) and post-filing defaults convert the case (11.16.5).

**11.16.3 The plan** (D-11.66, D-11.67). Only the player files it: `finance/fileReorgPlan { termWeeks, schedule, reservePct, surrender[], rejectLeaseIds[], rejectTenureIds[], ownerContributionUsd }`, by `planDueTurn`. §11 computes everything else from visible state, and `reorgPlanPreview(state, terms)` shows the same numbers before filing. Plan years are 52-week periods from the effective date (the confirmation week).

```
Projected disposable income (§1191(d))
E'     = 0.5 · (p10FineOz + p50FineOz), seasonProductionForecast(state, every held claim, the next full season) (11.19.6)
         // current plans; net of in-kind interests; the royalty buyer's conservative basis (11.12) without the history blend
rev    = E' × §10 netSalePerFineOz at the default channel and current spot (spot flat, D-11.22)
opex   = Σ_{t = 1..52} the 11.19.6 operating outflows over the 52 weeks after the hearing, from the current plans and roster: payroll
         with burden, fuel, R&M, camp, insurance, §6 fees and bond premiums, cash royalties and minimums, production and property
         taxes, G&A and bookkeeping; excluding debt service, plan payments, stayed claims, owner items and capex
living = max(0, game.ownerLivingCostPerWeek × cpiIndex × 52 − owner salary already in payroll)
capex  = finance.reorg.capexAllowancePct (0.05) × Σ resaleEstimate of the machines the company keeps
PDI0   = rev − opex − living − capex ;   PDI = PDI0 × (1 − reservePct),  reservePct ∈ [0, finance.reorg.reserveMaxPct (0.10)]
         // the reserve is the operating cushion the court treats as reasonably necessary; income taxes are not deducted
```

| Class | Claims | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Secured, collateral kept | Each stayed secured loan, finance lease, the DIP, prepay balances and arrears, and claims secured by a production-interest lien (§1 minimum shortfalls, rescue royalties) | Allowed secured claim S_k = min(claim_k, collateral value): machines at OLV (0.80 × §9 `resaleEstimate`), claims and patented ground at §5 `planInventory` `collateralCents` (V_buyer(summary), the player's view; D-5.60), metal at spot × 0.99. A new note (`reorgSecured`) of S_k at r_c = prime + `finance.reorg.cramdownSpread` (0.020), fixed, over max(term, remaining original term) months, capped at `finance.reorg.securedMaxMonths` (84); the lien stays (§1129(b)(2)(A); a prime-plus rate, *Till*). claim_k − S_k joins the general unsecured class |
| Secured, collateral surrendered (`surrender[]`) | Same | Machines go back through §9 `repossess` as a voluntary surrender (no lockout, half the repo cost) and claims through §5 `land.transferToCreditor`; credited at the 11.14 machine proceeds (FLV × (1 − 0.075) − ½ repo cost) and, for claims, at §5 `planInventory` `collateralCents`, the value the secured class used. The rest joins the unsecured class. A machine an active mine plan uses cannot be surrendered (`COLLATERAL_IN_USE`) |
| Priority and non-dischargeable | Pre-filing income, production, property and payroll taxes (trust and employer); §6 `inPlan` fines and agency judgments | Paid in full (`reorgPriority`), level monthly over min(term months, 60 − months since filing) at baseRate + `finance.tax.underpaymentSpread` (§1129(a)(9)(C); government fines are not discharged) |
| General unsecured | Vendors, cards, MCA, unsecured notes, deficiency loans, judgments, wages above the priority, deficiencies from the secured classes, §6 surety indemnity, rejected-lease damages (§9 rentals and operating leases: `finance.reorg.leaseRejectionPct` 0.50 × remaining rent; §5 mineral leases and JVs: `planInventory` `rejectionClaimCents`, §502(b)(6)) | Pro rata share of what is left of PDI each plan year (`reorgUnsecured`), capped at the class total C_U |
| Administrative | Unpaid case fees, unpaid post-filing bills, cure amounts of assumed leases (their pre-filing arrears) | Paid in cash on the effective date |
| Insider | `debt.ownerLoan` | Subordinated: nothing while the plan runs (`owner/repayLoan` fails with `REORG_OPEN`); not discharged, so it stays a company debt, senior to equity holders' claims (§1 1.13) |
| Equity | Owner and investors | Kept (§1181(a) switches off the absolute-priority rule) |

```
Per plan year y
r_t     = finance.reorg.trusteeFeePct (0.03)
D       = PDI / (1 + r_t)                                  // reaches creditors; r_t · D is the trustee's fee
Req_y   = Σ_k reorgSecured payments in y + reorgPriority payments in y
U_y     = max(0, D − Req_y), stopping once Σ U = C_U
E0      = effective-date payments (administrative class)
feasible     ⇔ Req_y ≤ D for every plan year  ∧  E0 ≤ unrestricted cash at the hearing
PV_U         = Σ unsecured installments discounted monthly at r_c + ownerContribution
bestInterest ⇔ PV_U / C_U ≥ LV_U / C_U7                    // each general unsecured creditor gets at least its Chapter 7 dividend (§1129(a)(7))
LV_U, C_U7   = the 11.16 final-settlement waterfall evaluated now (machines at FLV, gold at local-buyer net, claims at §5 `planInventory` `liquidationCents`, cash;
               secured creditors up to their collateral at those marks; Chapter 7 administration finance.bankruptcy.adminCostUsd plus
               unpaid case fees; tax priority): what it leaves for unsecured creditors, and their claims with deficiencies at FLV.
               Sole proprietor or filing guarantor: + max(0, own.cash − game.personalBankruptcyExemptionUsd) in the waterfall.
margin       = min_y D / Req_y − 1                          // shown as "feasibility margin"
```
Unsecured installments split U_y evenly over the plan year's pay months. The schedule is `level` (every month end) or `seasonal` (the primary climate's operating months plus one, as 11.7's seasonal structure, with no eligibility test or spread add). Validation refuses a plan that fails either test now (`PLAN_NOT_FEASIBLE`, `BEST_INTEREST_NOT_MET`); the preview names the shortfall. *Levers and trade-offs:* a longer term raises the unsecured recovery and stretches the secured notes, but keeps the draw cap and the conversion risk for longer; a seasonal schedule moves payments out of the cash trough; a bigger reserve buys slack and costs vote odds; surrendering iron cuts note payments but enlarges the unsecured class and may shrink the mine plan; rejecting leases sheds rent and adds damages; an owner contribution ("new value" from personal cash, paid to unsecured creditors on the effective date) buys the best-interest test directly; and because PDI reads the current mine plans, the plan is only as good as next season's plan.

**11.16.4 Confirmation** (D-11.67). The hearing is at `hearingTurn = planFiledTurn + finance.reorg.hearingWeeks` (6); filing an amended plan before it resets the date. In step 15 of that week:
1. **Tests.** The preview is re-run on the hearing week's state (cash, spot, plans, collateral values). A failure denies confirmation; one amended plan may be filed within `finance.reorg.amendWeeks` (4), with its own hearing. A second denial converts the case.
2. **Creditor vote** (drawn at every hearing, even when step 1 fails): `u` from `rng(seed, 'finance-reorg', turn, caseId, 'vote')`.
```
rec  = PV_U / C_U ;  recL = LV_U / C_U7
w̄    = Σ_k claim_k · L_k.patience.waiverBias / Σ_k claim_k     over lenders with secured claims (bank 0.5, captive 1.0, hard money −1.0)
z    = finance.reorg.voteBias (0) + finance.reorg.voteSlope (6) · (rec − recL) + 0.5 · w̄ + 0.02 · (reputation − 50)
consensual ⇔ u < logistic(z)
```
   - **Consensual** (§1191(a)): confirmed as filed. Discharge at confirmation (§1141(d)). The trustee's service ends at the first plan payment, so the trustee fee is charged on that payment only and the saving stays with the company.
   - **Non-consensual** (cram-down, §1191(b)): confirmed anyway, because both tests passed, but the court fixes the commitment period at `finance.reorg.planWeeksMax` (260): unsecured installments run on through year 5 at U_y, while the secured notes keep their schedules. The trustee disburses every payment (fee on all), and discharge comes only at completion (§1192).
   - The player sees the vote odds as a bucket (likely ≥ 0.8 / possible 0.4–0.8 / unlikely < 0.4, as lender quotes) and every input; never z or u.
3. **Effective date** (same step): pay E0 through `pay` (origin `pipeline`, ignoring the priority reserve: a court order); move the owner contribution from `own.cash` to `eq.ownerCapital` and pay it to the unsecured class; create the plan notes as §11 loans (`reorgSecured`, `reorgPriority`, `reorgUnsecured`, each with `reorgCaseId`; first installment at the first month end ≥ 4 weeks later, 11.7); post 11.16.6's confirmation entries; run the rejections (§5 lease rejection through its surrender path with notice from this week; §9 rentals and leases returned); status `confirmed`; `PaymentEvent { kind: 'reorgConfirmed' }`.
4. **Guarantees** (LLC or corp whose owner did not file). For each guaranteed debt (loans, leases, cards, guaranteed vendor accounts), a guarantee demand for min(remaining PG cap, claim − what the plan pays it: S_k or its surrender credit, plus its pro rata share of the scheduled unsecured distributions and the owner contribution), due in `finance.guaranteeDemandWeeks` (4) under the ladder's rules: paid from personal cash, any remainder to `own.guaranteeDue` with a `chargeOff` mark. A company's bankruptcy does not discharge its guarantor.

**11.16.5 Plan period, conversion and completion** (D-11.68).
- **Installments.** Plan installments are month-end `debt.secured` bills (11.4) and include the trustee fee while the trustee disburses. One unpaid at `dueTurn + 1` is a **missed plan payment**; it stays an arrear (stage 2, the 5% late fee) until paid. The ladder runs normally from confirmation; plan notes skip 11.14's lifecycle.
- **Anniversary true-up.** At the end of each plan year except the last:
```
DI_k     = lenderEBITDA over plan year k (11.14) + Δ(gold inventory at market − inv.gold) over the year − capex − living
           // production basis: holding gold neither hides nor creates income
trueUp_k = finance.reorg.trueUpShare (0.50) × max(0, DI_k − PDI0)
```
   trueUp_k is added to the next plan year's unsecured installments, up to C_U in total. The plan commits what was projected, and half of any outperformance is shared, so a plan built on a deliberately small mine plan gains little.
- **Conversion to liquidation** (game over; `distress.liquidation.cause = 'converted'`; checked in step 15):
  1. no plan filed by `planDueTurn` (checked in that week's step 15, so the last chance to file is turn `planDueTurn − 1`, §2.6);
  2. confirmation denied twice;
  3. `finance.reorg.missedPaymentsToConvert` (2) plan payments missed within any 52 weeks, or 1 while §1's `investor.conversionMotionActive(state)` is true (a hostile equity holder's motion, §1 1.8.1; §1112(b)(4)(N));
  4. involuntary trigger (a) at any time in the case; a post-filing trust-fund deposit unpaid `finance.reorg.postFilingTaxWeeks` (4) weeks (§1112(b)(4)(I)); after confirmation, involuntary trigger (b) as well;
  5. the debtor converts: `owner/fileBankruptcy` at any time in the case (as of right, §1112(a)).

  The final settlement follows (11.16), with unpaid case fees and the DIP as administration (the DIP first, from its own collateral) and plan notes as claims of their class. The TFRP clock resumes and any unpaid trust amount is assessed at once. §1 claws back draws from the 13 weeks before the original filing (D-1.59). §11 calls `permits.onReorganizationClosed(state, 'converted')`.
- **Completion.** When every installment due within the plan term is paid: status `completed`. A non-consensual plan's remaining unsecured balance is discharged now (11.16.6). §1 records `recordReputation(state, 'reorgCompleted', caseRef)`, the draw cap and court approval end, and §11 calls `permits.onReorganizationClosed(state, 'completed')`. A secured note that runs past the term continues as an ordinary loan under 11.14.
- **New credit during the plan** needs court approval: every `finance/apply` decision takes `finance.reorg.courtApprovalWeeks` (2) longer, and lenders price the bankruptcy marks (11.16.6). Vendor accounts follow 11.10's reinstatement rule, with the 13 clean COD weeks counted from confirmation.

**11.16.6 Ledger, tax and credit** (D-11.69, D-11.70).

| Event | Posting |
|---|---|
| Retainer at filing | `Dr exp.reorganization / Cr cash.operating` |
| Rest of the case fees | `Dr exp.reorganization / Cr accrued.other` (administrative claim, paid on the effective date) |
| Adequate protection | billed as interest: `Dr exp.interest / Cr accrued.interest`, paid like any bill |
| During the case | No entry: pre-filing balances stay in their accounts at their allowed amounts. Until confirmation the balance sheet groups them as **"Liabilities subject to compromise"** (presentation only, ASC 852 style) |
| Confirmation | Rejected-lease damages are first accrued (`Dr exp.reorganization / Cr accrued.other`) and an owner contribution is paid in (`Dr cash.operating / Cr eq.ownerCapital`; owner book `Dr own.equity / Cr own.cash`). Then one transaction: `Dr` each pre-filing claim in the case (`debt.<stayed loans>` and `lease.<finance leases>` with their accrued interest and fees, `ap.vendors`, `cc.cards`, the held `accrued.*`, `inPlan` §6 liabilities, prepay `deferred.revenue` and `liab.deliveryArrears`) / `Cr debt.<reorgSecured>` (S_k each), `debt.<reorgPriority>`, `cash.operating` (the owner contribution, paid to the unsecured class), `debt.<reorgUnsecured>` (consensual: Σ scheduled U_y; non-consensual: C_U − contribution), `gain.debtDischarge` (consensual: C_U − contribution − Σ scheduled U_y; non-consensual: 0). Surrendered collateral has already left through 11.14's repossession disposition entries, and its credit reduced the claim |
| Plan installments | as loan payments (interest on secured and priority notes; the unsecured note is principal only, since its balance is undiscounted), plus the trustee fee `Dr exp.reorganization` |
| True-up (consensual) | `Dr exp.reorganization / Cr debt.<reorgUnsecured>` |
| Completion (non-consensual) | `Dr debt.<reorgUnsecured> / Cr gain.debtDischarge` for the unpaid balance (§1192; §1 D-1.60) |

- **Statements.** "Reorganization items (net)" = `exp.reorganization` − `gain.debtDischarge`, shown after interest and before tax (11.19.1). Lender EBITDA and cost per ounce exclude it. `gain.debtDischarge` is non-cash; fees are operating cash; plan principal is financing. The non-cash disclosures list debt discharged and claims converted into plan notes.
- **Tax.** The discharge gain is excluded from taxable income in a bankruptcy case (IRC §108(a)(1)(A)). At that tax year's close the excluded amount reduces tax attributes: first the NOL of the book that carries it (company for a corp, owner for a pass-through), then the tax basis of machines pro rata, floor 0 (§108(b), simplified order). Case and trustee fees are deducted as paid. Simplification: for a single-member LLC the real exclusion tests the owner's own bankruptcy or insolvency (§108(d)(6)); here it applies whenever the company's case discharges the debt.
- **Credit.**
  - Owner file: the `bankruptcy` mark (11.5 table) when the owner is a debtor (sole proprietor, or an LLC or corp owner who files as guarantor). Otherwise the `affiliateBankruptcy` mark: every business credit application asks about a principal's business bankruptcy, and the owner score stands in for that question.
  - Company file: a bankruptcy derogatory of `finance.reorg.companyDerogPts` (150) with half-life `companyDerogHalfLifeWeeks` (156), dropping off at `companyDerogMaxWeeks` (507; business bureaus keep a filing 9 years 9 months), inside `companyDerog`. Stayed trade lines stop reporting to Paydex during the case.
  - The marks, not a separate gate, keep banks away for years: at U ≈ 0 and an owner score near 600, the bank's gates and the equipment lenders' minimum appetite are out of reach, and hard money (min 60, baseAdj +60) is what remains.

**11.16.7 Data, selectors and worked example.**

```ts
interface ReorgCase {
  id: Id /* reo_ */; filedTurn: number; how: 'voluntary' | 'involuntaryConverted'; ownerIsDebtor: boolean;   // sole prop or filing guarantor
  status: 'filed' | 'confirmed' | 'completed' | 'converted';
  planDueTurn: number; plan: ReorgPlanTerms | null; planFiledTurn: number | null; hearingTurn: number | null;
  denials: number; amendDueTurn: number | null;
  claims: { secured: { loanId: Id; claimCents: Cents; collateralValueCents: Cents }[];    // fixed at the filing; values reset at each hearing
            priorityCents: Cents; unsecuredCents: Cents; adminCents: Cents; debtsAtFilingCents: Cents };
  stayedBillIds: Id[]; stayedLoanIds: Id[]; reliefLoanIds: Id[];
  adequateProtection: Record<Id, { monthlyCents: Cents; unpaidSinceTurn: number | null }>;
  confirmation: { turn: number; consensual: boolean; termWeeks: number; pdiCents: Cents; pdi0Cents: Cents; noteIds: Id[];
                  scheduledUnsecuredCents: Cents; unsecuredClaimCents: Cents; effectiveDateCents: Cents;
                  dischargedCents: Cents; trusteeOnAllPayments: boolean } | null;
  missedPaymentTurns: number[];               // plan installments missed in the last 52 weeks
  trueUps: { turn: number; cents: Cents }[];
  feesCents: Cents;                           // retainer, case fees and trustee fees to date (§1 end report)
  closedTurn: number | null;
  closeReason: 'completed' | 'planNotFiled' | 'notConfirmed' | 'missedPayments' | 'payrollCollapse' | 'postFilingTaxes'
             | 'involuntary' | 'debtorConverted' | null;
}
interface ReorgPlanTerms { termWeeks: number; schedule: 'level' | 'seasonal'; reservePct: number; surrender: CollateralRef[];
  rejectLeaseIds: Id[]; rejectTenureIds: Id[]; ownerContributionCents: Cents;
  claimTreatments: Record<Id /* tenureId */, ClaimPlanTreatment> }   // §5 5.14: one per tenure (default keep / assume), validated by
  // land.validatePlanTreatment; the single source for claims, so claim entries of surrender[] and rejectTenureIds[] are derived from it
interface ReorgSlice { active: ReorgCase | null; history: ReorgCase[] }   // FinanceSlice.reorg; closed cases kept for the run (cooldown, §1 report)
```
Selectors: `reorgEligibility(state)`; `reorgLenderExposure(state, lenderId)` → `'none' | 'caseOnly' | 'dipOnly' | 'caseAndDip' | 'postConfirmation'` (a lender whose loans are all `stayed`, plan notes or `dip` is case-only or DIP-only; §12 `lenderPolicy` skips those, D-12.48); `reorgPlanPreview(state, terms)` → { E', rev, opex, PDI0, PDI, per-year Req_y / U_y / trustee fee, E0 against cash, PV_U, C_U, LV_U, C_U7, recoveries, margin, feasible, bestInterest, vote bucket, calc }; `distressStatus(state).reorg` → { caseId, status, filedTurn, planDueTurn, hearingTurn, next installment, missed payments in 52 weeks, payments to convert (2, or 1 under §1's motion), consensual, completion turn }. Every number explains down to the claims, collateral marks and forecast lines; nothing reads hidden state.

**Worked example** (LLC, northern, P4: local buyer at $3,667 per fine oz, prime 7.0%, cpiIndex 1.00). In June of year 2, at stage 4, the company owes Northline $380,000 on an excavator and loader (40 months left on the loan; resale $420,000, OLV $336,000), Klondike $150,000 of hard money on a dozer (a balloon due in 6 months; resale $200,000, OLV $160,000), $90,000 to vendors, $22,000 on cards and $24,000 of payroll taxes. It also owns an unencumbered plant, pumps and pickup (resale $150,000) and claims that cost $60,000 (§5 `planInventory`: $50,000 going-concern, $30,000 liquidation). debtsNCL = $666,000, far under the limit. It files, paying the $15,000 retainer and accruing $25,000 of case fees. Wage arrears are paid under the first-day order.
- **Chapter 7 benchmark at the hearing** (cash $70,000): machines at FLV $462,000 + claims $30,000 + cash $70,000 = $562,000. Secured creditors take $252,000 and $120,000. Administration takes $65,000 ($40,000 plus the $25,000 of unpaid case fees) and taxes $24,000. That leaves $101,000 for $270,000 of unsecured claims (deficiencies at FLV: $128,000 and $30,000): a **37.4%** dividend.
- **Plan** (260 weeks, level, reserve 5%): E' = 0.5 × (340 + 440) = 390 fine oz, rev $1,430,130; opex $1,190,000, living $46,800, capex 5% × $770,000 = $38,500 ⇒ PDI0 **$154,830**, PDI $147,088.50, D = $142,804.37 (trustee $4,284.13 a year). Notes at 9.0%: Northline S = $336,000 over 60 months, **$6,974.81**/month; Klondike $150,000 (fully secured) over 60 months, $3,113.75; priority taxes $24,000 at 7.0% over 57 months, $496.14. Req = $127,016.40 a year, so U = **$15,787.97** a year for years 1–4 and $17,276.39 in year 5 (the tax note ends in month 57): $80,428.27 scheduled to C_U = $90,000 + $22,000 + $44,000 = $156,000. PV_U = $64,370.85 = **41.3%** ≥ 37.4%: best interest met. Feasibility margin 12.4%; E0 = $25,000 ≤ $70,000.
- A **156-week** plan fails feasibility: the notes must then run over 40 and 36 months ($9,754.13 + $4,769.96 + $741.05 a month = $183,181.68 a year > D).
- **Vote:** w̄ = (380 × 0.5 + 150 × (−1.0)) / 530 = 0.075; reputation 45: z = 6 × (0.413 − 0.374) + 0.038 − 0.10 = 0.17 ⇒ consensual **54%** ("possible"). With no reserve, U = $23,303.99 a year, PV_U $94,543.52 (60.6%), z = 1.33 ⇒ 79%, but the plan then commits every projected dollar, so any year below the projection is a missed payment.
- **Confirmed consensually:** discharge gain $156,000 − $80,428.27 = **$75,571.73** (excluded from taxable income; it reduces the NOL). The owner did not file as guarantor, so the guaranteed creditors demand what the plan will not pay them: Northline min(PG cap, $44,000 − 44/156 × $80,428.27) = **$21,315.10** and the card issuer $22,000 − 22/156 × $80,428.27 = $10,657.55 (cards always carry a PG); Klondike is paid in full. Credit: the owner's 700 falls by 120 × 0.833 = 100 to **600** (`affiliateBankruptcy`), and company U 120 falls to 0 (tier D).

### 11.17 Insurance

```ts
interface Policy {
  id: Id; line: 'equipment' | 'breakdown' | 'gl' | 'wc' | 'auto' | 'goldStorage' | 'crime' | 'pollution' | 'umbrella';
  scheduled?: { machineId: Id; insuredValueCents: Cents }[];   // equipment/breakdown/auto
  limitCents: Cents; deductible: { kind: 'flat' | 'pct'; value: number }; annualPremiumCents: Cents;
  installments: 'annual' | 'monthly'; renewalWeek: 49; status: 'active' | 'lapsed' | 'nonRenewed' | 'forcePlaced';
  claimsMult: number; marketMult: number /* 1.0, E&S 1.6 */;
}
```

| Line | Annual premium | Deductible | Covers / excludes | Required by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Equipment (inland marine) | Σ_m insuredValue_m × 0.0125 × accessMult (highway 1.00, seasonal road 1.15, winter trail 1.35, fly-in 1.60) × (1 − 0.10·[§12 fire suppression on m]) × deductibleMult × claimsMult | $2.5k (×1.10) · $10k (×1.00) · 2% of value, min $10k (×0.85) | Theft, fire, overturn, collapse, flood. **Excludes** wear and mechanical breakdown. 80% coinsurance. Camps are scheduled here. | Lenders and lessors on financed iron (loss payee) |
| Breakdown endorsement | +0.0035 × insured value | $5k | §9 sudden failures, unless component health < 0.25 at failure or PM > 50% overdue | — |
| General liability ($1M/$2M) | max($6,000, $5,000 + $15 per $1,000 of trailing-52-week payroll) × claimsMult | $5k | Third-party injury and property damage (§12) | §6, bank, lessors |
| Workers' comp | payroll/100 × rate(jurisdiction, class) × EMR; min $1,500/yr | none | Employee injury costs (§8); owner excluded | §6 (mandatory with any employee) |
| Commercial auto | $4,000 per road vehicle × claimsMult | $2.5k | Road trucks and pickups | — |
| Gold storage (specie) | `campSafe`: `finance.ins.specieCampSafeRate` 2.0%/yr × average weekly gold value at that camp × claimsMult (needs §10's `campSafe` tier, i.e. §9 `campSummary(claimId).hasSafe` from a `campSafe` item or `goldRoom`, and an assigned gold-room operator; not offered at fly-in camps); `bankBox` rider: `finance.ins.specieBankBoxRate` 0.5%/yr × average value × claimsMult; `campOpen` uninsurable | camp safe 10% of the loss, min $5,000; bank box $2,500 | Theft and fire of gold at that location; employee theft excluded (crime bond). §11 owns these rates; §10 and §12 cite the keys | — |
| Crime / fidelity bond | $2,500 (limit $100k) | $5k | Employee theft incl. high-grading (§10) | — |
| Pollution | $6,000 ($1M) | $10k | §6 discharge clean-up and third-party claims | — |
| Umbrella | $5,000 per $1M | — | Above GL and auto | — |

Metal-account gold is insured inside §10's account fee; shipments and courier moves inside §10's transit fees. Policies renew in week 49 (Dec 1), paid annually or in monthly installments (+4%); additions are pro-rated weekly. Every premium is multiplied by Σ §12 modifiers `finance.insurancePremiumMult` (insuranceHardening) at renewal. A lapse on financed iron triggers lender force-placement at `finance.ins.forcePlacedMult` 2.5× the equipment premium, added to the loan balance.

```
claimsMult(line) = clamp(1 + 0.12 · Σ_{claims last 156 wk} w − 0.03 · cleanYears(≤ 3), 0.90, 1.75),
                   w = 1 (loss < $25k), 2 (< $100k), 3 (≥ $100k)
non-renewal      : Σ w ≥ 5 ⇒ p = 0.25 per line at renewal, rng(seed,'finance-insurance',year,line); then E&S market at marketMult 1.6
EMR (WC, NCCI structure, simplified):
  window   = the three policy years ending one year before the current one (claims hit ~1 year later, for 3 years)
  E        = Σ window manual premium × finance.ins.wcElr (0.45);  Ep = 0.30 · E; Ee = E − Ep
  Ap       = Σ min(incurred_k, $20,000) · (0.3 if medical-only);  Ae = Σ max(0, incurred_k − 20,000) · (0.3 if medical-only)
  EMR      = clamp((Ap + 0.05·Ae + 0.95·Ee + 15,000) / (E + 15,000), 0.70, 2.00);  = 1.00 until average annual WC premium ≥ $5,000 over the window
```
EMR example ($45k expected losses over the window): no claims ⇒ **0.75**; one $75k lost-time claim ⇒ **1.13**; two ⇒ **1.51**; three $15k claims ⇒ **1.50** (many small claims hurt as much as two big ones, as in the real plan).

**Claims process.** Loss events arrive through `finance.handleLoss(state, loss: LossEvent)` from §9 (failures, destruction; cause `overturn` for rollovers), §10 (gold theft: `{ source: '§10', cause: 'theft', lossCents, lotIds, locationKey }`), §12 (fire, flood, theft, overturn, liability, pollution), and §8 (injury ⇒ WC: the insurer pays the incurred amount; the company feels it through EMR). Property payout = min(limit, max(0, loss × min(1, insuredValue / (0.80 × FMV)) − deductible)) (the standard coinsurance formula: the ratio applies to the loss, then the deductible). Losses at or above the player's `autoFileThresholdUsd` (default $0, so every loss) file automatically; smaller ones wait 4 weeks for `finance/fileClaim` or `finance/absorbLoss` (default absorb). *Trade-off:* filing a $12k claim nets ~$2k after the deductible but adds w = 1 to three years of claims multipliers. Settlement arrives after U{3..6} weeks (`rng(seed,'finance-insurance',turn,claimId)`) as `ar.insurance`. A destroyed financed machine's payout goes to the lender first. Accounting: write off book value (`Dr exp.casualtyLoss, Dr ppe.accumDep / Cr ppe.equipment`); the recovery credits `exp.casualtyLoss` up to the book loss and `gain.insurance` above it. Stolen gold is written off to `exp.theftLoss` at lot cost (11.19.2), and its recovery credits `exp.theftLoss` the same way. Uninsured losses and deductibles stay in `exp.casualtyLoss`; uninsured third-party claims become judgments (`accrued.other`, unsecured; personal for a sole prop).

```ts
interface LossEvent {
  id: Id /* loss_ */; turn: number; source: '§8' | '§9' | '§10' | '§12';
  cause: 'fire' | 'flood' | 'theft' | 'overturn' | 'collision' | 'contamination' | 'breakdown' | 'injury' | 'liability' | 'other';
  lossCents: Cents;                    // repair cost, destroyed book/market value, stolen gold at spot, or third-party claim
  machineId?: Id; lotIds?: Id[]; employeeId?: Id; claimId?: Id;
  locationKey?: string;                // §10 storage location of stolen or burned gold (camp safe, camp open, bank box)
  thirdParty?: boolean; pollution?: boolean; totalLoss?: boolean;
  wc?: { incurredCents: Cents; medicalOnly: boolean };          // §8 injuries
  breakdown?: { component: ComponentKey; healthAtFailure: number; pmOverduePct: number };   // §9, for the endorsement test
}
function handleLoss(state, loss: LossEvent): { state; lossId: Id };      // routes to the covering line, or uninsured
function policyCovering(state, locationKey: string): Policy | null;      // §10: active gold-storage policy for that location, else null
function fileInsuranceClaim(state, kind: Policy['line'], lossCents: Cents, ref: EntityRef)  // §12 one-shot hook
  : { state; paidCents: Cents /* approved; settles later via ar.insurance */; deductibleCents: Cents; settleTurn: number | null };
function chargeLoss(state, cents: Cents, account: AccountCode, memo: string, ref: EntityRef);  // §12: uninsured costs through pay/bill
```
Routing: cause `breakdown` → breakdown endorsement (if held and eligible); fire/flood/theft/overturn/collision on a machine or camp → equipment; theft or fire of gold → the gold-storage policy `policyCovering(state, locationKey)` returns (camp-safe policy for that camp, or the bank-box rider for that district; `campOpen` → none), or crime for employee theft; `thirdParty` → GL (auto for road vehicles); `pollution` → pollution; `injury` → WC; excess over GL/auto limits → umbrella. No covering active policy ⇒ uninsured.

Examples: a $60k fire repair on a loader with FMV $200k insured at $120k and a $10k deductible pays 60 × 120/160 − 10 = **$35k** (coinsurance penalty); insured at $180k (≥ 80% of FMV) it pays $50k. Reference-op premiums: fleet $1.0M on a seasonal road ⇒ $14.4k; GL ($365k payroll) $10.5k; WC $27.4k × EMR; two road vehicles $8k ⇒ ≈ $60k/yr.

**P2 stub** (so §6's insurance gates work before P4; D-11.59): a single "required coverage" policy satisfies §6's GL and WC proofs. It **binds automatically, with no player action**, in step 14 of the week the company first needs plan-tier coverage (it submits its first plan-tier application, or §6 first applies a GL condition), with an inbox note ("General liability bound: $8,000/yr, billed now pro rata to week 49, then each week 49"). GL is `finance.ins.p2GlFlatUsd` $8,000/yr (category `insurance`; 4 weeks unpaid ⇒ lapse, §6 closes the gate); WC stays inside P1's flat 0.08 × payroll burden, so `insuredStatus` reports WC covered whenever payroll runs. No claims process; losses are uninsured until P4. `finance/setCoverage` arrives with the full insurance system in P4.

### 11.18 Taxes

Simplified, U.S. 2026 rules (R5) in year-1 dollars × `cpiIndex`. Tax year = calendar year; single filer; the owner has no outside income (D-11.19).

```ts
type TaxJurisdictionId = JurisdictionId;   // alias of §3's one type ('akStyle' | 'nvStyle' | 'temperateStyle' | 'yukon'; D-3.46), District.jurisdictionId; §8 payroll, §9 sales tax use the same key
interface TaxJurisdiction {
  id: TaxJurisdictionId;
  corpBrackets: { upTo: number; rate: number }[];       // state corporate income tax
  personalIncomeRate: number;                           // state tax on the owner's pass-through or salary/dividend income (flat)
  sutaRate: number; suiWageBase: number; suiEmployeeRate: number; mbtRate: number;
  wcRates: { mining: number; clerical: number };        // $ per $100 payroll
  productionTax: 'akLicense' | 'nvNetProceeds' | 'none';   // government royalties (AK state land, Yukon export) are §6 interests, not taxes
  propertyTax: { equipmentOnBook: number };            // patented land uses §5 land.patentedPropertyTaxRate × assessedValue
  currency: 'USD' | 'CAD';                              // CAD amounts convert at §10 market.cadToUsd (0.72)
}
```

§3 maps region templates to jurisdictions on `District.jurisdictionId`: `northernFederal` and `alaskaState` → `akStyle`, `aridFederal` → `nvStyle`, `temperateFederal` → `temperateStyle`, `yukon` → `yukon` (D-11.30, D-11.55).

| | `akStyle` (northern U.S. and Alaska-state districts) | `nvStyle` (arid districts) | `temperateStyle` (OR/ID/MT-style, P6 content) | `yukon` (P6) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Personal income tax (state) | none | none | 5.5% flat on the owner's taxable income [M] | federal + territorial (P6) |
| Corporate income tax | 0% ≤ $25k; 2% ≤ $49k; 3% ≤ $74k; 4% ≤ $99k; 5% ≤ $124k; 6% ≤ $148k; 7% ≤ $173k; 8% ≤ $198k; 9% ≤ $222k; 9.4% above (× cpiIndex) | none | 6.5% flat [M] | 9% combined ≤ C$500k (small business), 27% above |
| SUTA / wage base / employee SUI | 2.0% / $51,700 / 0.5% | 2.95% / $41,800 / 0 | 2.5% / $50,000 / 0 [M] | CPP/EI instead of FICA (P6) |
| Other payroll | — | MBT 1.853% of quarterly wages > $50k | — | — |
| WC rate mining / clerical | $7.50 / $0.25 | $4.00 / $0.20 | $6.00 / $0.25 [M] | C$3.00 (WCB) |
| Production tax | Mining license tax (below), 3.5-year new-operation holiday | Net proceeds of minerals (below) | none | none (the C$0.375/oz export royalty is §6's `governmentRoyalty` interest, settled at sale through §10) |
| Property tax | equipment 0 (unorganized borough); patented land per §5 | equipment 1.0% of book value; patented land per §5 (`land.patentedPropertyTaxRate` 0.9% × assessed value) | equipment 1.0% of book value; patented land per §5 | — |

A company with production in several jurisdictions apportions taxable income to each by its share of `rev.gold` (single sales factor) and applies each jurisdiction's state rates to its share.

**Federal income tax by entity.**

```
TI_biz = book pre-tax income
       + exp.depreciation − tax depreciation      + exp.depletion − tax depletion
       + reclamation provision & accretion − reclamation costs performed (the reclaim reclass, 11.19.3)
       + exp.fines (non-deductible) + book gain on disposals − tax gain on disposals
       − gain.debtDischarge (excluded in a bankruptcy case, IRC 108(a)(1)(A); attributes reduced at year end, 11.16.6)
       + C-corp only: 0.30 × exploration & development expensed this year − Σ_pools pool × monthsAmortizedThisYear / 60   (§291(b))
       (inventory: tax follows book absorption; interest fully deductible under the small-business §163(j) exemption;
        exploration (cost center prospecting) and pre-production stripping are deducted as incurred, §617/§616;
        royalty sales, streams, and prepays follow book: a production payment is a loan for tax (§636), so neither the
        upfront cash nor the in-kind deliveries are income or deductions beyond the deferred-revenue drawdown)
C-corp      : stateTax = brackets(TI); fedTax = 0.21 × max(0, TI − stateTax − NOLused);  NOLused ≤ 0.80 × (TI − stateTax)
              owner (owner book, week 15): brackets2026(max(0, salary − stdDed)) + finance.tax.dividendRate (0.15) × dividends
              + j.personalIncomeRate × (max(0, salary − stdDed) + dividends) − salary withholding (11.3); a negative balance is refunded
Pass-through: SE = 0.153 · min(0.9235·TI, ssWageBase) + 0.029 · max(0, 0.9235·TI − ssWageBase)   (TI > 0)
(sole prop,   AGI = TI − SE/2;  QBI = 0.20 · max(0, AGI − stdDed);  TIp = max(0, AGI − stdDed − QBI)
 LLC)         tax = brackets2026(TIp − NOLused) + SE + j.personalIncomeRate × max(0, TIp − NOLused), paid from the OWNER book;
              losses become the owner's NOL (80% rule)
brackets2026 (single): 10% ≤ 12,400 · 12% ≤ 50,400 · 22% ≤ 105,700 · 24% ≤ 201,775 · 32% ≤ 256,225 · 35% ≤ 640,600 · 37% above; stdDed 16,100
```
At typical profits ($100–250k) the pass-through marginal rate is 22–32% plus SE tax, which replaces §1.6's flat `finance.passThroughRate` (24–32% simplified; D-11.18).

**Return preparation** (`finance.tax.entityReturnPrepUsd`, × cpiIndex; billed week 10 to `exp.ga`, category `vendor.other`): sole proprietor **$0** (the business is a schedule on the owner's personal return, no company return); single-member LLC **$0** (disregarded entity, §1.6) rising to $1,500 while an equity holder makes it multi-member (partnership return); corp $3,000. This is one of the sole proprietor's concrete edges (§1.6, D-11.52), with the owner-file credit rule in 11.5; it keeps full personal recourse in exchange.

**Worked example** (one property bought for $50k (adjusted basis $50k), TI before depletion $230k, gross income from the property $1.70M): percentage depletion = min(0.15 × 1.70M, 0.50 × 230k) = $115k (cost depletion $10k). *Pass-through:* TI = $115k; SE $16,249; AGI $106,876; QBI $18,155; TIp $72,620; income tax $10,688 ⇒ **$26,937, paid by the owner**. *C-corp (AK):* §291 cuts 20% of the excess over basis, 0.20 × (115k − 50k) = $13k ⇒ depletion $102k, TI = $128k; state $3,720 + federal 0.21 × (128,000 − 3,720) = $26,099 ⇒ **$29,819, paid by the company**; an $80k dividend then costs the owner another $12,000. After the 3.5-year holiday, add the AK license tax: $5,050 on the pass-through's N = $115k, $5,960 on the corp's N = $128k.

**Estimates and payments.** Individuals: weeks 15, 24, 37, and 3 of the next year. Corps: weeks 15, 24, 37, 50. Return and balance due week 15. Method (`finance/setEstimateMethod`): `safeHarbor` (default; 25% of prior-year tax per installment, ×1.10 if prior AGI > $150k; individuals owe no estimates if the prior full year's tax was zero, so year 1 has none) or `annualized` (installment_k = max(0, tax(YTD income × f_k) × {22.5, 45, 67.5, 90}%[k] − paid so far); individuals f = {4, 2.4, 1.5, 1.0} for periods ending weeks 13/22/35/52; corps f = {4, 2.4, 1.5, 1.0909} for periods ending weeks 13/22/35/48). Underpayment interest: baseRate + 3% on each shortfall until paid. *Trade-off:* safe harbor is predictable; annualized defers payments to when the gold actually arrives. Pass-through taxes are the owner's: `taxDistributionPolicy: 'auto'` (default) draws each payment from the company in its due week (pro rata with an equity investor, §1); distributions are blocked at distress ≥ 3, so the owner pays from savings or accrues interest (in a reorganization case they continue, §1 1.9).

**Depreciation (tax).** Elected per tax year before week 52 (`finance/setDepreciationElection`): `bonus100` (default; 100% bonus is permanent for property acquired after 2025-01-19, which covers every in-game purchase; inherited property (§1.8.2) takes a stepped-up basis = the estate appraisal and is not bonus-eligible, so it uses MACRS) or `macrs` (GDS half-year: mining equipment, asset class 10.0, 7-year 14.29/24.49/17.49/12.49/8.93/8.92/8.93/4.46%; light trucks 5-year 20/32/19.2/11.52/11.52/5.76%; §9 supplies each machine's class). §179 is not modeled separately (D-11.20). Disposals: tax gain = proceeds − adjusted tax basis, all ordinary (§1245 recapture); a repossession is a disposal at net proceeds. Finance-leased machines are depreciated by the lessee; operating-lease rent is deducted. Book depreciation is §9's schedule. *Trade-off:* bonus zeroes this year's tax, but the NOL only offsets 80% later and selling the iron in a crisis creates taxable income with no cash.

**Depletion** (tax property = claim):
```
GIFP_c = rev.gold attributed to claim c (already net of in-kind royalty oz, §5 D-5.12) − exp.royaltyCash on c
TIP_c  = taxable income from c before depletion (direct + allocated costs per 11.19.4)
pct_c  = min(0.15 · GIFP_c, 0.50 · max(0, TIP_c))
cost_c = adjTaxBasis_c · ozSold_c / (ozSold_c + remainingRecoverableFineOzP50_c)    // player's §4 estimate; none ⇒ basis/5 per year
taxDepletion_c = max(cost_c, pct'_c);  pct'_c = pct_c − (C-corp ? 0.20 · max(0, pct_c − adjTaxBasis_c) : 0)   (§291)
                 basis falls by depletion taken, floor 0
book depletion = the cost formula on book basis (units of production)
```

**Production taxes** (all deductible; posted `Dr exp.taxesOther / Cr accrued.taxesOther`):
- **AK mining license tax** on N = AK mining net income (after depletion, before NOL): 0 if N ≤ $40k; 3% of N if ≤ $50k; $1,500 + 5% of (N − 50k) if ≤ $100k; $4,000 + 7% of (N − 100k) above. Exempt for 182 weeks (`finance.tax.akLicenseHolidayWeeks`) from the company's first cleanup in an `akStyle` district. Due week 18. §11 owns these brackets and the holiday rule; §6 cites them (its P6 Alaska license registration only records the license).
- **NV net proceeds**: NP = NV gold revenue − direct mining, processing, transport, and refining costs − depreciation of assets used (G&A, interest, royalties, income taxes not deductible). Rate by NP/gross: < 10% 2.0 · 10–18 2.5 · 18–26 3.0 · 26–34 3.5 · 34–42 4.0 · 42–50 4.5 · ≥ 50% 5.0; NP > $4M ⇒ 5% flat. Annual, due week 7 of the next year. Example: gross $1.9M, costs $1.3M ⇒ NP $600k, ratio 31.6% ⇒ 3.5% ⇒ **$21,000**.
- **Federal land:** no royalty. **AK state-land 3% net-income royalty** and **Yukon export royalty**: P6, created by §6 as `governmentRoyalty` interests. §11 settles every `trigger: 'annual'` cash interest at week 52 (accrued to `accrued.royalties`, due week 18, category `royalty.cash`, with §6's rental credit); `sale`-triggered ones (Yukon export) settle through §10.
- **Property tax:** equipment at the jurisdiction's rate × book value of machines located in the district at week 26 (NV 1.0%), plus §5's patented-land tax (`land.patentedPropertyTaxRate` × `assessedValueCents`) in every U.S. jurisdiction; billed week 26, due week 35.
- **Tax audits** (§12 `taxAudit` calls `applyTaxAudit(state, { pct, feesCents })`): fees post to `exp.ga`; the adjustment adds `pct` × prior-year TI to that year's TI, the extra tax is recomputed with that year's rules (from `tax.priorYear`), and interest at baseRate + 3% runs from week 15 of the following year; due in 4 weeks (category `tax`; owner book for pass-through). Returns `{ state, extraTaxCents, interestCents, dueTurn }`.

### 11.19 Reports

All reports are pure selectors over the ledger for a period (§13 period selector), each line explainable down to postings.

**11.19.1 Income statement.**

| Line | Accounts (cost center) |
|---|---|
| Revenue | `rev.gold` |
| Hedging gain (loss) | `inc.hedgeGainLoss` (§10, P5) |
| Site labor & staffing | `exp.wages` + `exp.payrollTax` + `exp.workersComp` + `exp.staffing` (site) |
| Fuel · Repairs & parts · Camp & consumables · Rentals & operating leases · Mobilization · Refining, assay & gold handling | `exp.fuel` · `exp.parts` + `exp.repairsContract` · `exp.camp` + `exp.consumables` · `exp.rental` + `exp.opLease` · `exp.mobilization` · `exp.refiningAssay` + `exp.goldHandling` (site) |
| Royalties (cash) · Production & property taxes · Site insurance, permits & bond premiums, claim fees | `exp.royaltyCash` · `exp.taxesOther` · `exp.insurance` + `exp.permitsFees` + `exp.claimFees` (site) |
| Change in gold inventory | `exp.inventoryChange` |
| **= Cash cost of sales** | sum of the above |
| Depreciation & depletion | `exp.depreciation` + `exp.depletion` (site) |
| **= Mine operating income** | |
| G&A | every expense with cost center `ga` |
| Exploration | cost center `prospecting` |
| Reclamation | `exp.reclamationProvision` + `exp.reclamationAccretion` |
| Other operating | `exp.fines` + `exp.casualtyLoss` + `exp.theftLoss` + `exp.inventoryWritedown` − `gain.insurance` |
| **= Operating income (EBIT)** | |
| Interest & finance fees | `exp.interest` + `exp.financeFees` |
| Reorganization items (net) | `exp.reorganization` − `gain.debtDischarge` (11.16.6; only in a run with a case) |
| Other income | `inc.interest` + `inc.other` + `gain.assetSale` |
| **= Pre-tax income** → Income tax (`exp.incomeTax`, corp) → **Net income** | Memo: owner's pass-through tax (owner book) |
| Memo | EBITDA (EBIT + D&D), lender EBITDA (11.14), in-kind royalty oz × spot, fine oz produced / sold |

**11.19.2 Gold inventory valuation** (D-11.7): absorption cost with lower of cost or net realizable value, plus a market column.
```
pool_c : for every week with WeekOpsResult.payWashedBcy_c > 0 (§7), all site expense lines tagged claim c — direct, machine costs and
         depreciation by hours on c, depletion, shared site costs allocated per 11.19.4 — accumulate from c's previous cleanup
pool close (step 14c, after this week's payroll and cost lines are posted) for each claim cleaned up this week in step 12:
         the lots §10 created from that cleanup share pool_c pro rata by est. fine oz → §10 GoldLot.costBasisCents
         (in-kind royalty/stream oz never become lots and carry no cost; high-graded gold is a loss inside the pool);
         Dr inv.gold / Cr exp.inventoryChange;  pool_c = 0
sale / delivery / forced sale: Dr exp.inventoryChange / Cr inv.gold at costBasis × (fine oz sold ÷ lot est. fine oz); a §10 split
         (parentLotId) divides cost the same way; a lot sold in step 12 of the week it was made is costed and released together in 14c
metal account (§10 toAccount): the refined oz stay in inv.gold at the source lots' cost (sub-ledger "metal account"); account fees → exp.goldHandling
theft (§10 status 'stolen'): Dr exp.theftLoss / Cr inv.gold at cost; any insurance recovery follows 11.17
weeks without washing: costs stay period expenses (idle capacity and pre-washing stripping are not inventoried)
LCNRV, month end: if cost/fine oz > §10 netSalePerFineOz(lot) ⇒ Dr exp.inventoryWritedown / Cr inv.gold (never written back up)
```
The BS shows inventory at cost with a memo column at market (est. fine oz × `netSalePerFineOz`); net worth uses market (§1.13). Example: a cleanup closes a $70,000 pool on 22.0 retained fine oz ⇒ $3,182/oz at cost vs $4,116/oz at refinery net: the BS carries $70,000 (market memo $90,550), and the margin hits the P&L only when the gold is sold.

**11.19.3 Reclamation liability** (D-11.8).
```
ARO_t = Σ_c §6 ReclamationLedger.liabilityCents_c       (own-contractor cost incl. mobilization and +15%, × cpiIndex: undiscounted current cost)
weekly (step 14c, from §6's step-13 deltas):  accretion_c = ARO_{c,t−1} × (cpiIndex_t / cpiIndex_{t−1} − 1) → exp.reclamationAccretion
                                              the rest of ΔARO_c (new disturbance, estimate revisions)   → exp.reclamationProvision
reclaim work: each §7 OpsCostLine carries reclamationShare r; §11 posts (1 − r) × cents with cost center 'site' and r × cents with
              cost center 'reclaim'; reclaim crew hours (§8) and §9 machine costs on reclaim hours are tagged 'reclaim' the same way.
              At week end §11 reclasses the week's 'reclaim' costs: Dr liab.reclamation / Cr those expense accounts, capped at the
              claim's carrying amount (excess stays expense); when §6 reduces the liability for finished acres, the reduction beyond
              the reclassed cost reverses through exp.reclamationProvision (the "gain" of reclaiming with your own iron, §6.8)
forfeiture (§6): Dr liab.reclamation (the claim's carrying amount) / Cr cash.restricted.bond or deposits.bonds (the forfeited bond);
              a difference posts to exp.reclamationProvision; surety forfeiture adds Cr liab.suretyIndemnity; agency excess adds
              Cr liab.agencyJudgment
```

**11.19.4 Per-claim P&L allocation rules.**

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Revenue | The lot's claim; deferred-revenue drawdowns to the delivering claim; company-wide interests by each claim's share of fine oz |
| Direct costs | Ledger lines carrying `claimId` |
| Machine costs (fuel, parts, depreciation, rental, lease) | By machine hours on each claim in the period; zero-hour periods to the claim where the machine sits; off-season shop work to "Unallocated site" |
| Labor | By employee hours per claim (§8 assignment); unassigned crew to "Unallocated site" |
| Shared site costs (camp, power, support vehicles) in a district | By person-days on each claim |
| Company overhead (cost center `ga`) | By share of `payWashedBcy` in the period (fallback: direct-cost share); shown as a separate "allocated overhead" line, so each claim shows contribution and after-overhead result |
| Not allocated ("Company" column) | Interest and finance fees, income tax, gains/losses on equipment sales, due diligence on unowned ground |
| Depletion; in-kind royalty value | The claim's own; memo at spot |

**11.19.5 Cost per ounce** (World Gold Council-style, simplified; D-11.21). Denominator: **gross recovered fine oz** in the period (before in-kind royalties; assayed fineness where known, else the estimate).
```
Cash cost/oz = [ site operating costs (site labor, fuel, repairs & parts, camp & consumables, rentals & operating leases, mobilization,
                 refining & assay, site insurance, permits, claim fees, bond premiums) + production & property taxes + cash royalties
                 + in-kind royalty and stream oz × spot at cleanup − stream ongoing cash received ] / grossFineOz
AISC/oz      = cash cost + [ G&A + reclamation provision & accretion + sustaining exploration (on producing claims)
                 + sustaining capex (cash plus financed principal of sustaining purchases) + finance-lease principal ] / grossFineOz
AIC/oz       = AISC + [ interest & finance fees + growth capex + other exploration ] / grossFineOz
Excluded     : income taxes, claim acquisitions, depreciation & depletion (capex replaces them), inventory changes,
               reorganization items (11.16.6)
Sustaining   : a purchase after which the class count ≤ the class's maximum count over the previous 52 weeks (a replacement);
               otherwise growth. The player can re-tag.
```
Example (`refSmallNorthDebt`, year 2, as in 11.15): 427 gross fine oz; site costs $1,284k (11.15's $1,344k of ops outflows less $60k of G&A); 42.7 royalty oz × $4,200 = $179k ⇒ **cash cost $3,427/oz**; + G&A $60k, reclamation $25k, sustaining capex $90k, sustaining exploration $15k ⇒ **AISC $3,872/oz**; + interest $68k (year 2 of the $900k loan; no growth capex in a steady year) ⇒ **AIC $4,032/oz**, against $4,200 spot and ≈ $4,135 refinery net. The thin all-in margin is the reference op's lesson: royalties and debt service decide the season.

**11.19.6 13-week cash forecast** (`forecast13Week`; method D-11.22). Start = `cash.operating + cash.reserve`; weeks t = 1…13; spot held flat (no price forecast); label "Uses your estimates and current plans". In a reorganization case, `stayed` bills and loans are left out of the outflows; adequate-protection bills, case fees and plan installments are in them (11.16).
```
inflowsSched(t) = refinery AR settling in t + insurance settlements + committed asset-sale proceeds + stream ongoing payments
inflowsProd_k(t) = Σ_claims Σ_cleanups settling in t: fineOz_k × netPerFineOz(claim's default channel, current spot)
   (cleanups per plant line from §7 productionForecast(…).cleanups, one entry per line cleanup with its lineId (each PlantLine has its own cleanupEveryWeeks); settlement lag 0 for the local buyer, §10's refinery lag otherwise; standing order decides the channel)
   fineOz_50 = Σ_weeks in the cleanup interval: §7 productionForecast(…, [claimId]).byWeek p50FineOz (the claim's plan)      // all phases; already net of in-kind interests
   fineOz_k (k = 10, 90; P4+) = Σ_weeks in the cleanup interval: washBcy(w) × tp_k × grade_k × recoveryEst × finenessEst × (1 − inKindShare)
   washBcy(w) = §7 projectOpsVisible(state, claimId).payWashedBcy × open_k(w)   // representative week from visible inputs only;
                open_k(w) = 1 if w is an operating week under §1's season forecast (freeze-up P50; P10 for k = 10, P90 for k = 90), else 0
   tp_k = 1 + z_k · finance.fc.throughputSigma (0.15), z = −1.2816 / 0 / +1.2816
   grade_k = volume-weighted §4 BlockEstimate gradeP10 / gradeP50 / gradeP90 over the planned cut's blocks     // comonotonic: a conservative band
   recoveryEst = projectOpsVisible's recovered ÷ contained ratio (player's estimated size mix);  finenessEst = §10 claimFineness value
   inKindShare = Σ in-kind ProductionInterest rates on the claim (§5), with step-downs applied at their thresholds
outflows(t) = payroll (roster × planned hours, burden, deposit lag) + fuel (§7 preview gal × delivered price, on vendor terms)
            + R&M (§9 expected $/h × planned hours; P3: + Σ hazard × expected repair cost) + camp (person-days × rate)
            + open bills by due week + debt service, lease and card dues + §6 obligations with amounts + insurance installments
            + tax installments + owner salary/draws/tax distributions + committed capex balances due
endCash_k(t) = start + Σ_{s ≤ t} (inflowsSched + inflowsProd_k − outflows)          k ∈ {P10, P50, P90}
memo lines: revolver availability; gold on hand at local-buyer net "if sold now" (held gold is not assumed sold unless a standing order exists)
output also: productionByClaim = { claimId, week, washBcy (P50), fineOz (fineOz_50) }[] over the 13 weeks
```
The P50 line is §7's `productionForecast` in every phase; the P10/P90 lines use the band formula (grade, throughput and freeze-up moved together), and each week's production is clamped so that P10 ≤ P50 ≤ P90.

**P1–P3 version** (D-11.49): scheduled outflows (payroll at current hours, fuel at the 4-week average, fixed loan payments, open bills) plus known receipts, **plus the P50 production line**: each planned cleanup in the next 13 weeks adds `fineOz_50` (Σ §7 `productionForecast` p50 over the weeks since the previous cleanup) × §10 `netSalePerFineOz` at the local buyer and the flat P1 price, in its cleanup week (the local buyer is the only channel before P5, settled the same week). One series (P10 = P50 = P90); shows runway; §13 labels the line "incl. planned cleanups (P50)" under "Uses your estimates". The P10–P90 band arrives in P4.

**Season baseline.** §13 owns the "production vs plan" baseline (UI-only `UiPersisted.baselines`, `ui/rebaseline`, D-13.30; D-11.48). §11 keeps no baseline state and has no rebaseline action. From P4 §13 may build its snapshot from `forecast13Week(state).productionByClaim`.

**Season production forecast** (`seasonProductionForecast(state, claimIds, year) → { p10FineOz, p50FineOz }`; used for royalty and stream offers and the hedging covenants; named so it never collides with §1's `seasonForecast(state, districtId)`, which forecasts breakup and freeze-up dates): Σ of §7 `productionForecast(…, claimIds).byWeek` p10FineOz and p50FineOz over every week of that year's season (the next season if the current one has ended), restricted to the plans on `claimIds`, with the player's current plans held fixed; §7 already nets in-kind interests and uses the P10 season length for P10. No cash lines.

**11.19.7 Balance sheet, cash flow, debt schedule.**
- **Balance sheet.** Current assets: cash (operating + reserve), refinery receivables, insurance and other receivables, gold inventory (cost; market memo), parts and fuel, prepaid. Non-current: restricted cash, bond deposits, equipment net, mineral properties net.
