Current liabilities: AP, accrued payroll and payroll taxes, accrued taxes, accrued royalties/interest/other, surety indemnity and agency judgments, forward close-outs owed, refinery advances, cards, revolver, current portion of debt (principal due in the next 52 weeks), current finance-lease liabilities, delivery arrears, current deferred revenue (expected deliveries in 52 weeks at spot, capped). Non-current: long-term debt, finance leases, owner loan (subordinated), deferred revenue, reclamation liability. Equity: owner capital, investor equity, retained earnings, current-year income, distributions. Memo: gold at market, operating-lease commitments, contingent guarantee exposure, forward-book MTM (§10). While a reorganization case is open and unconfirmed, the stayed pre-filing balances are grouped in one line, "Liabilities subject to compromise" (presentation only; 11.16.6). Check line: assets = liabilities + equity to the cent.
- **Cash flow (indirect).** Operating: net income + D&D + reclamation provision/accretion + write-downs and casualty book loss − gains − reclaim spending − deferred-revenue drawdowns ± Δ working capital. Investing: − cash capex (price − financed portion) − claim acquisitions + asset-sale proceeds ± Δ restricted cash and bond deposits. Financing: + loan proceeds − principal ± revolver ± cards − finance-lease principal + owner/investor contributions ± owner loans − distributions + royalty/stream/prepay receipts − loan fees. Insurance settlements are operating (they clear `ar.insurance`). Non-cash disclosures: financed purchases, lease additions, repossessions, in-kind deliveries, and in a reorganization the claims converted into plan notes and the debt discharged. Check: Σ = Δ(operating + reserve) ⇒ "Reconciles ✓".
  *Construction rule* (so the statement always reconciles; `deferred.revenue` counts as class F here and equity accounts as F). (1) **Direct CF**: a txn's lines on `cash.operating`/`cash.reserve` are investing or financing if the txn has any class-I or class-F line (the larger of the two wins), otherwise operating. A txn is **non-operating** if its cash is investing/financing, or if it has no cash line and contains any class N, I, or F line (depreciation, depletion, provision, accretion, reclaim reclass, write-downs, casualty write-offs, repossessions, deferred-revenue drawdowns, insurance-recovery accruals, financed purchases). (2) **Indirect CFO** = net income − Σ P&L effect of non-operating txns (this removes D&D, provisions, gains, netted loan fees, drawdowns) + Σ ΔW of operating txns (class-W lines; asset increase = use of cash). `exp.inventoryChange` is class O, so absorption costing reaches CFO only through Δ`inv.gold`. Capex is always paid through `pay` at closing, never billed to AP. (3) A property test asserts indirect CFO = direct CFO and CFO + CFI + CFF = Δ(operating + reserve) for every period.
- **Debt schedule.** Per instrument: lender, product, original, balance, rate incl. step-ups, schedule kind, payment, next due, maturity, collateral, guarantee, covenant status, cross-default flag; next 12 months' principal and interest by month; year-end balance; total debt service next 12 months; operating-lease commitments; contingent guarantee exposure.

### 11.20 Net worth

`netWorth(state, mode)` with `mode ∈ 'scoring' | 'book' | 'appraised'`.
- **`scoring`** implements §1.13 with every §11 account placed:
```
companyNW = cash.operating + cash.reserve + cash.restricted.* + deposits.bonds + prepaid
          + ar.refinery + ar.insurance + ar.other                         // at settlement value
          + Σ unsold lots: est. fine oz × §10 netSalePerFineOz(lot)        // lots only (camp, bank box, transit, refinery)
          + §10 metalAccountValueForScoring(state)                          // metal-account oz at spot × (1 − bid spread); pledged metal included
          + inv.parts × game.nw.partsResaleFactor (0.6) + inv.fuel (at cost)
          + Σ owned / financed / finance-leased machines: §9 resaleEstimate(machine)
          + mineral.properties − mineral.accumDepletion                     // claims at cost basis
          − ( ap.* + accrued.* + cc.cards + Σ debt.* principal + Σ lease.* + liab.reclamation (carrying value = §6 real-cost
              estimate, not bond face) + liab.suretyIndemnity + liab.agencyJudgment + liab.forwardDelivery + liab.deliveryArrears
              + liab.refineryAdvance + Σ deferred.revenue.* + §10 forwardMtmLossForScoring(state) )
ownerNW   = companyNW − Σ investorClaim (§1.8.1, each equity agreement) + own.cash − own.personalDebt
          − own.guaranteeDue − own.taxDue + own.loanToCompany            // debt.ownerLoan is in companyNW's debts, so it nets to 0
```
  Operating-lease commitments are excluded (as in §1's debt definition). `own.guaranteeDue` and `own.taxDue` are §11 additions to §1.13 (they are zero unless a demand or TFRP assessment exists). A reorganization adds no term: stayed claims stay in their accounts, plan notes are `debt.*`, and discharged claims leave only at the discharge (consensual: confirmation; non-consensual: completion; 11.16.6, §1 D-1.60), so filing alone never raises net worth.
- **`book`**: statement equity + the owner book's equity (shown on the BS screen), computed as total assets − liabilities on both books, contra assets included.
- **`appraised`** (information only): `scoring` with claims at the player's P50 value (§4/§5). Until §4 and §5 can value claims at P50 (P1), it equals `scoring`.
- **P0 form** (D-11.75): `scoring` uses ledger marks only. The lot, metal-account, machine-resale and forward-MTM terms and the investor waterfall are zero until §10, §9 and §1 hold those records, which is exact for a P0 game.

Contingent guarantees are not subtracted until a demand exists (they are shown as a memo). Hidden truth is never read (property test, §1.22).

The involuntary-petition decision (11.16.1) is answered with §13's `decision/answer`; its options run `finance/fileReorganization` or `owner/fileBankruptcy`. Quotes (`finance.quote`), statements, forecasts, `reorgEligibility` and `reorgPlanPreview` are selectors, not actions. §1 owns `owner/draw`, `owner/inject`, `owner/setSalary`, `owner/repayLoan` (§11 posts them). §6 owns the bond-instrument choice; picking `loc` calls §11 `issueStandbyLoc`. *Trade-offs, one line each:* reordering priority picks which creditor's remedy you face; accepting a bank hedging covenant buys half a point of rate with delivery risk; a quote is free but an application costs owner-score points; a PG buys credit with personal exposure; seasonal schedules buy a smaller spring trough for ~0.25 points; leasing keeps leverage clean but caps hours; royalty sales fund winter but tax every future ounce; a reorganization keeps the company and the run but takes three to five years of disposable income, marks both credit files, and costs a scenario's gold medal; equity has no payments but dilutes and adds a vote; filing small insurance claims nets little and raises premiums for three years; bonus depreciation defers tax but creates recapture and 80%-limited NOLs.

### 11.22 Weekly resolution

| Step (§2.6) | What §11 does (position among the step's acting sections, §2.6) |
|---|---|
| Action time | `finance/fileReorganization` opens the case at once (retainer, stay, `permits.onReorganizationFiled`, credit marks; 11.16.1); `finance/fileReorgPlan` records the plan and sets the hearing; `owner/fileBankruptcy` sets the liquidation request that step 15 settles |
| 6 Negotiations & pending deals | After §5, §9 and §10, before §4 and §7: decide loan applications whose decision turn arrived (11.6; a DIP loan on collateral alone, 11.16.2); expire offers (2 weeks); deliver royalty-co, investor, and rescue offers; issue forbearance offers on new default notices; schedule insurance settlements; fund §5 closings' carry notes (`createLoan`) |
| 12 Cleanup | After §7's gold room, §5 `settleProductionInterests` and §10 `addLot`, before §4 `recordProduction`, §12 `onCleanup` and §10's standing orders and forward delivery-week close-outs: post deferred-revenue drawdowns for in-kind royalty/stream deliveries reported by §5's settlement; record which claims cleaned up this week (their pools close in 14c). §10's prepay delivery results arrive later in the step and are booked in 14c |
| 13 Permits & compliance | No §11 step. §6 auto-pays statutory obligations from `dueTurn − 1` (retrying each week) through `pay` with `origin: 'pipeline'` (priority reserve, 11.4), applies statutory consequences at the end of step 13 on `dueTurn + graceWeeks`, and evaluates billable §5/§6/§1 obligations as missed at `dueTurn + graceWeeks + 1` (§2.6 obligation timing) |
| 14 Finance | **a** accrue loan interest (11.7), card interest, unused-line fees, deposit interest. **b** payroll run (11.3; §8 `payrollForWeek`). **c** post this week's §7 `OpsCostLine`s and §9 costs as bills (split by `reclamationShare`) and §8 staffing bills; create recurring bills: loan and lease payments (month-end weeks), MCA debits, card minimums, insurance installments, tax installments, owner salary/draws/tax distributions (§1); bill the billable obligations due this week (11.4); at month end, a bill for the `accrued.royalties` balance (§5 cash royalties and minimums accrued since the last month end and not already billed through an obligation; category `royalty.cash`, due this week); owner living cost on the owner book (§1); book §10's prepay delivery results from step 12 (arrears if short, 11.12); ARO remeasure from §6's deltas and reclaim reclass (11.19.3); close cost pools of claims cleaned up this week into lot cost (11.19.2); create or refresh §11 `Obligation`s; in a reorganization case, no bills for stayed loans and month-end adequate-protection bills (11.16.2), and plan installments from confirmation (11.16.5); P2–P3: bind the GL stub the first week plan-tier coverage is needed (11.17). **d** receipts through `receive`: refinery settlements (§10), insurance settlements, stream ongoing payments; the wage-lien sweep applies to gold-sale receipts (11.4). **e** settlement: auto-debits, then the priority queue (one settlement transaction), skipping `stayed` bills except pre-filing net wages up to the wage priority (11.16.2); arrears, NSF and late fees; then §8 `recordPayrollOutcome` for each employee. **f** status updates: loan lifecycle milestones (late → delinquent → notice → cure → acceleration; stayed loans and plan notes skip it), missed plan installments at `dueTurn + 1` (11.16.5), vendor statuses (stop-supply, collections, liens), §11 obligations missed at `dueTurn + graceWeeks + 1`, credit events, Paydex; wage-lien release at zero wage arrears. **g** revolver borrowing base and over-advance; gold-loan LTV and margin calls. **h** month end: book depreciation (the month's sum of §9's weekly `bookDepreciationSchedule`) and depletion, LCNRV, card statements, BBC due, liquidity tests, U refresh, deposit interest credit, outsourced bookkeeping fee ($900/month with no bookkeeper or controller), ledger compaction (11.1). **i** quarter end: leverage tests, monitoring DSCR, quarterly report obligations. **j** annual: week 1 revolver renewal and payroll-YTD reset; week 10 return-preparation fee (11.18); week 49 insurance renewal (EMR, claims multipliers, non-renewal rolls); at the season-year end (week 52 for a northern primary climate, week 26 for an arid one; 11.14) the DSCR and clean-up tests, then the primary-climate re-evaluation; week 52 tax-year close (depreciation, depletion, TI, NOL, the attribute reduction for any discharge gain (11.16.6), AK license and NV net-proceeds accruals, `annual` government-royalty accruals), annual-statement obligation (due week 18), close `eq.draws` to retained earnings. **k** sweeps out |
| 15 Distress | First in the step, then §5 `onForeclose` / `forcedSale` / `transferToCreditor` and §9 `repossess` as called: **(a)** the reorganization block (11.16.4–11.16.5): relief from the stay for unpaid adequate protection; plan-due and amendment deadlines; a hearing due this week (tests, vote, effective date, plan notes, rejections, guarantee demands); anniversary true-ups; conversion checks; completion (`permits.onReorganizationClosed`); the case signals for §13 (`reorg.planDue`, `reorg.hearingSoon`, `reorg.ruling`, `reorg.paymentShort`, `reorg.paymentMissed`, `reorg.adequateProtectionUnpaid`, `reorg.saleNotice`, `reorg.trueUp`, `reorg.completed`; levels and windows are §13's, 13.10, keys `game.alerts.reorg*`), with 14f raising `reorg.paymentMissed`; **(b)** evaluate the stage (11.16); acceleration, cross-default propagation, bank setoff (stayed loans excepted); repossession seizures (access permitting) and dispositions; guarantee demands; TFRP assessment (paused in a case); workout liquidation; P1 insolvency counter; **(c)** involuntary triggers → the petition decision for an eligible company or the liquidation flag; a filed or converted liquidation → final settlement and `distress.liquidation` for §1 step 16d |

### 11.23 Interfaces

**Provides.**
- Functions: `post`, `bill`, `pay`, `receive` (every receipt; wage-lien sweep), `queryLedger`, `quote`, `obligationPayCategory(obl)`, `vendorStatus(state, kind, scopeId)`, `lienStatus(machineId | claimId)`, `lienPayoff(state, collateralRef, proceedsCents)` (§5 and §9 closings, §5 forced sales; `LIEN_SHORTFALL`), `createLoan(state, spec)` (§1 estate note and banker stub, §5 `sellerCarry`), `createFinancedAcquisition(state, offerId, machineId)` (§9), `issueStandbyLoc(state, spec)` (§6), `handleLoss(state, LossEvent)`, `policyCovering(state, locationKey)` (§10), `fileInsuranceClaim(state, kind, lossCents, ref)` and `chargeLoss(state, cents, account, memo, ref)` (§12), `resetCovenant(state, loanId, deltas)` and `scheduleNonRenewal(state, loanId, turn)` (§12), `applyTaxAudit(state, { pct, feesCents })` (§12 `taxAudit`), `insuredStatus(machineId)`, `addWagePenalty(state, employeeId, cents)` (§12 walkout).
- Selectors (§2.11): `cashOnHand`, `availableLiquidity` (unrestricted cash + revolver availability), `dueThisWeek` (§10 standing orders: open bills due ≤ this week + this week's estimated payroll, tax deposit and loan dues), `workingCapital`, `tangibleNetWorth`, `creditTier`, `companyScore850` (§6 surety and §10 dealers; P2 stubs and P4 definitions in 11.5), `ownerPersonalNW` (§6 surety capacity), `credit01`, `netWorth(state, mode)`, `forecast13Week` (incl. `productionByClaim`), `seasonProductionForecast(state, claimIds, year)` (11.19.6), `costPerOunce(period, claimId?)`, `claimPnL(period)`, `statements.{income, balance, cashFlow}(period)`, `debtSchedule`, `covenantStatus` (value, threshold, headroom, next test), `creditProfile` (scores, factor table), `distressStatus(state)` (`stage`, `stageKey`, `form`, next trigger, counter-moves, `reorg`, `liquidation`; P2–P3 stub in 11.5; §12 reads `distressStatus(state).stage`, §6 and §13 `stageKey`), `reorgEligibility(state)` and `reorgPlanPreview(state, terms)` (11.16.7), the case's player deadlines (plan due turn, amendment deadline) for §13 `upcomingDeadlines`, `payrollSummary` (incl. the 13-week register), `claimsHistoryMult(line)` (§10).
- Hooks for others: §8 `recordPayrollOutcome` is called after each payroll settlement (§8 writes `staff.unpaidWages`); `PaymentEvent` stream (§1 reputation, §8 morale), including the case events `reorgFiled`, `reorgConfirmed`, `reorgConverted` and `reorgCompleted`; `vendorStatus` (§7, §9); the case calls into §6 (`permits.onReorganizationFiled`, `permits.onReorganizationClosed`) and §1 (`recordReputation` with `reorgFiled` and `reorgCompleted`); the blocking decision `finance.involuntaryPetition` (§2 `PendingDecision`). Event targets (§12 `EffectModifier`): `finance.lenderSpreadAdd`, `finance.lenderMaxLtvAdd`, `finance.lenderAppetiteShift` (scope lender or world), `finance.lineLimitMult` (multiplies revolver commitments at renewal and card limits), `finance.insurancePremiumMult`, `finance.vendor.limitMult`, `finance.wageLienSweep` (set 1, scope company; 11.4).
- Iteration: every `Record` in `FinanceSlice` is iterated through §2.3's sorted-key helper (no raw `Object.keys/values/entries` in engine code); `billIds` and `loanIds` are the canonical ordered lists for settlement and the lifecycle.
- Types: `FinanceSlice` (below), `Bill`, `PaymentRequest`, `PayResult`, `PayCategory`, `Loan`, `Lien`, `VendorAccount`, `FinancingAgreement`, `CovenantState`, `Policy`, `LossEvent`, `DistressState`, `ReorgCase`, `ReorgPlanTerms`, `ReorgSlice` (11.16.7), `TaxJurisdiction`, and the supporting shapes:

```ts
interface Lien { id: Id /* lien_ */; loanId: Id; collateral: CollateralRef; filedTurn: number; kind: 'pmsi' | 'specific' | 'blanket' | 'vendor'; releasedTurn?: number }
interface Arrear { id: Id /* arr_ */; billId: Id; category: PayCategory; amountCents: Cents; dueTurn: number; weeksLate: number; feesCents: Cents }
interface Lease { id: Id; lenderId: LenderId; machineId: Id; kind: 'operating' | 'finance'; costCents: Cents; paymentCents: Cents;
  termMonths: number; firstDueTurn: number; hourCapPerYear: number | null; hoursThisLeaseYear: number; status: LoanStatus;
  liabilityCents?: Cents /* finance only */; endOption?: 'return' | 'buyFmv' | 'renew' }
interface CardAccount { id: Id /* card_ */; lenderId: LenderId; limitCents: Cents; balanceCents: Cents; statementCents: Cents;
  statementDueTurn: number | null; paidInFullLast: boolean; consecutiveMisses: number; apr: number; penaltyApr: boolean; routing: PayCategory[] }
interface LoanApplication { id: Id /* lapp_ */; lenderId: LenderId; product: ProductId; amountCents: Cents; termMonths: number;
  schedule: PaymentScheduleKind; collateral: CollateralRef[]; purpose: string; submittedTurn: number; decisionTurn: number }
interface FinanceOffer { id: Id /* foff_ */; source: 'lender' | 'royaltyCo' | 'equity' | 'rescue' | 'forbearance'; counterpartyId: string;
  terms: Record<string, number | string>; expiresTurn: number; calc: CalcNode | null }
interface Derog { kind: string; turn: number; base: number; mult: number; halfLifeWeeks: number; maxAgeWeeks: number; ref: Id }
interface InsuranceClaim { id: Id /* icl_ */; lossId: Id; policyId: Id; approvedCents: Cents; deductibleCents: Cents; settleTurn: number; status: 'pending' | 'settled' }
interface TaxBasis { costCents: Cents; adjustedCents: Cents; placedTurn: number; method: 'bonus100' | 'macrs7' | 'macrs5' | 'inherited7' }
interface TaxInstallment { book: Book; dueTurn: number; requiredCents: Cents; paidCents: Cents; method: 'safeHarbor' | 'annualized' }
interface StandbyLoc { id: Id /* loc_ */; bondId: Id; faceCents: Cents; feeNextTurn: number; status: 'open' | 'drawn' | 'released' }
```

```ts

  books: Record<Book, { txns: Txn[]; balances: Record<AccountCode, Cents>; monthly: MonthlySummary[] }>;

  insurance: { policies: Record<Id, Policy>; claims: Record<Id, InsuranceClaim>; losses: Record<Id, LossEvent & { status: 'open' | 'filed' | 'absorbed' | 'uninsured'; decideByTurn: number }>; emr: number };
  tax: { elections: Record<number, 'bonus100' | 'macrs'>; estimateMethod: 'safeHarbor' | 'annualized';
         distributionPolicy: 'auto' | 'manual'; nol: { company: Cents; owner: Cents };

  payrollYtd: Record<Id, Cents>; payrollQtdByJurisdiction: Record<string, Cents>; distress: DistressState;
  reorg: ReorgSlice;                   // the open reorganization case and closed ones (11.16.7)

}
interface PayrollRegisterLine { employeeId: Id; costCenter: CostCenter; claimId?: Id; grossCents: Cents; hours: number;
  trustCents: Cents; netCents: Cents; employerTaxCents: Cents; wcCents: Cents; paidCents: Cents; shortCents: Cents }
interface MonthlySummary { year: number; month: number;
  rows: { account: AccountCode; costCenter?: CostCenter; claimId?: Id; cf: 'O' | 'I' | 'F' | 'X'; debitCents: Cents; creditCents: Cents }[] }
```

Save-size budget (D-11.47): a reorganization case adds a few kilobytes (its claims list and plan terms; the cooldown allows at most two cases in ten years). At year 10 the finance slice holds ≤ 52 weeks of transactions (≈ 1,500 for a two-claim operation, ≈ 0.35 MB), monthly summaries (≈ 0.15 MB), and bills, arrears and register rings capped by age, ≈ 0.5 MB uncompressed in total, inside §2's per-slice budget.

### 11.24 Phase plan

- **P1 (core loop).** Company and owner books; `cash.operating` only; full posting API and ledger UI, with 52-week detail and monthly compaction; `receive`; bills and `pay` with the fixed default priority (no reordering, no late fees); billable §5 obligations (lease advance royalties) become step-14 bills; P1 payroll (flat 1.22× burden, no withholding; one transaction per run and the 13-week register; `recordPayrollOutcome`); fixed loans with the generalized schedule and prepayment (Inheritor estate note on the Jun–Nov seasonal schedule, $10,281.75 × 6/yr, or $5,067.68/mo if `game.inheritor.noteSchedule` = 'level'; banker stub $3,113.75/mo); book depreciation from §9's P1 straight-line; **P1 P&L** (costs as incurred, revenue at sale, no inventory absorption; gold shown at market as a memo); per-claim P&L and cash cost per ounce; 13-week projection of scheduled outflows plus the P50 production line from §7 `productionForecast` at the local-buyer net (11.19.6); P1 insolvency counter → liquidation, listing the P1 levers (sell gold, sell iron, §5 quick sale or lease surrender, owner injection, cut hours; 11.16); §1's P1 net worth. Not in P1: reserve, credit, lenders, covenants, insurance, taxes, vendor terms (all bills due the week they arise; the Inheritor's $12k fuel AP is due week 4).
- **P2 (licensing).** `cash.restricted.*`, `deposits.bonds`, `liab.suretyIndemnity`, `liab.agencyJudgment`; surety premiums to `exp.permitsFees`; ARO (weekly provision and accretion from §6's liability, reclaim reclass, forfeiture postings); §6 statutory obligations paid by player action or auto-pay under the priority reserve in step 13, billable ones as step-14 bills (still the fixed default order); the insurance stub (GL flat $8k/yr, bound automatically when plan-tier coverage is first needed; WC stays in the P1 burden) that satisfies §6's insurance gates; surety-underwriting stubs (`companyScore850`, `creditTier`, `workingCapital`, `tangibleNetWorth`, stub `distressStatus(state).stage`, `ownerPersonalNW`; 11.5).
- **P3 (equipment depth).** Operating and finance lease accounting with one lessor at fixed B-tier terms (no credit check); rental billing; `inv.parts`; casualty write-offs for destroyed machines (uninsured until P4).
- **P4 (finance depth).** Everything else: reserve and sweeps; priority reordering; full payroll taxes and withholding; vendor credit and payment plans (fixed rule); credit profiles; bank, SBA, equipment finance, captives, hard money (incl. PER-certified claim collateral), cards, MCA; §5 seller carry notes; revolver (equipment sublimit and seasonal over-advance only, since gold and AR components need §10's metal accounts and refinery, D-11.11) and standby LOCs; royalty sales, streams and prepays (D-11.50; in P4 a prepay delivery takes the oldest held lots at the scheduled week and §10 marks them sold; P5 switches to §10's delivery path); equity raises; rescue partner; covenants and breach rolls, with the annual DSCR and clean-up tests at the primary climate's season-year end (D-11.62); called loans; payment-default lifecycle, repossession, workout (claims through §5 `land.forcedSale` as a forced listing, and `land.transferToCreditor`), full ladder, guarantees, TFRP; bankruptcy in both forms (11.16.1–11.16.7): Chapter 7 liquidation (game over) and the Subchapter V reorganization (eligibility, the involuntary-petition decision, the stay and adequate protection, DIP loans, the plan with its tests and vote, plan notes, true-ups, conversion, completion, discharge accounting and the COD exclusion, credit marks) in every game mode; insurance and the claims process; federal and state taxes (`akStyle`, `nvStyle`), entity return-preparation fees, audits; absorption costing and all reports; 13-week forecast with bands; owner living costs and personal credit (§1), with the sole proprietor's owner-file rule; §12 finance events (incl. the wage-lien sweep). Gold momentum is 0 until P5, so lender ripple terms are inert.
- **P5 (living market).** Gold-driven lender appetite and valuation ripples (goldMomentum ≠ 0); revolver metal-account, bank-box, and refinery-AR components; gold loans against metal accounts; hedging covenants (forwards, `inc.hedgeGainLoss`), including the bank hedging requirement (11.6); gold storage insurance tiers from §10 (`policyCovering`); negotiated restructures and vendor plans through §5; forced sales in auction format.
- **P6 (expansion).** Buy-sell provisions and pay-to-play dilution; `yukon` jurisdiction (Canadian payroll, small-business rate, amounts in C$ at `market.cadToUsd`; the export royalty is §6's interest); `temperateStyle` jurisdiction with §3's `temperateFederal` template (earlier if that template ships early as content); Alaska state-land net-income royalty (§6 interest, settled by §11 at week 52); multi-entity reporting depth for delegation. The optional hard-rock track's finance (capital projects, `ppe.cip` and `mineral.development`, project loans with a DSRA, pre-production streams, commercial-production and UoP depletion rules) is specified in §14 14.12 and extends this section's machinery; see §14.

### 11.26 Balance levers and risks

- **Survival levers** (most to least sensitive in early sims): the existence and timing of spring credit (bank history gate, seasonal eligibility, equipment-finance startup tier and $250k startup cap); `finance.defaultTimelineMult`, `paymentGraceWeeks`, and `repoLagWeeks` (how long a bad June can last); equipment-finance C/D spreads (a bootstrapper's iron at 17–25%); in-kind royalty and rescue terms; insurance on/off (uninsured fires end runs).
- **Reorganization levers.** A filing of either form fails the survival window it falls in (BALANCE O-01 gates both S2 and B2, owner ruling 2026-10-05), so reorganization moves no two-season target; it sets how many runs continue into later windows and how they fare there. Levers, in order: `finance.reorg.retainerUsd` and `debtLimitUsd` (who can file), `capexAllowancePct` and `reserveMaxPct` (how much PDI a plan commits and how often installments are missed), `voteBias` and `voteSlope` (the consensual share), `trueUpShare` (how much a recovering run pays back). Watch the share of reorganized runs that convert within two years; if nearly all convert, plans commit too much; if none do, too little.
- **Profitability levers:** captive promo frequency, depletion (worth ~5–8% of profit in good years), bonus depreciation timing, WC rate × EMR, revolver advance rates.
- **Growth vs caution.** Preflight runs show the cautious bot dominating the aggressive one over two seasons on deep frozen ground (scale buys little while stripping and thaw bind). BALANCE O-04 (no dominant strategy) is therefore judged at year 5 with P4 finance. BALANCE T-10 (b), the mature operation's unit-cost advantage over the reference op, is measured on thawed ground (0.81 against ≤ 0.85 in preflight), because an established mature operation strips a season or more ahead; the frozen-ground ratio (1.02 at permafrost 0.8, where `matureNorth` is limited by strip and thaw, not by its plant) is carried as a named O-04 risk (BALANCE R-4). If aggressive growth is still dominated there, the finance lever is `finance.startupCapUsd` ($250k per equipment lender or captive while < 104 weeks), which limits financed growth; the operations lever is §7's strip-ahead and thaw capacity.
- **Inheritor.** The estate note's Jun–Nov schedule (11.7) moves about $25k of debt service out of the first spring, and §1 has since raised the estate account to $300k (D-1.54; preflight Inheritor S2 60% in P1, 43% under full rules). If simulator runs still show the Inheritor below its survival band, the next levers are §1's Inheritor terms, not lender terms.

| Exploit / dominant strategy | Counter |
|---|---|
| Lease everything (operating) to dodge leverage covenants | Hour caps and overage charges on a 7-day schedule; no equity build; return-condition charges; LRF above loan cost for C/D tiers |
| Borrow max from every lender at once | One open application per lender; inquiries cut the owner score; blanket liens and negative pledges; DSCR capacity; cross-default |
| Sell royalties every winter as free money | Payback multiple 2.0× plus a perpetual tail; claims burdened by royalties fetch less (§5 valuation) and cut future royalty offers (E' net of existing interests) |
| Never file insurance claims, or self-insure | Uninsured losses fall on cash; lenders require coverage on financed iron (force-placement at 2.5×) |
| Starve payroll taxes to fund operations | TFRP makes it personal for every entity type, never discharged |
| Run an LLC into the ground and walk away | PGs on nearly all early debt; clawback (§1); unpaid wages and TFRP personal; score is personal NW |
| MCA every winter | Weekly debits through the off-season; ≈ 123% APR; 2 missed debits = default |
| Ping-pong reserve/operating for interest | Instant free sweep makes it pointless; yield < revolver cost |
| Hold gold in camp to inflate the borrowing base | Camp gold advance = 0; bank box only 25%; metal-account fees and refining needed for 75% |
| Time big purchases right before the covenant test | DSCR is annual on the season-year T12 (week 52 north, week 26 arid); capex limit; liquidity is monthly |
| Wash a few yards in the other climate to move the covenant test away from a bad season | The primary climate follows the most operated bcy over 52 weeks, a switch waits for the new climate's next end week, and that test still covers a full trailing 52 weeks |
| Banker background + captive promos to lever a startup at 0% (banker makes a new company tier B) | Promos need ≥ 104 weeks in business; equipment lenders and captives cap a startup's exposure at $250k each; after 104 weeks a 1.10× DSCR capacity test applies |
| Inflate royalty or equity offers with your own optimistic estimate | Buyers use only production history or a third-party §4 PER/technical report ($15–120k); equity credits P50 uplift only on report-backed claims |
| Use step-13 auto-pay to jump fees ahead of payroll | Pipeline payments respect the priority reserve (11.4) |
| Pick sole proprietor for the credit and fee edges | Full personal recourse on every debt; every hard inquiry and lateness hits the owner's file; no equity partners (rescue is royalty-only) |
| Accept the bank hedging covenant for the rate cut, then under-produce | Shortfall against forwards is a §10 close-out with penalty; the covenant test at weeks 18 and 31 is a breach roll if hedges lapse |
| Pay 1% short on payroll forever to dodge the involuntary-bankruptcy trigger | Any shortfall is still stage 3 (morale, walkouts, wage claims, reputation); the 25% threshold only decides the involuntary petition |
| File for reorganization to shed debt and keep the upside | Three to five years of projected disposable income; half of any outperformance in the true-up; $40k of case costs plus 3% trustee fees; draws capped at living costs; bankruptcy marks on both files for 7–10 years; guarantees, TFRP, fines and reclamation survive; a scenario's gold medal is lost; one filing per 8 years; the filing fails the survival window (BALANCE) |
| Shrink the mine plan before the hearing to lower disposable income, then expand | The best-interest test still demands the Chapter 7 dividend; vote odds fall with the recovery; the anniversary true-up takes half of production-basis EBITDA above the projection |
| File, sell the iron during the case, keep the cash | Sales need court approval and pay liens first; net proceeds raise the Chapter 7 dividend that the plan must beat; draws stay capped |
| Skip the reserve to win the vote | Every projected dollar is committed: two missed installments in 52 weeks convert the case (one under a hostile investor's motion) |
| Pay favored pre-filing creditors during the case | Stayed bills and loans refuse payment (`CLAIM_STAYED`); only the plan pays them |

### 11.27 Tests

- **Ledger (property, fast-check):** every entry balances; account balances equal the recomputation from monthly summaries plus the detailed journal; cash never negative; Σ assets = Σ liabilities + equity after every week; statements tie to balances; indirect CFO = direct CFO and CF reconciles to Δ(operating + reserve) for any period (incl. weeks with write-downs, depreciation capitalized into inventory, repossessions, and netted loan fees), and still reconciles for periods rebuilt from compacted summaries; compaction leaves every statement, per-claim P&L and balance unchanged; replay determinism with all finance streams; stream isolation (perturbing `finance-lender` changes no `finance-royaltyco`, `finance-equity`, or `finance-insurance` outcome); permuting the insertion order of every `FinanceSlice` record leaves the week's result unchanged (sorted-key iteration).
- **Save size:** the finance slice of a year-10 save (two-claim operation fixture) stays within §2's per-slice budget (≈ 0.5 MB uncompressed): ≤ 52 weeks of transaction detail, one payroll transaction per run, one settlement transaction per week, a 13-run register, and closed bills pruned after 52 weeks.
- **Amortization:** the six fixtures in 11.7 to the cent ($8,303.34; $9,494.99; $5,067.68; $10,281.75 × 6 seasonal estate note; $3,113.75; $16,860.95), plus the 11.15 curve's $19,122.34 level and $38,896.80 seasonal payments; generalized schedule with no skip months equals the level formula; B_n = 0 within 1¢ for all schedule kinds; weekly accruals within a month sum exactly to I_m; prepayment shortens the term with an unchanged payment; the seasonal estate note has no payment in January–May of year 1; a seller carry note on a northern claim pays only in week 44 (`payMonths: [10]`) and on an arid claim only in week 18 (`payMonths: [4]`).
- **Payroll:** the 11.3 example to the cent (trust $573.07, net $2,270.93, employer cost $3,348.81); FUTA stops at $7,000 YTD; SS stops at the wage base; MBT only above $50k quarterly; P1 burden = 1.22×; one ledger transaction per run whose lines equal the register's sums by account × cost center × claim; `recordPayrollOutcome` is called exactly once per employee per run, after settlement, with paid + short = net.
- **Priority and obligations:** with funds for exactly categories 1–4, categories 5+ become arrears; pro-rata payroll gives equal % shortfalls; reordering changes which arrears appear; autoDebit always first, owner always last; a step-13 claim-fee auto-pay fails when it would dip into this week's payroll under the default order, and succeeds when `regulatory.critical` is ranked above payroll; obligation categories map per 11.4; a statutory obligation never becomes a bill and takes its consequence at the end of step 13 on `dueTurn + graceWeeks` when unpaid; a billable obligation (a §5 advance royalty, a §11 loan payment) becomes a bill in its due week, is paid in that week's step 14, and is never "missed" in step 13 of its own due week; still unpaid when its owner evaluates it at `dueTurn + graceWeeks + 1` (§6 in step 13, §11 in 14f) it is missed exactly once (one `land.onObligationMissed`, one default notice).
- **Wage-lien sweep:** with `finance.wageLienSweep` set and $30k of payroll arrears, a $50k refinery settlement pays the $30k of arrears first (pro rata by employee) and leaves $20k for other uses even when the priority order ranks payroll below debt; non-gold receipts are not swept; the lien clears and the modifier ends in the week arrears reach zero.
- **Credit:** start scores match §1; the late30 example (−72, 724 at 52 wk, 748 at 104 wk); U examples (153; sole proprietor 168; 165; Inheritor 120; 241); a sole proprietor's owner-file rule ends at 104 weeks; thin file switches to a file at 3 trade lines and 13 weeks; tier cutoffs; banker shifts exactly one tier (`bankerCreditTierBonus` × `tierWidthPoints` = 35); `companyScore850` maps U 140/175/210 to 620/670/720; bankruptcy mark −240 at 850 and −168 at 580; P2 stubs: owner 720 ⇒ `companyScore850` 684 and tier B, owner 680 ⇒ 656 and tier C; stub `distressStatus(state).stage` = 3 with a payroll arrear, 2 with only a loan arrear, 0 with none; `ownerPersonalNW` = own.cash − personal debt − guarantee and tax dues.
- **Appetite:** bank declines a company with < 2 profitable years (1 with banker); equipment-finance startup floor C at owner ≥ 700; gm −25% (lagged 4 weeks) ⇒ bank +2.0 points (rate +0.020), LTV × 0.85, −20 appetite; captive promos suspended below −15%; a startup's total equipFinance exposure never exceeds $250k; a banker-background startup gets captive B pricing but no promo; DSCR capacity binds after 104 weeks; §12 modifiers shift A, rate, and LTV by exactly their values; a skill-91 controller (q = 1.3) adds 13 appetite points and −0.325 points of rate, a skill-35 controller (q = 0.5) adds 5 and −0.125; a bank offer at tier C or with exposure > $750k carries a required hedging covenant, and accepting it lowers the rate by exactly 0.50 points.
- **Revolver:** the 11.9 examples (BB $275k, $821k, over-advance $63.5k); camp gold contributes 0; pledged metal contributes 0; bank-box gold at 25%; a P4 base has no gold or AR terms; an open LOC reduces availability by its face, and a draw raises outstanding; clean-up breach when 4 zero weeks are missing in weeks 45–52 (northern primary climate) or 19–26 (arid), recorded in week 52 or 26.
- **Covenants:** DSCR, liquidity, leverage on hand-built statements; strictness scaling; season-year end (D-11.62): a company whose trailing-52-week washed bcy is mostly northern is DSCR-tested in week 52 and one whose bcy is mostly arid in week 26, never both in one season year; a company with no washed bcy is northern; a company that has washed only arid ground by week 26 of year 1 takes its first test there; a north-to-arid switch tests at week 52 and then at week 26 of the next year, each on a full trailing-52-week T12; tax-year close stays at week 52 for both; breach roll distribution matches logistic(z) over 10k draws (±1.5%); technical default path.
- **Default lifecycle:** milestone weeks per lender at each difficulty match the 11.14 table (bank notice D+13/D+10/D+8, repo D+25/D+18/D+14; hard money repo never earlier than acceleration + 2); late fee at D + 3/2/1 for the bank; cross-default propagation and auto-cure; setoff only by the depository bank; repo blocked when access is closed; the repo example (deficiency $59k); a seller carry default calls `land.onForeclose` and leaves no deficiency; a called loan unpaid at `callTurn` enters at default notice; a workout lists each claim through `land.forcedSale` with a reserve of 50% of cost basis and `proceedsTo` the loan, and an unsold claim passes by `land.transferToCreditor` credited at the reserve; a claim or machine sale whose proceeds plus cash fall short of the lien payoff fails with `LIEN_SHORTFALL` and changes nothing.
- **Gold loan:** margin call at $3,360 and forced sale at $2,965 for the 11.11 example.
- **Royalty / stream / prepay:** U = $462,000 example; royalty-sale and stream interests carry `origin: 'financing'`; the offer class never uses the player's own estimate confidence (scrambling `ClaimEstimate.confidence` leaves the offer unchanged when no PER exists); E' equals 0.5 × (P10 + P50) of `seasonProductionForecast` with no history; deferred revenue never goes negative; drawdowns equal §5's delivery values; deliveries after zero balance are memo only; buyback prices per 11.12; prepay shortfall creates arrears (from §10's `'prepay'` counterparty, never a close-out) and defaults after 8 weeks, transferring the covered claims through `land.transferToCreditor`.
- **Rescue:** the 11.13 example (65%, 10%).
- **Insurance:** EMR examples (0.75, 1.13, 1.51, 1.50); coinsurance example ($35k; $50k when insured ≥ 80% of FMV); claims multiplier bounds; force-placement on lapse; `LossEvent` routing table (breakdown with health < 0.25 is uninsured; a §9 `overturn` routes to equipment); fire-suppression credit −10% on that machine only; camp-safe specie premium on $209,160 of average gold at claimsMult 1.0 = $4,183/yr ($80.45/wk, §10's example); `policyCovering` returns the camp-safe policy only with a safe and never at fly-in, the bank-box rider for that district, and null for `campOpen`; a §10 theft `LossEvent` with `locationKey` writes the lots off to `exp.theftLoss` at cost; the P2 GL stub binds without any action in the week the first plan-tier application is submitted, posts an inbox note, and satisfies §6's insurance gates.

- **Reports:** cost per oz example ($3,427 / $3,872 / $4,032); the 11.15 curve from `refSmallNorthDebt` year 2 (level trough −$111k in June, seasonal −$35k, year +$15k level and +$11k seasonal, $3.9k of extra interest); inventory absorption example ($3,182/oz); a lot sold in step 12 of its cleanup week nets zero inventory change; LCNRV write-down never reverses; theft releases cost to `exp.theftLoss`; per-claim P&L columns sum to the company IS; `exp.staffing` appears in the site labor line for field roles and in G&A for office roles; forecast P10 ≤ P50 ≤ P90 every week; the forecast's P50 production equals Σ §7 `productionForecast` p50 over each cleanup interval in every phase; the P1 forecast includes those cleanup inflows at the local-buyer net (one series, P10 = P50 = P90) and a mid-season P1 runway with planned cleanups is longer than the outflows-only runway; the forecast reads no hidden fields; `seasonProductionForecast` equals the season sum of §7 `productionForecast`; ARO accretion equals prior ARO × Δcpi/cpi; reclaim reclass never exceeds the claim's carrying amount.
- **Reorganization (11.16):** eligibility at the debt limit ($3,424,000 × cpiIndex allowed, one cent more refused with `REORG_DEBT_LIMIT`), at the cooldown (a filing 415 weeks after the last refused, 416 allowed), below stage 2, and for P1–P3 rules (no path; the P1 counter liquidates); `debtsNCL` excludes `liab.reclamation`, undemanded guarantees, royalty-sale and stream deferred revenue, and `debt.ownerLoan`, and includes a sole proprietor's personal debts; a failed retainer changes nothing. *Stay:* a stayed loan accrues no interest, late fee or default interest, reaches no lifecycle milestone and is never repossessed while its adequate protection is paid; a claim or machine sale closes no earlier than 3 weeks after acceptance. *Plan:* the 11.16.7 worked example to the cent (PDI0 $154,830; D $142,804.37; notes $6,974.81 / $3,113.75 / $496.14; U $15,787.97 and $17,276.39; scheduled $80,428.27; PV_U $64,370.85; Chapter 7 dividend 37.4%; margin 12.4%; the 156-week plan refused with `PLAN_NOT_FEASIBLE` at $183,181.68 > D; z = 0.17, 54%; discharge gain $75,571.73; guarantee demands $21,315.10 and $10,657.55; owner score 700 → 600); unsecured distributions never exceed C_U; a surrendered machine credits FLV × 0.925 − ½ repo cost and an in-use machine is refused; the owner loan receives nothing and survives the discharge; the best-interest test uses a general creditor's recovery percentage and adds a debtor-owner's personal cash above $25,000. *Confirmation:* the vote draw happens at every hearing, also when the tests fail; logistic(z) matches over 10k draws (±1.5%); a non-consensual confirmation extends a 156-week plan to 260 weeks with secured schedules unchanged, puts the trustee fee on every installment and books no discharge gain until completion; a consensual one books it at confirmation and charges the trustee fee once; a second denial converts. *Plan period:* two installments missed within 52 weeks convert, one when `investor.conversionMotionActive` is true, and a missed installment paid before the second miss still counts within the window; involuntary trigger (a) converts in a case, trigger (b) only after confirmation; a 4-week-late post-filing trust deposit converts; the true-up adds 50% of DI above PDI0 to the next year and is unchanged by holding gold across the anniversary; an ineligible one liquidates the same week. *Ledger and tax:* every case transaction balances; the balance sheet balances through filing, confirmation and completion; CFO reconciles with the discharge gain non-cash; the discharge gain is excluded from TI and reduces the NOL, then machine basis, floor 0. *Isolation:* perturbing `finance-reorg` changes no other finance stream's outcome; scrambling hidden fields leaves `reorgPlanPreview` unchanged.
- **Distress:** stage transitions on scripted cash paths; stage 0 fires within `finance.distress.watchWeeks` (6/4/3 by difficulty) plus §8's `alertBonusWeeks`; 3 consecutive payrolls short by ≥ 25% ⇒ the involuntary petition (liquidation the same week for a company not eligible to reorganize; 3 runs short by 10% ⇒ stage 3 only); `nextTrigger` names the first forecast week where payroll cannot be met; draws blocked at stage ≥ 3; personal exposure by entity (sole prop personal levy, LLC guarantee demand, unguaranteed debt dies, TFRP always personal); P1 counter clears when arrears are paid; while it is open `distressStatus(state).counterMoves` lists the six P1 levers, and a P1 quick sale closes the next week at 0.6 × the visible buyer valuation.

- **Simulator gates (BALANCE; bots from §2.12.1):** `undercap` bankruptcy of either form (1 − B2) ≥ 60% by year 2; `cautious` pooled going-concern S2 (D-2.16) 60–70% **and** pooled no-bankruptcy B2 ≥ 75% over two seasons (BALANCE O-01 gates both, owner ruling 2026-10-05; a filing of either form inside the window fails both B_N and S_N, the reorganization share of filings is reported separately, and a reorganized run is measured normally in later windows); no financing strategy (`leaseOnly`, `allHardMoney`, `royaltyEveryWinter`) dominates the matrix; `aggressive` vs `cautious` (O-04) judged at year 5 with P4 finance; the sole-proprietor `cautious` bot's two-season survival within 5 pp of the LLC bot (§1.22).
- **Phase exit (§1.19):** P1 — amortization fixtures incl. the seasonal estate note, P1 payroll, priority, P1 forecast with production, P1 counter and levers, ledger properties and save size; P2 — obligation rule, ARO, P2 stubs and the GL auto-bind; P3 — lease accounting; P4 — CF reconciliation property, credit, appetite, covenants, default lifecycle, reorganization (eligibility, stay, plan example, vote, conversion, completion, discharge accounting), taxes, net-worth coverage, investor and rescue fixtures; P5 — gold loan, revolver gold/AR, hedging covenants, specie; P6 — Yukon and temperate jurisdictions.

### 11.28 Decisions

- **D-11.1** — Two double-entry books (company, owner), integer cents; cash accounts can never go negative; no overdraft facility. — Matches §2 invariants; "out of cash" is always an explicit failed payment the player can trace.
- **D-11.2** — Sections create bills; §11 settles them by priority in step 14. Immediate `pay` only for player actions and for pipeline payments (COD deliveries, §6 auto-pay of statutory obligations, margin calls) that respect the priority reserve (D-11.35). — One place decides who gets paid when cash is short.
- **D-11.3** — Weekly payroll, paid in the week earned; one tax deposit (federal, FUTA, SUTA, MBT) one week later. — Matches the turn; small placer camps pay weekly or biweekly; a semi-weekly depositor is the right IRS schedule for this payroll size; folding the quarterly state and FUTA filings into it moves < 1% of payroll by weeks.
- **D-11.4** — Loan payments are monthly, due in `monthEndWeeks`, with interest at APR/12 per month accrued weekly; deposit yields use §2's compounding. — Reproduces real lender quotes exactly (R5 fixtures); weekly loan schedules would match no real product.
- **D-11.5** — The player may reorder payment categories 1–11; auto-debits are locked first and owner items last; payroll is paid pro rata. — Choosing whom to stiff is the real decision of a distressed owner.
- **D-11.6** — Owner score is FICO-like with decaying derogatories; the company has a Paydex-like index and an SBSS-like U (0–300) with capitalization-based thin-file scoring. — R5's real structure; the SBA 165 minimum lands naturally inside tier B.
- **D-11.7** — Gold inventory at absorbed production cost (operating weeks only) with LCNRV; market shown as a memo; P1 uses as-incurred costs. — GAAP-like and teaches that margin arrives at sale; net worth still uses market. Owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (closes OQ-11.2).
- **D-11.8** — ARO carried at undiscounted current cost × CPI, expensed at disturbance (no ARO asset); CPI escalation is the "accretion"; reclaim costs are reclassed against the liability. — Consistent with §1's net worth and Inheritor numbers; simpler than PV accounting; same lifetime expense.
- **D-11.9** — Operating leases are off balance sheet (tax-basis presentation common in small private compiled statements); finance leases are capitalized. — Keeps the covenant trade-off between the two lease types visible.
- **D-11.10** — No separate sale-leaseback product; equipment finance offers cash-out refinancing of unencumbered machines. — Same economics (a financing secured by the iron) with one fewer product.
- **D-11.11** — The revolver borrowing base includes an equipment sublimit and a seasonal over-advance besides gold and refinery AR; eligible gold is §10's metal account (75%), bank box (25%), and refinery AR (80%), never camp gold; in P4 (before §10's refinery) the base is equipment + over-advance only. — A gold-and-AR-only base is zero in spring, exactly when a northern miner needs the line; this is also the default answer to §10's OQ-10.1, so refineries need not move into P4.
- **D-11.12** — Royalty, stream, and prepay financing is deferred revenue drawn down at spot (as §1's Backed royalty); royalty sales use a payback multiple then a tail. — One accounting rule for all production sales; R5 small-deal structure.
- **D-11.13** — The binding DSCR test is annual at week 52 (calendar year = exactly one northern season); quarterly T12 tests only after a breach. D-11.62 moves it to the company's season-year end (week 26 for an arid primary climate). — Standard seasonal-borrower practice; avoids artifacts from T12 windows that straddle two seasons.
- **D-11.14** — §1.11's knobs are used as published: `finance.paymentGraceWeeks` (3/2/1) is the late-fee grace (shifting each lender's base grace by value − 2) and `finance.defaultTimelineMult` (1.25/1.00/0.75) scales each lender's base notice weeks (bank 10, captive 8, equipment finance 7, hard money 4). — Standard lands bank notices at ~70 days and equipment lenders at ~50 (R5: 60–90 / 30–60). §1.11 (the table's owner) adopts both rows with these values and labels the appetite shift in U points; the earlier additive 4/2/1 notice buffer is retired.
- **D-11.15** — The depository bank sets off unrestricted balances when it accelerates. — Real right of setoff (R5); makes bank default visibly different from equipment-lender default.
- **D-11.16** — Repossession happens only when §1 access allows heavy haul; until then the machine is locked out. — Remote collateral is why banks dislike mining; the lockout still hurts the season.
- **D-11.17** — *Amended, owner ruling 2026-10-05 (closes OQ-11.1).* Bankruptcy has two forms. **Liquidation** (Chapter 7) is terminal: the final settlement runs and the run ends. **Reorganization** (Chapter 11 Subchapter V; a sole proprietor files the same case as an individual in business) continues the run under a court plan, in every game mode (11.16.1–11.16.7). Forbearance, restructuring, the rescue partner and the workout remain the out-of-court levers before either. — The owner chose to allow reorganization. It is the real path for a small miner with a working operation and too much debt, and its price (three to five years of disposable income, credit marks, a capped scenario medal, and liquidation if the plan fails) keeps it from being a reset. It replaces the earlier "bankruptcy is always game over".
- **D-11.18** — Pass-through income uses the real 2026 single-filer brackets + SE tax + QBI, paid from the owner book with automatic tax distributions; the "24–32%" in §1 is the resulting marginal range. — Brackets reward income smoothing and make the depreciation election matter; owner-paid tax is the real pass-through cash trap.
- **D-11.19** — Single filer with no outside income; no excess-business-loss limit, AMT, or NIIT; QBI without the wage/UBIA cap. — Removes rules that rarely bind for this owner; directionally real.
- **D-11.20** — Tax depreciation choice is `bonus100` (default) vs MACRS; §179 not modeled separately; all disposal gains ordinary. — §179 gives the same result except for the income limit; recapture is the lesson that matters.
- **D-11.21** — Cost per ounce uses gross recovered fine oz (produced), counts in-kind royalties at spot as cost, and auto-classifies sustaining vs growth capex. — Producers report per oz; WGC treats royalties as cost; deterministic classification the player can override.
- **D-11.22** — The 13-week forecast is scheduled obligations plus plan-based production from the player's estimates, with a comonotonic P10/P90 band on grade, throughput, and freeze-up; spot is flat; held gold is not assumed sold. — Explainable, never leaks truth, and conservative.
- **D-11.23** — Unpaid wages and trust-fund taxes are personal for every entity type. — FLSA "employer" and TFRP rules (R5); closes the LLC walk-away exploit. §1's table should list wages.
- **D-11.24** — All policies renew in week 49; WC is pay-as-you-go monthly; EMR uses a simplified NCCI formula (W 0.05, ballast $15k, split $20k). — Real formula shape, few parameters, reproduces R5's "one claim ⇒ 1.2–1.6".
- **D-11.25** — Regional payroll and WC rates refine the shared 1.22× burden anchor: AK-style SUTA 2.0% on $51.7k (+0.5% employee), NV-style 2.95% on $41.8k, WC $7.50 / $4.00 per $100. — R4 §14, R5 §16: total burden 1.15–1.20× rather than a flat 1.22× (P1 keeps 1.22×).
- **D-11.26** — Prime stays at the calibration anchor's 7.0% (base 4.0% + 3%) though R5 reports 6.75% in early 2026. — The opening rate is §10's anchor; a 25 bp gap is immaterial.
- **D-11.27** — The owner is never covered by workers' comp (sole prop and LLC members excluded; corp officer opt-out by default). — R5 practice; §1 already routes owner medical costs to personal cash.
- **D-11.28** — Fiscal months are §1's `monthEndWeeks` spans. — Identical to §13's first-day rule for every week; one definition.
- **D-11.29** — §1's lender-appetite difficulty shift (±30) applies on the U scale (≈ one tier). — Easy opens bank and captive doors a tier early; hard pushes startups to C/D.
- **D-11.30** — District tax jurisdictions come from §3's `District.jurisdictionId`, the same key §8 payroll and §9 sales tax use: northern and Alaska-state → `akStyle` (license tax with holiday, no equipment property tax), arid → `nvStyle` (net proceeds, MBT, equipment property tax), temperate → `temperateStyle`, Yukon → `yukon`; patented-land property tax is §5's rate in every U.S. jurisdiction. — Matches the templates' real analogs (§1.4.1); one field instead of three names.
- **D-11.31** — Hard money at 14% + 3 points + 1% exit, interest-only, LTV 0.60 × OLV (plus PER-certified claims at 10–20% of P10 value), default notice 4 weeks late at standard difficulty. — R5 midpoints; ≈ 18% effective; always available if you own iron or proven ground.
- **D-11.32** — Equity offers value the company at scoring net worth plus half the unrealized P50 value of claims that carry a §4 PER or technical report, haircut 30% in distress. — Investors pay for proven ground, but not fully, never from hidden truth, and never from the player's unverified estimate.
- **D-11.33** — Lender gold sensitivity is per-lender and momentum-based (lag 4 weeks), replacing §10's single recommended `finance.ripple.spread`/`appetite` elasticities; valuation ripples use §10's `ripple` on `goldIdxReal`. — Lenders differ (hard money barely cares; banks flee), and the level of gold already reaches them through EBITDA and DSCR capacity.
- **D-11.34** — Payment categories gain `margin` (rank 3, after payroll taxes) for §10 variation-margin and gold-loan calls. — §10 asks for it; an unpaid margin call is a forced close-out next week, harsher than any vendor remedy.
- **D-11.35** — Pipeline payments outside step 14 (§6 auto-pay of statutory obligations, COD deliveries, margin) respect a priority reserve; player actions do not. — Keeps one payment order without moving §6's resolution out of step 13.
- **D-11.36** — Third-party financiers never see the player's own estimate class: royalty, stream, equity, and claim-backed hard money use production history or §4's PER/technical report (`lendableResource`). — Real buyers demand independent evidence; it makes §4's paid reports worth buying and blocks estimate-inflation exploits.
- **D-11.37** — Startup exposure caps ($250k per equipment lender or captive) and a 1.10× DSCR capacity test for seasoned borrowers; captive promos need 104 weeks in business. — R5 startup programs; closes the banker-plus-promo leverage exploit and the no-cash-flow-test leverage path.
- **D-11.38** — Streams use §5's fixed `streamPricePerFineOzCents` set at 20% of spot at signing, with the step-down threshold expressed on gross delivered value (1.875 × U). — Uses §5's published fields (no new §5 work); older real streams used fixed per-ounce prices.
- **D-11.39** — Coinsurance pays ratio × loss − deductible; §11 owns the gold-storage rates (camp safe `finance.ins.specieCampSafeRate` 2.0% × claimsMult, 10% deductible with a $5k minimum, not at fly-in; bank-box rider 0.5%, $2,500 deductible), and §10 and §12 cite the keys. — The standard formula; one owner per number. 2.0% sits inside R5's 1–3% remote specie range, and claimsMult replaces the earlier flat surcharge.
- **D-11.40** — Involuntary bankruptcy from payroll needs three consecutive runs short by ≥ 25% of net; any shortfall still triggers stage 3. — A 1% short payroll is distress, not liquidation; three deep misses are. *Amended 2026-10-05:* an involuntary trigger now opens the petition decision for a company eligible to reorganize (D-11.64), and converts an open case (D-11.68).
- **D-11.41** — Seller carry notes (§5) and the estate note are §11 loans with their own patience; a carry default forecloses the claim through §5 with no deficiency. — Land-contract practice; §5 already specifies the outcome.
- **D-11.42** — Cash flow statement built by a txn-level rule (non-operating txns have their P&L effect removed; ΔW only from operating txns), with a direct-method cross-check. — Guarantees reconciliation with absorption costing, write-downs, and deferred revenue, where account-level add-backs double-count.
- **D-11.43** — ARO is §6's `liabilityCents` (own-contractor cost incl. mobilization and +15%), posted weekly; accretion is the CPI part of the change. — One number for §6, §11, and net worth; weekly posting keeps net worth current.
- **D-11.44** — Obligations follow §6.9's rule by `consequence.kind`: statutory items (eight kinds, §6 D-6.41) are settled only by a player action or §6 auto-pay or auto-file and take their consequence at the end of step 13 on `dueTurn + graceWeeks`; billable items become §11 bills settled in step 14 of the due week, and their owner evaluates "missed" at `dueTurn + graceWeeks + 1` (§2.6, D-2.12). §11 no longer receives "due-week obligation payments" in step 13. — Sept 1 forfeiture can still happen, and a lease or loan payment settled in step 14 is never "missed" in step 13 of its own week.
- **D-11.45** — Before P4, §6 surety underwriting reads stubs: `companyScore850` = 0.3 × 600 + 0.7 × owner score (§6's thin-file blend), `creditTier` on its 620/670/720 bands, `workingCapital` = cash − AP − 13 weeks of debt service, `tangibleNetWorth` = scoring company NW − mineral properties − restricted cash, a distress stage from the P1 counter's arrears, and `ownerPersonalNW`. — §6 underwrites from P2. The flat 600 enters only as the thin-file component, so a long P2 game does not freeze every company at one score.
- **D-11.46** — The walkout labor lien sweeps every gold-sale receipt through `receive` to wage arrears and wage-claim damages first, ahead of the priority order, until they are zero. — Statutory liens on mine output (R5). One receipt path covers every sale channel.
- **D-11.47** — Save budget: 52 weeks of transaction detail, then monthly summaries that keep account × cost center × claim and a fixed cash-flow bucket; one payroll transaction per run, with a 13-run register; one settlement transaction per week; closed bills pruned after 52 weeks. — Keeps the year-10 finance slice near 0.5 MB, and every statement still rebuilds exactly. Detail survives where the player inspects it.
- **D-11.48** — §13 owns the season baseline (UI-only). §11 keeps only the forecast engine and exposes the P50 per-claim weekly series. — Baselines are presentation data. This leaves one owner and one shape.
- **D-11.49** — The forecast's P50 production line is §7's `productionForecast` in every phase. P1–P3 add it at the local-buyer net; P4 adds the P10–P90 band. — An outflows-only runway is falsely pessimistic mid-season and teaches players to ignore the main cash tool. It also gives §7, §10, §11 and §13 one P50 source.
- **D-11.50** — Gold loans and the revolver's gold and refinery-AR components ship in P5, because they need §10's metal accounts and refinery settlement. Streams ship in P4 with royalty sales, because technical reports exist from P4 and D-11.12 already treats both under one rule. If the owner moves §10's refinery and metal accounts to P4 (§10's OQ-10.1), §11.11 and D-11.11's gold/AR components move with them (11.24 and §10's phase plan together). — Records the deviation from "all lenders and products in P4" and keeps it to what the market dependency forces.
- **D-11.51** — Bank hedging requirement (P5): required at tier C or with bank exposure above $750k, optional otherwise; hedge 30% of next season's P50 within 13 weeks; −0.50 points while in force. — Lenders "may require" hedging. This makes the trade-off (protected loan, shortfall risk) reach ordinary bank borrowers, not only prepay and mining-fund deals.
- **D-11.52** — Sole-proprietor edges: for the first 104 weeks the owner's file stands in for the company's payment history (U +15 for a typical Bootstrapper), and there is no company return fee (LLC $1,500, corp $3,000 a year). — Gives the third entity a real early-borrowing and cost edge; full personal recourse stays its price (§1.6).
- **D-11.53** — The Inheritor's estate note pays Jun–Nov on the generalized schedule by default ($10,281.75 × 6/yr), from P1 and with no seasonal spread; 'level' remains selectable. — Preflight showed the Inheritor failing on spring liquidity; a family operation's bank note would be structured around its season. This moves about $25k out of the first spring.
- **D-11.54** — The canonical cash curve (11.15) is BALANCE's `refSmallNorthDebt` in year 2: 427 gross fine oz, $1,588k of receipts, $1,344k of ops outflows, and about $110k of winter rebuilds paid in January–April. — Matches the engine and the restated reference anchor (about 430 fine oz in an established season). It keeps the lesson: a −$111k June trough in a profitable year.
- **D-11.55** — Jurisdictions: `temperateStyle` (5.5% personal, 6.5% corporate, SUTA 2.5% on $50k, WC $6.00 mining, no production tax, 1% equipment property tax); Yukon has no §11 production tax (the export royalty is §6's interest); C$ convert at §10's `market.cadToUsd`; multi-jurisdiction income is apportioned by gold revenue. — One owner per number. The temperate values are model-knowledge midpoints for OR/ID/MT-style states [M], to be refined when that template ships.
- **D-11.56** — The distress watch window is `finance.distress.watchWeeks` (6/4/3, owned by §11, listed in §1.11, plus §8's alert bonus), read by stage 0 and by §13's `cash.projectedNegative`; it replaces `game.alerts.cashNegWarnWeeks`. — Stage 0 is a finance rule, so the key is a finance key; its values match the difficulty scaling §13 already used.
- **D-11.57** — §11's RNG streams are `finance-lender`, `finance-royaltyco`, `finance-equity` and `finance-insurance` (§2.3 registry). — Section-prefixed, hyphenated names like the other sections' streams.
- **D-11.58** — Banker edge = `finance.bankerCreditTierBonus` (1) × `finance.tierWidthPoints` (35 U points). The bank's 1-year history gate for bankers is kept as a second edge, which §1.7 lists. — §1's key now exists in §11. The relaxed gate is what lets a banker open an early bank line, which §1's value estimate counts.
- **D-11.59** — The P2 GL stub binds automatically, with an inbox note, the first week plan-tier coverage is needed. — §13 has no insurance UI before P4, and a gate the player cannot buy through would block P2 operations.
- **D-11.60** — Lien enforcement uses §5's `land.forcedSale` and `land.transferToCreditor`, and closings pay liens through `lienPayoff`; seller carry notes keep `land.onForeclose`. — One forced-sale flow for workouts, prepay defaults and rescue liens; the carry note's land-contract outcome stays distinct.
- **D-11.61** — Controller effects scale with §8's `controllerQuality(s)` = q: appetite +10q, spread −0.25q points, forbearance odds × (1 + 0.2q). — The constants stand for a skill-70 controller; skill still matters (§8 D-8.23).
- **D-11.62** — Annual lender tests run on a per-climate **season year**: `finance.seasonYearEndWeek` northern 52, arid 26. The DSCR covenant test (D-11.13), the revolver clean-up window (the 8 weeks ending at the season-year end) and any other annual-at-week-52 finance test read the company's primary climate: the climate of the district with the most operated bcy over the trailing 52 weeks, northern if none. A change of primary climate takes effect at the new climate's next end week. Books, statements and taxes keep the calendar year. — The week-52 dates assumed the northern season (§15 Conflict 2): an arid operator works October–April, so it was DSCR-tested and forced to clear its line mid-season. Keying the tests to the climate where the company actually operates keeps D-11.13's rationale (one whole season in each T12) in both climates; the operated-bcy rule is visible, and it cannot be moved by a token week of work. Seller carry notes follow their own claim's climate instead (§5 D-5.56).

- **D-11.63** — Bankruptcy is one numeric distress stage, 7, with a `form`: `reorganization` while a case is filed and unconfirmed, `liquidation` at the terminal end (`distress.liquidation` tells §1 step 16d to end the run). From confirmation the stage is evaluated from the ordinary conditions again, with plan installments as loan payments; `distressStatus(state).stageKey` gives other sections a string to test (`'reorganization'`, `'liquidation'`). — Every existing "stage ≥ n" rule keeps its meaning (draws, mercy, vulture offers, surety cancellation), §1's metric still reads 7 while a case is open, and a three-to-five-year plan does not freeze the ladder at its top rung: a missed installment shows as stage 2 like any missed loan payment.
- **D-11.64** — An involuntary trigger is a creditors' liquidation petition, which an eligible company may convert to reorganization as of right (§706(a)): a blocking `finance.involuntaryPetition` decision whose options run `finance/fileReorganization` or `owner/fileBankruptcy`. An ineligible company liquidates at once. The bot rule is §2's (D-2.33, which superseded the rule first recommended here): bots never file voluntarily; every catalog bot answers *reorganize* (no guarantor filing) and files the first plan that passes both tests in a fixed search over 156/208/260 weeks, level then seasonal, 5% reserve. — Real debtors can convert a creditor petition, and the decision keeps a player who runs many weeks unattended from being liquidated without the choice. The bot rule gives BALANCE a measurable reorganization share without letting bots time a voluntary filing.
- **D-11.65** — The stay covers pre-filing loans, bills and accruals, setoff, repossession and forced sales, and pauses the TFRP clock. It does not cover regulators (§362(b)(4)), insurance, §10 forward contracts (safe harbor), post-filing obligations, or demands on the owner's guarantees unless the owner files. Pre-filing wages up to the priority keep being paid (first-day wage order). Secured lenders get monthly adequate protection at the contract rate on their collateral value, and one unpaid month lifts the stay for that lender. — These are the lines real small cases draw. They keep the stay from being a free pause: the claim fee, the payroll, the insurance and the equipment lender's interest still have to be paid.
- **D-11.66** — Projected disposable income uses E' = 0.5 × (P10 + P50) of next season's plan-based production (the royalty buyer's conservative basis, without the history blend, so revenue and costs read the same plans), a 52-week plan-based operating outflow, the owner's living allowance, a 5% fleet replacement allowance and an optional reserve up to 10%, with no income-tax deduction. All of it goes to the plan, and an anniversary true-up returns half of production-basis EBITDA above the projection to unsecured creditors. — Real plans commit projected income. A conservative production basis and a small reserve make plans survivable, and the true-up stops a player from confirming on a deliberately small mine plan and keeping the recovery.
- **D-11.67** — Plan classes and tests: secured claims crammed down to collateral value (OLV for kept machines; claims at §5 `planInventory` collateral value, the summary buyer view, D-5.60) at prime + 2% over max(term, remaining term) ≤ 84 months, with the lien kept; priority taxes and government fines paid in full within five years of the filing; general unsecured creditors take the rest of PDI, capped at their claims; the owner loan is subordinated and survives; equity is kept. Feasibility is tested year by year (secured plus priority ≤ PDI after the trustee's share, and effective-date cash on hand). Best interest compares a general unsecured creditor's recovery percentage with its Chapter 7 dividend from the 11.16 waterfall, with claims at `planInventory` liquidation value (the quick-sale price). One vote roll decides consensual (discharge at confirmation, trustee fee once) or non-consensual (term fixed at 260 weeks, trustee fee on every payment, discharge at completion). — Subchapter V's real tests in a form the player can compute ahead from visible numbers. The single roll stands in for class-by-class voting, and its inputs (recovery against liquidation, lender temperament, reputation) are what creditors actually weigh.
- **D-11.68** — Plan period: installments are monthly `debt.secured` bills; two missed within any 52 weeks convert the case (one while §1's conversion motion is active); so do a payroll collapse (trigger (a)), a post-filing trust deposit 4 weeks late, trigger (b) after confirmation, two denied confirmations, a missing plan, or the debtor's own conversion. New credit needs court approval (+2 weeks) until completion. — A rolling window forgives an isolated slip but not a pattern, as a court ruling on a motion to convert would. Counting a cured miss inside the window keeps a player from riding a permanent one-payment arrear.
- **D-11.69** — Accounting: no reclassification at filing (pre-filing balances stay in their accounts, grouped on the balance sheet as "Liabilities subject to compromise" while the case is unconfirmed); at confirmation one entry replaces the claims with plan notes and books the discharge gain (consensual), or carries the full unsecured claim in the note and discharges the unpaid balance at completion (non-consensual; §1 D-1.60); "Reorganization items" sit after interest; the discharge gain is excluded from taxable income and reduces the NOL, then machine basis. — Keeps TFRP, the trust accounts and the obligation store working through the case. Matches the legal timing of discharge, so filing alone never raises net worth, and avoids a phantom-income tax bill the real exclusion prevents.
- **D-11.70** — Credit: the owner's file takes the full `bankruptcy` mark when the owner is a debtor (sole proprietor, or a filing guarantor) and a 120-point `affiliateBankruptcy` mark otherwise; the company file takes a 150-point mark that halves every 156 weeks and drops off at 507. A company's bankruptcy does not discharge its guarantor: at confirmation each guaranteed lender demands from the owner what the plan will not pay, up to the PG cap. — The ruling asks for marks on both files for 7–10 years. Business bureaus keep a filing almost ten years, and every lender asks principals about past business bankruptcies; the owner score is the game's one place for that question. Guarantees surviving the company's case is real and closes the "reorganize the LLC, keep the cash" path.
- **D-11.71** — The only new credit during an unconfirmed case is a DIP loan from the hard-money lender, at its terms, approved after 2 weeks whenever the offered unencumbered collateral covers it (no appetite roll), and rolled into a plan-term secured note at confirmation. The rescue partner is withdrawn until confirmation. — The ruling sets DIP financing at hard-money terms. A court order rests on collateral and need, not on a credit score the filing just crashed, and the roll-over is the usual DIP-to-exit path.
- **D-11.72** — A sole proprietor files the same Subchapter V case as an individual in business (§1182(1)), so personal debts join the plan and personal cash above the $25,000 exemption counts in the best-interest test. An LLC or corp owner may join as guarantor (`guarantorFiles`): the guarantees then join the plan, at the price of the full personal mark and personal cash in the best-interest test. — Subchapter V is open to individuals, which avoids a second, Chapter 13-style path. The guarantor choice is the real decision a guarantor faces when the company files.
- **D-11.73** — Reorganization ships in P4 with the full ladder. In P1–P3, and under `--rules p1`–`p3`, the P1 insolvency counter has no reorganization path and ends in liquidation. — The plan needs lenders, credit, taxes and the 52-week forecast from P4. Keeping the counter terminal in early phases reproduces their balance runs exactly.
- **D-11.74** — `Txn.seq` is the txn id's counter value, unique across both books; balances are stored as signed debit-positive cents; `CASH_NEGATIVE` also guards the owner's `own.cash`; the chart of accounts lives in `engine/systems/finance/accounts.ts`, not in `src/data`. — One counter orders every posting in both books without a second sequence; one sign convention turns the balance check into a plain sum to zero; the owner's personal cash must never go negative either (§1 1.9); account codes are part of the save format, and data files are meant for designers to edit.
- **D-11.75** — `netWorth` is defined in every mode from P0: `appraised` equals `scoring` until §4 and §5 value claims at P50; `book` is assets − liabilities on both books; P0's `scoring` uses ledger marks only, with the lot, metal-account, machine-resale and forward-MTM terms and the investor waterfall at zero. — Scoring, the history ring and the end report need a number from the first week, and the zero terms are exact while no lot, machine, forward or investor exists.

### 11.29 Open questions

No open questions remain in §11. Both earlier questions are recorded decisions:
- **OQ-11.1: Is bankruptcy always the end?** *Resolved, owner ruling 2026-10-05: allow reorganization.* Liquidation ends the run; a Subchapter V reorganization continues it under a court plan, in every mode, from P4 (D-11.17 amended; 11.16.1–11.16.7, D-11.63–D-11.73). BALANCE counts a filing of either form as a failure of the survival window it falls in.
- **OQ-11.2: Absorption costing on the player-facing P&L.** *Resolved, owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed.* Absorption costing with a market memo (D-11.7).
