### 13.2 Conventions: formatting, color, tables

**Number formatting.** All formatting lives in `ui/format`. Locale is fixed to `en-US` regardless of browser locale (D-13.12). Rounding is half away from zero (`Intl.NumberFormat` `roundingMode: 'halfExpand'`), the same as the engine's `roundCents`.

| Quantity | Rule | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| USD, general | thousands separators; cents shown only if abs value < `ui.fmt.centsHiddenAboveUsd` ($1,000); negative `−$` with a true minus sign | `$1,234,568` · `$999.50` · `−$45,123` |
| USD, financial statements | whole dollars on every line; negatives in parentheses; totals computed from cents, then rounded; footnote "Totals may differ by $1 from rounding" | `($45,123)` |
| USD, ledger | always exact cents (it is the record of account) | `$45,123.07` |
| USD, compact (KPI tiles, chart axes only) | abs value ≥ `ui.fmt.compactAboveUsd` ($100,000) → 3 significant digits with k/M | `$1.23M` · `$412k` |
| Unit costs | 2 decimals always (they are < $1,000) | `$13.60/bcy` · `$212.40/hr` |
| Gold | 3 dp below 100 oz, 2 dp at or above 100; the word **raw** or **fine** always shown | `52.901 raw oz` · `1,234.50 fine oz` |
| Gold price | `$/fine oz`, cents hidden above $1,000 | `$4,200/fine oz` |
| Grade | raw oz per bcy to 4 dp; tooltip adds g/m³ (2 dp) using `ui.fmt.ozPerYd3PerGPerM3` = 0.024581 | `0.0095 oz/bcy (0.39 g/m³)` |
| Volume | bcy as integers; lcy only inside haul detail, labelled | `6,377 bcy` |
| Percentages | 1 dp; changes in rates as percentage points | `78.4%` · `+0.5 pp` |
| Interest rates, APR | 2 dp (exception, D-13.16) | `8.75%` |
| Hours | machine meter integer (`12,430 h`); weekly hours 1 dp (`71.5 h`) | |
| Area / water | acres 1 dp; gpm integer | `4.2 ac` · `680 gpm` |
| Scores | integer with scale | `62/100` · `714 (300-850)` |
| Estimate ranges | P50 in bold, P10–P90 in muted text (`ink-3`, ≥ 4.5:1) | **`0.0090`** `(0.0050–0.0160) oz/bcy` |
| Dates | game week first, calendar dates (§1 `weekRange`) for orientation; ranges use an en dash | `Y1 Wk 29 · Jul 16–22, 2027` |

**Color semantics.** Tokens come from one validated earth-tone palette with a Daylight and a Lamplight step for every role (13.20). Rules:

- **Status** (`good`, `warning`, `serious`, `critical`) is reserved for state and always paired with an icon and a text label: check, triangle, diamond, octagon. It is never used to tell series apart. Status chips are **filled** with the status color and carry their fixed `status-*-on` label token in both themes (lamp-black `#1c1813` on good, warning and serious; white on critical), because the warning and serious fills are under 3:1 against Daylight surfaces and a light Lamplight ink on an amber fill would fail; status shown as bare text uses the `status-*-text` tokens, each ≥ 4.5:1 on every surface in its theme (D-13.31, D-13.61).
- **Deltas** take their color from the metric's `goodDirection` (`up` | `down` | `none`), not from the sign. Cost/oz up is critical-colored with a ▲ and `+`. Cash up is good-colored with a ▲ and `+`. Direction is always also shown by arrow and sign.
- **Money** in tables: negatives use the primary ink plus a minus sign or parentheses, never red alone. Critical-colored text (`status-critical-text`, with its icon) is reserved for values that are actually a problem: overdrawn forecasts, missed payments, breached covenants, a plan payment that would convert a reorganization case.
- **Links** use the `link` token, not `accent`, so a link and a primary button never look alike; both pass 4.5:1 as text.
- **Series**: categorical slots in a fixed order (slate, ochre, spruce, plum, glacier, rust, indigo, fireweed; 13.20). A claim keeps its slot across every chart in a session (`slot = order in which the claim was acquired, mod 8`). Filtering never repaints the remaining series. Plant lines are never told apart by series color, because the claim already owns it: lines carry the label `L1`–`L3` and an outline style (13.7).
- **Brass** (the gold ornament token) marks the brand only: the wordmark, the active nav item and the rule under screen titles. It never encodes data or state.
- **Estimate heat maps** use the value-suppressing palette in 13.5, slate below cutoff and gold above it. **Ownership** on the map uses 3 fills plus patterns (13.6).
- **Texture mode** (Settings > Accessibility) adds 45°/135° line fills to status chips, heat-map bins and stacked bars, for color-vision deficiency and print. "Texture" always means these accessibility patterns; the decorative paper finish on headers is called **grain** (13.20) and is a separate setting (D-13.60).

**Tables (one `DataTable` component everywhere).** Built on TanStack Table + TanStack Virtual (D-13.19).
- Sort by header click (shift-click adds a secondary sort). Filters in one row above the table: text contains, numeric ranges, enum multi-select, week ranges, plus global search. Column chooser: show, hide, reorder (each table defines a default and an "all columns" set). Sort, filter and column state persist per `tableId` in `UiPersisted.tableLayouts`.
- Rows are virtualized above `ui.virtualizeRowThreshold` (100). Row height is 32 px (comfortable) or 26 px (compact). Sticky header and sticky first column.
- Numbers are right-aligned in the data face with `tabular-nums`. Units go in the header (`Price (USD)`), not in cells. Headers use the data face too (the display face never appears inside a table). A totals footer appears where a sum means something.
- Clicking a row opens the entity's quick view in the drawer; double-click or `Enter` opens the full route. Checkboxes allow bulk actions (sell lots, archive messages). Every table offers "Export CSV" of the current view (13.17).
- Columns are only ever player-visible fields, so no sort order can rank by hidden truth.

### 13.3 Dashboard

**Purpose:** answer, in ten seconds, "am I okay, what needs me this week, and is the season going to plan?"

**Layout (12-column grid at ≥ 1280 px; panels collapse with their state persisted; no drag-customization, D-13.20).**

| Row | Panels |
|---|---|
| 1. KPI tiles (6) | **Cash** (value; runway `≈ N wks` = first forecast week with P50 ending cash < 0, else `13+`; sparkline of the last 13 weeks actual + the next 13 weeks forecast: P1–P3 a single line from §11's `forecast13Week` (scheduled outflows and known receipts **plus the P50 production line**: each planned cleanup's §7 `productionForecast` P50 fine oz at the local-buyer net, 11.19.6), labelled `incl. planned cleanups (P50)`; P4 the P50 line with a P10–P90 band; lowest projected point labelled) · **Available liquidity** · **Gold spot** (52-week sparkline from P5; flat label in P1) · **Gold inventory** (raw oz held, est. fine oz, value at best-channel net, §10 `netSalePerFineOz`) · **Season-to-date production** (raw oz **weighed** vs baseline P50, ▲▼ %) · **Net worth** (§11 `netWorth(state, 'scoring')`; hover shows the informational appraised figure) |
| 2 | **Needs your attention** (cols 1-7): blocking decisions first, then critical, then warning, each sorted by deadline. A row shows the icon, title, deadline (`due Wk 23, 2 wks`), a one-line consequence, and its primary action button (`Answer`, `Pay now`, `Open`). · **Season clock** (cols 8-12) |
| 3 | **Production vs plan** by claim (cols 1-7) · **13-week cash** (cols 8-12): line of forecast ending cash (P1–P3 one line incl. planned cleanups (P50), with a cleanup-inflow chip in each cleanup week; band from P4), a zero line, and chips for the large scheduled payments |
| 4 | **Last week** (cols 1-7): per claim, bcy washed, bottleneck stage (§7 `bottleneck`, the claim view; with a line tag such as `L2` when the line with the most plant shortfall is not L1, P3), plant idle % (§7 `plantIdlePct`), direct cost, cost per bcy washed, and the supervision chip (13.7); then cash in and out by category · **Next 4 weeks** agenda (cols 8-12; same rows as the Calendar agenda) |
| 5 (as phases arrive) | Permit pipeline mini-kanban (P2) · Fleet status: working / down / in shop (P3) · Crew morale: avg, min, trend · Covenant headroom (P4) · Investor stance (P4, Backed equity) · Top event risks (P5, §12 `select.eventRiskIndicators`) · **Financial health ladder** (shown once distress stage ≥ 1, while the P1 insolvency counter is open, and throughout a reorganization case) |

**Season clock.** One horizontal 52-week strip per district, segmented by `SeasonPhase`, with a "today" marker. Phase boundaries that have not yet happened are drawn as **ranges** (labelled "likely range", §1 1.4.4) from §1 `seasonForecast`, with texture; a revealed boundary becomes a solid tick. The widget reads a `seasonView` that exposes only revealed dates and the current forecast: the unrevealed fields of `DistrictYearSeason` (true breakup and freeze-up weeks, the `z` drivers) are hidden truth and never reach the UI (D-13.38).

```
fc            = §1 seasonForecast(state, districtId)        // { asOfWeek, breakup {p10,p50,p90} | null, freezeUp {p10,p50,p90} | null }
opStart       = revealed.operatingStart ? operatingStartWeek : fc.breakup.p50 + round(breakupDurMean)       // §1 1.4.4
expectedOpEnd = revealed.freezeUp ? operatingEndWeek : fc.freezeUp.p50 − 1                                   // operatingEndWeek = freezeUpWeek − 1
weeksIn       = week − opStart + 1                       (operating phase only)                               [weeks]
expectedLen   = expectedOpEnd − opStart + 1                                                                   [weeks]
progress      = clamp(weeksIn / expectedLen, 0, 1)
weeksLeftP50  = max(0, expectedOpEnd − week);  weeksLeftRange = [max(0, fc.freezeUp.p10 − 1 − week), max(0, fc.freezeUp.p90 − 1 − week)]
```
Example (§1 `northernInterior`; breakup revealed wk 19, operating start wk 20; at wk 25 the latest freeze-up issue is the week-1 climatology, P10/P50/P90 = 40/42/44). The label reads `Operating · wk 6 of ~22 · freeze-up likely wk 42 (40–44) · ~16 wks left (14–18)`. At the wk 27 re-issue the range narrows. Arid districts show the operating strip with monsoon (§1 `monsoonStartWeek`/`monsoonEndWeek` once revealed) and fire-restriction overlays instead.

**Production vs plan.** "Plan" is the claim's **season baseline**: a frozen snapshot of the visible projection, taken automatically after the claim's first operating week of the year with an active plan, or when the player clicks `Re-baseline` (`ui/rebaseline`). Baselines are presentation data in `UiPersisted.baselines`, never in `GameState` (D-13.30); the run worker captures them too (13.18). §13 is the only owner of the season baseline: §11 keeps no baseline state and no rebaseline action (D-11.48). From P4 the capture reads the claim's P50 weekly series from §11 `forecast13Week(state).productionByClaim` (`washBcy` for `weeklyBcy`), which is the same `projectOpsVisible` figure in an operating week, so P1–P3 and P4 baselines agree.

```ts
interface SeasonBaseline { claimId: ClaimId; year: number; takenTurn: number; source: 'auto' | 'manual';
  weeklyBcy: number;                                   // §7 projectOpsVisible(state, claimId).payWashedBcy at capture (claim total, all lines)
  opStartWeek: number; expectedOpEndWeek: number;      // seasonView at capture (arid: first running week … 52)
  gradeP10: number; gradeP50: number; gradeP90: number;// bcy-weighted §4 BlockEstimate grades over the planned cut
  recoveryEst: number }                                // §7 visible recovery on the §4 size-mix estimate
```
```
weeksDone       = clamp(week − opStartWeek, 0, expectedOpEndWeek − opStartWeek + 1)    // operating weeks completed before this week
planBcyToDate   = weeklyBcy × weeksDone                                                  [bcy]
actualBcyToDate = Σ WeekOpsResult.payWashedBcy over weeks opStartWeek … week − 1          [bcy]
varPct          = planBcyToDate > 0 ? actualBcyToDate / planBcyToDate − 1 : 0
status          = 'on track' if varPct ≥ −ui.planVarianceWarnPct (0.10)
                  'behind' if varPct ≥ −ui.planVarianceBadPct (0.25), else 'well behind'
planRawOz_k     = weeklyBcy × weeksDoneAtLastCleanup × grade_k × recoveryEst              k ∈ {P10, P50, P90}   [raw oz]
                  // weeksDoneAtLastCleanup = weeksDone evaluated for the week after the season's latest cleanup (0 before any)
actualRawOz     = Σ CleanupResult.rawOzWeighed this season                                 [raw oz]
```
Example: baseline 3,264 bcy/wk (the §7 7.8 week), opStart wk 20. At wk 30, weeksDone = 10, plan 32,640 bcy; actual 29,670 bcy → varPct = 29,670 / 32,640 − 1 = −9.1% → `on track`. Shown as bullet bars per claim: a light track for the plan, a dark bar for actual, a tick for the P10 plan. Status uses icon + label.

**Financial health ladder.** A horizontal stepper of §11 `distressStatus` stages: 0 Watch … 6 Forced sales / workout, then stage 7 drawn as a fork with its two forms side by side, **Reorganization** (Chapter 11 Subchapter V: the run continues) and **Liquidation** (Chapter 7: the run ends). Labels come from `stageKey`, so a case open at stage 7 reads `Reorganization`, never `Bankruptcy`. It shows the current stage, `nextTrigger.text` (`Missed payroll if cash < $38,400 at Wk 24 payroll`; `Creditors' petition in 3 weeks`; during a case the next case deadline, `Plan due Wk 37`, or after confirmation `Next plan payment $11,900 at Wk 40 · one more miss converts the case`), and counter-move buttons (sell gold, list equipment, renegotiate, partner offers, owner injection; from stage 4 `File for reorganization` when §11 `reorgEligibility` passes; during a case `Build the plan`, `DIP loan`, court-approved sales and `Convert to liquidation`) that route to the owning screens. **P1 form** (§11 11.16): `Arrears $12,400 unpaid since Wk 22 · liquidated at Wk 28 unless every arrear is paid · net cash −$8,150`, where net cash = cash − arrears and the deadline = `p1.openSinceTurn + finance.p1InsolvencyGraceWeeks` (8/6/4 by difficulty). The P1–P3 counter has no reorganization path (§11 D-11.73), so the fork is drawn only from P4. Below it the tile lists the P1 levers from §11 `distressStatus(state).counterMoves`, one row each with its cash effect, its timing and a button to the owning screen:

| Lever | Shown as | Routes to |
|---|---|---|
| Sell gold | `Sell 46.553 raw oz at the local buyer: ≈ $143k, this week` (§10 quote) | Gold > Sell |
| Sell iron | `Sell to a dealer at 0.80 × resale: up to $X, this week` (§9) | Equipment > Fleet, sell |
| Sell a claim | `Quick sale: 0.6 × buyer value ≈ $X, closes next week; liens paid at closing` (§5 `land/quickSell`) | Claim > Overview |
| Surrender a lease | `Stops future minimums and AMR; the paid advance is forfeited` (§5 `land/surrenderLease`) | Claim > Overview |
| Owner injection | `Personal cash $X available, this week` (§1 `owner/inject`) | Company & owner > Owner |
| Cut hours or lay off | `Lower payroll from the next run` (§7 plan, §8 layoff) | Operations > Plan; Staff |

Negotiated restructuring, forbearance, the rescue partner and the reorganization filing appear only with the full ladder (P4/P5).

**Sees vs true.** Forecasts and baselines are built from the player's estimates and are labelled `Uses your estimates`. Production uses weighed gold only.

### 13.4 Inbox & Decisions, and Calendar

**Inbox.** Two panes: a list (440 px) and a detail pane.

- Blocking decisions are pinned at the top with a critical chip and the text `Blocks advance`.
- List columns: severity icon, title, subject (claim, machine or person), created week, deadline, status (open / resolved / answered / defaulted). Filters by severity, kind, subject and created-week range (a run's summary links here with its range, 13.9). Sort by deadline (default) or by created.
- **Decision detail** shows the context text with entity links, then one card per option. Each card shows the consequence text, the cost and `validateAction` result, the success probability where the outcome is stochastic (§12 event responses; with its explain tree), and any forecast delta via the owning section's preview selector. For a non-blocking decision it also shows the deadline and the **default option** in bold: `If you do nothing by Wk 23: Decline`. `Answer` dispatches `decision/answer { decisionId, optionId }`, whose handler validates and applies the option's stored engine action (`event/respond`, `land/respondCounter`, `finance/answerForbearance`, `investor/answerRequest`, …).
- **The involuntary petition** (§11 `finance.involuntaryPetition`, blocking, P4): the context names the trigger (three short payrolls, or 13 weeks at stage ≥ 4 with distressed asset value below zero) and the eligibility checks; option cards are *Reorganize* (`finance/fileReorganization`), *Reorganize with the owner as guarantor* (LLC or corp only; `guarantorFiles: true`) and *Liquidate* (`owner/fileBankruptcy`, ends the run). Each card carries the consequences listed on the Reorganization tab's filing step (13.11) and a link to it. Being blocking, it has no default option and is pinned with `Blocks advance`.
- **Agency messages** (§6 permits, inspections, violations; §12 enforcement events) name the body only through §6 `agencyFor(state, claimId, key)`: the full name with the abbreviation at the first mention (`Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)`), the abbreviation after that. They are plain game text in the normal inbox layout: no seals, logos, letterhead, signatures, names of real officials, form numbers or display-face mastheads, so nothing reads as a real filing or notice (D-13.67).
- **Event cards** (§12 `eventDisplay`): title, severity chip, scope label, start week and expected end, effects summary, loss and insured amounts, the mitigation text (`evt.<id>.mitigation`), and `Prepare next time` linking to the claim's Risk tab when a §12 preparation exists.
- **Grouped obligation messages** (13.10) show the count and total in the title (`12 claim maintenance fees due Wk 35 · $2,400`) and expand to one row per obligation (claim, amount, status, its own `Pay now` / `File`). The primary button acts on the whole group: `Pay all` dispatches §6 `permits/payObligations { ids }` (P1) and `File all` dispatches `permits/fileObligations { ids }` (P2), each over the group's open, payable or fileable IDs in §6's priority order; a `BATCH_PARTIAL` notice lists what was left unpaid.
- Messages that are not decisions offer `Open subject`, `Snooze` (1/2/4 weeks; not allowed on critical or blocking), `Mark read` and `Archive`. Info messages auto-archive after `ui.inboxAutoArchiveInfoWeeks` (8).
- Trade-off (non-blocking decisions): leaving the default avoids a click, but defaults are always the conservative choice (decline, standard package), never the best one.

**Calendar.** Game time is weekly, so there is no daily month grid (D-13.17).
- **Agenda** (default; P1): the next `ui.agendaWeeks` (26) weeks grouped by week, then by category. Rows: due week, category icon (§6 `ObligationCategory`, plus `payroll`, `cleanup`, `season` for non-obligation items), title, amount, consequence (§6 `consequence.text`, e.g. `Claim forfeited if unpaid`), status (§6: upcoming / due / satisfied via payment, filing, work or auto-pay / missed / waived / cancelled / cured / **in plan**, the last for an obligation a reorganization case pays through the plan, §6 6.8, shown with a link to the case and no `Pay now`), and an action (`Pay now` = `permits/payObligation` or `finance/payBill`; `File` = `permits/fileObligation`; `Auto-pay` where `autoPayEligible`). Each week header with two or more payable items carries **`Pay all due this week`** (`permits/payObligations { ids }` over that week's open obligations with `payableNow`, P1) and, from P2, `File all due this week` (`permits/fileObligations`). P1 content: §11 bills and fixed-loan payments, payroll weeks, §5 lease anniversaries and advance minimum royalties, scheduled cleanups, season dates.
- **Year planner** (P2): 52 columns (weeks) × category rows. Rows: season phases per district (forecast ranges textured), obligations by category, loan and lease payments (§11), payroll weeks, tax installments (P4), scheduled cleanups (§7 `cleanupEveryWeeks` projected), expected permit decision windows (P10–P90 bars from §6 `stageForecast`), auction closings (§5/§9), deliveries and mobilizations (§9), lease anniversaries (§5), announced event effects (§12 `select.scheduledEventEffects`), investor check-ins (§1, weeks 13/26/39/52).
- Filters by category and claim. Clicking any item opens its source entity; week cells show `Mon d–Mon d` on hover; obligations inside their alert lead window (13.10) carry the matching status chip.

### 13.5 Claims market, owned ground, claim detail, prospecting

**Claims market.** A toggle switches between cards and table. Filters: district, access, acres, title kind (§3 `ListingInfo.titleKind`: unpatented / patented / state, the parcel's legal type; patented listings appear from P2), deal (buy / lease / lease with option), price range, royalty range, water (gpm), distance to town, has history, inherited reclamation (P1: acres and §3's $6,000/acre stub, labelled `estimate (no enforcement until permits)`); P2 adds permit and bond status and open ground; P5 adds listing type (normal / estate / distressed / auction) and competing interest. Owned ground is described by §5 `Tenure.kind` (the player's holding), never by `titleKind`. A star **watches** a listing through §3's engine action `world/setWatch { claimId, on }` (a district is watched with `{ districtId, on }`). §3 refuses a 41st watched claim with `WATCH_LIMIT` (§4 `geology.maxTrackedClaims` 40). Watched claims are re-estimated weekly by §4 and raise §3's listing and price-change notices (D-13.45). "Save search" (P2) stores the filter (max `ui.maxSavedSearches` = 20) and can raise a match notice and a stop rule.

Table columns (default set marked *):

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| Listing* | name/ID, badges (Watched, Permitted P2 (seller statement until a records check), Estate P5, Distressed P5, Auction closes Wk N P5, Court sale · hearing Wk N P4 (a claim sold during a reorganization stay, §5 5.14)) |
| District / creek* | |
| Acres (blocks)* | |
| Access*, Dist. to town (mi)* | access icon + text |
| Water (gpm) | §3 baseline plus `Seasonal: see §1 flow` note |
| Title*, Deal* | `titleKind`; option and buy-down clause icons |
| Asking price*, $/acre | |
| Royalty %, Advance min. royalty | lease listings |
| Permits & bond | P2 (P1 column hidden) |
| Inherited reclamation | acres / est. $; P1 labelled `estimate (no enforcement until permits)` |
| Seller-claimed grade* | labelled **seller claim (unverified)** in muted italics |
| Seller check* | §4 status: unchecked / consistent / questionable / implausible (P1); verified / contradicted (P2) |
| Your est. grade P50 (P10–P90)* | from `knownEstimate`; `—` if no evidence beyond priors |
| Confidence* | `speculative / inferred / indicated / measured` chip |
| Listed (weeks), Expires* | |
| Competing interest | P5: §5 band (`Others viewing` / `Bid received`) |

A card shows a thumbnail of the block grid (your estimate layer, or uniform gray when unsampled), the key facts, the ask, and the badges.

**Owned ground** (Owned tab) columns: claim*, district/creek*, tenure* (owned / leased / staked / JV), acres*, site status* (§7), plant lines (active / allowed, `2 / 3`, P3), supervision* (the 13.7 chip), authority* (P2), minable raw oz P50 (P10–P90)*, confidence*, season bcy washed*, season raw oz weighed*, season cash cost per fine oz*, royalty burden %, holding cost/yr (§5 `holdingCostAnnual`), next obligation*, open disturbed acres and ARO (P2).

**Claim detail tabs.**

| Tab | Panels and content |
|---|---|
| Overview | Facts (acres, blocks, access, distance, water, regime, title kind, existing permits and bond (P2), inherited liability: P1 acres × §3's stub labelled `estimate (no enforcement until permits)`). **Listing:** terms and a **seller panel**: seller type (individual / estate / company / competitor), weeks on market, stated reason, records offered, presented permits and bond (P2, labelled `seller statement` until checked), disclosed issues, and the fixed note `Seller figures are unverified evidence`. Seller honesty type is never shown. Listing actions: `Records check` (§6 `permits/recordsCheck`, $250 and 1 week: the true permit tier and bond, P2; §5 also folds it into every P2+ closing) and `Request inspection` (§5 `land/requestInspection { weeks 2–8, allowedTier }`, a fixed-fee test-before-buy window, P2; refused by sellers with competing interest). **Owned:** a **tenure panel** from §5: tenure kind and start; production interests (holder, kind, basis, rate, settle, minimum, buy-down terms); lease terms (term, renewal, advance minimum royalty schedule and recoupable balance, work commitment progress, option price and expiry); actions `land/buyDownRoyalty`, `land/exerciseOption`, `land/setLeaseRenewal`, `land/surrenderLease`, `land/relinquish` (with `confirmUnreclaimed` from P2), `land/quickSell` (P1: `land.quickSaleFrac` 0.6 × the visible buyer valuation, closes next week; the P1 distress lever) and `land/listClaim` (P4). During a reorganization stay both create a **court sale** (§5 5.14): the panel shows the stalking-horse bid, the hearing week, qualified overbids as they arrive and the breakup fee, with the note `Court-approved sale: the ask cannot change after the stalking horse` (P4; competitor overbids P5). |
| Estimate | **Verdict line** at the top, from §4 `estimateVerdict(state, claimId)` (4.14): `Likely 970–2,100 oz in the 11 blocks that could pay (8 in 10). At current costs they pay back in about 9 of 10 cases. Biggest unknown: unsampled ground.` (the payback clause is omitted without a decision context). Its numbers are `<Num>`s that explain into the panels below. Until the end of the company's first operating season the panels below start collapsed, with `Show the full estimate` (the choice is kept per claim for the session); afterwards they start expanded (D-13.52). The same line heads the listing card and the listing's Overview. **Block-grid heat map** (below) with layer toggles. Summary from `ClaimEstimate`: contained raw oz P10/P50/P90, minable raw oz P10/P50/P90, minable bcy, average strip, average minable grade P50, recoverable raw oz P50, fine oz P50, and the confidence class with the gate that blocks the next class (§4 `gates.failing`: `Indicated needs coarse factor sd ≤ 0.10: now 0.20; a bulk sample would do it`). Panels: coarse factor P10–P90; size mix and fineness (P50 ± sd). **Estimate fan chart** from §4 `knowledge.history[claimId]` (`EstimateSnapshot`s): contained and minable P10–P90 bands with P50 lines, x = week, markers by snapshot trigger (program, records, production, seller, price, report), a dashed seller-implied line, certified-report markers. **Planning assumptions** (`prospect/setPlanning`): price basis, recovery (auto or override), mine-and-wash $/pay bcy, strip $/bcy, mining loss, dilution; trade-off `A higher planning price grows minable ounces on paper, not in the ground`. **Value of information** (P2): §4 `ClaimEstimate.voi` top three (cost, weeks, expected spread, class reachable; EVSI net of cost once a decision context is set), labelled `Approximation; not money you will earn`. |
| Evidence | Evidence log table: week, type (§4 `EvidenceRef` kinds: sample, production, records, family records (Inheritor), tell, geophysics, seller claim, report), blocks, volume (bcy), result, used in estimate? (`Yes` / `No: unverified seller claim`), source (program, consultant), logged by, notes. The seller check line from §4 (`Seller's figure is 2.3× your estimate; chance of honest sampling noise 2.5%`). Seller claims and family records stay in the log, flagged as biased evidence with zero weight until verified (§4 4.10). A **tell** row (a §3 `SellerTell` found by a records review, geologist review or site visit) shows its channel, found week and text (`The Notice file shows about 15 pits; 6 are reported.`) and links to the seller-check line; a tell can move the seller check (here to `contradicted`) but never the grade estimate. |
| Valuation | §5 5.13 from the player's estimate: NPV at P10/P50/P90 (`valueClaimForPlayer`), breakeven spot (`breakevenSpot`), breakeven grade at the claim's average strip (`breakevenGradeOzPerBcy`, includes royalty burden and capital charge), maximum price for the player's target return at P50, the ask and the seller-implied $/oz in the ground; **tornado chart** (`valueSensitivity`: NPV P50 at ×0.8 and ×1.2 of spot, contained oz, recovery, cost per bcy, strip; one axis); **structure comparison** (PV cost of sale vs lease terms at P10/P50/P90: the lease is cheaper at P10, dearer at P90); **walk-away loss** (price + one year's holding and AMR + reclamation of what was disturbed). Label `Uses your estimate; mine-as-estimated`. |
| Offer | Offer / lease stepper (below) |
| Risk (P5) | §12 `select.eventRiskIndicators(claimId)` chips (flood exposure, fire level, theft exposure, permafrost slump) and the §12 preparations that mitigate them, each with cost, build weeks, life, upkeep and effect; `Build` dispatches `prep/build` (trade-off `Cash and machine-hours now vs tail risk later`). Machine-scope preps (`fireSuppression`, `fuelPolishing`) appear on machine detail from P3. |
| Ops / Permits / P&L | Owned claims only: links to Operations, the claim's permits (13.8, P2) and §11 `claimPnL` for the claim |

**Block-grid heat map.** The grid follows §3: a claim is `nAlong × nAcross` blocks, block index i along the valley (downstream → upstream) and j across. Block labels are column letter (j) + row number (i + 1), e.g. `C4`. When `nAlong > ui.heatmapLongAxisRows` (10) the long axis runs horizontally so a 40 × 4 claim fits; cell size = clamp(floor(panel size / cells), 20, 48) px around `ui.heatmapCellPx` (32); a flow arrow marks downstream. Default layer: **estimated grade against cutoff**, using §4 `BlockEstimate.cutoffOzPerBcy` from the player's planning assumptions, so the colors agree with §4's minable outline (the Valuation tab shows §5's breakeven grade, which adds royalty burden and a capital charge; D-13.8). The palette is a value-suppressing uncertainty palette (VSUP): uncertain blocks collapse toward neutral gray, so "don't know" never looks like "rich".

```
gC        = BlockEstimate.cutoffOzPerBcy                    // raw oz/bcy; §4 planning assumptions and the block's strip
r         = log2(gradeP50 / gC)                             // > 0 means above cutoff
vBin      = clamp(round(r / ui.heatmapLog2Step), −3, +3)    // step 0.5 → edges at ×0.42/0.59/0.84/1.19/1.68/2.38 of gC
ratio     = gradeP90 / gradeP10                             // §4's spread measure for a block
uBin      = 0 if ratio ≤ ui.heatmapRatio1 (2); 1 if ≤ ui.heatmapRatio2 (4); 2 if ≤ ui.heatmapRatio3 (8); else 3
classes   = [7, 5, 3, 1][uBin]                              // value bins merged as uncertainty grows
mergedBin = sign(vBin) × min(|vBin|, (classes − 1) / 2)
fill      = diverging ramp (div-neg ← div-mid → div-pos) at mergedBin, blended toward div-mid by uBin × 0.25
texture   = none (uBin 0) | light hatch (uBin 1) | heavy hatch (uBin ≥ 2)      // = §4 4.14 hatching thresholds
glyph     = sample count (small, corner) if sampleCount > 0; '?' if uBin = 3;  outline = BlockEstimate.minable
```
Example: a block estimated at P10 0.0050, P50 0.0090, P90 0.0160 oz/bcy, with gC = 0.0060. Then r = log2(1.5) = 0.585, so vBin = round(1.17) = +1. ratio = 3.2, so uBin = 1 (5 classes) and mergedBin = +1. The block renders "above cutoff, light gold, 25% toward the neutral midpoint, light hatch" with its sample count. An unsampled block with prior P10–P90 of 0.001–0.030 has ratio 30, so uBin = 3: gray with `?`.

Other layers (one at a time, legend always visible), matching §4 4.14: grade P50 (`seq-gold`); uncertainty ratio (single-hue `seq-slate`); depth to bedrock; pay column; strip; margin $/pay bcy; block confidence class; worked areas (old workings from records); sample markers by method (a `status-critical` ring with a down-arrow glyph = short of bedrock, a `status-warning` ring with `?` = suspect false bedrock, hollow ring = seller's sample; the glyph, not the color, carries the meaning); seller-claimed grade (hatched, labelled `seller claim`); thaw progress (northern, §7); state overlay (mined = cross-hatch, disturbed = dashed rust border, reclaimed = dotted spruce border, selected cut = thick accent outline with sequence numbers; with several plant lines each line's cut keeps its own outline style and `L2·3` labels, 13.7). Keyboard: arrow keys move focus; each cell's accessible name reads like `Block C4: est. 0.0090 oz/bcy (0.0050–0.0160), 3 samples, above cutoff, moderate uncertainty`.

**Offer / lease stepper.**
(1) Structure: purchase, lease, or lease with option (as the listing allows). (2) Terms: price, down payment, royalty %, advance minimum royalty, work commitment. In P1 these are read-only at asking. (3) Affordability: §5 `previewOffer(state, listingId, structure, terms)` → cash at close, closing costs, first-year obligations, validation; plus the change to the 13-week forecast and runway after closing. (4) Review & submit: P1 dispatches `land/acceptAsk { listingId, structure }`; live `validateAction` errors appear inline. From P2 the closing runs §6's records check automatically in week 1 (its $250 shows in closing costs, skipped if one ran on the claim within 4 weeks) and a material finding arrives as the `land.titleFinding` decision.

In P5 the stepper dispatches `land/makeOffer` with editable terms and adds a round history (offer / counter table), the deadline in weeks, best-and-final, the competing-interest band, `Order diligence` (`land/orderDiligence`, report in 1 or 3 weeks) and the title-finding decision. Qualitative seller signals come from §5 (`Listed 14 wks`, `Estate sale`); the seller's hidden motivation is never shown. Trade-off line on step 2: `Lower price or royalty → better economics, higher chance the seller walks or a competitor wins`. **Auctions** (P5): a bid panel (`land/placeBid`: maximum bid or sealed bid, deposit moved to restricted cash, `Closes Wk N`). **Staking** (P2): open parcel (map or Staking tab) → units 1–8 → costs (location, processing, first year's fee per §6) → recording and filing windows (become obligations) → `Auto-file` (`land/setAutoFile`) → `land/stake`.

**Prospecting.**
- **Programs** table: program, claim, method, delivery (own / contractor), crew, machines, geologist, progress (`pits 6/10`), status (§4: planned / awaiting access, permit, contractor or season / mobilizing / active / paused with reason code / complete / cancelled), weekly cost, spend to date vs budget cap, permit tier needed. Row actions: modify, pause / resume, cancel (demobilization and deposit rules shown).
- **Program setup** form (`prospect/createProgram`): claim; method from §4's table showing cost, time, sample volume, what it measures and permit tier (P1: hand pit (rocker) / drywasher, run through §9's `rocker` or `drywasherHand` site tool, and excavator pit, own or contractor at $2,500/pit north (≈ $1,900 arid) with a 1-week lead; P2: trench, bulk sample, geophysics; P3: drilling); delivery; targets picked on the block grid (blocks, cross-valley fences, lines); sample bcy; crew and machines (conflicts with mine plans flagged as `ASSET_DOUBLE_BOOKED`); geologist (owner / staff / consultant); days/week, hours/day; budget cap; order (as listed, or by VOI from P2). It shows §4's cost and duration estimate. Trade-off on the form: `More or bigger samples → tighter estimate, more cash and weeks before you can bid or mine`.
- `Site visit` on any listing or owned claim (§3 `world/siteVisit { claimId, ownerTime? }`: travel cost by access, §1 owner desk days, ground features, seller tells; the report arrives as `siteVisit.report`). `Pan survey` (§4 `prospect/panSurvey { claimId, people, stations, ownerTime? }`) rides on a site visit and books one if none is booked this week; on a listing it needs §5 `samplingAccess` (P1: seller permission allows pans only, `NO_ACCESS` otherwise).
- **Records & consultants** tab: records review (`prospect/recordsReview`; P1 creek history and old workings, P2 all items), consultant engagements (`prospect/engageConsultant`: supervision P1, PER and audit P2, technical report P4), seller data request and verification (P2), contractor bookings and rig ETAs (P3 full).
- **Sample log** columns (§4 report): sample ID, week, claim, block, method, depth reached, bedrock Y/N, pay bcy, particles by size class, recovered mg, head grade (raw oz/bcy), non-coarse grade, flags.
- The **results report** opens as a drawer: before/after estimate and class, cost by line, findings, the fan chart, and up to three recommendations (only with a geologist, §4 4.12).

### 13.6 District map

A simple 2D SVG per district, with pan (drag), zoom (wheel, `+`/`−`) and `0` to fit. Its title names the district and its real jurisdiction (`Caribou Fork · fictional district in Alaska, federal land`; §6 6.1), drawn on the flat `surface-1` (never grain). It is drawn only from §3's `districtMap(state, districtId)`; the UI reads no `District` geometry directly. The frame is `{widthMi, heightMi}`; creeks are `creeks[].points` with stroke width by `order` and their names; claims are `claims[].polygon` (four corners from §3's geometry), with the `nAlong × nAcross` block grid drawn at zoom ≥ 2; the town is an icon at `town.positionMi` (an edge marker with road miles when it lies off the map) with `town.services` on hover; airstrips are icons; overlays (withdrawn, special status) are hatched `overlays[].polygon`s with their labels. Access: `routes[]` carries the district road from the map edge to the outlet and the trails beyond it, each segment tagged with its `access` (highway = thick solid, seasonal road = thin solid, winter trail = dotted with its window label from §1 `accessOutlook`, e.g. `open wk 2–13`). The **P1 base map** is exactly this plus the ownership fills below, because the P1 choice between the northern and arid districts turns on access and distance; the water, estimate, permit, risk and activity layers come later (D-13.49).

**Claim fills (≤ 3 categorical fills for an all-pairs form, D-13.24).**

| Status | Fill / pattern | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Yours (owned / leased / JV) | slot-1 slate solid / slate with 45° texture / slate with 135° texture | claim name |
| Listed for sale or lease | slot-2 ochre 2 px dashed outline, light ochre fill; star badge if watched | ask on hover |
| Competitor-held (P5) | neutral gray solid | company initials |
| Open ground (stakeable, P2) | no fill, thin outline | `open` |
| Private / unavailable / withdrawn | light gray, no label | |

Layers (P2+): water availability, your estimate (minable P50 per claim vs its cutoff, for claims with evidence), permit status, event risk (P5: flood exposure, fire level), recent activity (P5: new listings, competitor moves). Hover shows a tooltip card; clicking opens claim detail. The **Companies** tab (P5) lists competitors with only §12 `select.competitorPublic` fields: name, profile label, home districts, status (active / distressed / bust), claims held (count, acres, active this season), approximate fleet and crew size (±20%), auction results and disclosed claim deals, rumored last-season production (labelled `rumor`), and recent news. Actions: `Approach for a claim` (`competitor/approachForClaim`, P5) and `Approach acquisition` (P6).

### 13.7 Operations, Equipment, Staff

**Operations (per claim; `[` and `]` cycle claims).** A header shows the claim, the site status chip (§7 `SiteStatus`: none / mobilizing / ready / running / winterizing / winterized / demobilizing; plus `standby` when the plan is inactive), the supervision chip (below), the authority chip (P2), risk chips (P5), and the actions valid for the status: `ops/mobilizeSite` (cost, weeks and access window shown), `ops/startup`, `ops/setPlanActive`, `ops/setLineActive` (P3, per line), `ops/cleanupNow` (one line or every line), `ops/movePlant` (per line), `ops/winterize`, `ops/demobilizeSite`, `ops/drillWell` (P1; arid claims without a creek source, up to 2 wells, yield revealed after `ops.wellWeeks`), `ops/tailingsAudit` (per line), `ops/buildPond` (P2), `ops/cleanPond` (P2; sludge cleanout of the pond on a block), `ops/queueReclamation` (P2). Disabled actions show their validation code as the reason.

| Tab | Content |
|---|---|
| Site | Site lifecycle timeline (mobilization, start-up crew hours, winterizing), camp and pad, fuel on hand, water source and pond (P2), disturbance ledger by feature (P2), reclamation queue (P2) |
| Plan | The **plan editor** (below): claim-wide schedule and stripping, one tab per plant line, the supervision line for each line, cut selection, the assignments board and the preview panel |
| Flow | A **line selector** (`Claim`, then `L1` … `Ln` from P3) above everything: the claim view reads `WeekOpsResult` and its claim-view `bottleneck` and `plantIdlePct` (§7 7.8), a line view reads that line's `LineWeekResult`; strip, water and power are shared stages and carry a `shared` tag in a line view (D-13.62). **Stage bars** (the bottleneck view, D-13.6): one row per stage (strip, dig, haul, feed, plant, water, power, tailings), built by the UI selector `stageRows` below. Each row shows capacity (light track), achieved throughput (dark bar), utilization %, and a stacked bar of every scheduled hour by §7 `IdleCause` (labels below). The root stage `WeekOpsResult.bottleneck` carries a `Bottleneck` chip; root-only stages (`pay`, `thaw`, `crew`, `fuel`) appear as a banner (`Bottleneck: no exposed pay; stripping is behind`). A headline sentence comes from the largest plant idle cause (example below). **What-if hints** (§7 `hints`, top three by Δ washed bcy): `+1 30t truck: +891 bcy/wk, ≈ +7 raw oz/wk (visible model), ≈ $9.0k/wk` (§7 `WhatIfHint` `deltaWashedBcy`, `deltaVisibleRawOz`, `weeklyCostUsd`). **Stripping coverage** gauge (§7 `strip`: done vs need, coverage weeks, standalone coverage per strip machine: `The D8 alone keeps up (113%)`). **Water balance** (need vs pumps vs source vs recirculation vs trucks; plant hours water-limited; with several lines, each line's share `allocGpmAvg` and its water-limited hours, labelled `shared with L2`) and **power** (demand vs supply, shed loads). Per-machine utilization table: machine, role, line, scheduled h, worked h, utilization, idle h by top cause and root, fuel gal. Secondary: material-flow Sankey in bcy only (stripped → backfill / dumps; pay dug → hauled → pad Δ → washed → tailings) and a gold flow (visible model before cleanup, weighed after: washed → box (foreman's estimate) → weighed → in-kind royalties → lots). |
| Production | Follows the line selector (the baseline is a claim figure, so a line view shows no baseline). Weekly bcy washed (columns) with the baseline line; season-cumulative raw oz weighed (step line at cleanups) vs baseline P50 with a P10–P90 band; **grade reconciliation** chart (below); cost per bcy and per est. fine oz over weeks; estimated recovery by size class (§4 size-mix P50 × §7 capture for the circuit, bars with ranges); tailings audit results when run (estimated lost raw oz by size: the only window onto true recovery, §7 7.14) |
| Cleanups | Cleanup log from §7 `CleanupResult` (one row per line cleanup, so a week can hold two or three rows, ascending `lineId`): #, week, line, weeks covered, bcy washed since last, foreman's box estimate (raw oz), raw oz weighed, recovered grade (raw oz/bcy), in-kind interests taken (raw oz, by holder), net raw oz to inventory, lot ID, est. fineness and its basis (§10 `estBasis`; `assayed 0.847` once assayed), est. fine oz, reconciliation factor |

**Plan editor** (Operations > Plan; dispatches §7 `ops/setMinePlan`). Every range comes from §7, and new plans start from §7 `defaultMinePlan(state, claimId)`, never from UI constants (currently one line, L1; 6 days × 1 shift × 10 h; cleanup every 2 weeks on the off-day; feed = rated; bedrock take `ops.defaultBedrockTakeFt` 1.5 ft; piles on cut blocks first; D-13.55). The draft stays in the UI (`drafts.minePlans`) until `Apply plan`.

- **Claim-wide strip** (top): days/week (0–7), shifts/day (1–2), hours/shift (4–12), stripping ahead (blocks ahead, extra strip blocks, clearing; one strip queue serves every line), reclamation crew hours. **Advanced** (collapsed): bedrock take (ft), pay-top policy (tight / standard / generous), water-short policy, water mode (closed loop / discharge; discharge needs §6 coverage, P2) and recirculation, water trucks per day, allow redeploy, program priority, crew shift assignment, manual operator pairing, cut source per block (in situ / old tailings / own tailings / pile then in situ), winter ops, fuel fill target and fuel by air (P3). One water budget, one schedule and one disturbance footprint serve the whole claim (§7 7.2.1), so none of these is per line.
- **Line tabs** `L1` · `L2` · `L3` · `+ Add line`. Each tab holds that `PlantLine`: its cut, wash plant (`plantMachineId`), feed spread (the dig, haul and feed machines and the concentrators on its plant, `machineIds`), plant site block, pad stockpile cap, plant feed target (bcy/hr; slider to `ops.plantMaxOverfeed` × rated = 150%, with a warning band above 100%), cleanup every N weeks (0 = on demand, 1–8) with `Clean up on the off-day`, and the line's active toggle (`ops/setLineActive`; standby forces that line's cleanup and keeps its pad). Under P1–P2 rules §7's `maxPlantLines` is 1, so the strip shows `L1` alone with no add button. From P3 `+ Add line` is enabled while the plan has fewer lines than `maxPlantLines(state, claimId)` and is otherwise disabled with its reason (`LINE_LIMIT: a 20-acre claim supports 2 plant lines`). Removing a line confirms first (`L2's box is cleaned up this week; its pad stays for a later plan`). A bulk-sample plan has exactly one line. Trade-off on `+ Add line`: `A second line → more yards on big ground; a second plant and spread to buy, water and stripping shared, another plant operator, and a second foreman at three lines`.
- **Supervision line**, one per line, read-only from §8 `foremanFor(state, claimId, lineId)`; the **foreman is not a plan field** (§7 7.2, D-13.55). Texts by kind: `L1–L2 · Foreman J. Ruiz (skill 62)` (hired; lines covered from `lineIds`), `L1 · Owner (skill 85)`, `L1 · Lead hand, 2 weeks of cover left`, `L3 · Line lead hand (standing): 0.6 × best hand = 33`, `L1 · Small crew, no foreman: efficiency ×0.92, injuries ×1.15 · 3 of 3 hands`, or `No foreman: the plan cannot activate (FOREMAN_REQUIRED)`. Each number is a `<Num>` (tuning refs `ops.noForemanEfficiency`, `staff.noForemanIncidentMult`, `staff.smallCrewMaxNoForeman`, `staff.leadHandSkillFrac`, `staff.foremanMaxLines`). Links: Staff (`staff/assign`) and Company & owner (`owner/setAssignment`).
- **Permit limits are not a plan field either**: a line shows the claim's §6 compliance mode (`Strict: work is clamped to permit conditions`) and links to Permits & compliance, where `permits/setComplianceMode` lives (P2).
- **Cut selection** on the block grid works on the open line tab: click, shift-click for a range, ctrl-click to toggle; a sequence list with drag or `Alt+↑/↓` reorder. Every line's cut is drawn at once and told apart by outline and label, never by series color (the claim owns its slot): L1 solid, L2 dashed, L3 dotted, sequence labels `L2·3`, and each line's plant site marked with its line label. A block in another line's cut or under its plant site is refused with `BLOCK_OCCUPIED`. Selection summary per line and for the claim: blocks, acres, est. pay bcy P50, est. overburden bcy, strip ratio, est. contained raw oz P10/P50/P90, est. weeks at the plan rate.
- **Assignments board**: a **Shared** lane with the claim-level roles (strip, water, power, support, reclaim), one lane per line with the line roles (dig, haul, feed, plant), and **Unassigned**, holding machine and crew cards. A line-role machine sits in exactly one line (`LINE_INVALID`; in two, `ASSET_DOUBLE_BOOKED`); incompatible drops are refused with `ROLE_INCOMPATIBLE`. Crew cards stay claim-wide by (role, shift), because §7 pairs operators to machines claim-wide; a line lane shows the operators paired to its machines as read-only badges. Drag and drop, or keyboard: select a card, press `1`–`9` for the role in its lane, and `Alt+1` / `Alt+2` / `Alt+3` to move a line-role card to L1 / L2 / L3.
- **Preview panel** (right): §7 `projectOpsVisible(state, claimId, draftPlan)` (one representative week, player knowledge only): claim totals and one block per line with its stage capacities (bcy/wk), predicted bottleneck (`L2: plant limited to 38 bcy/hr by haul: 1 truck`), expected bcy washed, expected raw oz (P50 grade × visible recovery) and water share; the claim's weekly direct cost, cost per bcy, est. cash cost per fine oz, overtime and fatigue flags; §7's non-blocking warnings (trucks under-matched; water, power or fuel short, incl. `lines competing for water`; two shifts with one plant operator; stripping below need, counting every line; a surface pile set to be stripped as waste; `LINE_LEAD_HAND`; small crew without a foreman); and the errors that would refuse `Apply plan` (`FOREMAN_REQUIRED`, `LINE_NEEDS_PLANT_OPERATOR`, `LINE_LIMIT`, `LINE_INVALID`). Label: `Expected values; breakdowns and weather not included`.

**Supervision chip.** One chip per claim, wherever a claim is summarized (Operations header, Owned ground, dashboard Last week, the portfolio view in P6), built from §8 `foremanFor(state, claimId)` (L1's supervisor, the claim's senior one) plus a count of lines not covered by a foreman or the owner. Each kind has its own icon and text, so color is never the only cue:

| `foremanFor().kind` | Chip text | Style | Explain |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hired` | `Foreman · J. Ruiz` (`+1 line lead hand` when a third line is beyond his span) | neutral | skill, availability, lines covered |
| `owner` | `Owner as foreman` (`Owner as operator · skill −15` when assigned `operator`) | neutral | §1 owner skill |
| `leadHand` | `Lead hand · 2 wks cover left` | warning | §8 `leadHandWeeks` against `staff.leadHandMaxWeeks` (3) |
| `smallCrew` | `Small crew · 3 of 3 hands` | neutral with an info glyph | efficiency `ops.noForemanEfficiency` 0.92, injury hazard and site incidents × `staff.noForemanIncidentMult` 1.15, `fieldCrewCount` against `staff.smallCrewMaxNoForeman` (3), one line, one shift |
| `none` | `No foreman · stood down` | critical | the reason (reassigned, lead-hand weeks used up, small crew exceeded) |

Before an action ends a claim's small-crew exemption, the UI says so where the player acts, from the engine's non-blocking warning `SMALL_CREW_ENDS` (Needs from §8): the hire and assign modals (`Assigning a fourth hand to Claim B ends its small-crew exemption: from next week it needs a foreman or the plan stands down`) and the plan editor (a second shift or a second line). Example (§8 8.12): Claim B runs a skill-60 excavator operator, a skill-50 plant operator and a laborer with no foreman; the chip reads `Small crew · 3 of 3 hands`, its explain tree shows F = 0.92 against 0.94 with a skill-60 hired foreman ($2,933 a week loaded) and the injury hazard 0.173% → 0.199% a week, and hiring a truck driver raises `SMALL_CREW_ENDS` in the hire modal.

**Stage rows** (the Flow tab's UI selector; a claim view when `lineId` is omitted):
```
stageRows(r: WeekOpsResult, lineId?: LineId):
  src           = lineId ? the r.lines entry with that lineId : r                           // claim view: src = r
  shared        = { strip, water, power }                                                   // §7 7.2.1: claim-level stages
  capacity_s    = (s ∈ shared ? r : src).stageCapacityBcyWk[s]                              [bcy/wk]
  throughput_s  = strip: r.overburdenBcy · dig: src.payMinedBcy · haul: src.payHauledBcy
                  feed, plant: src.payWashedBcy · tailings: src.tailingsBcy                 [bcy/wk]
  machines_s    = { m : r.hoursByMachine[m].role maps to s, and (s ∈ shared or no lineId or r.hoursByMachine[m].lineId = lineId) }
                  // water and power rows show limited plant hours, not bcy
  scheduled_s   = Σ_m r.hoursByMachine[m].scheduled;  worked_s = Σ_m work_m                 [h]
  utilization_s = worked_s / scheduled_s
  idle_s        = Σ_m byCause_m by IdleCause; flow causes split by rootStage from src.idleBreakdown
                  (a line view: that line's items plus the shared-stage items)               // buckets sum to scheduled_s (§7 7.8)
  bottleneck    = src.bottleneck;  plantIdle = src.plantIdlePct                             // claim view: §7's claim-view rule
```

| `IdleCause` | Label | `IdleCause` | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| unstaffed | No operator | starved | Starved (root: stage) |
| operatorAbsent | Operator absent | blocked | Blocked (root: stage) |
| servicing | Servicing | water / power | Water short / Power short |
| coordination | Coordination losses | tailings | Tailings handling |
| weather / season | Weather / Season | noWork | No work |
| breakdown | Breakdown (P3) | permitLimit | Permit limit (P2) |
| fuel | Fuel short (P3 stock) | | |
| cleanup / plantMove / startup | Cleanup / Plant move / Start-up | program / redeployed | Lent to prospecting / Redeployed (worked elsewhere) |

Example (§7 7.8, "the plant sat idle 29%, mostly because of one rock truck"): `Plant idle 29.4% (19.4 of 66 h). Largest cause: starved by haul, 12.7 h (1 × 30t truck, 2,808 ft haul)`; the other rows are servicing 5.3 h and coordination 1.4 h. The `ops.plantIdleHigh` warning fires because 29.4% > `ops.alertPlantIdlePct` (25%).

**Grade reconciliation.** The player never sees contained gold. This view compares weighed gold with the estimate that was in force when the gravel was washed: §7's `foremanEstimateOz` (visible model, frozen per cleanup). Using the current §4 estimate instead would drift the factor toward 1, because §4 absorbs each cleanup as production evidence (D-13.44).
```
reconFactor  = CleanupResult.rawOzWeighed / CleanupResult.foremanEstimateOz                    [ratio]
recGrade     = CleanupResult.recoveredGradeOzPerBcy  (= rawOzWeighed / bcyWashedSince)           [raw oz/bcy washed]
inSituBcy    = Σ_b CleanupResult.inSituBcyByBlock[b]                                            [bcy, §3 pay-column basis]
impliedGrade = (rawOzWeighed − pileRawOzEst) / modeledChainFactor / inSituBcy                    [oz/bcy in situ, §4's grade basis]
estGrade     = (foremanEstimateOz − pileRawOzEst) / modeledChainFactor / inSituBcy               // the estimate's own in-situ grade
seasonFactor = Σ rawOzWeighed / Σ foremanEstimateOz over this season's cleanups on the claim    [ratio]
               // every line's cleanups in the claim view; one line's in a line view (each CleanupResult carries its lineId)
```
`modeledChainFactor` is §7's visible chain from in-situ metal to weighed raw oz (mining factor, capture by size, gold-room loss, estimated dirt), so `impliedGrade / estGrade ≈ reconFactor` when the cut has no pile feed (exact when the estimate did not change between cleanups); this is the comparison §4's `recordProduction` makes (D-13.53).

Example (§7 7.10): two weeks of the §7 7.8 claim wash 6,377 bcy with no pile feed. The foreman's box estimate, built from the player's P50 block grade 0.0105 through §7's visible chain, is 46.900 raw oz. The scale reads 52.901 raw oz, so reconFactor = 52.901 / 46.900 = 1.128, shown as `+12.8% vs your estimate (one cleanup; noisy)` (§7 rounds it to +13%); recovered grade = 52.901 / 6,377 = 0.00830 raw oz/bcy washed; implied in-situ grade = 0.0105 × 1.128 = 0.0118 oz/bcy against the estimate's 0.0105. The 12% raw-oz lease royalty (6.348 raw oz in kind) and the 46.553 raw oz lot come after the weighing and do not enter the factor. The chart plots per-cleanup factors as dots and the season factor as a line, with a reference at 1.0.

**Sees vs true (operations).** `containedRawOz`, `containedBySize`, `lostRawOzBySize`, `lostToWasteOz` and `leftInPitOz` are truth and are never displayed; `recoveredRawOz` and `recoveredBySize` stay hidden until cleanup (§7; D-13.7). The UI shows estimated contained gold (bcy × the player's block estimate), estimated recovery, the foreman's box estimate and weighed gold.

**Equipment.**

| Tab | Content |
|---|---|
| Market | Filters: class, size, brand, seller type (new / certified / private / auction), price, year, hours, district, financing available. Columns: model*, class*, size*, brand*, year*, hours*, condition* (P1 the visible grade A–D; P3 seller description + `Not inspected` or known range), seller type*, location, ask*, est. resale, delivery to selected claim (weeks + mobilization $, §9 transport and §1 access windows)*, listing expires*, financing. Row actions: Buy (P1 cash), Inspect (P3; free for the mechanic-background owner, §1 1.7), **Bid** (P3 equipment auctions: lot list with preview, opening bid and `Closes Wk N`; a sealed maximum bid through §9 `fleet/bid { listingId, maxBidCents }`; results arrive as `auction.won` / `auction.lost`; background bidders from P3, §12 competitor bids from P5; D-13.50), Finance / lease / rent (P3/P4). Trade-off on Buy: `Used/auction → less cash now, unknown condition and more downtime risk`. |
| Fleet | Columns: machine*, class*, status* (working / idle / in transit; down and in shop from P3), location*, assignment*, hours*, grade* (P1–P2: the visible A–D grade), maintenance $/SMR h* (P1–P2: §9's flat `fleet.p1MaintUsdPerHr[model]` × grade, operator and in-house multipliers), worst known component* (P3), next PM due (h)* (P3), cost/hr (TTM)*, book value, est. resale, insured (P4), lien (P4, §11 `lienStatus`), acquisition and finance ref. **Machine detail**: header (model, hours, status, location, acquisition); P1–P2: the grade and the flat maintenance rate with its explain tree (`$33 × grade C 1.25 = $41.25 per SMR h`), and no component bars, PM schedule or failure-risk chip, because P1 machines have no components (D-13.51); from P3 a **component health** panel with one range bar per component (known range from the last inspection, with inspection week and inspector; `Unknown` if never inspected) and a failure-risk chip from the known range; **cost per hour** stacked bar (depreciation, interest, insurance, fuel, PM, repairs, operator) from `machineCostPerHour` with TTM and season toggles; **maintenance schedule** table (P3: PM interval, last done, next due, overdue flag); work history; a **served by** line (`Site mechanic J. Lee`, `District pool · 1.5 h travel · 8 h response`, or `Operators only: no mechanic in reach`, P3); risk chips and machine preps (P3); actions: assign, move, sell (P1), schedule PM, inspect, repair, rebuild (P3) (each dispatches §9's action). Trade-off on rebuild: `Rebuild now → downtime and cash now, lower failure risk in season`. |
| Shop (P3) | One **board per shop** (§8 shop modes, §9 9.8.6): a `Site · <claim>` board for each claim with site-mode mechanics or welders and a `Pool · <district>` board for each district with pool-mode ones, picked from a board list that shows each shop's capacity, demand (§9 `shopDemand(shop)`), backlog in weeks and the `shop.backlogHigh` chip. **Backlog board** (kanban): Requested → Waiting parts → In progress → Done this week. Card: machine, job type (PM / repair / rebuild / inspection), est. labor h, parts ETA week, priority, assigned mechanic. Drag (or `Alt+↑/↓`) reorders priority, dispatching §9's work-order priority action. Header: mechanic capacity h/wk (§8 `shopCapacity(shop)`) vs backlog h, backlog in weeks, field-service option. **Pool boards** add to each card its claim, the week's travel charge (`fleet.poolTravelHoursPerJob` by the claim's access, once per job per week; the yard has none) and, on a held blocking order, the response delay (`Starts 8 h after workable`, `fleet.poolResponseDelayHours`); the header adds travel hours this week and their share of capacity; and a **reach table** lists the yard and every claim in the district: access, travel h per job, served this week (`yes` / `road closed (breakup)` / `fly-in: not served`), site mechanic present, routine coverage ρ (§9 9.8.3, D-9.54). Hours come from §9 `shopHours(state)`, travel included. The work-order assignee picker (`fleet/scheduleWork`) lists `auto`, field service, dealer and the mechanics whose mode can reach the machine; one who cannot is shown disabled with `ASSIGNEE_OUT_OF_REACH` and the reason (`Pool mechanics never serve fly-in claims`). Trade-off on the board list: `Pool → fewer mechanics for nearby road claims; travel hours on every job and an 8-h wait on every breakdown; remote ground still wants a mechanic on site`. |

| Rentals & leases (P3) | Active rentals and leases: machine, counterparty, rate, term, buyout, next payment, return condition |
