**Obligation ladder** (§6: alerts count back from `dueTurn − prepLeadWeeks`; D-13.34).
```
lead     = Obligation.dueTurn − Obligation.prepLeadWeeks − turn                                [weeks]
severity = lead ≤ game.alerts.obligationCriticalWeeks (1) ? 'critical'
         : lead ≤ game.alerts.obligationWarnWeeks (4)     ? 'warning'
         : lead ≤ game.alerts.obligationInfoWeeks (8)     ? 'info' : none
severity = min(severity, Obligation.consequence.severity)       // a late-fee obligation never goes critical
severity = needsAction(Obligation) ? severity : min(severity, 'info')   // billable payments, auto-paid or auto-filed: shown, never stops (13.9)
```
Signals are then grouped by (category, due week) in collation, so a pile of identical deadlines is one message, one stop per escalation and one `Pay all` button (D-13.46). A failed auto-pay raises §6's own critical alert, so capping self-settling items at info never hides a real miss.

**Escalation example (P2).** A company holds 12 unpatented claims (12 units) with auto-pay for `land` switched off. Each claim's annual maintenance fee is due Sept 1 = Wk 35, `prepLeadWeeks` 0, consequence `forfeitClaim` (critical). The 12 `obligation.dueSoon` signals collate into one message, `12 claim maintenance fees due Wk 35 · $2,400`, which appears as info in Wk 27, escalates to warning in Wk 31 (one stop for the group) and to critical in Wk 34 (toast, pinned). `Pay all` dispatches `permits/payObligations` with the 12 IDs and resolves it; paying 9 of them leaves the message open with `3 … · $600`. Missing it creates one `obligation.missed` (critical) message listing the forfeited claims. With auto-pay on (the default for `land` at every difficulty, §6 D-6.16) the group stays info and §6 pays it in step 13 of Wk 34. An arid county intent-to-hold filing (late fee $50/claim, consequence severity `warning`) tops out at warning, because a form still needs filing; a lease advance royalty (a billable payment §11 makes in its due week) stays info.

**Toast rules.** Toasts fire only for critical and blocking messages, plus action confirmations (`Bought Excavator 30t for $182,000 - Undo`, 6 s; the Undo link appears only for undoable actions). At most `ui.maxToastsVisible` (3) at once; any beyond that collapse to `+N more in Inbox`. Critical toasts never auto-dismiss.

### 13.11 Bank & loans, Gold sales, Reports, News

**Bank & loans.**

| Tab | Content |
|---|---|
| Accounts | One card per account (operating P1; restricted P2; reserve P4): balance, 13-week sparkline, interest rate. P4: transfer (`finance/transfer`) and sweep settings (`finance/setSweep`: operating target, auto-draw and auto-paydown of the revolver). |
| Bills & payments | Open bills (§11 `Bill`): payee, category (`PayCategory`), amount, due week, method (cash / card), status (open / partial / late / **stayed**, P4: a pre-filing bill held by a reorganization case, paid only through the plan), weeks late, fees; arrears table; `Pay now` (`finance/payBill`; disabled on a stayed bill with `CLAIM_STAYED`). **Payment priority** (P4, `finance/setPaymentPriority`): an ordered list of categories with drag and `Alt+↑/↓` reorder; `autoDebit` is locked first and `owner` last; moving the payroll tax deposit below a non-payroll category shows §11's trust-fund warning. Trade-off: `Every reordering trades one creditor's remedy for another's`. Vendor accounts (P4): limit, terms, balance, status (current / late / stop-supply). |
| Ledger | Virtualized table with a **book** selector (company / owner). Columns: week*, txn ID, account*, memo*, counterparty*, refs (entity links)*, cost center, claim, source (`§7/fuel`), debit*, credit*, running balance (only when one account is filtered). Filters: week range, account, category (account prefix), cost center, amount range, entity, text search across memo, counterparty and refs. Data from §11 `queryLedger(state, filter, page)`: transaction detail for the last 52 weeks, older months as balance-preserving monthly summary rows labelled `Monthly summary` (§11 D-11.47); payroll is one transaction per run, with per-employee lines in the Staff > Payroll register. Totals footer. Export CSV. |
| Loans & leases | Columns: lender, product, original, balance, rate (incl. step-ups), payment, frequency, next due, maturity, collateral, PG, status (current / late / delinquent / default / accelerated / stayed (P4)), covenant status. A reorganization's DIP loan and plan notes (`reorgSecured`, `reorgPriority`, `reorgUnsecured`) carry a `Plan note` badge and link to the case. Drill-down: amortization schedule table + balance-over-time line chart, collateral list (links to machines and claims), payment history; `Prepay` / `Pay off` (`finance/prepay`). P1 shows the fixed loans only (Inheritor estate note, banker starter loan). |
| Credit (P4) | Owner score (300-850) and company score / Paydex; factor table (factor, current value, impact in points, trend), incl. the bankruptcy marks (`bankruptcy` or `affiliateBankruptcy` on the owner file, the company derogatory) with their drop-off weeks; score history line; a qualitative **lender mood** chip per lender (patient / neutral / wary), never the underlying numbers (§11 11.5) |
| Offers (P4) | Application form (`finance/apply`: lender, product, amount, term, schedule incl. seasonal where eligible, collateral, purpose); pending applications with decision weeks; offers: lender, product, amount, rate, term, fees, collateral, PG required, covenants, expiry; accept / decline. Royalty, prepay and equity solicitations and the rescue partner live here. During a reorganization case only `product: 'dip'` can be applied for (`IN_REORGANIZATION` otherwise), and every decision shows its court-approval delay (`finance.reorg.courtApprovalWeeks`). Trade-off on hard money: `Fast and certain, expensive, and aggressive on repossession`. |
| Covenants (P4) | Loan, covenant, threshold, current value (explainable), headroom %, cadence, next test week, status chip, 12-test sparkline; a **cure calculator** for breaches (paydown that restores leverage or liquidity); `Request waiver` (`finance/requestWaiver`) |
| Revolver (P4) | Borrowing base certificate: eligible components (camp gold P4; metal account and refinery receivables P5) × advance rates, availability, drawn, over-advance; draw and repay |
| Insurance (P4; in P2–P3 the §11 GL stub binds automatically with an `insurance.bound` note and shows on the Permits Authority checklist) | Policies: line, insured values (scheduled machines), limit, deductible, annual premium, installments, renewal (Wk 49), status (active / lapsed / non-renewed / force-placed), required by. Losses awaiting a decision (`finance/fileClaim` or `finance/absorbLoss` within 4 weeks), with the trade-off `Filing nets the payout but raises three years of premiums`; open claims and expected settlement; EMR and claims multipliers with explain trees |
| Tax (P4) | Entity treatment, year-to-date taxable income estimate, installment schedule and amounts, estimate method (`safeHarbor` / `annualized`), depreciation election, tax distribution policy, NOL balances (company and owner), and the owner's pass-through tax on the owner book |
| Reorganization (P4) | The bankruptcy screen, both forms: eligibility and filing, the case, the plan builder, the plan period and past cases (below) |

**Reorganization** (Bank & loans > Reorganization, P4; §11 11.16.1–11.16.7 own every rule and number, D-13.65). The tab appears from distress stage 2, stays through an open case and keeps closed cases afterwards. It has four views, and every figure on them is a `<Num>` that explains down to the claims, collateral marks and forecast lines; nothing here reads hidden state.

1. **Filing** (no case open). An **eligibility card** from §11 `reorgEligibility(state)`, one row per condition with a check or a cross and its code: distress stage ≥ 2 (`STAGE_TOO_LOW`); debts against the Subchapter V limit (`Debts $666,000 of $3,424,000`, with the debts' build-up in the explain tree; `REORG_DEBT_LIMIT`); no filing within 8 years (`Next eligible Y9 Wk 24`; `REORG_COOLDOWN`); the $15,000 retainer against operating cash (`INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`, with an `Inject personal cash` link). A sole proprietor sees `You are the debtor: your personal debts join the plan and your personal cash above $25,000 counts toward creditors`. An LLC or corp owner chooses whether to **file as guarantor** (`guarantorFiles`), shown as two columns: *company only* (guarantee demands at confirmation for what the plan will not pay, estimated from §11's personal-exposure table; the lighter `affiliateBankruptcy` mark) and *owner files too* (demands stayed and paid through the plan; personal cash above $25,000 counts in the best-interest test; the full `bankruptcy` mark). Two actions side by side:
   - `File for reorganization (Chapter 11, Subchapter V)` → `finance/fileReorganization { guarantorFiles }`. The double confirmation lists what happens at once and after: the retainer now and about $40,000 of case fees in all, plus the trustee's 3% of plan payments; the automatic stay (no repossession, collection or lender default action on pre-filing debt); vendors on COD, cards and the revolver closed, new credit only as a court-approved DIP loan; both credit files marked; owner pay capped at the living allowance; reputation −10, a crew morale hit and a drop in investor stance; a plan due in 13 weeks; in a goal scenario, the gold medal is no longer available; `This cannot be undone`.
   - `File for liquidation (Chapter 7)` → `owner/fileBankruptcy`. The double confirmation shows §11's final settlement at distressed marks and the personal exposure by entity, and says `The run ends`.

   Trade-off line: `Reorganization keeps the company and the run, and costs three to five years of disposable income, both credit files and a scenario's gold medal; liquidation ends the run now`. An ineligible company sees the failing conditions and only the liquidation button.
2. **Case** (status `filed`). A **case timeline** in weeks: filed; plan due (`planDueTurn`; the last week to file is the one before); plan filed; hearing (`hearingTurn`); an amendment window after a denial; effective date. Once a plan is filed, an `If the court ruled today` line re-runs `reorgPlanPreview` on the filed terms and current numbers, because the hearing re-tests the plan on that week's cash, spot, plans and collateral. A **claims panel**: each secured claim (lender, claim, collateral and its 11.16.3 value, secured part S_k, deficiency), priority claims, general unsecured, administrative, and the debts at filing against the limit. **Stayed items**: bills and loans held by the stay. **Adequate protection**: one row per secured lender with the monthly amount and status; an unpaid one reads `Stay lifts for Northline's collateral at Wk 44` (critical). **DIP financing**: a link to Offers. **Court-approved sales**: open claim and machine sales with their stalking-horse bid, hearing week and overbids (§5 5.14, §9). Primary action: `Build the plan`; secondary: `Convert to liquidation` (`owner/fileBankruptcy`, which converts the case as of right; double confirmation; the run ends).
3. **Plan builder** (`#/bank/reorganization/plan`; `finance/fileReorgPlan`), bound live to §11 `reorgPlanPreview(state, terms)`:
   - *Controls:* term in weeks (156–260; presets 3, 4 and 5 years; `TERM_OUT_OF_RANGE`), schedule (`level` monthly or `seasonal`), reserve (0–10%, `finance.reorg.reserveMaxPct`), a surrender picker over the collateral (a machine an active mine plan uses is disabled with `COLLATERAL_IN_USE` and a link to the plan), a rejection picker over rentals, operating leases and mineral leases (each with its rejection damages), a **claims table** built from §5 `planInventory` (one row per tenure: holding, going-concern and liquidation values from the player's view, liens, cure or rejection amount) with a treatment picker per row (`keep` / `sell` with a reserve / `surrender` to a named creditor; `assume` / `reject` for leases and JVs; `REORG_LEASE_ELECTION` until every lease and JV has one), and the owner contribution (personal cash shown; `INSUFFICIENT_PERSONAL_CASH`).
   - *Disposable income:* E' (fine oz) → revenue → operating costs → living allowance → capex allowance → PDI0 → reserve → PDI → trustee → D, labelled `Uses your forecast and your current mine plans: the plan is only as good as next season's plan`.
   - *Per-year table:* plan year, D, secured-note payments, priority payments, required Req_y, unsecured U_y, trustee fee, margin (D ÷ Req_y − 1); cumulative unsecured against the class total C_U.
   - *The two tests* as status chips with their numbers: **Feasible** (worst-year margin; effective-date payments against cash at the hearing) and **Best interest** (`Unsecured creditors get 41.3%; a liquidation would pay 37.4%`). `File plan` is disabled with `PLAN_NOT_FEASIBLE` or `BEST_INTEREST_NOT_MET` and names the shortfall (`Year 1 needs $183,182; $142,804 reaches creditors`).
   - *Vote outlook:* the bucket only, `likely` (≥ 0.8), `possible` (0.4–0.8) or `unlikely` (< 0.4), with its inputs (unsecured recovery against liquidation, the secured lenders' patience mix, reputation); never z or the draw (§11 11.16.4). A note explains the two confirmations: consensual (discharge at confirmation, trustee fee on the first payment only) and cram-down (the court sets five years, the trustee takes every payment, discharge at completion).
   - *Trade-off lines:* `Longer term → more for unsecured creditors and gentler notes, but longer under the pay cap and the conversion rule` · `Seasonal schedule → payments out of the cash trough` · `Bigger reserve → slack in a bad year, worse vote odds` · `Surrender iron → smaller notes, a bigger unsecured class, maybe a smaller mine plan` · `Owner contribution → buys the best-interest test with personal cash`.
   - Example (§11 11.16.7 fixture): at 260 weeks, level, 5% reserve the builder shows PDI0 $154,830, D $142,804.37 a year, margin 12.4%, unsecured 41.3% against 37.4%, effective-date $25,000 against $70,000 cash, and a `possible` vote; switching to 156 weeks turns the Feasible chip to critical with its octagon and `Year 1 needs $183,182`.
4. **Plan period** (status `confirmed`). The confirmation (consensual or cram-down, term, notes), the installment schedule (next due, amount with any trustee fee, status), missed payments in the last 52 weeks against the conversion threshold (`1 of 2 missed: one more converts the case`; `1 of 1` while an equity holder's conversion motion runs, §1 1.8.1), anniversary true-ups (actual against projected disposable income, the amount added), the completion week and the owner pay cap, with the same `Convert to liquidation` action. **History** lists closed cases: outcome, fees, amount discharged.

Reorganization reaches other screens through their owners' data: the case chip in the top bar (13.1), the ladder's stage-7 fork (13.3), stayed bills and plan notes (above), the balance sheet's **Liabilities subject to compromise** grouping during a case and the income statement's **Reorganization items (net)** line (Reports, below), `in plan` obligations (13.4), court-sale listings (13.5), and the disabled reasons `REORG_OPEN` and `REORG_DRAW_LIMIT` on the owner, investor and community controls (13.12).

**Gold sales.**

| Tab | Content |
|---|---|
| Inventory | Lots (§10 `GoldLot`): lot ID*, source claim*, cleanup week*, raw oz*, fineness* (`est. 0.84 (district prior)` / `est. 0.82 (claim assays)` / `assayed 0.847`), est. fine oz*, location and status*, insured (P5), value at spot*, value at best-channel net*, theft risk band (P5: Low / Moderate / High / Very high with the 4-week probability). Bulk-select to sell, ship or move. |
| Sell | **Channel comparison calculator** for the selected lots, from §10 `quoteChannels(state, lotIds)`: one column per channel (P1 the district's local buyer; P5 adds each refinery that meets its minimum, deliver-into-forward, and hold). Rows: fine-oz basis (buyer's estimate / your estimate / assayed), gross, itemized deductions, net cash, cash week, net per raw oz, % of spot, price risk (none / until assay / locked); the local buyer column also shows the **buyer's implied fineness** next to yours; the hold column shows weekly carrying cost and the theft band. No future prices and no recommendation. Actions: sell (partial allowed on one lot), ship (P5). **Standing sale order** panel (P1, `gold/setStandingOrder`): none / sell all at cleanup (local buyer; refinery from P5) / keep cash above $X. Trade-off: `Local buyer → cash today at a discount; refinery → more money, minimum lot, weeks to settle; hold → price exposure, storage, theft risk; standing orders protect payroll in fast-forward but always take the discount`. |
| Shipments (P5) | Refinery, lots, raw oz, pricing (at assay / locked at ship), disposition (sell / metal account / deliver to forward), ship week, arrival, assay week, settlement week, advance, status; the assay certificate (doré oz, fine oz, payable oz, fees, net). Metal account balances by refinery, with sell and deliver actions. |
| Storage (P5) | Tiers per location (camp open, camp safe, bank box, metal account), cost, insurance, theft risk band with its explain tree; actions: buy safe, rent box, move lots (1-week insured courier), set insurance |
| Forwards (P5) | Forward book: contract, counterparty, fine oz, price F, delivery week, mark-to-market, collateral posted vs required, margin call status; actions roll, close, deliver from account, post margin. Coverage chart: forward oz vs forecast production P10/P50 by delivery month (bars, one axis). Coverage ratio = forward fine oz ÷ P10 forecast fine oz, warning chip above 1.0 (matching §10 `forward.shortfallRisk`). Implied vol is shown here; puts (stretch) in the same table. |
| History | Sales: week, lots, channel, fine oz, price, net, realized % of spot |

**Reports** (§11 defines every line; §13 defines presentation).
**Period selector** (one control row above the report): This week, Last 4 weeks, Month-to-date, Quarter, Season-to-date (per district), Year-to-date, Last year, Custom (week range). **Comparison**: none / prior period / same period last year / season baseline. Months are §1 `monthEndWeeks` spans and quarters are weeks 1–13, 14–26, 27–39, 40–52 (§11 11.1, D-13.18).

| Report | Layout |
|---|---|
| Income statement | §11 11.19.1 lines (revenue → cash cost of sales → mine operating income → G&A, exploration, reclamation, other → EBIT → interest, other income → reorganization items (net), P4, during and after a case → pre-tax → tax → net income; memo lines), collapsible groups; columns: period, comparison, Δ, Δ%; whole dollars, parentheses. **P1 P&L**: costs as incurred, revenue at sale, no inventory absorption, gold on hand as a memo at market |
| Balance sheet (P4) | as of the period end; comparison column; gold inventory at cost with a market memo column (§11 D-11.7); while a reorganization case is filed and unconfirmed, pre-filing claims grouped as **Liabilities subject to compromise** (presentation only, §11 11.16.6); check line `Assets = Liabilities + Equity ✓` |
| Cash flow, indirect (P4) | operating / investing / financing; non-cash disclosures (incl. debt discharged and claims converted into plan notes in a reorganization); reconciles to the ledger cash change (a check line shows `Reconciles ✓`) |
| Per-claim P&L | columns: each claim, `Unallocated site`, `Company`, total (§11 11.19.4); rows: revenue, in-kind royalty value (memo at spot), direct costs, machine costs, labor, shared site costs, **contribution**, allocated overhead, **after-overhead result**, depreciation and depletion, cash cost per fine oz |
| Cost per ounce | cash cost, AISC and AIC per gross recovered fine oz, by claim and company (§11 11.19.5) + bar chart ($/fine oz, one axis) with a spot reference line; purchases tagged sustaining or growth can be re-tagged from here (P4) |
| 13-week forecast | table (rows: §11 inflow and outflow categories; columns: weeks) + line chart of ending cash with a zero line; P1–P3: one series (scheduled outflows, known receipts and the P50 production line: each planned cleanup's fine oz at the local-buyer net, in its cleanup week) and runway, with the line labelled `incl. planned cleanups (P50)`; P4: P10/P50/P90 band; label `Uses your estimates and current plans`; memo rows for revolver availability and gold on hand at local-buyer net "if sold now" |
| Debt schedule (P4) | per instrument (§11 11.19.7), next 12 months' payments, balance at year end, maturity; stacked column chart of principal and interest per month for 12 months; operating-lease commitments and contingent guarantee exposure as memo lines |

Every report cell is clickable: line → contributing accounts → ledger entries.

**News (P5).** Feed: week, headline (rendered from §10 `NewsItem.templateId` + `vars`), body, tags (macro, gold, district, competitor, regulation, diesel), importance (1-3, filterable), related entity links, and the analyst view chip when present (bullish / bearish / mixed, 13-week target). The price **regime**, fair value and the `truthful` flag are **never shown**. **Analysts** tab: the three houses, their current calls and their trailing-104-week hit rates (§10 analyst track records). **Macro panel**: small multiples (each with its own axis): policy rate, real rate, CPI y/y, USD index, central-bank buying, geopolitical risk, equity mood, diesel rack. **Gold chart**: line of weekly spot with 13w / 52w / 3y / All ranges (3y uses §10's 156-week pre-history), news markers as dots (hover shows the headline), and a reference line for the player's average realized price. Clicking a week's price opens §10's explain tree (macro drift, same-week macro moves, shock with cause, and one `Other / unexplained` node).

### 13.12 Company & owner

**Purpose:** the owner as a person (§1 1.9) and the company's standing. Route `#/company/:tab`.

| Tab | Content |
|---|---|
| Profile | Name, entity (conversion `company/convertEntity`, P4, with fee and 4-week timing), owner background and its edge, start type, difficulty, **reputation** (0-100, explain tree listing the last 52 weeks of entries, §1 1.12) with its effects table, regulator standing (P2, links to 13.8), safety record (P2, §8), community sponsorship (`community/sponsor`); the optional hard-rock **readiness checklist** (§14 14.1, P6, only when `game.hardRockEnabled`). Run controls: `Retire` (`game/retire`, sandbox; double confirmation; during a reorganization case it scores the undischarged debts, §1 1.13) and, from P4, `File for reorganization` and `File for liquidation`, both routing to Bank & loans > Reorganization (13.11), where eligibility, the guarantor choice and the double confirmations live; outside stage ≥ 2 they show `STAGE_TOO_LOW`. |
| Owner | Assignment (`owner/setAssignment`: office / foreman of one claim / operator of one machine / shop (mechanic background), in site mode at one claim or, from P3, pool mode for a district (§8 shop modes) / field geologist (geologist); effect from next week; `FOREMAN_SLOT_TAKEN` and the `SMALL_CREW_ENDS` warning inline); salary (`owner/setSalary`); draw (`owner/draw`) and injection (`owner/inject`: equity or owner loan), each with its trade-off line from §1; during a reorganization case salary and draws are capped at the living allowance (`REORG_DRAW_LIMIT`, the cap shown) and owner-loan repayment, return payments, buyouts, sponsorship and entity conversion are disabled with `REORG_OPEN`; owner-loan repayment (P4); personal cash; personal debt, personal credit score, guarantees list and personal liabilities (guarantee demands, TFRP) with `Pay` (P4, `finance/payPersonalLiability`); owner net worth (scoring) and the informational appraised net worth, both explainable. |
| Investor | Backed starts only (§1 1.8.1). Terms (equity %, preference, contribution; or royalty rate, payback multiple, tail, minimum). P1: fixed terms, distributions and royalty deliveries. P4: stance chip (content / concerned / unhappy / hostile) and satisfaction with its check-in components, check-in schedule (weeks 13/26/39/52), annual plan submission (`investor/submitPlan`), approval requests (as decisions), **return payments** (`investor/payReturn { agreementId, amountUsd }`: pref arrears first, then distributions; shows `prefUnpaid` and `returnPaidYTD`, with the week-48 reminder), buyout or buyback price (`investor/buyOut`, BP/BB explain), redemption deadline when one is running; during a reorganization case the stance path through the case and, while a confirmed plan runs and an equity holder is hostile, the warning `Conversion motion: one missed plan payment converts the case` (§1 1.8.1). |
| Scenario (P6) | Goal conditions with current values, deadline, medal thresholds, and the score multiplier; after any reorganization filing the gold threshold is struck through with `Best medal: silver (reorganization filed Y1 Wk 44)` (§1 `game.scenario.reorgMedalCap`, D-1.57); `Forfeit scenario` (`scenario/forfeit`, double confirmation; the run ends as a loss with its report) |

### 13.13 The explain system

**Rule.** Every displayed value is rendered by `<Num>`, which takes an `ExplainRef`. Clicking it, or focusing it and pressing `E` or `Enter`, opens a popover. Exempt: axis ticks, row counts and pagination. An ESLint rule requires `explain` on every `<Num>` (`explain={null}` must carry a justification comment), and a crawler test clicks every `[data-num]` (D-13.29).

```ts
type ExplainRef =
  | { kind: 'live'; explainer: ExplainerName; args: readonly unknown[] }   // explain.<name>(state, ...args)
  | { kind: 'report'; turn: number; path: readonly string[] }             // into WeekReport calc trees
  | { kind: 'ledger'; filter: LedgerFilter }                              // sum of postings → ledger view
  | { kind: 'history'; metric: HistoryMetric; turn: number }              // snapshot value, no tree
  | { kind: 'tuning'; key: TuningKey }
  | { kind: 'input'; label: string; route: string };                     // a player-set value → its editor
interface NumProps { value: number; unit: Unit; explain: ExplainRef | null; fmt?: FmtOptions;
                     goodDirection?: 'up' | 'down' | 'none' }
```

**Popover** (320 px): label and formatted value; a formula line generated from `op` and children (`= Labor + Fuel + Maintenance + Camp + Consumables + Site fixed`); up to `ui.explainPopoverChildren` (5) children with values; `note`, if any; `Open breakdown` (drawer).

**Drawer** (440 px):
- The full tree, expanded to `ui.explainDefaultDepth` (2). Each row: label, value + unit, op symbol (Σ × ÷ min max lookup draw clamp), source chip, note.
- **Source chips:** *tuning* opens the read-only Tuning viewer: key, resolved value, base default, difficulty multiplier, scenario override, and the active `EffectModifier`s on it that come from **player-visible** event instances (an effect that has not been announced, such as a §12 season shift that has not landed, is omitted). *entity* navigates to the entity route. *rng* shows `Random draw - stream ops-grade/1043/clm_000012`; a percentile is shown only when the owning section flags the draw `publicParams: true`, meaning every parameter of its distribution is visible (D-13.37). Gold price draws are never shown as percentiles, because the GARCH state and regime are hidden; the price tree uses §10's decomposition with its `Other / unexplained` node. *ledger* opens the filtered ledger.
- **Compare with last week** (for `report` refs): the same path in the prior week's tree, with the children that changed most highlighted with Δ. **Copy as text** for bug reports. Breadcrumbs (`explain.stack`) walk back up after following links.

**Precomputed vs on demand.**

| Kind of number | How it is explained | Retention |
|---|---|---|
| Dice-dependent weekly results: bcy moved, stage capacities, idle breakdown, recovery, fuel, wear, failures, injuries, cleanup weights, gold price move, permit review progress | `report` ref into calc trees built during `advanceWeek` with explain on | full trees for the last `ui.calcRetentionWeeks` (4) weeks in memory; the last `ui.calcPersistWeeks` (1) week persisted in `UiPersisted.recentReports` (skipped if it serializes above `ui.persistReportMaxKb`, 200 kB); older weeks fall back to `history` value + ledger postings (D-13.10) |
| Pure functions of current state: net worth, liquidity, claim valuation, breakeven and cutoff grades, cost/oz, loan payoff, forecast, covenant ratios, capacity preview | `live` ref → `explain.*` on demand, memoized per (state ref, args) | always available for the current state |
| Money movements | `ledger` ref | always: transaction detail for the last 52 weeks, then §11's balance-preserving monthly summaries (D-11.47), so an older `ledger` ref opens the month's summary rows |
| Player inputs (hours/shift, feed target, planning price) | `input` ref → the editor | n/a |

**Redaction of hidden truth.** A calc tree can contain truth: contained gold uses the true block grade, a failure roll uses true component health. Every node built from a hidden field is tagged `hidden: true` at source (Needs from §2). Owning sections may attach `knownAlt`, a node built from the player's knowledge. The renderer replaces each hidden node with its `knownAlt`, or with `Not observable` if there is none, and drops the hidden subtree. Percentiles appear only under the `publicParams` rule above, because observed value + percentile would reveal a hidden mean or variance (D-13.9). The dev-only "reveal" toggle (§2.5) shows the raw tree with a striped `DEV TRUTH` banner and is compiled out of production builds.

**Worked example.** The player clicks "Direct cost per bcy $13.60" for last week on the §7 7.8 claim (seasonal road; owner as foreman; 4 operators, a plant operator and a laborer at 66 h; the numbers are §7 7.11.1's, including its P1 maintenance rates for grade-A iron, skill-50 operators and no in-house mechanic).
```
Direct cost per bcy washed                 $13.60/bcy   ratio
├─ Direct operating cost                   $44,379      sum
│  ├─ Labor incl. burden                   $19,951      product
│  │  ├─ Gross wages (6 crew, 66 h, OT>40)  $16,353     sum      [entity links to each employee]
│  │  └─ P1 burden 1 + 0.14 + 0.08          1.22        sum      tuning: finance.p1PayrollTaxRate, finance.p1WcRate (§11)
│  ├─ Fuel                                 $8,086       product
│  │  ├─ Fuel burned                       ≈1,797 gal   sum      [machines 1,625 (fuelBurnGalHr × hours) + camp 172]
│  │  └─ Delivered diesel                  $4.50/gal    sum      rack $3.60 (§10) + seasonal-road adder $0.90 (§3)
│  ├─ Maintenance (P1 flat)                $11,135      sum      325 SMR h, each machine × fleet.p1MaintUsdPerHr[model] (§9):
│  │                                                             excavator $33, truck $38, loader $33, trommel $15, pump $4, D8 $78
│  ├─ Camp                                 $2,695       product  49 person-days × $55 (ops.campUsdPerPersonDay)
│  ├─ Consumables                          $1,762       sum      3,264 washed, 3,114 dug, 6,999 stripped (1,909 frozen) (§7 tuning)
│  └─ Site fixed                           $750         lookup   ops.siteFixedUsdPerWeek
└─ Pay washed                              3,264 bcy    product  46.6 plant work-hours × 70 bcy/h feed target [report: ops flow]
```

### 13.14 Onboarding: setup wizard, guided first season, end of run

**Setup wizard** (`#/new`). It follows §1 1.6's order and builds a `NewGameSetup` exactly (D-13.42). A left step list and a right summary panel show the resulting starting position (company cash, personal cash, personal credit, assets, debts, starting reputation, owner net worth, from §1 1.8 scaled by difficulty). `Back` / `Next`; every step is validated before Next is enabled, with §1's codes (`NAME_EMPTY`, `NAME_TOO_LONG`, `BACKED_TERMS_REQUIRED`, `ENTITY_NOT_ALLOWED`, `SCENARIO_UNKNOWN`, `DISTRICT_TEMPLATE_NOT_IN_PHASE`, `INHERITOR_NEEDS_NORTHERN`).

| Step | Fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Mode | Sandbox, or a scenario card (goal, deadline, medals, fixed start/background/entity from §1 1.10) | P1: sandbox only; scenarios P6 |
| 2. Difficulty | Easy / Standard / Hard with §1's knob table summarized | Standard only in the UI until P6 (the simulator uses all three from P1) |
| 3. Company & owner | Company name and owner name (1-40 chars each) | |
| 4. Entity | Cards (sole prop / LLC / corp): formation cost, annual fees, liability shield, tax treatment, how lenders treat personal guarantees (§1 1.6). Disallowed combinations (sole prop + Backed equity) are disabled with the reason | P1 note: `Taxes, liability shield and guarantees take effect in a later version` (only formation and annual fees apply) |
| 5. Owner background | 5 cards (operator, mechanic, geologist, banker, landman), each stating its one edge with the number and its P1 stub (§1 1.7) | |
| 6. Start | Bootstrapper / Backed (equity) / Backed (royalty) / Inheritor cards with §1 1.8's numbers; Backed shows the investor terms; Inheritor warns `claim quality unknown, equipment worn, existing debt` | All four in P1 (§1 1.19) |
| 7. World | Seed (default: 26-char base32 from `crypto.getRandomValues`; editable; `Copy`), start year (default 2027), districts as `NewGameSetup.world.districtTemplates` of §3 region template IDs, each card showing its climate as a label and its real jurisdiction (`Fictional district · Alaska, federal land` / `· Nevada, federal land`; P6 adds Alaska state land, Yukon and the temperate state; §6 6.1) (P1–P5 fixed: `northernFederal` (climate `northernInterior`) + `aridFederal` (climate `aridDesert`); P6 adds up to 4 more), opening gold price (advanced; default $4,200) | the engine receives the seed string only; an Inheritor start needs a `northernFederal` district (`INHERITOR_NEEDS_NORTHERN`); the step ends with §6's disclaimer line, `Rules in this game are simplified game mechanics, not legal or regulatory advice.` |
| 8. Review | Summary; options: Guided first season (`NewGameSetup.tutorial`; default on for a first game, `ui.tutorialDefaultOnFirstGame`), Ironman (UI-only: one autosave slot, no undo); from P2 the auto-pay defaults per obligation category (§6 D-6.16: land on at every difficulty) with the trade-off `Auto-pay → no missed fees; cash leaves without a click` | `Start` calls `newGame` and saves slot 1 |

**Guided first season.** A coach panel docked bottom-right (collapsible). Steps are data in `data/text/tutorial.ts`; each has a title, a 1-2 sentence body with state params (`You have {cash} and no ground.`), a completion predicate (a pure selector over `GameState` + route), an optional `Show me` (navigates and spotlights a `data-tutorial-anchor`), and `Dismiss`. `Skip tutorial` turns it off; Help > Tutorial resets it. The coach **never blocks input, never advances time, and never chooses for the player** (D-13.23). The default steps implement §1 1.15's first ten turns (Bootstrapper, standard, arid district first while the north is frozen):

| # | §1 week | Step | Completes when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | Read your position: cash, runway, season forecast per district | Dashboard visited |
| 2 | 1 | Browse the claims market (arid district) | Market visited with a district filter applied |
| 3 | 1 | Watch three listings | `world.watch.claimIds.length ≥ 3` (§3, set by `world/setWatch`) |
| 4 | 1 | Seller data is not evidence | Evidence tab of a watched listing visited |
| 5 | 2 | Pay for information | ≥ 1 site visit (§3 `world/siteVisit`), pan survey (§4 `prospect/panSurvey`) or records review (§4 `prospect/recordsReview`) booked on a watched listing (§4 P1 allows only pans on listings, through a site visit) |
| 6 | 3 | Read the results; estimates have ranges | A results report opened and the Estimate tab visited afterwards |
| 7 | 3 | Acquire ground (lease vs buy) | tenure count ≥ 1 |
| 8 | 4 | Equip, hire and set your own role | machines that can fill dig and plant are owned, plus water unless the plant is a dry washer; ≥ 1 operator employed; a plan on the leased claim could activate (§7 `FOREMAN_REQUIRED` would not fire): the owner's current or pending assignment is foreman or operator on it (§1 `owner/setAssignment`), a hired foreman is assigned to it (§8), or it qualifies as a small crew (at most `staff.smallCrewMaxNoForeman` hands, one line, one shift; §8 8.12), in which case the coach explains the ×0.92 efficiency and ×1.15 injury cost of running without a foreman |
| 9 | 5 | Mobilize and write a mine plan | site status ≠ none and a `MinePlan` with ≥ 1 cut block exists |
| 10 | 6 | Read the bottleneck view | Flow tab visited after the claim's first operating week |
| 11 | 7 | Fix the constraint | the plan or fleet changed after step 10, and the preview viewed |
| 12 | 8 | First cleanup: raw vs fine, royalty in kind | a lot exists and the Sell tab visited (sale or hold) |
| 13 | 9 | Month-end P&L and cost per ounce | Reports visited after the first month-end week with revenue |
| 14 | 10 | Seasons and timing: the winter trail closes about Wk 13 | stop rules opened and a run used, or ground watched or acquired in the northern district |

Variants (§1 1.15): **From P2 (authority path).** A lease of raw ground has no operating authority, so step 2 filters the market to listings presenting a transferable plan (each starting district has a guaranteed starter permitted lease, §3/§5); step 5 adds a records check on the chosen listing (§6 `permits/recordsCheck`, $250, 1 week, the true permit tier and bond) and completes when its result is read, before step 7 commits. The coach also explains the alternative (a Notice bulk sample under 590 bcy on raw ground while a plan is prepared); if the player leases raw ground anyway, steps 9–12 route to the Notice and the bulk sample and the first full cleanup moves to the next season. **Inheritor** starts with the estate letter, the note statement, family records and fleet prompts (inspect the iron in P3, review records now, test-pit the family ground after thaw). **Backed equity** adds the investor's annual-plan request (a non-blocking decision whose default is the floor plan at week 4).

**End of run** (`#/end`; §1 1.14). Rendered from §1 `endReport(state)`, which returns the 1.14 fields once `runStatus ≠ 'active'` (weekly series from §2's `HistorySlice`). The headline uses the display face on a grain band; everything below it is data and sits on flat surfaces. Outcome and dates, with the liquidation path when the run ended in one (`Liquidated: filed` / `involuntary` / `converted from reorganization` / `insolvency counter`), seed with `Export action log` for replay; score = owner real net worth × `game.scoreMult` and the medal (scenarios), marked `capped at silver` when a reorganization capped it. **Reorganization** (when any case was filed; P4): filing week and debts at filing against the limit, plan length, scheduled payments and the share promised to unsecured creditors, confirmation week and whether it was consensual, payments made and missed, outcome (completed and discharged, converted, or still open when the run ended), total cost (filing, attorney, trustee), the amount discharged, and the investors' stance through the case. Charts: owner and company net worth by week (annual rollups beyond the 156-week history), cash, production by year (raw and fine oz), cash and all-in cost per oz by year. Claims table: how acquired, cost, ounces, per-claim P&L. **The reveal**: for each claim, three heat maps side by side (true block grades, the player's final estimate, the seller's claims) labelled with the seller's honesty type; inherited equipment's true condition history (P3+). A biggest-decisions timeline (purchases, loans, hires and sales above $50k, distress stages entered, and any reorganization filing, confirmation, missed plan payment and conversion) and rule-based lessons (`Bought clm_000042 on seller data only (seller was cherry-picked)`). `Export run report (CSV/JSON)`, `New game with same seed`, and `Continue in sandbox` after a scenario win only. After the report the save becomes read-only. This is the only screen that renders hidden truth, and only when `company.runStatus ≠ 'active'` (D-13.41).

### 13.15 Keyboard shortcuts

| Keys | Action | Keys | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ctrl+Enter` | Advance week | `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` | Run to next decision |
| `Esc` | Close popover/drawer; stop a run | `?` | Shortcut sheet |
| `Ctrl+K` or `/` | Command palette | `Ctrl+S` | Quick save to the current slot |
| `Ctrl+Z` | Undo the last undoable action this week (13.18) | `E` / `Enter` on a number | Explain |
| `g d` / `g i` / `g c` | Dashboard / Inbox / Calendar | `g l` / `g o` / `g e` | Claims (land) / Operations / Equipment |
| `g s` / `g p` / `g b` | Staff / Permits / Bank | `g g` / `g r` / `g n` | Gold / Reports / News |
| `g m` / `g x` / `g u` | Map / Prospecting (exploration) / Company & owner (you) | `j` / `k` | Next / previous row or message |
| `[` / `]` | Previous / next claim (Ops, Claim detail) | `1`-`9` on a selected card | Assign to role (assignments board) |
| `Alt+↑/↓` | Reorder (cut sequence, work orders, payment priority) | arrows on the block grid | Move focus; `Space` toggles selection |
| `+` / `−` / `0` | Map zoom in / out / fit | `Alt+1`–`Alt+3` on a selected card | Move a line-role card to plant line L1–L3 (assignments board, P3) |
| `{` / `}` | Previous / next plant line (Plan, Flow, Production, Cleanups; P3) | | |

Advance is deliberately on `Ctrl+Enter`, not a bare key, so a week can't be skipped by accident. Shortcuts are disabled while focus is in a text field, except `Esc`.

### 13.16 Save / load UI

- **Saves screen.** Slots table with columns: slot name, company, in-game date, cash, net worth (from `SaveFile.summary`), saved at (local wall clock), rules version, size, status (`active` / `ended` read-only). Actions: Load, Save here, Rename, Delete (with confirmation), Export.
- **Title screen.** Continue (latest autosave), New game, Load, Import.
- **Autosave** (D-13.25): after every `advanceWeek`, rotating across `ui.autosaveRotatingSlots` (3); a **year-start** snapshot at Wk 1 of each year, keeping the last `ui.autosaveYearlyKeep` (5); during runs the worker writes one every `ui.autosaveEveryRunWeeks` (8) weeks and at the stop, using the `UiPersisted` snapshot it received at run start. Writes are asynchronous; a failure shows a critical toast with `Export now`.
- **Export.** `.gmt.json`, optionally gzip `.gmt.json.gz`, with the action log included when the "Include replay log" setting is on. **Import.** File picker or drag-and-drop. Validation order: `format` → `schemaVersion` (older → migrate with a notice listing the migrations; newer → error `SAVE_TOO_NEW`) → parse → `tuningHash` (if it differs from what the current data resolve for the save's own setup, §2.9: notice `This game keeps the tuning it was created with`).
- **Size budget** (§2.13 per-slice budgets; D-13.10, D-13.54). §13's parts of a year-10 save: the inbox slice in `GameState` ≤ 0.3 MB (about 10 messages a week, kept until 104 weeks after closing, at about 250 bytes each ≈ 0.26 MB) and `SaveFile.ui` ≤ 0.25 MB (the persisted calc week, dropped above `ui.persistReportMaxKb` = 200 kB, plus inbox flags, layouts, stop rules and baselines of a few kB each). Test T26.
- **Ironman** saves have one slot plus autosave, no manual slots and no undo. The `Unsaved changes` dot appears after any action since the last write. An ended run's save loads straight into `#/end`.

### 13.17 CSV export

Generated in the browser (a Blob download). File name: `gmt_{companySlug}_{reportId}_{periodLabel}.csv`. RFC 4180 quoting; UTF-8 with BOM, so spreadsheets open it cleanly. Metadata lines start with `#` (company, period, in-game week generated, rules version), followed by one header row with units (`Net cash (USD)`). Numbers are unformatted: dollars with 2 decimals and no separators, negatives with `-`, gold to 3 dp, grades to 6 dp. Columns follow the current view (column chooser order). Available for every table and report.

### 13.18 UI architecture

**Store (Zustand).** One store with slices; components subscribe through selectors.
```ts
interface UiStore {
  game: { state: GameState | null; reports: WeekReportSummary[];      // newest first, ≤ ui.reportsInMemory (13)
          calcReports: WeekReport[];                                  // full trees, ≤ ui.calcRetentionWeeks (4)
          undo: { prev: GameState; action: Action }[];                // this week only, ≤ ui.undoMaxEntries (50)
          actionLog: LoggedAction[]; slotId: string | null; dirty: boolean };
  run:  { status: 'idle' | 'running' | 'stopping'; anchor?: RunAnchor; maxWeeks: number;
          progress: { turn: number; cashCents: Cents; weighedRawOz: number }[]; summary?: RunSummary };
  nav:  { route: Route };
  selection: { claimId?: ClaimId; machineId?: Id; employeeId?: Id; blockIds: Id[] };
  drafts: { minePlans: Record<ClaimId, MinePlanDraft>; offers: Record<Id, OfferDraft>; programs: Record<Id, ProgramDraft>;
            applications: Record<Id, ApplicationDraft>; reorgPlan?: ReorgPlanTermsDraft };   // §11 ReorgPlanTerms being built (P4)
  explain: { stack: ExplainRef[] };
  persisted: UiPersisted;                                            // written to SaveFile.ui
  prefs: Prefs;                                                      // global, localStorage (try/catch)
}
interface UiPersisted {
  inbox: Record<MsgId, { read: boolean; archived: boolean; snoozedUntilTurn?: number }>;   // pruned at save to ids still in state
  stopRules: StopRule[]; savedSearches: { id: string; screen: 'claims' | 'equipment'; filter: ListingFilter; alert: boolean }[];
  searchNotices: { searchId: string; listingIds: Id[]; turn: number }[];                   // UI-only match badges
  baselines: Record<ClaimId, Record<number /* year */, SeasonBaseline>>;
  tableLayouts: Record<string, { columns: string[]; sort: SortSpec[]; filters: FilterSpec[] }>;
  tutorial: { enabled: boolean; completed: string[]; dismissed: string[] };
  recentReports: WeekReport[];             // ≤ ui.calcPersistWeeks (1); omitted if it serializes above ui.persistReportMaxKb (200)
  ironman: boolean; uiVersion: number;
}
interface Prefs { theme: 'system' | 'daylight' | 'lamplight'; density: 'comfortable' | 'compact'; fontScale: 1 | 1.125 | 1.25;
  reducedMotion: 'system' | 'on' | 'off'; texture: boolean /* accessibility patterns */; headerGrain: boolean /* decorative, 13.20 */;
  confirmAdvanceSheet: boolean; compactTiles: boolean }
```
`UiPersisted` lives in `SaveFile.ui`, outside `GameState`. Inbox read flags, layouts, stop rules and baselines therefore never change replays or state hashes (D-13.3). Run identity (`runId`, `RunAnchor`) is UI-only as well (D-13.35).

**Engine client** (`ui/engine/engineClient.ts`):
- `apply(action)`: synchronous `applyAction`. On success it pushes an undo entry only if the result is `undoable` (the engine sets it false when the action drew from an RNG stream, revealed hidden information, or made a commitment to a counterparty; Needs from §2) and Ironman is off; it appends to `actionLog` and marks the state dirty. On failure it returns the typed error to the form.
- `validate(action)`: synchronous, used to enable or disable controls with a reason.
- `advance()`: synchronous `advanceWeek(state, { explain: true })`. Budget: ≤ `ui.advanceBudgetMs` (20 ms) engine with explanations on + ≤ 50 ms render (§2.13). The simulator budget (§2.13: ≤ 3.5 ms mean per week, explanations off) does not apply here; the extra time pays for calc trees and §7's what-if hints (six visible-model runs per claim). It clears the undo stack, runs `captureBaselines(prev, next, persisted)`, and schedules the autosave via `requestIdleCallback`.
- `run(opts)`: posts to the **run worker** (D-13.2).
- **Invariant:** the explain flag never changes `GameState`. Calc trees and other explanation-only outputs (§7 what-if hints included) live only in the `WeekReport` (D-13.36, test T18).

**Run worker** (`ui/engine/engine.worker.ts`, Vite module worker; it imports the same engine bundle):
```
main → worker: { type: 'run', runId, state, rules, anchor, maxWeeks, uiSnapshot }  |  { type: 'cancel', runId }
worker loop:   for i in 1..maxWeeks:
                 w = advanceWeek(s, { explain: true }); reasons = evaluateStops(s, w, rules, anchor)
                 baselines = captureBaselines(s, w.state, baselines); s = w.state
                 post { type: 'progress', runId, turn, cashCents, weighedRawOzWeek, alertCounts }
                 keep summaries of all weeks + full reports of the last ui.calcRetentionWeeks
                 if reasons.length or cancelled: break
                 every ui.autosaveEveryRunWeeks weeks: write autosave to IndexedDB from the worker
                 await yield (setTimeout 0)  // lets 'cancel' arrive; allowed here (ui/, not engine/)
worker → main: { type: 'done', runId, state, summaries, calcReports, baselines, stoppedBecause } | { type: 'error', runId, message }
```
The state crosses the boundary twice per run by structured clone (bounded by §2.13's year-10 save budget; about 10-30 ms each way). Progress messages are a few dozen bytes, so the main thread stays responsive. The loop is pure engine calls, so its result equals `runToNextDecision` for the same inputs (test T6), whatever the explain flag (T18).

**Selectors.** `useSel(selector, ...args)` memoizes per selector with a cache keyed on the state slices the selector declares (`deps: s => [s.finance, s.clock]`) plus args. Immer's structural sharing keeps unchanged slices reference-equal, so most lookups after a week are cache hits. Components never compute game math; they call `select.*` and `explain.*` and format with `ui/format`. The few UI-side derivations (stage rows, baseline variance, reconciliation factors, heat-map bins, the supervision chip's text) are pure functions in `screens/*/selectors.ts` over visible fields only, with unit tests.

**Component structure.**
```
src/ui/
  app/         AppShell, TopBar (incl. CaseChip), LeftNav, Router (hash), CommandPalette, Toasts, LiveRegion, ThemeRoot (data-theme)
  theme/       tokens.css (both themes, 13.20), fonts.css (@font-face, metric-matched fallbacks), grain.ts (the noise tile), tokens.test.ts (T20)
  store/       store.ts, gameSlice, runSlice, persistedSlice, prefs
  engine/      engineClient.ts, engine.worker.ts, summarizeRun.ts, baselines.ts
  explain/     Num.tsx, ExplainPopover, ExplainDrawer, redact.ts, formulaText.ts, TuningViewer
  format/      money, gold, grade, units, dates, csv
  components/  DataTable, StatTile, RangeBar, Meter, StatusChip, SupervisionChip, Kanban, BlockGrid, Stepper, EmptyState, PeriodPicker, LineTabs
  charts/      theme.ts, Sparkline, FanChart, StageBars, CashForecast, PriceChart, SeasonStrip, StackedCost, Tornado, Bullet
  screens/     dashboard/ inbox/ calendar/ claims/ map/ prospecting/ ops/ equipment/ (incl. shop boards) staff/ permits/ bank/ (incl. reorganization/) gold/ reports/
               company/ news/ saves/ settings/ help/ setup/ end/
  tutorial/    Coach.tsx, predicates.ts (texts and steps in data/text/tutorial.ts)
```
Each screen folder holds `Screen.tsx`, one file per tab or panel, and `selectors.ts` (screen-specific view models built from engine selectors).

**Recharts usage.** Recharts covers sparklines (`LineChart`, no axes), line and area charts, fan charts (`ComposedChart`: a stacked `Area` pair for the P10–P90 band on a transparent base, plus a `Line` for P50), column, stacked-bar, tornado and bullet charts (`BarChart`, `layout="vertical"`). Custom SVG covers the block grid, district map, season strip, meters, range bars and stage bars (stage bars need annotations Recharts handles poorly). Rules: one y-axis per chart; never dual-axis; every chart has a crosshair or tooltip rendered with `<Num>`, so values in tooltips are explainable; `isAnimationActive` only when reduced motion is off and the chart has < 500 points; every chart has a `Table view` toggle and a `<figure>` caption summary; colors come only from `charts/theme.ts`, which reads the CSS tokens.

### 13.19 Layout, theme, accessibility

**Breakpoints** (desktop-first; no touch-specific design, D-13.27):

| Width | Behavior |
|---|---|
| ≥ 1440 | full layout; drawer pushes content |
| 1280-1439 (`ui.layout.fullLayoutMinPx`) | full functionality; nav collapses to the icon rail by default; drawer overlays; dashboard keeps 12 columns |
| 1024-1279 (`ui.layout.minWidthPx`) | graceful: dashboard goes to 2 columns (rows 2-4 stack); season chips collapse into one `Seasons` chip; tables scroll horizontally inside their card; the assignments board scrolls horizontally |
| < 1024 | banner `Best on a screen at least 1280 px wide`; layout as at 1024 with page-level horizontal scroll |

Minimum height is 720 px. Content max width is 1680 px, centered.

**Theme** (owner ruling 2026-10-05, D-13.56). Business-software structure, density and accessibility are unchanged; the theme is a frontier mining look laid over them. Two themes: **Daylight** (parchment surfaces, lamp-black ink, slate chrome) and **Lamplight** (warm umber-black surfaces, parchment ink, near-black chrome), or `System`, which follows `prefers-color-scheme`. Each theme has its own selected token steps; there is no automatic inversion. Status fills and their chip labels are the same in both themes; status text tokens differ per theme (13.20). Charts use each theme's own series and ramp steps. The theme decorates chrome and titles only: tables, charts, the map, the block grid, forms and every number stay on flat surfaces in the data face.

**Accessibility (target WCAG 2.2 AA).**
- Contrast: text tokens ≥ 4.5:1 and UI component and graphic tokens ≥ 3:1 on every surface they are used on, in both themes and over the worst pixel of the header grain, checked by a token test (T20). Hairlines and axis baselines are decorative (values are read from labels, tooltips and table twins) and are exempt. Status fills under 3:1 (warning and serious on Daylight surfaces; good on the Daylight page) are only ever used as chip backgrounds with their `status-*-on` labels. Series colors below 3:1 (Daylight slots 2 and 5, Lamplight slot 4; 13.20) must be direct-labelled or come with the table view.
- Everything works by keyboard. The focus ring is 2 px `accent` with a 2 px offset on content surfaces and 2 px `brass-on-chrome` on the chrome, where slate accent on slate chrome would vanish. Drag-and-drop always has a keyboard equivalent (13.15).
- Semantics: tables are real `<table>` elements (`aria-rowcount`/`aria-rowindex` when virtualized); the block grid is `role="grid"`; kanban columns are lists with move buttons; popovers are `role="dialog"` and return focus to the triggering number on close.
- Never color alone: status = icon + label; deltas = arrow + sign; map = pattern + label; heat map = glyphs, hatching + legend; texture mode available.
- No real-time limits: all deadlines are in game weeks, and runs stop on anything critical.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` respected. `prefers-contrast: more` and `forced-colors: active` switch the grain off and draw chips and markers with system colors plus their icons and patterns. Font scale up to 125% without loss of content; the display face scales with it and never drops below `ui.theme.displayMinPx`. Polite live-region week summaries; assertive only for blocking and critical.
- Charts have table twins; tooltips are never the only way to read a value.
- All strings go through a `t()` catalog (English only) so copy can be edited and localized later (D-13.12).

### 13.20 Theme and design tokens (Tailwind)

The look is set by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-05: business-software structure, density and accessibility, dressed in a rugged mining theme (D-13.56). Tokens are CSS custom properties: Daylight values on `:root`, Lamplight values under `:root[data-theme="lamplight"]` and, for the `system` preference, under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="daylight"]) { … } }`, so an explicit choice always beats the OS setting. `ThemeRoot` sets `data-theme` from `Prefs.theme` (`daylight` or `lamplight`; no attribute for `system`) and the matching CSS `color-scheme`, so native scrollbars and pickers follow. `tailwind.config` maps utilities to the variables (`bg-surface-1`, `text-ink-2`, `border-hairline`, `fill-series-3`, `bg-chrome`). Every value below was computed, not eyeballed: WCAG 2.2 relative-luminance contrast, and OKLab ΔE × 100 with protanopia and deuteranopia simulated by Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes (2009) at severity 1.0, using the data-viz palette checks (lightness band, chroma floor, CVD separation, normal-vision floor, contrast). Figures are rounded to one decimal place unless quoted to two; T20 recomputes them in CI and checks each to within 0.1 (D-13.70).

**Palette.** Earth tones: parchment and umber surfaces, lamp-black and parchment ink, slate chrome and accent, brass ornament, and an ochre, spruce, rust, plum and glacier series. Contrast figures are the worst case over the theme's three surfaces unless a surface is named.

| Token | Daylight | Lamplight | Use; contrast (Daylight / Lamplight) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `surface-0` / `surface-1` / `surface-2` | `#f1ebdf` / `#faf7f1` / `#fffdf9` (parchment) | `#14110d` / `#1d1914` / `#27221b` (umber) | page / cards, tables and charts / raised (popover, drawer) |
| `ink-1` / `ink-2` / `ink-3` | `#1c1813` / `#4a4137` / `#665b4e` | `#f4ecdc` / `#cfc2ab` / `#a59882` | primary / secondary / muted text: 14.9 / 13.4, 8.4 / 9.0, 5.6 / 5.6 |
| `hairline` / `axis` | `#e0d6c4` / `#b5a78f` | `#342d24` / `#4a4135` | borders and gridlines / baselines; decorative, so exempt from 3:1 (13.19) |
| `border-control` | `#8b7e6a` | `#7a6e5c` | outlines of inputs, selects and checkboxes: 3.3 / 3.2 (WCAG 1.4.11) |
| `accent` / `on-accent` | `#2a669f` / `#ffffff` | `#4284c4` / `#14110d` | equals `series-1` (slate): focus ring, primary buttons, "yours" on the map: 5.05 / 4.0 on surfaces; button label 6.0 / 4.8 |
| `link` | `#2a5a8c` | `#8fb4de` | link text: 6.0 / 7.3 |
| `chrome` / `chrome-ink` / `chrome-ink-2` / `chrome-hairline` | `#2b3640` (slate) / `#f3ecdf` / `#c2c9ce` / `#3d4a55` | `#0f0d0a` / `#f4ecdc` / `#bdb09a` / `#2a251e` | top bar and nav: ink 10.5 / 16.5, ink-2 7.4 / 9.1 on flat chrome |
| `brass` / `brass-on-chrome` | `#a8761f` / `#e3b04b` | `#e0ad4a` / `#e0ad4a` | brand ornament only (wordmark, active-nav marker, title rule) and the focus ring on chrome; graphic, never text: 3.35 / 7.7 on surfaces, 6.2 / 9.5 on chrome |
| `status-good` / `-warning` / `-serious` / `-critical` | `#3f9e3a` / `#f2b233` / `#e6703a` / `#cc3340` | same | chip fills and status graphics. Lamplight: all ≥ 3.0 (critical 3.09 on raised). Daylight: critical 4.30 on the page (its worst surface), good 3.2 on cards (2.9 on the page), warning 1.6 and serious 2.6 by design, so used only as chip fills with labels |
| `status-*-on` | `#1c1813` on good, warning and serious; `#ffffff` on critical | same | chip label and icon: 5.2 / 9.4 / 5.7 / 5.1 |
| `status-*-text` | `#2c6e33` / `#80570a` / `#9c4419` / `#a8283a` | `#6cc06f` / `#f2b233` / `#ec9064` / `#f27c80` | status as bare text: ≥ 5.2 / ≥ 5.9 |
| `series-1..8` | `#2a669f #dc932e #1f8861 #853e80 #1fa3bb #ba4e25 #554ca0 #db6686` | `#4284c4 #c37c00 #46a37d #92478d #0f9db4 #c1552c #7c76c8 #cf6681` | categorical, fixed order: slate, ochre, spruce, plum, glacier, rust, indigo, fireweed (validation below) |
| `seq-gold-100..700` | `#fcedcd #f2d397 #e4b154 #d1900b #ae7206 #8d5401 #6a3a06` | same ramp | gold quantities: the grade P50 layer, contained and minable ounces |
| `seq-slate-100..700` | `#e4f0fb #c2dbf1 #99bfe3 #74a3d1 #5384b7 #3b6695 #28496f` | same ramp | every other magnitude: depth, strip, pay column, uncertainty ratio, water |
| `div-neg` / `div-mid` / `div-pos` (bins 1–3 per arm) | slate 300 / 500 / 700 · `#e9e3d8` · gold 300 / 500 / 700 | slate 500 / 300 / 200 · `#3b352d` · gold 500 / 300 / 200 | the heat map against cutoff (13.5): below cutoff slate, above it gold, uncertain blocks pulled toward the neutral midpoint |

Both ramps hold one hue (gold from OKLCH hue 86° at the pale end to 60° at the dark end; slate 245°–253°) at OKLCH L 0.95, 0.88, 0.79, 0.70, 0.60, 0.50 and 0.40, so lightness is monotone by construction. Daylight maps low → high to 100 → 700; Lamplight flips the anchor (700 → 100), so "more" is always the step farther from the surface.

**Categorical validation** (D-13.57). The order is the CVD-safety mechanism: candidate orders of the eight hues were enumerated and their lightness and chroma tuned until every gate passed in both themes.

| Check | Daylight (on `#faf7f1`) | Lamplight (on `#1d1914`) |
|---|---|---|
| OKLCH lightness band (0.43–0.77 / 0.48–0.67) and chroma ≥ 0.10 | pass | pass |
| Worst adjacent pair, protan or deutan (target ≥ 8) | 11.4 (plum–spruce) | 11.3 (spruce–ochre) |
| Worst adjacent pair, normal vision (floor ≥ 15) | 24.4 (spruce–ochre) | 16.9 (indigo–fireweed) |
| Slots 1–3 all-pairs, CVD / normal (map and scatter forms use ≤ 3) | 12.3 / 16.4 | 11.3 / 16.2 |
| Below 3:1 on the surface (relief: direct labels or the table view) | ochre 2.4, glacier 2.8 (fireweed 2.8 on the page) | plum 2.9 (2.6 on raised) |

Status against the nearest series hue (normal-vision ΔE): good–spruce 9.5 / 8.1, warning–ochre 8.7 / 16.0, serious–ochre 8.5 / 7.8, critical–rust 6.6 / 7.0. An earth palette with gold and rust in it puts status and series hues near each other, so a status color is never used as a series and always ships with its icon and label (13.2).

**Typography** (D-13.59).

| Role | Face | Sizes and weights | Fallback stack | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Display | **Besley** (Owen Earl; SIL Open Font License 1.1), a revival of Robert Besley's 1845 Clarendon, the slab face of frontier handbills and assay-office ledgers; bundled as static 600 and 700 files | 32 and 24 px at 700 (title screen, screen titles); 20 and 16 px at 600 (section and panel headers); never below `ui.theme.displayMinPx` (16 px) | `"Besley", "Besley Fallback", Rockwell, "Roboto Slab", Georgia, serif` | screen titles, section and panel headers, wizard step titles, the company name in the top bar, the end-of-run headline, empty-state titles |
| Data and UI | **Inter** (Rasmus Andersson; SIL Open Font License 1.1), bundled as static 400, 500 and 600 upright and a 400 italic | 12, 13 and 14 px for body and tables (400; 500 for emphasis; 600 for totals); KPI values 24 px at 600 | `"Inter", "Inter Fallback", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif` | everything else: body, labels, buttons, chips, table headers and cells, inputs, tooltips, axes and every number |

- Every number is set with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums`, KPI values included: they change every week, and fixed-width digits keep tiles and columns from jittering (this replaces the old proportional-figure rule for KPI tiles). IDs, seeds and codes also take a slashed zero (`font-feature-settings: "zero"`).
- The display face never sets a number, a table, a form control, a chip, a button, a tooltip or body text: slab serifs clutter small text, and a display number would break the tabular rule.
- Fonts ship inside the build as self-hosted WOFF2 files from @fontsource, one file per weight and subset (the packages carry no single variable files): a Latin subset (Basic Latin and Latin-1 Supplement, enough for en-US) for every face, and a Latin Extended subset (Yukon place names) for Besley 600 and 700 and Inter 400 and 600. Inter 500 and the italic have no Latin Extended file, so a rare extended glyph in those styles falls back down the font stack; that keeps the ten files within `ui.fonts.maxKb` (260 kB, read as 260,000 bytes; the bundle is 226,660 bytes; D-13.71). `unicode-range` keeps a Latin Extended file from downloading until a page needs one of its glyphs, and faces are preloaded and loaded with `font-display: swap`. The game makes no font request over the network (it is hosted locally, owner ruling 2026-10-05). The `… Fallback` faces are `local()` system fonts with `size-adjust` and `ascent-override` computed at build time to match Besley's and Inter's metrics, so a late load never changes a row height or a column width.
- Scale 12/13/14/16/20/24/32 px; line height 1.4 for text and 1.2 for headings; sentence case for headers. Spacing on a 4 px grid. Radius 6 px for cards, 4 px for controls. One elevation shadow, used only for popovers and the drawer.

**Texture and ornament** (D-13.60, D-13.70).
- **Grain** is the only surface texture: a 128 × 128 px noise tile generated once from an SVG `feTurbulence` filter (base frequency 0.8, two octaves, desaturated) and embedded as a data URI of about 1 kB, with no image files. Each theme has two tiles of one flat speckle color: `--grain-band`, `ink-1`-colored (lamp-black in Daylight, parchment in Lamplight), for title bands, the wizard header, the title screen, the end-of-run band and empty states; and `--grain-chrome`, `chrome-ink`-colored, for the nav and the top bar's brand block. Per-pixel alpha is at most `ui.theme.grainOpacityDaylight` (0.05) or `ui.theme.grainOpacityLamplight` (0.07). It never moves.
- **Where grain may appear:** the nav and the top bar's brand block (chrome), screen-title bands, the setup wizard's header, the title screen, the end-of-run headline band and empty states. **Never:** in or behind any element that contains a `<Num>`, a table, a chart, the map, the block grid, a form control, a chip, a toast, a popover, the drawer or the inbox list, or the top bar's status cluster. A DOM test enforces it (T28).
- Text on grain keeps AA against the worst pixel: the band color with its tile's speckle composited over it at full grain opacity, each channel rounded to 8 bits as a screen shows it. Daylight `ink-3` 5.0:1 on a grained page band and `chrome-ink` 9.1:1 on grained chrome; Lamplight `ink-3` 5.7:1 and `chrome-ink` 14.3:1 (T20).
- Grain switches off with Settings > Display > `Header grain` (`Prefs.headerGrain`, default on), under `prefers-contrast: more` and `forced-colors: active`, and in print.
- **Ornament** is limited to a 2 px brass rule under screen titles (with a 1 px hairline 3 px below it, letterpress style), the 3 px brass active-nav marker, the wordmark, and line icons at a 1.5 px stroke. No photographs, wood-plank or leather backgrounds, distressed or "wanted poster" type, torn edges, drop caps, seals, or anything that imitates an agency's or a real company's documents (D-13.67).

**Chart palette** (`charts/theme.ts` reads the tokens, so a theme switch repaints every chart). Series slots 1–8 in fixed order; a claim keeps its slot everywhere (13.2), and no chart shows two series in one slot: past eight series it folds the rest into `Other` or switches to small multiples. One ramp per sequential layer (`seq-gold` for gold, `seq-slate` for everything else; a second sequential layer on screen at once takes the other ramp). Diverging only where a value sits below or above a reference (the cutoff heat map, the tornado chart's low and high bars): slate below, gold above, a neutral midpoint. Deltas keep 13.2's rule (status color by `goodDirection`, with arrow and sign). Marks: 2 px lines, markers ≥ 8 px, a 2 px surface gap between adjacent fills. Gridlines in `hairline`, baselines in `axis`; labels, values and legends in ink tokens, never in a series color. Status tokens only for state: a series that means good or bad wears status tokens and icons, and one chart never mixes the two. Texture mode adds the 45°/135° line fills. A series below 3:1 on its surface is direct-labelled (any chart with ≤ 4 series labels directly) or read through the chart's table twin.

### 13.21 Player actions

Only `decision/answer` is an engine action owned here. The rest are UI store actions: they never enter `GameState` or the action log. Every engine action named on these screens belongs to its owning section and is dispatched under the owner's name and params (watching is §3 `world/setWatch`, site visits §3 `world/siteVisit`, pans §4 `prospect/panSurvey`, batch payments §6 `permits/payObligations`, plant lines §7 `ops/setMinePlan` and `ops/setLineActive`, shop modes §8 `staff/assign` and §1 `owner/setAssignment`, work-order assignees §9 `fleet/scheduleWork`, the bankruptcy filings §11 `finance/fileReorganization`, `finance/fileReorgPlan` and `owner/fileBankruptcy`); test T24 checks every name against the owners' handler tables.

| Action `type` | Params | Validation (error codes) | Effect | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decision/answer` (engine) | `decisionId, optionId, params?` | `DECISION_NOT_FOUND`, `DECISION_CLOSED`, `OPTION_INVALID`, plus the option action's own codes | applies the option's stored engine action through the owning system; message → `answered` | P1 |
| `ui/advanceWeek` | — | `BLOCKING_DECISION_OPEN`, `RUN_IN_PROGRESS`, `GAME_OVER` | `advanceWeek`; store report; clear undo; capture baselines; autosave | P0 |
| `ui/runToNextDecision` | `maxWeeks, rules?` | same as above | worker run; run summary | P1 (custom rules P2) |
| `ui/cancelRun` | — | `NO_RUN` | stops after the current week; keeps the last completed week | P1 |
| `ui/undo` | — | `NOTHING_TO_UNDO`, `UNDO_NOT_ALLOWED` (action not undoable), `UNDO_IRONMAN` | restores the pre-action state; pops `actionLog` | P1 |
| `ui/setStopRules` | `StopRule[]` | `RULE_INVALID` (e.g. pct ≤ 0, weeks outside 1-8) | persists | P2 |
| `ui/muteAlertKind` | `kind, muted` | `CANNOT_MUTE_CRITICAL` | persists | P2 |
| `ui/inbox.mark` | `msgIds, read? archived? snoozeWeeks?` | `CANNOT_SNOOZE_BLOCKING` | persists | P1 |
| `ui/saveSearch` | `screen, filter, alert` | `MAX_SAVED_SEARCHES` | persists; enables `listingMatch` | P2 |
| `ui/rebaseline` | `claimId` | `NO_ACTIVE_PLAN` | new `SeasonBaseline` from the current visible projection | P1 |
| `ui/save` / `ui/load` / `ui/deleteSlot` | `slotId` | `SLOT_NOT_FOUND`, `IRONMAN_MANUAL_SAVE` | IndexedDB | P0 |
| `ui/export` / `ui/import` | `slotId` / `file` | `SAVE_CORRUPT`, `SAVE_FORMAT`, `SAVE_TOO_NEW` (+ notice `TUNING_DIFFERS`) | file I/O, migration | P0 |
| `ui/setPrefs` | `Partial<Prefs>` (incl. `theme: 'system' \| 'daylight' \| 'lamplight'`, `headerGrain`) | — | localStorage; sets `data-theme` | P0 |
| `ui/setTableLayout` | `tableId, layout` | — | persists | P1 |
| `ui/tutorial` | `dismiss stepId` / `disable` / `reset` | — | persists | P1 |
| `ui/exportCsv` | `tableId or reportId, period` | `EXPORT_EMPTY` | file download | P1 |
| `ui/openExplain` | `ExplainRef` | `EXPLAIN_EXPIRED` (beyond retention → offers ledger view) | popover / drawer | P1 |

Trade-offs for the player's own UI decisions: Lamplight or Daylight and header grain change nothing in the game, only comfort; wider stop rules → fewer interruptions, less time to react before a deadline or cash crunch; muting a warning kind → quieter runs, but the inbox becomes the only place it shows; standing sale orders → payroll protected in fast-forward, at the local buyer's discount; Ironman → no safety nets, a more honest game.

### 13.22 Weekly resolution

| Step (§2.6) | What §13 does |
|---|---|
| 0 Guard | Engine refuses to run with a blocking decision open; the UI pre-checks and routes to the decision |
| 1-15 | Systems append `AlertSignal`s and calc trees (calc trees only when `explain: true`) to the `WeekReport`; nothing explanation-only enters `GameState`. A blocking `PendingDecision` created mid-week (e.g. §12 in step 4, or §11's involuntary petition in step 15c) is collected at step 16 like any other created this turn. §11 raises the `reorg.*` signals in step 14f (a missed installment) and step 15a (deadlines, rulings, adequate protection, conversion risk), so each reaches the same week's collation |
| 16 Wrap-up | Order within step 16 (§2.6): §1 16a–16d (16d is the run-end check) → the section wrap-ups that emit signals (§3, §4, §5, §7, §8, §9, §10, §12, §14) → **§13 collation** → history snapshot → `WeekReport` and stop candidates, so a run that ended this week reaches `evaluateStops` as `gameOver`. **Collation** (13.10): obligation grouping, level/edge handling, reopen within the dedupe window, auto-resolve level messages, assign `msg_` IDs in sorted order, drop closed messages beyond retention. Mark `stopCandidates`. Non-blocking decisions at their deadline: the owning system applies `defaultOptionId`; message → `defaulted` |
| After step 16 (worker or main thread) | `evaluateStops(prev, week, rules, anchor)` → `StopReason[]` (runs only) |
| UI after the week | store the report summary (13 kept) and the full calc report (4 kept, 1 persisted); capture due baselines; apply toast rules; announce in the live region; evaluate tutorial predicates; evaluate saved-search matches (UI notices, P2); prune `UiPersisted.inbox`; autosave |

### 13.25 Tuning constants

`ui.*` keys live in `data/tuning/ui.ts`. They are application configuration: they affect presentation only, are not part of `TuningResolved`, and are excluded from `meta.tuningHash`, so changing one never forks a save (D-13.32). `game.alerts.*` keys are engine tuning: they change inbox contents and therefore state hashes. Alert thresholds that an emitting section already defines are read from that section and not duplicated here: §7 `ops.alertPlantIdlePct` 0.25 and `ops.coverageAlertWeeks` 2; §9 `fleet.pmOverdueWarnPct` 0.10 and `fleet.shopBacklogWarnWeeks` 2; §11 `finance.distress.watchWeeks` (6 / 4 / 3 by difficulty, the `cash.projectedNegative` window) and the covenant watch at 10% headroom. §13 owns no difficulty-scaled key, so it adds no row to §1 1.11.

### 13.26 Balance levers and risks

| Risk | Why it matters | Counter |
|---|---|---|
| **Leaking hidden truth** through explain trees, previews, chart scales, color bins or season widgets | It would collapse the core game (unknown ground, unknown iron, unknown season) into perfect information | `hidden` tags + `knownAlt` + redaction; contained and lost gold never rendered; VSUP gray for uncertain blocks; cutoff from the player's planning assumptions; `seasonView` hides unrevealed dates; Tuning viewer omits unannounced effect modifiers; percentiles only with `publicParams`; **scrambled-truth UI test** (T8, T23) |
| **Dice scumming** via undo or reload | The player re-rolls inspections, offers or sample draws | Undo only for `undoable` actions (no RNG, no information revealed, no counterparty commitment); weekly dice are keyed by turn (§2.3) and every action-time draw by subject, a §2 rule (§6 by stage, §10 buyer error by claim, §1 investor approvals by agreement, subject and request index, §8 offers by candidate and offer index); Ironman for players who want it |
| **Peeking then undoing** | An immediate information action (e.g. a §6 records check) refunded by undo after the player has read it | Such actions are not `undoable` |
| **Alert fatigue** | Players mute warnings, then miss September 1 | Level messages update in place; edge repeats stay separate but rare; critical is unmutable; obligation alerts group by (category, due week), so 12 claim fees are one message and one stop; obligations that settle themselves (billable payments, auto-paid payments, auto-filed forms) stay info and never fire the deadline stop; the ladder ends in critical, capped by the consequence so late-fee items never cry wolf. BALANCE O-13 holds the result to 25–60 stops a year and ≤ 10 in the off-season |
| **False cash alarms** (P1–P3) | A runway built from outflows alone reads `cash runs out in 3 weeks` every producing week, so players learn to ignore it | The P1–P3 forecast carries §11's P50 production line from planned cleanups, labelled `incl. planned cleanups (P50)`; the pre-advance sheet counts gold only when a standing order will sell it (D-13.48) |
| **Over-skipping in runs** feels like unfair losses | A crash happens while the player was away | Critical and blocking always stop; deadline notice defaults to 2 weeks; pre-advance shortfall sheet names the first creditor that goes short; standing sale orders; run summary lists everything |
| **Calculators trivialize decisions** | A channel calculator or capacity preview "solves" the game | They show the current price and expected values only; no future prices, dice or breakdowns; valuation and forecasts use the player's (possibly wrong) estimate; grade reconciliation shows the error only after mining |
| **Defaults set perceived difficulty** | Notice windows and the tutorial make the early game easier | The only difficulty-scaled input to §13's alerts is §11's `finance.distress.watchWeeks` (6 / 4 / 3, §1 1.11); all UI help is the same on every difficulty |
| **Theme over legibility** | A themed look can creep onto data (grain behind a table, a slab face on numbers, gold-on-parchment text) and undo the business-software reading rules | Grain only on chrome and title bands, never on any element holding a `<Num>`, table, chart, map or form (T28); the display face only for titles and headers ≥ 16 px; every number in Inter with tabular figures; every token and every grain worst case contrast-checked in both themes (T20); grain off under high contrast, forced colors and print |
| **Reorganization read as a reset button** | A filing a click away could turn every bad season into a cheap restart and hollow out the survival targets | The filing sits behind the eligibility card and a double confirmation that lists its costs (fees, credit marks, the pay cap, investor stance, the silver cap); the ladder offers it only from stage 4 (the tab from stage 2, as §11 allows); the plan builder shows that the plan pays every projected dollar for 3–5 years and that two misses convert the case; BALANCE counts any filing as a failure of its survival window (D-1.49) |
| **Plant lines and pool mechanics add clutter** | Most claims run one line and site mechanics; tabs and pool boards on every screen would burden the common case | Line tabs, line selectors and pool boards appear only from P3 and only where they apply (a second line allowed, a pool assigned); the one-line claim view is identical to the pre-ruling screens |
| **Performance and size in year 10** | Large ledgers and histories make the UI sluggish and the save large | Virtualization; memoized selectors on slice references; paginated `queryLedger` over §11's 52-week detail; worker runs; one persisted calc week, skipped above 200 kB; §13's slices within their §2.13 budgets; perf and size tests (T13, T26) |

### 13.27 Tests

1. **T1 Formatting.** Table-driven: `123456789¢ → $1,234,568`; `99950¢ → $999.50`; `−4512300¢ → −$45,123` / report `($45,123)` / ledger `−$45,123.00`; compact `$1,234,567 → $1.23M`, `$99,999 → $99,999`; `52.9014 raw → 52.901 raw oz`; `1234.5 fine → 1,234.50 fine oz`; `0.009512 → 0.0095 oz/bcy (0.39 g/m³)`; `6435.4 bcy → 6,435 bcy`; `0.78432 → 78.4%`; `0.0875 rate → 8.75%`; `turn 28 → Y1 Wk 29 · Jul 16–22, 2027`; Wk 35 contains Sept 1. Output is identical under `de-DE` and `ar` browser locales.
2. **T2 VSUP binning.** The worked example → (vBin +1, uBin 1, merged +1, light hatch). The prior-only block → uBin 3, merged 0. P50 = cutoff → bin 0. Ratio exactly 2 / 4 / 8 → uBin 0 / 1 / 2. Monotonicity: for a fixed ratio, increasing P50 never decreases mergedBin. For every block, mergedBin > 0 implies `BlockEstimate.minable` and mergedBin < 0 implies not minable (both test P50 against the same cutoff).
3. **T3 Collation.** A repeated level signal updates the message (count 2), no new ID. A level message resolved and re-raised within 4 weeks reopens with the same ID; after 5 weeks it gets a new ID.
