A level warning → critical rise is a stop candidate; critical → warning is not. Two edge `machine.failure` signals on the same machine in consecutive weeks create two messages and two stop candidates. ID assignment is identical regardless of signal emission order. Retention drops closed messages > 104 weeks old and never drops open ones.
4. **T4 Obligation ladder and grouping.** Due Wk 35, `prepLeadWeeks` 0, critical consequence, auto-pay off → info Wk 27, warning Wk 31, critical Wk 34; paid in Wk 32 → resolved. `prepLeadWeeks` 2 shifts each step 2 weeks earlier. A `lateFee` consequence (severity warning) never exceeds warning. Twelve such fees due Wk 35 produce one message (`count` 12, total $2,400) and exactly two stop candidates (Wk 31, Wk 34); paying 9 leaves one open message with `count` 3 and no new stop; two categories due the same week stay two messages. For a payment with `autoPay` on, a billable lease advance royalty, or a routine form while a permitting specialist is employed, the severity never exceeds info and `deadlineWithin` never fires; a late-fee filing with no specialist keeps its warning.
5. **T5 Stop rules.** Each rule kind fires on a crafted week and not otherwise. `goldMove` uses the anchor, not last week. `deadlineWithin` fires once per item, once per (category, due week) group for obligations, and never for an obligation where `needsAction` is false. `monthStart` fires in exactly weeks 1, 6, 10, 14, 19, 23, 27, 32, 36, 40, 45, 49. `listingMatch` evaluates the filters carried by the rule with no UI state. A muted warning kind does not stop, but its escalation to critical does. `maxWeeks` stops at exactly N. A blocking decision stops even with all rules off. With `everyCleanup` on, a claim whose L1 and L2 both clean up in one week gives one stop reason naming both lines. From P4, `deadlineWithin` fires for a reorganization plan due date and never for a plan installment; a converted case stops with `gameOver` labelled from the liquidation path.
6. **T6 Worker equivalence.** For 20 seeds × 52 weeks with scripted actions, the worker loop (with yields, explanations on) and `runToNextDecision` (explanations off) produce identical final state hashes and stop reasons.
7. **T7 Cancel.** Cancelling after k weeks yields a state hash equal to k sequential `advanceWeek` calls.
8. **T8 Scrambled-truth UI.** Render every screen (jsdom + Testing Library) for an active-run state S and for S' with all hidden fields scrambled (the §2 scrambler used for bots). The DOM text and attribute values must be identical (dev reveal off). Then open every explain popover and drawer and the Tuning viewer on both and compare.
9. **T9 Num coverage.** A Playwright crawler visits every route with a mid-game fixture. Every `[data-num]` opens a popover with ≥ 1 node, or carries an exemption attribute that matches the allow-list.
10. **T10 Undo.** Undo restores a deep-equal previous state and pops the action log. It is refused after a non-`undoable` action (RNG draw, information reveal, counterparty commitment), in Ironman, and after advancing.
11. **T11 Saves.** Export → import round trip gives byte-identical `state` and `ui`. `SAVE_TOO_NEW` is rejected. v(N−1) fixture migrates. Autosave keeps 3 rotating + yearly snapshots. A corrupt file shows the error and changes nothing. Changing a `ui.*` constant leaves `meta.tuningHash` unchanged.
12. **T12 CSV.** RFC 4180 quoting of commas, quotes and newlines in memos. IS export totals equal statement totals to the cent. No thousands separators.
13. **T13 Performance.** Dashboard render ≤ 50 ms on a year-10 fixture. Ledger with 20,000 rows renders ≤ 60 DOM rows and scrolls without dropped frames (Playwright trace). Live explain ≤ `ui.explainLiveBudgetMs`. A main-thread week with explanations on ≤ `ui.advanceBudgetMs`. A 26-week worker run keeps the main thread free of long tasks > 50 ms.
14. **T14 Accessibility.** axe-core reports zero serious or critical violations per screen in both themes. A keyboard-only Playwright script completes: setup → watch and site-visit a listing → lease a claim → buy machines → hire → assign the owner as foreman → mobilize → set plan → advance → cleanup → sell gold.
15. **T15 Season clock and plan math.** §1 `northernInterior` with operating start wk 20 and a climatology freeze-up forecast 40/42/44 at wk 25 → `wk 6 of ~22`, 16 weeks left (14–18); after the freeze-up reveal the label uses `operatingEndWeek`. Production-vs-plan status thresholds at −9.9%, −10.1% and −25.1%; the 13.3 example gives −9.1% and `on track`.
16. **T16 Reconciliation.** A `CleanupResult` fixture from §7 7.10 (rawOzWeighed 52.901, foremanEstimateOz 46.900, bcyWashedSince 6,377, no pile feed, an estimate in-situ grade of 0.0105) gives reconFactor 1.128 (`+12.8%`), recovered grade 0.00830 raw oz/bcy and implied in-situ grade 0.0118 (= 0.0105 × 1.128). The season factor is Σ weighed ÷ Σ foreman estimates. Every figure is computed from `CleanupResult` fields only (no current-estimate lookup).
17. **T17 Pre-advance sheet.** Shown iff a default applies this week or week-1 net outflows exceed cash plus standing-order gold plus (with auto-draw) revolver availability; `firstShort` names the first unfunded category in the current payment priority order. In a cleanup week whose P10 cleanup inflow covers payroll, the sheet stays closed with a sell-at-cleanup order and opens without one; with `keepCashAbove`, gold already on hand also counts at the local-buyer net.
18. **T18 Explain invariance.** For 20 seeds × 52 weeks, `advanceWeek` with `explain: true` and `false` gives identical state hashes; only `WeekReport` calc fields differ.
19. **T19 End-of-run gating.** `#/end` renders true block grades only when `runStatus ≠ 'active'`; on an active fixture the route redirects and no truth reaches the DOM. An ended save opens read-only.
20. **T20 Tokens** (both themes, computed from `theme/tokens.css`). Every text token ≥ 4.5:1 against all three surfaces of its theme (`chrome-ink` and `chrome-ink-2` against `chrome`); `accent`, `border-control`, `brass`, `brass-on-chrome` and the Lamplight status fills ≥ 3:1 where they are used; `status-*-on` on its fill ≥ 4.5:1; `on-accent` on `accent` ≥ 4.5:1; every text token on a grained band ≥ its floor against the worst grain pixel at `ui.theme.grainOpacity*`. The categorical palette passes the data-viz checks in both themes (OKLCH band and chroma, adjacent protan/deutan ΔE ≥ 8, adjacent normal-vision ΔE ≥ 15, slots 1–3 all-pairs at the same floors) and its sub-3:1 slots match the list in 13.20; `seq-gold` and `seq-slate` are monotone in OKLCH L with hue spread ≤ 40°; the tests reproduce 13.20's figures to 0.1.
21. **T21 Alert kinds.** Every `AlertKind` emitted by any section's fixture (§1, §3–§12, §14) has a template, a severity rule and an owner in the taxonomy table (data validation); the threshold keys it names exist in the owner's tuning file (`fleet.pmOverdueWarnPct`, `finance.distress.watchWeeks`, …) and no `game.alerts.*` key duplicates one.
22. **T22 Inbox pruning.** Saving prunes `UiPersisted.inbox` to message IDs still present in state.
23. **T23 Season secrecy.** Scrambling the unrevealed `DistrictYearSeason` fields (true dates, `z`) leaves every season chip, season clock and calendar DOM identical.
24. **T24 Owner names.** Every engine action type that a §13 screen, the command palette or a tutorial step dispatches is registered in its owning section's handler table, and every state path a tutorial predicate reads exists in the `GameState` schema (`world.watch.claimIds`, not a §13-invented path); the watch star dispatches `world/setWatch` and shows `WATCH_LIMIT` on a 41st claim.
25. **T25 P1 runway.** A P1 fixture with cash $117,200, about $46,300 a week of outflows and a planned cleanup in forecast week 2 worth about $127k at the local-buyer net: the cash tile and 13-week report include the cleanup, carry the label `incl. planned cleanups (P50)`, and no `cash.projectedNegative` fires, although the outflows-only series of the same fixture goes below $0 in week 3 (the false alarm D-13.48 removes). Matches §11's P1 forecast test.
26. **T26 Save size.** On the year-10 fixture (two-claim operation, §11's fixture), the inbox slice serializes to ≤ 0.3 MB and `SaveFile.ui` to ≤ 0.25 MB; a `WeekReport` larger than `ui.persistReportMaxKb` is not persisted, and after a reload `ui/openExplain` on it falls back to the history value and ledger postings. Part of §2.13's per-slice test.
27. **T27 Tutorial paths.** A scripted P1 arid run completes steps 1–14 using only the owners' actions (`world/setWatch`, `world/siteVisit` or `prospect/panSurvey`, `land/acceptAsk`, …). Step 8 completes with a dry-washer fleet and no pump when the owner is assigned foreman or operator on the claim; with the owner in the office and no hired foreman it completes with three hands on the claim (a small crew, with the coach's ×0.92 / ×1.15 note) and does not complete with four. The P2 authority path completes step 5 only after a records check result is read.
28. **T28 Theme rules.** For every screen in both themes: no element using the display family contains a `[data-num]`, a table, a form control, a chip, a button or a tooltip, and none renders below `ui.theme.displayMinPx`; every `[data-num]` computes `font-variant-numeric` with `tabular-nums`; no element with a grain background contains a `[data-num]`, a table, a chart, the map, the block grid, a form control or the top bar's status cluster; grain is absent under `forced-colors: active`, `prefers-contrast: more`, print and `headerGrain: false`; `data-theme` and `color-scheme` follow `Prefs.theme` and `system` follows the media query; the bundled fonts total ≤ `ui.fonts.maxKb` and the app makes no network font request; swapping the fallback faces for the real ones changes no table row height.
29. **T29 Plant lines UI** (P3 fixture: a 40-acre claim with two `tr75` lines, §7 7.2.1's worked example). The editor shows L1 and L2 tabs and an enabled `+ Add line`; on a 20-acre claim with two lines the button is disabled with `LINE_LIMIT`; under `--rules p2` only L1 shows. Cuts render with line outlines and `L2·3` labels and no series color; a block of L1's cut refused for L2 shows `BLOCK_OCCUPIED`. The board has a Shared lane and one lane per line; moving a truck with `Alt+2` puts it in L2's `machineIds`. The Flow line selector shows `LineWeekResult` data; `stageRows(r)` on a one-line result equals `stageRows(r, 'L1')` on every non-shared row. Two cleanups in a week give two cleanup-log rows. `LINE_NEEDS_PLANT_OPERATOR` shows inline and disables `Apply plan`.
30. **T30 Supervision and shop modes.** From §8 8.12's fixtures: three hands, one line, one shift → chip `Small crew · 3 of 3 hands`, explain values 0.92 and 1.15 from tuning; the hire modal for a fourth hand shows `SMALL_CREW_ENDS`; a three-line claim with one hired foreman → `Foreman · <name> +1 line lead hand` and L3's line reads `Line lead hand (standing)`. From §9 9.8.6's three-highway-claim fixture with a pool of two skill-50 mechanics: the pool board's header shows 55.3 std h of demand against 96, travel 1.5 h per job; a fly-in claim in the district reads `fly-in: not served`; the assignee picker shows a pool mechanic disabled with `ASSIGNEE_OUT_OF_REACH` for a machine on that claim; `shop.backlogHigh` messages for a site shop and a pool are separate.
31. **T31 Reorganization flow** (P4, §11 11.16.7's company). The eligibility card reads `Debts $666,000 of $3,424,000` with every condition passing; at stage 1 the filing buttons show `STAGE_TOO_LOW`. After `finance/fileReorganization` the top-bar chip and the case timeline show the plan due 13 weeks out; stayed bills show `CLAIM_STAYED`. The plan builder at 260 weeks, level, 5% reserve shows PDI0 $154,830, margin 12.4%, unsecured 41.3% against 37.4% and vote `possible`; at 156 weeks `File plan` is disabled with `PLAN_NOT_FEASIBLE` and the year-1 shortfall. The vote odds appear only as the bucket. `reorg.planDue` is a warning at `planDueTurn − 4` and critical at `planDueTurn − 1`, each stopping a run once. After confirmation a missed installment raises `reorg.paymentMissed` (`1 of 2 missed`); a second miss converts the case, the run stops with `gameOver`, and `#/end` shows the reorganization block and `Liquidated: converted from reorganization`. Owner salary above the living allowance shows `REORG_DRAW_LIMIT`. In a scenario fixture the Scenario tab shows the silver cap.
32. **T32 Agencies and disclaimer.** Every agency name or abbreviation in the rendered DOM of the Permits screens, inbox messages, Help and the wizard comes from §6 `agencyFor` (a data scan finds none hard-coded in `ui/` or `data/text/`, and none of the retired fictional names); the northern fixture shows BLM, DEC, DNR, USACE and MSHA and the arid fixture BLM, NDEP, NDWR, USACE and MSHA; the disclaimer text `permits.disclaimer` appears at the foot of every Permits tab, at the top of the Help glossary and on the wizard's World step; no agency message renders a logo, seal or display-face masthead.

**Phase exit gates** (§1 1.19 owns the checklist). Every phase: all tests that apply to the screens shipped so far, and BALANCE O-13 (25–60 run stops a year, ≤ 10 in the off-season, cautious bot with §13's default stop rules). **P0:** T1, T11, T18, T20 and T28 on the shell, in both themes. **P1:** T2–T10, T12–T17 and T19–T28 (T27's P1 path; T26 on a year-10 run of the P1 rules), T30's small-crew part, with T14's keyboard path on the P1 arid start. **P2:** T4 and T5 with §6's obligations, grouping and the self-settling cap; custom stop rules and muting in T5; T8 over the Permits screens; T27's authority path; T32. **P3:** T8 and T9 over Fleet, Shop and Parts (known ranges only), and an equipment auction bid in T14's script; T29 and T30's line-span and pool parts; T5's two-line cleanup. **P4:** T12 for the balance sheet and cash-flow exports; T26 on the year-10 fixture with full finance; T31, and T5's reorganization deadlines and conversion stop; T8 over the Reorganization tab. **P5:** T5's `goldMove`; T8 with News (no regime, fair value or `truthful` flag in the DOM). **P6:** T8 and T9 over the Mine & Mill screen when hard rock is enabled; T19 for a forfeited scenario; T31's scenario silver cap; T32 with the Alaska state land and Yukon fixtures.

### 13.28 Decisions

- **D-13.1** — Hash-based router with a canonical route for every entity. — Deep links from explain trees, inbox and the command palette, and browser back/forward, with no server.
- **D-13.2** — `applyAction`, `validateAction`, `explain` and single `advanceWeek` run synchronously on the main thread; multi-week runs go to a module Web Worker that loops `advanceWeek` + `evaluateStops`, yielding between weeks; cancel keeps the last completed week. — Single calls fit the budget. Runs of up to 52 weeks would freeze the UI, and the loop keeps exact equivalence with `runToNextDecision`. SharedArrayBuffer was rejected because it needs cross-origin isolation headers on static hosting.
- **D-13.3** — Inbox read flags, stop rules, saved searches, baselines, table layouts, tutorial progress and the recent calc report live in `SaveFile.ui`, outside `GameState`. — Presentation state must not alter replays or golden hashes.
- **D-13.4** — Warnings stop runs by default but can be muted per kind; critical and blocking cannot. — Keeps §2.7's rule, prevents alert fatigue, and protects against catastrophic surprises.
- **D-13.5** — Signals are level- or edge-triggered; level messages auto-resolve when their condition clears. — Avoids stale "cash negative" messages without per-kind resolve code.
- **D-13.6** — Stage bars are the primary bottleneck view; a Sankey is secondary and covers material (bcy) only. — Stage bars show the binding constraint and idle reasons directly. A gold Sankey would imply knowledge of contained and lost gold.
- **D-13.7** — Contained gold, losses by size and pre-cleanup recovered gold are never displayed; the UI shows estimated contained gold, estimated recovery, the foreman's box estimate, weighed gold and a reconciliation factor. — Real operators only know what the scale says. Reconciliation is how they learn their estimate was wrong.
- **D-13.8** — The block heat map uses a diverging VSUP palette relative to §4's per-block cutoff grade (the player's planning assumptions); §5's breakeven grade, which adds royalty burden and a capital charge, is shown on the Valuation tab. — Cutoff is the mining decision and matches §4's minable outline; breakeven is the buying decision. Uncertainty collapsing to gray stops unsampled blocks from looking rich.
- **D-13.9** — Calc nodes from hidden fields are tagged and redacted (replaced by `knownAlt` or "Not observable"). — "Every number clickable" must not become a truth oracle.
- **D-13.10** — Full calc trees are retained for 4 weeks in memory and 1 week in the save; older numbers explain via history values and ledger postings. — Bounds save size (§2.13's per-slice budget; see D-13.54) while keeping recent weeks fully drillable.
- **D-13.11** — Undo applies within the current week only, only to actions the engine marks `undoable` (no RNG draw, no information revealed, no counterparty commitment), and never in Ironman. — Cheap misclick recovery without enabling re-rolls or peeks.
- **D-13.12** — Locale fixed to `en-US`; all strings go through a `t()` catalog. — USD conventions regardless of browser locale; localization stays possible later at low cost.
- **D-13.13** — Statements use whole dollars, the ledger uses exact cents, and everything else hides cents at or above $1,000. — Standard financial-report practice; the ledger is the record of account.
- **D-13.14** — Grade conversion is 1 g/m³ = 0.024581 oz/yd³, refining §2.4's ≈ 0.0243. — Unit arithmetic (1 g = 0.0321507 ozt; 1 m³ = 1.30795 yd³) matches R2's 0.0246. Flag to §2 for propagation.
- **D-13.15** — Ounces shown to 3 dp below 100 oz and 2 dp at or above. — Matches 0.001 oz cleanup weighing for small lots without false precision on large totals.
- **D-13.16** — Interest rates and APRs shown to 2 dp, an exception to the 1 dp percentage rule. — Rates are quoted in quarter points (8.75%); 1 dp would misstate them.
- **D-13.17** — The calendar is an agenda plus a 52-week year planner, with no daily month grid. — Game time resolves weekly; a day grid would imply precision that doesn't exist.
- **D-13.18** — Reporting months are §1's `monthEndWeeks` spans (each week belongs to the month containing its first day); quarters are 13-week blocks. — One definition shared with §11 (D-11.28); deterministic.
- **D-13.19** — TanStack Table + Virtual for tables; Recharts for standard charts; custom SVG for the block grid, map, season strip, meters and stage bars. — Headless table logic fits Tailwind; Recharts can't annotate the custom views well.
- **D-13.20** — The dashboard has a fixed layout with collapsible panels and no drag-customization. — Low value for the cost; consistent layout helps learning and testing.
- **D-13.21** — The pre-advance sheet appears only when a default applies this week or a payment shortfall is projected, and names the first creditor category that would go short. — Keeps the two-click off-season cadence while catching costly surprises in §11's own terms.
- **D-13.22** — Toasts only for critical and blocking messages plus action confirmations; critical toasts never auto-dismiss. — Toasts are interruptive; WCAG timing guidance.
- **D-13.23** — The tutorial is a state-predicate coach that never blocks, advances time or acts for the player; default on for the first game; its steps follow §1 1.15. — Teaching through real state, without the tutorial distorting the simulation.
- **D-13.24** — The district map uses ≤ 3 categorical fills (yours / listed / competitor gray) plus patterns and labels. — The map is an all-pairs form; only the first three palette slots validate all-pairs under CVD.
- **D-13.25** — Autosaves: 3 rotating + 5 yearly snapshots + every 8 weeks during runs, written from the worker during runs. — One corrupted write can't lose a game; yearly snapshots allow long rollbacks.
- **D-13.26** — Phasing: Calendar agenda in P1, year planner and map layers in P2, News in P5 (the base map moved to P1, D-13.49). — P1 already has loan payments, bills, lease obligations and cleanups to schedule; the planner and map layers matter once permits and staking exist.
- **D-13.27** — Desktop-first, mouse + keyboard; full layout from 1280 px, graceful to 1024 px; no touch-specific interactions. — Matches the brief. Owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (OQ-13.1; §0 smaller call 7).
- **D-13.28** — Seeds are generated in the UI with `crypto.getRandomValues` as a 26-char base32 string; the engine receives only the string. — The engine stays free of ambient entropy (§2.3).
- **D-13.29** — "Every number clickable" is enforced by an ESLint rule on `<Num>` and a crawler test; axis ticks and counts are exempt. — Makes the brief's requirement verifiable rather than aspirational.
- **D-13.30** — "Plan" in production-vs-plan is a frozen season baseline (automatic after the first operating week; re-baselinable), held in `UiPersisted` and captured by the main thread or the run worker. — A live forecast compared with itself always looks on plan; presentation data stays out of `GameState`.
- **D-13.31** — Status chips are filled with the status color and carry ink labels; bare status text uses separate per-theme `status-*-text` tokens; links use a `link` token; muted ink stays ≥ 4.5:1. — The earlier warning and serious fills (1.7:1, 2.5:1), light accent text (4.2:1) and light muted ink (3.4:1) failed WCAG AA. *Amended by owner ruling 2026-10-05 (themed look):* the values are now 13.20's earth-tone Daylight and Lamplight tokens (Daylight `ink-3` `#665b4e`, 5.6:1 on the page); the rules stand, and chip labels use fixed `status-*-on` tokens in both themes (D-13.61).
- **D-13.32** — `ui.*` keys are application configuration outside `TuningResolved` and `meta.tuningHash`. — A presentation tweak must never fork a save or a golden replay.
- **D-13.33** — Edge-triggered alerts never merge across weeks; level messages follow the current severity, reopen within 4 weeks, and become stop candidates only when severity rises. — A second machine failure must stop a run; a steady condition must not stop every week.
- **D-13.34** — Obligation alert severity counts back from `dueTurn − prepLeadWeeks` and is capped by the obligation's consequence severity. — Matches §6's contract and keeps late-fee items from crying wolf.
- **D-13.35** — Run identity (`runId`, `RunAnchor`) is UI-only; a run's messages are found by created-turn range. — Keeps `GameState` identical between UI runs and simulator runs.
- **D-13.36** — The explain flag never changes `GameState`; explanation-only outputs live in `WeekReport`. — Required for worker/simulator equivalence and golden hashes.
- **D-13.37** — RNG percentiles are shown only for draws flagged `publicParams`; gold price moves use §10's decomposition. — An observed value plus a percentile reveals hidden means and variances (GARCH state, true grade, true health).
- **D-13.38** — Season widgets read a `seasonView` that exposes only revealed dates and forecasts. — The true breakup and freeze-up weeks are fixed at week 1 and are hidden truth (§1 1.4.4).
- **D-13.39** — Calendar agenda in P1 (bills, loan payments, lease obligations, payroll, cleanups, season dates). — The P1 core loop already has deadlines; a dashboard list alone hides them past 4 weeks.
- **D-13.40** — Permit pipeline kanban cards are not draggable; actions are buttons. — Stage changes belong to the regulator; a draggable card would suggest control the player does not have.
- **D-13.41** — The end-of-run reveal is the only screen that renders hidden truth, and only when `runStatus ≠ 'active'`; the save then becomes read-only. — §1 1.14 allows the reveal because the run is over; read-only prevents using it to replay.
- **D-13.42** — The wizard follows §1 1.6's order and builds `NewGameSetup` exactly; Easy and Hard appear in the UI from P6. — One source of truth for setup; §1 1.19 phases the presets.
- **D-13.43** — Heat-map uncertainty bins use the block P90/P10 ratio at 2 / 4 / 8. — Same measure and first two thresholds as §4's hatching, so heat map, texture and §4's description agree.
- **D-13.44** — Grade reconciliation uses §7's frozen `foremanEstimateOz`. — §4 updates the estimate with each cleanup, so comparing with the current estimate would drift toward 1.
- **D-13.45** — Watching a listing or a district uses §3's engine action `world/setWatch { claimId | districtId, on }`, which writes `world.watch` and refuses a 41st claim with `WATCH_LIMIT` (§4 `geology.maxTrackedClaims` 40); season chips and the tutorial read `world.watch`, never a UI list. Site visits are §3's `world/siteVisit` and pans §4's `prospect/panSurvey`. — One record drives §4's weekly re-estimation, §3's listing and price-change notices and the UI; separate `prospect/watch` and `prospect/siteVisit` actions do not exist.
- **D-13.46** — Obligation alerts collate into one message per (kind, category, due week), with a count, a total and `Pay all` / `File all`; obligations that settle themselves (billable payments under §6 `settlementClass`, auto-paid payments, auto-filed forms) are capped at info and never fire the deadline stop; any form that still needs filing keeps its full ladder. — A 12-claim company would otherwise get a dozen rows and stops around Sept 1 and Dec 30, and every monthly loan payment would stop a run; BALANCE O-13 allows 25–60 stops a year. A failed auto-pay still raises §6's critical alert.
- **D-13.47** — The cash-warning window is §11's `finance.distress.watchWeeks` (6 / 4 / 3 in §1 1.11, plus §8's alert bonus); §13 deletes `game.alerts.cashNegWarnWeeks`, and likewise reads §9's `fleet.pmOverdueWarnPct` and `fleet.shopBacklogWarnWeeks` instead of keeping copies. — Distress stage 0 and `cash.projectedNegative` must be one rule; the section that owns a condition owns its threshold.
- **D-13.48** — From P1 the cash tile, runway, 13-week report and `cash.projectedNegative` use §11's forecast with the P50 production line (planned cleanups at the local-buyer net), labelled `incl. planned cleanups (P50)`; the pre-advance sheet counts gold only when a standing sale order will sell it in step 12, at the P10 figure. — An outflows-only runway cried wolf every producing week for three phases; the sheet must not count gold that nothing will sell before payroll.
- **D-13.49** — The district map's base form (claims, creeks, town, routes, ownership fills) ships in P1, drawn only from §3 `districtMap`; water, estimate and permit layers come in P2, risk, activity and Companies in P5. — The P1 choice between the northern and the arid district turns on access and distance; one geometry function keeps the UI off §3's internal fields.
- **D-13.50** — Equipment auctions (lot list, sealed maximum bid via §9 `fleet/bid`, `auction.won` / `auction.lost`) ship in P3 with background bidders; §12 competitor bids on iron and all claim auctions ship in P5. — §9 and the brief put auction markets in P3, and an engine feature with no UI cannot be played or tested. §9's kinds are used for iron; §5's `auction.result` stays for land.
- **D-13.51** — P1–P2 fleet screens show §9's visible grade A–D and the flat maintenance $/SMR h; component bars, the PM schedule and failure-risk chips arrive with components in P3. — P1 machines have no components, so an "exact health" bar would display data that does not exist.
- **D-13.52** — The Estimate tab and the listing card lead with §4's verdict line; in the player's first season the full estimate panels start collapsed. — One sentence answers the first-hour buying question; the depth stays one click away and is never removed.
- **D-13.53** — Grade reconciliation's implied grade uses §4's in-situ basis and §7's `modeledChainFactor`: (weighed − pile estimate) ÷ chain ÷ in-situ bcy. — §7's foreman estimate now runs through mining, capture, gold-room and dirt factors; dividing by recovery alone would mix bases and disagree with §4's `recordProduction`.
- **D-13.54** — The inbox slice (≤ 0.3 MB) and `SaveFile.ui` (≤ 0.25 MB) carry their own year-10 budgets inside §2.13's per-slice save budget, and the persisted calc week is skipped when it serializes above 200 kB (`ui.persistReportMaxKb`). — A single 2 MB cap could not hold every slice, so §13's parts are bounded on their own.
- **D-13.55** — The plan editor has no foreman or permit-limit fields: it shows §8 `foremanFor` and §6's compliance mode as read-only lines with links to their owners, and starts every plan from §7 `defaultMinePlan`. — The owners decide these; a second control would contradict `FOREMAN_REQUIRED` and `complianceMode`, and UI-held defaults drift (a 2 ft bedrock take in the UI against §7's 1.5 ft). *Extended by owner ruling 2026-10-05:* the read-only supervision line is shown per plant line and covers the small crew's no-foreman case (D-13.62, D-13.63).
- **D-13.56** — The interface keeps its business-software structure, density and accessibility and wears a frontier mining theme (owner ruling 2026-10-05): an earth-tone palette, two themes named **Daylight** and **Lamplight** (`Prefs.theme: 'system' | 'daylight' | 'lamplight'`, default `system`, which follows the OS), grain on chrome and title bands, a period slab display face for titles and headers, and a legible sans with tabular figures for data. Lamplight is its own selected set of steps, never an inversion. The theme dresses chrome and titles only; tables, charts, the map, forms and numbers stay on flat surfaces. — The owner asked for a rugged look on business software. Confining it to the frame keeps every reading rule of 13.2, and the theme names fit a mining camp while saying plainly which is light and which is dark.
- **D-13.57** — The categorical palette is eight earth hues in a fixed order, slate, ochre, spruce, plum, glacier, rust, indigo, fireweed, with a step per theme (13.20). Worst adjacent protan/deutan ΔE is 11.4 Daylight and 11.3 Lamplight (target ≥ 8), worst adjacent normal-vision ΔE 24.4 and 16.9 (floor 15), and slots 1–3 pass all-pairs (12.3 / 11.3 CVD, 16.4 / 16.2 normal); `accent` equals `series-1`; the map uses slots 1 and 2 plus neutral gray (D-13.24). Slots below 3:1 (Daylight ochre and glacier, Lamplight plum) rely on direct labels or the table twin. — The order is the color-vision safety mechanism, so it was chosen by enumerating orders and tuning steps until every gate passed in both themes. Slate leads because "yours" is also the interactive color, and slate against ochre stays far apart under every simulation (protan/deutan ΔE 27.3 Daylight, 22.7 Lamplight); ochre second puts the theme's gold in the most-used slot.
- **D-13.58** — Sequential layers use `seq-gold` for gold quantities (grade P50, contained and minable ounces) and `seq-slate` for every other magnitude, including the uncertainty ratio (was orange); the cutoff heat map is diverging slate (below cutoff) to gold (above), with a neutral parchment or umber midpoint toward which VSUP pulls uncertain blocks (was red to blue). — "Gold means it pays" reads at a glance; the blue–yellow axis survives protanopia and deuteranopia; red stays reserved for status, so a sub-cutoff block no longer looks like an alarm.
- **D-13.59** — Display face: Besley (SIL OFL 1.1; a revival of the 1845 Clarendon) for screen titles, section and panel headers, wizard steps, the company name and the end-of-run headline, never below 16 px and never on numbers, tables, controls, chips, buttons, tooltips or body text. Data and UI face: Inter (SIL OFL 1.1) for everything else, with tabular lining figures on every number, KPI values included (reversing the proportional-figure rule for KPI tiles), and a slashed zero on IDs and seeds. Both ship as self-hosted WOFF2 Latin subsets within 260 kB with metric-matched local fallbacks; the game fetches no font at run time. — Clarendon is the type of the period, and a slab reads as frontier without hurting a header; a slab on numbers or small text would. Tabular figures keep weekly-changing tiles from jittering. Open licenses permit bundling; local-only hosting (owner ruling 2026-10-05) and offline play rule out a font service; metric matching keeps table geometry stable during a load.
- **D-13.60** — Grain is the only surface texture: a generated noise tile at most 5% (Daylight) or 7% (Lamplight) alpha, on chrome, title bands, the wizard header, the title screen, the end-of-run headline and empty states, never in or behind anything that holds a number, table, chart, map, block grid, form control, chip, toast, popover, drawer or the inbox list, and off under high contrast, forced colors, print and the `headerGrain` setting. Ornament is limited to brass rules, the active-nav marker, the wordmark and line icons, with no photographs, faux materials or distressed type. "Texture" keeps its accessibility meaning (13.2's line fills); the decoration is called grain. — The owner asked for subtle textured headers never behind data; a bounded alpha keeps text on grain AA-compliant at the worst pixel, which T20 checks, and separate names stop a decorative setting from switching off an accessibility aid.
- **D-13.61** — Status chips use fixed `status-*-on` label tokens in both themes (lamp-black on good, warning and serious; white on critical); the focus ring on chrome uses `brass-on-chrome`; inputs carry a `border-control` token ≥ 3:1; hairlines and axis baselines are decorative and exempt from 3:1. — The old "ink-1 label" rule would set parchment text on an amber fill in a dark theme (about 1.8:1); slate accent on slate chrome would hide the focus ring; WCAG 1.4.11 needs 3:1 for component boundaries but not for gridlines whose values are read elsewhere.
- **D-13.62** — Plant lines in the UI (owner ruling 2026-10-05; §7 owns them): the plan editor has a claim-wide strip and one tab per line for the per-line fields; the assignments board has a Shared lane and one lane per line; lines are told apart by label and outline style, never by series color; Flow, Production and Cleanups take a line selector (`stageRows(r, lineId?)`; the claim view uses §7's claim-view bottleneck); the `everyCleanup` stop fires once per claim and week; `crew.noForeman` is one message per claim naming its lines, while `ops.plantIdleHigh` and `ops.cleanupDone` are per line. — The claim owns its series color across every chart, so a line needs another cue; per-line idle and cleanup notices keep a second line's problems visible, but one cause (no foreman) should stop a run once, not three times.
- **D-13.63** — Every claim summary carries one supervision chip from §8 `foremanFor` (hired, owner, lead hand, small crew, none), each with its own icon and text; a small crew shows its headcount against `staff.smallCrewMaxNoForeman` and explains its ×0.92 efficiency and ×1.15 injury cost; the hire, assign and recall modals show §8's `SMALL_CREW_ENDS` warning before a fourth hand ends the exemption. — The ruling made the foreman optional on tiny crews at a price; the player should see the price and the threshold where the choice is made, not discover a stand-down a week later.
- **D-13.64** — The Shop tab has one board per shop, a site board per claim with site mechanics and a pool board per district with pool mechanics; pool cards and headers show travel hours and response delay, a reach table shows which claims the pool serves this week, the assignee picker hides nothing but disables out-of-reach mechanics with their reason, and `shop.backlogHigh` is raised per shop. — §9 plans site shops and pools separately, so one board per shop matches the engine; the pool's costs (travel, delay, no fly-in reach) are the trade-off the ruling set, and they must be visible where the player chooses between modes.
- **D-13.65** — Bankruptcy, in both forms, lives on Bank & loans > Reorganization (P4): filing with the eligibility card and the guarantor choice, the case (timeline, claims, stayed items, adequate protection, DIP, court sales), a plan builder bound live to §11 `reorgPlanPreview` with both tests and the vote bucket, the plan period and history. The health ladder draws stage 7 as a fork of Reorganization and Liquidation; a top-bar chip shows an open case; the Company & owner run controls route to the tab; vote odds appear only as a bucket. — One place for the most consequential decision in the game, with every number §11 uses to judge the plan; showing feasibility, best interest and the vote inputs before filing lets the player build a plan that survives instead of guessing; a bucket matches how §11 shows lender quotes and hides the draw.
- **D-13.66** — Reorganization alerts: `reorg.planDue` (warning 4 weeks before the plan deadline, critical in the last week; the same for an amendment deadline), `reorg.hearingSoon` (the week before the hearing; a warning when the filed plan would fail its tests on today's numbers), `reorg.ruling` (warning on confirmation, critical on denial), `reorg.paymentShort` (warning 2 weeks ahead, critical when the miss would convert), `reorg.paymentMissed` and `reorg.adequateProtectionUnpaid` (critical), and info kinds for court-sale notices, true-ups and completion. §13 owns the windows (`game.alerts.reorg*`); plan installments and adequate-protection bills never fire the deadline stop, being billable payments §11 settles; a conversion stops a run as `gameOver`. — §2.7 left the levels to §13; each level matches what is at stake (a missed deadline converts the case and ends the run), and treating installments like other billables keeps runs from stopping every month end of a five-year plan.
- **D-13.67** — Real agency names (owner ruling 2026-10-05): every agency name or abbreviation on screen comes from §6 `agencyFor`; agency messages are plain game text with no seals, logos, letterhead, officials' names, form numbers or display-face mastheads; §6's disclaimer ("Rules in this game are simplified game mechanics, not legal or regulatory advice.") sits at the foot of every Permits tab, at the top of the Help glossary and on the wizard's World step; district cards and map titles name the real jurisdiction and call the district fictional. — Real names let players carry what they learn to the real thing; plain text and the disclaimer keep the simplified rules from reading as advice or as real notices, and one lookup keeps names consistent across regimes.
- **D-13.68** — The target player is the business-sim enthusiast (owner ruling 2026-10-05): dense default screens and an optional guided first season stay as designed (D-13.20, D-13.23, D-13.52 unchanged). The game is hosted locally for now (owner ruling 2026-10-05): the UI depends on no network service, and fonts, icons and the grain tile ship inside the build. — Both confirm the current design; recording them closes the questions and explains why nothing is fetched at run time.
- **D-13.69** — `defaultStopRules(params?: StopRuleParams)` takes the default rules' two numbers, `{ deadlineNoticeWeeks, goldMoveStopPct }`, which default to the engine's `STOP_RULE_DEFAULTS` (2, 0.05); the UI passes `ui.runDeadlineNoticeWeeks` and `ui.runGoldMoveStopPct`, the simulator uses the defaults, and a UI test keeps the defaults equal to the `ui.*` values. — The engine may not import `ui.*` configuration, which sits outside `TuningResolved` and its hash (§2.10, D-13.32), yet the UI and the simulator must stop on the same rules (T6, BALANCE O-13).
- **D-13.70** — 13.20's figures are rounded to one decimal unless quoted to two, and T20 checks each to within 0.1. The Daylight accent figure is 5.05 (it was quoted 5.0) and the Daylight critical fill 4.30 on the page (it was quoted "≥ 4.3", which 4.299 misses). Grain has two tiles per theme, `ink-1` speckle on content bands and `chrome-ink` speckle on chrome (amending D-13.60's "ink-1-colored"), and text on grain is judged against the composite pixel rounded to 8 bits per channel. — Those two figures were the only ones that did not round to their computed values. The chrome tile and the 8-bit rounding are what reproduce 13.20's grain figures (5.0, 9.1, 5.7, 14.3), and a screen shows 8-bit pixels, so the rounded composite is the real worst case.
- **D-13.71** — Fonts ship as @fontsource's static files, one per weight and subset: Besley 600 and 700 and Inter 400 and 600 in Latin and Latin Extended, Inter 500 and the 400 italic in Latin only; ten files, 226,660 bytes, within `ui.fonts.maxKb` read as 260,000 bytes. This replaces 13.20's earlier plan of three variable files; D-13.59's 260 kB budget stands. — The installed packages ship no variable files; dropping the two rarely needed Latin Extended files keeps the budget with room to spare, and `unicode-range` means no page downloads an extended file it does not use.

### 13.29 Open questions

- **OQ-13.1** — Is a tablet/touch target (≥ 1024 px landscape) required in any phase? *Resolved. Owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed* (D-13.27): desktop mouse + keyboard only, no touch target in any phase.

No open questions remain in this section.

### 13.30 Sources

- R2 fact sheet (2026-10-04): northern sluicing windows of ~18-22 weeks (Klondike), Alaska placer seasons of 13-21 weeks, breakup/freeze-up variability → season clock ranges (computed with §1's `northernInterior` template). Crude (raw) vs fine ounces, with ~20% impurities in crude gold and "mixing crude and fine overstates revenue by ~25%" → the always-label-raw-or-fine rule. Unit conversion 1 g/m³ = 0.0246 oz/yd³ → D-13.14.
- Shared calibration anchors (guide §4): labor rates, payroll burden 1.22 (§11's P1 0.14 + 0.08), camp $55/person-day, diesel rack $3.60 + seasonal-road adder $0.90, and the reference small northern operation → worked explain, run summary and reconciliation examples, taken from §7 7.8–7.11.
- W3C, *Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2* (2023): contrast 4.5:1 / 3:1 (1.4.3, 1.4.11), keyboard operability, timing, focus appearance; contrast ratios in 13.20 computed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula.
- Correll, Moritz & Heer, "Value-Suppressing Uncertainty Palettes," *CHI 2018*: VSUP heat-map encoding.
- Bank of England *Inflation Report* fan charts (since 1996): P10–P90 band presentation for the estimate and cash forecasts.
- Tufte, *Beautiful Evidence* (2006): sparklines for KPI tiles.
- The data-viz palette method and validator (lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent protan/deutan ΔE ≥ 8, normal-vision ΔE ≥ 15, contrast relief; status reserved and distinct from series): the 13.20 tokens were derived and validated with it, with the earth-tone hues substituted for the reference instance.
- Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes, "A Physiologically-based Model for Simulation of Color Vision Deficiency," *IEEE TVCG* 15(6), 2009: the protan and deutan simulation behind the 13.20 figures. B. Ottosson, "A perceptual color space for image processing" (OKLab, 2020): the ΔE and lightness space.
- Besley (Owen Earl, indestructible type*; SIL Open Font License 1.1), a revival of Robert Besley's Clarendon, registered in 1845; Inter (Rasmus Andersson; SIL Open Font License 1.1), with tabular figures and slashed zero: the two faces of 13.20. Both are distributed through Google Fonts and may be bundled.
- W3C, *Media Queries Level 5*: `prefers-color-scheme`, `prefers-contrast`, `forced-colors`; CSS Fonts Level 5: `size-adjust` and `ascent-override` for metric-matched fallbacks.
- MDN Web Docs (2025): Web Workers and structured clone, IndexedDB from workers, `Intl.NumberFormat` `roundingMode`; TanStack Table/Virtual and Recharts documentation (2025).

---

## 14. Hard-Rock Track (Phase 6, optional)

> **At a glance.** A placer company that has found where its creek gold came from can graduate into lode (hard-rock) mining: quartz veins and shear zones in bedrock, mined by blasting and processed by crushing, grinding, gravity and (optionally) cyanide leaching. It is the last item of Phase 6, optional, and built entirely from existing systems: §3 generates the lode truth, §4 estimates it, §5 holds lode claims, §6 permits it, §7's capacity and bottleneck machinery runs the site, §8 and §9 supply people and iron, §10 sells the doré and §11 finances it.
> - **The ladder:** (1) find a lode target, usually by tracing rough, quartz-attached gold up a placer creek; (2) explore it with rock chips, trenches, RC and core drilling and fire assays with QA/QC; (3) prove it with a consultant technical report; (4) mine a small oxide pit with the placer fleet and ship ore to a toll mill; (5) go underground through an adit or decline; (6) build your own mill and tailings facility.
> - **Core trade-offs:** year-round production that escapes placer seasons, against capital ten times larger and permits that take two to five years. A toll mill (no capital, quick, but $100–180 per ton, a weekly allotment and the mill's recovery terms) against your own mill ($3.5–25M and, for CIL, a cyanide permit, but $40–75 per ton and control of recovery). Shrinkage and resue mining (selective, labor-heavy) against longhole (cheap per ton, heavy dilution). Fine grind (recovery) against coarse grind (throughput). Drill-hole grades (cheap, nugget-dominated) against bulk samples and underground development (expensive, decisive).
> - **What stays hidden:** the vein's true width, grade, ore shoots, oxide depth, refractory share, hardness, gravity-recoverable gold and wall-rock grade. The player sees assays, estimates with P10/P50/P90, mill head and tail assays, and poured ounces.

### 14.1 Scope, unlock and readiness

**Ownership.** §14 owns the lode deposit model's shapes and generation rules (stored in §3's world slice), lode-specific sampling and assay parameters (run by §4's programs and estimator), lode claims and millsites as tenure variants (run by §5), the hard-rock site model (development, stoping, open pit, drilling and blasting, explosives stock), toll-mill contracts, the own mill and tailings storage facility (TSF), capital projects, and the hard-rock permit, equipment, staff and finance *content* that the owning sections run with their existing machinery. Nothing here forks a system: where an owner's function needs a new parameter, the need is listed in 14.17.

**Switch.** `game.hardRockEnabled` (§1 setup; default **on** in the P6 sandbox, set per scenario). When off, lode truth is still generated (stream isolation, D-14.2) but no lode target is ever revealed and the Mine & Mill screen stays hidden.

**Readiness.** Visible on the Company screen as a checklist (§13). Each tier unlocks actions (14.15):

```
explore  = knownLodeTarget                                   // a lode system revealed to the player (14.2)
develop  = explore ∧ R ≥ hardrock.unlock.minReputation (45) ∧ S ≥ hardrock.unlock.minStanding (50)
               ∧ planSeasons ≥ hardrock.unlock.minPlanSeasons (1)
ownMill  = develop ∧ ( companyNW / cpiIndex ≥ hardrock.unlock.minNetWorthUsd (1,500,000)
                       ∨ profitableSeasons ≥ hardrock.unlock.minProfitableSeasons (2) )
  R = company.reputation (§1 1.12), S = company.regulatorStanding (§6 6.11), both 0–100
  companyNW = the company part of §1 1.13 netWorth(state, 'scoring') (visible marks only)
  planSeasons = calendar years in which any claim produced under plan-tier authority (§6) for ≥ 8 weeks
  profitableSeasons = fiscal years with §11 net income > 0
```

The real world has no such gates (anyone may file a plan), so they are a design choice, not a model of agency behaviour (D-14.7). §6's own formulas would deny only ≈ 10–15% of lode plans filed at standing 30–40 (deny factor ×1.1–1.2, 6.11), which would make filing below the gate a cheap lottery on a $150–600k application. The gates do three jobs: they make graduation legible on the Company screen, they keep the track late-game (one season of plan-tier production is the operating record an agency, surety and lender look for), and they model the one hard rule that does exist: an operator on §6's non-compliance list is refused new plans. Below the standing gate, `fed.planLode` fails validation with `STANDING_TOO_LOW`. Exploration (`explore`) is never gated beyond knowing a target.

```ts
interface HardRockSlice {                        // §14's own player-side state (truth lives in world.lodes, 14.3)
  revealedSystemIds: LodeSystemId[];             // targets the player knows about (prefix 'lod')
  veinKnowledge: Record<VeinId, { shown: boolean; traceKnown: boolean; coverFtShown: [number, number] }>;   // 14.2
  hints: Record<CreekId, { quartzAttached: number; roughShape: number; lastTurn: number }>;   // 14.2 discovery counters
  labQaqc: Record<LabId, { standards: number; biasShown: [number, number] | null }>;          // 14.4 (labs are data, prefix 'lab')
  sites: Record<SiteId, HardRockSite>; siteIds: SiteId[];            // prefix 'hrs' (14.9)
  mills: Record<MillId, Mill>; millIds: MillId[];                    // prefix 'mil' (14.8.2)
  tollMills: Record<TollMillId, TollMill>;                           // regional custom mills (data + state; prefix 'tml', 14.8.1)
  tollContracts: Record<TollContractId, TollContract>; tollLots: Record<TollLotId, TollLot>;   // prefixes 'tc', 'tl'
  projects: Record<CapProjectId, CapitalProject>; projectIds: CapProjectId[];                   // prefix 'cap' (14.12)
  deliveries: { siteId: SiteId; kind: 'explosives' | 'detonators' | 'reagents'; qty: number; arriveTurn: number }[];
  readiness: { explore: boolean; develop: boolean; ownMill: boolean };                          // recomputed step 16
}
```

### 14.2 Lode ground: lode claims, millsites, discovery

**Lode claims.** Under the 1872 law a lode claim covers a vein in place and is up to **1,500 ft along the vein × 600 ft across = 900,000 ft² = 20.66 acres**, unlike the 20-acre aliquot placer. Holding cost is the same $200 per claim per year (BLM charges per lode claim, not per 20 acres), the same location and processing fees and the same Small Miner's Waiver count (§6 6.2; one lode claim = one claim). There are no association lode claims. A **millsite** (5 acres of non-mineral land for a mill, TSF or camp) costs the same $200 per year and carries no mineral rights. §6's `feeUnits(claim) = ceil(acres / 20)` would bill a 20.66-ac lode claim as 2 units, so §6 must return `feeUnits = 1` for `claimKind` `'lode'` and `'millsite'` (14.17).

| Parcel | Geometry | Grid | Fee (§6) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lode claim | 1,500 × 600 ft, long axis on the vein's strike | 30 × 12 surface cells of 50 ft; the vein-plane panel grid (14.3) is the geology | $200/yr | pre-generated over each vein (below) |
| Millsite | 5 ac, ≈ 467 × 467 ft | — | $200/yr | stakeable on any open non-mineral ground in the district; required for a mill or TSF off the lode claims |
| Yukon quartz claim (later content) | 1,500 × 1,500 ft = 51.65 ac | — | regime rules | data row only; hard rock ships under `usFederal` and `private` (D-14.28) |

**Parcel layout (a §3 extension).** At `newGame`, after placer parcels, §3 lays lode claims over each generated vein (14.3): `ceil(strikeFt / 1,500)` claims end to end along strike, centred on the vein trace; veins of one system within 600 ft share claims. A lode parcel that would overlap a placer parcel is shifted up-slope along the dip direction until clear (the "known lode" conflict of 30 USC 37 is not modeled). Lode parcels get §3 statuses by the same selection rule as placers, with the system's richness and visibility as the quality signal:

```
pHeld = logistic( logit(geology.world.lodeStakedFraction (0.55)) + hardrock.world.selSlope (1.2) × ln(S.richness) / systemSigma
                  + (S.public.outcropVisible ∨ S.public.oldWorkings ≠ 'none' ? hardrock.world.visibleLogit (+1.0) : hardrock.world.blindLogit (−2.0)) )
drawn on rng(seed,'world','lode','status',S.id); all claims of a system share the draw (one holder)
```

Rich, visible systems were staked long ago; blind systems (no outcrop, no workings) are mostly open ground, which is what the placer-hint path finds (D-14.32). Held lode claims list through §3's supply at `hardrock.supply.listHazardMult` (0.5) × the placer hazard. Panels belong to the claim whose strike interval contains them; extralateral (apex) rights are not modeled (D-14.6).

**Discovery (how a target becomes known).** A lode system is `revealed` for the player when any of these happens:

1. **Placer hints.** Every §4 pit, trench, bulk sample or §7 cleanup on a block that lies on the system's creek C, or on C's parent downstream of C's junction, within `4 × hintRangeMi` channel miles of C's head, rolls a `quartzAttached` flag and a `roughShape` flag on `rng(seed,'hr-hint',sourceId)` (sourceId = the sample id, or `cleanup|turn|claimId`):
   ```
   p_hint  = hardrock.discovery.hintBase (0.25) × coarseParticles / (coarseParticles + 3) × exp(−dMi / hardrock.discovery.hintRangeMi (1.5))
   p_rough = min(0.9, hardrock.discovery.roughMult (3) × p_hint)
     coarseParticles = colours of size 'coarse' in the sample (§3 colorsBySize; a cleanup counts as 100)
     dMi = channel miles from the block to C's head (a cleanup: the bcy-weighted mean over the blocks washed since the last cleanup)
   when Σ quartzAttached on C ≥ hardrock.discovery.hintsToReveal (3) and a geologist (owner, staff or consultant, §4 4.13) has
   logged at least one of them: reveal the system; inbox "Rough gold with quartz attached: source likely within ~X mi upstream",
   X = the smallest dMi among C's hint-bearing blocks, rounded up to 0.5 mi
   ```
   `roughShape` never reveals anything; it shows on the creek card ("rough, crystalline gold in 4 samples") so the player can steer sampling up-valley. Coarse gold that travelled less than ~1–2 km stays rough and crystalline (R3), so the hint points up-valley from the richest proximal placer. *Worked example:* a 10-bcy pit 0.5 mi below C's head with 9 coarse colours rolls p_hint = 0.25 × 9/12 × e^(−0.33) = 0.134; a cleanup 1 mi below rolls 0.25 × 100/103 × e^(−0.67) = 0.124. A season of ten cleanups about 1 mi below the head plus a dozen proximal pits expects ≈ 2.4 hints, so it reaches three about 40% of the time; mining farther down-valley rarely does.
2. **Records.** A §4 records review of a creek reveals each lode system at its head **that the old-timers found** (`oldWorkings ≠ 'none'`) with p = `hardrock.discovery.recordsP` (0.50) × district `recordsQuality` (§3), on `rng(seed,'hr-hint','records',creekId,S.id)`: "1898 Mining Record: quartz location, 40-ft adit". The key has no review id, so a second review of the same creek returns the same answer (no re-rolling). Blind systems are not in any record.
3. **Market.** A lode claim listing (§5) reveals its system.
4. **Field.** A §3 site visit to a parcel within 0.5 mi of a vein trace reveals the system with p 0.5 if an outcrop is visible, 0.9 if old workings are present (else 0), on `rng(seed,'hr-hint','site',turn,claimId,S.id)`.

A revealed system shows its outline, the claims over it, visible old workings and the trace of each **outcropping** vein (`traceKnown`). Blind veins of a revealed system (coverFt ≥ `hardrock.lode.outcropMaxCoverFt` 3) appear only when a soil line, trench or drill intercept finds them (14.4). Nothing about grade or width is revealed.

### 14.3 The lode deposit model (vein-plane panels)

**Representation.** A vein is a tabular body. Its geology is stored on a **vein-plane grid of 50 × 50 ft panels** (50 ft along strike × 50 ft down dip), each carrying a true width. A panel is also the game's stope unit: sublevels sit 50 ft apart, and one panel between two sublevels is one stope block. A "3D block model" view for the open pit and the UI is derived from the panels and the vein's attitude (D-14.3). 1 short ton (st) of vein quartz (SG 2.65) occupies 12.09 ft³, so 1 bcy = 2.233 st.

```ts
interface LodeSystem { id: LodeSystemId; districtId: DistrictId; creekId: CreekId; anchorMi: PointMi; strikeDeg: number;
  veinIds: VeinId[]; claimIds: ClaimId[];
  public: { outcropVisible: boolean; oldWorkings: 'none' | 'prospectPits' | 'adit' | 'stampMill' };   // true facts; shown once revealed
  hidden: { richness: number } }
interface Vein { id: VeinId; systemId: LodeSystemId; strikeFt: number; dipDeg: number; downDipFt: number;
  nS: number; nD: number; offsetFt: { across: number; along: number };      // panels along strike / down dip; position in the system
  aditPossible: boolean;                                                     // visible topography: a hillside below the vein
  hidden: { truthPack: string; truthHash: string;                             // packed PanelTruth[], decoded like §3 (D-3.1, D-3.32)
            coverFt: number;                                                  // true soil / muck cover over the trace (player sees a range)
            wallGradeOzSt: number; coarseMeanMg: number; sizeMix: [number, number, number];   // lode classes (below) mass shares
            groundClass: 'good' | 'fair' | 'poor'; oxideDepthFt: number; transitionFrac: number;
            refractoryShare: number; grg: number; alloyFineness: number; pagFactor: number } }
interface PanelTruth {                     // hidden; grade is FINE oz Au per short ton of vein (fire-assay basis), undiluted
  trueWidthFt: number; gradeOzSt: number; domain: 'oxide' | 'transition' | 'sulfide';
  bwi: number;                             // Bond ball-mill work index, kWh/st
  refractoryShare: number;                 // share of the panel's gold locked in sulfide (not gravity-recoverable; leaches poorly)
  grg: number;                             // share of the panel's gold that is gravity-recoverable; always ≤ 1 − refractoryShare
  pinched: boolean }
type LodeDomain = PanelTruth['domain'];
interface PanelState { minedFrac: number; brokenInStopeSt: number; developedSides: number; sterilizedTurn: number | null;
  sampledSt: number }                      // world.lodePanelStates, sparse, keyed `${veinId}|${i}|${j}`
```

**Generation** (`genLodeSystems(D, rng(seed,'world','lode',D.id))`, run after §3's placer generation on its own sub-stream, so placer truth is byte-identical with or without it; it reads `world.genParams` like §3, D-3.2):

```
genLodeSystems(D, r) — only for templates with tpl.lode (14.3 table); alaskaState and yukon have none in P6 (D-14.28)
n = U{tpl.lode.systemsPerDistrict}                              // north [1,3], arid [1,3], temperate [2,4]
pick creek C for each system (without replacement): weight = C.hidden.gradeFactor over gold-bearing creeks of order 2–3;
     barren creeks weight hardrock.world.barrenLodeWeight (0.15); system anchored U(300, 2,500) ft upslope from C's head
S.richness = LN(1, hardrock.world.systemSigma (0.45)) × (D.hidden.gradeFactor × C.hidden.gradeFactor) ^ hardrock.world.lodeCreekCoupling (0.5)
S.veins    = pick {1: 0.50, 2: 0.35, 3: 0.15};  S.strikeDeg = C heading at head + 90° + U(−35°, 35°)   // veins cross the drainage
  vein k ≥ 2: parallel, offset across strike U(150, 1,200) ft and along strike U(−500, 500) ft from vein 1
per vein v (rng(seed,'world','lode',S.id,v)):
  strikeFt = clamp(LN(1,500, 0.5), 400, 4,000);  downDipFt = clamp(LN(800, 0.35), 300, 1,500);  dipDeg = U(50, 85)
  coverFt = LN(tpl.lode.coverMedFt, 0.6)                       // north 8 (loess, muck), arid 2, temperate 4
  wMed = tpl.lode.widthMedFt × LN(1, 0.30);  G0 = tpl.lode.gMedOzSt × S.richness × LN(1, 0.35)
  oxideDepthFt = tpl.lode.oxideDepthMedFt × LN(1, 0.40);  transitionFrac = 0.30
  refractoryShare = clamp(tpl.lode.refractoryMed × U(0.5, 1.5), 0, 0.95);  grg = U(0.40, 0.80)   // grg: share of FREE gold that is gravity-recoverable
  alloyFineness = clamp(N(tpl.lode.alloyMean, 0.05), 0.55, 0.95)
  groundClass = pick {good 0.35, fair 0.45, poor 0.20};  wallGradeOzSt = LN(0.003, 0.6);  coarseMeanMg = LN(15, 0.6)
  sizeMix = normalize(0.35 × LN(1, 0.2), 0.40 × LN(1, 0.2), 0.25 × LN(1, 0.2))
       // lode size classes: coarse > 0.5 mm (visible gold), medium 0.15–0.5 mm, fine < 0.15 mm (not §3's placer SizeClass)
  pagFactor = U(0, 1) × (tpl.lode.sulfideRich ? 1 : 0.5);  aditPossible = r.u() < tpl.lode.aditP
  shoots: U{1..3} ellipses on the vein plane: centre uniform; half-length along plunge U(150, 450) ft; half-width U(60, 160) ft; plunge U(30°, 80°)
  fields on the nS × nD grid (separable AR(1) as §3 3.5.3): zw (ranges 200 ft strike / 150 ft dip), zg' (150 / 200 ft)
       zg = ρgw × zw + √(1 − ρgw²) × zg'                    ρgw = hardrock.lode.gradeWidthCorr (0.2)
  per panel (i along strike, j down dip):
    w = clamp(wMed × exp(σw (0.45) × zw), 0.2, 30);  pinched = w < hardrock.lode.pinchFt (0.5)
    g = pinched ? wallGradeOzSt : G0 × exp(σg (0.60) × zg + (inShoot ? +shootLog (1.0) : −offShootLog (0.6)))
    depthFt = coverFt + (j + 0.5) × 50 × sin(dipDeg)        // vertical depth to the panel centre
    domain  = depthFt < oxideDepthFt ? oxide : depthFt < oxideDepthFt × (1 + transitionFrac) ? transition : sulfide
    bwi     = LN(tpl.lode.bwiMed[domain], 0.10)             // oxide 9, transition 12.5, sulfide 15 kWh/st
    refr    = sulfide ? clamp(refractoryShare + N(0, 0.05), 0, 0.95) : transition ? 0.5 × refractoryShare : 0
    grgP    = clamp(grg + N(0, 0.05) + (domain = oxide ? 0.05 : 0), 0.05, 0.90) × (1 − refr)     // locked gold is never gravity gold
public facts (rng(seed,'world','lode','public',S.id)):
  outcropVisible = any vein with coverFt < hardrock.lode.outcropMaxCoverFt (3)
  oldWorkings    = outcropVisible ? pick {none 0.35, prospectPits 0.35, adit 0.20, stampMill 0.10} (adit and stampMill weights × S.richness)
                                  : pick {none 0.85, prospectPits 0.15}
  old stopes: 'adit' → in-shoot panels with depthFt < 100 get minedFrac U(0.3, 0.8); 'stampMill' → depthFt < 200, U(0.5, 1.0)
              (written to world.lodePanelStates at generation, like §3's old-timer footprint; the oxide tops were high-graded)
quantize per panel ≈ 9 bytes (width 0.01 ft, log-grade as §3, domain 2 bits, bwi 0.1, refr and grg 1/255); ≈ 5 kB per vein
```

The player sees each shown vein's cover as a range (`coverFtShown` = true × U(0.7, 1.4) rounded to 1 ft, from the surface expression) and `aditPossible` (topography). A blind vein's trace is located to ± 25 ft by a soil anomaly, a trench or the first intercept (`traceKnown`, 14.4).

| Template field (`tpl.lode.*`) | `northernFederal` | `aridFederal` | `temperateFederal` | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `systemsPerDistrict` | 1–3 | 1–3 | 2–4 | |
| `gMedOzSt` (G0 median) | 0.12 (4.1 g/t) | 0.10 (3.4 g/t) | 0.11 | in-shoot panels ×e^1.0 ≈ 0.33 oz/st (11 g/t) |
| `widthMedFt` | 3.5 | 5.0 | 4.0 | narrow quartz veins north; wider shear/fault zones arid |
| `oxideDepthMedFt` | 40 | 200 | 80 | shallow weathering under permafrost; deep Basin-and-Range oxidation |
| `refractoryMed` | 0.15 | 0.35 | 0.20 | share of sulfide-zone gold locked in arsenopyrite/pyrite |
| `alloyMean` (Au / Au+Ag in doré) | 0.85 | 0.70 | 0.80 | arid gold is silver-rich (R3) |
| `aditP` / `sulfideRich` | 0.6 / no | 0.5 / yes | 0.6 / no | adit needs a hillside below the vein |
| `coverMedFt` (σ log 0.6) | 8 | 2 | 4 | share of outcropping veins ≈ 5% / 75% / 32%: northern veins are found by soil lines and placer hints |

**Worked example (panel tonnage).** A panel with true width 3.5 ft holds 50 × 50 × 3.5 = 8,750 ft³ = **723.7 st** of vein. At 0.33 oz/st (an in-shoot panel) it contains **238.8 fine oz**. A 1,500 × 600 ft vein has 30 × 12 = 360 panels. Shoots cover a median 12% of a vein's area (p10–p90 4–29%), and a northern vein holds a median ≈ 31k fine oz above a 0.1 oz/st cutoff (interquartile 14–64k; p90 ≈ 116k), from a 4,000-vein Monte Carlo of this generator.

**Calibration target** (simulator, 14.13): of lode systems, about 70% uneconomic, 20% marginal, 8% good and 2% excellent under `refEconomicsLode` at $4,200, mirroring §3's placer pool. `gMedOzSt` and `shootLog` are the levers.

### 14.4 Exploration and assays (a §4 extension)

§4 defers core drilling and fire assay to the hard-rock track (§4 4.19), so §14 specifies the lode methods; they are data rows in §4's method table (`data/prospecting/methods.ts`, keys `geology.method.<id>.*`), run by §4 programs with the same crews, contractors, lead times, mobilization by access (`accessFactors().mobMult`), arid cost multiplier (`geology.prospectCostAridMult` 0.75), weekly progress, checks and results reports. The draw is §3's compound-Poisson physics re-parameterized for vein support (`drawSampleLode`, below). Year-1 USD (northern) before `cpiIndex`.

| Method `id` | Unit | Delivery and cost | §6 activity | Support (sample mass) | Measures | Season |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rockChip` | sample | geologist or prospector, 12/day; assay only | `handSample` | 2 kg grab | presence; grade with `biasMult` 1.6 (samplers pick mineralized pieces); never enters the resource | operating |
| `soilGrid` | line-km, 25 m stations | 2 people, 1.5 km/day; $25/station assay | `handSample` | — | locates blind veins (below); no grade | operating |
| `channel` | sample per 5 ft of outcrop or trench | 2 people with a saw, 10/day; $60 assay | `handSample` (outcrop) / in a trench | 3 kg per ft of width across the vein | true width (`widthCv` 0.05), grade | operating |
| `trenchLode` | 50-ft trench across the vein | §4 `trench` costs; channel samples included | `mechSample` (notice) | channel | surface width and grade; oxide only; sets `traceKnown` | operating |
| `rcLode` | ft | contractor $45/ft (≈ $148/m) + mob $30,000 × access; 350 ft/day; $45 per 5-ft interval | `drill` (notice) | 5-ft interval, 3 kg split | grade; width (`widthCv` 0.30); wet holes below the water table: `volumeCv` +0.20 | any (winter +15%) |
| `coreLode` (HQ) | ft | contractor $95/ft (≈ $310/m remote all-in; arid × 0.75 ≈ $71/ft) + mob $45,000 × access; 150 ft/day; $55 per interval; geologist logging required | `drill` (notice) | half core 2.5 kg/ft of core | width (`widthCv` 0.05), structure, density, BWi and metallurgy material | any (winter +15%) |
| `metTest` | composite | lab $25,000 per composite, 6 weeks; ≥ 150 kg of core or bulk | none | — | GRG ± 0.05; leach recovery by domain ± 0.03; BWi ± 0.5; refractory flag; acid-base accounting reveals `pagFactor` ± 0.15 ($8,000 add-on) | any |
| `bulkLode` | st | own pit or adit test round, or a contractor at $85/st broken; processed at a toll mill as a test lot (14.8.1) | `bulkSample` (notice: < 1,000 st, D-14.25) | 100–999 st | grade at large support; actual recovery | operating (pit); any (adit) |
| `ugChip` (automatic) | face sample every 10 ft of development on the vein | $50/sample with own assayer, else lab | — | 4 kg face chip | exposes panels: `developedSides` += 1 | year-round |

Drill hole layout uses §4's `SampleTarget`, which becomes a discriminated union: the existing shape is `kind: 'block'` (the default when `kind` is absent, so placer data is unchanged), and lode holes use `{ kind: 'pierce'; veinId; i; j }` (the panel where the hole crosses the vein). Footage per hole comes from geometry, with the collar on the hanging-wall side drilling against the dip:

```
holeFt    = depthFt / sin(holeDip) + hardrock.drill.tailFt (30)       depthFt = coverFt + (j + 0.5) × 50 × sin(dipDeg)
coreLenFt = trueWidthFt / sin(holeDip + dipDeg)                         // intercept length along the hole; sample mass uses it
  holeDip = 60° by default (45–75° allowed); a vein whose trace is not known (blind, not yet located) costs
  footage × hardrock.explore.blindTraceMult (1.6) for fan and scissor holes until the first intercept sets traceKnown
```

*Example:* panel j = 3 on a 70° vein under 50 ft of cover: depth 214.4 ft, hole 277.6 ft at 60°; a 4-ft vein gives 5.2 ft of core. Soil lines detect a blind vein they cross with `p = hardrock.soil.detectP (0.85) × exp(−coverFt / hardrock.soil.coverScaleFt (20))` (× 0.6 on frozen ground) when the vein's grade at the crossing is ≥ 0.02 oz/st, on `rng(seed,'sample',veinId,'soil',lineId)`; a hit shows the vein and sets `traceKnown`. Lode samples draw on §4's `'sample'` stream keyed `(veinId, i, j, methodId, k)`.

**Assays.** Every lode sample is fire assayed. The lab adds its own nugget error (the 30-g aliquot) and a hidden bias:

| Assay | Cost / sample | Aliquot CV | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fa30` (30-g fire assay, AA finish; gravimetric above 10 g/t) | $45 | `hardrock.assay.faAliquotCvRef` (0.6) × √(coarse share) | the default |
| `metallicScreen` (1 kg screened, coarse fraction assayed whole) | $120 | 0.05 | removes the lab nugget on coarse-gold ore |
| QA/QC program (blanks, certified standards, field duplicates at 12% insertion) | +12% of assay cost | — | needed for `indicated` (14.5); after ≥ 20 standards the lab's bias is shown ± 1% and corrected |

Each lab (1–2 per region, data) carries hidden `bias` ~ N(0, 0.03), drawn once per lab on `rng(seed,'hr-lab',labId)`. Without QA/QC the player cannot see it, and every estimate inherits it.

**Measurement model.** `drawSampleLode(panel, ps, req, method, rng)` runs §3's draw order with vein units: local grade (de Wijs), then §3 step 5's compound-Poisson particle draw per lode size class with λ_k = gLocal × 34.2857 × M_kg × mix_k / m_k, then the assay terms below as lognormal factors. The closed forms (used by the estimator, the VOI hints and the tests) are:

```
goldMg      = g × 34.2857 × M_kg                     // g in oz/st (1 oz/st = 34.2857 g/t = mg/kg); M_kg = sample mass, kg
m_eff       = Σ_k mix_k × m_k × (1 + c_k²)            // m = [vein.coarseMeanMg, 0.5, 0.02] mg; c = [2.0, 1.0, 0.7]
fieldCv     = √(m_eff / goldMg)                       // particle (field) nugget effect
aliquotCv   = assay = metallicScreen ? 0.05 : faAliquotCvRef × √mix_coarse
σL²         = hardrock.lode.deWijsAlpha (0.06) × ln(max(1, panelSt / sampleSt))   // sample-to-panel variability; 0 at ≥ panel support
logVar      = ln(1 + fieldCv²) + ln(1 + aliquotCv²) + σL² + ln(1 + volumeCv²)
gLocal      = panel.gradeOzSt × exp(σL × Z − σL²/2)          // Z ~ N(0,1) on the sample's rng (§4 'sample' stream, keys above)
reported    = gLocal × LNmean(1, fieldCv) × LNmean(1, aliquotCv) × (1 + lab.bias) × biasMult     // closed form of the particle draw
widthLogged = trueWidth × LNmean(1, method.widthCv)   // core 0.05, rc 0.30, channel 0.05
  panelSt = 2,500 × trueWidthFt / 12.09; a bulk sample larger than a panel is the tonnage-weighted mean of the panels it took
```

**Worked example (why one drill hole cannot value a panel).** A 4-ft HQ core intercept (10 kg of half core) in a panel at 0.33 oz/st, coarse share 0.35 of 15-mg particles: m_eff = 0.35 × 15 × 5 + 0.40 × 0.5 × 2 + 0.25 × 0.02 × 1.49 = 26.7 mg; goldMg = 0.33 × 34.29 × 10 = 113 mg; **fieldCv 0.49**. The fa30 aliquot adds CV 0.36, and the panel-scale term is 0.06 × ln(724 / 0.011) = 0.67. Total log-variance ≈ 0.21 + 0.12 + 0.67 = **1.00 (σ ≈ 1.0)**: one intercept fixes the panel grade only within a factor of ~2.7. Metallic screens remove 0.12 of it. A 500-st bulk sample through a mill has σL² = 0.06 × ln(724/500) = 0.02 (**σ ≈ 0.15**). That is the nugget effect at hard-rock scale: drill to find and outline, then sample in bulk or develop to know.

### 14.5 Estimation, classification and reports

**Estimator.** `estimateLode(priors, evidence, planning)` is §4's estimator (4.5–4.8) on the vein plane, not a new statistics engine (D-14.8):
- per panel, log grade and log width are separate fields (width is well measured by core, grade is not), each with the template hierarchy as prior and §4's kriging-lite on the separable covariance of 14.3; ore shoots enter as §4-style discrete hypotheses ("shoot through panels A–B plunging 45°") weighted by the intercepts;
- panel contained oz = `g × w × 50 × 50 / 12.09 × (1 − minedFrac)`, aggregated by Fenton-Wilkinson to claim and vein P10 / P50 / P90 for **tonnage, grade and contained fine oz**;
- the minable set uses 14.6's diluted grade and the planned method and processing route: `margin50_p = T_mined × (gDil50 × R × price × payable − c_mine − c_proc − c_ga) − devCost_p`, where T_mined is st mined from panel p (14.6.3), gDil50 its diluted P50 grade (oz/st), R the route's planning recovery (14.8), price $/fine oz (§4 planning), payable 0.99 refinery or the toll form's payable, c_mine / c_proc / c_ga $/st by method, route and site, and devCost_p = devFt_p × $/ft;
- production feedback: mill head assays and poured ounces by source panel become §4 production observations (4.4.6).

**Classification** (all gates must pass; spacing is measured on the vein plane; footprint F = the minable panels):

| Class | Coverage | Support | QA/QC | Spread (P90/P10 of minable oz, no pocket term) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| measured | ≥ 90% of F has `developedSides ≥ 2` (drifts above and below with chip samples) | development exposure | required | ≤ 1.5 |
| indicated | ≥ 70% of F within 1 panel (≤ 75 ft) of an intercept; ≥ 15 intercepts | metallic screens on ≥ 50% of ore intercepts, or a ≥ 500-st bulk sample reconciled | required on ≥ 80% of assays | ≤ 2.0 |
| inferred | ≥ 70% of F within 3 panels (≤ 150 ft); ≥ 6 intercepts | any | optional | ≤ 3.5 |
| speculative | otherwise (rock chips, seller claims, old records) | — | — | — |

Narrow nuggety veins rarely reach `indicated` from surface drilling alone. That is real (CIM and S-K 1300 practice): underground development is itself the last stage of exploration.

**Reports** (engagements of §4's consultant; independent; valid `reportValidityWeeks` 104):

| Scope (`prospect/engageConsultant` scope) | Cost | Weeks | Requires | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lodeTRS`: technical report summary with a mineral resource statement (S-K 1300 / NI 43-101 style) | $180,000 + $400 per intercept, cap $350,000 | 8 | ≥ inferred, QA/QC on | royalty sales; equity; hard-money certified-claim collateral (§11) |
| `pea`: preliminary economic assessment (inferred allowed; "not reserves") | $350,000 | 12 | a TRS ≤ 104 wk | pre-production stream (14.12); valuation uplift in §5 asks |
| `pfs`: pre-feasibility study declaring probable reserves | $1,200,000 | 26 | indicated on ≥ 60% of planned tonnage, a `metTest`, a geotechnical review ($60,000) | project finance (14.12); proven reserves once measured panels exist |

Reports use the **standard case** (price = min(EMA13, spot), default costs and recoveries), as §4 D-4.27 requires. `lendableResource` gains `{ reportLevel: 'trs' | 'pea' | 'pfs', byClass: { st, ozSt, fineOz }[], reserve?: { probableSt, provenSt, ozSt } }`.

### 14.6 Development paths: open pit vs underground

Both paths start from the same estimate and the same lode Plan of Operations (14.10). A site may run both: an oxide pit on the outcrop first, then an adit beneath it.

**14.6.1 Open pit.** A small pit on a steep vein is a trench that widens with depth. Per 50-ft vertical slice, per foot of strike (closed form; no pit optimizer, D-14.12):

```
w_h        = trueWidthFt / sin(dipDeg)                      // horizontal width of the vein, ft (per panel column i)
total_k    = (h2² − h1²) / tan(α) + (h2 − h1) × w_h         // ft² per ft of strike excavated in slice k (V-trench; independent of dip while α < dip)
ore_k      = max(0, h2 − max(h1, coverFt)) × w_h            // vein below the soil cover
waste_k    = total_k − ore_k                                // soil over the vein and both wall wedges
strip_k    = waste_k / ore_k                                // incremental strip ratio of slice k (same density assumed)
  h1, h2 = slice top and bottom depth below surface (ft); α = pit wall angle: oxide 40°, transition 45°, rock 50° (hardrock.pit.wallAngleDeg)
  slice ore maps to panel rows j by depth: panel j spans [coverFt + j × 50 sin(dip), coverFt + (j + 1) × 50 sin(dip)]; slice tonnage and
  gold are the overlap-weighted sums of those panels' tonnage and gold (so pit and underground draw on one inventory, PanelState.minedFrac)
dilution:  w_mine = w_h + 2 × hardrock.pit.contactSkinFt (1.0) × gcMult;  gDil = (g × w_h + wallGrade × (w_mine − w_h)) / w_mine
           gcMult = grade control none 1.5 | visual 1.0 | sampled 0.7;  mining recovery hardrock.pit.miningRecovery 0.95
blasting:  slices with depth < hardrock.pit.freeDigOxideFt (30) in the oxide domain are free-dig (excavator, dig mult 0.85); deeper is drilled and blasted
disturbance (§6 RCE): pit acres = Σ_i 50 × (w_h + 2 × depth_i / tan α) / 43,560; waste-dump acres = wasteBcy × 1.45 / (hardrock.pit.dumpHeightFt (60) × 1,613)
```

Loading and hauling reuse §7 7.6.2–7.6.3 with the placer fleet: excavator dig rate × `hardrock.pit.blastedDigMult` (0.70) for blasted rock, truck payload in st from §9 (weight-limited: a 40t ADT carries 44 st), and a pit-ramp haul distance. Cost per st moved with an owned fleet lands at **$3.5–5.0**.

*Worked example.* A 10-ft-true-width oxide shear zone dipping 70° (w_h = 10.64 ft), outcropping (coverFt 0), walls at 45°: slice 0–50 ft strips 2,500 / 532 = **4.7:1**, 50–100 ft **14.1:1**, 100–150 ft **23.5:1**. At 0.09 oz/st diluted, ore-purchase toll terms (14.8.1) leave ≈ $135 per wet ore st before stripping (payable $305 less TC $134, trucking $14, ore mining $4.50 and G&A $15), so at $4.50 per st moved the pit stops near a 30:1 incremental strip (≈ 175 ft deep). With an own mill (≈ $280/st margin) the same pit goes to ≈ 60:1 (≈ 350 ft), deep enough to reach the sulfide transition in most districts, where recovery drops (14.8.2).

**14.6.2 Underground access.** An **adit** (horizontal tunnel from a hillside; only if `aditPossible`) drains by gravity and suits rail or small trackless gear. A **decline** (ramp at 15%) works anywhere and lets trucks drive in, at higher cost per foot and with pumping below the water table. Development rate per heading:

```
devFtWk_h = roundsPerShift_h × advanceFt_h × shiftsPerDay × daysPerWeek × u_h × groundDevMult × min(1, ventRatio)
  jackleg heading 7 × 8 ft: 1 round/shift, 5.5 ft advance (6-ft steel, 92% pull); crew 2 ugMiner per shift; mucker or LHD
  jumbo heading 12 × 12 ft: 1 round/shift, 10 ft advance; crew 3 ugMiner per shift (jumbo, bolter, LHD)
  decline 14 × 14 ft: 1 round/shift, 10 ft; crew 4 ugMiner per shift (jumbo, bolter, LHD, truck); pumping below the water table
  every blasting shift also needs a blaster (own blasting) and an underground shift boss (§8 foreman with the trait) for the site
  u_h = §7 7.5 usable fraction (staffed × A × e × F × W × Z) over the heading's crew and machines; W = 1 and Z = 1 underground
  groundDevMult: good 1.05, fair 1.0, poor 0.80
  re-entry: the 1-round cycle already contains hardrock.ug.reentryHours (0.5) of post-blast clearance; it is reported as idle cause
            'reentry' for the heading's machines and stretches to 0.5 / ventRatio when ventilation is short (ventRatio, 14.9)
cost per ft: labor emerges from §8 payroll for the crew's hours (D-14.35) + nonLabor_h (explosives, bolts and mesh, services, consumables)
  + §9 fuel, power and wear on the heading's machines
  nonLabor: jackleg $380/ft, jumbo $820/ft, decline $1,100/ft (× supportStandard multiplier, below)
  all-in anchors at reference crews: jackleg ≈ $650–900/ft, jumbo ≈ $1,300–1,600/ft, decline ≈ $1,700–2,200/ft
```

*Worked example.* Two miners on a jackleg heading, 2 shifts × 6 days: 1 × 5.5 × 2 × 6 × 0.85 = **56 ft/week**. Labor ≈ 2 × 10 h × $58/h (burdened incl. underground WC) + supervision ≈ $1,400 per round = $255/ft, so all-in ≈ $255 + $380 + machines ≈ $700/ft. A 1,000-ft adit takes ~18 weeks and costs ~$0.7–0.9M. A 1,500-ft decline at 1 round per shift, 2 shifts × 7 days with a jumbo (u 0.80) advances 112 ft/week: 13–14 weeks and ~$2.9M.
