**14.6.3 Stoping methods, dilution and mining recovery.** The player picks a method per stope (panel). Dilution comes from the minimum mining width and overbreak; mining recovery from pillars and unrecovered broken ore.

```
w_mine  = max(trueWidthFt, minWidth[m]) + overbreak[m] × groundOverbreakMult × supportOverbreakMult
gDil    = (g × trueWidthFt + wallGradeOzSt × (w_mine − trueWidthFt)) / w_mine          // oz/st
T_dil   = 50 × 50 × w_mine / 12.09                                                     // st broken per panel
T_mined = T_dil × miningRecovery[m];  oz_mined = T_mined × gDil
devFt_p = devFtPerPanel[m]  (sublevel drift, raises, drawpoints, fill access; access drifts and levels are capital, 14.12)
```

| Method `m` | minWidth ft | overbreak ft | mining recovery | st per miner-shift | direct $/st (excl. dev) = nonLabor + labor | devFt per panel (heading type) | Powder lb/st | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shrinkage` | 4.0 | 1.5 | 0.85 | 12 | 70 = 24 + 46 | 85 (jackleg) | 1.4 | only the 35% swell is drawn while mining; the rest stays in the stope until final draw (cash lag) |
| `longhole` (sublevel) | 6.0 | 2.5 | 0.90 | 35 | 35 = 19 + 16 | 70 (jumbo) | 0.8 | needs dip ≥ 60°, a longhole drill and an LHD; best on wide, regular veins |
| `cutAndFill` | 5.0 | 1.0 | 0.95 | 9 | 110 = 48 (incl. fill $12) + 62 | 60 (jumbo) | 1.6 | selective; poor ground |
| `resue` | 2.5 | 0.5 | 0.92 | 5 | 160 = 49 + 111 | 70 (jackleg) | 2.0 | waste blasted first and left as fill; very narrow high-grade veins |

The engine posts only `nonLaborUsdSt[m]` per st broken (powder, timber and bolts, fill, air, power, consumables; `exp.explosives` for the powder share, `exp.consumables` for the rest). Miner labor is §8 payroll and becomes $/st through productivity; the labor column is the reference value (10-h shift, $42/hr, 1.32 burden incl. underground WC, `stPerMinerShift`) used in plans, previews and the tables below (D-14.35).

`groundOverbreakMult`: good 0.8, fair 1.0, poor 1.5. **Support standard** (`plan.supportStandard`): minimum / standard / conservative multiply non-labor support cost by 0.80 / 1.00 / 1.25, overbreak by 1.20 / 1.00 / 0.90 and the fall-of-ground injury hazard by 1.6 / 1.0 / 0.7 (14.10). *Trade-off:* cheaper support buys dilution and injuries.

*Worked example (one in-shoot panel, 3.5 ft at 0.33 oz/st, wall 0.003, fair ground, jackleg $850/ft, jumbo $1,450/ft):*

| Method | w_mine | gDil oz/st (g/t) | st mined | oz mined | Mining $/st | Mining $/oz | + own mill $60/st | + toll $165/st |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shrinkage | 5.5 | 0.211 (7.2) | 966.7 | 204.1 | 144.7 | 686 | **970** | 1,467 |
| longhole | 8.5 | 0.138 (4.7) | 1,581.9 | 217.7 | 99.2 | 720 | 1,156 | 1,919 |
| cutAndFill | 6.0 | 0.194 (6.6) | 1,178.7 | 228.4 | 183.8 | 949 | 1,258 | 1,800 |
| resue | 4.0 | 0.289 (9.9) | 760.9 | 220.0 | 238.2 | 824 | 1,031 | **1,394** |

On this narrow vein shrinkage wins with an own mill and resue wins when every ton pays a toll fee. On a 9-ft vein longhole drops to ≈ $318/oz mined against shrinkage's ≈ $385. The method choice depends on the vein *and* the processing route.

**Grade control and slices.** Each panel is mined in 4 slices (a pit slice uses the same factors for the panel rows it takes). A slice's realized grade is the panel's diluted grade × a slice factor; the four factors are drawn once per panel on `rng(seed,'hr-ops','slice',veinId,i,j)` (log-sd `hardrock.ops.sliceLogSd` 0.30, renormalized to mean 1 so the panel total is exact; they are truth, so they do not depend on the site or the week). Ore/waste routing uses the player's `cutoffOzSt` against the grade-control observation, drawn on `rng(seed,'hr-ops','gc',veinId,i,j,slice)`: none = the panel P50; visual = slice grade × LN(1, 0.7); sampled (chip or blasthole sampling, $3/st) = × LN(1, 0.35). Slices between `lowGradeOzSt` and the cutoff go to the low-grade stockpile. Misrouted slices dilute the mill or lose ore to the dump.

**High-grading.** A panel left unmined after a neighbour on the same sublevel is mined becomes `sterilized` after `hardrock.ug.sterilizeWeeks` (26): reaching it later needs re-development at `hardrock.ug.redevelopCostMult` (1.5) × its devFt (D-14.23).

**Contract mining.** Underground development and stoping can be let to a mining contractor at `hardrock.ug.contractMarkup` (1.25) × reference all-in costs (labor included), with the contractor's crew (skill 60), equipment and explosives licence, after a lead of 8–16 weeks. A contracted adit or decline is a §14.12 capital project (budget, overrun draw, LSTK option); own-crew development is a heading in the `LodePlan` at actual cost. *Trade-off:* no fleet capital, no ATF permit, no underground hiring, but a 25% markup and no say in productivity.

### 14.7 Drilling, blasting and explosives

**Consumption.** Explosives per st broken = `powderLbSt[m]` (14.6.3; development 2.5 jackleg / 2.2 jumbo; open pit 0.55 ANFO). Prices: packaged emulsion $1.80/lb, ANFO $0.60/lb, initiation $4.00 per hole (jackleg round 30 holes, jumbo round 45; pit $0.15 per st blasted). They post to `exp.explosives` (14.17).

**Own vs contract.** Open-pit blasting can be contracted (`contractDrillBlastUsdSt` $2.10 per st blasted, contractor brings drill, explosives, blaster and licence; no magazine) or done in-house (own top-hammer drill, magazines, a certified blaster, an ATF user permit, §6 `fed.explosives`; ≈ $1.00/st). Underground blasting is own or contract mining (14.6.3). *Trade-off:* the in-house route halves the per-ton cost but needs a permit that takes about 13 weeks, magazines and a blaster on every blasting shift.

**Magazines and custody** (27 CFR 555 Subpart K, simplified):
- Explosives are stored in a Type 1 (permanent, 20,000 lb game capacity, $25k) or Type 2 (portable, also used underground, 2,000 lb, $6k) magazine; detonators in a separate box ($3k). Each is a §9 `site` item on the claim.
- Deliveries (`explosives/order`) arrive after `hardrock.explosives.leadWeeks` (highway 1, seasonalRoad 2) by road or trail only: §3 `claimAccess.freightMode` must be `'road'` or `'trail'` in the arrival week, or the delivery waits (no air freight of high explosives). Fly-in and winter-trail sites therefore stockpile in the trail window, and magazine capacity caps the stockpile. Stock `explosivesLb` on the site; when it is empty no round fires (idle cause `explosives`).
- A daily-summary record and annual inventory are automatic with a blaster employed; without one, step 13's ATF compliance check fails.
- **Loss or theft** must be reported within 24 hours. §12's magazine-theft event calls `hardrock.loseExplosives(siteId, lb)`. With a blaster employed the daily summary finds it the same turn and it is reported automatically; without one it is found U{1..4} weeks later at the next delivery or inventory, and the late report is an `explosives.unreportedLoss` violation (§6 table, $15k, standing −6).

**Blast hazards** (per blast, `rng(seed,'hr-blast',turn,siteId)`): misfire p = `hardrock.blast.misfireBase` (0.01) × (2 − blasterSkill/50), costing 4–8 hours in that heading; flyrock (open pit only) p = 0.002 × (1.5 − blasterSkill/100), raising a §8 injury roll and an MSHA citation (S&S).

### 14.8 Processing: toll milling and an own mill

**14.8.1 Toll milling (the low-capital path).** Each region has 1–2 custom mills (data: `TollMill`), off the map at the hub, with a circuit (gravity + CIL at P80 75 µm), a weekly allotment for outside ore, a minimum lot, a queue and a hidden assay bias. Two contract forms:

| Form | Player gets | Player bears | Typical terms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orePurchase` | cash on settlement (3–4 weeks after delivery): payable oz × spot × (1 − refining deduction) − treatment charge | none of the mill's recovery risk | payable recovery oxide 0.85, transition 0.75, sulfide 0.70 (refractory penalty below); TC $140/dry st; min head 0.06 oz/st |
| `tollService` (campaign) | the doré poured from its own lot, as a §10 lot (`source: 'toll'`) | actual recovery on its ore; campaign delay 4–10 weeks | fee $150/dry st; minimum campaign 500 st (smaller lots pay the minimum) |

```
dryTons      = wetTons × (1 − moisture)                     moisture = hardrock.toll.moisture[domain] (oxide 0.04, transition and sulfide 0.03)
millAssay    = trueHead × (1 + tollMill.bias) × LNmean(1, 0.03)          bias ~ N(−0.015, 0.015), hidden, per mill (rng(seed,'hr-toll','mill',tollMillId))
ownAssay     = trueHead × (1 + lab.bias)   × LNmean(1, 0.03)          (player's split at the player's lab; optional, $60)
settleHead   = no ownAssay ? millAssay
             : |millAssay − ownAssay| / mean ≤ splittingLimit (0.05) ? mean : umpireAssay ($350, umpire lab, bias 0)   // the side further from the umpire pays it
  assay draws on rng(seed,'hr-toll',lotId) in the order mill, own, umpire
refrLot      = tonnage-weighted refractory share of the lot (the mill's cyanide-shake reads it ± 0.05 on the same stream)
payRecEff    = max(0.30, payRec[domain] − max(0, refrLot − hardrock.toll.refrFreeShare (0.15)))
penalties    = refrLot > hardrock.toll.refrPenaltyShare (0.25) ? hardrock.toll.refrPenaltyUsdSt (40) × dryTons : 0
orePurchase  : proceeds = settleHead < minHeadOzSt ? 0 (TC waived; the mill keeps the ore)
                        : dryTons × settleHead × payRecEff × spot × (1 − 0.01) − dryTons × TC − penalties
               a read refrLot > hardrock.toll.refuseShare (0.40) ends the site's ore-purchase contracts (REFRACTORY_REFUSED on new ones)
tollService  : recoveredFine = Σ contained fine × R_toll;  R_toll = R(lot, toll circuit) × (1 − hardrock.toll.campaignLoss (0.035))
               R from 14.8.2 with the toll mill's circuit (gravity + CIL, P80 75 µm, operator skill 60) and the lot's true mix;
               campaignLoss is circuit clean-out and carbon inventory the mill keeps on a short campaign
               doré rawOz = recoveredFine / alloy / (1 − 0.005)
trucking     : wetTons × (haulMi × hardrock.toll.truckUsdPerStMi (0.20) × truckMult[access] + loadingUsdSt (2.00))
               haulMi = claim distanceToTownMi + D.hub.roadMiFromTown (toll mills sit at the hub, §3)
               truckMult: highway 1.0, seasonalRoad 1.3, winterTrail 2.2 (trail window only); fly-in sites cannot ship ore
               a week ships only if claimAccess.freightMode ∈ {'road', 'trail'} (ore is never flown)
fees and ripple: TC and toll fee × cpiIndex × clamp(goldIdxReal_lag26^0.2, 0.9, 1.2); allotment × clamp(goldIdxReal_lag13^−0.5, 0.6, 1.2)  // busy mills in a boom; real index, §10 D-10.32
interests     : in-kind ProductionInterests on the source claims cannot take ore-purchase gold; §5 settles them in cash on the
               settlement's payable oz × spot (the `settleSaleInterests` path), NSR interests on the proceeds net of TC and trucking
```

```ts
interface TollMill { id: TollMillId; name: string; districtIds: DistrictId[]; circuit: 'gravityCil'; p80: 75; skill: 60;
  baseAllotmentStWk: number; minLotSt: number; queueWeeks: number; status: 'open' | 'shutdown'; shutdownUntilTurn: number | null;
  queue: TollLotId[]; hidden: { bias: number } }
interface TollContract { id: TollContractId; tollMillId: TollMillId; siteId: SiteId; form: 'orePurchase' | 'tollService';
  allotmentStWk: number; feeUsdSt: number; tcUsdSt: number; payRec: Record<LodeDomain, number>; startTurn: number; endTurn: number; ownAssay: boolean }
interface TollLot { id: TollLotId; contractId: TollContractId; wetSt: number; shippedTurn: number;
  status: 'inTransit' | 'queued' | 'processing' | 'assaying' | 'umpire' | 'settled' | 'refused';
  hidden: { dryStTrue: number; headOzSt: number; stByDomain: Record<LodeDomain, number>; refr: number; grg: number; alloy: number };
  estHeadOzSt: number;                                   // the player's grade-control estimate at shipment
  millAssay?: number; ownAssay?: number; umpireAssay?: number; settleHead?: number; proceedsCents?: Cents; goldLotId?: LotId }
```

*Worked example.* 800 wet st of oxide ore at a true 0.25 oz/st (refractory 0), 60 haul miles on a highway. Dry 768 st, contained 192.0 fine oz. Mill assay 0.2463, own assay 0.2509: 1.9% apart, so settle at the mean, 0.2486. **Ore purchase:** 768 × 0.2486 × 0.85 = 162.3 payable oz × $4,158 = $674.8k, less TC $107.5k and trucking $11.2k = **$556.1k (69% of contained value)**, cash in ~4 weeks. **Toll service:** the mill recovers 0.9336 on this oxide (R = 0.9674 at grg 0.55 and skill 60, less the 3.5% campaign loss): 179.2 fine oz of doré (211.9 raw oz at alloy 0.85) ≈ $745.3k at the refinery, less fee $115.2k and trucking = **$618.9k (77%)**, but 6–10 weeks later, and a transitional lot recovering 0.80 would net ≈ $107k less. *Trade-off:* certainty and speed against ~8 points of value.

**14.8.2 Own mill.** A mill is a capital project (14.12) built in modules on a millsite or lode claim: crushing, grinding, gravity, optional CIL (carbon-in-leach with elution, electrowinning, smelting and cyanide detox), a TSF and power. Circuits: `gravity` (crush, grind, centrifugal concentrators, shaker table) or `gravityCil`.

```
millStPerDay = ratedStPerDay × min(maxSoftOreMult (1.3), bwiRef / bwiFeed) × grindFactor(P80) × A_mill × ramp(t) × effective('hardrock.millAvailabilityMult')
  ratedStPerDay at bwiRef = 14 kWh/st and P80 = 106 µm;  bwiFeed = tonnage-weighted bwi of this week's feed
  grindFactor(P) = (1/√106 − 1/√F) / (1/√P − 1/√F),  F = 9,500 µm (−3/8 in crusher product)      // Bond's law at fixed mill power
  A_mill = hardrock.mill.availability (0.90; P3+: §9 health of `liners` and `drivetrain`)
  ramp(t) = 0.5 + 0.5 × min(1, weeksSinceCommissioning / hardrock.mill.rampWeeks (16))     // throughput and recovery losses ramp together
Bond specific energy (explains throughput, not billed) = 10 × bwiFeed × (1/√P − 1/√F)          // 12.16 kWh/st at BWi 14, 106 µm
power billed (kWh/week) = Σ_running mill-family machines (kW × hardrock.mill.loadFactor (0.85) × hours run) + otherKwhSt × millSt
  otherKwhSt: gravity 6, gravityCil 18 (pumps, agitators, elution, detox, lights); a ball mill draws near-constant power, so
  grinding kWh/st = 110 kW × 0.85 × 24 / millStPerDay: 22.4 at rated, 27.2 at 75 µm, 18.4 at 150 µm (100 st/day mill)
  plant total ≈ 50 kWh/st for a 100 st/day CIL mill at rated; grid $0.11/kWh ≈ $5.5/st, a 1 MW genset (0.073 gal/kWh) ≈ $13–15/st
```

Recovery splits each domain's gold into gravity-recoverable, free (leachable) and refractory (locked in sulfide) parts that never overlap (D-14.15, D-14.31). The week's feed is split by domain; `grg` and `refr` are the oz-weighted panel values of that domain's feed:

```
R_grav  = grg × (circuit = gravity ? eGravOnly (0.80) : eGravAheadOfCil (0.60))          // grg ≤ 1 − refr by construction (14.3)
lock    = 1 − kLock[dom] × max(0, (P80 − 75) / 75)        kLock: oxide 0.01, transition 0.05, sulfide 0.10
R_leach = circuit = gravityCil ? ((1 − refr − R_grav) × Lfree[dom] + refr × Lrefr) × lock × cnMult : 0
  Lfree: oxide 0.95, transition 0.88, sulfide 0.93;  Lrefr 0.40;  cnMult: cyanide low 0.98 / standard 1.00 / high 1.005
R_raw   = min(0.99, R_grav + R_leach)
R_skill = R_raw ^ (0.6 × skillRecoveryMult(s_met) + 0.4 × skillRecoveryMult(s_ops))     // §8 loss exponent; s_met = metallurgist, s_ops = mill operators (hours-weighted)
          // no metallurgist on a CIL mill: s_met = 20 (blended exponent ≈ 1.19 with skill-55 operators: 96.4% → 95.7%); gravity-only: s_met = s_ops
R       = 1 − (1 − R_skill) × (2 − ramp(t))                                             // losses 1.5× at commissioning, 1.0× once ramped
recovered = Σ_dom feedOz_dom × R_dom;  tails = feedOz − recovered → TSF (re-leachable later, as §7 7.14 re-mining of a deposit)
```

*Worked example (vein grg 0.55, P80 106 µm, skill 55).* Gravity-only on oxide: **44.0%** (the rest waits in the tailings for a future leach). Gravity + CIL on oxide (grg 0.55, refr 0): 0.330 + 0.670 × 0.95 × 0.9959 = **96.4%**. Free-milling sulfide (refr 0.10, panel grg 0.55 × 0.90 = 0.495): 0.297 + (0.603 × 0.93 + 0.10 × 0.40) × 0.9587 = **87.3%**. The same vein deeper where refractory reaches 0.60 (grg 0.22): 0.132 + (0.268 × 0.93 + 0.24) × 0.9587 = **60.1%**, the "sulfide surprise" a `metTest` is bought to avoid. At refr 0.95 CIL recovers ≈ 41%; the anchors (oxide 92–96, free-milling sulfide 85–92, refractory 30–60, gravity-only 35–65%) hold across the generator's ranges.

*Grind trade-off.* At 100 st/day rated, grinding free-milling sulfide ore (BWi 14, refr 0.10) at 0.20 oz/st to 75 µm gives 82.6 st/day at 89.8% (14.8 oz/day); at 106 µm 100 st/day at 87.3% (17.5 oz/day); at 150 µm 121.7 st/day at 83.8% (20.4 oz/day, if crushing and the mine can feed it). Coarse grind wins when the mill is the bottleneck; fine grind wins when ore is the limit (the reserve), exactly as §7's overfeed rule does for placer. Fine grind also costs power: 27.2 against 18.4 kWh/st of grinding.

**Costs.** Weekly lines: mill labor (§8 payroll), power (`exp.power`: grid $0.11/kWh where a line exists, else §9 gensets at fuel cost through `exp.fuel`), reagents (`exp.reagents`: NaCN 0.4 / 0.7 / 1.1 kg/st by cyanide level at $3.00/kg; lime 1.5 kg/st at $0.25; grinding media 1.0 kg/st at $1.50; carbon and detox $1.60/st; gravity-only $2.50/st total), liners and maintenance (§9). Anchors: **100 st/day gravity + CIL $55–75/st, 250 st/day $38–50/st, gravity-only $30–40/st.**

**Gold in circuit and pours.** CIL holds `hardrock.mill.goldInCircuitDays` (5) of leach-recovered gold on carbon (hidden):

```
gicTarget = (running ? R_leach-recovered oz this week / 7 × goldInCircuitDays : 0);   Δgic = gicTarget − gic
poured    = recovered − Δgic          // the first weeks after start-up pour less; care and maintenance releases the inventory
```

Gravity concentrate and electrowon gold are smelted at each weekly pour (step 12). Poured fine oz are allocated to source claims pro rata to each claim's share of the week's recovered oz (from the stockpile's per-claim tracking); per claim, §5 `settleProductionInterests` takes in-kind interests, then §10 `addLot({ claimId, rawOz: fine / alloy / (1 − 0.005), trueAlloyFineness: oz-weighted vein alloyFineness, trueDirtFrac: 0.005, location: 'camp', source: 'mill' })`. The player sees poured oz exactly, and calculated head grade, tail grade and recovery from the mill's own assays (each ± `hardrock.mill.metAccountingCv` 0.05, on `rng(seed,'hr-ops','met',turn,millId)`); true feed grade, gold in circuit and true recovery stay hidden.

**Tailings storage facility.** Capacity in st; each milled st fills one; footprint `hardrock.tsf.acresPerSt` (2.5e-5 ac/st, embankments included) feeds §6's `tsf` RCE type. Lined (required with cyanide) $15 per st of capacity; an unlined impoundment for gravity-only tails $5. Built and raised as capital projects; when full, the mill stops (§7 stage and cause `tailings`, D-14.36). Seepage risk scales with `pagFactor` and lining (§12 `tsfSeepage` event).

**Care and maintenance.** `mill/careAndMaintenance` stops the mill: hourly crews are laid off or reassigned through §8 (its layoff rules apply), salaried staff stay unless fired, gold in circuit is released at the next pour, and the mill costs `hardrock.mill.cmUsdWk` ($4,000: security, TSF monitoring, heat, minimum power) plus §6's monitoring obligations. Restart re-enters ramp-up at `ramp = 0.75` after ≥ 13 weeks idle.

```ts
interface Mill { id: MillId; siteId: SiteId; circuit: 'gravity' | 'gravityCil'; ratedStPerDay: number; machineIds: MachineId[];
  p80: number; targetStPerDay: number; cyanide: 'low' | 'standard' | 'high'; acceptNpcOre: boolean;
  status: 'building' | 'commissioning' | 'running' | 'careAndMaintenance'; commissionedTurn: number | null; commercialTurn: number | null;
  power: { source: 'grid' | 'genset'; genIds: MachineId[] };
  tsf: { capacitySt: number; filledSt: number; lined: boolean; hidden: { tailsFineOz: number } };
  hidden: { gicOz: number } }
```

**Toll milling for others (P6e stretch).** An own mill may accept NPC ore lots (reduced form: 0–2 offers a month at the district's toll terms), filling idle capacity at the toll fee less own cost.

### 14.9 Weekly site model and bottlenecks

A hard-rock site resolves in step 9 with §7's primitives: usable hours `u(m,t)` (7.5), stage capacities, buffers, and idle-cause attribution (7.8), aggregated weekly in short tons (D-14.13). The mill runs continuously on a 4-crew rotation; the mine runs the plan's shifts. Within the week the order is fixed (mine → ROM pad → mill or toll shipment), and every stage reads only this week's upstream output plus last week's stockpiles, so there is no circular dependency.

```ts
interface HardRockSite { id: SiteId; systemId: LodeSystemId; claimIds: ClaimId[]; veinIds: VeinId[];
  status: 'exploring' | 'permitting' | 'building' | 'rampUp' | 'producing' | 'careAndMaintenance' | 'closed';
  paths: { pit: boolean; underground: boolean };
  access: { kind: 'adit' | 'decline' | null; veinId: VeinId | null; levelsJ: number[]; accessFt: number; pumping: boolean };
  pit: { floorDepthFt: Record<string /* `${veinId}|${i}` */, number>; wasteBcy: number } | null;
  plan: LodePlan; blasting: 'own' | 'contract'; contractMining: { scope: 'development' | 'all'; fromTurn: number } | null;
  rom: Stockpile; lowGrade: Stockpile; wasteDumpBcy: number;
  explosivesLb: number; detonators: number;                 // magazines are §9 site items located on the site's claims
  millId: MillId | null; tollContractIds: TollContractId[];
  lastWeek: LodeWeekResult | null }
interface Stockpile { st: number; estFineOz: number;        // the player's grade-control estimate
  hidden: { fineOz: number; stByDomain: Record<LodeDomain, number>; ozByDomain: Record<LodeDomain, number>;
            bwiSt: number; grgOz: number; refrOz: number; alloyOz: number; ozByClaim: Record<ClaimId, number> } }   // Σ st×bwi, Σ oz×grg, …
interface LodePlan { daysPerWeek: number; shiftsPerDay: number; hoursPerShift: number;
  headings: { key: string; kind: 'jackleg' | 'jumbo' | 'decline'; target: 'access' | { veinId: VeinId; j: number };
              crew: EmployeeId[]; machineIds: MachineId[] }[];
  stopes: { panelKey: string /* `${veinId}|${i}|${j}` */; method: StopeMethod; crew: EmployeeId[]; machineIds: MachineId[]; finalDraw: boolean }[];
  pit: { columns: string[]; benchFt: number; fleet: Record<MachineId, OpsRole> } | null;
  supportStandard: 'minimum' | 'standard' | 'conservative'; gradeControl: 'none' | 'visual' | 'sampled';
  cutoffOzSt: number; lowGradeOzSt: number; route: 'mill' | 'toll' | 'stockpile'; tollShipStWk: number }
type StopeMethod = 'shrinkage' | 'longhole' | 'cutAndFill' | 'resue';
interface LodeWeekResult extends Omit<WeekOpsResult, 'claimId' | 'lines'> {   // bcy fields stay 0; §13 stageRows reads `unit`;
  // a hard-rock site has no placer plant lines (§7 7.2.1), so `lines` is omitted and `cleanups` stays []
  siteId: SiteId; unit: 'st'; devFt: number; oreMinedSt: number; wasteSt: number; brokenStoredSt: number;
  oreToMillSt: number; oreShippedSt: number; millSt: number; ventRatio: number;
  calcHeadOzSt: number; calcTailOzSt: number; calcRecovery: number; pouredFineOz: number; tsfFilledSt: number;
  explosivesLbUsed: number; kWh: number }
```

```
Underground supply (st/week):
  devFt     = Σ_h devFtWk_h (14.6.2); devMuckSt = devFt × headingArea (ft²) / 12.09; drifts on the vein carry grade
              g × min(w, dw) / dw + wall share (dw = heading width, ft); devOreSt = the part whose estimated grade ≥ cutoff (to the mill),
              the rest goes to the waste dump
  stopeSt   = Σ_s min(miners_s × stPerMinerShift[m] × skillProductivityMult(s_s) × shiftsPerDay × daysPerWeek × u, drillCap_s, brokenAvailable_s)
              s_s = hours-weighted effective skill of stope s's miners (§8); drillCap_s from jackleg / longhole drill rates (§9)
              shrinkage: drawn = 0.35 × stopeSt until the stope's last slice, then the stored 0.65 (D-14.29)
  muckSt    = Σ LHD or mucker: bucketSt × 60 / cycleMin(trammingFt) × hours × u            (§9 rates; trammingFt from stope to ore pass)
  haulSt    = trucks on the decline (§7 7.6.3 cycle with ramp length, payload in st, grade 15%) | rail tram | hoist
  ventRatio = min(1, Σ fan cfm / (hardrock.vent.cfmPerHp (100) × Σ dieselHp of underground units scheduled this week))
              every diesel unit underground runs × ventRatio; the lost hours are cause 'vent' (fans are §9 'light' machines needing power)
  oreSt     = min(stopeSt + devOreSt, muckSt, haulSt) → ROM pad (st and oz by domain and claim, from the slices' true values)
Open pit supply: drilled and blasted st (drill ft/hr × st per ft), load (§7 dig with blastedDigMult), haul (§7 haul) → ore to ROM pad, waste to dump
Mill (st/week): millSt = min(ROM st + low-grade reclaim, crusherStHr × crusherHours, millStPerDay × 7,
                             powerSt, tsf.capacitySt − tsf.filledSt, waterSt)
  powerSt = millStPerDay × 7 × min(1, available kW (grid line rating or Σ genset kW × availability) / plant kW draw at that rate)
  waterSt = freshWaterGpm × 10,080 min / freshWaterGalPerSt
  each binding limit's shortfall becomes mill idle hours with its cause: 'starved' (root muck/haul/develop), 'power', 'water', 'tailings'
Toll: shipped st = min(ROM st, contract allotment − st queued at the mill, plan.tollShipStWk) in weeks with freightMode ∈ {road, trail}
```

New stages extend §7's `Stage`: `develop | drill | blast | muck | hoist | crush | grind | leach | vent`; TSF capacity reuses §7's `tailings` stage and cause, and power and water reuse §7's `power` and `water` (D-14.36). New idle causes extend `IdleCause`: `vent | explosives | reentry | tollQueue`. The Flow tab reads them with §13's `stageRows` (with `unit: 'st'`): "Mill idle 18%: crusher fed 9.5 h/day by one LHD on a 900-ft tram; +1 LHD: +210 st/week".

**Season.** Underground and the mill have `Z = 1` all year; a northern open pit runs winter at `hardrock.pit.winterMult` (0.85; blasted rock does not care about permafrost, people and trucks do) and still pays §7's weather `W`. In the north, the off-season pit is where the placer fleet earns its keep in winter, at the cost of the rebuild window §9 would otherwise use. Water is small: the mill needs `hardrock.mill.freshWaterGalPerSt` (140 gal) of fresh makeup, about 10 gpm at 100 st/day, against ~750 gpm for a 50 bcy/hr placer plant; it is still above §6's 3.5-gpm authorization threshold, so a mill needs `st.waterUse`. *Trade-off:* year-round ounces and a flat cash curve (lenders like it, §11 11.15) against fixed costs that never stop: no laying off a mill crew in winter.

**Underground care and maintenance.** `mine/setSiteStatus('careAndMaintenance')` stops development and stoping: the site costs `hardrock.ug.cmUsdWk` ($9,000: dewatering, fans at low speed, caretakers, the mine-rescue contract) and every stope with broken ore keeps its sterilization clock running. A flooded decline (pumping stopped > 4 weeks below the water table) needs `hardrock.ug.dewaterWeeks` (6) of pumping before work resumes.

### 14.10 Permits and safety (a §6 and §8 extension)

Permit types are rows in §6's catalog, run by §6's pipeline (6.5), conditions, bonds, inspections and standing, using §6's existing `PipelineStage` values (no new stage kinds). Year-1 USD.

| `PermitTypeId` | Agency | Required when | Fee / direct / baseline | Desk / field wk | Stages: median wk (σ) [min–max] | Incomplete / info / deny / clean / contest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fed.noticeLode` | land | lode exploration ≤ 5 ac; bulk sample < 1,000 st | as `fed.notice` | 2 / 0 | completeness fixed 2 | 0.15 / — / 0 / 1.0 / 0 |
| `fed.planLode` (EA) | land | any lode mining or milling; scope flags `pit`, `underground`, `mill`, `cyanide`, `tsf` | 120,000 / 30,000 / 150,000 | 26 / 40 | completeness 6 (0.35) [3–16]; publicComment fixed 5; technicalReview 40 (0.5) [16–130]; decision 4 (0.4) | 0.35 / 0.65 / 0.08 / 0.05 / 0.12 |
| `fed.planLode` (EIS: `cyanide` with TSF > 40 ac, or sensitivity > 0.6, or special status, or > 160 ac) | land | as above | 600,000 / 100,000 / 400,000 | 40 / 60 | completeness 8; publicComment fixed 16 (draft-EIS 8 + final 8); technicalReview 130 (0.35) [80–260]; decision 8 | 0.30 / 0.75 / 0.12 / 0.03 / 0.30 |
| `fed.explosives` (§6's stub id, refined to the ATF user permit) | explosives | own blasting | 100 (renewal $50) / 1,000 / 0 | 1 / 0 | technicalReview labelled "ATF background check" 13 (0.3) [6–26] (responsible persons and employee possessors); term 156 wk | 0.10 / 0.10 / 0.02 / 1.0 / 0 |
| `st.blasterCert` (per blaster) | safety (state mine inspector) | each blaster employee | 150 + course 1,200 | — | fixed 4; pass p = 0.5 + 0.005 × skill | — |
| `st.airPermit` (minor source) | air (new `AgencyKey`) | crushing, milling, gensets > 500 kW | 8,000 / 2,000 / 0 | 3 / 0 | technicalReview 14 (0.4) [6–40] | 0.15 / 0.30 / 0.03 / 0.40 / 0.02 |
| `st.waterPollutionControl` (zero-discharge process facility) | water | any mill; mandatory with cyanide | 60,000 / 15,000 / 80,000 | 16 / 20 | publicComment fixed 4; technicalReview 30 (0.5) [12–78] | 0.30 / 0.55 / 0.06 / 0.10 / 0.08 |
| `st.reclamation`, `fed.mineId`, `st.waterUse` | as §6 | as §6; `fed.mineId` gains `underground: boolean` | as §6 | | | |
| ICMC certification (voluntary) | — | — | audit $80,000 + $20,000/yr | — | fixed 12 | lowers `water` inspection rate ×0.6; required by the project lender with cyanide |

**Agencies.** Names come from §6 6.1's `air` and `explosives` rows through `agencyFor` (D-6.1): explosives are the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) in the U.S. districts and Natural Resources Canada's Explosives Regulatory Division in Yukon; air permits are the Alaska DEC Air Permits Program, NDEP's Bureau of Air Pollution Control in Nevada, or the Yukon Department of Environment; mine safety is MSHA (Yukon: WSCB).

**Conditions.** A lode plan adds `maxTsfSt`, `maxMillStPerDay`, `cyanideMonitoring` (weekly WAD-cyanide sampling $400 while leaching; quarterly reports as `Obligation`s), `blastingHours`, and the usual disturbance cap. Exceeding `maxMillStPerDay` is a §6 exceedance like any limit.

**Activities.** §6's `ActivityKind` gains `blast` (any detonation: needs `fed.explosives` and a blaster, or a contractor), `underground` (development or stoping: plan with `underground` scope, Mine ID with `underground: true`, Part 48 Subpart A crew, mine rescue), `mill` (crushing and grinding: plan with `mill` scope, `st.airPermit`, `st.waterPollutionControl`, `st.waterUse`) and `leach` (cyanide: plan with `cyanide` scope and `cyanideMonitoring`). Lode `strip` and `mine` reuse §6's kinds on lode claims with `pit` scope.

**Bonds.** §6's RCE gains disturbance types and per-acre rates (direct, north / arid; then §6's access multiplier, mobilization and 45% indirects):

| Type | North | Arid | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsf` | $45,000/ac | $38,000/ac | cover, regrade, drain-down |
| `millSite` | $600,000 per 100 st/day + $15,000/ac | $550,000 + $14,000/ac | demolition and decontamination |
| `wasteRock` | $9,000/ac | $8,000/ac | |
| `openPit` | $3,500/ac | $3,000/ac | berms, safety, highwall |
| `portal` | $40,000 each | $40,000 | plug and seal |
| long-term water treatment | `hardrock.rce.waterTreatmentUsd` (1,500,000) × pagFactor (once sulfide is mined or a TSF exists) | same | revealed `pagFactor` from a `metTest`; else the template prior |

*Worked example.* Underground mine with a 100 st/day CIL mill on a northern seasonal road: TSF 12 ac $540k, mill $660k, waste rock 6 ac $54k, portal $40k, roads 5 ac $8k, water treatment 0.5 × $1.5M = $750k: direct $2.05M × 1.15 access + mobilization, × 1.45 = **$3.44M**.

**Mine safety (MSHA in the U.S. districts; Yukon's WSCB in Yukon, §6 6.1).** An underground mine is inspected `hardrock.safety.ugInspectionsPerYear` (4.0) times a year against 2.0 for surface (§6 6.10 base rate; R1, MSHA), with citation mean μ base 6.0 (more standards: ground control, ventilation, escapeways, explosives). §6's weekly rate divides the annual base by `expectedActiveWeeks`; a year-round hard-rock site (any underground work, or a mill) uses 52 instead of the district's ≈ 22 placer weeks, otherwise 4/yr would become ≈ 9.5 (D-14.40). An open pit uses the surface 2.0 over the weeks it actually ran. Underground miners need **Part 48 Subpart A** training: 40 hours before any underground assignment (8 at the mine), 8-hour annual refresher; experienced underground hires need 8 hours. §8 schedules it (contractor $1,200 per new underground miner). A contracted mine-rescue arrangement (`hardrock.safety.mineRescueUsdYr` $40,000) and self-rescuers ($1,000 per underground worker) are gates for underground work (`MINE_RESCUE_REQUIRED`). Injury hazard for underground hours × `hardrock.safety.ugInjuryMult` (1.8) × ground class (good 0.8, fair 1.0, poor 1.4) × support standard (14.6.3); §8 runs the rolls with new `M_role` values: `ugMiner` 1.4, `blaster` 1.4, `millOperator` 1.1, `assayer` 0.5, `metallurgist` 0.4.

| `gen1000` [`generator`] | 1 MW diesel genset | 750 kW continuous | 450 | 180 | 55 gph at 75% load (0.073 gal/kWh) | light |

The **mill** itself (CIL tanks, elution, electrowinning, detox, buildings, foundations, EPCM) is a capital project, not a machine (D-14.19): modules above are §9 machines inside it for wear and spares. Installed anchors: **gravity-only 100 st/day $3.5M; gravity + CIL 100 st/day $11M; 250 st/day $19M; 300 st/day ≈ $21.3M** (0.6 scaling exponent); a TSF and a power line (`hardrock.power.lineUsdPerMi` $150,000, grid only within 10 mi of a highway town) on top. A new §9 family `underground` (components engine, hydraulics, tires, drivetrain, electrical, structure; hazard ×1.2 for the environment) and `mill` (components `liners`, `drivetrain`, `electrical`, `structure`; `liners` is a new `ComponentKey`) are needed. §9 wear receives `GroundCtx.rock = true` for pit and underground work.

**Staff extension** (§8 roles; wages are northern base before burden):

| Role | Job | Base | Pay | Required for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ugMiner` | development and stoping crew: drill, blast-assist, muck, bolt, run underground machines | $42/hr | hourly | underground (crews per heading 14.6.2; stopes by `stPerMinerShift`) |
| `blaster` | loads and fires rounds; magazine custody; ATF employee possessor; state certificate | $44/hr | hourly | each shift that blasts (own blasting) |
| `millOperator` | crushing, grinding, CIL on shift; 4-crew rotation for 24/7 | $38/hr | hourly | own mill (3 per shift at 100 st/day CIL, 2 gravity-only) |
| `metallurgist` | process control, testwork, recovery skill | $125k/yr | salary | CIL mill (gravity-only: optional) |
| `assayer` | runs the on-site lab | $72k/yr | salary | `assayLab` |
| `foreman` with `underground` trait (shift boss) | supervises one underground shift | §8 base | salary | each underground shift |

Cross-role cover: operator → `ugMiner` (mucking and trucks only) at −15; `plantOperator` → `millOperator` at −10; `driller` → `ugMiner` (drilling only) at −10. Workers' comp is §11's: its per-jurisdiction `wcRates` gain `underground` = `finance.wc.undergroundMult` (2.4) × `mining` (AK-style $18.00, NV-style $9.60, temperate $14.40 per $100) and `mill` = 0.8 × `mining`, and §8's `wcClass` gains `'underground' | 'mill'` (R4/R5 class magnitudes [U]). Underground miner wages ripple with gold at elasticity 0.4 (lag 13), above placer labor's 0.3: the underground labor pool is thin. A 100 st/day underground mine with its own CIL mill runs ~40–45 people year-round.

### 14.12 Finance (a §11 extension)

**Capital projects.** Contracted portals, adits and declines, mills, TSFs, TSF raises and power lines are `CapitalProject`s with a budget, a schedule and an overrun drawn at award on `rng(seed,'hr-capex',projectId)`: `costMult` = LN(`hardrock.capex.overrunMed` 1.10, 0.15), `scheduleMult` = LN(1.15, 0.20). A lump-sum turnkey contract costs +15% and caps `costMult` at 1.05 (`hardrock.capex.lstkPremium`, `lstkCap`). *Trade-off:* pay certainty up front or carry the overrun risk.

```
weekly progress (step 6) Δp = 1 / (weeksPlanned × scheduleMult); the week's draw = budget × costMult × Δp is billed in step 14
  a draw that finance.pay could not pay in full in last week's step 14 stops progress this week (status 'stalled'; no circular
  dependency inside a week), costs hardrock.capex.standbyShare (0.004) × budget per week, and after 8 stalled weeks the contractor
  demobilizes (restart = +5% of budget and 4 weeks)
EAC shown at p ∈ {0.25, 0.50, 0.75}: budget × costMult × LNmean(1, 0.10 × (1 − p)) on rng(seed,'hr-capex',projectId,'eac',p)   // sharpens toward truth
commissioning: mill and TSF projects end at p = 1 with status 'commissioning'; the mill's ramp (14.8.2) starts then
```

```ts
interface CapitalProject { id: CapProjectId; kind: 'adit' | 'decline' | 'portal' | 'mill' | 'millExpansion' | 'tsf' | 'tsfRaise' | 'powerLine';
  siteId: SiteId; spec: Record<string, number | string>; contract: 'reimbursable' | 'lstk';
  budgetCents: Cents; spentCents: Cents; progress: number; weeksPlanned: number; startTurn: number; stalledWeeks: number;
  hidden: { costMult: number; scheduleMult: number }; eac: { atProgress: number; cents: Cents }[];
  status: 'planned' | 'building' | 'stalled' | 'commissioning' | 'done' }
```

**Accounting.** Construction posts to `ppe.cip` (construction in progress) and moves to `ppe.equipment` at commissioning; pre-production development (access, levels, and own-crew headings before commercial production) to `mineral.development`. **Commercial production** is declared when the mill runs at ≥ 60% of rated for 4 consecutive weeks (a toll-only site: the first 13 weeks of shipments); until then mill operating costs net of gold sales are capitalized (the older U.S. practice; IFRS since 2022 books the sales as revenue, a simplification recorded in D-14.20). After it, capitalized development depletes on units of production (fine oz poured ÷ reserve, or measured + indicated oz without a PFS), and sustaining development is capitalized and depleted the same way. New accounts `exp.explosives`, `exp.reagents`, `exp.power`, `exp.tollMilling` (fees and TC), `exp.trucking`.

**Financing options** (lenders are §11 data, run by §11's appetite, covenant and distress machinery):

| Product | Lender kind | Gates | Terms | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Project loan | `projectFinance` (new) | PFS ≤ 104 wk; plan, WPCP and air permits approved; equity ≥ 40% of capex funded first; ICMC if cyanide; an offtake with a refiner | ≤ 60% of capex; prime + 5.0%; 2.5% arrangement fee; 6 yr incl. 18 mo grace; DSCR ≥ 1.30; 6-month debt-service reserve in `cash.restricted.dsra`; hedge ≥ 50% of ounces over the tenor (§10 forwards); completion test (90% of rated for 13 weeks) with a full owner guarantee until passed | cheapest money, heaviest strings |
| Pre-production stream | `royaltyCo` | `lodeTRS` + `pea`; plan approved | deposit D ≤ 35% of capex in construction tranches; stream share solved from the deposit (below), clamped to 4–25% of payable gold for life of mine (no offer above 25%); ongoing payment 20% of spot; §11 11.12 accounting | no repayment schedule, permanent take |
| NSR royalty sale | `royaltyCo` | `lodeTRS` | §11 11.12 royalty sale on basis NSR (14.17) | small, simple, forever |
| Offtake prepay | `bullion` (the refiner; §11 adds the prepay product to this kind) | production ≥ 13 weeks | §11 prepay: up to 26 weeks of output at 1.20 annual discount | bridges ramp-up cash |
| Equipment finance | as §11 | — | underground and mill machines as collateral | |

```
streamShare = D / Σ_t ( Q_t × hardrock.finance.preProdStream.haircut (0.8) × (P − 0.20 × P) × (1 + irr)^(−t) )
  Q_t = the PEA's P50 payable fine oz in year t of its schedule (t in years from the first tranche, construction years included at 0)
  P = standard-case price (§4 D-4.27); irr = hardrock.finance.preProdStream.irr (0.18), R5's 12–20%+ for small producers
```

*Example (R3, 14.13).* D = 35% × $22M = $7.7M; Q = 6,440 oz/yr in years 3–10 (end-of-year discounting, annuity factor 2.93 at 18%); P = $4,200: each 1% of payable gold is worth 0.01 × 5,152 × $3,360 × 2.93 = $0.51M, so the streamer asks **≈ 15.2%** of payable gold. Raising less (D = $4M) cuts the take to ≈ 7.9%.

Equity investors (§11 11.13) credit lode value only from a TRS or PFS, as for placer.

### 14.13 Economics anchors and the BALANCE extension

| Anchor | Default (year-1 USD, $4,200 gold) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Small-mine diluted head grade | 3–10 g/t (0.09–0.29 oz/st); vein in shoots 8–30 g/t | R3 conversions; industry practice [U] |
| Recovery | CIL oxide 92–96%; free-milling sulfide 85–92%; refractory 30–60%; gravity-only 35–65% | [U] |
| Underground mining cost | $95–245/st by method, incl. stope development | Costmine development $/m (2024); small-mine opex $143/t [web] |
| Open-pit cost | $3.5–5/st moved (own fleet); contract drill and blast $2.10/st | §7/§9 fleet costs; [U] |
| Own mill opex | 100 st/day $55–75/st; 250 st/day $38–50/st; gravity-only $30–40/st | 911Metallurgist [web]; [U] |
| Toll | $100–180/dry st + $0.20/st-mi trucking | Nevada toll agreement at $148.50/st incl. trucking [web] |
| Mill capex | gravity 100 st/day $3.5M; gravity + CIL 100 st/day $11M; 250 st/day $19M; 300 st/day ≈ $21M (0.6 exponent); used 100 st/day plant ≈ $1M before installation | [web], [U] |
| Development | jackleg $650–900/ft; jumbo $1,300–1,600/ft; decline $1,700–2,200/ft | Costmine C$6,650/m all-in (2024) |
| Permits | lode EA 15–30 months from filing; EIS 36–72; ATF ~13 weeks | §6 calibration; ATF |
| Bonds | $0.4M (pit + toll) to $3–6M (mill + TSF) | §6 RCE method |

**Three reference projects** (the hard-rock analogues of the reference placer operation):

| | R1 oxide pit + toll purchase | R2 small underground + toll service | R3 underground + own 100 st/day CIL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ore / yr | 20,000 wet st (toll allotment 400 st/wk) | 20,000 wet st, shrinkage | 35,000 st (350 days) |
| Head / recovery | 0.09 oz/st, payable 0.85 | 0.211 oz/st, 0.92 | 0.20 oz/st, 0.92 |
| Fine oz (payable or poured) / revenue | 1,469 payable oz / $6.1M | 3,766 oz / $15.7M | 6,440 oz / $26.8M |
| Cash costs | mining $0.6M (strip 6:1); TC $2.7M; trucking $0.3M (60 haul mi); G&A $0.6M; NSR 3% $0.2M = **$4.4M** | mining $3.0M; toll $2.9M; trucking $0.3M; G&A $1.4M; NSR $0.5M = **$8.1M** | mining $4.9M; milling $2.3M; G&A $2.2M; NSR $0.8M = **$10.2M** |
| Sustaining capital | $0.1M (haul road, dump) | $0.8M (levels, raises, vent) | $1.5M (levels, ramp, TSF raise, mill sustaining) |
| Margin after sustaining / AISC | $1.6M / $3,060 per oz | $6.8M / $2,350 per oz | $15.1M / $1,820 per oz |
| Capital | $1.5–2.5M (reuses the placer fleet) | $7–9M | $20–25M |
| Time to first gold | 18–30 months | 24–36 months | 36–72 months |

Against the reference placer operation's ≈ $0.6–1.0M operating margin, R1 earns about two placer seasons a year, R2 about eight and R3 about nineteen, with ten times the capital and three times the wait. R1 is an arid-highway case: a northern site 250 haul miles from the hub pays ≈ $52/st to truck ore and R1's margin falls to ≈ $0.9M, which is why northern lode projects lean toward their own mill. These are good-class deposits; most targets are worse, and grade reconciliation, dilution and the sulfide transition are where real projects fail.

**BALANCE extension.** Add a `hardrock` module to the preflight model and simulator:
- generate lode systems on 40 districts per template; compute `refEconomicsLode` per system for each path (R1–R3 cost structures, capex $2M / $8M / $22M, mining every panel with a positive margin at its method's diluted grade) and classify on CDV, the NPV at `hardrock.balance.discountRate` (0.08) of the best path's pre-tax cash flows (capex over the path's build years, margin after sustaining at $4,200, the path's RCE as closure cost in the last year): excellent ≥ $25M, good ≥ $6M, marginal > 0, else uneconomic; **target shares (uneconomic / marginal / good / excellent) 65–78 / 15–25 / 5–10 / 0.5–2.5%**;
- a `hardrockSeeker` bot (cautious placer bot that pursues hard rock once `develop` is ready) on 500 seeds × 10 years; **targets:** 35–55% of fully explored targets (indicated) reach production; 25–45% of projects in production fail to repay capital within 5 years; median realized/estimated grade 0.75–0.95; hard rock does not raise year-2 survival by more than 2 points (`develop` needs a plan-tier placer season, so only a Notice bulk sample is reachable before year 3); in the strategy-dominance matrix, `hardrockSeeker` must not beat the best placer strategy's median year-10 net worth by more than 2× (14.20).

Route `#/mine/:siteId/:tab`, nav group Operations, shown once `readiness.explore` is true (§13 hides unbuilt nav). It reuses §13's Operations patterns (header with status, authority and risk chips; plan editor with preview; stage bars; production and reconciliation charts):

| Tab | Content |
|---|---|
| Overview | readiness checklist; site status (exploring, permitting, building, ramp-up, producing, care-and-maintenance); capital projects with EAC; permits and bonds summary |
| Long section | vein-plane heat map (strike × depth) with layers: grade P50 (hatching by uncertainty as §4 4.14), width, accumulation, domain (oxide / transition / sulfide, as known), class, pierce points by method, development, stopes by status, sterilized panels; pit outline on the same view |
| Plan | stope sequence and method per stope; headings; shifts; support standard; grade control and cutoff; ore routing (mill / toll / stockpile); blasting (own / contract); preview with §7-style expected tons, ounces and $/st (visible model only) |

| Production | weekly st and oz; mine-to-mill reconciliation (estimated vs calculated head vs poured); cost per st mined and milled; AISC per oz |

Long-section clicks open a panel quick view with its estimate and the explain tree (`explain.panelEstimate`). Alerts: `hr.explosivesLow` (< 2 weeks of cover), `hr.tsfFull` (< 8 weeks), `hr.ventLimit`, `hr.tollAllotmentCut`, `hr.recoveryDrop` (calculated recovery −5 points over 4 weeks), `hr.capexOverrun` (EAC > budget × 1.1).

Trade-offs, one line each:
- **Discovery hints vs records:** a records review is cheap and finds the old-timers' prospects, which are usually staked (a listing to buy); chasing quartz-attached gold needs a geologist and placer work near the creek head, but it finds blind systems that are mostly open ground ($200 a claim).
- **RC vs core:** RC is half the price and fast; core gives true width and metallurgy, without which nothing reaches indicated.
- **Soil lines vs blind drilling:** a soil line costs a few thousand dollars and finds the trace; drilling a blind vein without it costs 1.6× the footage.
- **fa30 vs metallic screens:** $75 more per sample buys out the lab nugget on coarse-gold ore.
- **QA/QC:** +12% assay cost; without it the lab bias stays hidden and no report can say indicated.
- **Bulk sample:** a Notice and a toll test lot of up to 999 st pin the grade, and the gold is sold.
- **Pit vs underground:** a pit reuses the placer fleet and starts fast, but strip ratios explode with depth on narrow veins.
- **Adit vs decline:** an adit is cheaper and drains itself but needs a hillside; a decline takes trucks anywhere and needs pumping.
- **Method choice:** selective methods cost more per ton and less per ounce on narrow veins.
- **Support standard:** saving on bolts buys dilution and injuries.
- **Own vs contract blasting or mining:** permits, magazines and crews against a markup.
- **Ore purchase vs toll service:** cash in 4 weeks with no recovery risk, against ~8 more points of value later and with risk.
- **Toll vs own mill:** no capital and no cyanide permit, against $100+ per ton more and an allotment cap.
- **Grind:** throughput against recovery; depends on whether the mill or the ore runs out first.
- **Gravity-only first:** a cheap, fast mill and permit now; the gold left in the tailings waits for a leach plant later.
- **LSTK vs reimbursable construction:** +15% for a capped overrun.
- **Project loan vs stream:** cheap debt with hedging, completion guarantees and covenants, against a permanent share of gold.

### 14.18 Phase plan

Everything here is optional P6 work, after the P6 regime, delegation and JV items. Each sub-step ends playable.
- **P6c — exploration and toll milling.** Lode generation and parcels; discovery (placer hints, records, listings, site visits, soil lines); lode claims and millsites; lode methods, fire assays, metallic screens, QA/QC and lab bias; `estimateLode` and classes; `lodeTRS`; `fed.noticeLode` bulk samples through toll test lots; `fed.planLode` with `pit` scope (EA path); oxide open pit with the placer fleet and contract drill-and-blast (own blasting with the ATF permit optional); toll mills with both contract forms; NSR royalty sales. **Stubs:** no underground, no own mill; mill recovery used only inside toll service; no competitor lode activity.
- **P6d — underground.** Adit and decline projects; development and all four stoping methods; LHD, jumbo, rail, trucks and ventilation; own explosives and magazines; underground staff, Part 48 Subpart A and underground inspections; contract mining; sterilization; `pea`.
- **P6e — own mill.** Gravity and gravity + CIL mills as capital projects; Bond throughput, grind, recovery by domain, gold in circuit, ramp-up; TSF; WPCP, air permit and ICMC; mill bonds and water-treatment provision; `pfs`; project finance, pre-production stream and offtake; NPC toll ore (stretch).

### 14.20 Balance levers and risks

**Levers that most affect outcomes:** `tpl.lode.gMedOzSt` and `shootLog` (how many targets are economic); `deWijsAlpha` and `faAliquotCvRef` (how expensive certainty is); `toll.allotmentStWk` and toll fees (how far the low-capital path goes); `mill.capexUsd` and `capex.overrunMed` (the big bet); `planLode` review times and `unlock` gates (when hard rock becomes reachable); `ug.method` dilution and costs; `mill.Lrefr` and `refractoryMed` (the sulfide trap); `discovery.hintBase` and `world.blindLogit` (how often the hint path finds open ground).

**Dominance risk.** At $4,200 gold a good small underground mine earns several times a placer operation (14.13). That is real, and it is the reward for a long, capital-hungry climb. Counters, all built in: rarity (≈ 10% of systems good or better); discovery needs placer work at the creek head plus a geologist; readiness gates; two to five years of permitting; capital of $7–25M with overrun risk; nugget-driven grade reconciliation (drill-based P50 carries σ ≈ 1 per panel, so 25–45% of projects should disappoint); dilution and sterilization; the sulfide transition; and fixed year-round costs that keep burning when the mill is down. If `hardrockSeeker` beats the best placer bot's median year-10 net worth by more than 2×, raise `planLode` technical-review medians and `capex.overrunMed` first, then lower `toll.allotmentStWk`.

**Exploits and counters.**
1. **Notice bulk sample on a bonanza shoot** (999 st at 1 oz/st ≈ $4M with no Plan; a 1-oz/st panel is ≈ 3% of in-shoot panels, so the typical windfall is 999 st at 0.3 ≈ $1M before toll costs). Real and legal once; §6's serial-notice rule (one per 104 weeks per claim group) and the toll test-lot minimum keep it a one-off windfall that also pins the estimate. Watch its frequency in the simulator.
2. **High-grading** the best panels only: sterilization (26 weeks) and the 1.5× re-development cost make skipped ore expensive to come back for.
3. **Ore purchase to dodge recovery risk on refractory lots:** mills refuse or penalize refractory lots, and payable recovery for sulfide is 0.70.
4. **Typing a high planning price** to inflate a TRS: reports use the standard case (§4 D-4.27).
5. **Gravity-only mill then never leaching:** legitimate (lower permit burden); the tailings gold is real deferred value but needs the full CIL permit later.
6. **Shrinkage cash lag ignored by bots:** the 65% of broken ore stored in stopes must show in `projectLodeVisible` or forecasts overstate cash.
7. **Re-rolling discovery:** records rolls are keyed on (creek, system), so repeat reviews return the same answer; pans never roll hints (only pits, trenches, bulk samples and cleanups, which cost real money).
8. **Skipping the own assay:** saves $60 a lot and pays the mill's hidden ≈ −1.5% bias on every settlement; legitimate, and a visible QA/QC choice.
9. **Staking every lode parcel in a district blind:** staking needs a revealed system (`LODE_TARGET_UNKNOWN`), and each claim costs $200 a year with the waiver capped at 10 claims (§6).

**Risks.** Save size (panels ≈ 0.1 MB) and performance (`resolveLodeSiteWeek` < 1 ms; it is weekly-aggregated). Scope creep: flotation concentrates, heap leach, roasting and autoclaves are out (refractory ore is a recovery penalty or a toll refusal, not a new circuit). The section is longer than a sketch because every number the P6 simulator needs is pinned here; the P6c sub-step uses about a third of it.

### 14.21 Tests

**Formula unit tests (Vitest).**
- Lode claim area 1,500 × 600 / 43,560 = 20.661 ac; 1 oz/st = 34.2857 g/t; SG 2.65 ⇒ 12.090 ft³/st and 2.233 st/bcy.
- Panel 50 × 50 × 3.5 ft = 723.7 st; at 0.33 oz/st 238.8 oz.
- Dilution table 14.6.3: shrinkage 0.2111 oz/st, 966.7 st, 204.1 oz; longhole 0.1376, 1,581.9, 217.7; cut-and-fill 0.1938, 1,178.7, 228.4; resue 0.2891, 760.9, 220.0 (± 0.1%). Mining $/st 144.7 / 99.2 / 183.8 / 238.2.
- Pit slices (w 10 ft, dip 70°, α 45°, cover 0): strips 4.70 / 14.10 / 23.50; with cover 10 ft the first slice's ore is 40 × 10.64 = 425.7 ft² and its strip 6.12.
- Hole geometry: panel j = 3, dip 70°, cover 50 ft, holeDip 60° ⇒ depth 214.4 ft, hole 277.6 ft; a 4-ft vein gives 5.22 ft of core.
- Placer hints: p_hint 0.134 (10-bcy pit, 9 coarse colours, 0.5 mi) and 0.1246 (cleanup, 1 mi).
- `grindFactor`: 75 µm 0.8257, 106 µm 1.0000, 150 µm 1.2168; Bond specific energy at BWi 14, 106 µm = 12.16 kWh/st; billed grinding energy (110 kW, load 0.85) 27.2 / 22.4 / 18.4 kWh/st at 75 / 106 / 150 µm.
- Recovery (vein grg 0.55, 106 µm, skill 55): gravity-only oxide 0.4400; oxide CIL 0.9639; sulfide refr 0.10 0.8730; refr 0.60 0.6010; refr 0.95 0.4107; grind example (refr 0.10) 0.8978 / 0.8730 / 0.8377 at 75 / 106 / 150 µm; no metallurgist on oxide CIL 0.9572.
- Toll settlement example: ore purchase net $556,066 ± $5 at settle head 0.2486; toll service R_toll 0.9336, recovered 179.24 oz, net $618,891 ± $5; no own assay ⇒ settle at the mill assay.
- Measurement: fieldCv 0.486 ± 0.005 for the 14.4 example; total log-variance 1.00 ± 0.02; bulk 500 st σL 0.15; a sample at or above panel tonnage has σL² = 0.
- Development: jackleg 2 shifts × 6 days at u 0.85 = 56.1 ft/week.
- Bond example $3.44M ± $0.01M.
- Readiness tiers on fixture companies (R 44 / 45, S 49 / 50, plan seasons 0 / 1, net worth below and above, profitable seasons 1 / 2).
- §6 fee units: a 20.66-ac lode claim and a 5-ac millsite each bill 1 unit ($200).
- Pre-production stream (R3 example): share 15.2% ± 0.2 at D $7.7M; 7.9% at D $4M; an implied share above 25% returns no offer.
- §6 MSHA (safety agency) weekly rate for a year-round underground site: 4.0 / 52 per week before multipliers.

**Property tests (fast-check).**
- Fine-gold conservation per site (±1e-6 oz): vein + wall gold in broken panels = ore delivered + ore misrouted to waste + broken ore left in stopes; ore delivered = mill feed + toll lots shipped + Δ ROM pad + Δ low-grade stockpile; mill feed = poured + Δ gold in circuit + tailings; poured = in-kind interests + lots (per source claim); toll lots = toll-service doré + campaign loss + toll tailings, or ore-purchase payable + the mill's retained share.
- Every generated panel has grg ≤ 1 − refractoryShare, and every recovery lies in [0, 0.99].
- Slice factors renormalize: Σ of a panel's 4 slices = panel truth exactly.
- Stream isolation: adding lode generation leaves every placer `truthHash` identical; toll, blast and capex draws never change ops or price streams; slice factors depend on (vein, panel) only, not on the site or the week; a second records review of a creek returns the same reveal.
- Monotonicity: recovery rises with finer P80 and falls with refractory share; throughput falls with BWi; strip rises with slice depth.
- The mill never processes more than TSF room; cash moves only through `finance.pay`/`post`; selectors never expose `hidden` vein fields.

**Simulator tests (200 worlds, standard).** Lode class shares within 65–78 / 15–25 / 5–10 / 0.5–2.5%; reference projects R1–R3 cash costs within ±15% of 14.13; `hardrockSeeker` targets of 14.13; P1–P5 BALANCE results unchanged with `game.hardRockEnabled` false.

### 14.22 Decisions

- **D-14.1** — Hard rock is a switchable optional track (`game.hardRockEnabled`, on in the P6 sandbox) whose content is always generated. — Keeps worlds identical whether or not a player uses it, and lets scenarios exclude it.
- **D-14.2** — Lode truth is generated at `newGame` on `'world','lode'` sub-streams, packed and immutable like §3 (D-3.1); older saves gain it at the P6 migration from the stored seed and `genParams`. — Placer truth stays byte-identical, and estimates can rely on immutability.
- **D-14.3** — Geology is a vein-plane grid of 50 × 50 ft panels with a true width, not 3D cubes; a cube view is derived. — Refines the suggested 25 ft / 10 m cubes: a vein is tabular, so cubes waste storage on barren rock (≈ 5 kB per vein instead of ≈ 50 kB+), and 50 ft matches sublevel spacing, so a panel is a stope.
- **D-14.4** — Hard-rock mass is in short tons and grade in fine oz Au per short ton (fire-assay basis), shown also in g/t; placer stays raw oz per bcy. — U.S. toll and mine contracts are in short tons; assays measure fine gold, so no raw/fine ambiguity arises before the doré.
- **D-14.5** — Lode claims are pre-generated 1,500 × 600 ft parcels (20.66 ac) at $200 per claim; millsites 5 ac at $200; no association lode claims. — 1872 law and BLM's per-claim lode fee (R1, BLM).
- **D-14.6** — Extralateral (apex) rights are not modeled; panels belong to the claim covering their strike interval. — Real but litigation-heavy; it adds nothing to owner-level decisions.
- **D-14.7** — Readiness gates: reputation 45, standing 50 and one plan-tier placer season to develop; for a mill, company net worth $1.5M (real) or two profitable years. — A design choice, not a model of agencies: §6 would deny only ≈ 10–15% of plans filed at low standing, so without the gate filing early is a cheap lottery. The gates make graduation legible, keep the track late-game, and stand in for the one real hard rule (operators on the non-compliance list are refused).
- **D-14.8** — Lode estimation reuses §4's estimator on log grade and log width over the vein plane, with ore-shoot hypotheses in place of paystreak hypotheses. — One statistics engine, one explain tree, one set of tests.
- **D-14.9** — `indicated` needs QA/QC and nugget control (metallic screens or a bulk sample); `measured` needs development exposure; reserves need a PFS. — CIM / S-K 1300 practice for narrow nuggety veins.
- **D-14.10** — The lab adds a 30-g aliquot nugget term and a hidden per-lab bias found only with QA/QC standards. — Real, cheap to model, and it gives QA/QC a visible payoff.
- **D-14.11** — Dilution is min mining width + overbreak by method and ground class, diluting at a per-vein wall-rock grade. — The standard narrow-vein dilution model; four numbers per method.
- **D-14.12** — Open pits use a closed-form trapezoid per 50-ft slice and per foot of strike. — Explainable and fast; narrow-vein pits really are shallow trenches.
- **D-14.13** — The site resolves as a weekly-aggregated stage model in short tons on §7's usable-hours and idle primitives, not §7's hour-block loop. — A continuous mill with stockpile buffers has no meaningful hour-to-hour starvation; this keeps the cost < 1 ms while the bottleneck view is unchanged.
- **D-14.14** — Mill throughput follows Bond's law with ore BWi and the chosen P80. — Gives the grind trade-off and the hardness-by-domain effect from one formula.
- **D-14.15** — Recovery = gravity-recoverable × gravity efficiency + leach of the free and refractory remainders by domain, with grind locking and §8's skill as a loss exponent (as §7 D-7.3). — Small closed form; reproduces 92–96% oxide, 85–92% free-milling sulfide, 40–60% refractory and 35–65% gravity-only.
- **D-14.16** — Toll milling has two contract forms, weekly allotments, a minimum lot, settlement assays with a splitting limit and an umpire, and a hidden mill bias. — How custom mills work (Nevada toll agreements); the allotment is what makes an own mill worth building.
- **D-14.17** — Refines §6's `fed.explosives` stub ($200, 156 wk) to ATF's user permit, keeping the id: $100 initial, $50 renewal, 3-year term, ≈ 13 weeks for background checks run as a `technicalReview` stage. — ATF fee schedule; extending the stub instead of adding `fed.explosivesUser` keeps one permit id and §6's stage enum unchanged.
- **D-14.18** — Underground mines: MSHA-style inspections 4/yr (surface 2) and Part 48 Subpart A training of 40 h before assignment. — Mine Act §103(a) and 30 CFR 48.5.
- **D-14.19** — Mills, TSFs, portals and declines are capital projects with hidden overrun and schedule multipliers; mill modules are §9 machines inside them for wear. — Construction risk is a real decision (LSTK vs reimbursable) and does not fit §9's buy-a-machine flow.
- **D-14.20** — Pre-production development and construction are capitalized; commercial production at 60% of rated for 4 weeks; pre-commercial mill costs are capitalized net of gold sales; capitalized costs deplete on units of production. — Older U.S. mining practice, simplified (IFRS now books pre-production sales as revenue); keeps the IS from showing a fake loss during construction and needs one switch.
- **D-14.21** — Toll allotments of 150–600 st per week cap the toll path at ~8–30k st/yr. — Custom mills are capacity-limited; without the cap toll milling would dominate own mills.
- **D-14.22** — In P6 no AI competitor mines hard rock; competitors may hold and sell lode claims; NPC ore lots feed only the player's own mill. — Keeps §12's reduced-form competitors unchanged.
- **D-14.23** — Panels skipped beside mined neighbours sterilize after 26 weeks and cost 1.5× to re-develop. — The real cost of high-grading in one rule.
- **D-14.24** — Underground and mills have no season factor; a northern pit runs winter at 0.85. — Year-round production is the track's core appeal; the counterweight is year-round fixed cost.
- **D-14.25** — The lode Notice bulk-sample cap is 1,000 short tons (statutory), one per 104 weeks per claim group (§6's serial rule). — 43 CFR 3809 states tons; the placer bcy conversion does not apply to rock.
- **D-14.26** — Underground wages: miner $42/hr, blaster $44/hr (northern base); underground WC = 2.4 × §11's mining rate ($18 per $100 AK-style), mill 0.8 ×. — Above placer operator anchors ($36) because the underground pool is thin; WC stays in §11's jurisdiction table instead of a §8 constant; R4/R5 class-rate magnitudes [U].
- **D-14.27** — Discovery comes from quartz-attached rough gold on proximal placer samples, records, listings and site visits, never from a free reveal. — Ties the track to the placer game ("find where the creek gold came from") and to R3's particle-shape evidence.
- **D-14.28** — Hard rock ships under `usFederal` and `private` regimes only; Alaska-style and Yukon-style hard-rock rules (quartz claims, quartz mining licence, Type A/B water licences) are later content rows. — Each regime's hard-rock permitting is a project of its own; the federal model is the template.
- **D-14.29** — Shrinkage stopes release only the 35% swell during mining and the rest at final draw. — The method's real cash-flow signature, and the reason its low cost is not free.
- **D-14.30** — Flotation, heap leach, roasting and pressure oxidation are out of scope. — Refractory ore appears as a recovery penalty and toll refusals; adding circuits would double the mill model for little decision value.
- **D-14.31** — Refractory share is a share of the panel's total gold, and the gravity-recoverable share is `grg × (1 − refr)`; recovery leaches the free and refractory remainders separately. — Without the (1 − refr) factor gravity would recover gold locked in sulfide (grg + refr could exceed 1), flooring refractory CIL recovery near 60% and breaking the 30–60% anchor.
- **D-14.32** — Records reveal only systems the old-timers found; blind systems are found by placer hints and soil lines, and are mostly open ground (status logit −2.0, visible +1.0). — Gives the two discovery paths different payoffs (buy a known prospect vs stake an unknown one) and rewards the geologist-led placer work the track is built on.
- **D-14.33** — The develop tier needs one year with ≥ 8 weeks of plan-tier placer production. — "Graduation" in the brief's sense; also keeps hard rock out of the first-two-seasons balance targets except a Notice bulk sample.
- **D-14.34** — The pre-production stream's share is solved from the deposit at an 18% streamer IRR on a 0.8 haircut of the PEA's P50 production, clamped to 4–25%. — A fixed 6–8% for 35% of capex would give the streamer a negative return (≈ 15% is the break-even at its hurdle rate), making the stream a free lunch.
- **D-14.35** — Underground labor emerges from §8 payroll; method and heading tables carry only non-labor $/st and $/ft, with labor shown as a reference split. — Posting a direct $/st that already contains wages would double-count every miner's pay.
- **D-14.36** — The hard-rock site reuses §7's `tailings`, `power` and `water` stages and causes, §6's `technicalReview` stage and `fed.explosives` id, and §4's `'sample'` stream; it adds only the stages and causes placer lacks. — Extend, never fork: the Flow tab, alerts and explain trees keep one vocabulary.
- **D-14.37** — Lode drilling: RC $45/ft and HQ core $95/ft north (≈ $148/m and $310/m), arid × 0.75 through §4's multiplier. — Lower rates ($28 and $55) would sit below §4's own placer RC ($75/ft) and the low end of all-in contractor rates; remote northern core is costlier than Nevada core.
- **D-14.38** — Mill power is billed on motor draw × hours (a ball mill draws near-constant power); Bond's law sets throughput only. — Makes fine grinding cost power per ton, as it does, and puts small-mill power at the real 40–60 kWh/st.
- **D-14.39** — Toll mills: settlement at the mill's assay unless the player assays a split; refractory lots lose payable recovery point for point above 15% and pay $40/st above 25%; toll-service recovery carries a 3.5% campaign loss. — Custom-mill practice (splits, umpires, refractory penalties, campaign clean-out) in three closed-form rules.
- **D-14.40** — Year-round hard-rock sites use 52 expected active weeks in §6's inspection rate. — Otherwise MSHA's 4 underground inspections a year become ≈ 9.5 when divided by a placer district's 22 weeks.
- **D-14.41** — No `hardrock.*` key is difficulty-scaled. Difficulty reaches the track only through §1 1.11's existing rows (§12 event frequency and severity for blast and ground events, §11 lender patience for project loans, §6 inspections and review times); there is no capex-overrun multiplier on hard. — §1's two-way test (D-1.44) requires every difficulty-scaled key to be a 1.11 row, and an optional P6 track should not add rows to the core difficulty table.

### 14.23 Open questions

- **OQ-14.1 — Panel resolution and save format.** *Resolved — owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (§0).* 50-ft vein-plane panels stay (D-14.3). The design packs 50 × 50 ft vein-plane panels (D-14.3). Changing to finer panels or true 3D blocks later changes the packed truth, the estimator's grid, slice draws and saves, so it is expensive to reverse. **Default: 50-ft vein-plane panels.**
- **OQ-14.2 — Does hard rock count toward scoring and the balance targets?** *Resolved — owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (§0).* Default: on in the sandbox; goal scenarios disable it unless they name it; BALANCE's brief targets (first two seasons) are measured with it off, and the dominance matrix is reported both ways. Reversing this after tuning would mean re-tuning both games.
- **OQ-14.3 — Is cyanide (CIL) in the own-mill path, or only gravity plus toll leaching?** *Resolved — owner ruling 2026-10-05: default confirmed (§0).* Default: CIL included in P6e with WPCP, ICMC and the water-treatment provision. Dropping it later removes the main recovery lever and a large slice of §6 and §11 content; adding it later means retrofitting permits and bonds into existing saves.

### 14.24 Sources

- R1 (U.S. federal law; 2026): lode claims up to 1,500 × 600 ft; patent price $5.00/acre for lode; 43 CFR 3809 Notice (< 1,000 tons bulk sample, ≤ 5 ac) and Plan tiers; MSHA Mine ID, Part 48 training, inspection minimums and penalty ranges; explosives excluded from casual use.
- R3 (geology and processing; 2026, [U]): 1 g/t ≈ 0.049 oz/bcy and short-ton conversions; rough, crystalline or quartz-attached gold has travelled < 1–2 km from its lode; compound-Poisson nugget model and particle counts; fineness and silver by district; doré weight chain.
- R4 (equipment, labor, costs; 2026, [U]): labor rates and burden, workers' comp class magnitudes, injury and fatality rates, generator fuel burn.
- R5 (finance; 2026, [U]): stream and royalty structures and multiples; equity terms; fire assay $40–100 per sample, umpire $150–300; refinery payables and silver credits.
- BLM, *Mining Claim Fees* (blm.gov, 2026): $200 maintenance fee per lode claim; lode claims up to 1,500 × 600 ft (≈ 20.66–20.7 ac).
- ATF, *Federal Explosives Licenses and Permits* and Form 5400.13/5400.16 (atf.gov): user permit $100, renewal $50, 3-year term; 27 CFR 555 Subpart K magazine storage; 27 CFR 555.30 theft/loss reporting.
- MSHA, *Mine Inspections* (msha.gov): every underground mine at least 4 times a year, surface mines twice (Mine Act §103(a)).
- 30 CFR 48.5 (Cornell LII): underground new-miner training ≥ 40 hours before assignment, ~8 hours at the mine site; 8-hour annual refresher.
- Costmine via *Canadian Mining Journal*, "The cost of driving drifts in various scenarios" and SRK (2024): all-in development ≈ C$6,650/m for a 3.6-m heading (≈ US$1,460/ft).
- *E&MJ*, Veris Gold toll-milling agreements (Nevada): toll fee $148.50 per short ton incl. trucking, adjusted quarterly; doré remains the miner's property; Jerritt Canyon recoveries ~86%.
- *Northern Miner*, Gunsteel 100 tpd B.C. project: used 100 tpd mill ≈ $1M installed; $143/t development-stage opex with a two-miner crew.
- 911Metallurgist, *Operating Costs of Gold Processing Plant*; Mining.com, *Gold toll milling in Peru* (150 tpd toll plant bought for US$3.3M); toll fee structures $8.80–18/t at large mills.
- IMARC (2025–26): U.S. sodium cyanide $1,840–3,200 per tonne; leach consumption 0.25–2 kg/t.
- Farmonaut (2025, low confidence): diamond core $85–150/m, RC $45–80/m before mobilization, consumables and standby (all-in often 2× base).
- 30 CFR Part 49 (mine rescue teams or a contracted arrangement for every underground mine) and 30 CFR 57.15030 (self-rescue devices for everyone underground); 27 CFR 555.203–.213 (magazine types; detonators stored apart from other explosives; Type 2 magazines usable underground).
- §11 11.18 (`wcRates` mining $7.50 / $4.00 / $6.00 per $100 by jurisdiction) as the base for the underground and mill multipliers; R5 streamer target IRR 12–20%+ for small producers (pre-production stream sizing).
- [U] = unverified model knowledge used for magnitudes where no source above applies: powder factors, explosive prices, mill capex at 100–250 st/day, recoveries by ore type, gravity-recoverable gold ranges, TSF costs, stoping method parameters, ore-shoot geometry, toll refractory rules and campaign loss, small-mill power (40–60 kWh/st), soil-anomaly detection, project-finance terms. Treat as starting values for the P6 simulator.
